abstract: Plant diseases pose escalating threats to global food security, particularly under climate change-driven shifts in pathogen biogeography and host susceptibility. Current predictive models inadequately capture the spatiotemporal complexity of polycyclic pathogen spread across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes, especially when integrating dynamic host-pathogen-environment interactions at multiple scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, agent-based computational framework to simulate epidemic emergence in staple crops, with an initial focus on soil-borne fungal pathogens in wheat systems. The model will integrate (1) spatially explicit soil microbiome metagenomic data, (2) real-time weather pattern projections, and (3) genetically diverse host resistance profiles to quantify emergent disease dynamics. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized execution of >10^6 parameter combinations across simulated landscapes, incorporating stochastic weather events and evolving pathogen populations through deep reinforcement learning algorithms. Key innovations include the implementation of hybrid neural networks to predict microenvironment-specific infection probabilities and GPU-accelerated cellular automata modeling for rhizosphere-level microbial community interactions. Expected outcomes include identification of critical leverage points for preemptive disease management through sensitivity analyses across biological, agronomic, and climatic variables. The framework will generate open-access risk projection maps with 1km² resolution, enabling targeted surveillance for high-risk pathogen genotype × environment combinations. This computational approach advances phytopathology by bridging molecular-scale host-microbe interactions with landscape-scale epidemiological patterns, providing a novel platform to optimize resilience in ecologically intensified cropping systems. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU clusters and distributed memory architectures to manage petabyte-scale outputs from coupled biological-physical simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: Child and adolescent mental health disorders, including anxiety, depression, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), represent a growing public health crisis, with significant heterogeneity in symptom presentation, treatment response, and long-term outcomes. Current diagnostic frameworks and intervention strategies lack precision, partly due to limited integration of multimodal biological, behavioral, and environmental data. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale neuroimaging, genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and real-time mobile sensor datasets from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 participants (ages 8–18). The computational demands of integrating these heterogeneous data types—including voxel-based morphometry MRI analyses, whole-genome sequencing, and natural language processing of clinical notes—exceed the capacity of standard clinical research infrastructure. We propose developing a machine learning pipeline using federated learning architectures to preserve data privacy while training predictive models for illness trajectories and treatment outcomes. Graph neural networks will map dynamic interactions between neurodevelopmental markers and environmental stressors, while Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify uncertainty in personalized risk stratification. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biobehavioral subtypes of depression and ADHD, validated against 12-month functional outcomes, and a scalable computational framework for optimizing intervention timing. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, HPC resources will directly accelerate translational insights, with the potential to transform clinical practice through data-driven diagnostic tools and adaptive treatment algorithms. This work aligns with national priorities in precision mental health, offering a paradigm to reduce long-term disability by computationally targeting mechanisms underlying illness heterogeneity.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of developmental, behavioral, emotional, and mental disorders of childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the transmission of Tibetan religious and cultural narratives across digital archives, with a focus on understudied texts produced in diaspora communities. While Tibetan Studies has increasingly engaged digital humanities methods, the scale and complexity of multilingual textual corpora—spanning classical Tibetan, modern vernaculars, and exile community publications—present computational challenges that exceed the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in doctrinal adaptation, lexical shifts, and cross-regional knowledge exchange within these texts, which are critical to understanding how Tibetan cultural identity is reconstituted in transnational contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will apply transformer-based language models fine-tuned for classical Tibetan and Himalayan languages to perform semantic similarity analyses, temporal topic modeling, and network mapping of textual references across 15,000 digitized manuscripts, pamphlets, and periodicals. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing on GPU clusters to handle non-Latin script tokenization, low-resource language alignment, and sparse-data training scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for cross-temporal and cross-community textual analysis in Tibetan Studies, (2) quantitative evidence of narrative preservation versus innovation in post-1959 exile literature, and (3) open-access visualization tools mapping doctrinal linkages between pre-modern and contemporary sources. By enabling large-scale interrogation of cultural production mechanisms, this work will provide new empirical foundations for theorizing resilience in diasporic knowledge systems while directly supporting the preservation priorities of Tibetan archival institutions. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets and train domain-specific models that account for Tibetan Buddhism’s unique lexico-conceptual structures, which mainstream NLP tools frequently misrepresent.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: The apparel and accessories industry faces mounting pressure to reconcile rapid trend cycles with sustainable practices, requiring agile operational strategies that minimize waste while maximizing customer engagement. Traditional demand forecasting and inventory management approaches struggle to account for real-time consumer sentiment, environmental impact metrics, and dynamic supply chain disruptions. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating social media analytics, IoT-enabled customer interaction data, and multi-objective optimization to balance sustainability targets with commercial viability. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing (to extract latent sustainability preferences from user-generated content) and graph neural networks (to model interdependencies among suppliers, materials, and distribution channels). Concurrently, agent-based simulations will test inventory allocation strategies under varying carbon pricing scenarios and geopolitical constraints. The computational intensity of training these models on terabytes of unstructured text, image, and transactional data—while maintaining low-latency responses for real-time scenario planning—necessitates distributed computing capabilities. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between production lead times, textile waste reduction, and personalized marketing efficacy, validated against historical data from three multinational apparel retailers. By enabling simultaneous optimization of environmental impact and customer retention metrics, this research aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven operational sustainability in fashion marketing ecosystems, addressing a critical gap in applied computational business research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of apparel and accessories. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, apparel technologies, distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of equine biomechanics and rider-horse interaction dynamics, a critical yet understudied area in equestrian science. Despite the global economic and cultural significance of equine industries, quantitative models capable of predicting stress patterns in horses during training or competition remain limited. Traditional methods rely on observational data and simplified physical assessments, which lack the resolution to map complex musculoskeletal loads or optimize welfare-focused training protocols. To address this gap, we propose developing a multiscale computational framework integrating motion-capture data, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and analyze equine movement under varying riding conditions. High-fidelity 3D models of horse-rider pairs, derived from MRI and LiDAR scans, will be subjected to dynamic load simulations across gaits (walk, trot, canter) and jumping sequences. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including muscle activation patterns, ground reaction forces, and saddle pressure distributions, while ML algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers for injury risk and performance efficiency. The project will validate models against empirical data from inertial measurement units (IMUs) and force plates collected from collegiate equestrian teams. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for trainers and veterinarians to customize training regimens, reduce musculoskeletal injuries, and improve equine longevity. By bridging computational biomechanics with equestrian practice, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven decision-making in a field traditionally reliant on subjective expertise, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-STEM disciplines aligned with animal welfare and human-equine partnerships.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the horse, horsemanship, and related subjects and prepares individuals to care for horses and horse equipment; ride and drive horses for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes; and manage the training of horses and riders. Includes instruction in horse breeding, nutrition, health, and safety; history of the horse and horsemanship; horse development and training; riding and equestrian technique; stable, paddock, and track management; and equipment maintenance and repair.

abstract: The increasing complexity of embedded systems in modern computing applications demands robust methodologies to optimize hardware-software co-design under stringent power, latency, and reliability constraints. This project seeks to address challenges in developing adaptive embedded architectures for edge computing devices, where traditional simulation tools fail to scale efficiently for heterogeneous system-on-chip (SoC) designs. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize and accelerate the simulation, validation, and optimization of configurable computing platforms. The research will focus on three computational phases: (1) emulating multi-core SoC architectures with reconfigurable peripheral interfaces using cycle-accurate models, (2) implementing machine learning-driven design space exploration to identify optimal task partitioning strategies, and (3) stress-testing fault tolerance mechanisms through Monte Carlo simulations of component failure scenarios. By distributing these compute-intensive tasks across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce simulation time for complex configurations from weeks to days while maintaining high modeling fidelity. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for scalable embedded system prototyping and quantitative guidelines for balancing computational parallelism with inter-process communication overhead in reconfigurable architectures. The results will directly support the development of energy-efficient edge computing solutions for industrial IoT applications while providing Computer Engineering Technology students with hands-on experience in HPC-accelerated hardware design workflows. This work bridges critical gaps between theoretical embedded systems concepts and practical large-scale computational evaluation, addressing a key need in engineering technology education and industry-ready tool development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of computer engineers engaged in designing and developing computer systems and installations. Includes instruction in computer electronics and programming, prototype development and testing, systems installation and testing, solid state and microminiature circuitry, peripheral equipment, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize maternal-fetal health outcomes in community-based midwifery care using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Despite the efficacy of direct-entry midwifery in supporting low-risk pregnancies, unpredictable complications such as postpartum hemorrhage, hypertensive disorders, or fetal distress remain critical challenges. Current risk stratification tools often lack precision due to limited integration of dynamic variables such as longitudinal biometric data, socio-environmental factors, and real-time physiological trends. This research will address this gap by constructing machine learning models trained on multi-source datasets, including de-identified electronic health records (EHRs), wearable device outputs, and community health surveys. Computational workflows will integrate time-series analysis of maternal vitals, natural language processing of clinical notes, and geospatial mapping of resource access disparities. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train deep neural networks for anomaly detection in labor progression patterns, and simulate population-level outcomes under varying intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated risk prediction dashboard to guide midwives in preemptive decision-making, personalized care plan optimization, and emergency readiness protocols. The models will also quantify the impact of socio-economic determinants on birth outcomes, informing policy recommendations for equitable maternal care. By leveraging distributed computing for parallelized model training and hyperparameter optimization, this work will advance precision midwifery practices while maintaining ethical standards for data privacy and bias mitigation. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools for midwifery educators and clinical partners, directly supporting the program’s mission to improve maternal health equity through evidence-based, community-centered care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide pre-natal, natural birth, and immediate postpartum care to pregnant women in jurisdictions licensing direct (non-nursing) training for midwives. Includes instruction in basic obstetrics, women's health, fetal development, childbirth education, maternal nutrition and health, labor support, natural childbirth, postpartum support, prebirth counseling and risk screening, management of obstetric emergencies, patient referral, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of vocal performance through computational modeling and analysis of physiological, acoustic, and pedagogical data. While voice training traditionally relies on subjective mentorship and qualitative feedback, the lack of standardized, data-driven frameworks limits the scalability of personalized instruction and the understanding of biomechanical factors influencing vocal health and artistic expression. The research will address this gap by developing computational models of vocal fold dynamics, respiratory patterns, and acoustic output under varying performance conditions (e.g., repertoire demands, vocal registers, linguistic diction). High-fidelity simulations will integrate MRI-derived anatomical datasets, real-time motion capture of expressive movement, and spectral analysis of recorded performances to map correlations between physiological parameters and artistic outcomes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in historical and contemporary vocal pedagogies, enabling the generation of adaptive training recommendations. Additionally, HPC resources will support the creation of a multimodal database for voice educators, linking performance metrics with pedagogical annotations. Expected outcomes include predictive models for injury prevention, tools to optimize rehearsal efficiency, and evidence-based frameworks for repertoire selection tailored to individual vocal profiles. By bridging computational science and performing arts methodologies, this work aims to transform vocal pedagogy into a data-enriched discipline while preserving the nuance of artistic tradition. The scalability of these tools will benefit both emerging artists and established professionals, fostering sustainable vocal practices across opera, concert, and ensemble contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the human voice and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers in concert, choir, opera, or other forms of singing. Includes instruction in voice pedagogy, diction, vocal physiology and exercise, expressive movement, repertoire, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of African-American/Black literary texts and oral traditions across the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean. While the cultural and aesthetic complexity of this literature—spanning novels, poetry, folklore, sermons, and musical forms like spirituals and hip-hop—has been richly documented, systematic computational studies of its linguistic patterns, thematic evolution, and intertextual networks remain limited. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to synthesize the vast, multilingual, and multimedia corpora that reflect the diaspora’s literary and folkloric diversity. This project addresses this gap by developing scalable text and audio analysis pipelines to map stylistic, rhetorical, and thematic connections across genres, periods, and regions. Computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned on African-American vernacular English (AAVE) and Creole-language texts, network analysis to trace the circulation of motifs (e.g., trickster figures, ancestral memory), and machine learning classifiers to identify rhetorical strategies tied to resistance and cultural preservation. Audio recordings of oral narratives and performances will be processed using speech-to-text algorithms and spectral analysis to correlate linguistic features with rhythmic or tonal patterns. HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s terabyte-scale datasets, training custom transformer-based models, and running parallelized analyses across hybrid text/audio workflows. Expected outcomes include a public digital archive of annotated texts and oral histories, visualizations of transnational literary networks, and new methodologies for computational humanities research centered on African diasporic contexts. By integrating computational rigor with cultural specificity, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of how Black literary traditions innovate, adapt, and sustain collective memory amid shifting sociopolitical landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the safety, efficacy, and innovation of nail care practices through computational modeling and data-driven analysis. While nail technology is traditionally a hands-on field, emerging challenges—such as optimizing sterilization protocols, predicting allergenicity of novel cosmetic formulations, and modeling the biomechanical interactions between nail products and natural nail structures—require sophisticated computational approaches. Current training and practice rely heavily on empirical knowledge, with limited tools to systematically evaluate risks or design evidence-based solutions. This research addresses gaps in understanding microbial persistence under salon conditions, chemical stability of hybrid gel polishes, and stress distribution in artificial nail extensions. Computational methods will include finite element analysis to simulate mechanical forces on nail architectures, molecular dynamics to study polymer-curing processes, and machine learning models trained on microbial genomic data to predict pathogen survival post-sterilization. Additionally, agent-based models will evaluate contamination risks in salon workflows. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to generate actionable insights for improving sanitization standards, reducing occupational hazards, and guiding product development. Outcomes will include open-access datasets on material properties and microbial thresholds, predictive tools for allergy risk assessment, and simulation frameworks for training nail technicians in virtual environments. This work bridges the technical-artisanal divide, positioning computational research as a transformative force in a field where empirical tradition and modern scientific rigor intersect.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shape fingernails and toenails, remove unwanted skin and blemishes, apply polish and cosmetics to nails, and function as licensed manicurists or nail technicians/specialists.  Includes instruction in manicuring theory; skin anatomy; nail growth, irregularities, and diseases; sterilization and sanitation; equipment and table maintenance; cuticle, blemish, and rough skin removal; nail filing, shaping, and polishing; cream application and extremity massage; nail sculpture and design art; product storage and use; customer service; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: Environmental toxicology faces critical challenges in predicting the health risks of complex chemical mixtures encountered in real-world environments, where dynamic interactions between pollutants, ecological systems, and biological organisms complicate traditional toxicity assessments. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the transport, bioaccumulation, and multi-organ toxicity of priority environmental contaminants, including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), heavy metals, and pesticide mixtures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate three-dimensional atmospheric dispersion models, watershed-scale hydrologic simulations, and physiologically based toxicokinetic (PBTK) models to quantify exposure pathways from emission sources to human tissues. Agent-based modeling will simulate population-level variability in susceptibility based on age, metabolic capacity, and co-exposure histories. Machine learning algorithms trained on EPA ToxCast data and historical biomonitoring datasets will predict synergistic effects of chemical combinations. The computational workflow requires parallel processing to manage stochastic simulations across spatial scales (molecular interactions to ecosystem-level transport) and temporal resolutions (acute exposure events to decades of bioaccumulation). Expected outcomes include predictive maps of regional toxicity hotspots, probabilistic risk assessments for vulnerable subpopulations, and a publicly accessible database linking chemical structures to tissue-specific toxicodynamic parameters. This resource will directly inform regulatory strategies for emerging contaminants and remediation prioritization in high-risk environments. The project's scale necessitates access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning components and large-memory nodes for geospatial analyses, exceeding the capacity of local institutional clusters. By bridging environmental fate modeling with mechanistic toxicology, this work advances precision public health interventions while addressing computational gaps in mixture toxicity research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the health effects associated with exposure to toxic chemicals and systems occurring in the natural, work, and living environments; the management of environmental toxins and toxicity; and the development of protections for humans, animals, and plants. Includes instruction in applied ecology; microbiology; toxin transport, fate, and degradation; dermal toxicology; reproductive and genetic toxicology; atmospheric and environmental chemistry; metals toxicology; environmental mutagens and biotransformation; nutrient interaction; chemical sensitivity, disorders, and disease; risk assessment; animal waste management; environmental health; and hazardous materials management.

abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying enzyme-substrate interactions and DNA-protein binding dynamics is critical for elucidating fundamental biological processes, yet experimental approaches alone often fail to resolve transient conformational states or quantify energy landscapes at atomic resolution. This project aims to investigate the structural and energetic determinants of helicase-mediated DNA unwinding and its regulation by cofactors, a system central to replication and repair. We propose to employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enhanced sampling techniques, and free energy calculations to characterize the mechanochemical coupling and nucleotide-dependent conformational changes in a model helicase complex. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve microsecond-scale simulations of multi-component systems (>500,000 atoms) and perform Markov state model analysis to map rare transitions. Parallelized workflows using AMBER and GROMACS will integrate experimental cryo-EM density maps as spatial restraints, while alchemical metadynamics will quantify ATP hydrolysis-driven remodeling of protein-DNA interfaces. Expected outcomes include identifying critical residues mediating processivity, predicting allosteric networks that synchronize motor domains, and modeling how post-translational modifications alter unwinding efficiency. These insights will advance mechanistic understanding of replication fidelity and provide a computational framework for studying helicase dysregulation linked to genetic disorders. The requested resources will enable parameterization of coarse-grained models for long-timescale studies and support machine learning approaches to classify functional conformational states from simulation trajectories. By bridging atomic-scale dynamics with cellular function, this work will establish predictive models of macromolecular interactions relevant to synthetic biology and enzyme engineering applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of biological macromolecules and the role of molecular constituents and mechanisms in supramolecular assemblies and cells. Includes instruction in such topics as molecular signaling and transduction, regulation of cell growth, enzyme substrates and mechanisms of enzyme action, DNA-protein interaction, and applications to fields such as biotechnology, genetics, cell biology, and physiology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of chemical processes in industrial applications, particularly in catalysis and reaction engineering, demands advanced computational tools to optimize efficiency and sustainability. Current challenges include accurately modeling multi-scale reaction dynamics, predicting catalytic performance under extreme conditions, and scaling laboratory-derived mechanisms to industrial reactor environments. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-scale computational models that bridge quantum mechanical simulations of molecular interactions with macro-scale fluid dynamics in industrial reactors. The research will focus on two primary systems: (1) transition-metal catalysts for green ammonia synthesis under low-temperature, low-pressure conditions, and (2) polymerization processes with complex rheological behavior in continuous flow reactors. Computational methods will combine density functional theory (DFT) for electronic structure calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) for intermediate-scale behavior, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with machine learning algorithms for system optimization. These multi-layered simulations require parallel processing capabilities to handle large parameter spaces, transient boundary conditions, and stochastic elements in reaction networks. The requested HPC resources will enable the execution of ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty in kinetic parameters and predict optimal operating conditions for industrial-scale processes. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel catalyst configurations with 20-30% improved energy efficiency compared to conventional Haber-Bosch systems, as well as validated models for polymer molecular weight distribution control within ±5% of target specifications. This work will directly support collaborative efforts with regional chemical manufacturers to reduce carbon footprints and transition toward modular, adaptive production systems. By integrating computational results with experimental validation from partner laboratories, the project aims to establish a framework for accelerated development of sustainable chemical technologies while training students in cutting-edge computational chemistry methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of chemical and biochemical research and industrial operations. Includes instruction in principles of chemistry and biochemistry, technical mathematics, computer applications, radiochemistry, industrial biochemistry, chemical instrumentation, physical chemistry, laboratory research methods, industrial processing methods and equipment, and test equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of psychodynamic processes in therapeutic interactions through computational modeling and large-scale natural language processing (NLP). Traditional psychoanalytic research has relied on qualitative case studies and manual coding of clinical sessions, limiting scalability and reproducibility. The proposed research addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to analyze longitudinal therapy transcripts, quantify patterns in transference-countertransference dynamics, and model the emergence of unconscious conflict resolution during treatment. Using anonymized datasets comprising over 10,000 hours of psychotherapy session transcripts across diverse clinical populations, we will implement neural language models to identify latent linguistic markers of defense mechanisms, emotional valence shifts, and therapeutic alliance fluctuations. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate dyadic patient-therapist interactions under varying psychodynamic principles to test hypotheses about optimal intervention timing. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing high-dimensional text data, training transformer-based architectures on therapeutic dialogue, and running parallelized simulations of complex interpersonal dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated NLP pipeline for automated detection of clinically relevant psychodynamic phenomena, (2) computational evidence linking specific interaction patterns to treatment outcomes, and (3) open-source tools enabling real-time analysis of therapeutic process variables. By bridging psychoanalytic theory with computational psychiatry methods, this work aims to establish quantitative foundations for psychodynamic research while providing clinicians with data-driven insights into intervention efficacy. The project represents a novel convergence of depth psychology and artificial intelligence, addressing core challenges in mental health care personalization and mechanistic understanding of psychotherapy.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to practice the provision of psychoanalytic counseling to individuals and groups based on the psychodynamic principles evolved from authorities such as Freud, Adler, and Jung. Includes instruction in self-analysis, personality theory, dream analysis, free association and transference theory and techniques, psychodynamic theory, developmental processes, applications to specific clinical conditions, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of energy-efficient, high-performance computer hardware systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As hardware complexity grows—driven by demands for edge computing, AI acceleration, and heterogeneous architectures—traditional design methodologies struggle to balance power consumption, thermal management, and computational throughput. We propose a multi-physics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model next-generation integrated circuits and hardware subsystems at unprecedented scales. The computational approach integrates finite-element analysis for thermal-electrical coupling, Monte Carlo methods for manufacturing variability prediction, and machine learning-driven topology optimization to co-design chip layouts and cooling solutions. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times for 3D-stacked architectures and photonic interconnects from weeks to days while maintaining nanometer-scale fidelity. The project will also develop open-source tools for automated design space exploration, enabling rapid benchmarking of novel materials and transistor geometries. Expected outcomes include validated models for low-power, high-reliability hardware configurations targeting IoT and data center applications, with projected energy savings of 15-20% over current commercial designs. These advancements will directly support academic research in reconfigurable computing and fault-tolerant systems while providing industry-relevant datasets for sustainable hardware innovation. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization loops inherent to multi-objective hardware co-design, which cannot feasibly run on local clusters. This work bridges computational engineering and applied computer hardware research, offering foundational insights for next-generation device development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and evaluation of computer hardware and related peripheral equipment. Includes instruction in computer circuit and chip design, circuitry, computer systems design, computer equipment design, computer layout planning, testing procedures, and related computer theory and software topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in reconstructing and interpreting fragmented ancient texts, a critical barrier in classical and ancient studies. Thousands of papyri, inscriptions, and manuscript fragments from Greco-Roman, Near Eastern, and early medieval contexts remain unreadable due to physical degradation, disordering, or linguistic ambiguities. Traditional manual reconstruction methods are labor-intensive and limited in scalability, particularly for cross-referencing multilingual corpora or detecting patterns across vast spatiotemporal contexts. This project proposes a computational pipeline integrating machine learning (ML), natural language processing (NLP), and image analysis to automate fragment reassembly and contextual analysis. Neural networks will be trained on digitized text corpora (e.g., the Papyri.info database, epigraphic archives) and 3D-scanned artifact datasets to identify linguistic, stylistic, and material features that signal fragment relationships. Parallelized algorithms will map syntactic structures and semantic networks across languages (e.g., Greek, Latin, Coptic), while probabilistic models simulate plausible textual reconstructions. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution multispectral imaging data, train deep learning models on heterogeneous datasets (textual, visual, and archaeological), and run large-scale simulations of fragment alignment hypotheses. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for fragment analysis, newly reconstructed texts with confidence metrics, and interactive visualizations of textual networks. These results will advance understanding of cultural exchange, administrative practices, and literary transmission in antiquity, while establishing methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary collaboration between computational sciences and humanities. The project’s open-source tools and datasets will provide a foundation for future research in digital philology, reducing barriers to studying fragmentary heritage. By addressing computational bottlenecks in data integration and model training, this work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in unlocking inaccessible dimensions of ancient history.
cip_definition: Any program in classical and ancient studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for precision in equine hoof care necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize farriery practices, which currently rely heavily on empirical knowledge and manual craftsmanship. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the biomechanical interactions between horseshoes, hoof morphology, and equine locomotion through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled modeling and simulation. Traditional approaches to corrective shoeing and gait analysis lack the granularity to account for dynamic, three-dimensional stress distributions or material behavior under varying load conditions, leading to suboptimal outcomes in hoof health and performance. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain modeling of hoof-shoe systems, machine learning (ML)-driven gait pattern recognition, and thermodynamic simulations of metal forging processes. The FEA component will model hoof tissue response to different shoe geometries and alloys, calibrated using micro-CT scan data of equine hooves. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze motion-capture datasets from equine gait laboratories to identify correlations between shoeing modifications and biomechanical efficiency. A parallel computational study will simulate coal- and gas-based forging environments to optimize thermal profiles for producing durable, customized shoes. By leveraging HPC resources, these computationally intensive models—which require iterative parameter adjustments and high-resolution volumetric meshes—can be executed at scales unachievable with local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for farriers to preemptively address pathologies like laminitis, data-driven guidelines for alloy selection, and energy-efficient forging protocols. This interdisciplinary effort merges veterinary biomechanics, materials science, and computational engineering, establishing a novel paradigm for evidence-based farrier science while preserving the artisan traditions central to the field. The resulting open-access models and datasets will serve as foundational resources for both practitioners and educators in this specialized domain.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to become specialists in equine hoof care (farriers). Includes instruction in equine science, equine health and first aid, general horseshoeing, corrective horseshoeing, gait analysis, and metal forging techniques using gas or coal.

abstract: Veterinary medicine faces growing challenges in addressing complex, multifactorial diseases that impact animal health and intersect with public health through zoonotic transmission. A critical bottleneck lies in analyzing vast, heterogeneous datasets—ranging from genomic sequences to population-level epidemiological data—to uncover patterns of disease spread, host-pathogen interactions, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) evolution. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale computational analyses aimed at advancing predictive modeling of infectious disease dynamics in animal populations. The research will integrate whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from veterinary pathogens with clinical metadata, environmental variables, and livestock movement records to identify drivers of AMR emergence and transmission across species. Agent-based models will simulate disease spread under varying intervention scenarios, while molecular dynamics simulations will probe structural mechanisms of drug resistance in priority pathogens such as *Salmonella enterica* and *Staphylococcus pseudintermedius*. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to predict outbreak risks and optimize treatment protocols based on regional pathogen surveillance data. By leveraging parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated computing, these analyses will overcome limitations of conventional computing infrastructures, which lack the capacity to process terabyte-scale datasets or execute complex simulations at necessary resolutions. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into AMR transmission networks, validated strategies for outbreak mitigation in livestock systems, and open-access tools for real-time genomic surveillance. This work will directly inform veterinary clinical decision-making, antimicrobial stewardship policies, and One Health initiatives aimed at reducing zoonotic threats. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieving the scale, speed, and integration required for transformative advances in veterinary computational epidemiology and precision medicine.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of veterinary medicine, involving the diagnosis, treatment, and health care management of animals and animal populations and the prevention and management of zoonosis. Includes instruction in the veterinary basic sciences, infectious and noninfectious disease, diagnostic procedures, veterinary clinical medicine, obstetrics, radiology, anesthesiology, surgery, toxicology, animal health and preventive medicine, clinical nutrition, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to simulate fire dynamics and suppression strategies in complex built environments, addressing critical gaps in predicting fire behavior under real-world conditions. Current fire modeling tools often rely on simplified assumptions that neglect coupled phenomena such as turbulent combustion, heat transfer to structural elements, and the interaction of suppression agents with evolving fire plumes. These limitations hinder the design of optimized fire protection systems and evidence-based emergency response protocols. To overcome these challenges, we propose a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve multi-scale, multi-physics processes inherent in fire scenarios. Large-eddy simulations (LES) will model turbulent combustion and soot formation using detailed chemical kinetics, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict heat-induced structural degradation. Coupled agent-based modeling will simulate occupant evacuation dynamics influenced by real-time fire spread predictions. The computational workflow will integrate experimental data from bench-scale fire tests to validate submodels for water mist suppression efficiency and toxic gas dispersion. Machine learning techniques will be employed to accelerate parameter optimization and uncertainty quantification across millions of simulated scenarios. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this research aims to produce predictive tools that inform next-generation fire codes, improve the resilience of building materials, and enable AI-driven decision support systems for fireground operations. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation modules for the fire science community, risk assessment guidelines for high-occupancy structures, and training datasets for firefighter situational awareness technologies. The requested computing resources will directly support the parallelized execution of 3D transient simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (<1 cm) and temporal scales (<10 ms), which are computationally infeasible with existing institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: Epilepsy remains a significant neurological disorder, with approximately one-third of patients experiencing drug-resistant seizures. Surgical intervention can offer relief, yet outcomes depend critically on accurate localization of epileptogenic zones, which current diagnostic tools—including scalp EEG, MRI, and clinical semiology—often fail to resolve with sufficient precision. This project seeks to address this challenge by developing patient-specific computational models of seizure generation and propagation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multimodal neuroimaging, electrophysiological data, and biophysical neural network simulations. The core research problem centers on improving the spatial and temporal resolution of epileptogenic zone mapping to guide surgical planning and reduce post-operative recurrence. To achieve this, we will construct individualized brain models using structural MRI, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and intracranial EEG (iEEG) data, incorporating neuron-glial interactions and network connectivity derived from empirical patient records. Large-scale simulations of seizure dynamics will be performed using parallelized implementations of coupled neural mass models and finite-element methods to account for tissue heterogeneity. Machine learning pipelines will analyze simulation outputs alongside clinical datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of seizure spread. The computational demands of these tasks—including the need for real-time parameter optimization, high-dimensional data processing, and ensemble modeling across heterogeneous cohorts—necessitate HPC resources for memory-intensive workloads and GPU-accelerated computation. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated framework for integrating multimodal data into dynamic seizure propagation models, (2) improved preoperative localization accuracy compared to current clinical standards, and (3) open-source tools for simulating patient-specific therapeutic interventions, such as virtual resections or neurostimulation protocols. By enabling precise mapping of epileptic networks, this work has the potential to directly enhance surgical outcomes, reduce invasive monitoring burdens, and provide a platform for in silico testing of novel antiepileptic therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of patients with epileptic seizures or with symptoms and signs whose differential diagnosis includes epileptic seizures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design and fabrication of structural and ornamental ironwork, addressing critical challenges in load distribution, thermal stress management, and material efficiency. While traditional ironworking relies on empirical methods and standardized codes, increasingly complex architectural demands and sustainability requirements necessitate data-driven approaches to predict structural behavior under dynamic conditions. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in large-scale metal structures, including stress-strain dynamics during welding, thermal deformation in ornamental components, and fatigue resistance in high-load environments. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify optimal beam configurations, welding parameters, and reinforcement patterns. Simulations will integrate real-world data from strain gauges and thermal sensors to validate models against physical prototypes. The computational workload requires parallel processing to manage iterative optimizations across millions of mesh elements and time steps, which is infeasible with local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing material waste in fabrication, enhancing the safety margins of custom architectural designs, and reducing reliance on physical prototyping. These tools will be disseminated as open-source modules for educational use in ironworking programs, bridging gaps between traditional trade skills and computational literacy. By advancing the precision of structural simulations, this work aims to set new benchmarks for energy-efficient metal construction and support the development of next-generation building codes. The project aligns with national priorities for sustainable infrastructure and workforce development in technical fields, offering a template for integrating HPC-driven innovation into trade education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to make and install structural, ornamental, and reinforcing metal structures and supports. Includes instruction in drafting, technical mathematics, blueprint interpretation, welding, riveting, beam placement, ornamental design, structural reinforcement, crane operation, safety, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing epigenetic editing for tissue-specific gene therapy using high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic chromatin interactions. While CRISPR-based gene editing has advanced therapeutic targeting, epigenetic modifiers—such as CRISPR-dCas9 systems—require precise spatiotemporal control to avoid off-target effects and ensure stable transcriptional modulation. Current experimental approaches struggle to predict how epigenetic editors interact with the 3D genome architecture of specific cell types, particularly in dynamic disease contexts like fibrosis or neurodegenerative disorders. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omic data (ATAC-seq, Hi-C, and single-cell RNA-seq) with molecular dynamics simulations to predict optimal epigenetic editing windows and delivery strategies. The HPC component will involve two phases: (1) large-scale parallelized modeling of chromatin conformational changes under editing perturbations using coarse-grained molecular dynamics, and (2) machine learning-driven optimization of guide RNA designs for cell-type specificity by training on epigenomic landscapes from diverse human tissues. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to process terabyte-scale chromatin interaction datasets, while the ML models will employ federated learning techniques to maintain data privacy across collaborating clinical partners. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas of editable epigenetic loci for 12 high-priority therapeutic targets, validated in vitro using patient-derived iPSC models. This work will establish a pipeline for rational design of epigenetic therapies, reducing experimental trial-and-error cycles and accelerating translational workflows. By prioritizing computational exploration of off-target risks and tissue-specific efficacy, the project addresses a critical bottleneck in scalable, ethical gene therapy development. The resulting tools and datasets will be disseminated via a cloud-based platform to support reproducibility and community-driven refinement of epigenetic editing strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the supporting structures of teeth, is driven by complex interactions between dysbiotic microbial communities, host immune responses, and genetic and environmental factors. Current clinical strategies often fail to predict disease progression or personalize therapeutic interventions due to gaps in understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of host-microbe crosstalk at the gingival interface. This project seeks to address this challenge by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that integrate single-cell transcriptomic data, spatially resolved metabolomic profiles, and biomechanical simulations of periodontal tissue remodeling. A hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, deep learning for pattern recognition in microbial metagenomic datasets, and finite element analysis will be employed to simulate the evolution of periodontal microenvironments under inflammatory stress. The computational framework will be trained and validated using longitudinal clinical data, including 3D intraoral scans, cytokine profiles, and microbial sequencing from a cohort of 200 patients with stage III/IV periodontitis. Key objectives include identifying nonlinear signaling thresholds that trigger irreversible bone loss, mapping metabolic networks linking specific pathobionts to tissue degradation phenotypes, and predicting patient-specific responses to biomechanical interventions such as occlusal adjustment. By elucidating mechanistic drivers of periodontitis heterogeneity, this work aims to generate actionable biomarkers for early intervention and computational tools to optimize regenerative therapies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling petabyte-scale datasets, parallelizing stochastic simulations, and iterating complex neural networks. Outcomes will advance precision periodontics by bridging molecular-scale discovery with clinical decision-making, while establishing a computational pipeline adaptable to other oral-inflammatory pathologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural semantic alignment in global corporate communication networks using advanced natural language processing (NLP) and graph analytics. As multinational corporations increasingly rely on decentralized, AI-driven communication platforms, mismatches in context-specific meaning—particularly in idioms, metaphors, and culturally embedded terminology—create operational risks and stakeholder misinterpretations. Traditional approaches to localization fail to address real-time semantic drift across distributed teams, necessitating computational methods to model how meaning evolves in multilingual organizational ecosystems. The study will analyze 12+ terabytes of multi-modal corporate communications data (emails, meeting transcripts, internal social media, and press releases) across six languages from three multinational enterprises. A hybrid transformer-graph neural network architecture will be developed to map semantic networks across languages, identifying high-risk zones of conceptual divergence and latent alignment opportunities. High-performance computing resources are essential for training cross-lingual embeddings on industry-specific corpora, running large-scale graph traversals to detect emergent semantic patterns, and simulating communication cascade effects under cultural adaptation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for predictive semantic risk assessment, adaptive retraining protocols for enterprise language models, and evidence-based guidelines for structuring multicultural communication teams. By bridging computational linguistics with organizational communication theory, this work aims to reduce cross-cultural friction in global operations while establishing new metrics for evaluating semantic coherence as a business continuity factor. The computational artifacts developed will be open-sourced to support research at the intersection of AI ethics, decentralized collaboration systems, and intercultural business practices.
cip_definition: Any program in business or corporate communications, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: The therapeutic mechanisms underlying hypnotherapy remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of standardized protocols and objective outcome measures. Current neuroimaging and behavioral studies generate complex, high-dimensional datasets that challenge conventional analytical methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neurophysiological correlates of hypnotic trance states and their relationship to therapeutic efficacy. Multimodal data—including high-density EEG, functional MRI, and real-time behavioral metrics—will be collected from participants undergoing clinically administered hypnotherapy sessions. Computational pipelines will integrate signal processing, dynamic network modeling, and machine learning to identify state-specific neural signatures and predictors of individual susceptibility. HPC capabilities will enable large-scale parallel processing of neuroimaging time series, Bayesian inference of brain-state transitions, and ensemble classification of therapeutic responsiveness across heterogeneous cohorts. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothesized cortico-thalamic interactions modulating trance depth and suggestibility. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomarkers for hypnosis susceptibility, data-driven optimization of induction protocols, and the development of open-source tools for neurophenotypic analysis in hypnotherapy research. By elucidating the dynamical brain systems engaged during therapeutic trance, this work aims to establish empirically validated guidelines for personalized intervention strategies while advancing computational methods for studying altered states of consciousness in clinical populations. The requested resources are critical for handling the project's terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive analyses, which exceed the capacity of local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized neuromotor rehabilitation protocols for individuals with rare neuromuscular disorders, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome current limitations in real-time biosignal processing and adaptive modeling. Current rehabilitation strategies for conditions such as hereditary sensory-motor neuropathies or focal dystonias often rely on generalized therapeutic approaches, which fail to account for the high inter-individual variability in neuromuscular pathophysiology and real-time biomechanical responses. The research problem centers on the lack of dynamic, patient-specific models that integrate electromyographic (EMG), inertial measurement unit (IMU), and neuroimaging data to predict optimal therapeutic interventions. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational pipeline combining finite element modeling of muscle-tendon dynamics with machine learning-driven analysis of neural activation patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multimodal data streams (sampled at 2 kHz across 16 channels) during simulated therapeutic tasks, coupled with GPU-accelerated training of recurrent neural networks to identify latent biomarkers of motor adaptation. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for generating patient-specific rehabilitation profiles, capable of predicting optimal resistance levels, movement trajectories, and neurofeedback timing in simulated environments. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and clinical rehabilitation by establishing a scalable platform for precision therapeutics in underserved neuromuscular populations. The requested resources will specifically support the parameterization of multi-scale musculoskeletal models, real-time data assimilation, and validation against a longitudinal dataset of 120 patients across five rare disorder subtypes. Successful implementation could redefine therapeutic paradigms for rare neuromuscular conditions while providing a template for HPC-enabled adaptive rehabilitation across broader health contexts.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rehabilitation and therapeutic professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing programming skill acquisition through adaptive, data-driven pedagogical frameworks, an emerging niche intersecting computational education and cognitive ergonomics. Traditional programming instruction often employs static curricula, which fail to account for heterogeneous learner backgrounds, cognitive styles, and knowledge retention patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computational infrastructure to model and simulate individualized learning trajectories. The core methodology involves deploying ensemble machine learning algorithms on multimodal educational datasets—including code submission histories, error-resolution patterns, and temporal engagement metrics—to identify latent correlations between instructional strategies and competency development. These models will drive dynamic content generation systems that adjust problem difficulty, conceptual focus, and feedback mechanisms in real time. The computational demands arise from processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning decades of anonymized student records, coupled with parallelized reinforcement learning architectures that require iterative optimization across thousands of simulated learner personas. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for personalized programming education, validated through longitudinal A/B testing against conventional teaching paradigms. Success metrics will quantify reductions in skill attainment disparities across demographic groups and improvements in complex problem-solving transfer rates. By establishing scalable, evidence-based approaches to programming pedagogy, this work aims to redefine how computational resources can democratize access to technical education while advancing interdisciplinary research at the nexus of educational psychology and adaptive systems design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer programming, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance adaptive interface design for immersive augmented reality (AR) environments by integrating real-time cognitive-affective modeling with user behavior analytics. While current AR systems adapt layouts based on basic gaze or gesture inputs, they often fail to account for dynamic cognitive load, perceptual biases, or emotional states, limiting accessibility and exacerbating user fatigue. Our research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that synthesizes multi-modal data streams—including eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and physiological signals—to predict and respond to nuanced user states. The core challenge lies in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive data at low latency while maintaining robust model accuracy across diverse user populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (sampled at 1kHz from 120+ participants) and for simulating interface adaptations through agent-based modeling. The computational pipeline involves three phases: 1) real-time feature extraction from biometric sensors using parallelized signal processing, 2) ensemble learning to classify cognitive load and emotional valence via federated learning architectures, and 3) probabilistic reasoning to optimize interface parameters through differentiable user simulations. Expected outcomes include an open-source library for adaptive interface prototyping and empirical validation showing ≥30% reductions in task completion errors and cognitive strain metrics across neurodiverse user groups. This work bridges human-computer interaction, cognitive neuroscience, and machine learning, offering novel methodologies for personalized human-technology collaboration. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to establish scalable design principles for AR systems that dynamically align with users' biological and perceptual needs, particularly benefiting high-stakes domains like medical visualization and industrial training.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for evaluating the effectiveness of forensic social work interventions. Forensic social workers operate within complex systems where variables such as mental health status, substance use history, criminal justice involvement, and systemic inequities intersect, complicating efforts to assess program outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to account for these multidimensional interactions or to process large-scale administrative data from correctional facilities, healthcare providers, and social service agencies. The proposed research will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble models and neural networks, to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing demographic, clinical, and criminal justice records. Agent-based simulations will also be developed to model the cascading effects of interventions—such as diversion programs or trauma-informed care—on individual outcomes and system-wide costs. HPC resources are critical for training these models on sensitive, high-dimensional data while maintaining privacy through federated learning frameworks. Expected outcomes include the identification of intervention components most strongly associated with reduced recidivism, improved mental health trajectories, and equitable service access. The computational tools generated will enable forensic social work practitioners to dynamically simulate policy impacts, optimize resource allocation in underfunded systems, and advocate for data-driven reforms. By integrating computational social science methodologies with domain-specific expertise, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for evidence-based decision-making in justice-involved populations, ultimately contributing to more effective and ethically grounded service delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as social workers in correctional facilities, mental health hospitals, the justice system, substance abuse treatment programs, and victim assistance. Includes instruction in forensic social work, criminal justice administration, domestic violence, ethics, juvenile justice systems, mental illness and crime, program evaluation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social behavior, neurocognitive development, and digital environmental exposure in adolescents using a novel computational framework. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous patterns of social media engagement influence emergent mental health outcomes through bidirectional interactions with neurobiological maturation—a question requiring integration of behavioral, psychological, and neuroimaging data at scales that challenge conventional analytical methods. We propose developing a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) coupled with machine learning pipelines to simulate longitudinal biobehavioral systems across 10,000+ synthetic adolescent agents. The ABM will incorporate neurodevelopmental trajectories derived from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) datasets, real-world social network topologies, and temporally resolved digital interaction logs to capture multilevel feedback loops between prefrontal cortex maturation, peer influence dynamics, and platform-specific engagement behaviors. Computational challenges include optimizing parallelized parameter sweeps across neurocognitive growth variables, scaling graph neural networks to process time-varying social connectivity data, and implementing Bayesian inference for personalized risk stratification. The HPC resources will enable simulations at population-representative scales, reducing sampling bias inherent in single-cohort studies. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical neurodevelopmental windows where digital exposure disproportionately impacts emotional regulation pathways, (2) predictive biomarkers linking platform-specific interaction patterns to latent anxiety/depression risk, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for simulating digitally mediated biobehavioral systems. This work bridges gaps between computational social science, developmental neuroscience, and digital epidemiology, offering a paradigm to study emerging technology’s role in shaping adolescent mental health through an interdisciplinary lens. Results will inform targeted intervention strategies and ethical AI design principles for youth-facing platforms.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on the social sciences, psychology, and biomedical sciences to study complex problems of human individual and social growth and behavior.

abstract: Polymer chemistry faces significant challenges in predicting and controlling the dynamic behavior of synthesized macromolecules under varying environmental and operational conditions. A critical unsolved problem lies in understanding how polymerization pathways, molecular architecture, and intermolecular interactions collectively influence the stability, reactivity, and phase transitions of functional polymers. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model polymerization kinetics, polymer-solvent dynamics, and degradation mechanisms at atomistic and mesoscopic scales. The proposed work will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with reactive force fields to track bond formation/cleavage during polymerization, hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) methods to study electronic interactions in catalytic polymer systems, and coarse-grained models to probe long-timescale phase behavior. These simulations will be validated against experimental data from collaborators on polymer rheology and spectroscopic characterization. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallelization to manage systems containing >100,000 atoms over microsecond trajectories, as well as advanced sampling techniques to access rare transition states in degradation pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for designing polymers with tailored thermal stability and solvent resistance, (2) mechanistic insights into how branching density and copolymer sequences affect ion transport in electrolyte applications, and (3) identification of kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable polymer upcycling processes. By bridging molecular-scale interactions to bulk material properties, this research will directly inform the synthesis of next-generation polymers for energy storage and environmentally degradable materials. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in system size and sampling fidelity, enabling unprecedented resolution of transient intermediates and interfacial phenomena critical to industrial polymer applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: Understanding the dynamics of contaminant transport in heterogeneous aquifers is critical for safeguarding groundwater resources, yet existing models struggle to resolve fine-scale geological variability and transient hydrologic processes. This project seeks to advance predictive capabilities for contaminant migration—particularly arsenic and nitrate species—in complex aquifer systems by integrating high-resolution 3D hydrogeological modeling with reactive transport simulations. The research will employ parallelized finite-element models (e.g., MODFLOW coupled with PHT3D) to simulate coupled groundwater flow, solute advection-dispersion, and geochemical interactions across scales. Stochastic methods will quantify uncertainty in hydraulic conductivity fields and redox zonation, informed by geophysical and borehole data from two case study aquifers in arsenic-affected regions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve meter-scale heterogeneity across domains exceeding 100 km², execute ensemble simulations for parameter sensitivity analysis, and optimize machine learning surrogates to accelerate Monte Carlo-based risk assessments. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for coupling stochastic hydrostratigraphic models with reactive transport codes, (2) improved quantification of timescales for contaminant mobility under pumping-induced hydraulic gradient shifts, and (3) probabilistic risk maps identifying vulnerable zones in target aquifers. The computational workflows will be containerized for community reuse via HydroShare. By advancing the integration of HPC-driven stochastic modeling with geochemical realism, this work will directly inform managed aquifer recharge strategies and wellfield management policies, addressing a critical need for predictive tools in regions where groundwater contamination threatens drinking water security. The project aligns with national priorities on water resource resilience while demonstrating how compute-intensive hydrologic models can transition into operational decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the occurrence, circulation, distribution, chemical and physical properties, and environmental interaction of surface and subsurface waters, including groundwater. Includes instruction in geophysics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, chemical physics, geomorphology, mathematical modeling, hydrologic analysis, continental water processes, global water balance, and environmental science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in student counseling interventions by analyzing complex, multi-modal datasets to identify patterns in student mental health outcomes. Student counseling services face growing demand due to escalating mental health challenges among diverse student populations, yet evidence-based frameworks for personalizing interventions remain underdeveloped. Traditional statistical methods struggle to integrate heterogeneous data sources—such as anonymized session transcripts, longitudinal well-being surveys, and behavioral engagement metrics—while preserving privacy and scalability.
