This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and graph neural networks (GNNs) to model dynamic interactions between counseling strategies, student characteristics, and institutional support systems. Computational workflows will be optimized to process sensitive text data securely, extract latent psychosocial features, and simulate intervention pathways across hypothetical student cohorts. By parallelizing model training on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to overcome memory and processing bottlenecks associated with high-dimensional datasets spanning multiple universities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating counseling intervention efficacy under varying demographic and resource constraints, as well as actionable insights into how institutional policies and counselor training programs can adapt to systemic stressors. This work bridges gaps in education research by providing computational methods to study counseling processes at scale, with potential applications in developing adaptive support systems that reduce disparities in student mental health outcomes. Results will be disseminated through counseling education networks to inform data-driven practices in student personnel services.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the operational reliability and tactical effectiveness of next-generation aircraft armament systems through advanced predictive modeling and real-time simulation. Modern military platforms integrate complex, interdependent subsystems—such as targeting sensors, munitions deployment mechanisms, and countermeasure interfaces—that require precise coordination under dynamic environmental and combat conditions. Current maintenance protocols and failure prediction models lack the granularity to address emergent vulnerabilities arising from hardware-software interactions, material fatigue in extreme climates, and electromagnetic interference patterns. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute multi-physics simulations combining computational fluid dynamics, structural stress analysis, and machine learning-driven anomaly detection. These simulations will synthesize terabyte-scale datasets from operational flight recorders, component wear analytics, and synthetic threat scenarios to model system degradation pathways and failure thresholds. A parallelized Monte Carlo approach will assess probabilistic outcomes across diverse mission profiles, while neural networks trained on historical maintenance logs will identify latent risk factors in subsystem interoperability. The resulting framework aims to reduce unplanned maintenance downtime by 25–40% and improve threat response accuracy through adaptive decision-support algorithms. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing of novel armament configurations, this work will directly inform lifecycle management protocols and enhance the operational readiness of legacy and next-generation platforms. The computational outputs will be validated against live-fire exercise data and integrated into a classified predictive maintenance toolkit for joint service use, addressing a critical capability gap in sustainment logistics for modern aerial warfare systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of aircraft weapons systems and associated peripherals. Includes instruction in basic science and quantitative methods, computer science, electronics, engineering graphics, fluid power, heavy equipment operation, armament systems, weapon materials and processes, weapon safety, corrosion control, aircraft systems maintenance, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dynamic resource allocation in decentralized economic systems, integrating advances in algorithmic game theory, econometrics, and high-performance computing. The research addresses the challenge of modeling large-scale, adaptive markets where heterogeneous agents with bounded rationality interact under evolving constraints, such as energy markets with real-time renewable generation shifts or decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms. Existing equilibrium-based models often fail to capture the temporal and spatial complexity of such systems, particularly when accounting for strategic behavior, network effects, and incomplete information. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling approach combining evolutionary optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive agent strategies, and econometric validation against historical market data. The computational architecture will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across multiple market scenarios, implemented using MPI for distributed memory systems, with graph neural networks to model inter-agent influence patterns. Key innovations include a novel mechanism for endogenous preference formation using attention-based architectures and a scalable auction protocol optimizer tested through evolutionary algorithms. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of interacting agents across extended time horizons, with anticipated workloads exceeding 50,000 core-hours for parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available toolkit for simulating decentralized resource allocation systems, 2) empirical insights into the computational tractability of incentive-compatible mechanisms in large networks, and 3) policy-relevant findings on market design under high volatility. Results will advance both economic theory by quantifying previously intractable forms of strategic interdependence and computer science through developments in scalable mechanism design, with applications to sustainable infrastructure planning and digital market regulation.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the theoretical and practical connections between computer science and economics. Includes instruction in data analysis, database design, data mining, computer algorithms, economics, econometrics, computer programing, mathematics, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multilingual textual and visual datasets central to the study of cultural identity formation in East Asian diasporic communities. Focusing on 20th-century Chinese, Korean, and Japanese migrant populations, the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how transnational communities preserved and transformed cultural narratives through media production, including newspapers, vernacular photography, and ephemeral publications. Traditional methods struggle to process the volume and linguistic diversity of these materials, which span multiple dialects, orthographic systems (e.g., Hanja, simplified/traditional Chinese), and hybrid visual-textual formats. The computational approach combines transformer-based language models fine-tuned for historical East Asian languages with computer vision techniques to trace thematic continuities and adaptations across diasporic archives. Key tasks include cross-lingual semantic alignment of texts, style transfer analysis in visual materials, and network mapping of cultural references within and between migrant hubs such as San Francisco, Singapore, and Lima. The workflow requires parallelized processing of over 500,000 digitized pages and 200,000 images, with iterative model training to address low-resource language challenges and script variation. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable pipeline for analyzing culturally embedded visual-textual relationships in non-Western contexts, 2) quantitative evidence of how diasporic groups negotiated cultural preservation amid assimilation pressures, and 3) open-access multilingual embeddings optimized for historical East Asian materials. By enabling systematic comparison of cultural production patterns across dispersed communities, this work will provide new methodological frameworks for digital humanities in area studies while advancing scholarly debates about transnational identity in modern East Asia. The scale of data processing and model training, particularly for GPU-intensive multimodal tasks, necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve project timelines.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of East Asia, defined as including China, Korea, Japan, Mongolia, Taiwan, Tibet, related borderlands and island groups, and including the study of the East Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: The increasing complexity of interior design challenges—such as optimizing spatial functionality, material sustainability, and human-centered experiential quality—demands advanced computational tools to bridge creativity and technical precision. This project seeks to develop a scalable, AI-driven framework for simulating and evaluating dynamic interior environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address limitations in traditional design workflows. Current methods for modeling lighting, acoustics, and ergonomic flow rely on simplified approximations or compartmentalized analyses, which fail to capture the interdependent variables inherent in real-world spaces. By integrating parametric design algorithms, finite element analysis (FEA), and generative adversarial networks (GANs), this research will enable real-time, multi-physics simulations of interior spaces under diverse operational scenarios (e.g., fluctuating occupancy, adaptive lighting, or material wear). The computational pipeline will process high-resolution 3D scans, environmental sensor data, and user behavior datasets to iteratively refine design solutions that balance aesthetic intent, structural efficiency, and occupant well-being. Key objectives include automating compliance checks against building codes, predicting long-term material performance under stress, and generating data-driven alternatives for sustainable furnishings. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing GPU-accelerated rendering, training deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, and running parallelized optimization loops for complex spatial configurations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for interior designers, validated through case studies in healthcare and educational facilities. This work will advance the field by establishing a methodological bridge between visual creativity and quantitative analysis, fostering evidence-based design practices while reducing reliance on physical prototyping. By addressing scalability challenges in simulating heterogeneous design variables, the project aims to set new benchmarks for computational efficiency and ecological responsibility in the built environment.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling in the field of professional hair design, addressing gaps in the quantitative understanding of hair fiber dynamics under chemical and mechanical stress. Current training and product development in cosmetology rely heavily on empirical observation and trial-and-error methodologies, limiting the precision and scalability of innovations in hair treatments (e.g., coloring, perming) and styling tool design. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of keratin-protein interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) of hair strand biomechanics, and machine learning (ML) models trained on experimental datasets. The MD component will simulate the structural effects of chemical agents (e.g., oxidative dyes, relaxers) at the molecular level, while FEA will model macro-scale stresses imposed by heat styling tools under varying humidity and temperature conditions. ML algorithms will correlate simulation outputs with empirical data from tensile strength tests and microscopic imaging of treated hair samples. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high computational load of multi-scale simulations and optimizing ML hyperparameters across thousands of iterations. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for hair damage risk, optimized chemical formulation guidelines, and data-driven insights into tool design parameters (e.g., heat distribution profiles). Results will be disseminated through cosmetology training platforms and collaborations with product manufacturers, bridging computational science and applied aesthetic practices. This work establishes a novel framework for evidence-based innovation in hair design, reducing reliance on resource-intensive physical testing while enhancing safety and efficacy standards in the profession.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shampoo, cut, style, set, and dress the scalp hair of women and/or men, braid hair, apply hair cosmetics and wigs, and prepare for licensure as professional cosmetologists, hairdressers, and barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in hair design theory and concepts, hair cleaning and shampooing, hair coloring, chemical applications and permanent reconstructions, hair anatomy and physiology, scalp diseases and treatments, wig and hairpiece fitting, hair braiding, customer service, shop management, equipment operation, health and safety, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address unresolved questions in computational complexity theory regarding the practical limits of solving NP-hard optimization problems under resource constraints. While theoretical frameworks classify these problems as intractable in the worst case, real-world instances often exhibit structures that permit efficient approximation or heuristic solutions. However, characterizing the boundaries of tractability for such instances remains an open challenge. We propose a computational study to systematically explore the relationship between problem structure, algorithmic strategies, and runtime performance across a spectrum of NP-hard problems, including graph coloring, traveling salesman, and satisfiability. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale simulations of classical and quantum-inspired algorithms, such as simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, and hybrid quantum-classical solvers. These simulations will analyze runtime distributions, solution quality, and scalability across problem sizes up to 10^6 variables, generating empirical data to refine complexity-theoretic models. Computational workloads will parallelize parameter sweeps over algorithm configurations and problem ensembles using MPI-based task farming, with individual trials requiring up to 48 hours on multi-core nodes. Memory-intensive phases, such as constraint matrix operations for mixed-integer programming, will utilize distributed-memory architectures. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of structural features correlating with practical tractability, (2) optimized heuristic portfolios for common NP-hard problem classes, and (3) statistical evidence informing refinements to the polynomial hierarchy. Results will be disseminated through computational complexity venues and open-source algorithm libraries, bridging theoretical insights with practical optimization tools for scientific and industrial applications. This work directly advances the program’s mission by elucidating the nature of computation through rigorous empirical analysis at scales previously inaccessible to purely theoretical methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computability theory, complexity theory, and the nature of computation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing pedagogical strategies for social science teacher candidates by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the longitudinal impacts of training interventions on instructional efficacy. Social science education requires teachers to navigate complex, interdisciplinary content and diverse classroom dynamics, yet existing teacher education programs often lack data-driven frameworks to predict how specific training methods translate to real-world teaching outcomes. The proposed research will develop computational models to simulate how variations in curricular emphasis, practicum experiences, and mentorship structures affect teacher candidates’ ability to design inclusive, inquiry-based social science lessons. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques, we will analyze multi-year datasets from 15 partner teacher preparation programs, incorporating variables such as candidate demographics, mentor feedback, and K-12 student performance metrics. HPC resources are critical for processing these heterogeneous datasets (totaling ~50 TB) and running parallelized simulations that test thousands of training scenarios under differing socioeconomic and institutional constraints. Expected outcomes include identifying key leverage points in social science teacher development pathways and generating predictive tools to personalize training modules based on candidate strengths and contextual needs. By elucidating the nonlinear relationships between training inputs and teaching competencies, this work aims to advance evidence-based reforms in teacher education, ultimately improving secondary students’ civic engagement and critical analysis of societal systems. The computational framework will be made accessible to education researchers, enabling scalable replication studies across disciplinary domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific social science subjects and programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biophysical mechanisms underlying energy-based therapies, specifically the effects of biofield modulation (e.g., Qi Gong, Therapeutic Touch) on cellular redox homeostasis and mitochondrial function. While such therapies are increasingly integrated into holistic health practices, their molecular and systemic effects remain poorly characterized, hindered by the complexity of modeling low-energy bioelectromagnetic interactions and nonlinear cellular responses. The research problem centers on developing a multiscale computational framework to simulate how externally applied biofields interact with endogenous bioelectric networks, influencing reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling and metabolic regulation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the dual challenges of scale: quantum mechanical modeling of putative electromagnetic field interactions with ion channels (timescales <1 ns) and systems biology simulations of ROS-mediated signaling cascades across tissues (timescales >1 hr). The computational approach integrates 1) molecular dynamics simulations using polarized force fields to assess field-induced conformational changes in voltage-gated channels, 2) finite element modeling of endogenous bioelectric gradients perturbed by external fields, and 3) stochastic reaction-diffusion models of ROS propagation and antioxidant responses. Machine learning will be employed to parameterize models using sparse experimental data from coupled in vitro electrophysiology and metabolomics studies. Expected outcomes include the first predictive map of biofield intensity/duration thresholds that transition ROS signaling from physiological to pathological regimes, identification of critical intervention windows for metabolic synchronization, and optimization of treatment parameters for specific mitochondrial dysfunction phenotypes. This work will establish a computational foundation for evidence-based protocol design in energy therapies, bridging biophysical theory with clinical applications in managing chronic inflammatory and metabolic disorders. By resolving mechanistic uncertainties, the project aims to catalyze interdisciplinary collaboration between systems biology, quantum biophysics, and integrative medicine communities.
cip_title: Energy and Biologically Based Therapies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative, complementary, and somatic health and therapeutic services not elsewhere classified (bioenergetics, cranio-sacral therapy, Therapeutic Touch, Qi Gong, and others).

abstract: Integrative medicine emphasizes holistic, evidence-based care that addresses the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing health. A critical challenge in advancing this field lies in analyzing multidimensional datasets—such as electronic health records (EHRs), genomic profiles, lifestyle logs, and patient-reported outcomes—to identify personalized treatment pathways while preserving the centrality of the practitioner-patient relationship. Current computational methods struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data types at scale, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between interventions, patient biology, and environmental contexts. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive frameworks for optimizing integrative treatment strategies. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining mechanistic modeling of physiological networks with machine learning-driven analysis of clinical and multi-omics data. Agent-based models will simulate patient-specific responses to combined conventional and complementary therapies, while natural language processing tools will extract qualitative insights from practitioner notes and patient narratives. Graph neural networks will map relationships between treatment components, biomarkers, and long-term health outcomes across diverse demographic groups. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of large-scale EHR datasets (from 50,000+ patients), real-time optimization of treatment combinations, and sensitivity analyses across hypothetical clinical scenarios. By enabling the integration of sparse, high-dimensional data sources, this approach aims to identify reproducible patterns in treatment efficacy, predict adverse event risks for complex intervention bundles, and uncover novel biomarkers of therapeutic synergy. Successful implementation will produce an open-source framework for designing personalized integrative care plans, validated through retrospective analysis of existing clinical cohorts and pilot prospective trials. This work directly supports the development of evidence-based protocols that balance systemic healing with precision medicine principles, ultimately strengthening the scientific foundation for whole-person care in clinical practice.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine in a way that reaffirms the importance of the relationship between practitioner and patient; focuses on the whole person; is informed by evidence; and makes use of all appropriate therapeutic approaches, healthcare professionals, and disciplines to achieve optimal health and healing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of community resilience and spiritual engagement in underserved urban environments. While urban ministry has historically relied on qualitative and ethnographic methods, this study pioneers a computational approach to model how socio-spiritual interventions influence community networks over time. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate the longitudinal impact of ministry programs—such as neighborhood outreach, crisis counseling, and interfaith collaboration—on social cohesion and collective agency in rapidly gentrifying urban areas. Using anonymized demographic data, geospatial records, and anonymized textual archives from partner organizations, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between residents, religious institutions, and municipal systems. Machine learning techniques, including natural language processing (NLP), will be applied to historical sermon texts, community meeting transcripts, and social media artifacts to identify patterns in how theological narratives adapt to shifting urban stressors. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale ABM iterations and training transformer-based models on heterogeneous datasets, enabling the team to test hypotheses about intervention scalability and cultural contextualization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for ministry leaders to visualize potential ripple effects of programmatic decisions and a peer-reviewed framework for quantifying spiritual capital in urban policy contexts. By integrating computational social science with theological ethics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based urban ministry while contributing interdisciplinary methods to the digital humanities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: Surgical site infections (SSIs) remain a critical concern in postoperative care, with breaches in sterile technique contributing to preventable complications. Current protocols for maintaining aseptic environments in operating rooms (ORs) rely on static guidelines that may not adequately address the dynamic, multifactorial risks posed by human activity, equipment interactions, and robotic surgical systems. This project proposes a computational approach to model contamination risks and optimize real-time sterile field management. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based simulations of OR workflows to quantify microbial transmission pathways influenced by personnel movement, airflow, and instrument handling. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective SSI incidence data, surgical robot telemetry, and environmental sensor logs to predict contamination events and identify protocol vulnerabilities. Additionally, finite element analysis will assess the efficacy of sterilization techniques for robotic end-effectors and reusable instruments under varying clinical conditions. The computational framework will enable scenario testing of interventions, such as adjusted scrubbing protocols or redesigned equipment workflows, to minimize microbial load. Expected outcomes include dynamic, data-driven guidelines for sterile field maintenance, predictive tools for SSI risk stratification, and virtual training modules for surgical technologists. By integrating HPC-driven insights into surgical practice, this research aims to reduce infection rates, lower healthcare costs, and enhance patient safety. The project aligns with the Surgical Technology program’s emphasis on innovation in aseptic technique, providing a scalable computational foundation for advancing evidence-based practice and education in sterile processing and robotic surgery support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and surgical nurses, to maintain, monitor, and enforce the sterile field and adherence to aseptic technique by preoperative, surgical team, and postoperative personnel. Includes instruction in instrument and equipment sterilization and handling, surgical supplies management, wound exposure and closure, surgical computer and robot operation and monitoring, maintenance of hemostasis, and patient and team scrubbing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven predictive framework to optimize personalized care plans for homebound individuals by integrating multimodal data from wearable sensors, environmental monitors, and caregiver observations. The central challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, high-frequency data streams (including motion patterns, vital sign fluctuations, and home environment variables) to detect subtle precursors of adverse health events such as falls, medication errors, or acute episodes in chronically ill patients. Current clinical decision support systems lack the temporal resolution and contextual awareness required for dynamic home care environments, where limited supervision and diverse living conditions create unique risks. We propose a hybrid computational architecture combining graph neural networks to model patient-environment interactions, transformer-based time series analysis for longitudinal biomarker tracking, and physics-informed reinforcement learning to simulate intervention outcomes. The framework will be trained on a novel dataset aggregating anonymized sensor data from 450 home care recipients, augmented with synthetic cohorts representing understudied populations. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: 1) Parallel processing of terabyte-scale sensor datasets with subsecond temporal alignment, 2) Multi-agent simulations of caregiver-client-environment dynamics across 10^5 potential scenario permutations, and 3) Federated learning protocols preserving privacy across distributed care provider networks. Anticipated outcomes include a real-time risk stratification system that alerts home health aides to emerging threats with quantified uncertainty estimates, plus adaptive recommendation engines for tailored intervention timing. This computational infrastructure could reduce preventable hospitalizations by 18-22% in pilot populations while establishing methodological foundations for AI-assisted home care—a critical need as aging populations drive demand for scalable, precision-focused support systems outside institutional settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of doctrinal evolution across Buddhist philosophical traditions, with a focus on Madhyamaka, Yogacara, and Zen textual corpora. While Buddhist studies has historically relied on close textual and philological methods, the scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources—spanning multilingual manuscripts, commentaries, and ritual texts—present challenges for systematic comparative analysis. This research aims to address these limitations by developing computational workflows to identify patterns in philosophical argumentation, trace conceptual shifts across historical periods, and map cross-cultural transmission routes. Key objectives include training multilingual natural language processing (NLP) models on digitized Buddhist texts in Classical Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit; implementing semantic network analysis to compare doctrinal frameworks; and simulating textual transmission pathways through agent-based modeling. The proposed computational architecture will integrate optical character recognition for non-Latin scripts, transformer-based language models fine-tuned on Buddhist philosophical terminology, and graph databases to represent intertextual relationships. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable pipeline for analyzing understudied commentarial traditions, 2) quantitative evidence for doctrinal hybridization processes in East Asian Buddhism, and 3) open-access tools for computational religious studies. By combining HPC capabilities with domain-specific hermeneutics, this project will enable novel investigations into how Buddhist philosophical concepts were reinterpreted across cultural contexts while establishing methodological frameworks for large-scale comparative analysis in religious studies. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, parallel processing of multi-terabyte text corpora, and storage of high-resolution manuscript images, addressing critical bottlenecks in processing premodern religious texts at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy preached by Siddartha Gautama, the Buddha, in ancient India and subsequently interpreted by his disciples and apostles; together with the intellectual, cultural, social, and ritual developments of the faith and its branches. Includes instruction in Buddhist sacred literature (Tripitaka, etc.) and study of one or more of the main branches including Early Buddhism, Hinayana, Theravada, Madhyamaka, Yogacara, Pure Land, Shingon, Tendai, Nichiren Shu, Zen, Tibetan, Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational modeling of aberrant neurovascular coupling mechanisms in early-stage neurodegenerative disorders, a poorly understood phenomenon intersecting neurology, vascular biology, and systems physiology. Current clinical paradigms lack tools to analyze the dynamic, multiscale interactions between cerebral blood flow modulation and neuronal metabolic demand—a process increasingly implicated in preclinical Alzheimer’s pathology and cerebral small vessel disease. The research problem centers on developing a novel computational framework integrating hemodynamic simulations with neural activity patterns derived from multimodal imaging (fMRI, ASL) and invasive electrophysiological recordings in animal models. The computational approach employs finite element modeling to simulate vascular responses across cortical microdomains, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on high-resolution spatiotemporal datasets to identify predictive signatures of neurovascular decoupling. Key challenges include managing petabyte-scale imaging archives, optimizing parallel processing for biologically constrained neural network models, and resolving time-dependent fluid-structure interactions in anatomically accurate vascular geometries. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source simulation platform for neurovascular coupling analysis, (2) validated biomarkers of early perfusion-metabolism mismatch, and (3) mechanistic insights into how vascular dysregulation precedes macroscopic neurodegeneration. This work bridges a critical gap between cellular neuroscience and clinical neurology by establishing computational methods to study neurovascular physiology at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. Successful implementation could inform targeted therapeutic strategies for preserving cerebrovascular function in prodromal neurodegenerative states, addressing a pressing need in translational medical research that falls outside conventional clinical trial frameworks. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the iterative, multiscale simulations and large-scale data integration required to advance this emerging interdisciplinary niche.
cip_title: Medical Clinical Sciences/ Graduate Medical Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in medical clinical sciences or graduate medical studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance diagnostic accuracy and operational efficiency in medical sonography through the development of advanced computational tools for real-time ultrasound image analysis and pattern recognition. A critical challenge in sonography is the variability in image interpretation, particularly in complex cases involving atypical anatomies or early-stage pathologies, which can lead to diagnostic delays or errors. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of processing high-resolution ultrasound datasets with low latency. The computational workflow will involve three phases: 1) preprocessing raw ultrasound data to reduce noise and standardize image quality across devices, 2) training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers on a multi-institutional dataset of annotated sonographic images spanning diverse clinical scenarios (e.g., cardiovascular, obstetric, and abdominal applications), and 3) validating model performance through retrospective clinical case simulations. The HPC environment is essential for managing the scale of data (estimated at 250 TB of DICOM files) and enabling rapid hyperparameter optimization across distributed GPU nodes. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive sonographic analysis, optimized to assist clinicians in identifying subtle biomarkers of disease while maintaining compliance with patient privacy regulations. Successful implementation could reduce image interpretation time by 30–50% in preliminary trials and provide sonography students with AI-augmented training modules to improve diagnostic competency. This work aligns with the program’s mission to integrate emerging technologies into sonographic practice while upholding rigorous ethical standards for patient-centered care.
cip_title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography/ Sonographer and Ultrasound Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to utilize medical ultrasound techniques to gather sonographic data used to diagnose a variety of conditions and diseases. Includes instruction in obtaining, reviewing, and integrating patient histories and data; patient instruction and care; anatomic, physiologic and pathologic data recording; sonographic data processing; sonography equipment operation; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern agricultural machinery, particularly in hydraulic, electrical, and combustion systems, demands advanced computational tools to optimize performance and reduce operational failures. Current maintenance protocols for equipment such as crop-spraying systems, tractors, and automated harvesters rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches, which often lead to inefficient resource use, unexpected downtime, and environmental risks from leaks or over-application of inputs. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing predictive maintenance frameworks through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations and machine learning. We propose to model multi-physics interactions within hydraulic and combustion systems under diverse operational conditions, integrating sensor data from field equipment to train neural networks for anomaly detection. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will analyze fluid behavior in irrigation pumps and sprayer nozzles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess mechanical stress in tillage and harvesting components. These simulations will be coupled with real-world telemetry data to identify failure precursors, such as pressure fluctuations or thermal imbalances, and predict component degradation timelines. The HPC resources will enable parallel processing of large datasets from IoT-enabled machinery and accelerate iterative design optimization for critical subsystems. Expected outcomes include validated predictive maintenance algorithms deployable on edge computing platforms, reduced machinery downtime by 20–30%, and design recommendations for next-generation agricultural equipment with improved energy efficiency. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to agricultural mechanization, this research will directly support the sustainability of farm operations, lower maintenance costs, and minimize environmental impacts from equipment inefficiencies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural Mechanics and Equipment/ Machine Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to maintain and repair specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment and vehicles. Includes instruction in the principles of diesel, combustion, electrical, steam, hydraulic, and mechanical systems and their application to the maintenance of terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos; irrigation and pumping equipment; dairy, feeding, and shearing operations; and processing systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic decision-making in complex supply chain networks under uncertainty, a critical problem in business administration and management. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the interdependencies, real-time disruptions, and behavioral factors inherent in global supply chains, limiting their practical utility. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning to evaluate adaptive inventory and logistics strategies. The computational model will simulate multi-echelon supply networks with 10,000+ node configurations, incorporating stochastic demand shocks, supplier reliability data, and transportation bottlenecks. By parallelizing scenario analyses across HPC clusters, we aim to assess resilience strategies—such as flexible sourcing protocols and buffer stock policies—at unprecedented granularity while reducing simulation runtime from weeks to hours. Initial pilot studies on regional pharmaceutical supply chains demonstrate the method’s ability to quantify trade-offs between cost efficiency and disruption risks. Scaling this work requires dedicated HPC resources to manage memory-intensive optimization tasks and generative AI components that predict emergent bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool for supply chain managers, validated through partnerships with three multinational firms, and new insights into balancing lean operations with robustness. This project will advance computational methods in operations management while providing actionable frameworks to mitigate systemic risks in critical industries. The requested computing infrastructure is essential to handle petabyte-scale logistics datasets and deliver real-time prescriptive analytics at enterprise-relevant resolution.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: The optimization of chemical manufacturing processes is hindered by the complex interplay of reaction kinetics, transport phenomena, and thermodynamic equilibria, which are computationally prohibitive to model at industrial scales using conventional methods. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale simulations of catalytic reactor systems and separation processes central to petroleum refining and pharmaceutical production. The research will integrate quantum chemical calculations for catalyst surface interactions, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for reactor-scale hydrodynamics, and machine learning algorithms to predict process bottlenecks and optimize operating conditions. A key focus is modeling transient behaviors in fluidized bed reactors and membrane-based separations, where traditional steady-state assumptions fail to capture dynamic inefficiencies. The computational workflow will utilize parallelized solvers in OpenFOAM and LAMMPS, coupled with custom Python-based optimization frameworks, to reduce simulation timescales from weeks to days while maintaining atomistic resolution in critical regions. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting catalyst deactivation pathways, optimizing energy consumption in distillation sequences, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions in methane reforming processes. By enabling high-fidelity virtual prototyping, this work will directly address scalability challenges in sustainable chemical manufacturing, particularly for carbon capture and hydrogen production systems. The requested HPC resources will support large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and the training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets spanning molecular dynamics trajectories and plant-scale sensor data. Successful implementation will provide open-access simulation tools for the chemical processing community, reduce reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches, and accelerate the translation of laboratory-scale innovations to industrial deployment. This project aligns with broader goals of enhancing process safety, minimizing environmental footprints, and training the next generation of computational researchers in science-driven industrial problem-solving.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of chemical processing equipment in industries such as chemical manufacturing, petroleum refining, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and waste water treatment. Includes instruction in mathematics, chemistry, and physics; computer applications; chemical and refinery plant operations, processes, and equipment; safety, health, and environment; instrumentation; troubleshooting; and applications to specific industries.

abstract: Landscape architecture faces growing challenges in addressing dynamic environmental systems under climate change, yet traditional design methods often rely on static, historical data or simplified models. This project seeks to develop a computational framework that integrates real-time environmental data, predictive ecological modeling, and human behavioral patterns to simulate landscape performance across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The research problem centers on the inability of conventional tools to account for the complex feedback loops between microclimatic conditions, vegetative adaptation, and public space utilization in rapidly urbanizing areas. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a coupled modeling system combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for wind and thermal analysis, agent-based modeling (ABM) for pedestrian movement simulations, and machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal ecological datasets. These components will be spatially synchronized through GPU-accelerated raster processing and validated against sensor data from three pilot sites undergoing climate-adaptive redesign. The computational approach addresses scalability challenges in rendering high-resolution 3D terrain models while maintaining real-time interactivity for scenario testing. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform that quantifies trade-offs between ecological resilience, thermal comfort, and social equity in landscape interventions. By enabling probabilistic forecasting of plant community succession under varying management strategies and climate scenarios, this work aims to advance evidence-based design protocols that transcend current horticultural databases and static zoning paradigms. The requested computing resources will specifically support the parallel processing of LiDAR-derived point clouds, calibration of neural networks for phenology prediction, and multi-objective optimization routines balancing carbon sequestration potential with recreational carrying capacity. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges gaps between landscape architecture, urban ecology, and computational social science while operating outside traditional STEM domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of landscape architecture and research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; soils, groundcovers, and horticultural elements; project and site planning; landscape design, history, and theory; environmental design; applicable law and regulations; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fitting of patient-specific orthotic and prosthetic devices using high-performance computing (HPC). Current clinical practices rely heavily on manual adjustments and static biomechanical models, which often fail to account for dynamic, individualized factors such as tissue compliance, gait variability, and real-time pressure distribution. These limitations contribute to suboptimal device performance, prolonged fitting processes, and increased risk of secondary musculoskeletal complications. To address this, we propose integrating multi-scale biomechanical simulations, machine learning (ML), and patient-specific sensor data to predict device-patient interactions under dynamic conditions. HPC resources will enable finite element analysis (FEA) modeling of tissue-device interfaces at unprecedented resolution, coupled with ML-driven optimization of device geometry and material properties. Sensor-derived gait and pressure data from wearable devices will inform boundary conditions for simulations, ensuring alignment with real-world biomechanical loads. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine designs by minimizing interfacial stresses, maximizing functional alignment, and incorporating patient-reported comfort metrics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for generating patient-optimized orthotic/prosthetic designs, reducing iterative fitting sessions by 30–50%, and improving long-term user mobility outcomes. This work bridges gaps in personalized assistive device design by merging clinical orthotics/prosthetics with computational engineering, advancing a niche area within health sciences that remains underserved by traditional analytical methods. The resulting open-source tools will empower clinicians to leverage computational insights during device customization, fostering translation of HPC-driven innovation into routine care. By addressing the intersection of biomechanics, materials science, and data science, this project establishes a paradigm for computational resource applications in specialized health technology domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of large-scale digital communication networks and their role in shaping contemporary public discourse, with a focus on polarization and misinformation diffusion. As digital platforms generate unprecedented volumes of multimodal data—including text, image, and network interaction patterns—traditional analytical tools struggle to capture the complexity of these systems. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to model how communication theories of agenda-setting, framing, and cultivation manifest in algorithmically mediated environments, particularly examining emergent patterns that diverge from legacy media contexts. The proposed methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques with dynamic network analysis to process terabyte-scale datasets from social media platforms, news archives, and collaborative fact-checking databases. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models to detect rhetorical strategies across linguistic and visual modalities, while parallelized graph algorithms will map temporal shifts in information cascades and community formation. Agent-based modeling will simulate how platform affordances interact with human communication behaviors under different theoretical assumptions. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel taxonomy of digital persuasion tactics grounded in communication theory, (2) quantifiable metrics for assessing the entrenchment of polarized belief systems through machine learning-derived latent variables, and (3) open-source tools enabling researchers to analyze cross-platform communication flows at scale. By bridging computational social science with critical media theory, this work aims to advance methodological paradigms for studying 21st-century communication ecosystems while providing empirically grounded insights into the systemic risks and democratic potentials of networked public spheres. The requested computing resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous media corpora, and real-time visualization of multidimensional communication networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on theories of communication. Includes instruction in theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for analyzing underdocumented Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, many of which lack digitized corpora or tools for large-scale linguistic analysis. The research focuses on three languages from the region—Tagalog (Philippines), Māori (Aotearoa/New Zealand), and Javanese (Indonesia)—to investigate syntactic and morphological patterns that challenge existing typological frameworks. A key problem is the limited scalability of traditional manual methods for parsing complex agglutinative structures and tracking dialectal variations across historical texts. To overcome this, the project proposes deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on newly assembled multilingual datasets, including transcribed oral narratives, pre-colonial epigraphic materials, and modern literary works. Computational workflows will integrate NLP pipelines for morpheme segmentation, dependency parsing, and semantic role labeling, optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters. Phonetic modeling of tonal shifts in Māori dialects will further leverage parallel processing to analyze terabyte-scale audio recordings. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational grammars for these languages, datasets annotated with cross-linguistic metadata standards, and a containerized toolset for low-resource language analysis. Results will advance theoretical understanding of argument marking systems in Austronesian languages while providing practical resources for endangered language revitalization initiatives. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the need for distributed training of deep learning architectures, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and comparative analyses across 50+ related languages—tasks infeasible on local computing resources. This work bridges computational linguistics and area studies, offering methodological innovations applicable to understudied languages globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Southeast Asian and Australasian/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Southeast Asian and Australasian/Pacific languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the complex interplay of biopsychosocial factors influencing symptom trajectories in patients receiving hospice and palliative care. Current clinical tools inadequately capture the dynamic, nonlinear relationships between physical symptoms (e.g., pain, dyspnea), psychological distress, social determinants, and therapeutic interventions, limiting personalized care planning. We propose an integrative approach using high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets spanning electronic health records, wearable sensor data, patient-reported outcomes, and caregiver narratives from 15,000+ historical cases. Agent-based modeling will simulate individual patient trajectories under varying care protocols, while natural language processing will extract latent psychosocial patterns from unstructured clinical notes and advance care planning documents. Graph neural networks will map temporal dependencies between symptoms, treatments, and quality-of-life metrics, with particular attention to rare but clinically critical events like terminal restlessness or rapid functional decline. Computational experiments will evaluate the impact of alternative care schedules, complementary therapy integrations, and ethical decision-making thresholds on predicted outcomes. The resulting models aim to identify high-risk transition points and optimize intervention timing for heterogeneous patient subgroups, validated through retrospective survival analysis and prospective pilot data from three hospice networks. By enabling real-time simulation of care pathway outcomes at scale, this work addresses a critical gap in precision palliative medicine, offering a decision-support tool to balance symptom control, patient autonomy, and resource allocation in end-of-life care. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets, training deep learning architectures with attention mechanisms, and running parallelized sensitivity analyses across diverse demographic and diagnostic cohorts.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to work with patients in hospice and palliative care and focuses on the physical, psychological, spiritual, and social needs of patients and families affected by advanced illness. Includes instruction in aging, thanatology, pharmacology, complementary and integrative therapies, pathophysiology, and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing decentralized resource networks for small businesses engaged in circular economy practices—a critical gap in entrepreneurial operations where dynamic resource flows, regulatory constraints, and sustainability goals intersect. Small enterprises often lack the computational tools to model complex, multi-stakeholder systems required for efficient material reuse, energy recovery, and waste valorization. Traditional linear optimization models fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies and real-time variability inherent in these networks, particularly when integrating IoT-generated supply chain data with ecological impact metrics. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a graph-based reinforcement learning framework to simulate and optimize decentralized resource exchanges across spatially distributed small businesses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training multi-agent models that account for heterogeneous business objectives, time-varying resource availability, and regulatory scenarios. The computational architecture will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing supplier geolocation, material composition analytics, and carbon accounting records. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system that enables small businesses to dynamically reconfigure resource partnerships while maximizing circularity metrics. This work advances computational entrepreneurship by introducing scalable methods for ethical AI in resource allocation, directly addressing the operational bottlenecks faced by sustainability-driven small enterprises. The project’s significance lies in its potential to democratize access to advanced predictive tools for circular economy adoption, fostering resilience in entrepreneurial ecosystems without requiring proprietary software investments. Results will be validated against case studies from urban manufacturing cooperatives and rural agro-industrial networks, establishing performance benchmarks for decentralized circularity optimization.
cip_title: Entrepreneurial and Small Business Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in enterprise management and entrepreneurship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern engineering and architectural projects demands advanced computational tools capable of handling high-fidelity simulations and large-scale design optimizations. Current drafting and design workflows often rely on simplified models due to limitations in processing power, which can lead to suboptimal material usage, structural inefficiencies, or delayed project timelines. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable real-time, multi-physics simulations and generative design processes within drafting and design applications. The research will focus on developing and validating computational workflows that integrate finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization. These methods will be applied to case studies in modular construction, aerospace component design, and sustainable urban planning, where iterative testing of high-resolution models is critical. Key computational tasks include parallelized meshing algorithms, distributed solving of partial differential equations, and GPU-accelerated rendering of 3D simulations. The project will utilize open-source frameworks such as CalculiX and OpenFOAM, augmented by custom Python scripts for automation and data analysis. Expected outcomes include scalable templates for cloud-based HPC workflows, benchmarks comparing traditional and HPC-enhanced design cycles, and open-access datasets demonstrating efficiency gains in material usage and energy performance. By reducing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to democratize access to advanced simulation tools for educational institutions and small firms, fostering innovation in drafting pedagogy and industry practices. The requested computing resources will support parametric studies involving 10,000+ design permutations per project phase, enabling statistically robust conclusions about the trade-offs between computational cost and design precision. Successful implementation will provide a foundation for future interdisciplinary research in smart manufacturing and digital twin technologies, aligning with broader goals of sustainability and resilience in engineered systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze ethical decision-making processes in complex, real-world professional environments, with a focus on identifying and mitigating systemic biases in organizational policies. Despite advances in ethical theory, practical applications often struggle to account for dynamic, multi-stakeholder scenarios where competing values and power imbalances complicate outcomes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model large-scale simulations of ethical dilemmas across healthcare, corporate governance, and environmental policy contexts. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be used to represent diverse actors (e.g., professionals, institutions, communities) and their interactions under varying ethical frameworks (utilitarian, deontological, care ethics). Machine learning techniques will then identify patterns in emergent ethical conflicts and evaluate the efficacy of intervention strategies. A key innovation is the integration of empirical datasets—such as historical case law, public health records, and corporate ethics reports—to ground simulations in observed behavior. The computational demands of this approach are significant: ABM scalability requires parallel processing to manage thousands of concurrent agents, while NLP-driven analysis of unstructured ethical case texts necessitates GPU-accelerated transformers. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated ethical scenarios with annotated decision trees, (2) quantitative metrics for assessing bias and fairness in organizational ethics protocols, and (3) predictive models to guide policy redesign in high-stakes domains like AI governance and crisis triage systems. By bridging normative ethics with data-driven systems analysis, this work aims to equip practitioners with tools to navigate increasingly granular ethical trade-offs in sociotechnical systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the required computational depth and real-world validation at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for integrating multi-modal biomedical data with dynamic 3D medical illustrations to enhance precision in oncological visualization and decision support. The research addresses a critical gap in current clinical informatics systems, which often lack the capacity to synthesize high-resolution imaging, genomic data, and real-time physiological metrics into interactive, spatially contextualized models. Traditional approaches to medical illustration and data interpretation remain siloed, limiting their utility in complex cases such as heterogeneous tumor microenvironments. To overcome this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs) and agent-based modeling to simulate cellular-scale interactions within patient-specific anatomical reconstructions. The computational workflow will process raw data from histopathology slides, single-cell RNA sequencing, and functional MRI scans, aligning these inputs with biomechanical constraints derived from finite element analysis. By deploying distributed GPU-accelerated training and multi-scale optimization algorithms on HPC clusters, the project aims to generate adaptive 3D visualizations that dynamically update in response to simulated treatment perturbations. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for collaborative annotation of hybrid data-illustration models, validated against retrospective glioblastoma datasets. The resource-intensive nature of iteratively rendering high-fidelity environments—requiring petabytes of memory bandwidth and parallelized tensor operations—necessitates access to advanced computing infrastructure. Success in this interdisciplinary effort could redefine standards for precision medicine workflows, offering clinicians an intuitive interface to explore spatiotemporal relationships between molecular heterogeneity, drug penetration, and structural deformation in solid tumors.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in medical illustration and informatics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Otolaryngologic disorders, such as head and neck cancers, chronic sinusitis, and hearing loss, involve complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and structural factors. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to integrate multimodal data—including high-resolution imaging, genomic sequencing, and patient-specific clinical records—at scales necessary to uncover actionable insights. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that elucidate disease mechanisms and optimize therapeutic strategies. Using machine learning algorithms, we will analyze multi-omics datasets from tumor biopsies to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response and metastasis in squamous cell carcinoma. Concurrently, computational fluid dynamics simulations will model sinonasal airflow in chronic rhinosinusitis patients, enabling personalized surgical planning to restore physiologic function. HPC infrastructure is critical to process terabytes of imaging data, perform real-time probabilistic network analyses on genomic interactions, and execute large-scale parameter sweeps in patient-specific anatomies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for oncology decision support, optimized surgical approaches for airway disorders, and open-source tools for integrating heterogeneous clinical data. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this research aims to accelerate translational discoveries in otolaryngology, bridging gaps between molecular insights and patient-centered care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in real-time court interpretation by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for improving the accuracy, latency, and contextual adaptability of machine-assisted legal interpretation. Court interpreters face unique demands, including rapid processing of specialized legal terminology, adherence to strict procedural norms, and management of complex linguistic phenomena (e.g., code-switching, regional dialects) under time-sensitive conditions. While human interpreters remain essential, existing translation technologies lack the domain-specific optimization required for courtroom environments. This project proposes a novel computational framework combining neural machine translation (NMT) with real-time acoustic and semantic analysis, trained on a curated multilingual corpus of legal proceedings, court documents, and interpreter training materials. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing for three core tasks: (1) training transformer-based models on legal discourse patterns and jurisdictional terminology variations; (2) simulating high-stress interpretation scenarios through generative adversarial networks (GANs) to stress-test system robustness; and (3) optimizing latency thresholds for simultaneous interpretation using distributed GPU-accelerated inference pipelines. The computational architecture will integrate speech recognition, domain-constrained translation, and prosody preservation modules, with validation against certified court interpreter benchmarks. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for interpreter training, prototype systems for real-time decision support, and quantitative models of interpretation quality under varying courtroom conditions. By bridging computational linguistics with legal procedural requirements, this work aims to establish new standards for human-AI collaboration in justice systems while addressing equity gaps in language access. The requested HPC allocation will specifically support distributed training of multi-modal models across 10+ languages and runtime optimization for sub-500ms latency thresholds at 95%+ BLEU scores on legal text.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to provide accurate translation and interpretation between two or more languages for parties involved in a legal proceeding. Includes instruction in courtroom standards and procedures, court interpreting, legal terminology, consecutive interpretation, simultaneous interpretation, and sight translation.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predictive modeling for nanoscale thermal transport in hybrid quantum-material systems, an emerging area at the intersection of nanoscale engineering, quantum physics, and computational science. Current models for heat dissipation in nanodevices rely on simplified bulk approximations or single-material frameworks, failing to capture the complex, non-equilibrium dynamics of hybrid systems such as 2D material heterostructures coupled to quantum dots or superconducting resonators. These limitations hinder the design of energy-efficient nanoelectronics and quantum technologies, where thermal management at interfaces governs performance and stability. To overcome this gap, we propose a multiscale computational approach integrating first-principles density functional theory (DFT), non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) methods, and machine learning-accelerated molecular dynamics (ML-MD) simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve atomic-scale phonon scattering, interfacial thermal resistance, and quantum confinement effects across heterogeneous material boundaries at experimentally relevant scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-optimized codes for DFT (VASP) and MD (LAMMPS), coupled with custom Python-based ML force fields trained on ab initio datasets to extend simulation timescales. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for predicting thermal transport in hybrid nanosystems, new insights into interfacial phonon engineering for heat mitigation in quantum devices, and design guidelines for next-generation thermal interfaces in superconducting qubit arrays. This work bridges a critical gap between quantum device engineering and nanoscale thermal sciences, with potential applications in cryogenic computing, photonic-integrated circuits, and energy-efficient nanoelectronics. The requested resources will enable simulations spanning 10^4–10^6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, exceeding the capabilities of current local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, growth, properties, and fundamental interactions of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across scientific disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize traditional and modern woodworking processes by analyzing the mechanical behavior of wood under diverse environmental and operational conditions. Despite wood’s widespread use, its anisotropic nature, moisture sensitivity, and variable grain structures pose challenges in predicting performance during cutting, carving, or assembly. Current trial-and-error approaches in toolpath planning, joinery design, and material selection lead to inefficiencies, material waste, and suboptimal product durability. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and 3D digital twin simulations. The FEA models will simulate stress distribution, vibration, and deformation during machining operations across species-specific wood datasets. ML algorithms will correlate historical craft data with simulation outputs to predict optimal tool geometries, feed rates, and clamping configurations. Concurrently, digital twins of workshop environments will test virtual prototypes under dynamic humidity and temperature conditions to evaluate long-term structural integrity. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized workflows to manage multi-scale simulations (microscopic grain interactions to macroscopic assembly dynamics) and large datasets spanning material science, traditional craft knowledge, and sensor-derived machining metrics. The HPC resources will accelerate model training, enable parametric studies of 500+ wood-tool combinations, and support real-time rendering of digital twins. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational toolkit for woodworkers, predictive models to reduce material waste by 20-30% in craft production, and a framework for digitizing traditional woodworking expertise. This interdisciplinary effort bridges computational engineering and artisanal practice, offering scalable solutions to enhance precision in custom woodcraft while preserving manual techniques through data-driven refinements. Results will be disseminated via workshops for vocational training programs and partnerships with heritage craft preservation initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out and shape stock; assemble wooden articles or subassemblies; mark, bind, saw, carve, and sand wooden products; repair wooden articles, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: Soil systems are dynamic interfaces where complex chemical and microbiological interactions govern nutrient cycling, organic matter decomposition, and carbon sequestration. Current models often treat soil chemistry and microbial community dynamics in isolation, limiting predictive accuracy for soil health under changing agricultural practices and climate conditions. This project seeks to address this gap by developing an integrated, multiscale computational framework to simulate coupled biogeochemical and microbial processes in soil ecosystems.
