High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of soil environments, parameterize reaction networks involving organic-inorganic colloids and microbial metabolisms, and quantify feedbacks between soil microbiota and plant-root exudates. We propose a hybrid modeling approach combining molecular dynamics simulations of mineral-organic interactions, agent-based microbial community models, and reactive transport algorithms to capture processes from nanometer to field scales. Machine learning will augment these simulations by assimilating experimental data from soil metagenomics, spectroscopy, and gas flux measurements. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration to manage the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and stochastic microbial behaviors. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking soil microbiome composition to carbon stabilization efficiency, nitrogen leaching rates, and phosphorus bioavailability under varying management practices. These tools will advance precision soil management strategies to optimize crop productivity while minimizing fertilizer inputs and greenhouse gas emissions. The resulting open-source software will provide a scalable platform for interdisciplinary soil research, bridging molecular-scale mechanisms to ecosystem-scale outcomes. By elucidating synergies between soil chemistry and microbiology, this work aims to inform sustainable agricultural systems resilient to environmental stressors.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for identifying early risk factors associated with student behavioral challenges in K–12 educational settings. School psychologists face growing demands to design proactive, data-informed interventions, yet existing tools for analyzing complex, multidimensional student data—including academic performance, socio-emotional assessments, and demographic variables—lack the computational power to model nonlinear interactions or longitudinal patterns at scale. The research problem centers on overcoming limitations in traditional statistical methods, which struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets (e.g., behavioral observation logs, school climate surveys, and individualized education program records) while accounting for contextual factors such as classroom dynamics and community resources. To address this, the project will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble models and graph neural networks, to identify latent predictors of behavioral outcomes and simulate intervention efficacy across diverse student subgroups. Computational workflows will process anonymized datasets from partner school districts, encompassing over 50,000 student records with 200+ variables per case, to train models that optimize for both accuracy and interpretability in real-world school contexts. By parallelizing model training and validation cycles on HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce runtime for iterative hypothesis testing from weeks to days, enabling rapid refinement of actionable insights. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for school psychologists to prioritize intervention targets based on risk trajectories and resource availability. This work will directly inform equitable resource allocation strategies in education, particularly for underserved populations disproportionately impacted by behavioral health disparities. The requested computing resources are critical to handling memory-intensive tasks, such as graph-based analyses of social networks within schools, and ensuring scalability as datasets expand. Findings will contribute to the broader integration of computational social science methodologies into school psychology practice, bridging gaps between counseling theory and data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing and optimizing generative architectural designs that integrate biophilic principles with structural efficiency, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational complexity of multi-objective spatial optimization. Traditional architectural design workflows often struggle to balance ecological, aesthetic, and functional criteria in large-scale or unconventional structures, particularly when incorporating dynamic environmental feedback or biomimetic patterns. The proposed research addresses this gap by creating a hybrid algorithmic pipeline combining parametric modeling, agent-based simulations of environmental interactions, and machine learning-driven topology optimization. The computational workload arises from iteratively simulating microclimatic impacts, material stress distributions, and occupant behavior patterns across thousands of design variants, requiring parallelized processing of high-dimensional datasets. HPC resources will enable the use of distributed neural networks to predict performance trade-offs in real time, coupled with evolutionary algorithms to explore non-dominated design solutions. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for generating architecture that dynamically responds to ecological and social variables while maintaining structural integrity, with applications in sustainable urban development and adaptive reuse projects. The project also aims to establish benchmarks for computational resource allocation in architectural research, particularly for problems requiring simultaneous optimization of qualitative human-centric metrics and quantitative engineering parameters. By bridging computational design, environmental psychology, and materials science, this work advances methodological capabilities for next-generation architectural practice while contributing to HPC utilization paradigms in non-traditional STEM domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance, sustainable polymers in industrial applications necessitates advanced computational tools to overcome the limitations of traditional trial-and-error material development. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize the synthesis, processing, and performance of novel polymer systems, with a focus on biodegradability and recyclability. The primary challenge lies in predicting macromolecular behavior under dynamic manufacturing conditions, including polymerization kinetics, thermal stability, and stress-response properties, which are experimentally time-intensive and cost-prohibitive to characterize. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms. MD simulations will model molecular interactions during polymerization and degradation, while FEA will assess mechanical performance under industrial processing parameters. ML models trained on experimental and simulated datasets will identify correlations between polymer architectures, processing variables, and end-use properties, enabling inverse design of materials with tailored characteristics. The HPC environment is critical for managing the computational intensity of these tasks, particularly for simulating large-scale polymer networks (>100,000 atoms) and iterative optimization workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for designing biodegradable polymers with equivalent or superior mechanical properties to conventional plastics, as well as energy-efficient processing protocols to reduce manufacturing carbon footprints. This work will directly support ongoing industry partnerships aimed at commercializing circular-economy-compliant materials, while providing a computational resource framework for future research in polymer engineering education and applied R&D. The requested allocation will enable simulations at experimentally relevant timescales and system sizes, which are unfeasible with current institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using industrial polymers. Includes instruction in the principles of macromolecular chemistry, polymerization and plastic manufacturing processes and equipment, design and operational testing procedures, equipment maintenance and repair procedures, safety procedures, applications to specific products, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of multiscale electrophysiological data in clinical neurodiagnostics, with a focus on improving the detection and interpretation of subtle neurological biomarkers. Current electroneurodiagnostic (END) workflows rely heavily on visual inspection of electroencephalographic (EEG) and evoked potential (EP) recordings, a process limited by inter-rater variability and the challenge of identifying transient or spatially diffuse anomalies in high-dimensional data. The research problem centers on developing automated, adaptive algorithms capable of integrating raw EEG/EP signals with patient-specific clinical metadata (e.g., medication history, comorbidities) to predict neurological dysfunction earlier and with greater specificity. Computational methods will combine time-frequency analysis, graph-based network modeling of neural connectivity, and hybrid machine learning architectures (convolutional neural networks coupled with attention mechanisms) trained on a curated dataset of >10,000 hours of annotated recordings from diverse neurological pathologies. HPC resources are critical for three phases: 1) parallel processing of long-term monitoring data to establish baseline population models, 2) iterative optimization of dynamic neural networks that adapt to individual patient electrophysiology, and 3) real-time simulation of clinical deployment scenarios requiring sub-second latency for potential intraoperative applications. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework that quantifies spatially distributed neural network instability—a proposed precursor to overt seizures and post-traumatic encephalopathies—with demonstrable improvements over conventional amplitude-based metrics. This work bridges clinical neurophysiology, computational neuroscience, and edge computing, aiming to translate theoretical advances in network neuroscience into practical tools for END technologists. Success would enhance diagnostic precision in understudied conditions such as subclinical seizure propagation and mild traumatic brain injury, while establishing scalable methodologies for integrating HPC-driven analytics into routine END workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to study and record electrical activity in the brain and nervous system for purposes of patient monitoring and supporting diagnoses. Includes instruction in patient communication and care; taking and abstracting patient histories; application of recording electrodes; EEG, EP, and PSG equipment operation and procedural techniques; and data recording and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized learning pathways for middle school students in special education programs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational data. Students with disabilities often exhibit heterogeneous learning profiles, yet educators face challenges in efficiently integrating diverse data sources—such as academic performance, behavioral logs, individualized education program (IEP) goals, and real-time classroom interactions—to inform instructional decisions. Current tools lack the scalability to process these complex datasets or simulate longitudinal outcomes of pedagogical strategies. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline that processes structured and unstructured data (e.g., written teacher feedback, sensor-based engagement metrics) using natural language processing and time-series analysis. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of ensemble models to predict student progress across learning domains (e.g., literacy, numeracy) under varying intervention scenarios. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom-scale interactions, testing how resource allocation (e.g., assistive technology deployment, paraeducator support timing) affects both individualized and group outcomes. The computational workflow will integrate anonymized datasets from 15 middle school special education programs, comprising over 5,000 student-hours of observational and assessment data. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable tool for generating dynamic IEP recommendations based on predictive analytics, (2) quantified thresholds for intervention efficacy across disability categories, and (3) optimized scheduling strategies for special education classrooms derived from simulation results. This work will provide evidence-based frameworks to help teachers prioritize instructional targets, reduce trial-and-error in intervention design, and allocate limited classroom resources more effectively. By coupling educational theory with computational modeling, the project aims to advance data-driven practices in special education teacher preparation and middle school classroom implementation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Junior High/ Middle School Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in junior high/middle school. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for middle school special education; and principles of middle school instruction in specific subjects.

abstract: Adolescent healthcare presents unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay of biological maturation, psychosocial development, and environmental influences. Current clinical models often struggle to predict health outcomes in this population, particularly for conditions like eating disorders, substance use, and mental health crises, where multifactorial causality complicates intervention strategies. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a computational framework to integrate multi-modal datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, genomic profiles, and social determinant surveys—to identify predictive biomarkers and social-environmental risk factors for adolescent health trajectories. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage and analyze large-scale, high-dimensional datasets, which are computationally prohibitive to process on standard systems. Machine learning models, including ensemble methods and graph neural networks, will be trained to detect latent patterns across heterogeneous data types, while mechanistic simulations will test hypotheses about intervention efficacy under varying biological and social conditions. A key innovation involves coupling natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes with agent-based modeling to simulate how provider-patient communication dynamics influence treatment adherence. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for adolescent-specific health risks, (2) personalized intervention strategies optimized through in silico trials, and (3) open-source tools for scalable analysis of adolescent health data. By elucidating interactions between biological, behavioral, and social variables, this work aims to advance clinical decision-making and reduce disparities in adolescent care. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the project’s computational demands, including parallel processing of neuroimaging data (~500 TB), genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across 10,000+ samples, and real-time optimization of simulation parameters. Results will inform the development of adaptive clinical guidelines and establish a replicable framework for translational research in adolescent medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the unique physical, psychological, and social characteristics of adolescents and their healthcare problems and needs.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing multimedia content delivery across heterogeneous digital networks, a critical issue in an era dominated by bandwidth-intensive applications such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and ultra-high-definition streaming. While existing compression algorithms and adaptive bitrate streaming techniques mitigate some latency and quality concerns, their performance degrades under dynamic network conditions and diverse user device capabilities. This research proposes the development of a machine learning-driven framework to model real-time user Quality of Experience (QoE) and dynamically optimize multimedia encoding parameters, network resource allocation, and content prioritization. The computational approach involves training deep reinforcement learning (DRL) models on large-scale datasets of user interaction logs, network telemetry, and perceptual quality metrics. These models will simulate multi-agent environments where competing data streams (e.g., 4K video, interactive 3D assets) must share constrained network resources while maintaining strict QoE thresholds. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized training of DRL agents across thousands of simulated network topologies, (2) real-time inference across distributed edge computing nodes during model validation, and (3) large-scale sentiment analysis of user feedback datasets to refine QoE metrics. Expected outcomes include novel adaptive encoding heuristics, a predictive model for bandwidth allocation in 5G/6G edge networks, and an open-source toolkit for evaluating multimedia delivery systems under constrained conditions. The research directly advances the field of digital communication by providing empirically grounded strategies for managing the computational-intensity of next-generation media formats while informing policy discussions about equitable bandwidth distribution in public infrastructure. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for neural architecture search and distributed memory clusters for simulating global-scale content delivery networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, critical evaluation, and regulation of new electronic communication technologies using computer applications; and that prepares individuals to function as developers and managers of digital communications media. Includes instruction in computer and telecommunications technologies and processes; design and development of digital communications; marketing and distribution; digital communications regulation, law, and policy; the study of human interaction with, and use of, digital media; and emerging trends and issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic evolution of Swedish dialects and their sociolinguistic interfaces using advanced computational methods, with a focus on modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variation across historical and contemporary corpora. Despite Sweden’s rich dialectal diversity, systematic large-scale analyses of regional language change—particularly under the influence of urbanization, digital communication, and language policy—remain underexplored due to the technical challenges of processing heterogeneous, unstructured text and speech data. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based models on a curated multilingual corpus spanning 19th-century manuscripts, modern regional speech recordings, and social media texts. Computational workflows will integrate dialectometric clustering, neural machine translation for historical orthographies, and prosodic feature extraction from audio data, enabling comparative analyses across temporal, geographic, and sociodemographic axes. Key challenges include managing non-standard orthographies in pre-20th-century texts, aligning audio recordings with dialect-specific phonetic inventories, and scaling semantic role labeling for low-resource Swedish variants. The HPC environment is critical for parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, fine-tuning large language models, and running iterative simulations of language contact scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated Swedish dialect features, (2) quantitative models correlating linguistic shifts with extralinguistic factors (e.g., migration patterns, education policies), and (3) novel methods for diachronic dialectology applicable to minority languages globally. By bridging computational linguistics with Swedish philology, this work aims to redefine scholarly approaches to language preservation and policy while providing infrastructure for cross-disciplinary humanities research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Swedish language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of public resource allocation in multi-level governance systems. A critical challenge in public administration is optimizing limited resources across competing priorities while balancing equity, efficiency, and political feasibility. Traditional analytical tools often oversimplify the interdependencies between policy actors, fiscal constraints, and socioeconomic variables, limiting their predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models that simulate decision-making processes among municipal, state, and federal entities under varying policy scenarios. The models will integrate empirical datasets—including historical budget allocations, demographic trends, and service delivery outcomes—with machine learning techniques to identify patterns in resource prioritization. HPC capabilities are essential for running thousands of parallel simulations that account for nonlinear feedback loops, stochastic variables (e.g., economic shocks), and heterogeneous stakeholder preferences. Key computational tasks include parameter calibration using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, real-time visualization of fiscal trade-offs, and sensitivity analysis of equity-focused allocation rules. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework to evaluate how decentralized decision-making structures affect distributive justice in areas such as emergency response funding and educational infrastructure investment. The results will provide actionable insights for designing adaptive resource allocation mechanisms that align with public administration ethics while maintaining computational reproducibility. By bridging policy informatics with administrative theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based governance in an era of increasing fiscal uncertainty and complex public needs.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Administration and Public Policy and with an emphasis the administration and management of public policies. Includes instruction in the roles, development, and principles of public administration; the management of public policy; executive-legislative relations; public budgetary processes and financial management; administrative law; public personnel management; professional ethics; research methods; role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation; and resource allocation.

abstract: Woodworking practices have historically relied on empirical methods to predict material behavior, optimize toolpaths, and ensure structural integrity in finished products. However, the anisotropic nature of wood, coupled with variable environmental factors like humidity and temperature, introduces complex nonlinear dynamics that challenge traditional trial-and-error approaches. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model wood deformation, stress distribution, and tool interaction at unprecedented resolution, enabling data-driven design and manufacturing processes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) simulations to capture multi-scale mechanical responses in wood under varying grain orientations, moisture levels, and machining forces. These simulations will integrate machine learning models trained on experimental datasets—including digital image correlation measurements and CNC machining telemetry—to predict optimal cutting parameters, minimize material waste, and prevent tool wear. The computational workflow will also couple hygrothermal models with structural analyses to assess long-term durability of joinery systems under cyclic environmental loads. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to generate a parametric library of material performance profiles applicable to furniture design, architectural components, and heritage restoration. Expected outcomes include open-source simulation tools tailored to woodworking education, a decision-support system for sustainable material selection, and predictive metrics to reduce energy consumption in kiln-drying processes. This research bridges gaps between traditional craftsmanship and computational engineering, offering scalable methodologies to preserve material resources while advancing precision in wood-based manufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out and shape stock; assemble wooden articles or subassemblies; mark, bind, saw, carve, and sand wooden products; repair wooden articles, and use a variety of hand and power tools.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize the design and operational efficiency of wind turbine arrays in complex terrain using high-fidelity computational modeling, a critical challenge in expanding wind energy adoption. Current industry tools for wind farm layout optimization rely on simplified wake models and static atmospheric data, limiting their accuracy in predicting energy losses due to turbulent interactions in non-uniform landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for microscale turbulence analysis with mesoscale weather model data to capture site-specific atmospheric dynamics. The computational workflow will integrate open-source computational fluid dynamics (CFD) software (e.g., OpenFOAM) with custom Python-based optimization algorithms to evaluate turbine placement configurations under varying wind regimes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve turbulent flow structures at meter-scale resolutions across multi-kilometer domains while iterating through thousands of potential layouts. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for wake-induced power losses in topographically diverse regions and a decision-support tool that balances energy output with infrastructure costs. This work directly supports regional wind energy developers aiming to site projects in underserved mountainous areas, where poor layout choices can reduce array efficiency by 15–25%. By leveraging HPC capabilities to account for real-world complexity, the project aims to reduce levelized energy costs through improved capacity factors while providing students in Wind Energy Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge computational methods. The resulting datasets and workflow templates will be shared through public repositories to advance collaborative research in renewable energy systems integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing wind-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in wind energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven computational framework to optimize the design of personalized educational interventions for individuals with multiple disabilities (MD). Students with MD exhibit heterogeneous combinations of sensory, motor, cognitive, and socioemotional impairments, making it challenging to generalize effective teaching strategies across individuals. Current approaches to creating individualized education programs (IEPs) rely heavily on educator expertise and qualitative assessments, which may overlook complex interactions between disabilities and limit scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including behavioral, physiological, and learning outcome data—and simulate intervention efficacy across diverse disability profiles. Machine learning models will be trained on anonymized student records and real-time classroom interaction data to identify patterns linking specific disability combinations, instructional methods, and learning outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate how varying classroom environments and assistive technologies interact with individual student profiles. The computational workload requires parallel processing of high-dimensional data (e.g., eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and biometric signals) and large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated against longitudinal classroom data from three special education schools. This work will provide educators with a predictive framework to anticipate student needs, reduce trial-and-error in intervention design, and improve resource allocation for assistive technologies. By quantifying relationships between multidimensional disabilities and pedagogical strategies, the project aims to advance precision education paradigms in special needs teaching while maintaining strict ethical standards for student data privacy.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in therapeutic recreation (TR) by developing computational models to optimize personalized intervention plans for individuals with disabilities. Current TR practices rely on generalized frameworks to design recreational activities that address physical, cognitive, or emotional health goals. However, these frameworks often lack granularity to account for dynamic interactions between individual patient factors (e.g., medical history, psychosocial needs, activity preferences) and therapeutic outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning-driven approach to analyze multimodal datasets, including electronic health records, patient-reported outcomes, and real-time biometric data (e.g., heart rate, motion sensors), to identify patterns predictive of intervention efficacy. HPC resources will enable the processing of large-scale datasets and the training of ensemble models that integrate reinforcement learning to simulate patient responses under varying therapeutic scenarios. Additionally, agent-based modeling will be employed to simulate social dynamics in group-based TR interventions, assessing how peer interactions influence adherence and outcomes. The computational pipeline will be validated using retrospective data from clinical TR programs, with iterative feedback from licensed recreational therapists. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool to recommend patient-specific activity modifications, a deeper understanding of mechanistic links between recreational modalities and health outcomes, and a framework for dynamically adapting interventions based on real-time data. This work will provide novel computational methodologies tailored to TR, a field underrepresented in data-driven health research, while directly supporting the development of precision therapeutic strategies to enhance quality of life for individuals with disabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, organize, and direct recreational activities designed to promote health and well-being for patients who are physically, mentally, or emotionally disabled. Includes instruction in the foundations of therapeutic recreation, leisure education and counseling, program planning, therapeutic recreational modalities, basic anatomy and physiology, psychology, medical terminology, human growth and development, patient observation and evaluation, special needs populations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impacts of shifting climatic gradients on the population dynamics and adaptive capacity of a keystone species in montane ecosystems, using high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome critical scalability challenges in spatially explicit ecological modeling. The research problem centers on disentangling how temperature-mediated habitat fragmentation and altered biotic interactions (e.g., predator-prey relationships, competition) collectively influence metapopulation persistence under projected climate scenarios. Current models often simplify landscape heterogeneity or assume static species traits, limiting their ability to predict eco-evolutionary feedbacks over decadal timescales. To address this gap, we propose an integrative computational framework combining individual-based models (IBMs) with dynamic landscape layers and quantitative genetics modules. The IBM will simulate 10^5–10^6 individuals across a spatially resolved elevation grid (1 km² resolution), incorporating stochastic demographic processes, dispersal constraints, and trait evolution under selection pressures from both abiotic and biotic factors. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing parameter sweeps across climate projection ensembles (CMIP6), scaling genetic algorithm optimizations for trait-space exploration, and managing petabyte-scale output from 50-year simulations across multiple emission scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of threshold rates of climate change beyond which adaptive tracking fails for focal species, (2) quantification of emergent metacommunity stability metrics under hybrid disturbance regimes, and (3) open-source modular code for coupled eco-evolutionary forecasting. Results will directly inform regional conservation strategies and provide a template for integrating genomic-ecological data into predictive frameworks for climate-vulnerable taxa. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented resolution in capturing genotype-to-ecosystem linkages across realistic spatial and temporal scales.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_title: Ecology, Evolution, Systematics and Population Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ecology, evolution, and systematics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize medical office workflow efficiency and patient data management using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Medical offices face growing challenges in balancing administrative tasks—such as scheduling, billing, and electronic health record (EHR) management—with patient care demands. Existing software tools often lack adaptability to dynamic clinic environments, leading to inefficiencies that impact both staff productivity and patient outcomes. This research will address these gaps by analyzing anonymized clinic operational datasets (e.g., appointment logs, EHR access patterns, and billing timelines) to model workflow bottlenecks. Leveraging HPC resources, we will implement parallelized agent-based simulations to replicate multi-staff medical office environments under varying patient loads and regulatory constraints. Machine learning models, trained on historical data, will predict no-show probabilities and prioritize task automation pathways. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be deployed to analyze unstructured clinical notes for integration with structured EHR data, enhancing interoperability. The computational scale of these tasks—particularly the simulation of clinic networks and NLP processing across millions of text entries—necessitates HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and accuracy. Outcomes will include predictive tools for resource allocation, such as dynamic staff scheduling algorithms and task prioritization protocols, validated against real-world clinic performance metrics. This work will directly support the training of Medical Office Assistant students by generating open-access, simulated training modules that reflect computationally optimized workflows. By bridging healthcare administration education with advanced computational methods, the project aims to reduce administrative burdens in clinical settings, improve patient data accessibility, and establish scalable models for clinic operations research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers and other professionals, to perform routine administrative duties in a medical, clinical, or health care facility/system office environment. Includes instruction in general office skills, data processing, office equipment operation, principles of medical record-keeping and business regulations, medical/clinical office procedures, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of information dissemination across 17th-century European scholarly networks and its impact on political and intellectual developments. Traditional historical methods face challenges in systematically analyzing the vast corpus of surviving correspondence and publications from this period, which includes thousands of letters, pamphlets, and treatises. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, social network modeling, and agent-based simulations to reconstruct and analyze the flow of ideas among scholars, institutions, and political actors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing multilingual texts through natural language processing pipelines, identifying semantic patterns, and mapping evolving network connections across temporal and geographic dimensions. The agent-based model will simulate how information spread through these networks under varying sociopolitical constraints, requiring iterative parameter adjustments and large-scale parallel processing. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously unrecognized hubs of intellectual exchange, quantitative assessments of censorship effects on knowledge diffusion, and visualizations of network resilience during key historical events such as the Thirty Years' War. By integrating computational methods with archival research, this study aims to establish a new framework for analyzing historical information ecosystems, providing insights into how networked communication shaped early modern state formation and scientific revolution. The proposed work will also produce open-source tools tailored for historical network analysis, enabling future researchers to apply similar methodologies to other periods and regions. This interdisciplinary approach demonstrates the transformative potential of HPC resources in advancing historical scholarship through large-scale data synthesis and complex systems modeling.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in history, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of dynamic, granular forecasting models for real-time market sentiment analysis in decentralized digital asset markets. Traditional business statistics methods struggle to process the high-velocity, unstructured data generated by blockchain-based trading platforms, social sentiment feeds, and cross-platform liquidity pools, which exhibit nonstationary patterns and complex network dependencies. The proposed computational framework integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) with Bayesian hierarchical time-series models to capture latent relationships between micro-level trader behaviors and macro-level market volatility. By parallelizing graph embedding computations across GPU clusters and optimizing memory-intensive Monte Carlo simulations for HPC architectures, the project aims to overcome scalability barriers in existing econometric toolkits. Key challenges include developing adaptive sampling algorithms to handle streaming ledger data and creating hybrid CPU-GPU workflows for simultaneous parameter estimation across heterogeneous datasets (order books, social media APIs, on-chain transaction graphs). Success metrics will focus on reducing prediction error rates for 15-minute volatility windows compared to conventional ARIMA and GARCH models, while maintaining computational feasibility for sub-second updates. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source library for high-frequency decentralized finance (DeFi) analytics, with applications to risk management systems and regulatory stress-testing frameworks. This work bridges gaps between computational economics, distributed systems research, and business statistics by formalizing methods to quantify emergent market behaviors in blockchain ecosystems—a critical need as traditional financial metrics fail to address the combinatorial complexity of Web3 markets. Resource requests emphasize GPU node allocation for deep learning components and high-memory nodes for large graph processing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of immersive, real-time networked virtual environments (NVEs) through the development of scalable computational models for dynamic, AI-driven character behavior and procedural world generation. Current approaches in game and interactive media design face limitations in simulating large-scale, persistent virtual worlds with high-fidelity interactions, particularly when balancing real-time responsiveness with complex systems such as crowd dynamics, environmental physics, and emergent narrative structures. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in simulating these interconnected systems, which require simultaneous execution of resource-intensive tasks including pathfinding for thousands of autonomous agents, physics-based object interactions, and machine learning-driven character adaptation. The proposed computational approach combines parallelized behavior tree architectures with neural network-based decision-making models, leveraging GPU-accelerated simulations for crowd dynamics and terrain deformation systems. High-performance computing resources will enable parameter space exploration for optimizing load distribution across hybrid CPU/GPU architectures, testing neural architecture search configurations for adaptive non-player characters (NPCs), and stress-testing networked synchronization protocols under scaled user concurrency scenarios. Methodologies include developing modular simulation components using Unity3D’s Data-Oriented Technology Stack (DOTS) integrated with distributed computing frameworks, implementing CUDA-optimized physics engines for destructible environments, and training reinforcement learning models on heterogeneous agent populations. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for dynamically scaling interactive media simulations, quantitative benchmarks for HPC resource allocation in cloud-based game engines, and novel techniques for maintaining real-time performance in environments exceeding 10,000 concurrent interactive entities. This work will provide foundational insights into computational resource thresholds for next-generation interactive media while establishing best practices for deploying HPC capabilities in artistic and design-focused development pipelines. Results will directly benefit academic researchers in game studies and industry professionals seeking to implement large-scale persistent worlds, with implications for educational simulations, collaborative virtual spaces, and AI-augmented design tools.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and programming of interactive media entertainment, including computer and video games, virtual environments, Internet applications, and other interactive media. Includes instruction in theory of games, turn-based games, real-time games, visual and interactive design, story development, animation, simulation, and programming.

abstract: This project seeks to advance bicycle mechanics and repair technology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical challenges in the design, durability, and maintenance of human-powered vehicles. While empirical methods dominate current repair practices, the increasing complexity of modern bicycle systems—such as lightweight composite frames, adaptive gear mechanisms, and aerodynamic components—demands a computational approach to optimize performance and longevity. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive models for stress distribution, material fatigue, and dynamic load responses in bicycle components under real-world conditions, which limits the development of data-driven repair protocols and preventive maintenance strategies. To address this, the project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to model mechanical and aerodynamic stresses across bicycle frames, drivetrains, and wheel assemblies. These simulations will integrate multi-physics datasets, including material properties, environmental factors, and usage patterns, to predict failure points and optimize component geometries. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze large-scale sensor data from instrumented bicycles, identifying correlations between riding conditions and wear rates. The computational workflows will require HPC resources to manage the high-resolution meshing, iterative solvers, and parallel processing needed for accurate, large-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for component failure, validated repair guidelines for emerging materials (e.g., carbon fiber, titanium alloys), and open-access tools to assist technicians in diagnosing complex mechanical issues. By bridging computational engineering with practical repair techniques, this research aims to elevate industry standards, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance the safety and efficiency of human-powered transportation systems.
cip_title: Bicycle Mechanics and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain bicycles and other human-powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication, adjustments of moving parts, and wheel building.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational legal studies inquiry into the evolution of judicial decision-making patterns within decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). As blockchain-based entities governed by smart contracts and distributed consensus mechanisms, DAOs present novel challenges to traditional legal frameworks, particularly in resolving disputes and interpreting governance protocols. The research problem centers on identifying emergent legal norms in DAO governance through large-scale analysis of on-chain dispute resolution data and off-chain community deliberations. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques adapted for smart contract bytecode and forum discourse, the project will construct temporal network models to trace how quasi-legal principles develop across 50,000+ DAO transactions and associated social metadata. Computational demands arise from processing heterogeneous blockchain data (Ethereum, Solana) while maintaining cryptographic integrity, analyzing multilingual forum interactions, and simulating governance scenarios through agent-based modeling. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based architectures on limited annotated legal texts specific to decentralized governance, as well as for running parallelized simulations of hypothetical disputes under varying regulatory assumptions. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of algorithmic legal reasoning in decentralized organizations, 2) probabilistic models predicting conflict escalation paths based on smart contract design features, and 3) an open-source toolkit for auditing governance protocols against emergent jurisprudential patterns. By bridging computational social science with legal informatics, this work aims to establish methodological foundations for studying law in algorithmically mediated environments while providing actionable insights for policymakers grappling with the juridical status of Web3 institutions.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on law and legal issues from the perspective of the social sciences and humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to advance health services research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multi-source healthcare datasets, with the goal of identifying drivers of disparities in care access, quality, and outcomes. A key challenge in this field is integrating heterogeneous data—including electronic health records (EHRs), insurance claims, socioeconomic indicators, and public health surveillance data—to model complex interactions between patient characteristics, systemic factors, and health service utilization. Traditional computing infrastructures struggle with the volume and velocity of these datasets, particularly when analyzing unstructured clinical notes, geospatial trends, or longitudinal outcomes across millions of patients. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) for clinical text mining, Bayesian hierarchical models for spatial-temporal analysis, and machine learning (ML) to predict care gaps and simulate intervention impacts. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets, training of deep learning models on GPU clusters, and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to quantify uncertainty in policy-relevant scenarios. The project will focus on case studies in maternal health and chronic disease management, examining how facility capacity, insurance networks, and social determinants influence avoidable hospitalizations and mortality. Expected outcomes include predictive models for service demand, optimized resource allocation strategies for underserved regions, and open-source tools for scalable health services analytics. By facilitating rapid analysis of nationally representative datasets, this work will provide actionable evidence for policymakers and health systems aiming to reduce inequities. The requested computing resources are critical to overcoming memory and runtime constraints, ensuring robust statistical inference, and generalizing findings across diverse populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on basic and applied inquiry, that examines access to, and the use, costs, quality, delivery, organization, financing, and outcomes of health care services to produce new knowledge about the structure, processes, and effects of health services for individuals and populations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in beverage program optimization within the hospitality industry, focusing on the intersection of mixology, consumer behavior analytics, and operational logistics. Traditional approaches to cocktail development, inventory management, and menu design rely heavily on manual experimentation and static historical data, limiting adaptability to dynamic consumer trends and supply chain variability. The research problem centers on developing predictive models capable of simulating flavor interaction networks, regional ingredient availability patterns, and real-time demand forecasting to optimize beverage programs holistically. Using agent-based modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous datasets (including chemical compound databases, sales histories, and sensory preference surveys), the project aims to create a computational framework for generative cocktail design and resource allocation. The models will account for variables such as seasonal ingredient costs, cultural flavor preferences, and molecular compatibility between compounds to propose novel recipes, minimize waste, and predict market success. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for beverage directors to simulate menu changes, forecast inventory needs, and dynamically adjust pricing or promotions. By integrating domain-specific knowledge from mixology with computational analytics, this work bridges a critical gap in hospitality technology, offering data-driven solutions to enhance sustainability and profitability in bar operations. The requested HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of flavor interaction simulations and high-dimensional optimization tasks that are computationally intractable on local systems, establishing a foundation for computational mixology as an emerging interdisciplinary field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to professionally prepare mixed alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages and related products and manage bars, lounges, and beverage service operations in the hospitality industry.  Includes instruction in mixology, oenology, accounting and cash management, inventory and cellar management, bar and lounge management, applicable laws and regulations, customer service, and labor/employment regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dental restorative procedures demands precise, patient-specific approaches to optimize clinical outcomes and material longevity. Current methods for predicting biomechanical performance of dental restorations—such as crowns, bridges, and implants—rely on simplified models that fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale interactions between restorative materials, oral tissues, and occlusal forces. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and predict the biomechanical behavior of dental restorations under clinically relevant conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct patient-specific 3D models derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and intraoral scans, integrating material properties, mastication dynamics, and temporal degradation factors. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to model stress distribution, fatigue failure, and interfacial interactions between restorations and biological tissues. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze large datasets of clinical outcomes to identify predictive patterns linking restoration design parameters to long-term success rates. The computational workflow will be validated against in vitro experiments and retrospective clinical data. This project requires HPC capabilities to manage the high-resolution meshing, multi-physics simulations, and iterative optimization processes inherent to modeling complex oral biomechanics. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for optimizing restoration design, reducing clinical failure rates, and informing material selection guidelines. By bridging computational engineering and clinical dentistry, this work aims to advance personalized treatment planning, reduce costs associated with restorative failures, and contribute foundational insights into the biomechanical adaptation of dental materials. The proposed resource allocation will enable scalable, parallelized simulations that are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure, directly supporting innovation in evidence-based dental practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: Turfgrass systems are critical for recreational, aesthetic, and environmental health, yet their sustainability is challenged by climate variability, biotic stressors, and resource limitations. Traditional turfgrass breeding and management strategies are often constrained by the slow pace of phenotypic evaluation and the complexity of genotype-environment interactions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of turfgrass performance under diverse environmental and management scenarios. Specifically, we aim to integrate genomic, phenotypic, and environmental datasets to optimize the selection of turfgrass cultivars with enhanced drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze high-throughput genotyping data (e.g., SNP arrays) and multi-year field trial data, including hyperspectral imaging and soil sensor outputs. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate microclimate conditions affecting turfgrass health, such as heat stress and water distribution patterns, while agent-based models will explore pest and pathogen spread dynamics. These parallelized workflows require significant computational capacity due to the scale of genomic datasets (>10^6 markers per population) and the iterative nature of parameter optimization in predictive models. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid calibration of models against experimental data, reducing the time needed to identify candidate genes and optimal management practices. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for turfgrass genomics and precision management, as well as publicly accessible datasets linking genetic markers to stress-resilience traits. By accelerating the discovery of climate-adapted turfgrasses, this work will directly support sustainable landscaping, sports field maintenance, and urban green space preservation, aligning with broader agricultural priorities to mitigate resource use while maintaining ecosystem services.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: Nuclear medicine research faces critical challenges in modeling the dynamic behavior of radiopharmaceuticals and their interactions with biological systems, which are essential for advancing diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficacy. Current computational approaches often lack the resolution and scalability needed to simulate complex tracer kinetics, radiation dosimetry, and multi-scale physiological processes, limiting the development of optimized imaging protocols and personalized therapies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models of radiopharmaceutical distribution, metabolism, and radiation transport in heterogeneous biological tissues. The research will employ Monte Carlo simulations to model radiation interactions at the molecular and cellular levels, coupled with pharmacokinetic modeling to predict tracer dynamics across organ systems. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to analyze high-dimensional imaging datasets and refine image reconstruction algorithms for positron emission tomography (PET) and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT). The computational workflows will utilize open-source frameworks such as GATE/Geant4 for radiation transport and custom Python-based pipelines for data analysis, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of simulated and clinical imaging data. Expected outcomes include the optimization of tracer dosing protocols, improved quantification of metabolic pathways in oncology and neurology applications, and enhanced dosimetric precision for targeted alpha therapy. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of radiopharmaceutical behavior, this work will accelerate the translation of novel tracers into clinical practice, reduce patient radiation exposure, and advance theranostic strategies for precision medicine. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming current computational bottlenecks, ensuring scalable and reproducible analyses that are infeasible with conventional infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the tracer principle, most often with radiopharmaceuticals, to evaluate molecular, metabolic, physiologic and pathologic conditions of the body for the purposes of diagnosis, therapy and research. Includes instruction in tracer kinetics, the biologic effects of radiation exposure, the fundamentals of the physical sciences, and the principles and operation of radiation detection and imaging systems.

abstract: The commercial poultry industry faces persistent challenges from infectious diseases such as avian influenza, Newcastle disease, and bacterial infections, which threaten animal welfare, food security, and public health. Current strategies for disease prevention and management are hindered by gaps in understanding pathogen evolution, host-pathogen interactions, and the influence of environmental and genetic factors on disease transmission. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and analyze large-scale datasets, enabling data-driven interventions. The research integrates epidemiological surveillance data, whole-genome sequencing of pathogens and poultry populations, and environmental variables to investigate disease spread dynamics, genetic resistance markers, and optimal biosecurity protocols. Computational methods include agent-based modeling to simulate disease transmission across poultry flocks under varying management practices, machine learning algorithms to identify risk factors for outbreaks, and phylogenetic analyses to track pathogen evolution and zoonotic potential. Additionally, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will be conducted to pinpoint genetic variants linked to disease resilience in poultry. The scale of these datasets—spanning millions of genomic sequences, high-resolution environmental metrics, and real-time flock health records—necessitates HPC infrastructure for efficient processing, storage, and parallelized computation. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into targeted vaccination strategies, genetic selection for disease-resistant poultry lines, and early-warning systems for outbreak prediction. By enhancing the precision and scalability of these analyses, the project aims to reduce economic losses in the poultry sector, mitigate antimicrobial use, and minimize zoonotic spillover risks. This work aligns with broader goals of advancing sustainable livestock production and global health security through translational clinical research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the commercial poultry industry, providing services and technical support pertaining to prevention, diagnosis, and management of disease; epidemiology; genetics; and nutrition.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize nurse staffing allocation in acute care settings, addressing critical gaps in balancing patient safety, workforce well-being, and operational costs. Current staffing practices often rely on static nurse-to-patient ratios, which fail to account for dynamic factors such as fluctuating patient acuity, interdisciplinary care demands, and real-time workload variability. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate staffing scenarios under diverse clinical conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets—including patient outcomes, nurse workflow patterns, and institutional cost structures—while running parallelized simulations to identify optimal staffing configurations. The ABM will model interactions between nurses, patients, and care environments, incorporating stochastic elements such as emergent patient deteriorations and shift-to-shift workflow disruptions. ML algorithms, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will analyze historical EHR data to predict acuity trends and quantify workload impacts on clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated simulation platform for testing staffing policies, (2) dynamic staffing recommendations calibrated to real-time patient and operational variables, and (3) predictive metrics linking staffing flexibility to reduced burnout rates and preventable adverse events. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will provide nurse administrators with evidence-based tools to align staffing decisions with evolving care demands, improving both resource efficiency and care quality. The computational pipeline developed here will be scalable to other healthcare settings, offering a template for data-driven nursing management in complex clinical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to manage nursing personnel and services in hospitals and other health care delivery agencies. Includes instruction in principles of health care administration, resource and financial management, health care law and policy, medical personnel management, and managed care operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of personalized employee development pathways using computational modeling to enhance workforce adaptability in dynamic organizational environments. The research addresses a critical gap in Human Resources Development: the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to design individualized training interventions that balance employee skill growth, job role evolution, and organizational objectives amid rapidly changing market conditions. Current approaches often rely on static competency models that fail to account for complex interdependencies between learning patterns, team dynamics, and emergent organizational needs. We propose developing an adaptive simulation platform leveraging agent-based modeling and reinforcement learning to simulate workforce ecosystems at enterprise scale. The computational approach will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including skill assessments, collaboration networks, and performance metrics—to model how micro-level learning decisions propagate through organizational hierarchies. High-performance computing resources are essential to process longitudinal employee data (simulated and anonymized real-world datasets) while running parallelized simulations of alternative training policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel metric framework for quantifying "adaptive capacity" at individual and team levels, plus evidence-based recommendations for aligning personalized learning architectures with strategic workforce planning. The research will provide organizations with predictive tools to optimize human capital investments, reduce skill obsolescence risks, and improve retention through computationally designed career pathways. By bridging cognitive science, network theory, and operations research within an HR context, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for next-generation organizational development strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply integrated training, organizational development, and career planning and counseling skills to the design, management, and evaluation of programs to improve individual productivity, employability, and job satisfaction and organizational effectiveness. Includes instruction in psychology; organizational behavior; principles of adult education; occupational counseling; skill testing and evaluation; program design; consulting practice; organizational development; and applications to issues such as training, management development, customer service, and total quality management.

abstract: Public works systems are critical to community well-being, yet municipalities face persistent challenges in optimizing infrastructure maintenance, resource distribution, and operational resilience under constrained budgets. This project seeks to develop a computational decision-support framework to model public works management scenarios, with a focus on balancing fiscal responsibility, equity, and long-term infrastructure performance. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to simulate the interdependencies between aging infrastructure networks, climate stressors, and dynamic population needs—a gap that limits evidence-based policymaking. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models to simulate infrastructure degradation patterns, workforce allocation dynamics, and budget trade-offs across multiple urban systems (e.g., transportation, water, utilities). Computational workflows will integrate geospatial data, historical maintenance records, and demographic projections to evaluate "what-if" scenarios under varying funding levels and policy interventions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify non-linear relationships between maintenance investments and service outcomes, while optimization algorithms will propose resource allocation strategies that minimize lifecycle costs and maximize equity metrics. The project will validate models against case studies from three midsized U.S. cities, calibrating parameters through partnerships with municipal agencies. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for public works planners, a comparative analysis of management strategies under fiscal constraints, and a cost-benefit framework for prioritizing infrastructure upgrades. By quantifying the long-term impacts of budgetary decisions on service quality and community resilience, this work aims to advance operational standards in public administration while providing scalable computational methods for resource-limited jurisdictions. The HPC environment is essential to process high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets and run parallelized simulations at metropolitan scales, enabling insights that traditional analytical tools cannot capture.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address inefficiencies in digital textile pattern optimization, a critical challenge in apparel manufacturing that intersects computational design, material science, and industrial engineering. Traditional methods for generating and validating textile patterns rely on iterative manual adjustments and physical prototyping, leading to prolonged development cycles, material waste, and limited scalability for custom or adaptive designs. To overcome these constraints, the research proposes a computational framework integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate and optimize textile patterns under dynamic mechanical and aesthetic constraints. The project will develop machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets—including fabric tensile properties, historical design archives, and consumer preference metrics—to generate pattern variations that balance structural integrity, material efficiency, and stylistic coherence. Concurrently, FEA simulations will model stress distribution and drape behavior across diverse body geometries and movement scenarios, enabling virtual validation of digitally generated patterns before physical production. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-resolution textile datasets, parallelizing computationally intensive FEA workloads, and iterating GAN architectures at scale. Anticipated outcomes include a reduction in physical prototyping by 40–60%, a predictive framework for sustainable material utilization, and novel methods for mass-customized apparel production. By bridging gaps between computational design automation and industrial textile workflows, this research aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven manufacturing in non-science and engineering domains, with potential applications in adaptive fashion, wearable technology, and circular economy initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and production of textile products and related processes and systems. Includes instruction in functional and aesthetic design, human factors research, production planning, manufacturing processes, quality assessment, and distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the economic impacts of renewable energy integration in regional electricity markets using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome computational constraints in large-scale dynamic stochastic modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in applied microeconomic analysis: existing models of energy market transitions often oversimplify agent heterogeneity, regulatory feedback, and resource allocation trade-offs under uncertainty, limiting their utility for real-world policy design. The study focuses on a multi-agent framework simulating interactions between utilities, regulators, and consumers across three U.S. regions with divergent energy portfolios. Computational challenges arise from modeling thousands of strategic agents with time-dependent decision rules, incorporating high-resolution weather data, and solving dynamic equilibria under stochastic demand and supply shocks. The proposed approach combines parallelized agent-based modeling with econometric estimation techniques, requiring HPC resources for 1) Monte Carlo simulations of policy scenarios (carbon pricing, subsidy structures), 2) Bayesian estimation of heterogeneous agent parameters using historical market data, and 3) optimal control algorithms to identify cost-minimizing transition pathways. Expected outcomes include quantifying the non-linear relationship between renewable adoption rates and wholesale price volatility, evaluating the distributional impacts of grid infrastructure investments, and identifying regulatory mechanisms that mitigate allocative inefficiencies during energy transitions. Results will provide policymakers with empirically grounded tools to balance decarbonization goals with economic stability, particularly in regions facing acute resource constraints. The computational architecture developed through this project will be adaptable to other applied economics contexts requiring large-scale simulation of regulated markets with strategic actors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic principles and analytical techniques to the study of particular industries, activities, or the exploitation of particular resources. Includes instruction in economic theory; microeconomic analysis and modeling of specific industries, commodities; the economic consequences of resource allocation decisions; regulatory and consumer factors; and the technical aspects of specific subjects as they relate to economic analysis.

abstract: The application of protective and decorative coatings to structural surfaces involves complex interactions between materials, environmental conditions, and application techniques.
