Traditional empirical approaches to optimizing coating performance—such as adhesion, durability, and aesthetic outcomes—are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and often fail to account for the multivariate nature of real-world conditions. This project proposes a computational research initiative to model and simulate the physicochemical processes governing coating behaviors, enabling predictive insights into material performance under diverse environmental and operational scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to develop multiscale models that integrate molecular dynamics simulations of coating-substrate interactions, computational fluid dynamics analyses of application processes (e.g., spraying, rolling), and machine learning frameworks to correlate environmental variables (humidity, temperature, pollution) with long-term coating degradation. These models will be validated against experimental data from controlled laboratory tests and field studies. The computational approach addresses critical gaps in understanding how micro-scale material properties (e.g., polymer chain mobility, pigment dispersion) influence macro-scale outcomes like crack propagation, moisture resistance, and color retention. By simulating thousands of parameter combinations, the project will identify optimal coating formulations and application protocols for specific environmental and structural conditions, reducing reliance on trial-and-error methods. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for selecting coatings that maximize longevity and compliance with sustainability standards, directly benefiting industry practices in surface preparation, waste reduction, and regulatory adherence. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, large datasets from hyperspectral imaging of coating failures, and the parallel processing demands of real-time simulation workflows. This research aligns with the program’s focus on advancing technical methodologies in painting and wall covering while addressing environmental and economic challenges in the field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to finish exterior and interior structural surfaces by applying protective or decorative coating materials, such as paint, lacquer, and wallpaper. Includes instruction in surface preparation; selecting, preparing, and applying paints and other coatings; hanging wallpaper; equipment operation and maintenance; finish selection; safety and clean-up; environmental effects on finishes; adhesion properties; and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation, analysis, and revitalization of the Hawaiian language (‘Ōlelo Hawai‘i) and its regional dialects, which face critical endangerment despite ongoing preservation efforts. While existing scholarship has produced foundational lexicographic and grammatical resources, significant gaps remain in understanding syntactic variation across historical and contemporary texts, dialectal divergence in understudied communities, and the application of computational tools to support pedagogical and community-driven language initiatives. This project addresses these challenges through two interconnected computational workflows. First, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to analyze a digitized corpus of 19th-century Hawaiian-language newspapers, mele (chants), and archival manuscripts, identifying patterns in morphology, loanword integration, and discourse structures. Second, we will develop a parallelized framework for dialect mapping using acoustic and phonetic data from native speaker recordings, integrating spectral analysis and machine learning classifiers to quantify phonological shifts across geographic regions. These workflows demand HPC capabilities due to the scale of textual data (over 20,000 digitized pages), the complexity of training custom NLP models for a low-resource language, and the computational intensity of real-time signal processing for audio datasets. Outcomes will include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Hawaiian texts, a dialect classification tool for educational applications, and evidence-based recommendations for orthographic standardization of regional variants. By bridging computational linguistics with Indigenous language revitalization frameworks, this project aims to empower Hawaiian-speaking communities with scalable digital resources while contributing novel methodologies for the study of endangered languages globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hawaiian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale multimedia datasets in journalism research, addressing the growing challenge of misinformation detection and narrative tracking across decentralized media ecosystems. Traditional journalism research methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and variety of digital content—including text, images, and video—generated by social platforms, news outlets, and user communities. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational tools to identify emerging disinformation campaigns, map the diffusion of narratives, and assess bias in multimedia reporting. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis, computer vision techniques for image and video verification, and graph-based network modeling to trace cross-platform content sharing. Deep learning models, including transformer architectures and multimodal neural networks, will be trained on heterogeneous datasets comprising social media posts, historical news archives, and fact-checking databases. HPC resources are critical for handling parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimizing hyperparameters for complex models, and simulating information diffusion dynamics in near-real time. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for journalists to detect synthetic media, visualize narrative networks, and prioritize high-risk content for manual review. The project aims to advance computational journalism methodologies by establishing reproducible pipelines for auditing media ecosystems at scale, with implications for improving public trust in journalism and supporting evidence-based policy responses to misinformation. By integrating HPC-driven insights with traditional reporting practices, this work will empower news organizations to address evolving ethical challenges in the digital age while maintaining rigorous standards of accountability.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in journalism, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The sustainable production of bioenergy from plant and microbial feedstocks requires balancing environmental resilience, resource efficiency, and economic viability. Current models often fail to capture the complex, multi-scale interactions between bioprocessing dynamics, regional ecosystem constraints, and supply chain logistics, limiting the accuracy of sustainability assessments. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing an integrated computational framework to optimize bioenergy systems across spatial, temporal, and biological scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate feedstock cultivation impacts on watershed hydrology, microbial metabolic networks for biofuel conversion, and lifecycle emissions under diverse climate and land-use scenarios. Leveraging geospatial datasets, genome-scale metabolic models, and agent-based supply chain simulations, the framework will evaluate trade-offs between biofuel yield, water use, soil health, and economic returns. Computational workflows will combine machine learning for parameter optimization, hydrodynamic modeling to predict nutrient runoff, and flux balance analysis to engineer microbial consortia for enhanced bioseparations. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of scenarios, the project will quantify uncertainties in feedstock viability under climate variability and identify region-specific strategies to minimize ecosystem disruption. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for policymakers and industry to prioritize bioenergy pathways that align with conservation goals, such as reducing freshwater withdrawals or protecting carbon-rich soils. The research will also advance methodologies for coupling ecological and bioprocess models—a critical step in scaling sustainable bioenergy. Access to HPC resources is vital to manage the petabyte-scale integration of remote sensing data, genomic databases, and real-time sensor inputs from partner biorefineries, enabling predictive analytics at unprecedented resolution. This work directly supports national priorities for decarbonizing energy systems while safeguarding natural resources.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems operate under extreme thermal, mechanical, and aerodynamic conditions, demanding precise maintenance protocols to ensure safety and efficiency. Current industry practices rely heavily on historical failure data and standardized inspection intervals, which may not fully account for dynamic operational stresses or material degradation patterns unique to modern high-performance engines. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models that simulate powerplant component behavior under real-world operating conditions. The research will focus on turbine blade fatigue, combustion chamber thermal dynamics, and fuel system performance variability, integrating multiphysics simulations to map failure risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) datasets, finite element analysis (FEA) of thermal-mechanical stresses, and machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous sensor data from engine telemetry. Simulations will model scenarios such as rapid throttle changes, altitude-induced pressure fluctuations, and prolonged exposure to high-temperature gradients, correlating computational outputs with empirical wear data from engine tear-down analyses. The anticipated outcomes include a framework for condition-based maintenance prioritization, reducing unplanned downtime by 15–20% in commercial aviation fleets. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and modular simulation tools adaptable to emerging hybrid-electric propulsion systems, directly supporting technician training programs in diagnosing next-generation powerplant anomalies. By leveraging HPC capabilities to resolve complex, coupled physical interactions at scale, this work aims to advance predictive maintenance strategies while providing a computational foundation for optimizing powerplant lifecycle management in alignment with evolving aviation sustainability goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: Orthodontic treatment planning requires precise prediction of craniofacial growth patterns, biomechanical responses to orthodontic forces, and long-term stability of dental alignment. Current clinical methods rely heavily on generalized population data and static imaging, which inadequately account for patient-specific biomechanical variability, dynamic tissue adaptation, or complex interactions between orthodontic appliances and craniofacial structures. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution, patient-specific computational framework to simulate craniofacial growth, orthodontic tooth movement, and bone remodeling under varying treatment conditions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multiscale finite element models integrating cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) data, intraoral scan-derived occlusal forces, and mechanobiological bone response algorithms. Simulations will account for anisotropic bone properties, periodontal ligament viscoelasticity, and appliance-specific force systems, enabling dynamic 3D visualization of tissue displacement and stress distributions over treatment timelines. Machine learning models trained on longitudinal clinical outcome data will augment simulations to predict individual treatment durations and relapse risks. The computational pipeline will be validated against retrospective patient records and in vitro force measurement studies. Successful implementation of this framework will provide clinicians with a decision-support tool to optimize appliance selection, force application protocols, and retention strategies, reducing treatment times and improving post-treatment stability. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated biomechanical responses for common malocclusions, fostering collaboration in computational orthodontics. By addressing the critical gap in personalized, dynamic treatment planning, this work advances the translation of biomechanical research into clinical orthodontic practice, with potential applications in complex cases such as cleft palate rehabilitation and surgical orthodontics. The scale of data integration, parallelized simulation of heterogeneous tissues, and iterative model training necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically feasible processing times and resolution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the guidance of growing dental structures and the correction of misalignments, disproportionate growth, and traumas caused by genetics, disease, injuries, and dysfunctional behaviors. Includes instruction in craniofacial growth and development, malocclusion, design and fabrication of orthodontic appliances, craniofacial alignment, physiological function and analysis, cephalometrics, model analysis, space analysis, surgical orthodontics, cleft lip and palate, and treatment planning and management.

abstract: Occupational and Environmental Health Nursing (OEHN) practitioners face complex challenges in assessing multifactorial health risks arising from workplace exposures, which often involve dynamic interactions between environmental contaminants, occupational tasks, and individual health factors. Current risk assessment models lack the computational power to integrate real-time sensor data, longitudinal health records, and workplace exposure metrics at scale, limiting proactive interventions. This project proposes developing a machine learning framework to predict adverse health outcomes in worker populations by analyzing high-dimensional datasets from wearable sensors, employer safety reports, and electronic health records. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train ensemble models to identify exposure-response patterns across diverse occupational settings, including manufacturing, healthcare, and agriculture. Computational workflows will integrate time-series analysis of physiological data, natural language processing of clinical notes, and geospatial mapping of exposure hotspots. A novel agent-based simulation component will model intervention scenarios to evaluate mitigation strategies under varying workplace conditions. The scale of data—anticipated to include >10 million worker-hours of sensor data and >50,000 occupational health records—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for early identification of at-risk workers, validated thresholds for exposure limits in understudied industries, and a simulation platform to optimize workplace safety protocols. This work directly addresses gaps in evidence-based practice for OEHN professionals by enabling data-driven decision-making at individual and population levels. Successful implementation will advance computational methods in occupational health surveillance while providing scalable infrastructure for future studies on emerging workplace hazards. By prioritizing HPC capabilities, this project bridges nursing science with computational analytics to strengthen health protections for workers in high-risk environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of consumer decision-making in emerging digital marketplaces, with a focus on behavioral economic factors influencing expenditure patterns in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems. While traditional consumer economics has addressed conventional markets, the rapid growth of blockchain-based platforms introduces novel challenges, such as non-linear price volatility, trustless transaction mechanisms, and algorithm-driven liquidity pools, which defy classical utility-maximization assumptions. The research problem centers on modeling how cognitive biases—including hyperbolic discounting and loss aversion—interact with technical features of DeFi platforms to produce suboptimal consumption choices. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with high-frequency blockchain analytics. The ABM component will simulate heterogeneous consumer agents operating under bounded rationality, incorporating dynamic learning algorithms to adapt strategies in response to smart contract parameters and market shocks. Parallelized network analysis will map transactional interdependencies across Ethereum-based platforms using graph convolutional networks, while time-series forecasting of asset flows will employ transformer-based architectures. These methods require high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of behavioral scenarios, process terabyte-scale blockchain ledger data, and optimize deep learning models through hyperparameter tuning across multiple GPU nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical inflection points where platform design amplifies behavioral biases, (2) predictive metrics for consumer vulnerability in protocol-governed markets, and (3) an open-source toolkit for simulating regulatory interventions. By bridging consumer economic theory with computational social science methods, this work aims to establish normative frameworks for evaluating digital consumption environments that currently operate outside conventional policy paradigms. The requested resources will enable iteration cycles necessary to account for DeFi’s rapid protocol evolution and validate models against real-world transaction networks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of micro- and macro-economic theory to consumer behavior and individual and family consumption of goods and services. Includes instruction in modeling, economic forecasting, indexing, price theory, and analysis of individual commodities and services and/or groups of related commodities and services.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate the behavioral dynamics of adversarial decision-making in hybrid threat environments, where physical and cyber elements intersect with human cognitive factors. The research addresses a critical gap in security science: current risk assessment tools often treat human adversaries as static actors, neglecting adaptive strategies influenced by real-time feedback, misinformation, or cultural context. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to create agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate cognitive architectures, game-theoretic principles, and machine learning to capture the nonlinear evolution of adversarial intent across multiple operational domains. The computational approach will combine discrete-event simulations with neural network-driven pattern recognition to analyze how adversaries might exploit systemic vulnerabilities in interconnected infrastructure, accounting for psychological biases, resource constraints, and deception tactics. Key innovations include the development of multi-resolution modeling techniques to bridge individual decision-making scales with organizational behavior, and the implementation of ensemble simulation workflows to quantify uncertainty in threat prediction. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of adversarial behavior scenarios, validated through retrospective analysis of historical security breaches, and predictive metrics for resilience planning in critical systems. This work will provide security practitioners with novel analytical tools to anticipate emergent threat patterns in an era of increasingly sophisticated hybrid operations, while advancing methodological paradigms for computational social science applications in security contexts. The requested HPC resources are essential for scaling simulations to realistic complexity levels, enabling parallelized scenario testing across diverse parameter spaces that reflect the multidimensional nature of modern security challenges.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized rehabilitation protocols for individuals with musculoskeletal impairments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between biomechanical, physiological, and patient-specific factors. Current approaches to designing therapeutic interventions often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for the high variability in patient anatomy, injury mechanisms, or functional recovery trajectories. This project aims to develop a computational framework integrating musculoskeletal modeling, machine learning, and multi-scale simulations to predict patient responses to therapeutic exercise regimens. Using tools such as OpenSim for biomechanical analysis and custom Python-based pipelines for data assimilation, we will simulate neuromuscular activation patterns, joint loading dynamics, and tissue adaptation processes under varying therapeutic conditions. Clinical datasets—including gait analysis, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes—will inform model parameters, while machine learning algorithms will identify predictive features linking intervention parameters to functional outcomes. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational demands of iterative simulations across diverse virtual patient cohorts, real-time optimization of intervention variables (e.g., exercise intensity, duration), and sensitivity analyses to quantify uncertainty in model predictions. Expected outcomes include the identification of biomechanical and physiological thresholds that maximize recovery efficiency, the development of adaptive intervention templates for common conditions (e.g., post-stroke gait dysfunction, rotator cuff injuries), and actionable insights into dose-response relationships for therapeutic exercise. This work will advance precision physical therapy by providing clinicians with evidence-based, computationally derived guidelines to tailor rehabilitation strategies, potentially reducing recovery times and improving long-term functional outcomes. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated as open-source resources to support broader research in movement science and rehabilitation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) represent a heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by disruptions in biochemical pathways, leading to complex clinical presentations and variable treatment responses. Current diagnostic and management strategies often rely on fragmented clinical and biochemical data, limiting the ability to predict disease progression or optimize therapies. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (genomic, metabolomic, proteomic) with clinical records to identify predictive biomarkers and model metabolic network perturbations in IEMs. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale datasets, perform genome-scale metabolic reconstructions, and apply machine learning algorithms to uncover genotype-phenotype correlations. Key computational steps include variant prioritization using deep learning models trained on population and disease-specific genomic data, dynamic flux balance analysis to simulate metabolic dysregulation under varying physiological conditions, and unsupervised clustering of patient cohorts to stratify disease subtypes. The project will utilize existing clinical datasets from [Institution]’s metabolic clinic, encompassing over 1,500 patients with confirmed IEMs, and will validate models against longitudinal outcomes. By enabling rapid analysis of complex datasets, HPC resources are critical for handling the computational intensity of these tasks, particularly the iterative optimization required for metabolic network modeling and high-dimensional data integration. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool for early diagnosis of rare IEMs using multi-omics signatures, (2) in silico models to guide personalized dietary and pharmacological interventions, and (3) publicly accessible computational workflows for the metabolic genetics community. This work will directly inform clinical decision-making, reduce diagnostic odysseys, and advance precision medicine approaches for IEMs, ultimately improving outcomes for patients with these complex disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and medical management of individuals with inborn errors of metabolism, including the provision of direct care and consultative care for individuals of all ages.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time decision-making in customer service support operations through advanced computational modeling of dynamic interaction networks. Call centers and teleservice environments face persistent challenges in balancing service quality, operational efficiency, and workforce constraints, particularly as customer expectations evolve toward hyper-personalized, omnichannel support. Traditional queuing theory and discrete event simulation approaches struggle to account for the complex interdependencies between heterogeneous customer profiles, agent skill matrices, multi-platform communication flows, and real-time sentiment dynamics. The proposed work will develop an adaptive neural architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with reinforcement learning to model emergent patterns in large-scale customer-agent interaction systems. High-performance computing resources are required to process historical interaction datasets encompassing 2.5 million voice and digital customer service transcripts, train multi-modal models integrating linguistic, paralinguistic, and operational telemetry, and simulate system behavior under variable demand scenarios. The computational framework will incorporate transformer-based natural language processing to analyze unstructured dialog data, coupled with temporal graph convolutions to capture time-dependent service process flows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for service outcome optimization, real-time recommendation systems for adaptive resource allocation, and sensitivity analyses identifying critical leverage points in customer journey workflows. By bridging computational social science techniques with operational analytics, this research aims to advance the design of next-generation customer service systems capable of maintaining service integrity during demand surges while reducing average handling time. The resulting methodologies could inform both technological infrastructure investments and workforce training paradigms in the $350 billion global contact center industry.
cip_title: Customer Service Support/ Call Center/ Teleservice Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist customers with inquiries and problems in frontline call centers, help desks, teleservice centers, and online. Includes instruction in user interfaces and user behavior, principles of hardware and software systems operation, customer interaction skills, telephone and e-mailing skills, data entry, and database and Internet searching and retrieval.

abstract: Pediatric critical care medicine faces significant challenges in predicting and managing life-threatening organ failure in children, where rapid clinical deterioration demands precise, individualized interventions. Current approaches rely on generalized protocols that may not account for dynamic physiological complexity, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multimodal patient data—including high-resolution vital signs, laboratory results, imaging, and genomic markers—to model real-time risk stratification and optimize therapeutic strategies. The research problem centers on overcoming computational barriers to analyzing heterogeneous, time-sensitive datasets at scale, which is critical for advancing precision medicine in this vulnerable population. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on retrospective datasets from 5,000+ pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, capturing nonlinear interactions between organ systems during critical illness. Agent-based modeling will simulate responses to interventions under diverse physiological scenarios, while parallelized Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment effect predictions. A novel multiscale computational architecture will link molecular pathways to systemic hemodynamics, enabling in silico testing of resuscitation protocols. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for acute respiratory distress syndrome progression and septic shock trajectories, which will be prospectively tested in a pilot clinical decision-support system. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to uncover previously intractable patterns in critical care data, reduce latency in clinical decision-making, and establish a foundation for adaptive, patient-specific care pathways. The computational infrastructure will also support open-source tool development for pediatric physiological signal processing, benefiting the broader critical care research community. Successful implementation could transform management of life-threatening pediatric illness by bridging the gap between complex pathophysiology and actionable clinical insights.
cip_definition: Research focused on advanced life support for children, from the term or near-term neonate to the adolescent. This includes critical care management of life-threatening organ system failure in both medical and surgical patients and support of vital physiological functions.

abstract: Wildland fire management faces escalating challenges due to climate change, urbanization encroaching on fire-prone ecosystems, and the increasing complexity of fire investigations. Current predictive models for fire behavior and post-event forensic analysis often lack the resolution to account for micro-terrain variability, dynamic fuel moisture interactions, or the stochastic nature of human-caused ignition patterns. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale simulation framework that integrates fire spread dynamics, forensic data assimilation, and probabilistic risk assessment. The computational approach combines physics-based fire modeling using coupled atmospheric-fire interactions (WRF-Fire) with machine learning algorithms trained on historical fire incident data, satellite-derived vegetation maps, and forensic evidence from arson cases. By parallelizing stochastic simulations of ignition scenarios and fire progression across diverse landscapes, the framework will quantify uncertainty in fire origin determination and evaluate the efficacy of mitigation strategies such as adaptive firebreak placement or prescribed burn scheduling. Additionally, real-time data assimilation workflows will be prototyped to ingest streaming inputs from IoT sensors, drones, and airborne infrared imagery during active fire events, enabling dynamic resource allocation. Outcomes include open-source tools for fire investigators to reconstruct ignition sequences with higher confidence and operational dashboards for incident commanders to optimize suppression tactics. The project’s interdisciplinary integration of computational fluid dynamics, forensic statistics, and environmental sensing addresses a critical gap in non-engineering wildfire research, directly supporting agencies in mitigating ecological losses, protecting communities, and improving evidentiary rigor in fire cause determination.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of fire science, firefighting and investigation to the prevention, control and mitigation of wildland fires and the analysis of causes. Includes instruction in fire science and behavior, wildland environments, meteorology, wildland fire hydraulics and dynamics, water and chemical supply systems, wildland firefighting operations, airborne firefighting, firebreak engineering, communications systems, wildland arson, forensic procedures, wildland fire prevention, investigation techniques, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and fitting of personalized ophthalmic prosthetics and corrective lenses using biomechanical modeling and machine learning. Current opticianry practices rely on static anatomical measurements and generalized optical corrections, which often fail to account for dynamic factors such as micro-movements of ocular implants, tear film dynamics, or tissue deformation under mechanical stress from contact lenses. To address this, we propose integrating high-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT) data, finite element modeling (FEM), and real-time sensor feedback from smart contact lens prototypes into a unified computational platform. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate the multiphysics interactions between ocular tissues, prosthetic materials, and optical surfaces at micron-scale resolutions across diverse patient anatomies. Machine learning models will be trained on a curated dataset of 10,000+ de-identified patient scans to predict optimal lens curvature, material stiffness, and edge profiles that minimize corneal abrasion risks while maximizing optical clarity. A parallelized optimization algorithm will iteratively refine designs using feedback from coupled optical-ray-tracing and biomechanical stability simulations. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific lens designs that reduce adaptation periods by 40% compared to conventional methods, as well as novel metrics for quantifying dynamic fit quality. This work bridges opticianry, computational biomechanics, and materials science, offering a paradigm shift from reactive adjustments to predictive, physics-informed prosthetics customization. The resulting open-source tools will enable opticians to leverage computational insights during clinical decision-making, advancing precision eye care for patients with complex ocular geometries or post-surgical anatomical variations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing resource allocation in large-scale, stochastic operational systems, with applications in healthcare logistics and manufacturing supply chains. A core challenge in these domains is balancing competing objectives—such as cost minimization, service-level adherence, and resilience to disruptions—under uncertainty in demand, processing times, and resource availability. Existing methods often rely on simplifying assumptions that limit real-world applicability or fail to scale to industry-relevant problem sizes. To address this gap, we propose an integrated approach combining two-stage stochastic programming, simulation-based digital twin modeling, and parallelized reinforcement learning. The stochastic programming component will formalize multi-objective trade-offs using mixed-integer optimization models with scenario trees capturing demand and supply uncertainties. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the generation and evaluation of thousands of scenarios through distributed Monte Carlo simulations, implemented via MPI-based task parallelism. A digital twin of the operational environment will be developed using discrete-event simulation techniques to validate optimization results under dynamic conditions. For real-time adaptive decision-making, we will train deep reinforcement learning agents on HPC clusters using GPU-accelerated neural networks to approximate optimal policies for dynamic resource reallocation. The computational workflow will leverage containerized environments for reproducibility and hybrid OpenMP-MPI parallelization to efficiently manage memory-intensive scenario analyses. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source algorithmic implementations for stochastic resource allocation, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing solution quality and computational efficiency across problem scales, and (3) case studies demonstrating 10-20% cost reductions in hospital bed allocation and production line workforce scheduling under uncertainty. This work will advance operations research methodology by bridging gaps between traditional optimization and modern machine learning techniques while providing decision-support tools for practitioners in critical infrastructure sectors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analytics, an emerging interdisciplinary domain intersecting legal research, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning (ML). The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing vast, unstructured legal corpora—including judicial opinions, legislative texts, and contractual agreements—to identify latent patterns, biases, and decision-making frameworks that are inaccessible through traditional legal methodologies. Current tools for legal text analysis remain limited in scalability and nuance, particularly when handling cross-jurisdictional datasets or temporally evolving legal principles. The project proposes a computational pipeline integrating transformer-based NLP models, graph neural networks (GNNs), and temporal analysis frameworks to process multi-terabyte legal datasets spanning federal and state court records, international treaties, and regulatory filings. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of domain-specific language models fine-tuned on legal lexicons, coupled with network analyses of case citation graphs to map precedent influence and doctrinal shifts. A key innovation involves simulating hypothetical legal scenarios via generative AI to assess the robustness of inferred judicial decision patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for legal practitioners and scholars to query large-scale legal data with granular contextual awareness, as well as empirical insights into systemic inequities in case outcomes. By bridging computational scalability with jurisprudential rigor, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for data-driven legal research while adhering to ethical frameworks for AI in professional legal contexts. The requested resources are critical to handling the memory-intensive processing of heterogeneous legal texts and achieving statistically significant results across diverse jurisdictional contexts.
cip_title: Legal Research and Advanced Professional Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in legal research and advanced professional studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the impacts of rapid environmental change on multispecies community dynamics and ecosystem resilience. A critical challenge in environmental biology lies in disentangling how shifting abiotic conditions—such as temperature extremes, altered precipitation regimes, and habitat fragmentation—interact with biotic processes to drive population declines, community restructuring, and ecosystem function loss. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, context-dependent interactions among species and environmental drivers at ecologically relevant scales. To address this, we propose developing spatially explicit, hierarchical Bayesian models that integrate long-term ecological monitoring data, remote sensing inputs, and experimental climate manipulation datasets. These models will simulate population viability, interspecific interactions, and nutrient cycling processes under projected environmental scenarios, explicitly accounting for uncertainty in parameter estimates and stochastic disturbances. The computational workflow will involve parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for model calibration, agent-based simulations of species movement and resource competition, and machine learning techniques to identify tipping points in ecosystem stability. By coupling fine-scale process-based models with regional-scale environmental covariates, this approach will quantify how biodiversity buffers against—or amplifies—ecosystem responses to concurrent stressors. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for prioritizing conservation efforts in vulnerable communities, identifying keystone species that disproportionately affect resilience, and forecasting feedbacks between ecological change and environmental processes. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, processing terabytes of multispectral imagery and sensor network data, and executing ensemble simulations across diverse climate and land-use scenarios. Results will directly inform adaptive management strategies for ecosystems facing unprecedented rates of environmental change while advancing methodological integration in ecological forecasting.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling large-scale, dynamic communication patterns in digital public relations and advertising campaigns, where traditional computational tools struggle to process real-time, multi-platform data at the speed and scale required for actionable insights. The research problem centers on the inability of existing frameworks to predict emergent audience behaviors or optimize cross-channel messaging strategies in environments characterized by high-volume, unstructured data (e.g., social media, streaming platforms, and interactive ad exchanges). To overcome these limitations, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling simulations and machine learning pipelines tailored to analyze terabytes of heterogeneous communication data. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for sentiment and thematic analysis of user-generated content, graph neural networks to map information diffusion across networks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to simulate adaptive audience responses under varying campaign conditions. By leveraging parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated model training, the project aims to identify patterns in engagement dynamics, predict viral messaging thresholds, and test crisis communication strategies in synthetic yet realistic scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for real-time campaign optimization, validated against historical case studies from corporate and nonprofit communication contexts. The findings will advance theoretical understanding of nonlinear communication effects in digital ecosystems while providing practitioners with evidence-based tools to allocate resources efficiently, mitigate reputational risks, and maximize message resonance in increasingly fragmented media landscapes. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in addressing complex, data-driven challenges unique to modern organizational communication research.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_title: Public Relations, Advertising, and Applied Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in organizational communication, public relations, and advertising, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the biomechanical and optical interactions of the human eye under various pathological and therapeutic conditions, with the goal of advancing personalized interventions for complex visual disorders. A key challenge in optometry is predicting patient-specific responses to treatments such as specialty contact lenses, corneal reshaping therapies, or intraocular pressure management strategies for glaucoma. Current clinical tools lack the resolution to capture subtle biomechanical changes in ocular tissues or simulate dynamic light propagation through irregular optical surfaces. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale finite element models of corneal deformation, fluid-structure interaction simulations of aqueous humor dynamics, and Monte Carlo ray-tracing algorithms for personalized optical systems. These models will integrate patient data from corneal topography, optical coherence tomography, and intraoperative pressure sensors, requiring parallelized processing of multi-terabyte datasets. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize model parameters and identify predictive biomarkers of treatment efficacy. The computational pipeline will be validated against clinical outcomes from a longitudinal cohort of 500 patients with keratoconus, post-LASIK ectasia, and primary open-angle glaucoma. Successful implementation will enable the creation of open-source simulation tools for optimizing contact lens designs, refining laser therapy protocols, and forecasting disease progression patterns. This work directly aligns with the program's focus on advancing evidence-based optometric practice by bridging gaps between clinical observation, biomechanical theory, and therapeutic innovation. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the nonlinear, multi-physics nature of ocular simulations, which exceed the capacity of local workstations in both computational intensity and memory requirements. Outcomes will contribute to precision optometry paradigms while providing trainees with hands-on experience in computational vision science methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of optometry and that focuses on the principles and techniques for examining, diagnosing and treating conditions of the visual system. Includes instruction in prescribing glasses and contact lenses, other optical aids, corrective therapies, patient counseling, physician referral, practice management, and ethics and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance nursing science through the analysis of complex, multidimensional healthcare datasets. The research problem centers on optimizing clinical decision-making and patient outcomes in high-acuity care settings, where heterogeneous data—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time physiological monitoring streams, genomic profiles, and patient-reported outcomes—create computational challenges for predictive modeling and intervention design. Current methods struggle to integrate these data types at scale, limiting the ability to identify patterns in patient deterioration, treatment responsiveness, and care-delivery inefficiencies. To address this, the project proposes a computational workflow combining machine learning (ML) and simulation-based approaches. EHR data will be preprocessed using natural language processing (NLP) to extract latent clinical features from unstructured notes, while time-series physiological data will undergo feature engineering for integration with genomic and demographic variables. Federated learning frameworks will be employed to train predictive models for sepsis onset and pressure injury risk across distributed datasets, preserving patient privacy. Agent-based modeling will simulate nurse-patient interactions and workflow scenarios to evaluate the impact of staffing ratios and intervention protocols on care quality. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources for parallelized model training, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and real-time simulation ensembles. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive tools for early clinical deterioration, (2) a scalable framework for multimodal data integration in nursing research, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for staffing and workflow redesign. By enabling rapid analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, HPC access will directly support the development of precision nursing interventions, reduce computational bottlenecks in hypothesis testing, and accelerate the translation of findings into clinical practice. This work aligns with national priorities to reduce healthcare disparities through data-driven innovation, positioning nursing science at the forefront of computational health research.
cip_definition: A research program that focuses on the study of advanced clinical practices, research methodologies, the administration of complex nursing services, and that prepares nurses to further the progress of nursing research through experimentation and clinical applications.

abstract: Histologic analysis remains a cornerstone of disease diagnosis, yet the increasing complexity of multi-scale imaging data—spanning light microscopy, electron microscopy, and multiplex immunohistochemistry—poses significant challenges for manual interpretation. Current workflows struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets efficiently, leading to subjective variability and delayed diagnostic outcomes. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and high-performance computing (HPC) to automate the identification of tissue microstructures and subcellular biomarkers across heterogeneous imaging modalities. The research focuses on creating deep learning models capable of correlating ultrastructural features from electron microscopy with functional tissue characteristics, enabling real-time detection of subtle pathological anomalies. Key computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale imaging datasets, optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for multi-resolution feature extraction, and implementing generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize rare pathological samples for training augmentation. The HPC resources will be critical for parallelized training of 3D CNN architectures, dynamic storage of annotated imaging repositories, and validation of model generalizability across diverse tissue types. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for automated histologic quantification, reducing diagnostic turnaround times by 40–60% in preliminary pilot studies, and novel insights into understudied extracellular matrix biomarkers linked to early-stage fibrosis. By integrating ML with advanced histotechnological methods, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for precision histopathology, directly addressing gaps in diagnostic reproducibility while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational scientists and histotechnologists. The tools developed will be validated against gold-standard manual annotations from certified histotechnologists, ensuring clinical relevance and adherence to ethical standards for AI-assisted diagnostics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, at the request of physicians, researchers, and laboratory scientists, to identify tissue structures and cell components and relate these findings to physiological functions and to the detection and diagnosis of diseases and other abnormalities. Includes instruction in medical chemistry, histochemistry, biochemistry, anatomy, physiology, medical informatics, applied mathematics, electron microscopy, instrumentation, quality control procedures, data recording and analysis, laboratory administration, medical terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cultural dynamics, environmental change, and societal decision-making across historical and contemporary contexts through an integrative computational framework. The research problem centers on understanding how complex, nonlinear interactions among cultural narratives, ecological pressures, and institutional structures shape human behavior and collective outcomes—a challenge requiring analysis of heterogeneous datasets spanning archaeology, environmental science, political philosophy, and digital humanities. Current methodologies struggle to reconcile the scale and diversity of relevant data or model emergent phenomena arising from cross-domain feedback loops. To address this, we propose deploying high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop agent-based models simulating decision-making processes in resource-constrained environments, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for analyzing historical texts and oral histories. These computational methods will be integrated with geospatial analysis of environmental data and network-based approaches to trace the evolution of cultural ideas. The agent-based models will parameterize agents using behavioral patterns extracted from ethnographic records and sociological surveys, enabling large-scale simulations of societal responses to environmental stressors. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the scale of these simulations, which involve thousands of agents interacting across multi-layered networks, and for processing terabyte-scale corpora of digitized historical documents. Expected outcomes include novel insights into resilience strategies adopted by past and present societies, identification of cultural-institutional configurations that promote sustainable resource use, and open-access tools for interdisciplinary data integration. This work will advance methodological innovation in digital humanities by demonstrating how computational modeling can bridge qualitative and quantitative approaches, while contributing actionable knowledge for addressing contemporary challenges at the intersection of cultural preservation and environmental stewardship.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences/ Liberal Studies
cip_definition: A program that is a structured combination of the arts, biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities, emphasizing breadth of study. Includes instruction in independently designed, individualized, or regular programs.

abstract: Genetic counseling faces a critical challenge in accurately interpreting complex genomic data to assess disease risk and guide patient decisions. Current clinical tools often rely on simplified models that prioritize single-gene or panel-based analyses, neglecting the cumulative effects of structural variants, epigenetic modifiers, and polygenic interactions. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to integrate multi-omics data—including whole-genome sequencing, methylation profiles, and chromatin accessibility data—with clinical histories to improve risk prediction for hereditary conditions such as cardiomyopathies and neurodevelopmental disorders. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale genomic datasets from diverse populations, train ensemble models to identify combinatorial genetic and epigenetic risk factors, and simulate population-specific variant penetrance. Computational workflows will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, GPU-accelerated deep learning for feature selection, and distributed computing for genome-wide association meta-analyses. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model that quantifies multifactorial risk with higher precision than existing clinical tools, (2) identification of novel regulatory elements or structural variants contributing to variable expressivity in understudied populations, and (3) an open-access decision-support toolkit for genetic counselors to generate patient-specific risk visualizations. By bridging gaps between genomic complexity and clinical interpretability, this work aims to empower counselors to address inequities in variant interpretation, reduce diagnostic odysseys for rare diseases, and personalize preventive care recommendations. The HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the project’s computational demands, including petabyte-scale data storage, parallelized model training across >10,000 genomes, and real-time sensitivity analyses during patient consultations.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel patients and families concerning inherited genetic disorders and diseases; assess risk factors and planning options associated with potential and actual inherited conditions; and serve as patient advocates and provide referral services in relation to private and public support services. Includes instruction in clinical/medical genetics, methods of genetic testing, interviewing and counseling skills, genetic and support services delivery, principles of public health, medical ethics, law and regulations, patient advocacy, and professional standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Mongolian linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in digital methodologies for under-resourced languages. The primary research problem centers on the lack of scalable tools for analyzing Mongolian’s complex morphology, dialectal variations, and historical texts, which hinder large-scale philological studies and applications in natural language processing (NLP). Current approaches rely on manual annotation or limited datasets, constraining insights into linguistic evolution, cross-dialectal patterns, and the preservation of oral traditions. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline integrating machine learning (ML) models, corpus linguistics, and optical character recognition (OCR) tailored for Classical and Modern Mongolian scripts. The first phase involves training transformer-based models on a curated multilingual corpus of digitized texts (spanning 13th–20th centuries) to automate morphological segmentation, syntactic parsing, and dialect classification. Concurrently, OCR models will be optimized for historical manuscripts using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to handle non-standardized orthographies and degraded materials. The second phase applies these tools to analyze semantic shifts in literary motifs across time and regions, linking linguistic features to sociocultural contexts. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of text and image data, training deep learning architectures with parallelized workflows, and running large-scale simulations of language change. Expected outcomes include open-access digital lexicons, annotated corpora, and adaptive NLP frameworks for Mongolian, enabling novel research on language contact, literary canon formation, and pedagogical tools for language revitalization. By bridging computational linguistics with traditional philology, this project aims to establish a replicable infrastructure for studying non-dominant languages while expanding interdisciplinary connections between humanities scholarship and advanced computing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Mongolian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; oral and written literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in safeguarding human health under the extreme and dynamic conditions of air and space travel, where crews and passengers are exposed to unique stressors such as microgravity, radiation, prolonged confinement, and rapid shifts in atmospheric pressure. Current clinical models for predicting and mitigating health risks in these environments lack the resolution to account for complex, interacting physiological and psychological variables. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating cardiovascular, neurocognitive, and immune system responses to simulate human adaptability and resilience during long-duration space missions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these dynamics at scale, coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of hemodynamic changes in microgravity with agent-based simulations of stress-induced cognitive performance decline. Machine learning algorithms will analyze multimodal datasets from astronaut biometrics, environmental sensors, and ground-based analogs to identify early biomarkers of decompensation. Additionally, the project will simulate emergency medical scenarios—such as trauma management in partial gravity or pharmacological interventions under altered pharmacokinetics—to optimize protocols for autonomous healthcare delivery. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated workflows for real-time parameter optimization and probabilistic risk assessment. Expected outcomes include predictive models of crew health degradation, validated countermeasures for mission-critical tasks, and adaptive guidelines for medical system design in next-generation spacecraft. By quantifying interactions between physiological thresholds and environmental variables, this work will advance clinical strategies to enhance crew safety, mission success, and passenger well-being in commercial spaceflight. The HPC infrastructure will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling human-environment interactions, with translational applications for terrestrial aviation medicine and extreme-environment healthcare.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the safety and diagnostic accuracy of multi-modal medical imaging through advanced computational modeling and optimization. Current clinical imaging protocols for x-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and ultrasound systems rely on generalized parameters that may not account for patient-specific anatomical variability or optimize the trade-offs between image quality and radiation dose (for ionizing modalities). To address this, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to simulate and optimize imaging parameters across these modalities. The research will focus on three aims: (1) creating patient-specific digital phantoms using generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on anonymized clinical CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets; (2) implementing Monte Carlo simulations for x-ray/gamma-ray transport and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) models for ultrasound and MRI field interactions; and (3) deploying deep reinforcement learning algorithms to identify optimal imaging protocols that minimize radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic utility. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallel processing to manage stochastic simulations across diverse anatomical models and imaging scenarios. Expected outcomes include validated protocol optimization pipelines capable of reducing patient dose by 20-40% in radiographic exams without compromising diagnostic value, along with open-source tools for simulating hybrid imaging systems. This work directly supports radiation safety advancements in diagnostic radiology and provides a foundation for personalized imaging approaches. The scale of data processing (>1 PB of simulated imaging studies) and complexity of coupled physical models necessitate access to HPC resources with GPU-accelerated nodes, high-memory capacity, and parallel file systems to achieve clinically relevant turnaround times for protocol validation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnostic applications of x-rays, gamma rays from sealed sources, ultrasonic radiation, and magnetic resonance; and in the use of equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in high-volume, complex document processing workflows by developing and optimizing computational models for next-generation word processing systems. While conventional word processors excel at basic tasks, they struggle with scalability, real-time collaboration on large documents, and integration of advanced features such as context-aware formatting or AI-driven content optimization—particularly in technical domains requiring precise formatting (e.g., code documentation, engineering reports, or mathematical manuscripts). To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize and accelerate core word processing operations, including dynamic rendering of multi-user edits, automated semantic analysis for error detection, and large-scale template optimization. Our approach combines distributed computing frameworks with machine learning models trained on technical document corpora to enable real-time processing of documents exceeding 1,000 pages with embedded multimedia, cross-references, and collaborative annotations. Key computational challenges include minimizing latency during concurrent editing sessions, optimizing memory allocation for heterogeneous document elements, and developing GPU-accelerated natural language processing pipelines for style consistency checks. By simulating user interaction patterns and document complexity scenarios on HPC clusters, we aim to create a proof-of-concept architecture that reduces processing delays by 40–60% compared to existing solutions while maintaining sub-millisecond response times for critical operations. The outcomes will directly benefit technical fields requiring robust documentation tools, such as software development and academic publishing, while providing a framework for integrating AI-assisted writing features without compromising performance. This work will also generate open-source benchmarks for evaluating computational efficiency in word processing systems, addressing a significant gap in language-driven HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform text typing, table construction, and document formatting tasks on personal computers at a high rate of accuracy and proficiency. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, word processor operation, textual draft interpretation, audio and tape dictation, and specific word processing program software.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-dependent decision-making in rodents, with a focus on how dynamic interactions between prefrontal cortex and basal ganglia networks modulate behavioral flexibility. A critical gap persists in understanding how real-time, population-level neural activity integrates sensory cues, internal states, and learned associations to drive adaptive choices—a process frequently impaired in Parkinson’s disease and obsessive-compulsive disorder. To address this, we propose a computational neuroscience approach combining large-scale spiking neural network (SNN) simulations with analysis of in vivo electrophysiological and calcium imaging datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model networks of >100,000 neurons incorporating biophysically realistic dopamine-dependent plasticity rules, while simultaneously optimizing parameters against experimental recordings from behaving animals. The SNN architecture will replicate multiregional connectivity derived from viral tracing studies and incorporate activity-dependent fMRI signatures to bridge cellular and systems-level dynamics. Parallelized parameter sweeps will identify circuit configurations that reproduce behavioral phenotypes observed during probabilistic reward tasks. Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will process terabytes of spike-sorting and imaging data to detect state-specific oscillatory motifs and project neural trajectories into low-dimensional manifolds. By iteratively aligning model outputs with empirical data, we aim to establish how cortico-striatal communication gates exploratory versus exploitative actions through phase-amplitude coupling mechanisms. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational framework linking synaptic plasticity rules to network-level decision-making processes, 2) predictive models of how dopaminergic depletion alters computational hierarchies in disease states, and 3) open-source tools for simulating large-scale neural circuits with clinically translatable biomarkers. This work will advance fundamental knowledge of brain-behavior relationships while providing a platform to virtually test neuromodulation strategies for neuropsychiatric disorders.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to address computational bottlenecks in the creation and optimization of dynamic, high-resolution visual content for emerging graphic communications platforms. As demand grows for immersive, real-time media in areas such as augmented reality (AR) advertising, interactive digital publications, and adaptive branding systems, existing workflows struggle to process complex vector-raster hybrid assets at scale. The research focuses on developing parallelizable algorithms for intelligent asset optimization, leveraging machine learning to automate format conversion, resolution scaling, and color space harmonization across multi-device ecosystems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of industry-standard design files (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite outputs) and for simulating rendering performance across heterogeneous end-user hardware configurations. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic quality-of-service predictions with graph-based representations of design element interdependencies, enabling predictive optimization before asset deployment. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for automated graphic system adaptability, reducing manual rework in cross-platform publishing by an estimated 40-60% based on preliminary benchmarks. This work directly responds to industry needs identified through partnerships with digital media publishers and AR development studios, who require scalable solutions for maintaining visual fidelity across increasingly fragmented display technologies. The requested computing resources will enable comparative analysis of optimization strategies at unprecedented parameter scales, particularly for temporal design elements in motion graphics. By establishing computational best practices for next-generation graphic workflows, this project aims to bridge persistent gaps between creative production pipelines and technical deployment constraints in communication design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in graphic communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of syntactic and morphological patterns in historical and contemporary Czech literary texts. Despite the growing availability of digitized Czech corpora, large-scale investigations into linguistic evolution and stylistic variation remain constrained by the computational demands of processing complex, morphologically rich structures across centuries of texts. The research will focus on two interrelated problems: (1) quantifying syntactic shifts in Czech prose from the National Revival period (late 18th–19th centuries) to post-1989 literature, and (2) modeling dialectal influences on morphological choices in regional narratives. Computational workflows will integrate rule-based morphological analyzers with transformer-based language models (e.g., Czech BERT variants) to disambiguate lexical and grammatical features at scale. Parallelized pipelines will process approximately 10TB of text data, employing distributed computing for frequency analysis, dependency parsing, and temporal clustering. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive diachronic profile of Czech syntactic complexity, a geolocated dataset linking morphological trends to regional dialects, and open-source tools optimized for Czech literary analysis. These resources will directly support philological research on language standardization processes while providing methodological frameworks applicable to under-resourced Slavic languages. The project addresses critical gaps in Czech linguistic scholarship by enabling data-driven inquiry into literature’s role in shaping national identity, with broader implications for computational humanities methodologies in morphologically complex languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of edge computing environments, characterized by heterogeneous hardware, fluctuating resource availability, and stringent latency requirements, presents a critical challenge for adaptive runtime systems. Traditional static resource allocation strategies fail to dynamically optimize performance under these conditions, leading to suboptimal utilization and energy inefficiency. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven runtime framework that autonomously adjusts computational resource allocation, task scheduling, and power management in real time for edge devices operating in dynamic, resource-constrained settings. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale edge networks with varying topologies, workloads, and hardware configurations. Computational methods will include the design of lightweight reinforcement learning models trained on synthetic and real-world IoT workload traces, coupled with discrete-event simulations to evaluate system behavior under stochastic network conditions. Key innovations include a hybrid architecture that balances centralized coordination with decentralized decision-making and a novel metric for quantifying the trade-offs between latency, energy consumption, and hardware wear.
