Expected outcomes include an open-source framework demonstrating ≥20% improvement in energy efficiency and ≤15% reduction in task completion time variance compared to state-of-the-art schedulers across simulated manufacturing and smart city use cases. The HPC component is essential for validating scalability across 10,000+ node configurations and stress-testing fault tolerance mechanisms under simulated hardware failures. This work bridges gaps between embedded systems programming, distributed systems theory, and machine learning operations (MLOps), offering a programmable foundation for next-generation edge computing infrastructures while advancing methodologies for self-optimizing systems in transient computational environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general writing and implementation of generic and customized programs to drive operating systems and that generally prepares individuals to apply the methods and procedures of software design and programming to software installation and maintenance. Includes instruction in software design, low- and high-level languages and program writing; program customization and linking; prototype testing; troubleshooting; and related aspects of operating systems and networks.

abstract: Understanding the multi-scale interactions between soil minerals, organic matter, fluid dynamics, and microbial activity is critical for advancing sustainable soil management practices. However, experimental approaches alone struggle to capture the complexity of these processes, particularly across spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to integrate molecular-scale simulations, pore-scale fluid dynamics modeling, and machine learning to predict soil behavior under varying agricultural management scenarios. The primary research problem centers on quantifying how soil amendments and environmental stressors influence nutrient retention, water permeability, and carbon sequestration in heterogeneous soil matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of ion exchange and organic-mineral interactions at atomic resolution, coupled with 3D lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) simulations of water and solute transport in digitally reconstructed soil pore networks. These simulations will parameterize machine learning models trained to predict macroscale soil properties, such as hydraulic conductivity and cation exchange capacity, using inputs from molecular and pore-scale data. The computational workflow requires parallelized GPU-accelerated MD simulations (via GROMACS or LAMMPS), high-memory nodes for LBM-based fluid dynamics (Palabos), and distributed training of neural networks (TensorFlow/PyTorch) on heterogeneous soil datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking soil amendment chemistry to water-nutrient dynamics, validated against experimental X-ray tomography and spectroscopy data. This work will advance mechanistic models of soil biogeochemical cycles, directly informing strategies to optimize soil fertility, mitigate nutrient leaching, and enhance climate resilience in agricultural systems. By bridging atomic-scale processes to field-scale outcomes, the project will provide a scalable computational toolkit for soil scientists, reducing reliance on resource-intensive empirical trials. The requested HPC resources will enable the high-throughput simulations and data integration necessary to address these computationally demanding, multi-disciplinary challenges.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution and cross-jurisdictional influence of medieval religious legal systems, with a focus on understudied canonical traditions outside the Roman Catholic mainstream. While canonical studies traditionally emphasize textual analysis of ecclesiastical decrees, this project addresses a gap in computational approaches to modeling how non-Roman canon laws—such as those of the Armenian Apostolic Church, Coptic Orthodox Church, and Syriac Christian communities—developed networked relationships with secular legal systems and neighboring religious traditions. The core challenge lies in processing fragmentary, multilingual primary sources (Syriac, Armenian, Ge‘ez, and Arabic) spanning the 6th–14th centuries, which require advanced optical character recognition (OCR) correction, semantic tagging, and spatial-temporal alignment. The computational methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource historical languages with graph neural networks to reconstruct legal influence networks. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on canonical corpora to detect intertextual legal citations, developing a geospatial database of legal dissemination nodes, and simulating the diffusion of norms through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) the first quantitative map of cross-cultural legal borrowing between Eastern Christian canon laws and Islamic fiqh systems in medieval Anatolia and Mesopotamia, 2) a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking canonical provisions to socio-political contexts of enforcement, and 3) novel metrics for measuring the "resilience" of religious legal principles under shifting political regimes. By integrating computational historiography with canon law studies, this work aims to establish a framework for analyzing legal pluralism in premodern religious societies while advancing digital humanities methodologies for non-Latin script historical texts. The scale of data processing—requiring parallelized OCR of 50,000+ manuscript images, alignment of heterogeneous temporal taxonomies, and graph computations across ~1 billion potential node relationships—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime for iterative model training and large-scale network analysis.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the history, theology, and philosophy of religious, church, and ecclesiastical law and that prepares individuals to serve as professional canonists.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in modeling large-scale, algorithmically generated musical compositions and analyzing their structural coherence. Current approaches to automated music generation and analysis often rely on simplified harmonic or rhythmic models, which struggle to capture the complexity of human-composed works—particularly in advanced domains such as polyphonic counterpoint, spectral harmony, or real-time improvisation systems. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework that integrates symbolic AI (for rule-based tonal and formal structures) with machine learning models (trained on diverse corpora of 20th-21st century art music) to simulate and evaluate compositional processes. The core research problem involves optimizing these models to operate across multiple temporal scales, from micro-level timbral manipulations to macro-formal development, while maintaining auditive plausibility and stylistic consistency. HPC resources will be critical for three components: (1) parallelized training of transformer-based architectures on high-resolution MIDI and audio datasets encompassing complex orchestral textures; (2) real-time rendering of physically modeled instrument interactions in virtual ensembles; and (3) evolutionary algorithms for stress-testing harmonic progressions against psychoacoustic constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for computational music theory research, a repository of algorithmically generated works demonstrating previously undocumented harmonic-contrapuntal configurations, and quantitative metrics for assessing computational creativity in music systems. By enabling the synthesis and analysis of music at unprecedented complexity levels, this work aims to advance both pedagogical tools for composition students and methodological frameworks for studying emergent musical structures through computational means.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the principles of sound manipulation as applied to the creation of music, and the techniques of creating and arranging music. Includes instruction in aural theory, melody, counterpoint, complex harmony, modulation, chromatics, improvisation, progressions, musical writing, instrumentation, orchestration, electronic and computer applications, studies of specific musical styles, and development of original creative ability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on the cultural and social dynamics of Ukrainian identity formation as reflected in 20th-century literary and archival materials. The research problem centers on the understudied interplay between state-driven narratives and grassroots cultural expressions in Soviet and post-Soviet Ukraine, particularly how these interactions shaped regional identities in contested border zones. Current scholarship relies heavily on manual analysis of limited textual corpora, leaving critical gaps in understanding the scale, diffusion, and evolution of identity markers across time and space. This project will computationally analyze a curated corpus of 50,000+ Ukrainian-language texts (novels, poetry, samvydav publications, and regional newspapers) spanning 1920–2000, integrating previously fragmented archival collections from seven institutions. Using natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical Ukrainian lexicography and transformer-based models fine-tuned on domain-specific data, we will map semantic shifts in identity-related terminology, trace intertextual networks across genres, and quantify regional variations in cultural production. HPC resources are essential for training custom word embeddings on heterogeneous textual data (including OCR-corrected scans and handwritten manuscript transcriptions), running large-scale topic modeling across temporal slices, and simulating information diffusion patterns under different sociopolitical constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal visualization platform documenting centripetal and centrifugal forces in Ukrainian cultural identity, 2) quantitative evidence challenging monolithic interpretations of Soviet-era cultural policies, and 3) new methodologies for computational analysis of non-Russian Slavic linguistic heritage. The work will directly support emerging digital humanities initiatives in Ukrainian studies while providing scalable tools for underrepresented language communities in cultural analytics. Resource requests focus on GPU-accelerated workloads for deep learning tasks and parallelized processing of multi-terabyte textual datasets.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced commercial photography workflows, particularly in processing high-resolution imagery, simulating complex lighting environments, and integrating machine learning (ML) for artistic enhancement. As commercial photographers increasingly adopt 8K-resolution imaging, multi-sensor capture systems, and AI-driven post-processing tools, existing consumer-grade hardware struggles to manage the scale, speed, and precision required for iterative creative exploration. The research problem centers on bridging this technical gap to enable novel artistic methodologies while maintaining practical production timelines. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize pipelines for three core applications: (1) parallel rendering of photorealistic 3D product visualizations using physics-based light transport simulations, (2) training generative adversarial networks (GANs) on terabyte-scale image datasets to automate context-aware retouching and style transfer, and (3) real-time fusion of multi-spectral imaging data for augmented reality (AR) previsualization systems. Computational methods will include distributed rendering via ray-tracing engines, GPU-accelerated ML model training with PyTorch, and OpenCL-based image stacking algorithms. Expected outcomes include a framework for scalable hybrid photography (combining physical captures with synthetic elements), quantifiable reductions in processing latency for high-bit-depth composites, and open-source tools to democratize HPC access in photography education. By enabling complex computational workflows previously inaccessible to individual artists and small studios, this research aims to expand the creative possibilities of commercial photography while contributing new benchmarks for computational efficiency in visual arts applications. The project will directly support curriculum development in computational photography and provide case studies for integrating HPC resources into media production pipelines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of predicting and modeling the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) through advanced computational approaches. Despite advances in early detection, OSCC prognosis remains highly variable due to the complex interplay of tumor microenvironment heterogeneity, genomic instability, and host immune responses. Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multiscale biological processes driving tumor evolution, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics data and simulate disease mechanisms. The research will employ a hybrid computational framework combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data with spatially resolved proteomic profiles from clinical biopsy samples. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to identify predictive signatures of metastasis and treatment resistance. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate cell-cell interactions within tumor-immune ecosystems, parameterized by patient-derived data. These computational workflows require massive parallelization for parameter optimization, 3D spatial reconstruction of tumor architectures, and probabilistic inference across terabyte-scale datasets. The integration of HPC resources will enable the creation of a scalable digital twin platform to test personalized therapeutic strategies in silico. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for risk stratification, predictive models of therapeutic response, and mechanistic insights into immune evasion pathways. This work will provide a paradigm for computationally driven precision oncology in oral cancers, with implications for clinical trial design and real-time adaptive treatment planning. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between molecular discovery and clinical translation in head and neck oncology, ultimately improving survival rates and quality of life for patients with advanced OSCC.
cip_title: Advanced/ Graduate Dentistry and Oral Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in advanced/graduate dentistry and oral sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance precision in large animal surgical and medical interventions through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address high morbidity rates linked to postoperative complications in food animals and equines. Despite advancements in veterinary care, variability in patient outcomes persists due to complex interactions between species-specific anatomy, metabolic demands, and disease pathophysiology. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized protocols, which inadequately account for individual biomechanical, physiological, and genomic factors. To bridge this gap, we propose developing species-specific multiscale models integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for biomechanical stress prediction during surgical procedures, machine learning (ML)-enabled risk stratification using retrospective electronic health records (n > 50,000 cases), and genomic variant analysis to identify biomarkers associated with recovery trajectories. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of high-resolution imaging data (CT/MRI), whole-genome sequencing datasets, and real-time sensor data from wearable monitoring devices deployed in perioperative care. Computational workflows will be optimized using GPU-accelerated frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) for ML model training and ANSYS for FEA simulations. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing surgical planning (e.g., orthopedic implant design in equines, cesarean section protocols in dairy cattle) and personalized analgesia/anesthesia regimens. This work will establish open-access computational pipelines tailored to veterinary applications, directly addressing critical gaps in food animal and equine medicine. By reducing complication rates through data-driven precision, the project aims to improve welfare in production and sport animals while mitigating economic losses linked to prolonged recovery. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the computational burden of multimodal data integration and deliver scalable, translatable solutions for clinical veterinary practice.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Large Animal/ Food Animal and Equine Surgery and Medicine
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the internal medicine and invasive and noninvasive treatment of herd, work, sport, and food animals. Includes instruction in equine medicine, swine and dairy medicine, food animal medicine, pathophysiology, large animal diseases, large animal anesthesiology and surgical procedures, preoperative and postoperative care, and specific medical specialties such as dentistry, ophthalmology, oncology, obstetrics/theriogenology, and orthopedics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics and textual analysis in Vietnamese language studies. While Vietnamese is spoken by over 90 million people globally, computational tools tailored to its tonal, syntactic, and dialectal complexity remain underdeveloped compared to widely studied languages like English. This gap hinders large-scale analysis of historical and contemporary Vietnamese texts, limiting insights into linguistic evolution, sociocultural trends, and regional dialect variation. The project aims to address this by constructing a scalable corpus of Vietnamese texts spanning pre-modern Chữ Nôm scripts to modern digital media, then applying neural language models and phonetic alignment algorithms to analyze linguistic patterns. Key computational challenges include training transformer-based models on non-Latin scripts with diacritics, optimizing grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for six major dialects, and performing diachronic sentiment analysis on literature across political eras. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale text datasets, distributed training of deep learning architectures, and high-memory phonetic alignment tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source NLP tools for Vietnamese dialect classification and historical text normalization, (2) quantitative maps of lexical and semantic shifts in 20th-century literature, and (3) a public corpus with metadata linking linguistic features to sociocultural contexts. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this work will provide new methodologies for preserving endangered dialectal forms, enhance machine learning applications for Vietnamese language technologies, and offer empirically grounded perspectives on how linguistic changes reflect Vietnam’s modern sociohistorical trajectory. The requested resources are critical given the computational intensity of processing tonal embeddings and aligning cross-dialectal speech corpora, tasks infeasible on standard academic infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Vietnamese language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex challenges in Talmudic Studies, a field requiring advanced analysis of multilayered legal, ethical, and philosophical texts. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of Talmudic hermeneutics—specifically, the systematic reconstruction of legal reasoning across dispersed textual loci. Traditional methods of manual comparison struggle to map the interplay of dialectical arguments, cross-references, and historical commentaries spanning centuries. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning (ML) to identify patterns in argumentation, trace conceptual dependencies, and quantify shifts in interpretive methodologies. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on digitized Talmudic texts (e.g., Mishnah, Gemara, and major commentaries) to recognize legal syllogisms and ethical axioms, followed by graph-based network analyses to visualize how specific jurisprudential principles evolve across time and cultural contexts. A parallel focus involves processing high-resolution scans of rare manuscripts to detect marginal annotations and textual variants using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), enabling large-scale comparative studies of scribal traditions. These computational workflows demand significant GPU-accelerated processing for training deep learning models and handling terabytes of unstructured text and image data. The expected outcomes include (1) an open-access digital corpus of annotated Talmudic arguments linked to their philosophical and legal underpinnings, (2) quantitative frameworks for assessing the influence of sociohistorical factors on rabbinic discourse, and (3) novel tools for scholars to simulate hypothetical legal scenarios based on reconstructed hermeneutic principles. By integrating computational rigor with traditional Talmudic scholarship, this project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in religious studies while preserving the intellectual dynamism of rabbinic thought for contemporary ethical and jurisprudential challenges.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize computer-aided design (CAD) and drafting processes for complex, multi-disciplinary engineering projects, with a focus on addressing scalability challenges in parametric modeling and simulation. Current CAD/CADD systems often struggle to efficiently manage high-resolution 3D geometries, dynamic design iterations, and multi-physics simulations—particularly when handling large assemblies or real-time collaborative environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA), automate topology optimization, and accelerate generative design algorithms. The research will employ GPU-accelerated solvers and distributed computing frameworks to enable rapid evaluation of design alternatives under constraints such as material efficiency, structural integrity, and manufacturability. Key computational methods include the development of machine learning models for predictive design validation and the implementation of adaptive meshing techniques to reduce computational overhead in multi-scale simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for cloud-based CAD collaboration, reduced iteration times for complex assemblies, and benchmark data quantifying the relationship between computational resource allocation and design optimization efficiency. This work will directly benefit engineering technology education by providing case studies and workflows that integrate HPC into CAD/CADD curricula, while offering industry-relevant tools for energy-efficient design processes. The resource allocation will support parametric studies involving 10,000+ variable design spaces, real-time rendering of assemblies exceeding 1 million components, and comparative analyses of optimization algorithms. By bridging the gap between conventional CAD workflows and HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish best practices for resource-aware design in engineering technology applications, with potential impacts across manufacturing, architectural systems, and industrial equipment development.
cip_title: CAD/ CADD Drafting and/ or Design Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and advanced computer software and hardware to the creation of graphic representations and simulations in support of engineering projects. Includes instruction in engineering graphics, two-dimensional and three-dimensional engineering design, solids modeling, engineering animation, computer-aided drafting (CAD), computer-aided design (CADD), and auto-CAD techniques.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in understanding the electronic structure and reactivity of transition metal complexes with non-innocent ligands, a class of compounds central to catalytic processes and energy storage applications. These systems exhibit complex multiconfigurational electronic ground states and dynamic ligand-metal interactions that are poorly described by conventional computational methods, limiting predictive design of novel inorganic catalysts. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve short-lived intermediates or disentangle overlapping spectroscopic signatures, necessitating advanced theoretical approaches. This project will employ high-level ab initio calculations, including multireference methods such as CASSCF and NEVPT2, to model electronic states and spin-crossover phenomena in iron- and cobalt-based coordination complexes. Density functional theory (DFT) with hybrid functionals will supplement these calculations for geometry optimizations and thermodynamic analyses. To address solvent and solid-state effects, explicit solvent molecular dynamics simulations and periodic boundary condition models will be implemented. The computational workflow requires significant resources due to the need for large active spaces (up to 18 orbitals), relativistic corrections for heavy atoms, and statistical sampling of configurational space. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into redox-induced ligand non-innocence in catalytic cycles, (2) predictive models for tuning metal-ligand charge transfer transitions via substituent effects, and (3) validation of computed spectroscopic parameters (XAS, EPR) against experimental collaborators’ data. The requested high-performance computing allocation will enable systematic studies across diverse ligand architectures, providing fundamental guidelines for designing air-stable coordination complexes with targeted redox potentials and photophysical properties. This work directly advances inorganic chemistry by bridging gaps between synthetic approaches, quantum mechanical descriptions, and functional material development, with potential applications in sustainable oxidation catalysis and next-generation battery materials.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the elements and their compounds, other than the hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Includes instruction in the characterization and synthesis of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and their bonding, conductivity, and reactive properties; research techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis; and the study of specific compounds, such as transition metals, and compounds composed of inorganic and organic molecules.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dance as a dynamic, embodied cultural practice through computational analysis of large-scale movement datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in dance studies: the lack of scalable methods to systematically analyze and compare movement patterns across diverse dance traditions, populations, and contexts. While qualitative methods remain central to dance scholarship, the increasing availability of motion capture data—drawn from archival recordings, ethnographic fieldwork, and laboratory-based experiments—presents an opportunity to quantitatively model dance movement at unprecedented resolution. However, processing and analyzing these complex, multidimensional datasets requires computational resources beyond typical workstation capacities. This project will develop and implement machine learning pipelines to classify movement signatures, simulate biomechanical constraints in choreographic sequences, and identify latent patterns in cross-cultural dance repertoires. Key computational tasks include training 3D convolutional neural networks on annotated motion capture data, running iterative optimization algorithms for generative choreography models, and conducting high-dimensional statistical analyses of movement variability. These methods will be applied to two case studies: 1) tracing the evolution of rhythmic footwork patterns in Afro-diasporic dance forms, and 2) quantifying the relationship between improvisational structures and physiological load in contemporary dance practice. By integrating HPC-enabled computational techniques with dance ethnography and performance studies, this work aims to produce new frameworks for preserving intangible cultural heritage, inform inclusive dance pedagogy through evidence-based movement analysis, and establish benchmarks for computational dance research. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for dance data visualization, a public repository of processed movement datasets, and novel theoretical insights into the relationship between embodied knowledge and computational modeling in the performing arts.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of understanding how the interplay between painting materials, application techniques, and environmental variables influences the visual and structural outcomes of artworks. Traditional experimental approaches to exploring these relationships are limited by the time, cost, and material waste inherent in physical trials, particularly when examining complex variables such as pigment-binder interactions, drying kinetics, or the impact of brush dynamics on texture. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes the development of a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The framework integrates molecular dynamics simulations to model pigment dispersion and binder chemistry, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate paint application processes (e.g., brushstroke fluidity, impasto techniques), and machine learning (ML) to analyze correlations between process parameters and visual outcomes. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing these computationally intensive simulations, which involve millions of particle interactions and high-resolution spatial-temporal data. Additionally, the project will utilize ML algorithms trained on datasets of historical and experimental paintings to predict the effects of novel material combinations or techniques. Expected outcomes include an open-access predictive tool for artists to virtually test techniques, optimize material usage, and explore unconventional methods without physical constraints. The research will also contribute to a deeper scientific understanding of traditional painting practices, offering insights into the material decisions of historical artists. By bridging computational science and studio practice, this work aims to advance pedagogical tools in visual arts education, support sustainable creative practices through reduced material waste, and foster innovation in contemporary painting methodologies. The scalability of the models developed here may further inform interdisciplinary collaborations at the intersection of art, materials science, and computational design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by the application of paints and related chemical color substances to canvases or other materials. Includes instruction in color and color mixing, surface preparation, composition, oil and acrylic media, watercolor media, painting techniques, and personal style development.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic, multi-objective financial planning strategies under conditions of extreme uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in personalized financial service modeling. Traditional financial planning tools often rely on static assumptions or simplified Monte Carlo simulations, failing to integrate real-time macroeconomic volatility, heterogeneous client risk profiles, and evolving regulatory constraints into adaptive decision pathways. The proposed work will focus on creating an agent-based model that simulates interdependent financial ecosystems, incorporating stochastic market behaviors, client lifecycle events, and nonlinear interactions between tax policies, investment vehicles, and insurance products. Using GPU-accelerated optimization algorithms, the system will process terascale datasets spanning decades of global financial indicators, demographic trends, and crisis events to train deep reinforcement learning agents capable of generating robust, client-specific strategies. Key computational challenges include parallelizing nested risk-reward calculations across thousands of simulated scenarios while maintaining explainable AI outputs for regulatory compliance. The HPC infrastructure will enable real-time sensitivity analyses across 50+ parameters, from interest rate shock scenarios to climate-related market disruptions. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform for stress-testing financial plans against Black Swan events, along with empirical insights into optimal rebalancing thresholds for hybrid human-AI advisory systems. This work aims to establish new benchmarks for computational resilience in financial services, particularly for emerging challenges like cryptocurrency integration and intergenerational wealth transfer in decentralized finance environments. By bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and computational finance, the project will provide practitioners with scalable tools to navigate 21st-century complexity while maintaining fiduciary rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage the financial interests and growth of individuals and institutions. Includes instruction in portfolio management, investment management, estate planning, insurance, tax planning, strategic investing and planning, financial consulting services, and client relations.

abstract: Respiratory care protocols for mechanically ventilated patients rely on generalized guidelines that may not account for dynamic, patient-specific cardiopulmonary interactions. This project proposes to develop a real-time computational framework to optimize ventilator waveform analysis and predictive intervention strategies for critically ill patients with heterogeneous respiratory pathologies. The research problem centers on the limitations of current clinical practices in detecting subtle, subclinical patterns of patient-ventilator dyssynchrony (PVD) and maladaptive gas exchange, which contribute to ventilator-induced lung injury and prolonged weaning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will process high-frequency ventilator waveform data (sampled at 200 Hz) alongside concurrent hemodynamic and capnography signals from a retrospective cohort of 1,200 ICU patients. A hybrid machine learning architecture combining temporal convolutional networks and transformer-based attention mechanisms will be trained to identify latent features predictive of deteriorating compliance, occult air trapping, and regional overdistension. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model patient-specific airway pressure gradients under varying ventilation modes. The HPC environment is essential for managing the 45 TB multimodal dataset, enabling parallel processing of waveform time series, and reducing model training times from estimated 3,200 GPU-hours to feasible workflows. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive algorithm for early PVD detection and a simulation toolkit to test individualized positive end-expiratory pressure titration strategies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges respiratory physiology, critical care medicine, and computational engineering, offering a paradigm shift from population-based thresholds to adaptive, patient-centric ventilation management. Successful implementation could reduce average ventilator days by 18-22% in targeted populations, as projected by preliminary Bayesian network analyses, while establishing a scalable computational framework for real-time critical care decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer general respiratory care procedures under the supervision of respiratory therapists in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in patient data collection and monitoring, airway management, installation of nebulizers and other respiratory assistance devices, application and monitoring of breathing gases, equipment operation and maintenance, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of scopist workflows in legal transcription through advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. Scopists, tasked with editing court reporter transcripts, face challenges in reconciling machine shorthand outputs with contextual legal terminology, particularly in complex or multi-speaker scenarios. Traditional computer-aided transcription (CAT) tools lack adaptive contextual analysis, leading to time-intensive manual corrections. This research addresses the gap by creating domain-specific language models tailored to legal discourse, optimized to identify and resolve ambiguities in real-time stenographic data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will train transformer-based models on a curated corpus of legal transcripts, court opinions, and statutory texts to capture syntactic, semantic, and pragmatic features unique to judicial proceedings. Computational workflows will integrate phonetic alignment algorithms to map stenographic inputs to contextual legal concepts, with parallel processing pipelines to handle multi-channel audio-text synchronization. The proposed system will be evaluated against industry-standard CAT software using metrics for error reduction, processing latency, and usability in instructional settings. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for context-aware legal transcription, benchmark datasets for scopist training, and empirical insights into human-AI collaboration in specialized editorial workflows. By addressing computational bottlenecks in real-time legal language processing, this work aims to establish scalable methods for preserving transcript integrity while reducing cognitive load for scopists, with broader implications for accessibility and precision in judicial record-keeping.
cip_definition: An instructional program that prepares individuals to perform editing and word processing on a court reporter transcript to ensure the accuracy of the transcripts. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcriptioning, machine shorthand, and computer-aided transcription software.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing multimodal transportation networks under dynamic demand and climate resilience constraints, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome computational bottlenecks in large-scale infrastructure modeling. Urbanization and climate change necessitate transportation systems that balance efficiency, safety, and sustainability, yet existing simulation tools struggle to integrate real-time traffic data, freight logistics, and extreme weather impacts at metropolitan scales. The research will develop a parallelized computational framework combining dynamic traffic assignment models, agent-based freight movement simulations, and probabilistic flood-risk analysis. By coupling GPU-accelerated traffic microsimulations with graph neural networks trained on multi-source datasets (e.g., connected vehicle telemetry, IoT sensor feeds, and climate projections), the framework will enable scenario testing of adaptive traffic management policies, infrastructure hardening strategies, and emergency evacuation routing. The HPC environment is essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10^6+ agent interactions across 24-hour periods while maintaining sub-minute temporal resolution. Anticipated outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for evaluating tradeoffs between congestion pricing schemes, electric vehicle charging infrastructure placement, and flood-resistant highway designs. This work will provide state DOTs and metropolitan planning organizations with quantitative metrics to prioritize investments that reduce travel delay by 15-25%, lower transportation-related emissions, and enhance network robustness against 100-year flood events. The computational workflows will be open-sourced to enable replication in diverse geographic contexts, advancing scalable methods for next-generation transportation systems analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems for the physical movement of people, materials and information, including general network design and planning, facilities planning, site evaluation, transportation management systems, needs projections and analysis, and analysis of costs.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impact of quantum computing-driven market microstructure dynamics on financial decision-making under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model emergent trading behaviors in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems. Traditional financial models struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between algorithmic trading agents, liquidity fragmentation across blockchain-based platforms, and real-time risk propagation in markets dominated by quantum-inspired optimization strategies. The research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation framework that integrates quantum annealing techniques with game-theoretic liquidity provision models, calibrated to multi-chain DeFi transaction data. Using HPC clusters, we will simulate order book evolution across synthetic markets under varying quantum computing adoption scenarios, analyzing cascading effects on price discovery, arbitrage opportunities, and systemic stability. Computational experiments will employ hybrid quantum-classical optimization algorithms to resolve high-dimensional portfolio allocation problems in environments with nanosecond latency constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative benchmarks for quantum advantage in dark pool routing efficiency, 2) topology-aware risk metrics for cross-protocol liquidity shocks, and 3) adaptive hedging strategies resilient to quantum-accelerated front-running attacks. By mapping the computational complexity frontier where classical HPC infrastructure intersects with emerging quantum financial technologies, this work aims to establish foundational frameworks for next-generation market surveillance systems while informing regulatory approaches to quantum-ready financial infrastructure. The requested resources will enable large-scale parallelism of market scenario simulations, storage of petabyte-scale limit order book reconstructions, and real-time analysis of quantum circuit optimization patterns across heterogeneous compute architectures.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and analyze the financial and monetary aspects and performance of business enterprises, banking institutions, or other organizations. Includes instruction in principles of accounting, financial instruments, capital planning, funds acquisition, asset and debt management, budgeting, financial analysis, and investments and portfolio management.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in healthcare administrative workflows, particularly in scheduling, communication, and resource coordination, which contribute to operational delays, increased costs, and reduced patient satisfaction. Medical administrative professionals are critical to managing these workflows, yet existing tools often lack the computational power to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., electronic health records, appointment logs, staff communications) required for optimizing decision-making. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that identify bottlenecks in healthcare operations. Using anonymized datasets from partner clinics, we will train machine learning algorithms to forecast patient no-show rates, predict resource utilization conflicts, and model the impact of alternative scheduling protocols. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze communication patterns between administrative staff and clinical teams, identifying inefficiencies in task delegation and urgency prioritization. Agent-based simulations will further test the scalability of proposed workflow adjustments under varying patient volumes and staffing conditions. The computational intensity of processing multi-modal data (structured records, unstructured text, temporal sequences) necessitates HPC infrastructure to enable parallelized model training and real-time simulations. Outcomes will include actionable insights for redesigning administrative protocols, reducing patient wait times, and improving alignment between staffing resources and demand. This work directly supports the training goals of medical administrative professionals by advancing data-driven tools for operational decision-making, while adhering to healthcare privacy regulations and ethical standards. Results will be disseminated through open-source workflow optimization frameworks tailored for non-technical users, ensuring accessibility for healthcare administrators and educators.
cip_title: Medical Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Medical Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing physicians and nurses, health care facilities and services administrators, and other health care professionals. Includes instruction in business and medical communications, medical terminology, principles of health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing personalized care plans for elderly patients with multiple chronic conditions, a population often underrepresented in clinical trials despite their complex healthcare needs. Current approaches to predicting adverse events—such as polypharmacy complications, falls, or hospital readmissions—rely on generalized models that fail to account for the heterogeneity of aging-related physiological changes, social determinants of health, and comorbidities. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models capable of integrating multi-modal geriatric health data, including longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), medication histories, wearable device outputs, and patient-reported outcomes. The computational workflow will involve preprocessing large-scale EHR datasets (spanning 10+ years) to extract geriatric-specific features, followed by training ensemble ML algorithms to identify risk patterns and simulate interventions. Deep learning architectures will be tested for their ability to model temporal relationships in medication adherence and disease progression, while natural language processing (NLP) techniques will parse unstructured clinical notes for social and cognitive risk factors. The HPC environment is essential for managing data volumes (>100 TB), parallelizing hyperparameter tuning across thousands of model iterations, and conducting real-time simulations of care pathway outcomes. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for adverse event risk stratification, optimized medication reconciliation protocols accounting for age-related pharmacokinetic changes, and dynamic care plan recommendations adaptable to individual patient trajectories. By enabling computationally intensive analyses of geriatric-specific datasets, this work will advance evidence-based precision nursing practices, inform policy for aging populations, and reduce preventable complications in vulnerable elderly patients.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: The increasing frequency of marine heatwaves and shifting nutrient regimes in coastal ecosystems has raised urgent questions about their impacts on microbial community dynamics and biogeochemical cycling. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of how these stressors alter microbial metabolic networks and carbon export efficiency in temperate and polar coastal systems. We propose a high-resolution, trait-based modeling framework to simulate microbial community interactions, metabolic plasticity, and organic matter remineralization across multiple spatial scales (1 km to 10 m resolution). The model will integrate multi-omics datasets from ongoing field campaigns in the Gulf of Maine and Antarctic Peninsula with hydrodynamic and biogeochemical observations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve (1) submesoscale physical-biological coupling using a nested-grid approach within the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS), and (2) genome-informed flux balance analysis of microbial functional guilds under varying temperature and dissolved organic carbon regimes. Anticipated computational requirements include 200,000 core-hours monthly for ensemble simulations spanning decadal timescales, with parallelized parameter optimization through Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into climate-driven regime shifts in coastal carbon storage capacity, with particular attention to polar systems where microbial responses remain poorly constrained. The resulting open-source model framework will enable improved projections of marine carbon-climate feedbacks while providing critical benchmarks for international programs like GEOTRACES and the UN Ocean Decade. By quantifying thresholds in microbial resilience, this work directly addresses management needs for coastal ecosystems facing unprecedented environmental change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize additive manufacturing processes for complex, multi-material structures, addressing critical gaps in process reliability and material efficiency. Current approaches struggle to predict thermo-mechanical distortions and interfacial defects in heterogeneous material systems due to the interplay of rapid phase changes, residual stresses, and anisotropic thermal gradients. To overcome these limitations, the research will implement a coupled finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) model, integrated with machine learning (ML)-driven parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve micron-scale melt pool dynamics and layer-wise stress accumulation across macro-scale geometries, which require parallelized simulations across millions of elements. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for thermal-fluid interactions and distributed memory architectures for stochastic defect propagation analysis. Key outcomes include predictive models for defect formation under varying process parameters (e.g., laser power, scan speed) and a generative design tool to recommend material-specific printing strategies. Successful validation against experimental tomography and strain gauge data will establish a benchmark for virtual process certification. By reducing trial-and-error iterations in industrial settings, this work aims to lower energy consumption by 15–20% in metal additive manufacturing and enable reliable production of load-bearing components with embedded sensors. The proposed framework will be disseminated as open-source modules to support workforce training in advanced manufacturing technologies, aligning with national priorities for sustainable industrial innovation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of decentralized, multi-agent quantum-thermal systems (QTS) in hybrid energy networks—an emerging niche at the intersection of quantum engineering, thermodynamics, and distributed systems. Current approaches to managing thermal and quantum energy flows in microgrids remain siloed, relying on classical optimization methods ill-suited for real-time coordination of quantum-enhanced devices (e.g., coherent heat pumps, superconducting sensors) with conventional infrastructure. The research problem centers on overcoming scalability bottlenecks in modeling dynamic interactions between quantum and classical subsystems, which exhibit nonlinear, high-dimensional behavior under fluctuating loads. The computational approach integrates tensor network simulations of quantum thermal states with graph-based reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize energy distribution across hybrid networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for training graph-RL agents on large-scale parametric sweeps of QTS configurations (10^4–10^5 nodes) and for executing parallelized density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations to capture entanglement-driven thermal transport. Expected outcomes include an open-source library for adaptive QTS control, validated against experimental data from collaborating labs, and generalized protocols for minimizing entropy generation in heterogeneous energy systems. This work aims to establish foundational principles for engineering quantum-aware thermal networks, with potential applications in precision manufacturing, quantum data center cooling, and grid resilience. The project bridges gaps between quantum thermodynamics and distributed control theory, advancing a new paradigm for sustainable energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to solve a wide variety of practical problems in industry, social organization, public works, and commerce. Includes instruction in undifferentiated and individualized programs in engineering.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the design and optimization of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC-R) systems through high-fidelity computational modeling, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current HVAC-R systems face challenges in balancing energy efficiency, thermal comfort, and environmental impact, particularly under dynamic operating conditions and diverse climatic scenarios. Traditional experimental approaches and low-resolution simulations are insufficient for capturing the complex, multi-physics interactions—including turbulent fluid flow, conjugate heat transfer, and refrigerant phase change—that govern system performance. This project will employ HPC to conduct large-scale, transient simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) techniques. High-resolution models of heat exchangers, compressors, and airflow distribution networks will be developed to analyze energy losses, refrigerant behavior, and component-level stresses. Parallelized solvers will enable parametric studies of system configurations under variable loads, while ML-driven surrogate models will accelerate the exploration of design spaces for optimal efficiency. The computational workflow will leverage open-source and commercial software (e.g., OpenFOAM, ANSYS Fluent) scaled across distributed-memory architectures to manage memory-intensive meshes and iterative solvers. Expected outcomes include validated frameworks for predicting system performance with sub-5% error margins relative to experimental data, identification of design modifications to reduce energy consumption by 15–20% in residential HVAC systems, and scalable strategies for integrating low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. By addressing computational bottlenecks in simulating multi-phase flows and system-level interactions, this work will provide actionable insights for sustainable HVAC-R innovation, directly supporting industry efforts to meet decarbonization targets and regulatory standards. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the resolution, throughput, and parametric scope required for these advancements.
cip_title: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, and heating systems. Includes instruction in principles of heating and cooling technology, design and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, installation and operation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize animal grooming practices through biomechanical and behavioral modeling, addressing gaps in standardized, evidence-based methodologies for diverse species and coat types. Despite the growing demand for specialized pet grooming services, current techniques often rely on anecdotal expertise, leading to variability in outcomes, potential animal stress, and suboptimal coat health. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose to simulate interactions between grooming tools (e.g., clippers, brushes) and biological systems (skin, fur, muscle) across species, integrating data from 3D coat texture scans, physiological stress markers, and behavioral response datasets. Computational models will employ finite element analysis to map tool pressure distribution, machine learning to predict coat matting dynamics, and agent-based modeling to assess animal discomfort thresholds during grooming procedures. The workflow will parallelize simulations across grooming variables (tool type, speed, angle) and biological parameters (coat density, skin sensitivity, species-specific anatomy). Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends grooming protocols tailored to individual animals, minimizing stress while maximizing coat health. This research bridges computational biomechanics and animal care, establishing quantitative metrics for grooming efficacy and safety. By formalizing data-driven guidelines, the project aims to advance professional training standards, reduce industry reliance on trial-and-error practices, and improve welfare outcomes for companion animals. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling high-resolution biological datasets and scaling simulations across the combinatorial space of grooming scenarios, which cannot feasibly be tested in vivo due to ethical and logistical constraints. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and collaborations with grooming certification bodies, fostering innovation in this understudied yet socially impactful domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research, focusing on the dynamic interplay between emerging technologies and the evolution of legal frameworks. The research problem centers on the inadequacy of traditional legal analysis methods to process and interpret the vast, unstructured datasets generated by decentralized technologies (e.g., blockchain-based smart contracts, AI-driven regulatory compliance tools) and their real-world legal implications. Current approaches struggle to model the nonlinear, adaptive interactions between technological systems and legal norms, particularly in cross-jurisdictional contexts. To address this gap, the project proposes a hybrid computational methodology combining natural language processing (NLP), graph-based network analysis, and agent-based modeling. Legal texts (statutes, case law, treaties) and technology governance artifacts (smart contract code, algorithmic audit trails) will be processed using transformer models fine-tuned on legal corpora to extract semantically rich representations of rule structures and obligations. These outputs will inform the construction of multilayer networks mapping relationships between technical systems, legal entities, and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions. Agent-based simulations will then model how perturbations in technological ecosystems—such as protocol upgrades or adversarial exploits—cascade through legal and institutional frameworks. The computational workflow demands HPC resources to handle terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize graph traversals for cross-jurisdictional analysis, and execute high-fidelity simulations at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel framework for quantifying legal adaptability to technological change, 2) predictive models identifying systemic vulnerabilities in tech-law interfaces, and 3) an open-access repository of annotated legal-technical corpora. By enabling granular, data-driven analysis of legal systems as complex adaptive systems, this work aims to inform the design of more resilient governance mechanisms for emergent technologies while establishing computational methods as critical tools in advanced legal studies.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program in one or more of the legal research or advanced practice fields.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multidimensional datasets in fields such as climate science, public health, and materials engineering demands innovative approaches to visual representation that bridge domain-specific knowledge with human perceptual capabilities. Existing visualization frameworks often struggle to balance computational scalability, interactive exploration, and cognitive accessibility when applied to datasets with high dimensionality, temporal granularity, or spatial heterogeneity. This project proposes the development of an adaptive visualization pipeline that integrates perceptual psychology principles with distributed computational architectures to enable real-time rendering of terabyte-scale datasets while optimizing for human pattern recognition. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to implement GPU-accelerated dimensionality reduction algorithms, dynamic tessellation techniques for multiresolution data sampling, and machine learning models trained on eye-tracking data to predict visualization efficacy across user cohorts. Computational workflows will be tested against three interdisciplinary case studies: 1) visualizing microbiome-metabolome interaction networks in inflammatory disease research, 2) rendering multidecadal aerosol dispersion patterns with sub-kilometer spatial resolution, and 3) analyzing real-time sensor arrays from smart material stress tests. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for perception-aware distributed visualization, quantitative metrics for evaluating visualization efficiency relative to computational resource allocation, and novel hybrid rendering techniques that adaptively prioritize visual elements based on both statistical significance and human visual saliency. By co-optimizing computational efficiency and cognitive effectiveness, this work aims to establish new standards for resource-conscious visualization in data-intensive interdisciplinary research, particularly for domains where traditional dimension reduction sacrifices critical contextual relationships.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing architectural designs that integrate adaptive cultural heritage preservation with contemporary urban resilience strategies. The research addresses a critical gap in architectural practice: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to model how historic structures and culturally significant sites can be dynamically preserved while adapting to modern environmental pressures, such as climate change and urbanization. Current approaches often treat preservation and innovation as separate processes, leading to fragmented solutions that fail to balance cultural value with functional sustainability. To address this, the project proposes a novel computational method combining generative design algorithms, agent-based modeling, and multi-objective optimization. These tools will process heterogeneous datasets—including 3D LiDAR scans of historic sites, climate projections, material degradation models, and socio-cultural usage patterns—to generate design alternatives that maximize preservation integrity, energy efficiency, and community utility. HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of real-time simulations that account for nonlinear interactions between structural, environmental, and human factors across multiple temporal scales (decadal weathering, seasonal use patterns, and emergency scenarios). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform enabling architects to test hybrid preservation-adaptation strategies, validated through case studies on UNESCO World Heritage sites facing acute climate threats. The project’s significance lies in advancing architecture’s capacity to serve as an interdisciplinary mediator between cultural memory and futurity, offering scalable methodologies applicable to global heritage challenges. By situating computational power at the intersection of archival precision and speculative design, this work redefines architectural problem-solving in contexts where tradition and transformation must coexist.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in classical philology and digital humanities, focusing on the analysis of textual transmission and linguistic evolution in understudied ancient Greek and Latin corpora. A central challenge in classics is reconstructing fragmented or corrupted texts and tracing their dissemination across centuries, which requires comparing vast manuscript networks and identifying subtle linguistic patterns. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for processing large-scale datasets or modeling complex relationships between textual variants. The proposed research will develop computational pipelines integrating natural language processing (NLP) techniques, phylogenetic algorithms, and machine learning models to analyze syntactic structures, stylistic features, and scribal errors across multilingual manuscripts. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on non-standardized orthographies, running parallelized comparisons of textual variants, and simulating probabilistic reconstructions of lost archetypes. The project will apply these methods to two case studies: (1) quantifying dialectal shifts in post-classical Greek technical writings, and (2) mapping the circulation of marginal annotations in Carolingian-era Latin codices. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for automated paleographic analysis, a database of annotated textual variants, and statistically grounded hypotheses about transmission pathways. By bridging computational linguistics and classical scholarship, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for analyzing historical languages while addressing longstanding debates about textual authenticity and scribal practices. The requested computing resources will enable processing terabytes of digitized manuscripts and running computationally intensive alignment algorithms, tasks impractical on standard infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary publications and integrated into digital humanities curricula, fostering new collaborations between classics and data science.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical pathology laboratories generate vast multidimensional datasets through advanced diagnostic modalities, yet integrating these data to improve disease classification and predictive modeling remains computationally challenging. This project proposes developing a machine learning framework to harmonize clinical chemistry, genomic, proteomic, and digital pathology data for enhanced diagnosis of complex autoimmune disorders and hematologic malignancies. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabyte-scale datasets from mass spectrometry, next-generation sequencing, and whole-slide imaging systems. Computational workflows will employ federated learning architectures to maintain data privacy across collaborating institutions while training neural networks on distributed GPU clusters. Key methods include variational autoencoders for dimensionality reduction of heterogeneous biomarkers, graph-based models to map molecular interactions in immune dysregulation, and explainable AI techniques to validate clinically actionable patterns. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these analyses across 10,000+ patient cases and enabling real-time inference compatible with diagnostic laboratory workflows. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated multimodal classifier for early detection of treatment-resistant autoimmune profiles, (2) dynamic risk stratification models for myelodysplastic syndromes integrating cytogenetic and flow cytometry data, and (3) an open-source pipeline for clinical laboratories to implement adaptive machine learning in test interpretation. This work addresses critical gaps in precision diagnostics by enabling robust integration of cross-disciplinary laboratory data while establishing computational infrastructure for rapid validation of emerging biomarkers. Successful implementation could reduce diagnostic delays by 30-40% in target conditions and provide a template for AI-driven analytics in clinical pathology practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease. Includes instruction in performing clinical chemistry, cytogenetics, immunology, laboratory management, microbiology, molecular biology, quality control, serology, toxicology, and virology.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the critical challenge of predicting and preventing early childhood caries (ECC) progression in pediatric populations through advanced computational modeling of oral microbiome dynamics and enamel demineralization processes. Despite established clinical protocols, ECC remains the most common chronic disease in children globally, with complex, multifactorial etiology involving microbial ecology, host immunology, and behavioral factors. Current diagnostic tools lack predictive precision for individual risk trajectories, particularly in patients with developmental disabilities who exhibit unique oral microbiome profiles. This project will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling of biofilm formation, finite element analysis of enamel stress distribution, and machine learning analysis of longitudinal clinical-metagenomic datasets from a diverse pediatric cohort (n=1,200). High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate 3D tooth surface interactions across micron-scale spatial resolutions while concurrently processing terabyte-scale genomic data from saliva samples. The computational pipeline will parameterize microbial community networks (including *Streptococcus mutans*, *Candida albicans*, and aciduric symbioses) against pH cycling patterns and dietary variables, then validate predictions through parallel in vitro microfluidic tooth models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a predictive risk stratification algorithm for ECC progression incorporating real-time sensor data from smart dental devices, 2) identification of keystone microbial taxa influencing caries acceleration in neurodiverse patients, and 3) optimized remineralization protocols personalized to salivary biochemistry. By bridging gaps between computational microbiology, materials science, and clinical pedodontics, this work will establish a novel paradigm for precision prevention in pediatric oral health, with particular significance for patients requiring special care dentistry. The resource-intensive simulations (requiring >200,000 core-hours) and integrative data analytics exceed current institutional computing capacities, necessitating access to large-scale GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: Clinical training environments face challenges in balancing educational quality with patient safety, particularly in high-stakes, unpredictable clinical scenarios. Traditional simulation-based training methods are resource-intensive and struggle to replicate the dynamic decision-making required in real-world settings. This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven clinical training platform that generates adaptive, personalized simulation scenarios using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research problem centers on optimizing scenario complexity, learner assessment granularity, and ethical constraints in AI-generated clinical training modules.
