Traditional analytical tools are insufficient for processing the vast, heterogeneous datasets generated by global eBook platforms, social media engagement metrics, and digital rights management systems. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models and natural language processing (NLP) pipelines capable of analyzing multi-terabyte datasets spanning decades of publishing records, reader interactions, and legal disputes. Computational methods will include sentiment analysis of reader feedback to predict demand, network analysis to map author-publisher collaboration patterns, and simulation of digital distribution strategies under varying copyright regimes. Additionally, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect potential ethical conflicts in publishing contracts or content moderation decisions. The scale of data—encompassing millions of titles across multiple languages and formats—requires distributed computing architectures for efficient processing. Expected outcomes include actionable frameworks for dynamic pricing models, automated rights clearance workflows, and ethics-aware recommendation systems tailored to academic and trade publishing contexts. By quantifying historical trends in copyright disputes and content removal requests, the project will also generate novel insights into systemic biases in publishing workflows. These results aim to equip publishers with data-driven strategies for balancing commercial objectives with professional standards, ultimately strengthening trust in digital publishing ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process of managing the creation, publication, and distribution of print and electronic books and other text products and prepares individuals to manage the editorial, technical, and business aspects of publishing operations. Includes instruction in product planning and design, editing, author relations, business and copyright law, publishing industry operations, contracting and purchasing, product marketing, electronic publishing and commerce, history of publishing, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of next-generation electrical power transmission systems through advanced computational modeling. The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, coupled with aging grid infrastructure and dynamic load demands, has introduced unprecedented complexity in ensuring grid stability, fault tolerance, and energy efficiency. Traditional analytical methods and small-scale simulations are insufficient to model the interdependencies between distributed energy resources, transmission line behavior under extreme weather conditions, and real-time load balancing at regional scales. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a multi-physics computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale power networks with high spatial and temporal resolution. The approach integrates finite element analysis for electromagnetic transient modeling, machine learning algorithms for predictive fault detection, and graph theory-based optimization to evaluate grid reconfiguration strategies under contingency scenarios. Key simulations will model cascading failure propagation, transient stability during renewable intermittency, and the impact of novel high-temperature superconducting materials on transmission efficiency. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve a 50-100x acceleration in simulation throughput compared to conventional workstations, enabling parametric studies across thousands of grid configurations. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for grid resilience improvement, validated control strategies for adaptive voltage regulation, and open-source simulation tools tailored for atypical transmission architectures not covered by existing software. These results will directly inform curriculum development for emerging power transmission technologies while providing actionable insights for utilities modernizing critical infrastructure. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the project's petabyte-scale datasets and complex optimization loops, which require sustained GPU-accelerated computations and distributed memory architectures.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural and cultural dynamics of congregational hymnody across underrepresented religious traditions using computational methods, with a focus on patterns of melodic adaptation and lyrical transmission in diasporic communities. While existing scholarship has cataloged liturgical music within major traditions, the evolution of hymns in marginalized or syncretic practices—such as Indigenous Christian blends, Afro-Caribbean spirituals, or post-Soviet Baptist communities—remains understudied due to the scale and complexity of cross-cultural analysis required. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process and analyze a multilingual corpus of over 20,000 hymn texts and 15,000 audio recordings spanning 150 years, integrating optical music recognition (OMR), semantic network analysis, and phylogenetic modeling. Custom machine learning pipelines will identify melodic motifs and lyrical adaptations, tracing regional variations against historical migration data and ethnographic records. By parallelizing feature extraction across audio and textual datasets, the computational workflow will map how theological narratives and musical practices mutate in response to sociopolitical pressures, linguistic shifts, and interfaith contact. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated hymns, statistical models of cultural retention thresholds in displaced communities, and a framework for quantifying the interplay between musical complexity and congregational participation. This work bridges ethnomusicology, diaspora studies, and digital humanities, offering methodological innovations for analyzing cultural resilience through performative worship traditions. The scale of data processing—requiring GPU-accelerated OMR, distributed NLP for low-resource languages, and Monte Carlo simulations of transmission pathways—necessitates HPC resources to achieve feasible runtime for iterative model training and large-scale comparative analysis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious music and worship, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical grids, driven by the integration of renewable energy sources, distributed generation, and smart grid technologies, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize power transmission infrastructure. This project seeks to address critical challenges in dynamic load balancing, fault prediction, and grid resilience by developing a high-fidelity simulation framework for power transmission networks. Current analytical models often lack the resolution to account for real-time variability in energy demand, intermittent renewable generation, and cascading failure risks in interconnected systems. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a hybrid computational approach combining machine learning (ML)-based predictive analytics with physics-informed numerical simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallelization of power flow analyses, Monte Carlo simulations for probabilistic fault scenarios, and training of deep neural networks on historical grid performance data. The computational workflow will integrate grid topology datasets, real-time sensor inputs, and weather-dependent generation profiles to model transmission line stresses, voltage stability, and failure propagation under diverse operating conditions. Key outcomes include a scalable software toolkit for utilities to simulate grid behavior at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, identify high-risk infrastructure segments, and test mitigation strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in traditional power system analysis, enabling rapid scenario evaluation for grids with 10,000+ nodes. The results will provide actionable insights for upgrading aging transmission infrastructure, improving renewable integration capacity, and minimizing outage risks. This work aligns with national priorities for modernizing energy systems while advancing computational methodologies applicable to emerging smart grid technologies. All developed models and simulation datasets will be made publicly available to support industry and academic collaboration.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installers, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and power transmission installation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics datasets in comparative biomedical research necessitates advanced computational tools to model disease mechanisms and optimize experimental animal use. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in analyzing large-scale genomic, proteomic, and physiological data from murine and porcine models of human cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. Current limitations in processing capacity restrict the integration of heterogeneous datasets, hindering the identification of conserved molecular pathways and predictive biomarkers. Our computational approach employs parallelized workflows for genome-wide association studies (GWAS), machine learning-based feature selection, and multi-scale mechanistic modeling to resolve genotype-phenotype relationships across species. Agent-based simulations will further evaluate how genetic diversity and environmental variables influence disease penetrance in controlled animal colonies, enabling predictive optimization of breeding strategies and experimental protocols. By leveraging GPU-accelerated deep learning frameworks, we aim to develop predictive models of drug-induced cardiotoxicity and metabolic syndrome progression, validated against high-resolution imaging and functional genomics data. The proposed work will advance translational insights into conserved disease pathways while refining ethical frameworks for experimental animal use through data-driven reductions in sample sizes and invasive procedures. Outcomes will include open-source tools for cross-species data integration, colony management simulations, and AI-driven experimental design recommendations tailored to veterinary researchers. This project bridges critical gaps in computational comparative medicine, supporting both biomedical discovery and the ethical imperatives central to laboratory animal science.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in casino operations using high-performance computing (HPC) to address the challenge of balancing real-time customer demand with operational constraints. Casinos represent complex, high-stakes environments where spatial layouts, staffing, and gaming equipment must adapt to fluctuating patron behavior, regulatory requirements, and profitability targets. Traditional static planning models fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between variables such as crowd density, slot machine utilization, security response latency, and hospitality service queues. We propose an agent-based simulation platform coupled with reinforcement learning (RL) to model multi-objective decision-making under uncertainty. The computational model will integrate anonymized customer movement data (via IoT sensors), gaming transaction logs, and staff scheduling inputs to simulate scenarios ranging from routine operations to peak-hour or event-driven demand surges. HPC resources are critical to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of potential resource configurations while accounting for probabilistic outcomes in gaming revenue, regulatory compliance risks, and guest satisfaction metrics. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends optimal adjustments to floor layouts, security patrol routes, and staff deployment in near real time, validated against historical operational data from partner casinos. The project contributes to the understudied intersection of computational game theory, behavioral analytics, and service operations in gaming environments, offering a scalable framework that advances resource optimization beyond conventional hospitality management paradigms. Results will be disseminated through gaming industry partnerships and computational economics forums, demonstrating how HPC-enabled models can address niche operational challenges in regulated entertainment sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage casinos and gaming establishments. Includes instruction in business and financial management; casino operations; casino security and surveillance; hospitality, facilities, and personnel management; and principles of the gaming industry, ethics, and gaming law.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the relationship between digital art creation practices and pedagogical outcomes in K–12 art education. While art teacher education programs increasingly emphasize digital tools, there is limited empirical understanding of how specific software workflows, interface interactions, or creative constraints influence skill development in pre-service teachers and their future students. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process multimodal datasets from classroom observations, digital art portfolios, and biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking during software use). Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks for image analysis and temporal transformers for interaction pattern recognition, will be trained to identify correlations between digital art-making processes and measurable competencies in areas like compositional decision-making, technical experimentation, and adaptive problem-solving. By parallelizing the analysis of high-resolution artwork timelines and user behavior logs across GPU nodes, the project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing terabytes of temporally dense creative process data. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing digital art tool instruction in teacher preparation programs and (2) open-source visualization tools to help educators assess developmental trajectories in trainee portfolios. This work addresses a critical gap in art education research by applying scalable computational methods traditionally reserved for STEM domains to questions of pedagogical design in the arts, ultimately aiming to improve how future art teachers scaffold technology-mediated creative learning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistics research in Chinese dialectology and classical text analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable methods for processing understudied regional dialects and premodern literary corpora. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of analyzing morphosyntactic and phonological patterns across vast, heterogeneous datasets of spoken and written Chinese, including digitized historical texts (e.g., Tang dynasty poetry, Ming-Qing vernacular novels) and contemporary dialect recordings. Traditional methods struggle to efficiently parse non-standardized orthographies, dialectal variations, and classical grammar structures at scale, limiting insights into language evolution and regional linguistic diversity. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based neural language models fine-tuned on classical Chinese corpora with dialectometric algorithms optimized for parallel processing. Key tasks include training bidirectional encoder models on a curated corpus of 10,000+ classical and dialect texts, implementing distributed computing pipelines for phonetic alignment of oral dialect data, and developing graph-based visualization tools to map diachronic syntactic shifts. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of large-scale embeddings, reduce runtime for dialect comparison workflows by 80% compared to local clusters, and support memory-intensive analyses of multi-register texts (e.g., ritual bronzes, woodblock prints). Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for classical Chinese-dialect cross-comparison, a phonologically annotated database of Jiang-Huai Mandarin variants, and quantitative models tracing lexical borrowing between literary and vernacular traditions. This work will directly benefit philological research, inform language preservation initiatives, and provide methodological frameworks for applying HPC resources to under-resourced non-Western languages. Results will be disseminated through the Journal of Chinese Linguistics and an open-source platform for digital humanities scholars.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages of China and associated dialects and literature. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in classical philology and digital humanities, addressing challenges in analyzing fragmented and multilingual textual corpora from antiquity. The core research problem centers on reconstructing and interpreting understudied classical texts—such as papyri, inscriptions, and palimpsests—that are often physically degraded, linguistically hybrid, or dispersed across archives. Traditional manual methods struggle to efficiently process these materials at scale, particularly when analyzing syntactic patterns, cross-cultural linguistic exchange, or textual reuse across Greek, Latin, and neighboring languages. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and phylogenetics. HPC resources will enable large-scale tokenization, morphological tagging, and semantic modeling of digitized texts using transformer-based architectures fine-tuned for ancient languages. Parallelized algorithms will trace lexical and stylistic diffusion across regions and periods, while Monte Carlo simulations will test hypotheses about textual transmission pathways. A key innovation involves deploying graph neural networks to map intertextual networks in fragmentary literature, reconstructing plausible connections between works. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital corpus annotated with linguistic and historical metadata, new quantitative frameworks for assessing authorship in anonymous texts, and visualizations of cultural exchange dynamics in the ancient Mediterranean. This work will provide novel methodologies for integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, offering insights into multilingualism, textual production, and intellectual networks in antiquity. By demonstrating scalable computational approaches to classical studies, the project aims to bridge disciplinary gaps and establish best practices for HPC-driven humanities research.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of sustainable urban development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-dimensional interactions between environmental, economic, and social variables in real estate projects. Traditional planning tools often fail to dynamically integrate real-time data streams such as climate projections, population mobility patterns, and fluctuating market demands, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and missed opportunities for resilience. The proposed work employs an interdisciplinary computational framework combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and geospatial analysis to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes, predict long-term viability of development scenarios, and optimize site design under constraints of carbon neutrality and community equity. By processing large-scale datasets—including satellite imagery, municipal infrastructure records, and demographic surveys—the HPC environment enables iterative testing of hybrid urban forms (e.g., mixed-use districts, green corridors) at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support platform that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, ecological impact, and social benefit across development timelines. This tool aims to empower developers, municipalities, and community organizations to collaboratively prioritize projects that balance growth with sustainability imperatives. The computational demands of parallelized scenario analysis, coupled with the need for AI-driven pattern recognition in heterogeneous data sources, necessitate access to advanced GPU clusters and distributed storage systems. Successful implementation will advance methodological synergies between real estate practice and computational urban science while addressing critical gaps in adaptive planning for climate-resilient cities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create and redevelop housing, offices, retail centers, and industrial sites. Includes instruction in architectural design and construction, historic preservation, landscape architecture, urban planning and design, business, real estate and land use law, public policy, and engineering.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methodologies in architectural design, specifically targeting the emergent niche of generative systems for culturally adaptive urban spaces. Traditional architectural workflows often prioritize efficiency or aesthetics but lack robust frameworks for integrating dynamic socio-cultural data—such as community interaction patterns, historical narratives, or localized spatial practices—into generative design processes. This gap limits the ability of architects to create environments that respond meaningfully to evolving cultural contexts. To address this, the project proposes a hybrid computational approach combining parametric modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning (ML) to generate architectural prototypes that dynamically adapt to socio-cultural inputs. The research problem centers on developing scalable algorithms capable of processing heterogeneous datasets (e.g., ethnographic surveys, mobility traces, and heritage records) and translating them into spatial configurations that balance structural feasibility with cultural resonance. Computational workflows will involve training ML models on curated datasets of culturally significant architectural case studies, followed by iterative simulations using HPC to optimize multi-objective design criteria (e.g., spatial connectivity, material efficiency, and symbolic meaning). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework for culturally adaptive design, validated through case studies in post-industrial urban redevelopment contexts. The project’s significance lies in bridging architectural theory with computational innovation, offering tools to address pressing challenges in equitable urban regeneration. By utilizing HPC to manage complex, non-linear relationships between cultural data and spatial design, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for interdisciplinary architectural research, with implications for policy, heritage preservation, and community-driven design practices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture and related programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of emergency medical services (EMS) demands innovative approaches to optimize prehospital care delivery. This project addresses a critical gap in emergency care attendant (ECA) operations: real-time, dynamic resource allocation during mass casualty incidents (MCIs) or surge events, where traditional dispatch protocols often fail due to unpredictable patient distributions and resource constraints. We propose developing a machine learning-driven simulation framework to model ambulance routing, ECA skill matching, and equipment utilization under high-stress scenarios. The research problem centers on minimizing time-to-treatment intervals while balancing crew fatigue, equipment availability, and evolving patient acuity levels—a multidimensional challenge requiring high-dimensional optimization. Computational methods will integrate discrete-event simulation with reinforcement learning agents trained on synthetic MCI datasets generated through probabilistic injury progression models. High-performance computing resources are essential for parallelizing thousands of scenario variations, processing real-time geospatial data streams, and training neural networks on emergent triage patterns. Expected outcomes include a predictive decision-support system that adapts to evolving incident landscapes, providing ECAs with optimized patient transport sequences and resource deployment strategies. The model’s significance lies in its potential to reduce preventable mortality through computational anticipation of bottleneck scenarios while maintaining operational feasibility for EMS systems. By focusing on the unique constraints of prehospital emergency care rather than hospital-based interventions, this work occupies an emerging niche at the intersection of operational informatics, emergency medicine, and computational logistics. Successful implementation could establish a new paradigm for data-driven EMS management, directly impacting the 240 million emergency calls annually handled by EMT personnel worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist licensed EMTs, under the supervision of a physician, to prepare and transport ill or injured patients, and to operate emergency vehicles and equipment such as life support units. Includes instruction in first aid and emergency medicine field techniques, patient stabilization and care, medical field communications, equipment operation and maintenance, emergency vehicle operation, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in bioethics research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, large-scale datasets related to clinical decision-making, health equity, and ethical dilemmas in emerging medical technologies. Current studies in bioethics often rely on qualitative or small-sample analyses, limiting their ability to model systemic biases, forecast long-term societal impacts, or evaluate trade-offs in resource allocation under diverse ethical frameworks. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ computational modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and multi-agent simulations to examine patterns in clinical ethics consultations, public health policy outcomes, and patient autonomy conflicts documented in electronic health records, institutional reports, and global bioethics repositories. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including unstructured text from clinical narratives and policy documents, as well as the simulation of population-level ethical scenarios (e.g., triage protocols during resource scarcity, AI-driven diagnostics in culturally diverse contexts). Machine learning models will be trained to identify latent biases in historical ethics committee decisions, while discrete-event simulations will test the resilience of proposed ethical guidelines under demographic and epidemiological shifts. Expected outcomes include the development of open-access predictive tools to support ethics review boards, evidence-based frameworks for equitable AI deployment in healthcare, and scalable models for assessing the justice implications of genetic editing technologies. By integrating computational rigor with normative analysis, this work aims to advance translational bioethics, providing stakeholders with empirically grounded strategies to navigate moral complexity in rapidly evolving medical landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: Clinical genetics faces a critical challenge in efficiently interpreting the growing volume of genomic data to diagnose rare genetic disorders accurately. While next-generation sequencing has enabled rapid identification of genetic variants, distinguishing pathogenic mutations from benign variants remains computationally intensive and time-consuming, particularly for underrepresented populations with limited reference datasets. This project seeks to address this bottleneck by developing a scalable, machine learning-driven framework to improve variant prioritization and clinical interpretation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-omics data—including whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic profiles, and epigenomic annotations—from 50,000 patients with suspected genetic disorders, alongside publicly available datasets. Deep neural networks will be trained to predict variant pathogenicity using context-aware features such as tissue-specific gene expression, 3D chromatin structure, and evolutionary conservation patterns. Concurrently, population genetics simulations will model allele frequencies and linkage disequilibrium across diverse ancestries to reduce interpretation bias. The computational pipeline will utilize parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, distributed training of ensemble models, and large-scale hypothesis testing. Expected outcomes include a validated clinical decision-support tool that reduces diagnostic turnaround time by ≥40% in retrospective validation cohorts, novel insights into noncoding variants affecting regulatory elements in developmental disorders, and publicly shared benchmarking datasets to improve equity in genomic resources. This work will directly enhance the clinical utility of genomic testing, enabling personalized management strategies for patients with Mendelian diseases and complex structural variants. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the petabyte-scale data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and millions of simultaneous simulations required to achieve these aims.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide comprehensive diagnostic, management, and counseling services for individuals and families at risk for clinical disorders with a genetic basis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the neurocognitive and emotional correlates of art-making processes in pre-clinical populations, with the goal of establishing objective biomarkers for art therapy efficacy. Current art therapy research relies heavily on qualitative assessments, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this gap, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating high-density electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking data, and digital art process recordings (e.g., brushstroke kinematics, color choice dynamics) from participants engaged in structured art tasks. The primary computational challenge involves modeling multivariate time-series data across disparate modalities (neural, behavioral, and artistic) at millisecond resolution, requiring alignment of temporal patterns and identification of cross-modal signatures predictive of therapeutic outcomes. High-performance computing resources will enable the implementation of custom recurrent neural network architectures optimized for temporal fusion of heterogeneous data streams, alongside large-scale permutation testing to validate robustness. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated pipeline for quantifying art-making behaviors as multidimensional time-evolving signals, 2) predictive models linking specific neurodynamic patterns during creative expression to post-intervention psychological state improvements, and 3) open-source tools for visualizing art process biomarkers. This work will establish quantitative foundations for art therapy assessment while advancing computational methods for analyzing creative cognition. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training across >10,000 parameter combinations, storage/processing of petabyte-scale multimodal datasets, and parallelized statistical validation—capabilities unattainable with standard laboratory infrastructure. By bridging computational neuroscience and expressive therapies, this project aims to transform art therapy from a subjective practice to an evidence-based intervention modality.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional art therapy program.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between visual environmental stimuli and cognitive restoration through an interdisciplinary lens integrating environmental psychology, computational neuroscience, and urban design. While exposure to natural environments is known to reduce cognitive fatigue, the specific visual features driving restorative effects—such as fractal patterns, color spectra, and spatial complexity—remain poorly quantified. Current analytical approaches lack the resolution to model how dynamic, high-dimensional visual inputs interact with individual neurocognitive processes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining eye-tracking, EEG, and behavioral data from 300 participants exposed to immersive virtual environments simulating natural and urban settings. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable three key innovations: (1) large-scale parallel processing of multimodal data streams (120Hz gaze paths, 256-channel EEG, and continuous affect ratings) across participants; (2) training deep convolutional neural networks to identify latent visual features predictive of alpha-band EEG modulation and self-reported restoration; and (3) agent-based modeling of attention restoration dynamics through GPU-accelerated simulations incorporating individual differences in perceptual styles. The computational pipeline will leverage PyTorch and CUDA-optimized libraries for real-time data fusion, while graph neural networks will map how specific environmental attributes propagate through cognitive subsystems. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model of visual restoration potential and an open-source toolkit for simulating cognitive impacts of architectural designs. By establishing quantitative links between environmental aesthetics and neural markers of cognitive recovery, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for mental health-promoting urban planning while developing novel methods for scaling ecological psychology research through computational modeling. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the project's data intensity (estimated 450TB of raw neurobehavioral data) and supporting the complex parameter spaces of our machine learning architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis of multi-scale interactions between climate variability, agricultural productivity, and market dynamics in domestic and international contexts. A critical challenge in agricultural economics lies in modeling complex, non-linear relationships across heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution climate projections, spatially disaggregated crop yields, and global commodity trade flows—while accounting for stochastic shocks and adaptive decision-making by farmers, policymakers, and supply chain actors. Current methods often rely on simplified assumptions due to computational constraints, limiting their capacity to inform resilient resource allocation strategies. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating dynamic stochastic economic models with machine learning techniques to simulate adaptive behaviors under diverse climate and market scenarios. The project will employ parallelized econometric estimation of panel data spanning 40 years of agricultural production, trade, and environmental variables across 150 countries, coupled with agent-based modeling to capture decentralized decision-making. HPC resources are essential for scaling Bayesian hierarchical models to process terabytes of satellite-derived land-use data and for running Monte Carlo simulations evaluating the fiscal and welfare impacts of climate-adaptive policies. Expected outcomes include empirically grounded insights into optimal investment thresholds for drought-resistant infrastructure, price stabilization mechanisms for volatile global markets, and spatially explicit risk maps to guide regional agricultural subsidies. By enhancing the granularity and robustness of agricultural economic models, this work will directly contribute to evidence-based policies that balance productivity, sustainability, and equity in resource allocation. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source packages to support reproducible research in the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics to the analysis of resource allocation, productivity, investment, and trends in the agricultural sector, both domestically and internationally. Includes instruction in economics and related subfields as well as applicable agricultural fields.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale digitized archives of Japanese cultural artifacts, textual materials, and visual media to investigate evolving representations of identity and social belonging in Japan from the late Edo period to the present. The research addresses a critical gap in Japanese Studies: while historical and cultural datasets are increasingly digitized, existing methods lack the capacity to systematically trace nuanced patterns in language use, visual symbolism, and cross-media narratives across centuries. Computational approaches are essential to map how concepts such as regional identity, gender roles, and community boundaries have been constructed, contested, and renegotiated in public discourse. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze multilingual corpora spanning historical newspapers, literature, and governmental records, alongside computer vision algorithms to classify iconographic motifs in ukiyo-e prints, photography, and contemporary media. Transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to detect semantic shifts in culturally specific terminology, while graph neural networks will model the intertextual relationships between visual and textual narratives. By integrating these methods, the research aims to identify previously unrecognized correlations between socio-political events and representational trends in popular culture. Outcomes will include open-access datasets of annotated materials, a computational framework for interdisciplinary cultural analysis, and new insights into how marginalized groups—such as Ainu, Okinawan, and zainichi communities—have been depicted in mainstream Japanese media. This work will advance methodological innovation in area studies by demonstrating how HPC can bridge qualitative cultural scholarship and data-driven inquiry, while contributing to broader debates about heritage preservation and the ethics of representation in digitized archives. The requested resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets, training of domain-specific machine learning models, and large-scale parallelism for comparative timeline analysis across regions and media types.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the interdisciplinary study of molecular gastronomy, a field blending culinary arts, chemistry, and materials science to innovate food design and sensory experiences. While molecular gastronomy has transformative potential for culinary practices and consumer engagement, its computational modeling remains underdeveloped due to the complexity of multi-phase interactions (e.g., emulsions, gels, foams) and the lack of tailored simulation frameworks. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and limited in probing dynamic, non-equilibrium systems critical to achieving precise textures, flavors, and visual effects. This research aims to bridge this gap by developing a computational pipeline to simulate and optimize novel culinary processes, such as spherification or temperature-dependent gelation, at microscale resolutions. The project will employ hybrid numerical methods, combining lattice Boltzmann simulations for fluid dynamics, molecular dynamics for interfacial interactions, and machine learning to map parameter spaces (e.g., pH, ionic strength, shear rates) to sensory outcomes. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC architectures, the team will resolve time-dependent behaviors of hydrocolloids, proteins, and lipid assemblies under conditions mimicking real-world culinary environments. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for predictive culinary material design, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in recipe development. The work will also establish quantitative correlations between molecular-scale phenomena and macroscopic sensory properties, offering foundational insights for personalized nutrition and sustainable food engineering. This project highlights the role of HPC in democratizing innovation for culinary professionals while positioning computational gastronomy as a benchmark for interdisciplinary research in non-traditional STEM domains.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of cross-species signaling networks in rapidly changing coastal ecosystems, integrating ecological, geochemical, and acoustic data streams to model anthropogenic impacts on interspecies communication. Coastal zones face unprecedented pressures from urbanization, climate change, and industrial activity, yet the computational synthesis of multi-modal biological and environmental data remains underdeveloped. Our research addresses this gap by developing a novel framework to analyze how noise pollution, chemical contaminants, and habitat fragmentation disrupt vibrational and chemical signaling among invertebrates, fish, and marine mammals—processes critical to mating, predation avoidance, and collective behavior. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will process petabyte-scale datasets from hydrophone arrays, mass spectrometry, and satellite imagery using hybrid convolutional neural networks and graph-based dynamical systems models. The computational workflow will synchronize heterogeneous temporal resolutions (millisecond acoustic events to decadal chemical concentration trends) and spatially explicit interactions across three study regions with varying anthropogenic footprints. Key innovations include adaptive attention mechanisms for cross-domain feature fusion and agent-based simulations of signaling cascades under future climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include the first unified atlas of coastal biosignaling networks, predictive models of threshold effects on communication resilience, and open-source tools for real-time monitoring of ecosystem-scale stress indicators. By bridging marine biology, complexity science, and environmental informatics, this work will establish computational standards for assessing multispecies vulnerability while informing policy frameworks for acoustic and chemical pollution mitigation. The scale of data integration and need for ensemble simulation across parameter spaces necessitates HPC resources to achieve sufficient temporal granularity and spatial coverage for robust ecological inference.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the dynamics of intergenerational caregiving networks and their impact on family resilience in rapidly aging populations. Traditional qualitative and survey-based methods in human development research struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions, feedback loops, and adaptive behaviors that characterize these complex social systems. Our work addresses this gap by employing agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate caregiving ecosystems across diverse cultural and socioeconomic contexts. The research integrates longitudinal demographic data, household economic surveys, and psychosocial metrics from public repositories with ethnographic case studies to parameterize multi-scale models. Computational challenges include simulating thousands of autonomous agents with heterogeneous decision-making algorithms, tracking resource flows across kinship networks, and analyzing emergent patterns through temporal graph metrics. HPC resources will enable sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces, Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention scenarios, and machine learning approaches to identify critical leverage points for policy design. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of caregiving network stability under demographic and economic stressors, (2) evidence-based criteria for tailoring community support programs to kinship structures, and (3) open-source tools for simulating culturally situated family dynamics. By bridging computational social science with human development theory, this work advances methodological capacity to study relational systems that defy traditional disciplinary boundaries. The results will inform interventions addressing the global care crisis while establishing scalable computational workflows for family studies research. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale graph database management, and comparative analysis of terabyte-scale synthetic population datasets.
cip_title: Human Development, Family Studies, and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in human development, family studies, and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Early childhood education programs face complex administrative challenges in optimizing resource allocation to meet dynamic enrollment demands, regulatory compliance, and equitable service delivery. This project seeks to develop computational models to simulate and analyze resource distribution strategies for early childhood education centers, with a focus on balancing operational costs, staff-to-child ratios, and facility utilization under fluctuating enrollment patterns. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven decision-support tools for administrators navigating multi-dimensional constraints, including budget limitations, space availability, workforce training requirements, and state-mandated quality standards. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations that account for stochastic variables such as seasonal enrollment shifts, staff absenteeism, and emergency operational scenarios. These models will integrate geospatial data on community demographics, historical enrollment trends from 15 regional early childhood programs, and policy-driven constraints encoded as optimization parameters. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive patterns in resource bottlenecks and evaluate intervention strategies. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing capabilities due to the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of operational scenarios across heterogeneous program types (e.g., full-day, part-day, and subsidized care models). Expected outcomes include a framework for dynamically adjusting staffing matrices, facility expansion plans, and budget reallocation thresholds under uncertainty. This work will provide administrators with evidence-based strategies to enhance program sustainability while maintaining compliance with professional standards and ethical guidelines for service accessibility. The resulting open-source toolset will undergo validation through partnerships with three state early childhood agencies, with scalability potential to inform policy decisions at regional and national levels.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on early childhood educational program administration and prepares individuals to serve as a principal or director of an early childhood educational program. Includes instruction in early childhood education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, early childhood growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of high-impact weather systems in a changing climate by improving the representation of mesoscale convective processes in regional atmospheric models. Current models struggle to resolve critical interactions between microphysics, turbulence, and large-scale dynamics that govern the intensity and evolution of severe storms, leading to uncertainties in predictions of extreme precipitation and convective initiation. To address this gap, we propose a series of high-resolution numerical experiments using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model at convection-permitting resolutions (1-3 km grid spacing) across selected case studies of historic storm systems in the central United States. The simulations will incorporate advanced spectral bin microphysics schemes and large-eddy simulation (LES) techniques to explicitly represent cloud-aerosol interactions and subgrid-scale turbulent motions typically parameterized in coarser models. Computational demands are substantial, requiring access to high-performance computing resources for ensemble-based sensitivity analyses (50+ members per case) and multi-day simulations with frequent data output to capture rapidly evolving storm structures. The requested allocation would support 800,000 core-hours on parallelized CPU clusters, supplemented by GPU-accelerated preprocessing for initial condition optimization. Expected outcomes include new insights into how aerosol loading and land-surface heterogeneity modulate convective system organization, with direct implications for improving short-term severe weather forecasts and climate projection downscaling methods. Results will be disseminated through open-source model configurations and a publicly accessible database of high-resolution simulation outputs, providing community resources for studying precipitation extremes under projected warming scenarios. By bridging scale gaps in current modeling frameworks, this work aims to enhance predictive capacity for weather hazards that pose growing risks to infrastructure and ecosystems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of the atmospheric envelopes surrounding the earth, the effect of earth's atmosphere on terrestrial weather, and related problems of environment and climate. Includes instruction in atmospheric chemistry and physics, atmospheric dynamics, climatology and climate change, weather simulation, weather forecasting, climate modeling and mathematical theory; and studies of specific phenomena such as clouds, weather systems, storms, and precipitation patterns.

abstract: This research project investigates the computational modeling of cross-linguistic semantic change driven by multilingual online communication, with a focus on under-resourced languages. As digital platforms accelerate language contact and hybridization, traditional frameworks for analyzing semantic shifts struggle to capture the dynamic, large-scale interactions between speakers of typologically diverse languages. The project addresses this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to model semantic networks across 50+ languages, prioritizing Indigenous and minority languages with limited digital corpora. Using transformer-based architectures adapted for low-resource settings, we will train multilingual embeddings on scraped web data (social media, forums, collaborative platforms) and historical texts, then quantify cross-linguistic convergence/divergence patterns through graph-based metrics. Key computational challenges include scaling dynamic time warping algorithms for diachronic comparisons across language pairs and implementing distributed training for morphologically complex languages. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of 15TB+ unstructured text data, iterative refinement of attention mechanisms for code-switched utterances, and agent-based simulations of semantic propagation in language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include: 1) a publicly accessible database tracking semantic shifts in under-documented languages, 2) novel metrics for quantifying language vitality based on digital interaction patterns, and 3) open-source tools enabling real-time monitoring of emergent semantic phenomena in multilingual online spaces. This work advances computational linguistics by bridging typological research with sociocultural language dynamics, offering methodological innovations for analyzing language change in the digital age while supporting efforts to document and preserve linguistic diversity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language, language development, and relationships among languages and language groups from a humanistic and/or scientific perspective. Includes instruction in subjects such as psycholinguistics, behavioral linguistics, language acquisition, sociolinguistics, mathematical and computational linguistics, grammatical theory and theoretical linguistics, philosophical linguistics, philology and historical linguistics, comparative linguistics, phonetics, phonemics, dialectology, semantics, functional grammar and linguistics, language typology, lexicography, morphology and syntax, orthography, stylistics, structuralism, rhetoric, and applications to artificial intelligence.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of federal-provincial policy coordination in Canada through computational modeling of intergovernmental negotiation processes. The research problem centers on understanding how institutional design, partisan alignment, and regional disparities influence the efficiency and outcomes of multilateral agreements, such as those addressing climate policy or healthcare funding. While qualitative studies dominate existing literature, quantitative gaps persist in systematically analyzing how institutional rules (e.g., formal consultation requirements) interact with political incentives to shape bargaining success. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate negotiation scenarios using parameters derived from historical federal-provincial agreements (1982–present), constitutional frameworks, and electoral data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of modeling 13 provincial/territorial agents with heterogeneous preferences, dynamic party affiliations, and variable resource dependencies. Simulations will test hypotheses about veto point thresholds, side-payment effectiveness, and the impact of asymmetric decentralization. Complementary NLP methods will process parliamentary debate transcripts and intergovernmental communiqués to refine model inputs. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable computational framework for simulating multilevel governance interactions, (2) empirical insights into institutional bottlenecks affecting contemporary policy coordination, and (3) open-access datasets mapping negotiation trajectories across policy domains. Results will advance scholarly debates about Canadian federalism’s adaptability to collective action challenges while providing actionable evidence for constitutional and intergovernmental affairs practitioners. The requested resources will support parallelized simulation runs, large-text corpus analysis, and validation exercises requiring GPU-accelerated computation for deep learning classifiers applied to political discourse.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of Canadian political institutions and behavior. Includes instruction in British and North American political theory, political parties and interest groups, provincial and local governments, Constitutional law, federalism and national institutions, executive and legislative politics, judicial politics, popular attitudes and media influences, political research methods, and applications to the study of specific issues and institutions.

abstract: Agricultural businesses face growing challenges in optimizing operational efficiency and resilience amid climate variability, market volatility, and supply chain disruptions. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to integrate high-resolution spatial, temporal, and economic datasets, limiting predictive accuracy for critical outcomes such as crop yield forecasting, resource allocation, and risk mitigation. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a scalable computational framework to model complex interactions between agronomic practices, environmental conditions, and market dynamics. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating farm-level decision-making processes and supply chain networks across regional scales. These models will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including satellite-derived soil moisture indices, historical commodity pricing, and real-time logistics data, to evaluate adaptive strategies under scenarios of climatic stress and economic uncertainty. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify probabilistic outcomes for key performance indicators, such as profit margins and input-use efficiency, while machine learning pipelines will identify emergent patterns in system resilience. The computational workload necessitates large-scale memory and processing capabilities due to the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and iterative optimization requirements. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic risk assessment and a decision-support platform enabling stakeholders to test operational interventions in silico. By bridging gaps between agronomic data science and business analytics, this work aims to advance evidence-based management practices, enhance supply chain agility, and improve the long-term viability of agricultural enterprises in resource-constrained environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage agricultural businesses and agriculturally related operations within diversified corporations. Includes instruction in agriculture, agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, finance, marketing, planning, human resources management, and other managerial responsibilities.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between decentralized social media architectures and emergent collective decision-making processes, focusing on how platform design influences consensus formation in polarized information environments. While existing studies have centered on mainstream platforms, the rapid growth of federated and blockchain-based social networks presents novel dynamics that challenge traditional models of digital discourse. The research employs large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interaction patterns across 10^6 synthetic users with heterogeneous belief-updating algorithms, incorporating neurocognitive constraints on information processing. High-performance computing resources are critical for parameter space exploration across 1) varying network topologies (scale-free, small-world, and emergent decentralized structures), 2) multiple incentive systems for content sharing, and 3) evolving trust calibration mechanisms. Simulations will integrate real-world data from ActivityPub-based platforms through federated learning techniques, requiring distributed computation across GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of platform architectures that either mitigate or amplify belief polarization, validated through multi-agent reinforcement learning experiments. The computational framework will advance methodological capabilities for studying socio-technical systems at scale, providing evidence-based design principles for next-generation social platforms. Results will contribute foundational insights to the emerging field of computational social architecture, addressing critical gaps in understanding how technical infrastructures co-evolve with human collective behaviors beyond current centralized paradigms.
cip_definition: Any program in general social sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of human-environment interactions in informal urban settlements through advanced geospatial modeling and high-resolution temporal analysis. As cities globally face rapid, unplanned growth, traditional cartographic methods and static geographic information systems (GIS) struggle to capture the fluidity of these environments, where spatial configurations and land use evolve unpredictably. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to model these dynamic processes at scale, integrating heterogeneous data sources—including satellite imagery, crowd-sourced mobility traces, and socio-economic surveys—to generate predictive maps of settlement morphologies and resource accessibility. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with deep learning architectures to simulate how informal settlements adapt to environmental stressors, policy interventions, and community-driven spatial practices. Key computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale raster datasets, optimizing spatial graph algorithms for real-time simulations, and training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on irregularly sampled geospatial time series. The proposed methods will extend cartographic theory by formalizing probabilistic map projections that account for temporal uncertainty and non-Euclidean urban geometries. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive cartography, validated against case studies in three megacities, which will provide policymakers and grassroots organizations with actionable insights into equitable infrastructure planning. By bridging computational scalability with social science rigor, this work aims to redefine how transient human landscapes are represented, analyzed, and ethically intervened upon in contexts of urban informality.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of map-making and the application of mathematical, computer, and other techniques to the analysis of large amounts of geographic data and the science of mapping geographic information. Includes instruction in cartographic theory and map projections, computer-assisted cartography, geographic information systems, map design and layout, photogrammetry, air photo interpretation, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geodesy, cartographic editing, and applications to specific industrial, commercial, research, and governmental mapping problems.

abstract: Dairy product quality and safety are heavily influenced by microbial communities during fermentation, yet predicting their complex interactions remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model microbial dynamics in industrial dairy fermentation processes, with a focus on cheese production. Current empirical approaches cannot adequately resolve strain-level metabolic interactions or predict outcomes under varying environmental conditions, leading to inconsistencies in product quality and inefficiencies in resource use. We propose to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-omics data (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metabolomic) with genome-scale metabolic models of key lactic acid bacteria and spoilage organisms. Agent-based simulations will model spatial heterogeneity in microbial colonies within cheese matrices, while machine learning algorithms will identify critical parameters governing fermentation stability. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental data from pilot-scale fermentations, including pH, metabolite profiles, and microbial composition time series. Successful implementation will enable predictive optimization of starter culture ratios, temperature regimes, and inhibitory strategies against pathogens or spoilage microbes. This work is expected to provide novel insights into microbial resource competition and cross-feeding in dairy systems, directly addressing industry needs for improved process control and waste reduction. By establishing a scalable computational platform, this project will enhance the safety, consistency, and resource efficiency of fermented dairy products, with broader applications in microbial food ecology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the production and management of dairy animals and the production and handling of dairy products. Includes instruction in animal sciences, nutrition sciences, food science and technology, biochemistry, and related aspects of human and animal health and safety.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of neurodevelopmental mechanisms underlying pediatric anxiety disorders, with a focus on identifying biomarkers and optimizing early intervention strategies. Current limitations in clinical child psychology stem from the complexity of integrating multimodal data—including neuroimaging (fMRI), genetic susceptibility markers, and longitudinal behavioral assessments—while accounting for dynamic developmental trajectories. Traditional analytical approaches struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between biological, cognitive, and environmental risk factors that drive disorder onset and progression. The proposed research will employ machine learning frameworks to analyze high-dimensional datasets from a cohort of 800 children (ages 6–12) with anxiety symptoms, incorporating resting-state fMRI connectivity, polygenic risk scores, and caregiver-reported psychosocial stressors. Computational workflows will include federated learning to preserve participant confidentiality across collaborating clinical sites, graph neural networks to model evolving brain-behavior relationships, and Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify uncertainty in developmental predictions. HPC resources are critical for training these models efficiently, given the scale of imaging data (~10 TB) and the need for real-time parameter optimization in iterative simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of neural circuitry patterns predictive of treatment resistance, (2) risk stratification algorithms to guide personalized therapeutic interventions, and (3) open-source tools for developmental psychopathology research that integrate ethical AI practices. By clarifying how neurocognitive vulnerabilities interact with environmental contexts during critical developmental windows, this work aims to transform clinical decision-making in pediatric mental health while adhering to FAIR data principles. The computational infrastructure will enable scalable replication of findings across diverse populations, directly addressing gaps in equitable access to precision child psychology frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the developmental processes of children and associated disorders and that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical child psychology. Includes instruction in developmental neuropsychology, child psychopathology, testing of children and adolescents, pediatric psychology, psychosocial variables in child development, clinical skills, family therapy, behavioral assessment and intervention, clinical skills, consultation, professional standards and ethics, and applications to topics such as infancy, childhood, and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive computational framework to simulate urban fire dynamics and optimize emergency response strategies under complex, real-world conditions. Despite advances in fire science, existing models often fail to account for the interplay between heterogeneous urban infrastructure, evolving fire behavior, and human evacuation patterns, leading to suboptimal resource deployment during crises. The research addresses this gap by integrating high-fidelity simulations of fire spread, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for smoke dispersion, and agent-based modeling (ABM) for crowd movement into a unified, scalable platform. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, particularly when modeling large-scale urban environments with diverse building materials, ventilation systems, and real-time meteorological data. The computational approach leverages parallelized solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to balance accuracy and efficiency, while machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs associated with uncertainty quantification across thousands of stochastic scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolset for fire departments to simulate disaster scenarios, test mitigation strategies, and prioritize infrastructure retrofits. The framework will also inform policy by identifying vulnerabilities in current fire codes related to modern urban design trends, such as high-density mixed-use developments and green building materials. By bridging fire science, urban planning, and emergency management, this work aims to reduce civilian and responder risks while enhancing community resilience. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across fire intensity, occupancy types, and suppression tactics at unprecedented resolution, providing actionable insights for fire-safe urban development.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision pharmacotherapy by optimizing drug dosing and therapeutic outcomes in complex clinical populations. A critical challenge in clinical pharmacy is the interindividual variability in drug response, driven by factors such as genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, polypharmacy, and organ dysfunction. Traditional pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to account for these multidimensional interactions, leading to suboptimal dosing recommendations and increased risks of adverse events or therapeutic failure. To address this, we propose the development of a machine learning-enhanced, multi-scale modeling framework integrating real-world patient data from electronic health records (EHRs), genomic datasets, and dynamic physiological parameters. The computational workflow will involve (1) natural language processing (NLP) of unstructured clinical notes to extract medication histories and comorbidities, (2) Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify covariate effects on drug disposition, and (3) neural network architectures predicting individualized dosing thresholds based on simulated patient trajectories. Large-scale parallelization will be required for parameter estimation across heterogeneous virtual patient cohorts and sensitivity analyses of dosing protocols under diverse physiological scenarios. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate drug-receptor interactions in patients with rare genetic variants affecting drug metabolism. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this project aims to generate validated, adaptive dosing algorithms for high-risk medications such as anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, and oncology therapies. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for model-informed precision dosing, risk stratification dashboards for clinical pharmacists, and a computational framework adaptable to emerging therapeutics. The resource-intensive nature of these analyses—particularly the integration of multi-omics data with real-time PK simulations—necessitates access to high-memory nodes and GPU clusters to achieve clinically actionable timelines. Successful implementation will directly support safer, more effective medication management in hospital and managed care settings while establishing scalable methodologies for computational pharmacy research.
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: Veterinary practice faces growing challenges in integrating large-scale clinical data to optimize care delivery, manage complex practice workflows, and predict patient outcomes. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in data-driven decision-making for veterinary medicine. The primary research problem centers on the computational limitations of processing heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), diagnostic imaging (e.g., MRI, CT, radiographs), and longitudinal treatment histories—which are often high-dimensional, temporally dynamic, and spatially resolved. Current workflows lack the capacity to analyze these datasets cohesively, hindering advancements in personalized treatment planning, early disease detection, and operational efficiency in veterinary practices. This project proposes a multi-modal computational framework combining machine learning (ML) models, image analysis algorithms, and discrete-event simulations to model clinical workflows, predict treatment responses, and automate diagnostic image interpretation. HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on terabyte-scale imaging repositories, parallelized simulation of clinic operations under diverse scenarios, and real-time integration of EHR data with predictive analytics. Key computational challenges include optimizing GPU-accelerated pipelines for 3D medical image segmentation, developing federated learning protocols to aggregate anonymized data across partner clinics, and implementing agent-based models to evaluate resource allocation strategies in emergency care settings. Expected outcomes include validated ML tools for detecting early-stage pathologies in diagnostic images, predictive models for post-surgical complications in companion animals, and simulation-based guidelines for reducing patient wait times in high-volume practices. By scaling these analyses beyond the capabilities of local computing infrastructure, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-enhanced veterinary care, directly improving clinical outcomes, operational sustainability, and accessibility of advanced services in community practices. The results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits tailored for veterinary applications, fostering collaboration across clinical and computational research domains.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of regular and long-term care to animals, health services to owners, and the management of independent veterinary practices. May included related research in comprehensive care and specialist referral, basic surgery, emergency medical procedures, and diagnostic imaging.
