Custom NLP pipelines will be developed to handle multilingual texts, dialect variations, and non-Western feminist terminologies, while computer vision tools will classify visual motifs in art and protest materials. Network graphs will map the circulation of ideas across regions and temporal periods, identifying hubs of influence and underrepresented contributors. The computational workflow requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, train machine learning models on GPU clusters, and run parallelized analyses of cross-cultural correlations. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated feminist cultural artifacts, visualizations of discourse networks, and peer-reviewed findings on how regional sociohistorical contexts shaped feminist aesthetics and rhetoric. This work will provide scholars in gender studies and digital humanities with new methodologies to analyze intersectionality at scale, while centering computationally underrepresented voices in global feminist movements. By bridging computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, the project aims to redefine canon-formation processes and inform contemporary equity-oriented cultural policies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: Infant and toddler mental health is a critical yet understudied area, with early developmental disruptions having lifelong consequences for emotional regulation, social functioning, and cognitive outcomes. Current research is limited by the inability to model dynamic, multi-modal developmental data at scale, particularly for populations experiencing socioeconomic adversity or caregiver instability. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex longitudinal datasets integrating behavioral, neuroimaging (EEG), and caregiver-reported data from 2,000+ infants and toddlers enrolled in community mental health programs. The computational approach employs multilevel Bayesian network modeling to identify latent profiles of risk and resilience across developmental domains (social, emotional, cognitive), while accounting for temporal dependencies and missing data common in real-world clinical samples. Parallelized processing will enable simultaneous optimization of network structures and parameter estimation across subgroups. A second aim involves agent-based modeling to simulate intervention scenarios, testing how variations in service timing, dosage, and modality affect projected developmental trajectories. These simulations will incorporate neurodevelopmental constraints derived from empirical growth curves and caregiver-child interaction patterns. The computational workflow requires large-memory nodes for in-memory processing of high-dimensional EEG time series and GPU acceleration for deep learning components that extract interaction features from video data. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of transdiagnostic biomarkers predictive of service response, (2) optimization frameworks for personalizing early mental health interventions, and (3) open-source tools for developmental network analysis tailored to sparse, irregularly sampled data. By elucidating mechanisms linking early adversity to emergent psychopathology, this work directly informs prevention strategies while advancing computational methods for developmental science. The requested HPC resources are essential given the exponential scaling of model comparison tasks (≥10^5 candidate networks) and the need for real-time parameter adaptation in simulated cohorts exceeding 100,000 agent-years.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide mental health services to infants, toddlers, and preschoolers and their families. Includes instruction in developmental psychology, cognitive and biological development, social and emotional development, research methods, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance research in adaptive learning systems by developing computational models to optimize personalized educational content delivery in large-scale online learning environments. A critical challenge in instructional design is the dynamic alignment of multimedia resources, assessment tools, and pedagogical strategies with diverse learner needs, particularly when operating at scale. Current systems often rely on static rulesets or simplistic recommendation algorithms, limiting their ability to process multimodal learner data (e.g., interaction logs, assessment performance, and biometric feedback) in real time. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep reinforcement learning models on heterogeneous educational datasets. The computational approach involves three phases: 1) Parallelized preprocessing of terabyte-scale learner interaction data from MOOC platforms using distributed computing pipelines, 2) Training of transformer-based architectures to model learner behavior sequences and knowledge state trajectories, and 3) GPU-accelerated simulations of virtual classroom environments to test instructional interventions. The project will utilize HPC capabilities for hyperparameter optimization across competing model architectures and large-batch training with synthetic data augmentation to improve generalization. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time adaptive content generation validated through A/B testing with 50,000+ learners across three partner online education platforms. This research will contribute novel methodologies for computational instructional design, enabling more effective scaling of personalized learning technologies while maintaining rigorous privacy-preserving data practices. The resulting models and simulation tools will be disseminated to the educational research community, providing infrastructure for future investigations into human-computer interaction patterns and cognitive load optimization in technology-mediated learning environments.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing and integrating technology into educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, utilizing technology for assessment, multimedia instruction, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in modeling and analyzing complex ballet movement patterns to advance research in choreographic preservation, pedagogical innovation, and biomechanical efficiency. While ballet relies on embodied knowledge transmission, current methods for documenting choreography (e.g., Labanotation, video) lack the granularity to capture nuanced physiological and spatial relationships critical for technical training and archival fidelity. We propose developing a computational framework to process high-resolution motion capture data from professional dancers performing canonical ballet repertoire, integrating biomechanical metrics with stylistic annotations. The research will employ graph neural networks to model dynamic interactions between body segments during jumps, turns, and port de bras, while reinforcement learning algorithms will simulate adaptive coaching strategies for technique optimization. A parallelized pipeline will process terabytes of 3D kinematic data, requiring GPU-accelerated computing to train models on heterogeneous movement vocabularies across ballet styles (e.g., Vaganova vs. Bournonville). Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-access repository of computationally annotated ballet sequences, linking motion data to historical stylistic descriptors; (2) predictive models identifying injury-risk movement signatures in training regimens; and (3) tools for generating augmented feedback interfaces for dance education. By leveraging high-performance computing to bridge qualitative artistic traditions with quantitative movement analysis, this work aims to establish new methodologies for preserving choreographic heritage while advancing evidence-based approaches to dancer training. The computational infrastructure requested will enable large-scale ensemble simulations and real-time processing of multi-modal data streams (motion, force plates, electromyography), which are intractable on local workstations. This resource will directly support the first systematic effort to computationally codify ballet’s physical and aesthetic complexities, with implications for dance science, digital humanities, and augmented performance technologies.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to express ideals and feelings through interpretation of classical dance choreography. Includes instruction in ballet exercise, solo and ensemble dance, history of ballet, ballet choreography, Laban notation, ballet technique, and interpretations of specific styles and schools.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize strategic decision-making in sport organization management through advanced computational modeling of dynamic, multi-variable systems inherent to athletic program operations. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks for simulating complex interactions between operational factors—including facility utilization patterns, staff scheduling constraints, financial variables, and participant engagement metrics—in sport and fitness environments. Current industry tools rely on simplified linear models that fail to capture the nonlinear relationships and emergent behaviors critical to organizational efficiency. We propose developing a high-fidelity agent-based model leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate facility ecosystems at unprecedented scale, incorporating real-world data streams from partner organizations spanning collegiate athletics, municipal recreation departments, and commercial fitness operators. The computational approach integrates discrete-event simulation for resource allocation patterns with machine learning components trained on historical operational data to predict stress points in scheduling systems and equipment utilization. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess thousands of scenario permutations to identify robust management strategies under variable conditions, including fluctuating membership demand and facility maintenance disruptions. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support framework capable of forecasting operational bottlenecks 6-18 months in advance with quantified confidence intervals, paired with prescriptive optimization algorithms for staff deployment and capital investment prioritization. The computational toolkit developed through this research will provide sport administrators with evidence-based strategies to balance service quality, financial sustainability, and infrastructure longevity—a critical advancement as organizations face increasing pressure to deliver data-driven management solutions in complex, resource-constrained environments.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized learning pathways for adult literacy learners through adaptive, AI-driven analysis of multimodal interaction data. Adult literacy education faces unique challenges, including heterogeneous learner backgrounds, variable motivation, and the need for functional skill application in real-world contexts. Traditional methods often rely on static curricula or instructor intuition, which struggle to address these complexities at scale. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model diverse datasets—including written responses, speech recordings, eye-tracking metrics, and behavioral engagement patterns—from adult learners interacting with digital literacy platforms. The research will employ transformer-based neural architectures to perform real-time natural language processing (NLP) of learner-generated text and speech, combined with temporal convolutional networks to analyze non-linguistic behavioral signals. These models will be integrated through a reinforcement learning framework that simulates iterative tutor-learner interactions, enabling the system to predict optimal instructional interventions based on evolving learner states. By parallelizing training across GPU nodes, we aim to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional, longitudinal interaction data from a target cohort of 5,000+ learners. The resulting system will generate actionable metrics for tutors, such as dynamic skill gap visualizations and context-aware resource recommendations, while preserving explainability through attention mechanism analysis. Outcomes will advance the scalability of precision education in adult literacy contexts, offering empirically validated strategies for balancing foundational skill development with immediate practical application. This work contributes to emerging interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computational pedagogy, adult learning theory, and human-AI collaboration, with potential applications in community education programs and workforce development initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as instructors and mentors for adults in basic or functional literacy programs in school, institutional, community, and private settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate change and anthropogenic land-use patterns on biodiversity in critical forest ecosystems, with a focus on identifying conservation priorities in rapidly changing regions. Current models often lack the resolution and integration of socio-environmental drivers necessary to inform adaptive management strategies. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run spatially explicit, dynamic simulations that couple ecological niche models, climate projections, and land-use change data at unprecedented scales. The computational approach will integrate multi-decadal remote sensing datasets, species occurrence records, and regional climate models (RCMs) within a Bayesian hierarchical framework to quantify uncertainty in biodiversity responses. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to identify non-linear relationships between ecosystem health metrics and stressors such as temperature extremes, habitat fragmentation, and resource extraction patterns. These workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and iterative parameter optimization, necessitating HPC capabilities. The resulting models will predict shifts in species distributions and ecosystem services under multiple climate scenarios, enabling the identification of regions most vulnerable to cascading biodiversity loss. Outcomes will directly support conservation planning by highlighting corridors for assisted species migration and zones requiring urgent policy intervention. By quantifying trade-offs between economic development and ecological resilience, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in environmental decision-making tools. The scalability of the framework will allow future adaptation to other ecosystems, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration across environmental science, computational modeling, and policy analysis. Successful implementation will provide stakeholders with actionable, data-driven strategies to mitigate anthropogenic impacts on natural resources while addressing socio-economic realities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on environment-related issues using scientific, social scientific, or humanistic approaches or a combination. Includes instruction in the basic principles of ecology and environmental science and related subjects such as policy, politics, law, economics, social aspects, planning, pollution control, natural resources, and the interactions of human beings and nature.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges in systematically analyzing the syntactic and lexical evolution of Dutch dialects and Creole varieties, which remain understudied due to the scale and heterogeneity of textual sources. Traditional philological methods struggle to manage the vast corpora spanning medieval manuscripts, early modern print sources, and contemporary digital texts, alongside Dutch Creoles with divergent grammatical structures. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational linguistics approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will compile and preprocess a multi-register corpus of over 10 million tokens, integrating historical Dutch texts, modern dialectal data, and Creole documents. Using NLP pipelines optimized for parallel processing, we will perform large-scale tokenization, morphological analysis, and dependency parsing to track syntactic shifts across time and space. Machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures, will be trained to identify latent patterns in lexical variation and contact-induced changes in Creole morphology. HPC infrastructure is critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training deep neural networks on heterogeneous text data and running comparative phylogenetic algorithms to model dialectal relationships. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus, novel findings on the divergence and convergence of Dutch varieties, and methodological advances in applying computational methods to low-resource historical languages. This research will enhance understanding of Dutch linguistic heritage, support preservation efforts for endangered Creoles, and provide a scalable framework for similar studies in other language families.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Dutch language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; literature; Dutch Creoles; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Archival institutions face escalating challenges in managing exponentially growing volumes of digitized and born-digital records, particularly those with complex formats (e.g., multimedia, dynamic web content, or interactive datasets). Traditional archival workflows struggle to scale efficiently, risking data degradation, incomplete metadata generation, and accessibility barriers. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational frameworks for automating and optimizing archival processes, with a focus on preserving context-rich digital materials and enabling scalable access. The research centers on three interconnected objectives: (1) designing machine learning models to identify, classify, and extract metadata from heterogeneous digital collections, (2) simulating long-term digital preservation environments to test format migration strategies under diverse technological constraints, and (3) creating parallelized workflows for integrity verification of large-scale archival holdings. Computational methods will include natural language processing for contextual analysis of unstructured text, computer vision techniques for image and video appraisal, and distributed computing architectures to manage petabytes of data. HPC resources are critical to train models on diverse archival corpora, replicate multi-decade preservation scenarios, and process high-resolution multimedia assets efficiently. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated metadata enhancement, predictive models to prioritize at-risk digital objects, and benchmarks for evaluating computational preservation efficacy. By integrating archival theory with scalable computational practices, this project aims to redefine stewardship paradigms for complex digital collections, reduce manual labor in archival workflows, and ensure equitable access to culturally significant materials. The work will establish methodological precedents for computational archival science, offering transferable strategies for institutions navigating resource limitations while confronting the technical and ethical complexities of 21st-century digital preservation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to identify, manage, preserve, and make available records with long-term value for documentation, legal, research, and other purposes. Includes instruction in appraisal and collection development, information and records management, archival preservation, access systems, management of electronic records, archival outreach, and legal and ethical issues.

abstract: The integration of multi-scale clinical laboratory data—including histopathological images, genomic profiles, and clinical metadata—remains a critical challenge in advancing diagnostic precision for complex diseases such as cancer and autoimmune disorders. Current methodologies often fail to efficiently synthesize these heterogeneous datasets, limiting the ability to identify subtle anatomic abnormalities or correlate molecular signatures with disease progression. This project proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, integrative analysis of multimodal pathology data. The research will focus on creating machine learning models to automate the detection of diagnostically significant features in whole-slide imaging (WSI) of tissue samples, coupled with genomic variant prioritization pipelines to uncover biomarkers predictive of clinical outcomes. Computational methods will include deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for WSI segmentation, graph-based algorithms for spatial transcriptomics integration, and federated learning architectures to maintain patient privacy while aggregating data across institutional partners. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of high-resolution imaging data, train complex models with millions of parameters, and perform genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for automated identification of underrecognized histologic patterns in renal and hepatic biopsies, (2) predictive models linking tumor microenvironment features to immunotherapy responses, and (3) open-source tools for quality control in digital pathology workflows. The project will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in anatomic pathology while providing a template for computational pathology resource sharing. By bridging gaps between traditional morphologic analysis and modern omics technologies, this work aims to establish scalable computational strategies for personalized disease classification, ultimately reducing diagnostic turnaround times and improving reproducibility in clinical laboratories.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cognitive workload and decision-making accuracy in complex human-machine systems, with a focus on optimizing interface design to enhance performance and reduce operational errors. While existing models of cognitive load provide foundational insights, they often lack the granularity to account for real-world variability in task demands, individual differences, and dynamic system feedback. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate human-system interactions at scale. Agent-based models will be developed to represent heterogeneous user populations, incorporating psychophysiological data (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency) from empirical studies to parameterize agents’ cognitive processing and adaptive behaviors. Monte Carlo simulations will explore system performance under stochastic task conditions, while machine learning techniques will identify critical design thresholds associated with performance degradation or error escalation. The HPC environment is essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of multi-agent scenarios, iterative parameter optimization, and real-time analysis of high-dimensional interaction data. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for interface customization based on user cognitive profiles, evidence-based recommendations for error mitigation in safety-critical systems (e.g., aviation, medical technology), and methodological advancements in modeling human factors at ecological scales. By integrating computational rigor with human-centered design principles, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of cognitive resilience in sociotechnical systems while delivering actionable tools for practitioners. The requested resources will directly support the generation of open-access simulation platforms and datasets to catalyze interdisciplinary collaboration in human factors research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to understand of interactions among humans and other elements of a system. Includes instruction in applying theory, principles, data and methods to design in order to optimize human well-being and overall system performance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and optimize multimodal corporate communication strategies in dynamic, globalized environments. While corporate communications play a critical role in organizational success, existing frameworks often fail to account for the real-time interplay between linguistic patterns, visual media, cultural variables, and stakeholder network dynamics. The computational complexity of modeling these interdependent factors at scale—particularly across multilingual datasets and evolving digital platforms—exceeds the capacity of conventional analytical tools. This project proposes the development of an adaptive neural architecture combining transformer-based language models, computer vision algorithms, and graph neural networks to simulate communication impact across heterogeneous stakeholder ecosystems. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale datasets comprising internal memos, social media interactions, crisis response transcripts, and visual branding materials, while incorporating real-time cultural sentiment metrics and geopolitical event data. Key challenges include implementing attention mechanisms that weight communication elements across modalities, optimizing distributed training for temporal network embeddings, and validating model outputs against organizational performance metrics. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting communication cascade effects, identifying latent cultural biases in content dissemination, and generating adaptive messaging recommendations during crisis scenarios. By enabling granular analysis of communication efficacy across spatial, temporal, and cultural dimensions, this research aims to establish computational benchmarks for strategic corporate communications while addressing critical gaps in scalability and predictive accuracy. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive multimodal fusion tasks, parallelized hyperparameter optimization across communication scenarios, and large-scale simulations of stakeholder network evolution. Results will provide actionable insights for optimizing global communication pipelines while advancing methodological integration between computational linguistics, organizational behavior, and decision science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function in an organization as a composer, editor, and proofreader of business or business-related communications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of novel ceramic materials and glazes through predictive modeling and simulation, addressing a critical gap in the empirical trial-and-error methods that dominate ceramic arts. Traditional approaches to formulating glazes and optimizing kiln firing conditions are time-intensive, resource-heavy, and limited by the physical constraints of material experimentation. By integrating computational chemistry, thermodynamics, and machine learning, this research aims to simulate the molecular behavior of clay bodies and glaze components under varying thermal and atmospheric conditions. Key objectives include modeling phase transitions in crystalline glazes, predicting crack propagation in clay substrates during drying and firing, and optimizing kiln temperature profiles for energy efficiency and artistic outcomes. Finite element analysis (FEA) will be employed to simulate thermal stress distributions in ceramic structures, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will explore interactions between organic additives and inorganic glaze matrices. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on datasets of historical and contemporary ceramic artworks to propose innovative texture and color combinations. The computational workflows will be validated through parallel physical experiments, with iterative feedback loops refining model accuracy. Expected outcomes include open-access databases of simulated glaze properties, predictive tools for reducing material waste in studio practice, and new methods for replicating historical ceramic techniques with modern sustainability standards. By bridging computational science and ceramic arts, this project aims to establish a framework for data-driven artistic innovation while preserving craft traditions, ultimately expanding the technical and expressive possibilities of the medium.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: Electromechanical systems are increasingly complex, integrating mechanical, electrical, and control components to meet demands for automation, energy efficiency, and precision. A critical challenge lies in modeling and optimizing these systems under dynamic, real-world conditions, where nonlinear interactions between domains lead to computationally intensive simulations that exceed the capabilities of standard computing resources. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, multiphysics simulations of advanced electromechanical systems, such as hybrid robotic actuators and energy-harvesting devices. The research will focus on developing coupled finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to study thermal, structural, and electromagnetic behaviors concurrently. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization and predictive maintenance algorithms. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers in ANSYS Mechanical and COMSOL Multiphysics, with custom Python scripts for data integration and control system emulation. Expected outcomes include validated models for high-torque, low-latency servo mechanisms and thermally stable power electronics, which will inform prototype development and testing. By resolving multiphysics bottlenecks in simulation scalability, this work aims to reduce iterative design cycles by 40–60% compared to traditional methods. The results will advance electromechanical system reliability and energy efficiency, with direct applications in smart manufacturing, renewable energy infrastructure, and autonomous robotics. Furthermore, the project will provide training for undergraduate and graduate students in HPC-driven engineering design, strengthening institutional expertise in computational electromechanics. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the tera-scale datasets and real-time co-simulation demands inherent to this multidisciplinary research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing and testing automated, servomechanical, and other electromechanical systems. Includes instruction in prototype testing, manufacturing and operational testing, systems analysis and maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, installation, and maintenance of overhead and underground electrical and communication infrastructure, with a focus on improving safety, efficiency, and resilience in linework operations. Aging power grids, increasing demand for reliable broadband connectivity, and climate-driven stressors such as extreme weather necessitate innovative approaches to infrastructure planning. Current industry practices rely heavily on manual inspections and static safety margins, which lack predictive capabilities for dynamic risks like equipment fatigue, thermal expansion in high-voltage lines, or soil instability near underground cables. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in power distribution systems. Computational workflows will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) to model mechanical stresses on utility poles and towers under wind and ice loads, machine learning algorithms trained on historical fault data to predict cable degradation patterns, and geospatial modeling to assess trenching routes for underground fiber-optic networks. Large-scale simulations will evaluate the cascading impacts of equipment failures on grid stability, while reinforcement learning frameworks will optimize real-time decision-making for emergency repairs. By coupling these models with LiDAR-derived terrain data and real-time sensor inputs, the project aims to generate adaptive risk assessment tools for lineworkers, including dynamic load-calculation systems for crane operations near live conductors and probabilistic maps of excavation hazards. Outcomes will include open-source simulation modules for training programs, validated against field data from partner utilities, and a digital twin framework to test infrastructure upgrades under climate change scenarios. This research will directly enhance the technical precision of lineworker education, reduce occupational hazards through predictive analytics, and inform standards for next-generation smart grid deployments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain and repair local, long-distance, and rural electric power cables and communication lines; erect and construct pole and tower lines; and install underground lines and cables. Includes instruction in cable installation and repair, fibre-optic technology, trenching, mobile equipment and crane operation, high-voltage installations, maintenance and inspection, safety, remote communications, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly threatened by anthropogenic stressors, including nutrient pollution, climate change, and invasive species, yet predicting their ecological responses remains a critical challenge in limnology. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to simulate multi-trophic interactions and emergent ecosystem dynamics in temperate lakes under varying disturbance regimes. The research combines long-term limnological datasets (water chemistry, plankton communities, fish populations) with spatially explicit environmental data to parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) and hydrodynamic-biogeochemical models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve complex feedbacks among physical lake processes (e.g., stratification, nutrient mixing), species behavior (e.g., predator-prey dynamics, algal bloom formation), and stochastic disturbance events (e.g., heatwaves, pollutant pulses). Parallelized simulations will assess how biodiversity loss and shifting thermal regimes alter ecosystem stability across gradients of lake depth, trophic status, and connectivity. Machine learning workflows will further identify early warning signals of regime shifts from multidimensional output data. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into resilience thresholds for keystone aquatic species, spatially resolved projections of habitat suitability under climate scenarios, and scalable methods to prioritize lakes for conservation interventions. By bridging ecological theory with computational scalability, this work will advance predictive capacity for freshwater resource management while addressing fundamental questions in aquatic community ecology. The requested allocation supports iterative model calibration, large ensemble simulations (>10,000 core-hours), and high-dimensional data synthesis, enabling novel analyses of cross-scale interactions that cannot be feasibly studied through empirical approaches alone.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the ecology and behavior of microbes, plants, and animals inhabiting inland fresh waters such as lakes, ponds, rivers, creeks, estuaries, and wetlands. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; aquatic ecosystems; microbiology; mycology; botany; ichthyology; mammalogy; population biology and biodiversity; studies of specific species, phyla, and habitats; and applications to fields such as natural resources conservation, fisheries science, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making for elementary and middle school administrators by modeling the complex dynamics of school operations. School principals face multifaceted challenges in resource allocation, including balancing staffing needs, facility utilization, budget constraints, and safety protocols while addressing diverse student needs. Traditional qualitative approaches often struggle to account for the interdependencies among these variables. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create agent-based models (ABMs) simulating school environments. These models will integrate real-world data on student demographics, staff schedules, classroom capacities, and emergency response protocols to evaluate the impact of administrative decisions under varying scenarios. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical datasets to identify patterns in resource utilization and predict outcomes of policy adjustments. The computational workflow requires parallel processing to manage large-scale simulations of school districts, enabling sensitivity analyses of factors such as redistricting proposals, budget reallocations, or pandemic-style disruptions. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit that quantifies trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., class size reductions vs. specialist staffing levels) and generates evidence-based recommendations for equitable resource distribution. This work will advance computational approaches in educational leadership by providing administrators with predictive analytics capabilities traditionally unavailable at the K-8 level. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the combinatorial complexity of school systems, particularly when modeling longitudinal outcomes across multi-year budgetary cycles or assessing emergency preparedness scenarios requiring real-time simulation. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with statewide principal networks to bridge the gap between computational social science and practical school administration.
cip_title: Elementary and Middle School Administration/ Principalship
cip_definition: A program that focuses on educational administration at the elementary and middle school (K-7) levels and prepares individuals to serve as principals and masters of elementary and middle schools. Includes instruction in elementary and/or middle school education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, childhood and pre-adolescent growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing acute, life-threatening conditions in veterinary patients—such as sepsis, trauma, or multi-organ failure—demands advanced tools to optimize time-sensitive clinical decisions. Current protocols for emergency and critical care rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of physiological variables, comorbidities, and treatment responses in individual animals. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive modeling framework to analyze real-time and retrospective clinical data from veterinary intensive care units (ICUs). Leveraging electronic health records, continuous vital sign monitoring, and biomarker data from dogs and cats admitted to tertiary care facilities, we will train machine learning models to predict patient-specific risks of decompensation, treatment efficacy, and long-term outcomes. Computational workflows will integrate multi-modal datasets, including time-series hemodynamic parameters, laboratory results, and imaging findings, to simulate disease trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The models will employ ensemble learning and mechanistic modeling to address data sparsity and physiological heterogeneity inherent in veterinary critical care. By deploying these tools on HPC infrastructure, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional data and enable real-time decision support during emergencies. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for early detection of sepsis-induced organ dysfunction, optimized fluid resuscitation strategies, and personalized prognostic scoring systems. This work will provide a foundation for data-driven critical care protocols, directly improving survival rates and resource allocation in veterinary ICUs while advancing translational insights into human-animal comparative medicine. The requested computing resources are essential for scaling complex simulations, hyperparameter optimization, and validation across diverse patient cohorts.
cip_title: Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care Medicine
cip_definition: Research focused on the emergency treatment and management of care for animals with acutely life-threatening conditions which may include multiple organ failure. May included related research in the management of critical care units, emergency procedures, and long-term care of critically diseased animals.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the systemic impacts of tax law complexity on compliance behavior and revenue outcomes in U.S. jurisdictions. Tax law’s intricate regulatory frameworks, coupled with dynamic interactions between taxpayers, policymakers, and enforcement mechanisms, present a computational challenge that traditional legal or economic methodologies struggle to address at scale. The research problem centers on quantifying how iterative changes to tax code provisions—such as deductions, credits, and reporting requirements—influence compliance strategies, enforcement efficacy, and long-term fiscal equity. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations, the project will simulate taxpayer decision-making under varying regulatory scenarios, incorporating real-world data from IRS filings, audit outcomes, and macroeconomic trends. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in historical noncompliance risks, while natural language processing (NLP) will parse textual legal ambiguities in tax statutes and case law to parameterize model inputs. The computational approach requires parallelized processing to manage the high dimensionality of taxpayer agents (millions of heterogeneous entities) and stochastic legal-environment variables. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to assess the downstream effects of proposed tax reforms, such as the Inflation Reduction Act’s corporate minimum tax provisions, on compliance burdens and revenue collection. By bridging computational social science with tax law scholarship, this work aims to generate actionable insights for policymakers to design equitable, efficient tax systems while reducing administrative friction. The requested HPC resources will enable iterative scenario testing at unprecedented granularity, fostering a novel evidence-based paradigm for tax law analysis that transcends traditional doctrinal or qualitative approaches. Outputs will include open-access datasets, visualizations of policy trade-offs, and a scalable computational toolkit for interdisciplinary tax research.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of tax law and taxation procedures in U.S. or Canadian jurisdictions affecting individuals and corporations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex dynamics of digital engagement and spiritual formation among adolescents in contemporary youth ministry contexts. As digital platforms increasingly mediate religious practices, ministry leaders face challenges in understanding how online interactions—such as virtual worship, social media discourse, and AI-driven pastoral tools—shape youth identity, community belonging, and ethical decision-making. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and nonlinearity of these interactions, necessitating computational approaches. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze multi-modal datasets, including anonymized text from youth-led prayer forums, video transcripts of virtual small-group sessions, and longitudinal survey responses measuring spiritual resilience. Agent-based modeling will simulate how algorithmic content delivery on platforms like TikTok and Discord influences the spread of theological ideas within adolescent networks. Additionally, graph neural networks will map evolving peer influence patterns across hybrid (online/in-person) ministry ecosystems. By integrating computational social science with practical theology, this project aims to identify scalable strategies for mitigating digital polarization while fostering inclusive spiritual growth. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time analysis of youth engagement metrics, predictive models to optimize ministry resource allocation, and ethical guidelines for AI-augmented pastoral care. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training deep learning architectures on sensitive conversational datasets, and running large-scale simulations of emergent community behaviors. This interdisciplinary work bridges gaps between humanities research, adolescent psychology, and computational innovation, offering novel methodologies for faith-based organizations navigating rapidly evolving digital landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing social service delivery systems for vulnerable populations. Social work interventions, such as child welfare case management and disability counseling, involve complex, dynamic interactions between clients, providers, and policy constraints. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model these systems at scale, limiting the ability to predict service gaps or evaluate policy impacts in real time. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that simulates service access patterns, resource allocation decisions, and longitudinal client outcomes across heterogeneous populations. The ABM will integrate anonymized administrative data from multiple agencies (e.g., foster care placements, unemployment claims, and mental health service utilization) to parameterize agents representing clients, social workers, and institutions. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions over multi-year time horizons while incorporating stochastic variables like economic shocks or staffing shortages. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to test intervention scenarios—such as reallocating caseworkers during crisis events or adjusting eligibility thresholds—with statistically robust sample sizes. Expected outcomes include identifying resource distribution strategies that reduce service delays for high-risk groups and generating predictive metrics to guide proactive policy adjustments. By quantifying trade-offs in equity, cost, and administrative burden, this work aims to provide actionable tools for social service administrators while advancing computational social work as a methodological discipline. The project will also produce open-source code to help non-technical stakeholders visualize system dynamics, fostering collaboration between researchers and practitioners in public administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the professional practice of social welfare administration and counseling, and that focus on the study of organized means of providing basic support services for vulnerable individuals and groups. Includes instruction in social welfare policy; case work planning; social counseling and intervention strategies; administrative procedures and regulations; and specific applications in areas such as child welfare and family services, probation, employment services, and disability counseling.

abstract: The increasing complexity of veterinary administrative operations, driven by evolving regulatory requirements, client expectations, and data management demands, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize workflows and decision-making. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model and analyze large-scale administrative datasets from veterinary practices, including client interactions, appointment scheduling, billing cycles, and inventory logistics. Current systems often rely on fragmented software solutions that lack interoperability, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and compliance tracking. The research problem centers on identifying systemic bottlenecks and predicting operational risks through computational simulations that integrate heterogeneous data streams, such as electronic health records, staff performance metrics, and supply chain variables. Leveraging parallelized agent-based modeling and machine learning algorithms, the project will simulate clinic operations under varying constraints (e.g., staffing shortages, seasonal demand fluctuations) to generate adaptive resource allocation strategies. A key innovation lies in applying graph-based network analysis to map dependencies between administrative tasks and clinical outcomes, enabling proactive adjustments to workflow prioritization. The computational architecture will utilize GPU-accelerated clustering techniques to process real-time data from anonymized multi-site veterinary practices, ensuring scalability while adhering to ethical standards for data privacy. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for veterinary administrators to optimize staffing schedules, inventory procurement, and compliance auditing cycles, with preliminary simulations targeting a 15–20% reduction in operational overhead. By bridging computational analytics and veterinary administrative science, this work establishes a foundation for data-driven governance in animal care facilities, addressing a critical gap in non-science and engineering research while advancing professional standards for operational efficiency in the sector.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to provide administrative support services in a veterinary office or animal care facility. Includes instruction in business office operations, customer service, principles of veterinary health care operations, record-keeping, veterinary terminology, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions aim to enhance patients’ functional independence, yet variability in individual responses to therapy remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, neurological, and environmental factors. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive computational models that optimize personalized OT intervention strategies. The proposed research will analyze multimodal datasets, including motion-capture recordings of patients with upper-limb mobility impairments, neuroimaging data, and longitudinal clinical outcomes from stroke and traumatic brain injury cohorts. Using scalable machine learning frameworks, we will train neural networks to identify patterns in motor recovery trajectories and simulate the biomechanical efficacy of different therapeutic exercises under varying physiological constraints. HPC resources are critical for handling the high dimensionality of these datasets, running parallelized simulations of musculoskeletal models, and performing real-time optimization of treatment parameters. Expected outcomes include a computational toolkit that predicts patient-specific responses to OT interventions, identifies optimal exercise regimens, and quantifies the biomechanical load thresholds to prevent injury during therapy. This work will advance the evidence base for precision OT by enabling data-driven clinical decision-making, potentially reducing trial-and-error approaches that delay patient progress. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and models to support broader research in rehabilitation sciences. By integrating computational modeling with clinical practice, this research aligns with the Pre-Occupational Therapy Studies program’s mission to prepare future practitioners for technology-driven healthcare environments, fostering innovation in therapeutic strategies and improving functional outcomes for diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: Maintaining the reliability and efficiency of modern energy systems demands advanced predictive and diagnostic capabilities, yet current maintenance practices often rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches that result in unnecessary downtime, resource waste, and safety risks. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize maintenance and repair protocols for heterogeneous energy infrastructure, including wind turbines, photovoltaic arrays, and grid-scale battery systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will integrate multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal, mechanical, and electrochemical degradation models) with machine learning algorithms trained on historical failure datasets and real-time sensor inputs. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent material stresses across varying operational conditions, automating anomaly detection in terabyte-scale sensor datasets, and optimizing repair schedules via combinatorial optimization algorithms. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulation of degradation pathways at component and system levels, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine maintenance strategies. Expected outcomes include predictive fault classification models with quantified uncertainty bounds, physics-informed digital twins for critical infrastructure, and adaptive decision-support tools for prioritizing repairs under resource constraints. By transitioning maintenance paradigms from heuristic to data-driven approaches, this work aims to reduce operational costs by an estimated 15–20% in modeled systems while extending asset lifespans. The resulting computational toolkit will be disseminated as open-source modules to support workforce training programs in energy systems technology, directly aligning with the program’s mission to advance technical proficiency in next-generation maintenance practices. This project’s integration of HPC-driven analytics with applied energy systems repair represents a novel cross-disciplinary contribution to sustainable infrastructure management.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The spatial organization and dynamic behavior of cells within complex anatomical systems are fundamental to understanding tissue morphogenesis, homeostasis, and repair. Traditional experimental approaches in cell biology and anatomy often lack the resolution to capture multicellular interactions across 3D anatomical scales, limiting insights into how cellular dynamics translate into emergent tissue-level structures. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a multiscale computational model of cell-matrix interactions within vertebrate limb bud development—a classical system for studying anatomical patterning. The research will integrate high-resolution imaging data from confocal microscopy and histological sections with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how localized cellular behaviors (e.g., adhesion, migration, and differentiation) drive the formation of spatially organized tissues. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the iterative simulation of millions of interacting cellular agents within a 3D extracellular matrix environment, incorporating biophysical parameters such as tensile forces and matrix stiffness. Computational outputs will be validated against time-lapse imaging of ex vivo embryonic mouse limb cultures and compared to anatomical landmarks in developing human embryos. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework linking subcellular signaling to regional anatomical patterning, (2) identification of critical mechanical and biochemical thresholds required for robust tissue organization, and (3) mechanistic insights into developmental defects such as syndactyly or limb hypoplasia. By leveraging HPC to resolve multiscale dynamics, this work will advance the field of developmental anatomy by providing a quantitative, systems-level understanding of how cellular heterogeneity gives rise to anatomical complexity. The computational tools developed will be adaptable to studying tissue regeneration and degenerative diseases, offering broader applications for translational research in congenital anomalies and musculoskeletal disorders.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: An integrated, combined program that focuses on the scientific study of cell structure, function, and dynamics within the context of organismic, regional, and gross anatomical systems. Includes instruction in molecular biology, cell biology and histology, structural biology, anatomy, embryology, endocrinology, and applications to specific systems, diseases, defects, and processes.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how organizational leadership practices in higher education institutions influence workforce development outcomes during periods of rapid technological change. As institutions face growing demands to align training programs with evolving industry needs, leaders must navigate complex decision-making processes involving stakeholder priorities, resource constraints, and workforce skill gaps. Current qualitative approaches provide limited capacity to model dynamic interactions between these variables at scale. We propose leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate decision pathways in institutional leadership teams and predict their downstream effects on workforce readiness. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing longitudinal workforce data from public repositories (e.g., IPEDS, O*NET) and running thousands of parameterized simulations capturing diverse leadership scenarios. The ABM framework will model agents representing administrators, faculty, and industry partners, incorporating behavioral patterns derived from interview transcripts and policy documents analyzed through transformer-based NLP models. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of leadership strategies that optimize alignment between institutional training investments and regional labor market needs, and 2) predictive metrics for evaluating how decision timelines affect workforce retention in critical technology sectors. Results will provide actionable insights for designing leadership development programs that enhance adaptive capacity in educational organizations, particularly regarding AI integration and digital transformation challenges. By combining computational social science methods with human resource development theory, this work advances empirical foundations for data-driven leadership in education while demonstrating novel applications of HPC resources to administrative decision science.
cip_title: Education and Human Resource Studies/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: The emergence and spread of zoonotic pathogens at the interface of wildlife, livestock, and human populations present complex challenges to global public health and food security. Current epidemiological models often lack the resolution to account for dynamic, multi-host transmission networks, environmental drivers, and heterogeneous data sources, limiting their utility in predicting outbreak trajectories or optimizing intervention strategies. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to model zoonotic disease transmission dynamics, with a focus on pathogens impacting both animal health and food safety (e.g., Salmonella, avian influenza). Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement spatially explicit agent-based models (ABMs) integrating real-world datasets on livestock movements, wildlife habitat overlap, climate variables, and genomic surveillance data. These models will simulate pathogen spread across species barriers, incorporating stochastic transmission events, host immunity landscapes, and anthropogenic factors such as agricultural practices. Parallelized parameter sweeps and Bayesian calibration methods will be used to infer transmission pathways and identify high-risk spatiotemporal interfaces. Additionally, machine learning approaches will analyze model outputs to prioritize surveillance targets and forecast intervention efficacy under varying scenarios. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the ABMs operating at regional scales with millions of agents and the integration of high-dimensional genomic and environmental data—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and storage. Outcomes will advance predictive capacity for zoonotic hotspots, inform One Health policies to mitigate cross-species transmission, and provide actionable insights for veterinary public health practitioners. This work will also establish an open-source toolkit for adaptive disease modeling, enhancing collaborative responses to emerging threats at the intersection of animal and human health.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology, and Public Health
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the prevention and control of communicable animal diseases, diseases affecting humans, and prepares veterinarians to function as public health specialists. Includes instruction in animal epidemiology, biostatistics, food safety and quality assurance, food toxicology, zoonotic and infectious diseases, disease vectors and transference, production medicine, animal health, veterinary public health practice, and inspection and evaluation methods.

abstract: The rapid evolution of labor markets driven by technological advancements necessitates dynamic approaches to workforce education. Current methods for curriculum design often rely on static competencies, leading to misalignment between training outcomes and employer needs. This project addresses the challenge of developing adaptive, data-driven strategies for workforce education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale labor market data and simulate training interventions. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including job postings, occupational forecasts, and skills taxonomies, to model emerging skill demands across industries. Machine learning techniques, such as natural language processing and time-series forecasting, will identify temporal and sector-specific trends, while graph-based analytics will map interdependencies among technical and transversal competencies. Agent-based simulations will evaluate the efficacy of different instructional strategies in virtual learning environments, optimizing for scalability and regional economic variability. The computational intensity of processing multi-terabyte datasets and running iterative simulations necessitates HPC resources to achieve feasible runtime and model fidelity. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for anticipating skill gaps, an open-source toolkit for curriculum optimization, and evidence-based guidelines for integrating real-time labor market analytics into pedagogical decision-making. By enabling educators to design responsive programs aligned with industry trajectories, this research aims to enhance workforce readiness and reduce skill mismatches in rapidly changing economic landscapes.
detailed_field: Adult, continuing, and workforce education and development
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach programs designed to develop or upgrade specific employment-related knowledge and skills in various settings, and to various age groups.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance and fault diagnosis for complex electrical and electronic systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current diagnostic protocols in electrical/electronics repair often rely on reactive or rule-based strategies, which struggle to adapt to dynamic operating conditions, leading to unplanned downtime, costly repairs, and safety risks. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and multiphysics simulations to model equipment degradation, predict failure modes, and optimize repair workflows. HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on large-scale datasets of sensor telemetry, historical maintenance records, and synthetic fault scenarios generated via finite element analysis (FEA). These models will simulate thermal, mechanical, and electrical stress interactions in critical components such as power converters, motor drives, and embedded control systems. Parallelized computation will facilitate parameter sweeps across diverse operating environments and accelerated testing of hypothetical failure cascades. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that identifies emerging faults with >90% accuracy 48–72 hours prior to failure, validated through case studies on industrial automation systems and renewable energy infrastructure. The project will also produce open-source simulation templates to help technicians visualize failure mechanisms and test repair strategies in silico. By bridging computational modeling with hands-on repair practices, this work aims to advance adaptive maintenance paradigms, reduce lifecycle costs of electrical systems, and inform curriculum updates for technician training programs. The requested HPC allocation is critical to handling the project’s computational demands, including GPU-accelerated ML training, distributed FEA jobs, and real-time digital twin simulations requiring low-latency data processing.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronics equipment installation and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that optimize decision-making processes in educational supervision and curriculum administration. A critical challenge in educational leadership is the dynamic allocation of instructional resources—such as staff, training, and curricular materials—across diverse learning environments. Traditional methods for modeling these complex systems are limited in scalability and fail to account for real-time variables, including fluctuating student needs, staff capacity, and interdisciplinary program requirements. To address this gap, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate interactions between administrators, educators, and students under varying resource constraints, using anonymized district-level datasets on staffing patterns, student performance, and budget allocations. Second, machine learning algorithms will identify optimal supervisory strategies by analyzing historical outcomes and iteratively refining predictive models. The HPC environment is essential for processing large-scale datasets (spanning 10+ years from 200+ institutions) and running parallel simulations to evaluate thousands of resource allocation scenarios. Expected outcomes include a framework for real-time decision support in curriculum supervision, validated through retrospective comparison with existing administrative data. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing inefficiencies in staff deployment and curricular resource distribution, directly addressing priorities in education leadership training programs. By open-sourcing the computational tools developed, the project aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven supervision in K-12 and higher education settings, advancing the integration of computational analytics into administrative practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable livestock production necessitates advanced genetic strategies to improve disease resistance, productivity, and environmental adaptability in agricultural animals. Current genomic selection models struggle to account for the complexity of polygenic traits, genotype-by-environment interactions, and the integration of multi-omics data, limiting their predictive accuracy and applicability across diverse populations. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing scalable computational frameworks for optimizing breeding programs using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose to analyze whole-genome sequencing data from cattle, poultry, and swine populations (n ≈ 50,000 animals) alongside longitudinal environmental and phenotypic records to identify causal variants, epigenetic modifiers, and adaptive gene networks. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and gradient-boosted trees, will be implemented to model non-linear genetic effects and predict trait expression under varying management and climate scenarios. Bayesian hierarchical models will concurrently estimate population parameters while accounting for pedigree structure and spatial-temporal covariates. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized genomic prediction tools, Markov chain Monte Carlo samplers, and distributed tensor operations to process terabytes of genomic data. Expected outcomes include novel breeding value estimation methods with improved generalizability, open-source software for genomic selection under environmental constraints, and actionable insights into pleiotropic loci affecting multiple production traits. By enabling rapid analysis of complex genotype-phenotype-environment relationships at unprecedented scale, this research will directly inform breeding strategies to enhance animal welfare, reduce agricultural emissions, and secure food systems against climate variability. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive computations, iterative model training, and large-scale simulations of breeding program outcomes over generational timescales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural animal health, the development of new animal breeds, and the selective improvement of agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, animal health, animal husbandry, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Burmese language studies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze and model the linguistic and literary structures of Burmese texts. Despite its rich literary tradition and unique grammatical features, Burmese remains understudied in computational linguistics due to limited digitized corpora and a lack of language-specific tools. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers to enable large-scale textual analysis, syntactic parsing, and diachronic studies of Burmese literature, which are currently infeasible with standard computing resources. The project will compile and preprocess a diverse corpus spanning classical to modern Burmese texts, including rare manuscripts, using OCR and manual transcription. Computational methods will include the development of custom NLP pipelines for Burmese, integrating transformer-based models for syntactic and semantic analysis, and applying graph-based algorithms to map intertextual relationships in literary works. HPC resources are essential to train language models on distributed GPU clusters, process terabytes of text data, and run parallelized simulations to model language evolution across historical periods. Expected outcomes include the first open-access, annotated Burmese corpus with metadata, a suite of computational tools tailored to Burmese philology, and novel insights into stylistic shifts in Burmese literature linked to sociohistorical contexts. These resources will significantly advance research capabilities in Burmese studies, enabling quantitative literary analysis, cross-linguistic comparisons, and applications in language education or preservation. By democratizing access to scalable computational methods, this project aims to position Burmese language research within broader digital humanities discourse while preserving the linguistic heritage of Myanmar.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Burmese language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual and conceptual analysis of Catholic philosophical and theological writings, focusing on the evolution of key ethical frameworks in Catholic social thought and bioethics. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in doctrinal development, synthesizing interdisciplinary debates, and mapping the influence of classical philosophical traditions (e.g., Thomism) on modern Catholic ethical discourse. Current manual methods are insufficient to analyze the vast corpus of digitized primary texts (in Latin, Greek, and modern languages), conciliar documents, and scholarly commentaries, necessitating computational scalability. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for theological Latin and multilingual semantic analysis, to trace terminological shifts, argumentative structures, and cross-referential networks across centuries of Catholic writing. Topic modeling and sentiment analysis will quantify thematic emphasis in debates on issues such as human dignity, distributive justice, and biomedical ethics. Phylogenetic algorithms will model doctrinal "genealogies" to test hypotheses about the reception of Augustine, Aquinas, and other thinkers in 20th-century encyclicals.
