This work bridges gaps between traditional nuclear engineering and emerging computational techniques, advancing predictive capabilities for next-generation reactor systems while establishing open-source benchmarks for multiphysics integration in HPC environments. Successful implementation will enhance the viability of LFRs as low-carbon baseload power sources, supporting global decarbonization goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern theatrical productions, which integrate dynamic spatial, auditory, and narrative elements, presents significant challenges in pre-production planning and real-time performance optimization. Traditional rehearsal and design methods often rely on iterative physical adjustments, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and unable to model the interdependencies of variables such as actor positioning, acoustic propagation, lighting interactions, and audience immersion. This project proposes the development of a computational simulation framework to address these challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze multi-dimensional production parameters. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate actor movement patterns and ensemble coordination across diverse stage geometries, coupled with finite element analysis to predict acoustic behavior and lighting dispersion in complex set designs. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical performance data to identify optimal blocking strategies and emotional impact correlations, while real-time ray tracing will visualize audience sightline obstructions and spatial engagement metrics. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale parametric studies of design alternatives and predictive scenario testing. The outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for directors and production teams to virtually prototype stagings, quantify artistic choices, and preemptively resolve technical conflicts. By enabling data-informed creative decisions, this work aims to reduce production costs, minimize technical rehearsals, and enhance performative coherence. The project bridges computational analytics with artistic practice, establishing a methodological precedent for integrating HPC-driven simulation into performing arts pedagogy and professional theatrical workflows.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the cultural and textual dynamics of Irish identity formation across historical and diasporic contexts. The research problem centers on the fragmented nature of primary source materials—including digitized manuscripts, newspapers, folklore collections, and emigrant correspondence—which span multiple centuries, geographies, and formats. Traditional humanities methodologies struggle to systematically trace patterns of cultural transmission, linguistic evolution, or thematic continuity within such large, heterogeneous datasets. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to identify latent connections between Irish cultural production in Ireland and diaspora communities (e.g., North America, Australia) from the 18th to early 20th centuries. Key tasks include training custom transformer models on historical Irish English and Gaelic texts to detect semantic shifts in concepts like “community,” “exile,” or “heritage”; constructing co-occurrence networks to map the dissemination of literary motifs and oral traditions; and applying spatial-temporal modeling to correlate linguistic patterns with migration waves. The scale of data—over 500,000 pages of text and 10,000 archival records—requires distributed computing for parallelized text extraction, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale graph analytics. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated datasets, visualizations of cultural exchange pathways, and statistical frameworks for quantifying narrative persistence in diasporic contexts. This work aims to advance interdisciplinary Irish Studies by bridging qualitative cultural analysis with computational rigor, offering new insights into how collective memory and identity were negotiated across dispersed populations. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume and complexity, enabling methods impractical on local infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Ireland and the Irish Diaspora, from the early Christian period to the present.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between cultural narratives, collective memory, and the evolution of sports fandom through advanced computational modeling. The central problem lies in understanding how large-scale sociocultural dynamics—such as shifting gender norms, regional identity formation, and transgenerational storytelling—shape fan engagement patterns across different sports ecosystems. While qualitative studies have explored isolated aspects of sports culture, there remains a critical gap in quantitatively modeling these multidimensional interactions at population scales over decadal timeframes. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) frameworks enhanced with natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze historical sports media archives (1940-present), fan-generated content, and demographic datasets. High-performance computing resources are essential for constructing parallelized simulations that incorporate 1) neural language models trained on 80+ years of sports journalism, 2) spatial-temporal analyses of regional affiliation networks, and 3) dynamic belief systems reflecting evolving cultural values. The computational architecture will enable parameter sweeps across diverse historical contexts while maintaining fine-grained representations of individual and community-level decision-making processes. Expected outcomes include the development of novel metrics for measuring cultural inertia in sports traditions, predictive models of fandom migration during societal upheavals, and visualizations of narrative propagation pathways through fan communities. By creating the first computational framework that bridges historical sociology with sports studies, this work aims to provide athletic organizations and cultural institutions with evidence-based strategies for navigating rapidly changing landscapes of community engagement. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale text corpus analysis, and multi-agent simulation environments requiring petascale storage and high-memory nodes.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological, sociological, and historical aspects of sport and physical activity. Includes instruction in theory of sport, sport psychology, sport in American society, gender and race/ethnicity and sport, and sports history.

abstract: The administration of anesthetic agents requires precise titration to balance efficacy with patient safety, yet current protocols rely on generalized dosing models that inadequately account for dynamic intraoperative variables, including real-time biometric fluctuations and pharmacogenomic heterogeneity. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a machine learning framework to predict individualized anesthetic requirements using high-dimensional physiological, genomic, and pharmacokinetic data. The research will integrate multimodal inputs—including continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) waveforms, hemodynamic trends, and single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles—to model interpatient variability in drug metabolism and sedation depth. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets (>10 TB) from retrospective electronic health records and prospective intraoperative monitoring systems, enabling parallelized training of deep neural networks and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations. Key computational challenges include optimizing time-series analysis of EEG data to detect subclinical arousal states and resolving stochastic differential equations for real-time drug distribution modeling. The resulting predictive algorithms will be validated against clinical outcomes in a simulated surgical environment, with performance metrics compared to standard dosing protocols. Successfully linking patient-specific biological signatures to anesthetic responsiveness will advance precision sedation practices, reducing postoperative complications such as delirium and hemodynamic instability. This work bridges computational neuroscience, systems pharmacology, and clinical anesthesiology, establishing a novel paradigm for data-driven perioperative care. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to deliver an open-source software toolkit for anesthesiologist assistants to dynamically adjust anesthetic regimens, enhancing both patient safety and procedural efficiency in diverse surgical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in developing and implementing patient anesthesia care plans, including preoperative, surgical theater, recovery room, and postoperative/intensive care procedures. Includes instruction in patient data collection, catheter insertion, airway management and drug administration, assisting the administration and monitoring of regional and peripheral nerve blockades, support therapy, adjusting anesthetic levels during surgery, interoperative monitoring, postoperative procedures, pain clinics and patient education, and administrative tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cultural identity and intersectional gender narratives across Latin American and Caribbean digital archives through advanced computational text analysis. The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing vast, multilingual corpora—including historical newspapers, literary works, and grassroots publications—to trace evolving representations of marginalized communities and hybrid cultural expressions. Current methodologies in regional studies lack scalable tools to process heterogeneous, non-standardized texts spanning Spanish, Portuguese, Creole languages, and indigenous linguistic variants. Our approach integrates transformer-based natural language processing models optimized for low-resource languages with graph-based network analysis to map semantic shifts and discourse networks across temporal and geographic axes. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom multilingual language models on distributed text datasets (>10 TB), conducting parallelized sentiment and topic coherence analyses, and simulating cultural transmission dynamics via agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 20th-century Caribbean feminist writings, quantitative frameworks for assessing cultural hybridity in postcolonial contexts, and visual analytics tools to contextualize identity formation processes. By enabling large-scale interrogation of underrepresented narratives, this work aims to redefine methodological paradigms in area studies while informing contemporary debates on cultural preservation and inclusive historiography in digitization initiatives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the cascading impacts of dynamic cross-jurisdictional tax policies on multinational enterprise (MNE) decision-making in digitally integrated economies. The increasing complexity of global tax regimes—particularly with the rise of digital services taxes, cryptocurrency transaction reporting frameworks, and real-time VAT/GST systems—has created a computational challenge for simulating how MNEs adapt fiscal strategies across overlapping regulatory environments. Current analytical models struggle to account for high-dimensional variables, including real-time currency fluctuations, decentralized ledger transactions, and adaptive regulatory responses, which require iterative, agent-based simulations at scale. The project will develop a modular computational framework integrating stochastic optimization algorithms, multi-agent system (MAS) modeling, and machine learning-driven policy scenario generation. By simulating millions of parallel tax strategy permutations across synthetic but law-compliant jurisdictions, the system will identify emergent patterns in tax-efficient capital allocation, intellectual property licensing, and supply chain reconfiguration. The HPC environment is critical for managing the combinatorial explosion of scenarios arising from simultaneous consideration of 50+ national tax regimes, 10,000+ synthetic corporate entity structures, and sub-second market data updates. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible taxonomy of high-risk cross-border tax arbitrage patterns under proposed OECD framework updates, plus predictive metrics on how real-time tax data reporting requirements may influence blockchain-based accounting adoption. Results will provide policymakers and corporate strategists with evidence-based tools to anticipate systemic vulnerabilities in increasingly automated global tax ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide tax advice and management services to individuals and corporations. Includes instruction in tax law and regulations, tax record systems, individual and corporate income taxation, tax planning, partnerships and fiduciary relationships, estates and trusts, property depreciation, capital gains and losses, dispositions, transfers, liquidity, valuation, and applications to specific tax problems.

abstract: Sleep disorders present complex challenges in diagnosis and management, often requiring the integration of multimodal physiological data. Traditional polysomnographic analysis relies on manual scoring of sleep stages and events, a process limited by subjectivity, time-intensive protocols, and an inability to capture dynamic interactions between neurophysiological signals, cardiorespiratory patterns, and environmental factors. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model sleep architecture and disorder phenotypes using large-scale polysomnography datasets. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process and analyze terabytes of multichannel recordings (EEG, EMG, EOG, respiratory effort, SpO2) from 5,000+ clinical sleep studies, integrating concurrent actigraphy, environmental sensor data, and electronic health records. Machine learning pipelines will be optimized to identify latent patterns in sleep-wake transitions, autonomic instability during REM sleep, and microstructural biomarkers of neurodegenerative comorbidity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model upper airway collapse mechanisms in obstructive sleep apnea, correlating real-time pressure gradients with anatomical imaging data. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of signal decomposition tasks, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for event detection, and large-scale validation of predictive algorithms across heterogeneous patient subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) automated tools for quantifying sleep continuity disturbances with sub-second precision, (2) novel metrics linking sleep microstructure to cognitive decline trajectories, and (3) personalized airflow collapse risk profiles derived from biomechanical simulations. By advancing computational methods in polysomnography, this work aims to establish scalable infrastructure for precision sleep medicine, reducing diagnostic latency for rare parasomnias and improving prognostic accuracy in complex cases where sleep pathology intersects with neurological, metabolic, and cardiovascular disease states.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: Earth science educators face significant challenges in teaching complex, interconnected systems such as climate dynamics, geophysical processes, and planetary evolution, particularly when constrained by limited access to advanced computational tools. This project seeks to address this gap by developing and deploying high-fidelity, interactive earth system simulations tailored for classroom use. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to generate multi-scale models of geological and climatic phenomena, including real-time visualization of tectonic plate interactions, probabilistic wildfire spread under varying climate scenarios, and ocean-atmosphere feedback loops. These simulations will be integrated into modular teaching frameworks designed for pre-service and in-service earth science teachers, aligning with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) and inquiry-based pedagogy. Computational workflows will employ parallelized numerical solvers for partial differential equations governing fluid dynamics and heat transfer, coupled with machine learning emulators to reduce latency for classroom applications. The project will also analyze the scalability of adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques to balance resolution needs with computational costs. Expected outcomes include open-access simulation toolkits, lesson plans co-developed with educators, and quantitative assessments of how HPC-enabled visualization improves pedagogical efficacy. By bridging cutting-edge computational earth science with teacher training, this work aims to enhance STEM education quality, equipping educators to contextualize abstract concepts through data-driven, immersive learning experiences. The requested HPC allocation will directly support model development, parameter space exploration, and the creation of reproducible workflows for academic institutions lacking dedicated infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach earth science programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to advance personalized rehabilitation strategies for neuromusculoskeletal disorders by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific biomechanical and neurological interactions. Current rehabilitation protocols often adopt generalized approaches, leading to variable functional outcomes due to the complex interplay of tissue healing, neural adaptation, and biomechanical loading across diverse patient populations. To address this, we propose developing multiscale computational models that integrate neuromuscular activation patterns, joint kinematics, and tissue remodeling processes at unprecedented resolution. These models will be parameterized using patient data from motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging, requiring iterative simulations to optimize rehabilitation prescriptions. A key computational challenge involves solving coupled partial differential equations for soft tissue mechanics and neural signal propagation across anatomically accurate domains, necessitating GPU-accelerated finite element analysis and machine learning-based surrogate modeling. Additionally, we will employ ensemble machine learning techniques to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets (demographics, biomarkers, treatment histories) from our institution’s rehabilitation registry, aiming to identify predictors of optimal intervention timing and dosage. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to quantify uncertainty in model predictions and validate against longitudinal outcome data from ongoing clinical trials in post-stroke mobility recovery and spinal cord injury rehabilitation. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for virtual testing of rehabilitation strategies, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. This work will directly inform the design of adaptive rehabilitation protocols that dynamically respond to individual recovery trajectories, potentially decreasing time to functional independence by 15-30% in modeled cohorts. The requested resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale multimodal datasets and computationally intensive multiscale simulations within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, etiology, treatment, prevention and rehabilitation of neuromusculo-skeletal, cardiovascular, pulmonary and other system disorders common to patients of both sexes and all ages. May included related research in physical examinations, design and prescription of rehabilitation strategies and the supervision of rehabilitation teams.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing the thermal and power efficiency of next-generation computer processors through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As processor architectures scale toward smaller transistor sizes and higher component densities, managing heat dissipation and power distribution becomes increasingly complex, directly impacting device reliability and performance. Traditional empirical testing methods are insufficient for exploring the vast design space of modern multi-core processors and heterogenous computing units, necessitating high-fidelity simulations to guide hardware design. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model thermal gradients, material stress, and power delivery networks at the microarchitecture level. These simulations will integrate machine learning-driven optimization to iteratively refine cooling solutions, substrate materials, and power gating configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multi-physics interactions across nanometer-scale geometries and millisecond-scale operational cycles, which require parallelized solvers and large memory allocations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting thermal runaway thresholds, identifying optimal layouts for on-chip cooling structures, and proposing material interfaces to mitigate electromigration in high-current conditions. This work will directly support the development of energy-efficient processors for high-performance computing clusters and edge devices, while advancing methodologies for virtual prototyping in computer hardware design. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ design permutations, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating iteration cycles for industry partners in semiconductor manufacturing. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and collaboration with hardware testing laboratories to bridge computational predictions with empirical validation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: Soil microbial communities drive critical biogeochemical processes, yet their interactions with dynamic soil chemistry remain poorly quantified, limiting predictive understanding of soil carbon cycling and resilience. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating microbial genomic potential, metabolite exchange networks, and abiotic soil parameters to predict carbon stabilization mechanisms under varying agricultural management practices. Current models lack sufficient granularity to resolve species-specific metabolic contributions or feedbacks between microbial activity and soil mineralogy, particularly at scales relevant to field applications. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will construct agent-based models parameterized with multi-omics datasets (metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metabolomics) from long-term agricultural trials, combined with spectroscopic soil chemistry profiles. Parallelized simulations will map microbial functional guild interactions across spatial gradients of iron-aluminum oxides, pH, and organic matter composition, while machine learning pipelines will identify key predictors of carbon use efficiency. The computational architecture will implement dynamic flux balance analysis for microbial metabolism and finite element methods for solute transport, requiring distributed memory parallelism to handle an estimated 10^6 microbial agents interacting with 3D soil chemistry grids. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source platform for simulating microbiome-soil chemistry feedbacks, (2) quantitative linkages between specific microbial taxa, extracellular enzyme production, and organo-mineral complex formation, and (3) optimization strategies for tillage and crop rotation practices that maximize carbon sequestration via microbial- mineral synergy. By bridging molecular-scale microbial processes with field-scale soil chemistry dynamics, this work will provide actionable insights for maintaining soil health in intensive agricultural systems while advancing fundamental knowledge of terrestrial carbon-climate feedbacks.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and microbiological theories and methods (in combination) to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instructional combination of microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: Chronic disease management in primary care requires dynamic treatment strategies tailored to individual patient trajectories. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) presents significant heterogeneity in treatment response, leading to suboptimal glycemic control and increased risk of complications. Current clinical decision-support tools lack the capacity to adaptively model long-term outcomes based on evolving patient data, limiting personalized care. This project proposes the development of a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to optimize adaptive treatment regimens for T2DM using longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs). The research will integrate structured EHR data—including medication histories, laboratory results, and comorbidities—with unstructured clinical notes processed via natural language processing (NLP) to capture nuanced patient contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training deep RL models on large-scale datasets, enabling the simulation of multi-step treatment pathways across diverse patient cohorts. Computational challenges include handling high-dimensional data, managing temporal dependencies, and ensuring model interpretability for clinical translation. The project will validate model predictions against real-world outcomes and assess potential reductions in hemoglobin A1c levels and diabetes-related complications. Successful implementation will yield a scalable tool for generating personalized treatment recommendations, enhancing primary care providers' ability to make data-driven decisions. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between machine learning innovation and practical clinical applications in Family Medicine, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare costs associated with T2DM management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Family Medicine

abstract: The rapid digitization of visual arts and media ecosystems has created complex challenges in understanding audience engagement, content valuation, and sustainable distribution models at scale. Current arts management practices often rely on limited datasets and qualitative methods, struggling to account for the nonlinear interactions between digital platforms, generative AI art markets, and evolving consumer behavior. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from global online art marketplaces, social media platforms, and immersive media installations using high-performance computing resources. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in cross-cultural aesthetic preferences, while network analysis techniques will map the diffusion pathways of visual trends through digital communities. Agent-based simulations will test resource allocation strategies for hybrid physical-digital exhibitions, incorporating real-time data streams from augmented reality interfaces. The computational architecture will employ parallel processing to handle heterogeneous data types, including 3D asset metadata, blockchain-based provenance records, and eye-tracking datasets from virtual gallery environments. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing exhibition curation cycles, dynamic pricing tools for algorithmically generated art, and risk assessment frameworks for emerging media formats. By establishing quantitative relationships between computational creativity metrics and audience retention rates, this research aims to advance evidence-based decision-making in cultural institutions while preserving artistic innovation. The results will provide arts managers with scalable strategies to navigate decentralized creation ecosystems, address digital preservation challenges, and ethically leverage generative AI in visual culture stewardship. This interdisciplinary approach demonstrates how advanced computing can bridge gaps between data science, design theory, and arts administration in the post-digital era.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_title: Arts, Entertainment, and Media Management, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage various aspects of the visual arts, performing arts, and entertainment media industries. Includes instruction in business and financial management, marketing and fund-raising, labor relations for the arts, event promotion and management, product and artist management, and applicable law.

abstract: Preventive medicine aims to reduce disease burden through early intervention, yet a critical gap remains in leveraging large-scale, multidimensional health data to predict risk and optimize prevention strategies at the population level. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and environmental exposures to model disease trajectories and evaluate targeted interventions for cardiovascular disease (CVD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) in diverse populations. Current approaches struggle with the computational demands of analyzing heterogeneous datasets spanning millions of patients, hundreds of genetic loci, and time-varying environmental factors while accounting for complex interactions. We will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized machine learning pipelines for risk prediction, including ensemble methods and neural networks optimized for sparse, longitudinal EHR data. Agent-based modeling will simulate population health outcomes under different prevention scenarios, requiring iterative parameter sweeps across demographic and socioeconomic variables. A key innovation involves federated learning architectures to process distributed EHR data across multiple health systems without compromising patient privacy. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory CPU nodes for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) integrating polygenic risk scores with clinical variables. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models with improved accuracy for CVD/T2D onset, (2) scalable tools for simulating intervention impacts across subpopulations, and (3) open-source software enabling resource-efficient analysis of preventive strategies in real-world settings. By addressing computational bottlenecks in handling multimodal health data, this work will advance evidence-based prevention paradigms and provide a template for data-driven public health decision-making.
cip_definition: Research focused on Preventive Medicine

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the understanding of wood microstructure and its influence on mechanical performance through high-fidelity computational modeling, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The mechanical behavior of wood is inherently tied to its hierarchical, anisotropic structure, which varies significantly across species, environmental conditions, and processing methods. Traditional experimental approaches to characterize these relationships are time-intensive, limited in spatial resolution, and unable to isolate microstructural variables. This project proposes a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM), and machine learning (ML) to simulate multiscale wood behavior under diverse loading, moisture, and thermal conditions. HPC resources will be critical for resolving micron-scale anatomical features (e.g., tracheid networks, ray cells) in 3D models while scaling simulations to representative macro-scale volumes. The computational pipeline will integrate micro-CT scan data from experimental samples into physics-based models, validated through parallel mechanical testing. ML algorithms will then identify predictive relationships between microstructural descriptors and mechanical outcomes, enabling inverse design of processing parameters to optimize strength-to-weight ratios or moisture resistance. Anticipated outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for the woodworking community, novel datasets correlating microstructure to performance in non-traditional wood species, and guidelines for data-driven material selection in sustainable construction and manufacturing. By bridging computational mechanics with wood science, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in industrial applications, support the development of engineered wood products, and inform educational curricula on digital woodworking technologies. The scale and complexity of the models—requiring parallelized solvers, large memory nodes, and GPU acceleration—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically realistic resolutions within feasible computation times.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in woodworking, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The installation and structural performance of transparent building materials, such as glass and plexiglass, present unique challenges in modern architectural design, particularly as demand grows for larger, more complex glazing systems in energy-efficient structures. Traditional empirical methods for evaluating stress distribution, thermal behavior, and failure modes in these materials are limited in scalability and precision, especially when applied to non-standard geometries or dynamic environmental conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate the mechanical and thermal performance of advanced glazing systems under real-world operational stresses. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate multi-physics interactions—including wind loading, thermal expansion, and impact resistance—across diverse architectural configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve these computationally intensive models at scale, enabling parametric studies of material thickness, joint design, and anchoring systems across millions of mesh elements. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize installation parameters by training on simulation-derived datasets, reducing trial-and-error in field applications. The outcomes will include predictive frameworks for identifying failure-prone glazing designs, data-driven guidelines for retrofit projects in aging buildings, and open-access simulation tools tailored for vocational training programs. By bridging computational engineering with glazier trade practices, this work aims to enhance the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of transparent building enclosures while informing updates to industry codes and standards. The requested computing resources will support parallelized simulations across 500+ cores, reducing runtime for iterative design optimization from weeks to days, and enabling the processing of hyperspectral thermal imaging data collected from field validation studies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install and repair fixtures, sheets, windows, and skylights made of glass, plexiglass, and other transparent materials. Includes instruction in site measurement, job analysis and estimation, material cutting and trimming, window and door installation, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, specification interpretation, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Geriatric patients exhibit unique oral health challenges due to age-related physiological changes, polypharmacy, and comorbidities, which complicate caries and periodontal disease management. Current preventive strategies often lack personalization, as they fail to integrate the dynamic interplay between salivary biochemistry, microbial ecology, and systemic health in aging populations. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models of geriatric oral ecosystems to optimize personalized prevention protocols. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will simulate multi-scale interactions between host factors (e.g., saliva composition, immune response), pharmacological agents (e.g., drug-induced xerostomia), and microbial communities under varying clinical scenarios. Agent-based modeling will capture spatial and temporal dynamics of oral biofilms, while machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal clinical datasets (including metabolomic, proteomic, and microbiome profiles) will identify risk signatures for rapid caries progression. A parallel computational workflow will model drug-saliva interactions using molecular dynamics simulations to predict medication-related oral health impacts. The integration of these models into a unified framework will enable probabilistic treatment planning tailored to individual geriatric patients. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into age-specific drivers of oral dysbiosis, (2) predictive tools for identifying high-risk patients requiring targeted interventions, and (3) optimized recommendations for preventive regimens accounting for polypharmacy effects. By elucidating complex interactions inaccessible to traditional clinical methods, this computational approach has the potential to transform geriatric dental care, reducing preventable tooth loss and associated systemic health burdens in aging populations. The project’s scale—involving terabyte-scale multi-omics integration and millions of simulated microbial interactions—necessitates HPC resources for parallel processing, high-memory nodes, and GPU-accelerated simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of geriatric patients. Includes instruction in aging, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, geriatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and patient management.

abstract: Forest operations face critical challenges in balancing ecological preservation with the demand for efficient timber production, particularly as climate variability intensifies and regulatory frameworks evolve. Traditional forest harvesting optimization models often rely on static environmental parameters or simplified spatial assumptions, limiting their ability to adapt to dynamic conditions such as soil moisture fluctuations, habitat fragmentation risks, and real-time equipment performance data. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize forest harvesting systems under spatially and temporally variable constraints. The research will integrate multi-source geospatial data (LiDAR, satellite imagery, IoT-enabled soil sensors) with agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between harvesting machinery, forest ecosystems, and environmental conditions at unprecedented scales. Machine learning techniques will be applied to predict equipment wear patterns and energy consumption across diverse terrain types, while constraint programming will address multi-objective optimization of extraction routes that minimize soil compaction, carbon emissions, and canopy disturbance. The computational framework will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets encompassing multi-year environmental observations and detailed forest structural inventories. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool capable of generating adaptive harvesting plans that respond to real-time environmental feedback, reducing operational costs by an estimated 15-20% while maintaining compliance with biodiversity protection thresholds. The HPC resources will enable sensitivity analyses across 10^6+ parameter combinations to identify critical thresholds in system resilience, providing novel insights into the coupled dynamics of mechanized forestry operations and ecosystem health. This work bridges gaps between precision forestry, ecological engineering, and industrial systems optimization, offering a replicable methodology for sustainable resource extraction in climate-vulnerable regions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and forestry principles to the design of mechanical devices and processes for efficient forest management, timber production and related forest logistics systems. Includes instruction in forest products processing, forest management, forest harvesting, timber structure design, production analysis, road and bridge construction, vehicle adaptation and design, and harvesting equipment design.

abstract: The development of scalable control frameworks for quantum dynamical systems represents a critical engineering challenge at the intersection of quantum physics, computational mathematics, and control theory. Current approaches to optimizing control protocols for quantum devices—such as qubits in quantum computers or sensors—struggle with the exponential scaling of computational complexity as system size increases. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and validate efficient, adaptive control algorithms for multi-qubit systems. The research will employ tensor network simulations to model quantum dynamics, combined with gradient-based optimization and machine learning techniques to iteratively refine control sequences under realistic noise conditions. By parallelizing these simulations across GPU clusters, the project aims to achieve system sizes of 20+ qubits, a regime where classical computational methods typically fail. The anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools for quantum control optimization, experimentally validated protocols for error suppression in near-term quantum devices, and fundamental insights into the trade-offs between control fidelity and computational resource demands. This work will directly address bottlenecks in the engineering of reliable quantum technologies, with potential applications in quantum computing, precision sensing, and materials simulation. The computational demands of simulating quantum systems in a parameter-optimized framework necessitate access to HPC resources, including GPU nodes for accelerated linear algebra operations and high-memory nodes for managing large state-vector representations. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating physics-informed machine learning with HPC infrastructure to tackle emerging engineering problems in quantum device design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges of analyzing large-scale digitized textual corpora and historical documents using advanced computational methods to uncover patterns in cultural, linguistic, and editorial practices. While digital archives and born-digital texts offer unprecedented access to materials, their size, complexity, and heterogeneous formats—including manuscript images, OCR outputs, and multi-version editions—exceed the capacity of conventional tools. Existing workflows struggle to integrate textual criticism with computational analysis, particularly when handling non-standardized orthographies, marginalia, or multi-layered annotations. To bridge this gap, the project proposes a hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and network analysis, deployed on high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Key tasks include training custom transformer models for semantic and stylistic analysis of historical texts, constructing graph-based representations of intertextual relationships across corpora, and automating collation of variant manuscript versions at scale. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of image-based texts, optimizing OCR correction pipelines, and running computationally intensive tasks such as topic modeling across multilingual datasets. The project will also develop open-source tools to visualize textual variants and editorial decisions in interactive formats, enhancing scholarly collaboration. Anticipated outcomes include new methodologies for reconciling computational scalability with humanistic interpretability, a publicly accessible framework for dynamic archival curation, and case studies demonstrating how HPC-enabled analysis can revise understandings of textual transmission in understudied genres. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to establish scalable, interoperable practices for digital textual scholarship while advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between the humanities and computer science.
cip_title: Digital Humanities and Textual Studies, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on digital textual editing, archiving, and publishing, and on the study of new media and computing platforms from the perspectives of the humanities and computer science. Includes instruction in archiving, computer programming, cultural studies, and textual criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between Holocene-era human settlement patterns and dynamic paleoenvironmental conditions in the semi-arid regions of Central Asia using advanced geospatial modeling and high-resolution sedimentological datasets. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how early agro-pastoral communities adapted to rapid climatic shifts between 8,000–3,000 BP, particularly in contexts where traditional archaeological records are fragmented by erosional processes. We propose to integrate multi-proxy sediment core data (XRF, magnetic susceptibility, grain size) from 12 archaeological sites with regional paleoclimatic reconstructions to model human-environment interactions at sub-centennial scales. The computational challenge lies in processing 45+ TB of high-dimensional geochemical and stratigraphic data while resolving temporal uncertainties through Bayesian chronological modeling. A custom machine learning pipeline will be developed to classify sedimentation regimes associated with anthropogenic versus natural depositional processes, leveraging PyTorch-based convolutional neural networks trained on modern analog datasets. Concurrently, agent-based models simulating population mobility and resource use will be deployed on high-performance computing clusters to test hypotheses about settlement resilience under variable hydroclimatic scenarios. The workflow requires parallel processing of ensemble climate simulations (CESM-LME) coupled with archaeological site taphonomy assessments, necessitating 250,000+ core-hours on GPU-accelerated nodes. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of threshold responses in settlement systems during key aridification events, 2) probabilistic maps of preserved archaeological deposits based on erosional/ depositional histories, and 3) open-source tools for coupling geological and cultural timelines in understudied dryland environments. By bridging computational earth science methods with archaeological inquiry, this work aims to establish a new framework for assessing cultural adaptation to environmental change while optimizing remote sensing survey strategies in areas threatened by modern landscape degradation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of analytical techniques, concepts, and field methods from the earth sciences to solve archaeological questions related to human settlement, artifacts, site taphonomy, and paleoenvironments. Includes instruction in anthropology, ancient civilizations, archeology, geology, paleoclimatic reconstruction, sedimentology, and site taphonomic research.

abstract: Prosthodontic rehabilitation requires precise integration of biomechanical principles, material science, and patient-specific anatomies to optimize functional and aesthetic outcomes. However, current methods for designing and evaluating dental prostheses, implants, and occlusal devices rely heavily on static clinical metrics and trial-and-error adjustments, limiting their ability to predict long-term performance under dynamic physiological loads. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework to simulate multiscale biomechanical interactions within the masticatory system, including bone-implant interfaces, stress distribution in prostheses, and soft tissue responses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model these complex systems at clinically relevant resolutions, incorporating patient-derived 3D imaging data, heterogeneous material properties, and time-dependent loading conditions representative of mastication, parafunction, and speech. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will be employed to assess stress concentrations, fatigue resistance of restorative materials, and fluid flow patterns around implant surfaces. Machine learning algorithms will further analyze large datasets from clinical cohorts to identify predictors of prosthetic failure or complications. The proposed simulations will enable virtual prototyping of patient-specific prosthodontic solutions, reducing iterative physical adjustments and chairside time. Expected outcomes include validated computational models for predicting biomechanical risks in implant-supported prostheses, guidelines for material selection in geriatric and high-load cases, and open-source tools for optimizing occlusal device design in temporomandibular joint dysfunction. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance evidence-based prosthodontics, improve clinical decision-making, and enhance the longevity and patient satisfaction of restorative treatments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the restoration and maintenance of teeth, oral function, and aesthetic form through the use of single or compound materials, structures, and artificial devices. Includes instruction in implant dentistry, surgical procedures, denture design and fabrication, fixed and removable prosthodontics, restorative techniques, occlusion therapy and devices, geriatric dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, and temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for analyzing high-dimensional stochastic processes with complex dependency structures, a problem central to advancing statistical theory but hindered by prohibitive computational demands. Traditional approaches to inference in such settings—particularly for infinite particle systems, non-Markovian processes, and Banach space-valued stochastic systems—rely on simplifying assumptions that limit their applicability to real-world data. We propose a framework combining measure-theoretic probability, Bayesian hierarchical modeling, and resampling techniques to address these limitations. The core computational challenges involve (1) approximating high-dimensional integrals in posterior distributions arising from Bayesian nonparametric models, (2) simulating particle system trajectories with long-range dependencies, and (3) validating asymptotic properties of estimators under weaker regularity conditions than current limit theory permits. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling with adaptive preconditioning, distributed computation of exchangeable sequences via tensor decomposition methods, and large-scale numerical studies comparing frequentist and Bayesian uncertainty quantification in non-Donsker function classes. Expected outcomes include new convergence guarantees for sequential Monte Carlo methods in Banach spaces, optimized algorithms for stochastic partial differential equation parameter estimation, and open-source software implementing robust inference tools for non-ergodic processes. This work will directly impact statistical theory by bridging gaps between abstract probabilistic results and computationally feasible implementations, while providing methodological advances for applications requiring inference on complex stochastic systems, such as spatially interacting particle models in epidemiology and functional time series analysis in climate science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical theory underlying statistical methods and their use. Includes instruction in probability theory parametric and non-parametric inference, sequential analysis, multivariate analysis, Bayesian analysis, experimental design, time series analysis, resampling, robust statistics, limit theory, infinite particle systems, stochastic processes, martingales, Markov processes, and Banach spaces.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing clinical decision-making and patient care workflows in practical nursing settings. A critical challenge in vocational nursing and nursing assistance is the timely identification of patients at risk for adverse events (e.g., falls, pressure injuries, or medication errors) amid high workloads and heterogeneous patient populations. Existing risk assessment tools often rely on static, manual inputs, limiting their adaptability to dynamic clinical environments. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating real-time patient data—such as electronic health records (EHRs), vital sign trends, and mobility metrics—with machine learning (ML) algorithms to generate dynamic risk predictions. The project will utilize HPC resources to train and validate ensemble ML models (e.g., gradient-boosted trees, recurrent neural networks) on multi-modal datasets spanning 50,000+ patient encounters from partnered clinical sites. Computational workflows will prioritize scalability to process high-frequency sensor data and optimize hyperparameters for imbalanced class distributions common in nursing-related adverse events. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model nursing workflow adaptations under predicted risk scenarios to evaluate feasibility and resource trade-offs. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools tailored for bedside nursing staff, enabling proactive interventions and resource prioritization. By aligning computational advances with practical nursing workflows, this work aims to reduce preventable patient harm, enhance nurse efficiency, and inform evidence-based protocols for vocational training programs. The HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the computational complexity of real-time data integration, large-scale model training, and simulation-based validation within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the longitudinal outcomes of mental health interventions in diverse populations, addressing the critical challenge of predicting patient-specific treatment efficacy in real-world settings. Mental health disorders exhibit significant heterogeneity in symptom presentation, treatment response, and social determinants, yet existing clinical decision-support tools lack the capacity to integrate multi-modal data at scale. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging datasets, and socio-environmental data from public health repositories. Machine learning models—including ensemble methods and graph neural networks—will be trained to identify dynamic patterns linking biological, psychological, and social variables to intervention outcomes. A key innovation involves natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to extract latent psychosocial features from unstructured clinical notes, enabling the synthesis of qualitative clinician observations with quantitative biomarkers. Computational demands arise from the need to process terabytes of multi-temporal data, optimize hyperparameters across competing model architectures, and perform permutation-based significance testing to mitigate overfitting in high-dimensional datasets. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to guide personalized treatment selection for depression and anxiety disorders, (2) an open-source software package for adaptive intervention modeling, and (3) population-level insights into how systemic factors (e.g., access disparities, community support networks) modulate treatment effectiveness. By enabling rapid iteration of complex, data-driven hypotheses, HPC resources will directly support the translation of computational psychiatry research into actionable clinical tools. This work bridges a critical gap between traditional psychosocial intervention research and emerging computational methodologies, with potential to inform both precision mental healthcare delivery and public health policy.
cip_title: Mental and Social Health Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mental and social health services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design, fabrication, and acoustic optimization of musical instruments through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulations and material analysis. Traditional instrument crafting relies heavily on empirical trial-and-error methods, which are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict complex acoustic behaviors. The research problem centers on overcoming these constraints by modeling the nonlinear interactions between materials, structural geometries, and sound propagation in both acoustic and electric instruments. Key challenges include simulating high-resolution vibrational modes in irregular instrument bodies, optimizing material composites for durability and tonal quality, and analyzing airflow dynamics in wind instruments under varying performance conditions. To address these, the project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, augmented by machine learning algorithms trained on acoustic datasets from historical and experimental instruments. These models will integrate material property data (e.g., wood grain anisotropy, metal fatigue patterns) and performance metrics (e.g., frequency response, harmonic distortion) to predict optimal fabrication parameters. The HPC environment is critical for handling the multi-physics complexity of these simulations, which require parallel processing of large-scale meshes and real-time parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for luthiers and repair technicians to preemptively identify stress points in instrument designs, reduce material waste, and customize instruments for specific acoustic profiles. Additionally, the project will generate open-access computational workflows tailored to instrument fabrication, bridging gaps between traditional craftsmanship and data-driven innovation. By enabling precise virtual prototyping, this work aims to enhance the sustainability of rare materials, expand access to high-quality instrument repair, and support the development of novel hybrid acoustic-electric instruments. The requested computing resources will directly contribute to reducing computational bottlenecks in simulating multi-scale physical interactions, ensuring robust validation against experimental data from collaborative workshops.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to make, repair, maintain, and tune acoustic and electric musical instruments. Includes instruction in methods and equipment for making musical instruments, electronic instrument amplification systems, techniques of cleaning, and methods of tuning musical instruments.

abstract: The increasing demand for personalized prosthetic and orthotic devices requires advanced computational tools to optimize biomechanical performance, patient comfort, and long-term usability. Current design workflows often rely on static, population-level data, limiting their ability to address dynamic physiological changes, heterogeneous patient anatomies, and real-world functional demands. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and predict the biomechanical interaction between assistive devices and patient-specific anatomy under dynamic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-modal patient data—including gait analysis, musculoskeletal modeling, medical imaging, and material stress-strain profiles—into a unified simulation environment. Finite element analysis (FEA) and machine learning (ML) algorithms will be employed to model tissue-device interfaces, predict pressure distribution during ambulation, and iteratively optimize device geometry and material properties. The computational pipeline will also incorporate reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive device behavior in response to real-time sensor data, such as changes in gait patterns or residual limb volume. By parallelizing these resource-intensive simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in parametric design exploration and enable rapid prototyping of patient-specific solutions. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for reducing pressure-related injuries in prosthetic users, a data-driven framework for custom orthotic stiffness tuning in neuromuscular disorders, and open-source tools for simulating device fatigue under cyclic loading. This work addresses a critical gap in orthotic/prosthetic research by bridging clinical expertise with scalable computational innovation, ultimately advancing the development of next-generation assistive technologies that improve mobility and quality of life for individuals with limb loss or musculoskeletal impairments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with physicians and other therapists, to design and fit orthoses for patients with disabling conditions of the limbs and/or spine, and prostheses for patients who have partial or total absence of a limb or significant superficial deformity. Includes instruction in biomechanics, gait analysis, pathomechanics, kinesiology, pathology, neuroanatomy, materials science, diagnostic imaging, patient analysis and measurement, impression taking, model rectification, assistive/restorative technology and engineering applications, product finishing, diagnostic and definitive fitting and alignment, power devices, postoperative management, and patient counseling and follow-up.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern graphic communications workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize complex, multi-stage production processes. Traditional methods for managing prepress, press, and postpress operations—such as color calibration, substrate behavior prediction, and workflow scheduling—often rely on iterative physical trials, leading to material waste, energy overuse, and time delays. As digital and hybrid printing technologies expand, the need for predictive computational tools to simulate interactions between inks, substrates, and dynamic press conditions has grown. This research will develop physics-informed machine learning models to predict outcomes across diverse printing methods, including offset lithography, flexography, and digital inkjet systems. High-fidelity fluid dynamics simulations will analyze ink dispersion and drying behaviors under variable environmental conditions, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize job scheduling in multi-device production environments. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing of high-resolution image data (e.g., spectral reflectance maps, 3D substrate textures) and real-time parameter adjustments across millions of iterative scenarios. Access to HPC resources will enable the training of neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets of historical print job logs, material specifications, and sensor-derived press telemetry. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to reduce substrate waste by 15–25% in trial phases, dynamic calibration protocols for cross-media color consistency, and generative models for automating prepress adjustments in variable-data printing. The project will also produce open-source computational workflows tailored to graphic communications education, allowing students to virtually explore press mechanics and material science principles. By integrating HPC-driven insights into production pipelines, this work aims to advance sustainable practices in the industry while bridging gaps between traditional print methodologies and computationally enabled design-to-production systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the manufacture and distribution or transmission of graphic communications products. Includes instruction in the prepress, press, and postpress phases of production operations and processes such as offset lithography, flexography, gravure, letterpress, screen printing, foil stamping, digital imaging, and other reproduction methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in reconstructing and analyzing ancient trade networks across the Mediterranean and Near East (ca. 2000 BCE–500 CE). Traditional archaeological methods struggle to synthesize vast, fragmented datasets—including textual records, ceramic distributions, isotopic analyses, and maritime archaeology findings—into dynamic models of economic interaction. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of resource exchange, cultural influence, and political dependency that shaped Bronze Age through Late Antique societies. To overcome computational limitations in handling heterogeneous spatial-temporal data at scale, the project will develop machine learning pipelines to classify trade goods from digitized excavation reports, apply network analysis algorithms to map connectivity between sites, and employ agent-based modeling to simulate trade route viability under environmental and socio-political constraints. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution satellite imagery to detect submerged ports or eroded caravan paths, as well as for running Monte Carlo simulations that account for chronological uncertainties in artifact dating. Expected outcomes include an open-access geospatial database of trade nodes and a probabilistic model of interaction spheres linking regions such as Mesopotamia, Anatolia, and the Nile Delta. This computational framework will enable hypothesis testing about the role of trade in state formation and collapse, with implications for understanding cross-cultural exchange mechanisms. By integrating archaeological, philological, and environmental data through scalable analytical tools, the project aims to establish new best practices for digital humanities research in ancient studies while providing reproducible workflows for future interdisciplinary investigations.
cip_title: Classical, Ancient Mediterranean, and Near Eastern Studies and Archaeology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the classical ancient civilizations of the ancient Near East, Europe, and the Mediterranean Sea, such as Athens, Anatolia, Egypt, Greece, Israel, Mesopotamia, North Africa, and Rome. Includes instruction in ancient languages, ancient history, archaeology, anthropology, Greek and Roman mythology, philosophy, and religion.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing executive coaching strategies for organizational change by leveraging computational modeling to predict the cascading effects of leadership interventions on complex workplace dynamics. While executive coaching is widely utilized to drive behavioral change in leaders, its systemic impact on team performance, communication networks, and organizational resilience remains poorly quantified. Current approaches often rely on qualitative assessments or simplified metrics that fail to capture nonlinear interactions in large, heterogeneous organizations. The project will develop an agent-based simulation framework integrating psychometric data from coaching sessions, organizational network structures, and performance benchmarks to model how targeted leadership development propagates through multi-level systems. High-performance computing resources will enable the creation of synthetic organizations with >10,000 agent-employees, incorporating adaptive learning algorithms to simulate the evolution of trust, decision-making patterns, and innovation capacity under different coaching paradigms. Machine learning techniques will be applied to anonymized real-world coaching interaction datasets (including linguistic patterns, feedback cycles, and goal achievement metrics) to parameterize agent behaviors. The computational infrastructure will support parallelized scenario testing across diverse organizational architectures and crisis simulations. Expected outcomes include a predictive model to identify coaching intervention leverage points that maximize ROI on leadership development programs, along with evidence-based guidelines for tailoring coaching approaches to specific organizational cultures. By bridging computational social science with coaching psychology, this work aims to establish quantitative foundations for strategic human capital investments in turbulent business environments.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance foundational problems in algebraic number theory and arithmetic geometry through large-scale computational experiments. The project focuses on two interconnected objectives: (1) investigating the distribution of class groups in families of number fields with prescribed ramification properties, and (2) analyzing the geometric structure of modular curves at primes of bad reduction. A key challenge lies in handling the exponential growth of computational complexity as field discriminants increase and modular parameters become large, necessitating high-performance resources. The research will employ optimized C++/MPI implementations of lattice-based algorithms for class group computations, combined with parallelized Gröbner basis calculations in Magma to study singularities in modular curve models. For the number-theoretic component, distributed computing will enable systematic sampling of class groups across families of quintic fields, testing refined versions of the Cohen-Lenstra heuristics. In parallel, GPU-accelerated symbolic computations will characterize reduction types of modular curves at primes dividing the level, with implications for local-global compatibility in Galois representations. Expected outcomes include new conjectures about higher-rank class group statistics in non-abelian extensions and explicit equations governing modular curve singularities—results that will inform ongoing work in Iwasawa theory and the geometric Langlands program. The generated datasets will be disseminated through an interactive LMFDB-compatible database, creating community resources for further theoretical analysis. This computationally intensive approach bridges abstract algebraic structures with empirical pattern discovery, addressing questions inaccessible to purely analytic methods while maintaining direct relevance to core problems in modern number theory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the expression of quantities and their relationships by means of symbols, vectors, matrices, and equations, and the properties of integers. Includes instruction in algebraic structures, quadratic and automorphic forms, combinatorics, linear algebra, and algebraic geometry.

abstract: This research project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual and conceptual analysis of early Christian theological debates and their development across denominational traditions. The primary research problem lies in the complexity of tracing doctrinal evolution within Christianity, particularly the interplay between scriptural interpretation, philosophical frameworks, and cultural contexts in foundational texts from the first five centuries CE. Manual analysis of these interconnected dynamics is hindered by the vast corpus of multilingual patristic writings, conciliar documents, and apocryphal literature, necessitating computational methods to identify patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-referential networks. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for Koine Greek, Latin, and Coptic texts to analyze theological terminology, argumentative structures, and citation practices across approximately 10,000 digitized documents. Machine learning models will be trained to classify doctrinal positions, map conceptual relationships, and detect intra-textual influences, while graph-based algorithms will visualize the diffusion of ideas among early Christian communities. Computational demands include parallel processing for corpus-wide topic modeling, GPU-accelerated transformer training for low-resource ancient languages, and large-scale semantic similarity calculations. Expected outcomes include a searchable database of cross-denominational theological linkages, quantitative maps of doctrinal development timelines, and interactive tools for comparative analysis of exegetical strategies. These resources will provide scholars with novel methodologies to investigate understudied connections between scriptural hermeneutics and philosophical reasoning in formative Christian thought, offering empirical insights into how cultural and intellectual contexts shaped core theological concepts. The project aligns with contemporary interdisciplinary approaches in religious studies, bridging traditional hermeneutics with computational humanities to deepen understanding of Christianity’s intellectual heritage.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy and teachings of Jesus Christ and his apostles, and the subsequent intellectual and cultural movements and institutions based on Christianity. Includes instruction in Christian sacred scripture, Christian literature and philosophy, and studies of one or more of the main branches of the faith and their cultural context including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, Evangelicalism, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and control of active matter systems, a rapidly emerging interdisciplinary field at the intersection of statistical physics, soft matter engineering, and autonomous systems. Active matter—composed of self-propelled units such as synthetic colloidal particles or biohybrid microswimmers—exhibits collective behaviors with transformative potential for applications in targeted material transport, adaptive infrastructure, and microrobotics. However, engineering these systems requires overcoming significant challenges in predicting and directing their nonequilibrium dynamics across scales.
