The research will focus on two interconnected strands: (1) training machine learning models to analyze large-scale datasets of user engagement metrics and visual content, identifying patterns in how audiences perceive and interact with dynamic designs across platforms; and (2) implementing parallelized simulation frameworks to iteratively generate and evaluate design variations within complex parameter spaces, including real-time rendering of 3D environments and data-driven packaging prototypes. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing for neural network training and distributed processing for design optimization tasks, this approach will enable rapid prototyping of solutions that balance aesthetic intent, functional requirements, and behavioral insights. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scalable generative design in visual communications, empirical frameworks for quantifying perceptual effectiveness across media formats, and optimized workflows for creating adaptive branding systems. These contributions will advance both methodological capabilities in computational design and practical strategies for addressing industry challenges in personalized marketing, sustainable packaging, and cross-platform visual storytelling. The project’s computational demands—particularly its need for large-scale memory allocation, parallel processing nodes, and accelerated rendering infrastructure—necessitate dedicated HPC support to achieve its objectives within viable timeframes.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that focuses on the general principles and techniques for effectively communicating ideas and information, and packaging products, in digital and other formats to business and consumer audiences, and that may prepare individuals in any of the applied art media.

abstract: The roofing industry faces critical challenges in optimizing material performance, structural integrity, and longevity under dynamic environmental stressors. Current methods for evaluating roofing systems rely heavily on physical prototyping and standardized testing, which are time-consuming, cost-prohibitive, and limited in capturing complex interactions between materials, climate variables, and structural loads. This project proposes a computational approach to model and simulate roofing systems at unprecedented resolution, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these limitations. We will develop multi-physics models integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for water infiltration and wind uplift, and machine learning (ML) to predict material degradation under cyclic thermal and moisture exposure. These simulations will account for regional climate data, substrate interactions, and material properties (e.g., asphalt shingles, metal panels, synthetic membranes) to generate predictive insights into failure modes. A key innovation involves creating a scalable digital twin framework to simulate entire roof assemblies over multi-decadal timescales, compressing real-world aging processes through accelerated computational testing. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing large-scale parametric studies across diverse roofing configurations and environmental scenarios, requiring parallel processing of 3D transient simulations with fine spatial-temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include data-driven guidelines for material selection, installation practices, and maintenance schedules tailored to geographic and climatic conditions. This work will directly inform revisions to industry standards (e.g., ASTM International, NRCA) and enable the development of AI-driven design tools for roofers, reducing waste from premature failures by an estimated 15–20%. By bridging computational engineering with roofing tradecraft, this project establishes a foundation for evidence-based innovation in a traditionally empirical field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare, install, and maintain exterior roofing materials and roofs. Includes instruction in building materials, flashing, lag bolts, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, layering, site preparation, basic internal structural design, finishing, waterproofing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern masonry systems, which integrate advanced materials like high-performance concrete, fiber-reinforced composites, and adaptive thermal barriers, demands a deeper understanding of their structural and environmental behavior under dynamic loads. Traditional empirical methods for evaluating masonry performance are limited in predicting nonlinear stress distributions, long-term durability under climate variability, or the impact of novel material combinations. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing computational models to simulate multi-scale masonry behavior, optimize material configurations, and predict failure mechanisms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute finite element analysis (FEA) and discrete element method (DEM) simulations, which require parallel processing to handle the high-resolution meshing and iterative load-testing scenarios inherent to heterogeneous masonry assemblies. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning algorithms to identify correlations between material properties, mortar composition, and environmental exposure data, enabling predictive analytics for masonry performance. Key objectives include modeling seismic resilience in decorative masonry façades, analyzing thermal bridging effects in insulated structural masonry systems, and optimizing reinforcement strategies for sustainable masonry-infilled concrete frames. The scale of these simulations—involving millions of elements and multiphysics interactions—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible runtime and data storage. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for advancing masonry codes and standards, reducing material waste through computational prototyping, and enhancing energy efficiency in building envelopes. This work will also support educational initiatives by generating open-access datasets for masonry technology curricula, bridging hands-on training with computational literacy in the masonry trades. By integrating HPC-driven research with applied masonry science, the project aims to position computational modeling as a transformative tool for innovation in this historically craft-based field.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the laying and/or setting of exterior brick, concrete block, hard tile, marble and related materials, using trowels, levels, hammers, chisels, and other hand tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, blueprint reading, structural masonry, decorative masonry, foundations, reinforcement, mortar preparation, cutting and finishing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to address the challenges of creating scalable, high-fidelity digital illustrations that integrate dynamic data sources and real-time interactivity. Traditional illustration workflows often struggle to adapt to scenarios requiring rapid iteration, such as interactive children’s books, augmented reality (AR) visualizations, or data-driven editorial graphics. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks in rendering complex, multi-layered visual narratives that respond to user input or live data streams. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate and optimize these processes, particularly for projects involving large-scale datasets, physics-based simulations of artistic media (e.g., watercolor diffusion, ink dispersion), or AI-driven style transfer across thousands of frames. The computational approach combines procedural generation algorithms, neural networks trained on artistic style corpora, and GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines. For example, one proposed method involves using generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate texture synthesis for background elements in storyboard illustrations, reducing manual labor while preserving artistic intent. Another focus area is real-time collaboration tools for distributed illustration teams, requiring low-latency synchronization of high-resolution assets. The project will leverage HPC clusters to parallelize tasks such as batch processing of 3D model textures, training domain-specific AI models on historical illustration datasets, and stress-testing interactive platforms under simulated user loads. Expected outcomes include open-source software plugins for popular illustration tools, optimized workflows for data-intensive projects, and case studies demonstrating reduced production timelines for complex commissions. By bridging computational efficiency with artistic nuance, this work aims to expand the scope of illustration as a medium for responsive, adaptive storytelling in education, journalism, and entertainment, while establishing best practices for integrating HPC resources into creative disciplines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: Military information systems face escalating demands for real-time adaptability in contested cyber environments, where traditional static resource allocation frameworks struggle to balance computational efficiency with dynamic threat response. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision support system to optimize resource distribution across heterogeneous military networks under adversarial conditions. The research addresses the critical gap in scalable, predictive models capable of simulating multi-domain cyber-physical attacks while maintaining mission-critical latency thresholds. Leveraging parallelized agent-based simulations, the project will model network nodes as autonomous agents with embedded reinforcement learning policies, iteratively trained on HPC clusters to maximize resilience against emergent attack vectors. Computational workflows will integrate graph-theoretic representations of network topology with stochastic game theory to anticipate adversarial behavior, dynamically reallocating bandwidth, storage, and processing resources through distributed optimization algorithms. Key challenges include developing hybrid architectures that synchronize GPU-accelerated machine learning inference with CPU-bound cryptographic verification processes across distributed military clouds. The proposed work will validate models using anonymized operational data from field exercises, scaled through HPC-enabled synthetic data generation to preserve security constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation framework for testing resource allocation strategies under cyber warfare conditions, quantitative metrics for infrastructure hardening prioritization, and novel protocols for edge computing coordination in bandwidth-constrained tactical environments. This research directly supports next-generation command-and-control systems by providing computational tools to maintain information superiority through adaptive resource management, with potential applications in allied interoperability frameworks and automated cyber defense systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, design and application of computer and networking technology to the military environment. Includes instruction in planning; program development; graphical user interfaces; rapid prototyping; program construction; data types, operations; control flow; arrays; records; file I/O; database access; event-driven OOP structures; and enabling global-networked communications, including databases, systems analysis and design, decision support systems, and network security.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how variations in electoral systems influence the emergence and persistence of political polarization in multiparty democracies. While existing literature highlights correlations between electoral rules and polarization, the causal mechanisms driving these relationships remain poorly understood, particularly in dynamic, interactive environments. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based computational model simulating voter-party interactions under different electoral frameworks, including proportional representation and mixed-member systems. The model will incorporate adaptive party strategies aimed at vote maximization, voter preference shifts based on ideological proximity, and real-time feedback mechanisms between electoral outcomes and strategic behavior. Due to the high-dimensional parameter space and the necessity for Monte Carlo simulations to assess robustness across diverse initial conditions, the project requires high-performance computing resources. These resources will enable parallelized execution of thousands of simulation iterations, each modeling complex interactions among hundreds of agents over extended temporal horizons. Expected outcomes include identifying specific electoral configurations that mitigate polarization by incentivizing centrist policy positions, as well as characterizing threshold effects where minor rule changes precipitate significant shifts in party system fragmentation. The findings will contribute to theoretical debates on institutional design and provide actionable insights for policymakers considering electoral reforms. By leveraging computational social science methodologies, this research advances the study of political systems beyond static comparative analyses, offering a dynamic framework to evaluate the long-term consequences of institutional choices.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to analyze temporally dynamic human behavioral data derived from mixed-method studies, integrating qualitative narrative inputs with high-frequency sensor data. The research addresses a critical gap in social science methodology: the lack of tools to model complex, time-dependent interactions between self-reported experiences and physiological or environmental signals (e.g., wearables, geolocation tags). Traditional longitudinal analysis methods struggle with the heterogeneous temporal resolutions and latent dependencies inherent in such datasets, particularly at scales exceeding 10,000 participants. To overcome this, we propose a hybrid approach combining Bayesian hierarchical models with transformer-based architectures, optimized for parallel processing on GPU clusters. The computational workflow will first preprocess and synchronize multimodal data streams using Apache Spark, then train temporal attention networks to identify phase-dependent predictors of behavioral outcomes. A second layer will apply Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to quantify uncertainty in cross-level interactions (individual vs. contextual factors). The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage memory-intensive operations during model training (estimated 250 TB of temporal graph data) and to run distributed simulations validating robustness across synthetic missing-data scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for temporal mixed-methods analysis and novel insights into the nonlinear dynamics of decision-making under sensory-cognitive feedback. This work will advance methodological capacity to study emerging interdisciplinary questions in digital behavioral phenotyping, with applications ranging from personalized intervention design to ethical AI development. By bridging computational scalability with methodological rigor, the project aims to establish new standards for reproducibility in high-dimensional social science research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of research studies, measurement of variables, data analysis, and formulation of models. Includes instruction in experimental, quasi-experimental, and case study methods; historical research; participant observation; questionnaire design; sampling theory; and statistical methods.

abstract: The increasing complexity of patient care demands in modern healthcare systems necessitates data-driven approaches to optimize clinical decision-making and resource allocation. Registered nurses, as frontline providers, require tools to predict patient outcomes, personalize interventions, and mitigate risks in dynamic care environments. However, existing predictive models in nursing often lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time sensor data, and socio-behavioral factors—at the scale necessary for actionable insights. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning (ML) frameworks tailored to nursing-specific challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating predictive models for adverse event prevention (e.g., sepsis, falls, medication errors) using time-series analysis of EHR data and wearable device streams, and (2) simulating nurse staffing patterns through agent-based modeling to identify optimal care delivery strategies under resource constraints. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer models for clinical note analysis, LSTM networks for temporal data) and parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess intervention scalability. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project will enable rapid iteration of complex models across multi-terabyte datasets while maintaining compliance with healthcare privacy standards through federated learning approaches. Expected outcomes include open-source predictive tools for clinical nursing practice, evidence-based staffing recommendations, and novel methodologies for integrating HPC into nursing informatics research. This work aims to advance precision nursing care while establishing computational pipelines that bridge gaps between nursing theory, big data analytics, and real-world implementation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of personalizing instructional strategies for K–12 students with hearing impairments, including deafness, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate dynamic student-teacher interactions. Current approaches to adapting pedagogy for deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) learners often rely on static frameworks that do not account for real-time communication nuances, such as variations in sign language proficiency, auditory residual use, or multimodal comprehension (e.g., combining visual aids with tactile feedback). To overcome these limitations, this research will employ machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze large-scale datasets of classroom interactions, student assessments, and longitudinal educational outcomes. These datasets will include video recordings of sign language instruction, eye-tracking data to gauge visual attention patterns, and student-generated content (e.g., written responses, digital artifacts). HPC resources will enable the training of transformer-based models to identify patterns in communication efficacy and predict individualized instructional adjustments. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate diverse classroom environments to test the scalability of adaptive strategies across student cohorts with varying hearing loss profiles. The outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for educators, providing real-time feedback on lesson customization and scaffolding techniques tailored to DHH learners. By integrating computational analytics with evidence-based pedagogy, this project aims to advance teacher preparation programs, equipping educators with data-driven methods to optimize engagement and language acquisition for students with hearing impairments. The proposed work directly aligns with the program’s focus on innovative educational design, emphasizing practical tools to enhance teaching efficacy and student outcomes in deaf education.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Hearing Impairments Including Deafness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with hearing impairments including deafness which adversely affect their educational performance, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with hearing impairments, including deafness, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising hearing-impaired students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal analytics in the domain of Family/Child/Elder Law, an interdisciplinary field intersecting legal theory, policy analysis, and sociodemographic data science. The research addresses a critical gap in the systematic evaluation of how dynamic legal frameworks—spanning custody disputes, elder guardianship, and child welfare policies—generate inequitable outcomes across marginalized populations. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case analysis or small-sample qualitative studies, limiting scalability and predictive rigor. To overcome this, we propose a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), graph-based network modeling, and machine learning (ML) to analyze large-scale legal corpora, including court decisions, legislative texts, and administrative records. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, spanning decades of case law and policy revisions, to identify latent patterns in judicial reasoning, temporal shifts in statutory interpretation, and systemic biases in procedural outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate the cascading effects of hypothetical policy changes on family structures and resource allocation, incorporating demographic variables such as income, race, and geographic location. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models quantifying the impact of specific legal precedents on case resolution timelines and equity metrics, (2) an open-access toolkit for visualizing policy-driven disparities in custody and guardianship proceedings, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for legislative reforms to mitigate algorithmic bias in automated decision-support systems used by courts. By bridging computational scalability with sociolegal inquiry, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven jurisprudence, offering stakeholders—from policymakers to advocacy groups—actionable insights into the intersection of law, technology, and familial well-being.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting domestic relations across the lifespan.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of legal reasoning in complex, precedent-driven judicial systems through large-scale computational modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in legal scholarship: the lack of empirically grounded, dynamic frameworks to quantify how legal principles transform over time in response to societal, technological, and institutional pressures. By focusing on appellate court decisions in data privacy law—a rapidly evolving domain intersecting technology, ethics, and jurisprudence—the study aims to map the nonlinear interactions between case outcomes, judicial language, and external socio-technical factors. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for legal texts, network analysis of citation patterns, and agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making dynamics across multi-layered judicial hierarchies. Custom algorithms will process terabyte-scale corpora of case law, dissenting opinions, and legislative histories to identify latent doctrinal shifts and feedback loops. Graph neural networks will model the propagation of legal concepts through jurisdictional boundaries, while probabilistic classifiers will assess the impact of non-legal variables (e.g., public sentiment metrics, technological adoption rates) on judicial outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is essential for training transformer-based models on legal language, running Monte Carlo simulations of alternative legal histories, and handling the sparse, high-dimensional data inherent in longitudinal legal systems. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for legal impact forecasting, novel metrics for quantifying legal uncertainty in emerging technology domains, and evidence-based insights into systemic bottlenecks in judicial adaptation processes. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, offering a paradigm to study law as a complex adaptive system while maintaining rigorous alignment with jurisprudential theory.
cip_title: Legal Research and Advanced Professional Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any program in legal research and advanced professional studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Plant diseases caused by airborne fungal pathogens pose significant risks to global food security, yet the interplay between localized microclimatic dynamics and spore dispersal mechanisms remains poorly quantified. This project seeks to model the multiscale environmental drivers of *Puccinia graminis* (stem rust) epidemics in wheat agroecosystems, integrating high-resolution atmospheric data, host phenology, and pathogen life cycle traits to predict outbreak trajectories. Current limitations in forecasting stem rust spread stem from an inability to resolve fine-scale turbulence, moisture gradients, and thermal fluctuations that govern spore viability and deposition patterns. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining large-eddy simulation (LES) for 3D wind field reconstruction, agent-based modeling of spore cloud dynamics, and probabilistic machine learning to link microclimate heterogeneity with infection risk. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel execution of ensemble simulations across diverse agro-meteorological scenarios, processing terabytes of remote sensing data and in-field sensor inputs to parameterize boundary conditions. Key innovations include the coupling of Lagrangian particle tracking for spore transport with reaction-diffusion models of leaf surface infection processes, scaled across canopy architectures. Expected outcomes include the first spatially explicit risk maps of stem rust propagation under shifting precipitation regimes, validated against experimental plot trials in collaboration with the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT). By quantifying threshold conditions for epidemic emergence, this work will inform real-time decision support systems for precision fungicide deployment and climate-resilient crop placement. The computational pipelines developed will establish a template for analyzing aerially transmitted plant pathogens, bridging gaps between micrometeorology, fluid dynamics, and disease ecology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant diseases and plant health, and the development of disease control mechanisms. Includes instruction in plant anatomy and physiology, pathogenesis, molecular plant virology, molecular genetics, bacterial epidemiology, causal agent identification, host/agent interactions, disease resistance and response mechanisms, developing plant disease treatments, disease prevention, and disease physiology and control.

abstract: Fire dynamics in complex urban and industrial environments present critical challenges for firefighter safety, structural preservation, and emergency response efficiency. Current predictive models often lack the resolution to account for multi-scale interactions between turbulent combustion, heat transfer, and suppression system performance, particularly in large-scale or geometrically intricate scenarios. This project proposes an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to advance fire behavior prediction and mitigation strategy optimization. Using coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis, we will simulate fire spread, structural degradation, and suppression agent dispersion at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Large eddy simulations (LES) will resolve turbulent combustion dynamics, while machine learning models trained on HPC-generated datasets will identify optimal nozzle configurations and water droplet size distributions for varied fuel loads and ventilation conditions. The research will also model thermal-induced failure thresholds of modern construction materials under combined mechanical and fire stresses. By parallelizing Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS) workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to achieve real-time predictive capabilities for incident commanders during evolving emergencies. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for adaptive ventilation tactics in high-rise fires, predictive tools for wildfire-urban interface scenarios, and quantitative guidelines for retrofitting fire protection systems in energy storage facilities. These advancements will directly enhance firefighter operational decision-making, improve building code recommendations, and reduce collateral damage in complex fire events. The computational datasets and open-source model extensions produced will serve as critical resources for both academic research and industrial fire safety engineering applications within the homeland security ecosystem.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the theory and practice of fires and fire-fighting. Includes instruction in fire chemistry and physics, combustible materials, computer science, building construction, fire codes and related laws, fire hydraulics, fire command, fire prevention/inspection, fire protection systems, fire suppression systems, fire/arson investigation, occupational safety, equipment operation, emergency medicine and communications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling and synthesizing immersive, multidimensional soundscapes that integrate cultural, spatial, and temporal dynamics. Sound arts research faces a critical challenge in simulating and rendering complex acoustic environments that reflect diverse cultural narratives while maintaining technical precision, particularly in real-time interactive contexts. Current tools for spatial audio design and dynamic sound synthesis are limited by the computational demands of high-fidelity wave propagation modeling, machine learning–driven soundscape generation, and multi-channel spatialization. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these bottlenecks through parallelized acoustic simulation, large-scale neural network training for generative sound models, and real-time distributed processing for interactive installations. Computational methods will include finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations of 3D reverberation profiles, transformer-based models trained on ethnographically curated sound databases, and GPU-accelerated spatial audio engines for multichannel diffusion. The research will produce novel algorithms for culturally situated sound design, validated through collaborations with performing artists and public installations. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for adaptive soundscape generation, a repository of annotated computational models linking acoustic parameters to cultural contexts, and performance benchmarks for HPC-driven audio art. By enabling the creation of large-scale, dynamically responsive sound works that integrate technical rigor with cultural specificity, this project aims to expand the methodological possibilities of sound arts while fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between performing arts, computational acoustics, and critical sound studies. The requested resources will directly support GPU node allocations for neural network training, high-memory nodes for wave simulation, and low-latency networking for distributed real-time audio processing across campus performance spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on sound as a form of cultural expression, and its relationship to other disciplines such as computer programming, performance, and video. Includes instruction in acoustics; arranging, composing, and editing music; music theory; musicology; orchestration and scoring; and sound design.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an AI-driven predictive framework to optimize personalized care strategies for homebound individuals by analyzing multimodal data streams collected during home health aide (HHA) visits. The research addresses the challenge of mitigating acute health crises (e.g., falls, septic infections, or cardiac events) in decentralized home environments, where traditional clinical monitoring systems are absent. Current HHA protocols rely on episodic manual assessments, which may fail to capture subtle physiological or behavioral patterns indicative of impending deterioration. We propose a computational approach integrating wearable sensor data (heart rate variability, gait kinematics), environmental IoT metrics (room temperature, activity frequency), and free-text visit notes from aides into a unified predictive model. A transformer-based architecture will process temporal sequences of vitals and sensor data, while a fine-tuned clinical language model will extract latent risk factors from narrative documentation. The system will be trained on a retrospective dataset of 12,000+ anonymized HHA client records, including outcomes such as emergency hospitalizations or condition progression. High-performance computing resources are essential for three components: 1) parallelized hyperparameter optimization across heterogeneous data modalities, 2) synthetic data generation via GANs to address class imbalance in rare events, and 3) real-time simulation of intervention scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include a risk stratification tool that alerts HHAs to high-probability deterioration windows and recommends context-specific preventive actions, validated against historical cases with 85% temporal precision. The computational pipeline will be designed for eventual deployment on edge devices in home settings, requiring iterative compression experiments via neural architecture search. By fusing real-world HHA observational data with multimodal AI, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive home care that reduces preventable adverse events by 30-40% in pilot populations, while providing insights into the socio-environmental determinants of health destabilization in home care contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide routine care and support services for homebound disabled, recovering, or elderly people. Includes instruction in basic nutrition, home sanitation, infection control, first aid, taking vital signs, personal hygiene, interpersonal communication skills, supervised home management, emergency recognition and referral, geriatric care, and legal and ethical responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural and intellectual exchanges across the Near and Middle East from the 12th to the 18th century through computational analysis of multilingual manuscript corpora. The primary challenge lies in processing and interpreting vast, fragmented textual sources spanning Arabic, Persian, Ottoman Turkish, and Syriac, which are often dispersed across digital archives. Traditional methods struggle to manage the scale and linguistic diversity of these materials, limiting comprehensive analysis. This research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for cross-lingual semantic mapping and entity recognition, to trace the transmission of ideas, literary motifs, and scholarly networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training custom multilingual language models, processing high-resolution manuscript images via convolutional neural networks, and conducting large-scale network analyses of textual citation patterns. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts, visualizations of knowledge diffusion pathways, and new methodological frameworks for computational humanities in understudied historical contexts. The project will advance understanding of intercultural dynamics in premodern Southwest Asia while developing open-source tools tailored to non-Latin script processing, addressing critical gaps in digital scholarship infrastructure for regional studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, related borderlands and island groups, and including emigrant and immigrant groups.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radiation therapy planning, diagnostic imaging optimization, and radiopharmaceutical dosimetry demands advanced computational tools to address unresolved challenges in clinical radiologic physics. Current limitations in modeling radiation-tissue interactions, particularly for heterogeneous anatomies and emerging modalities like MRI-guided radiotherapy and alpha-emitting radionuclides, restrict the precision of treatment delivery and diagnostic accuracy. This project proposes to develop a high-fidelity, multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate radiation transport, energy deposition, and biological effect prediction across therapeutic, diagnostic, and nuclear medicine applications. The research will implement GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations (using Geant4/GATE toolkits) coupled with finite element biomechanical models to account for patient-specific tissue heterogeneity and dynamic motion (e.g., respiratory shifts, cardiac cycles). Machine learning architectures will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to optimize real-time adaptive radiotherapy dose calculations and reduce uncertainties in SPECT/CT quantitative imaging. A dedicated focus will address the computational bottlenecks in modeling short-range alpha-particle interactions for targeted radionuclide therapy, requiring massively parallelized track structure simulations. The HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^6+ beam configurations, 4D anatomical phantoms, and radiobiological models incorporating DNA damage repair kinetics. Expected outcomes include validated open-source modules for clinical translation, reducing systematic errors in tumor control probability calculations by ≥15% compared to current commercial algorithms. The work will directly inform safety protocols for FLASH proton therapy and improve dosimetric accuracy for pediatric nuclear medicine patients, addressing critical gaps in personalized radiologic care. By integrating HPC-driven insights into clinical workflows, this project aims to establish scalable computational standards for next-generation radiologic physics applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on that branch of physics which includes the physical aspects of radiation therapy, radiologic diagnosis, and/or nuclear medicine. Radiologic physicists must specialize in at least one of the three subspecialty areas: therapeutic radiological physics, diagnostic radiological physics, and/or medical nuclear physics.

abstract: Current approaches to complex maxillofacial reconstruction often rely on static anatomical models, which fail to account for dynamic biomechanical forces during postoperative functional loading. This limitation contributes to suboptimal outcomes, including implant failure, delayed healing, and compromised occlusal function. To address this gap, we propose the development of a high-fidelity computational framework integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling with machine learning-driven optimization to predict and enhance surgical outcomes. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute finite element analysis (FEA) simulations derived from preoperative computed tomography (CT) scans, incorporating anisotropic bone properties, soft tissue viscoelasticity, and mastication force variability. Concurrently, a deep learning model trained on retrospective surgical outcomes data will iteratively refine implant positioning and fixation strategies. The computational workflow will dynamically couple biomechanical simulations with neural network-based optimization, requiring parallel processing capabilities to manage iterative analyses across >10,000 degrees of freedom. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for strain distribution patterns in reconstructed mandibles, an open-source surgical planning toolkit optimized for HPC architectures, and clinical guidelines for force-adaptive reconstruction protocols. This research will establish a novel paradigm for biomechanically intelligent oral surgery, potentially reducing revision rates by 30-40% in complex trauma and oncology cases while advancing computational methods for personalized surgical interventions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the diagnosis and intrusive and adjunctive treatment of diseases, injuries, and defects of the oral and maxillofacial regions, including functional and aesthetic aspects. Includes instruction in pharmacology, analgesia, anesthesia, anxiety control, surgical procedures and techniques, surgical instrumentation, exodontia, oral diseases and malfunctions, soft and hard tissue pathology, dentoalveolar surgery, infection management, and prosthetic implantation.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the design and operational efficiency of next-generation marine vessels through high-fidelity computational modeling of fluid-structure interactions in dynamic ocean environments. A critical challenge in naval architecture lies in predicting hydrodynamic performance and structural response under complex, multiphase flow conditions—particularly where wave action, cavitation, and turbulent boundary layers induce time-varying loads on hulls and appendages. Current design methodologies often rely on simplified empirical correlations or decoupled analyses that inadequately capture coupled physics, leading to conservative designs with excess weight, reduced efficiency, or unanticipated failure modes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) for large-eddy simulation (LES) of multiphase flows with nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA) of composite hull structures. The simulations will resolve microscale bubble dynamics in cavitating flows, wave slam events, and their synergistic effects on structural fatigue in novel materials. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate the identification of critical load cases from stochastic sea state data. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to achieve the necessary spatiotemporal resolution across billion-element meshes, requiring petascale parallelization and GPU-accelerated solvers. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for cavitation-induced erosion, slamming pressures, and hydroelastic vibrations, enabling optimized hull forms with improved fuel efficiency and service life. The computational tools developed will provide a foundation for digital twin frameworks applicable to autonomous surface vessels and subsea platforms, directly supporting the Navy’s priorities in sustainable maritime systems and resilient infrastructure. By bridging high-resolution fluid dynamics with materials-aware structural modeling, this work aims to establish new best practices for risk-informed design in marine engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of self-propelled, stationary, or towed vessels operating on or under the water, including inland, coastal and ocean environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as corrosion, power transfer, pressure, hull efficiency, stress factors, safety and life support, environmental hazards and factors, and specific use requirements.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative decision-making in multiparty systems and its impact on economic policy coherence, using advanced computational methods. The core problem addressed is the lack of scalable frameworks to model how fragmented political institutions—particularly in proportional representation systems—generate economic policies with varying degrees of stability, equity, and efficiency. Existing studies often rely on simplified game-theoretic models or case studies, limiting their ability to account for complex interactions among ideologically diverse actors, institutional veto points, and dynamic public opinion. To address this gap, the project will develop an agent-based model (ABM) simulating legislative bargaining processes, integrating granular data on party platforms, voter preferences, and macroeconomic indicators from 25 parliamentary democracies (1990–2020). The ABM will incorporate neural network modules to approximate boundedly rational negotiation strategies, trained on historical coalition formation outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing 10^6+ policy negotiation scenarios under different electoral rules and economic shocks; (2) evolutionary algorithms optimizing parameter space exploration for coalition stability thresholds; and (3) real-time visualization of emergent policy cascades across multi-dimensional ideological and economic landscapes. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of policy instability drivers in multiparty democracies, predictive metrics for economic reform durability, and open-source tools for computational political economy. Results will advance scholarly understanding of institutional design trade-offs while providing policymakers with evidence-based insights into mitigating boom-bust cycles exacerbated by legislative fragmentation. The proposed HPC allocation enables computationally intensive analysis that standard political science methods cannot achieve, particularly in scaling from individual actor interactions to system-level policy outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction between politics and economics in the formation of public policy. Includes instruction in microeconomics; macroeconomics; political theory; American, comparative, and international political economy; and quantitative methods.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable energy technologies necessitates advancements in controlled nuclear fusion, where plasma confinement and stability remain critical challenges. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity simulations of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities in tokamak plasmas, specifically addressing the interplay between edge-localized modes (ELMs) and turbulent transport. Current predictive models lack the resolution to capture multiscale interactions between global MHD phenomena and localized turbulence, limiting their accuracy in experimental scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining 3D nonlinear MHD simulations with gyrokinetic turbulence modeling, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layer dynamics near plasma-facing components while maintaining global stability constraints. A key innovation involves coupling the NIMROD code for MHD with the GENE code for microturbulence via a novel iterative interface, which requires parallelization across thousands of CPU cores to manage memory-intensive data exchanges. The HPC allocation will support parameter scans across magnetic configuration space, including varying triangularity and safety factor profiles, to identify optimal regimes for ELM suppression. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive criteria for instability thresholds under reactor-relevant conditions, (2) quantitative analysis of heat flux patterns on divertor surfaces, and (3) open-source release of optimized coupling algorithms for the fusion modeling community. By elucidating multiscale plasma behavior, this work will directly inform the design of next-generation fusion devices, accelerating progress toward commercially viable fusion energy. The computational demands—exceeding 2 million core-hours annually—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve the required spatiotemporal resolution and statistical convergence.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics to a technical discipline or with the interface between physics and other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize workflow automation and document integrity verification in legal administrative settings, addressing inefficiencies in managing high-volume, compliance-sensitive legal documentation. Legal administrative assistants routinely handle complex workflows involving document drafting, version control, and adherence to jurisdictional formatting standards—processes that remain error-prone and time-intensive despite existing software tools. The research problem centers on the lack of adaptive, scalable systems capable of dynamically parsing heterogeneous legal templates, detecting compliance anomalies, and predicting workflow bottlenecks in real time. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on a corpus of legal documents (e.g., contracts, pleadings, affidavits) and procedural metadata from diverse practice areas. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of legal terminology, graph-based algorithms to model document dependency networks, and anomaly detection techniques to flag formatting or procedural deviations. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration across multiple hyperparameter configurations for ensemble models while processing terabytes of structured and unstructured data. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predictive workflow optimization, integrating real-time compliance checks and automated template adaptation. This work aims to reduce manual review burdens by 30–50% in pilot testing with partner law offices while improving error detection rates for jurisdictional formatting rules. By focusing on computational efficiency in legal administrative tasks, this project bridges a critical gap between legal informatics and operational workflow management, offering a replicable model for enhancing accuracy and scalability in non-scientific, compliance-driven domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as legal office managers, special assistants, and legal secretaries. Includes instruction in office management, secretarial science, principles of U.S. or Canadian law, legal terminology and documentation, legal research, legal software applications, law office procedures, record-keeping, billing, applicable policies and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the thematic and stylistic evolution of Canadian literature across historical periods, regional traditions, and oral storytelling practices. While existing scholarship has mapped key movements in Canadian literary history, the integration of large-scale computational methods remains underutilized, limiting the capacity to trace subtle patterns in language use, intertextual influences, and sociocultural shifts within a corpus spanning centuries. The research will compile a digitized collection of primary texts, including novels, poetry, folklore transcriptions, and Indigenous oral narratives (in collaboration with cultural stakeholders), to investigate how regional identities, multilingual encounters, and colonial legacies have shaped literary production. Computational approaches will include natural language processing (NLP) for semantic topic modeling, sentiment analysis to track evolving representations of national identity, and network analysis to visualize connections between authors, genres, and folkloric motifs. Stylometric algorithms will identify shifts in narrative structure and diction, particularly in works bridging oral and written traditions. Given the scale and heterogeneity of the corpus—encompassing over 5,000 texts in English, French, and Indigenous languages (with ethical protocols for culturally sensitive materials)—HPC resources are critical for parallel processing, managing memory-intensive tasks, and training machine learning models to classify underrepresented themes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of annotated Canadian literary works, visualizations of transnational influence networks, and new frameworks for analyzing the interplay between formal literature and grassroots storytelling. By bridging computational humanities methodologies with decolonial literary theory, this project aims to redefine canonical narratives of Canadian literature while preserving the complexity of its regional and oral traditions. The findings will inform pedagogical tools, heritage preservation initiatives, and interdisciplinary collaborations exploring technology’s role in cultural scholarship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: The development of advanced drug delivery systems is hindered by the complex interplay between nanoparticle carriers, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and biological environments. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize nanoparticle self-assembly, stability, and drug release kinetics are time-intensive and resource-limited, particularly when evaluating multifactorial variables such as polymer composition, surface functionalization, and physiological conditions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multi-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML)-driven analysis to predict the behavior of polymeric nanoparticles in drug delivery applications. Coarse-grained MD simulations will model the self-assembly of block copolymer nanoparticles at physiologically relevant scales, while all-atom simulations will resolve API-polymer interactions critical to drug loading and release. Concurrently, ML algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets to identify predictive relationships between polymer properties, nanoparticle morphology, and in vitro release profiles. The computational workflow demands HPC capabilities to manage the high-throughput execution of simulations across parameter spaces and the processing of terabyte-scale trajectory data. Expected outcomes include predictive design rules for nanoparticle formulations with enhanced targeting efficiency and controlled release, directly addressing challenges in oncology and chronic disease therapies. By integrating computational modeling with experimental validation, this project aims to accelerate the development of next-generation nanomedicines while reducing reliance on iterative trial-and-error approaches. The resource allocation will support advancements in pharmaceutical sciences by bridging molecular-level insights with translational drug delivery applications, aligning with priorities in dosage formulation, manufacturing innovation, and precision medicine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the basic sciences that underlie drugs and drug therapy and that prepares individuals for further study and/or careers in pharmaceutical science and research, pharmaceutical administration and sales, biotechnology, drug manufacturing, regulatory affairs, and related fields. Includes instruction in mathematics, biology, chemistry, physics, statistics, pharmaceutics, pharmacology and toxicology, dosage formulation, manufacturing, quality assurance, and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing spinal adjustment protocols in chiropractic care by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the biomechanical and neurophysiological effects of manual therapies. Current clinical decision-making relies heavily on static imaging and qualitative assessments, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic, patient-specific responses to spinal manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of spinal kinematics with machine learning (ML) analysis of multimodal patient data, including dynamic motion capture, radiographic imaging, and real-time electromyography (EMG) recordings. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of spinal segment interactions under varying adjustment forces, coupled with ML-driven pattern recognition to identify correlations between treatment parameters, biomechanical stressors, and patient outcomes (e.g., pain reduction, mobility improvement). A key innovation is the incorporation of probabilistic modeling to account for anatomical variability across diverse patient populations, enhancing the generalizability of findings. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of 3D imaging data and sensor-derived biomechanical metrics, requiring parallelized workflows for FEM solvers and GPU-accelerated neural network training. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool to recommend patient-specific adjustment techniques, reducing trial-and-error approaches in clinical practice. This work will also establish quantitative benchmarks for spinal load distribution during manipulations, informing safer, more effective protocols. By advancing computational methodologies tailored to chiropractic technical practice, this project aims to enhance the precision of assistant-delivered therapies while contributing novel data science frameworks to the broader field of manual medicine research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a chiropractor, to provide patient management, examination, and treatment services. Includes instruction in the principles and procedures of chiropractic, radiographic X-Ray procedures and techniques, X-Ray film analysis and media studies, orthopedic and neurological testing, clinical laboratory procedures, patient management and education, office administrative skills, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the pedagogical frameworks within Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) education by integrating computational modeling and data-driven insights into teacher training curricula. A critical challenge in FCS instruction lies in equipping educators to address multifaceted, real-world issues—such as sustainable resource management, nutritional epidemiology, and household economic decision-making—with methodologies that reflect systemic complexity. Traditional approaches often rely on static case studies or simplified theoretical models, limiting teachers’ ability to contextualize dynamic interactions between socioeconomic, environmental, and health-related variables. To address this gap, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and analyze large-scale simulations of household systems, consumer behavior patterns, and community health dynamics. Agent-based models will simulate decision-making processes in diverse family structures, while machine learning algorithms will identify trends in public datasets related to nutrition, budgeting, and sustainable practices. These computational tools will generate actionable insights into how interrelated factors influence outcomes in domains central to FCS education. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-dimensional datasets, running parallelized simulations, and training predictive models that capture nonlinear relationships. Outcomes will include modular teaching resources—such as interactive simulation dashboards and data-driven case studies—that enable FCS teacher candidates to explore complex systems in classroom settings. By grounding pedagogical strategies in computationally derived evidence, this project aims to improve the preparedness of future educators to teach critical thinking and problem-solving skills aligned with real-world challenges. The work will also establish a framework for integrating computational literacy into FCS teacher education, fostering interdisciplinary connections between home economics and emerging data science methodologies.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on maternal and child health (MCH) disparities by modeling the complex interplay of social, environmental, and biological factors influencing health outcomes. Despite progress in public health, inequities persist in maternal mortality, preterm birth, and childhood developmental outcomes, particularly among marginalized populations. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to account for dynamic, multi-level determinants (e.g., socioeconomic conditions, healthcare access, environmental exposures) operating across spatial and temporal scales. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) and machine learning frameworks to simulate population-level health trajectories and identify intervention leverage points. The ABMs will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including electronic health records, geospatial environmental data, and longitudinal social surveys, to represent individual and community interactions within evolving policy contexts. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian inference for model calibration and ensemble machine learning to predict risk factors for adverse outcomes. HPC resources are essential due to the scale of data (millions of patient records, high-resolution environmental layers) and the computational intensity of simulating stochastic interactions across diverse synthetic populations. Parallelized simulations will enable sensitivity analyses to test hypothetical policy scenarios, such as expanded prenatal care access or pollution reduction initiatives. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of modifiable risk factors contributing to MCH disparities, (2) predictive tools to prioritize high-risk populations for targeted interventions, and (3) policy-relevant insights into the cost-efficacy of intervention strategies. By enabling large-scale, multi-domain simulations, this project will advance precision public health approaches in MCH, with potential applications to state and federal health agencies collaborating on this research. The requested resources will support model training, validation, and real-time scenario testing, which are infeasible with standard computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of LGBTQ+ cultural narratives and community formation through computational analysis of large-scale multimedia archives. Current research in Gay/Lesbian Studies often relies on qualitative methods, limiting the scope to isolated case studies. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze digitized collections spanning literature, visual art, film, and activist publications from the 20th and 21st centuries. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for thematic modeling of texts, computer vision techniques to identify visual motifs in art and film, and network analysis to trace collaborative relationships among creators and organizations. These approaches require HPC capabilities due to the volume of data (over 10 million text pages and 500,000 visual artifacts) and the computational intensity of transformer-based models for cross-modal pattern detection. Expected outcomes include mapping shifts in LGBTQ+ representation across media, identifying understudied contributors to cultural movements, and uncovering intersections between artistic production and legal/policy milestones. The findings will advance scholarly understanding of how marginalized communities negotiate visibility in hostile environments while informing contemporary efforts to preserve LGBTQ+ heritage. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying identity-based cultural phenomena at scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on homosexuality in history, society, politics, and cultural life; usually with an emphasis on the modern emergence of gays and lesbians as a sociocultural minority movement, the identification of social, literary, and artistic themes and the definition of, and public policy and legal issues surrounding, the gay and lesbian community.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of analyzing dialectal variation and historical linguistic shifts in under-documented Malay and Indonesian languages through large-scale textual analysis. Despite the rich diversity of Malay/Indonesian dialects, many remain understudied due to fragmented records, non-standardized orthographies, and the resource-intensive nature of comparative analysis. Traditional methods struggle to process the growing corpus of digitized historical texts, oral narratives, and modern social media data, limiting insights into language evolution and regional variation. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational pipeline for automated dialect classification, semantic change tracking, and phonological pattern detection. The project will compile a multilingual corpus spanning classical manuscripts, transcribed oral histories, and contemporary digital sources, which will be preprocessed using distributed computing to handle non-Latin scripts and irregular orthographies. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer-based models will be trained to identify syntactic and lexical shifts across time and geography, while phylogenetic algorithms will model dialect relationships. Computational demands include parallel processing for training models on heterogeneous text data, memory-intensive alignment of cross-dialectal lexical databases, and GPU-accelerated simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dialect atlas of the Malay/Indonesian archipelago, annotated datasets for low-resource language NLP, and a framework for quantifying the impact of sociohistorical factors on language change. This work will advance philological research methodologies, support endangered language preservation efforts, and provide tools for applications in education, localization, and cross-cultural communication technologies. By integrating computational linguistics with area studies, the project bridges gaps in humanities scholarship while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in under-resourced language contexts.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Malay and Indonesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational models that advance the design of personalized educational interventions for students with hearing impairments, including deafness. Current tools for tailoring instruction to this population often rely on static, generalized frameworks that inadequately address the diverse linguistic, cognitive, and sensory profiles of learners. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating dynamic, data-driven models capable of simulating individualized learning pathways and predicting the efficacy of multimodal teaching strategies (e.g., visual, tactile, or sign language-based interventions) in real time. The project will employ machine learning techniques to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including eye-tracking patterns during sign language acquisition, tactile response metrics, and longitudinal academic performance data from deaf and hard-of-hearing students. These datasets will train neural networks to identify optimal instructional sequences and adaptive feedback mechanisms tailored to individual needs. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments under varying conditions—such as differing instructor-to-student ratios or assistive technology configurations—to evaluate scalable teaching approaches. HPC resources are critical due to the computational intensity of processing high-dimensional sensory data and running parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating individualized education plans (IEPs) with embedded predictive analytics, as well as evidence-based guidelines for integrating computational tools into teacher training programs. By quantifying the impact of specific interventions on learning outcomes, this work aims to empower educators with empirically validated strategies, reduce trial-and-error in classroom practice, and improve equitable access to quality instruction for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Hearing Impairments Including Deafness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with hearing impairments including deafness which adversely affect their educational performance, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with hearing impairments, including deafness, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising hearing-impaired students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Public sector decision-making increasingly relies on complex, data-driven analyses to optimize resource allocation during crises, yet existing computational tools often fail to address the dynamic interdependencies between infrastructure systems, population behavior, and institutional constraints. This project seeks to develop an adaptive simulation framework for evaluating emergency response strategies in multi-hazard urban environments, with a focus on equity in service delivery. The research employs high-performance computing to integrate agent-based modeling of citizen mobility patterns, Monte Carlo simulations of hazard cascades (e.g., concurrent extreme weather and power grid failures), and multi-objective optimization algorithms that balance response efficiency with distributional fairness metrics. Key computational challenges include real-time processing of heterogeneous datasets (satellite imagery, IoT sensor networks, and social services records) and parallel execution of scenario ensembles across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 combinations. By leveraging GPU-accelerated graph neural networks, the framework will model spatial dependencies in critical infrastructure networks at metropolitan scales, while differential privacy techniques will safeguard sensitive health and demographic information embedded in synthetic population models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated decision-support system for municipal governments to stress-test contingency plans under competing priorities, (2) quantitative benchmarks for equitable resource distribution during simultaneous crises, and (3) open-source modules for vulnerability assessment compatible with existing geospatial information systems. This work directly addresses gaps in computational social policy design by enabling rapid scenario prototyping that accounts for both systemic risks and socioeconomic disparities—a capability currently limited by conventional workstation capacities. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for over 150 U.S. cities participating in the National Emergency Management Association’s resilience planning initiative.
cip_definition: Any program in public administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform information diffusion in decentralized knowledge-sharing networks, with a focus on resilience to systemic biases and misinformation cascades. While existing models of information flow often assume centralized architectures or homogeneous networks, emerging decentralized platforms—such as federated wikis, distributed fact-checking initiatives, and community-curated archival systems—exhibit complex interdependencies between human trust behaviors, modular content verification processes, and self-organizing governance structures. The research problem centers on developing computational models that can capture how these systems balance efficiency, accuracy, and democratic participation under scale. The project will employ large-scale agent-based simulations to model interactions between autonomous user clusters, information validation protocols, and adaptive reputation systems across heterogeneous network topologies. High-performance computing resources are essential for parameter space exploration across 1) varying levels of network decentralization, 2) multi-modal information credibility assessment workflows, and 3) culturally situated user behavior patterns derived from empirical datasets. Simulations will integrate graph neural networks to predict emergent stability thresholds and phase transition points in information quality. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying trade-offs between participatory scalability and epistemic robustness in next-generation knowledge infrastructures, with applications to the design of fault-tolerant collaborative platforms. The computational models will also generate testable hypotheses about intervention strategies to mitigate coordinated manipulation in decentralized environments while preserving user agency. This work bridges gaps between social information behavior research, distributed system dynamics, and computational social science methodologies—advancing theoretical foundations for building equitable information ecosystems amid growing concerns about centralized platform governance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, organization, and process of information collection, transmission, and utilization in traditional and electronic forms. Includes instruction in information classification and organization; information storage and processing; transmission, transfer, and signaling; communications and networking; systems planning and design; human interfacing and use analysis; database development; information policy analysis; and related aspects of hardware, software, economics, social factors, and capacity.

abstract: The increasing complexity of regulatory submissions for novel biomedical products necessitates advanced computational tools to ensure compliance, safety, and efficacy. Current approaches to analyzing multi-dimensional datasets—spanning clinical trials, real-world evidence, manufacturing quality metrics, and post-market surveillance—are hindered by scalability limitations and inefficiencies in processing heterogeneous data. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through the development of machine learning (ML) models, large-scale simulations, and automated natural language processing (NLP) workflows. ML algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on integrated datasets to predict adverse events, optimize clinical trial enrollment criteria, and identify risk factors in manufacturing deviations. Parallelized simulations will model drug product stability under diverse environmental conditions to assess compliance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). NLP pipelines will automate the extraction of critical data from regulatory documents, such as FDA submissions and adverse event reports, enabling real-time synthesis of evidence for regulatory decision-making. The computational intensity of training complex models on terabyte-scale datasets, coupled with the need for rapid iteration of simulations across parameter spaces, requires HPC infrastructure for efficient execution.
