Anticipated outcomes include scalable tools for automating regulatory workflows, reducing submission review times, and enhancing predictive accuracy in safety assessments. These advancements will directly support regulatory scientists in navigating evolving FDA frameworks while maintaining rigorous standards for product quality. The resulting open-source software and validated models will be disseminated to the regulatory science community, fostering collaboration and innovation in public health policy and industry practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: Climate variability and soil nutrient heterogeneity present significant challenges to optimizing crop productivity and sustainability. Current agronomic models often lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between root architectures, soil biogeochemistry, and microbial communities under spatially variable field conditions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to predict crop responses to nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium (NPK) fertilization strategies across diverse soil types and hydrological regimes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate mechanistic models of root growth and nutrient uptake with machine learning algorithms trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles) from experimental wheat and soybean trials. The computational pipeline will couple 3D soil-plant hydrology simulations with Bayesian optimization to identify nutrient management plans that maximize yield stability while minimizing environmental losses. A key innovation involves agent-based modeling of rhizosphere microbial communities to quantify their role in mediating plant stress responses to drought and nutrient limitations. The research will utilize existing field data from 14 USDA-ARS sites while generating new validation datasets through sensor-equipped lysimeters. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of optimal fertilizer regimes for key US cropping systems under projected climate scenarios, (2) identification of root phenotype-microbiome synergies that enhance nutrient use efficiency, and (3) open-source tools for real-time adjustment of precision agriculture recommendations. By resolving submillimeter-scale processes across hectare-scale simulations, this work will advance fundamental understanding of plant-soil feedbacks while directly addressing the urgent need for climate-resilient nutrient management strategies. The requested computing resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale environmental sensor data, running ensemble climate simulations, and training deep neural networks on hyperspectral plant phenotyping imagery. Results will be disseminated through the CyVerse platform to support evidence-based decision-making for farmers and extension specialists.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the chemical, physical, and biological relationships of crops and the soils nurturing them. Includes instruction in the growth and behavior of agricultural crops, the development of new plant varieties, and the scientific management of soils and nutrients for maximum plant nutrition, health, and productivity.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for optimizing enterprise risk management strategies under dynamic, high-dimensional market conditions. Traditional risk models often struggle to integrate real-time data streams, stochastic variables, and nonlinear dependencies across financial, operational, and cybersecurity domains, leading to suboptimal risk mitigation decisions. Our approach combines agent-based market simulations with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to model complex risk interdependencies and identify adaptive risk control policies. The computational workflow requires parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of catastrophic event scenarios, coupled with neural network training on historical insurance claim datasets and synthetic stress-testing environments. Key challenges include optimizing portfolio risk allocation under liquidity constraints, simulating cascading failure modes in supply chain networks, and quantifying cyber-physical system vulnerabilities through probabilistic graph models. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization for DRL agents, distributed computation of value-at-risk metrics across 10,000+ asset portfolios, and real-time sensitivity analyses for emerging geopolitical and climate-related risks. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for enterprise risk decision-making, validated against multinational corporation case studies, that improves capital efficiency in risk financing by 15-20% compared to conventional methods. This work will advance computational methodologies in strategic risk management while providing actionable insights for optimizing self-insurance retention levels, reinsurance structures, and business continuity investments. The scale of required Monte Carlo trials (10^8+ simulations) and the need for GPU-accelerated neural network training necessitate cluster computing capabilities beyond typical institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles of business risk measurement, mitigation, and management. Includes instruction in business analytics, foundations of insurance and risk management, investments, life and health insurance, loss prevention, property and liability insurance risk assessment, risk control, risk financing, and security.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study analyzing the transnational evolution of feminist thought and cultural production as documented in women’s literature, art criticism, and grassroots periodicals from 1960–2000. The research addresses a critical gap in Women’s Studies: the lack of large-scale, cross-cultural analyses tracing how feminist ideas and creative practices circulated among diverse communities globally, particularly in underrepresented regions. Traditional methods struggle to synthesize the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources, including digitized archives of feminist journals, multilingual literature, and visual art collections. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques, we will computationally map thematic networks, conceptual shifts, and artistic influences across these materials. Key tasks include training multilingual transformer models to detect feminist discourse in English, Spanish, and Hindi texts; applying topic modeling to identify region-specific and transnational intellectual trends; and employing graph algorithms to visualize connections between authors, artists, and activist networks. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of unstructured data, run parallelized analyses of image-text relationships in art criticism, and train custom machine learning models for non-Western linguistic and cultural contexts. Outcomes will include an open-access interactive platform showcasing transnational feminist networks, a public dataset of annotated materials for future scholarship, and methodological frameworks for decolonial computational analysis in gender studies. This work will deepen understanding of how marginalized feminist voices shaped global cultural movements while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven approaches in humanities research. By centering computational rigor and inclusivity, the project aims to reshape archival practices in Women’s Studies and empower interdisciplinary collaborations at the intersection of technology, culture, and gender equity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: Law enforcement agencies face escalating challenges in managing digital evidence and records due to the exponential growth of heterogeneous data sources, including body-worn cameras, IoT devices, and multimedia submissions from the public. Existing record-keeping systems often lack the scalability, interoperability, and security required to handle these datasets efficiently, risking procedural delays, data integrity breaches, and compliance failures. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to optimize evidence lifecycle management through advanced data structuring, predictive analytics, and privacy-preserving automation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ graph-based databases to model complex relationships in case files, apply natural language processing (NLP) to automate metadata tagging of unstructured reports, and simulate blockchain-inspired protocols for audit trail integrity. A key innovation involves training federated machine learning models on distributed evidence repositories to identify patterns in storage access and chain-of-custody workflows without centralizing sensitive data. Computational experiments will benchmark system performance under multi-jurisdictional data-sharing scenarios and stress-test encryption schemes against adversarial attacks. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic evidence prioritization, anomaly detection in access logs, and risk-aware storage allocation algorithms. These resources aim to reduce administrative bottlenecks in law enforcement operations, enhance compliance with evolving data privacy regulations, and mitigate vulnerabilities in digital evidence handling. By integrating computational scalability with domain-specific legal and operational constraints, this work seeks to establish a replicable model for modernizing public safety infrastructure in an era of data-driven policing.
cip_title: Law Enforcement Record-Keeping and Evidence Management
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and procedures for managing records in police or other security offices, including storing and retrieving evidence and related data. Includes instruction in administrative law and procedures, office management, report preparation, organizational software, database software, physical and digital evidence properties, controlled storage and retrieval, investigative file inventories, case management, security systems, and communications skills.

abstract: Public health research increasingly relies on complex computational models to address multifaceted challenges in disease prevention, health equity, and policy evaluation. Existing approaches often struggle to integrate high-resolution demographic, environmental, and behavioral data at scale, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making. This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling framework to simulate the spread of emerging infectious diseases in urban environments while accounting for heterogeneous population mobility, socioeconomic disparities in healthcare access, and dynamic public health interventions. The computational demands of simulating millions of individual agents with time-varying interactions, coupled with the integration of multi-terabyte geospatial and electronic health record datasets, necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will parallelize model components using MPI and OpenMP to optimize scalability across thousands of CPU cores, enabling stochastic parameter sweeps to quantify uncertainty in outbreak trajectories. Machine learning methods will be applied to reduce dimensionality in parameter calibration, leveraging GPU-accelerated nodes for training neural networks on synthetic epidemic scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive disease transmission modeling, (2) policy-relevant projections of intervention efficacy under varying resource allocation strategies, and (3) novel metrics quantifying equity impacts of containment measures. By enabling rapid scenario testing at unprecedented spatial granularity, this work will advance capacity to prioritize targeted vaccination campaigns and mobility restrictions during emerging outbreaks. The requested HPC allocation directly supports public health agencies’ need for computationally intensive models that reflect real-world complexity, ultimately strengthening evidence-based pandemic preparedness in diverse urban settings.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public health, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying acupuncture needle manipulation, a core component of traditional East Asian medicine. Despite clinical evidence supporting acupuncture’s efficacy in pain modulation and tissue repair, the biophysical interactions between needle manipulation techniques (e.g., lifting-thrusting, twisting) and connective tissue microstructure remain poorly characterized. Current experimental models face limitations in resolving real-time, microscale tissue deformation and mechanotransduction signaling cascades triggered by mechanical stimuli. To address this gap, we propose multiscale computational simulations integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of needle-tissue interactions with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of force-induced cellular responses. HPC resources will enable high-resolution modeling of collagen fiber networks under dynamic mechanical loading, paired with atomistic simulations of integrin activation and downstream signaling pathways (e.g., FAK/PI3K) linked to therapeutic effects. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated datasets to identify optimal needle manipulation parameters (depth, frequency, torque) for maximizing mechanobiological responses in specific tissue types. This computational framework will be validated against in vitro measurements from collagen hydrogels and fibroblast cultures subjected to controlled needle stimuli. Outcomes will yield the first predictive model linking manual acupuncture techniques to quantifiable cellular responses, advancing the rational design of precision needling protocols. By bridging traditional practice with computational biophysics, this work aims to establish mechanistic benchmarks for acupuncture research while providing a template for integrating HPC-driven approaches into the study of complex manual therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of acupuncture, a Chinese system of health care and healing based on the use of pulse diagnosis, acupuncture point selection, and needle insertion, as well as herbs and other Asian treatment modalities. Includes instruction in basic Western medical sciences, Asian philosophy, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbs, diagnostic techniques, patient observation and communication, acupuncture points and point selection, acupuncture techniques, acupuncture treatment of disease, pain management, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in large-scale, cross-cultural analyses of folklore as dynamic expressions of collective identity and creativity. While folklore studies have traditionally relied on qualitative methods, the increasing availability of digitized oral histories, folk narratives, and performance records from diverse communities presents an opportunity to systematically investigate patterns of aesthetic adaptation and cultural transmission. However, analyzing these heterogeneous datasets—spanning multilingual texts, audiovisual materials, and ethnographic metadata—requires computational resources beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and dialectal variations to trace motif distributions across regional folklore corpora. Concurrently, graph-based algorithms will model the nonlinear dissemination of narrative elements through social and kinship networks inferred from ethnographic records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on fragmented or non-standardized textual data, running multilevel simulations of cultural exchange dynamics, and processing high-resolution audiovisual materials documenting performative traditions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable framework for identifying understudied intersections between gender roles and genre evolution in folk narratives; (2) computational evidence for how marginalized communities reconfigure shared folklore motifs during cultural disruptions; and (3) open-access tools tailored for ethically sourcing and analyzing Indigenous knowledge systems. By enabling the integration of previously siloed regional collections, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for preserving intangible cultural heritage while centering the agency of tradition-bearers in large-scale analyses. The requested resources directly support the program’s mandate to investigate creativity as a socially embedded practice, offering new paradigms for studying cultural resilience without relying on anthropological or sociological paradigms.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, as expressed in narrative, literature, performing arts, culture, work, family and community.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociocultural networks of 19th-century missionary movements and their role in shaping cross-regional knowledge exchange. While missionary studies traditionally focus on theological or historical narratives, this research applies computational methods to interrogate understudied dimensions of missionary activity—specifically, how missionary networks facilitated the transfer of ecological, linguistic, and medical knowledge between Indigenous communities and colonial institutions. The primary challenge lies in processing and correlating heterogeneous datasets, including digitized missionary journals, colonial administrative records, Indigenous language corpora, and environmental surveys, which span multiple continents and languages. These sources, often fragmented and non-standardized, require advanced computational integration to identify patterns of knowledge circulation obscured by conventional archival methods. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and historical orthographies to extract semantic and relational data from textual sources. Graph-based network analysis will model the connectivity of missionary nodes and their interlocutors, while geospatial machine learning will track the diffusion of ecological knowledge against environmental variables. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to overcome scalability constraints in handling terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping transnational knowledge flows, alongside methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary humanities research at the intersection of colonial studies, environmental history, and digital anthropology. This work will provide new insights into the asymmetrical dynamics of knowledge exchange in missionary contexts, while demonstrating how HPC can enable humanities scholars to address complex, data-rich questions that transcend traditional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Child care environments play a critical role in early development, yet optimizing these settings remains challenging due to the dynamic interplay of spatial, social, and pedagogical factors. Traditional approaches rely on observational studies, which lack scalability and real-time predictive capacity. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate child interactions within varied childcare environments, enabling data-driven optimization of space utilization and activity planning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models that integrate behavioral data, developmental psychology principles, and environmental variables to dynamically replicate group interactions and individual responses. The simulations will incorporate real-world data from motion sensors, video recordings, and caregiver reports, processed through machine learning algorithms to parameterize agent behaviors. By running large-scale parameter sweeps across virtual environments, the project aims to identify configurations that maximize engagement, minimize stress indicators, and promote equitable access to learning resources. The computational intensity of modeling hundreds of children simultaneously across thousands of scenarios necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and large memory allocation. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for room layout design, staff deployment strategies, and activity sequencing tailored to developmental stages. This interdisciplinary approach bridges early childhood education with computational modeling, offering a novel methodology to enhance care quality through predictive analytics. The resulting open-source tools will empower providers to make evidence-based decisions, potentially transforming standards in childcare practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be primary providers of home, family, residential, or institutional-based child care services. Includes instruction in child growth and development, nutrition, recreation, planning and supervision of play and learning activities, child abuse and neglect prevention, parent-child relationships, and applicable legal and administrative requirements.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear reactors relies on accurate modeling of complex, multi-physics phenomena, including neutron transport, thermal-hydraulic behavior, and material degradation under extreme conditions. Current simulation tools often rely on simplified models or decoupled physics due to computational limitations, introducing uncertainties that impact reactor design, fuel cycle optimization, and safety protocols. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity, coupled simulations of advanced nuclear reactor systems. The research will focus on a sodium-cooled fast reactor (SFR) design, integrating neutronics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and thermomechanical strain models to predict reactor behavior under steady-state and transient scenarios. A hybrid computational approach will be employed, combining Monte Carlo methods for precise neutron transport modeling, finite volume techniques for resolving turbulent coolant flow, and machine learning algorithms to accelerate convergence and optimize coupling between physics modules. The simulations will utilize open-source frameworks such as OpenMC and MOOSE, adapted for massively parallel execution on GPU-accelerated architectures. Key deliverables include validated multi-physics workflows for SFR analysis, sensitivity studies on fuel-cladding interaction under thermal stress, and predictive models for coolant voiding effects. By enabling previously intractable resolution of coupled phenomena at reactor scale, this work aims to reduce conservatism in safety margins, improve fuel utilization efficiency, and inform waste reduction strategies through enhanced burnup calculations. The resulting computational toolkit will be shared with the broader nuclear research community, providing a foundation for next-generation reactor simulations while advancing workforce training in HPC-enabled nuclear engineering. Successful completion of this project will directly support national priorities in clean energy innovation and nuclear infrastructure modernization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: Healthcare systems face persistent challenges in optimizing resource allocation, predicting patient outcomes, and scaling innovative solutions due to the complexity of clinical, operational, and biological data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models that address these challenges through systems-level innovation. The research focuses on two interrelated aims: (1) creating predictive models for hospital readmission risks and resource utilization by integrating multi-source data (electronic health records, wearable devices, and genomic profiles), and (2) simulating the impact of novel medical devices and care protocols within virtual healthcare environments. Machine learning algorithms, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on terabyte-scale datasets to identify patterns in patient outcomes, while agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation frameworks will evaluate proposed interventions under diverse operational scenarios. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage data dimensionality, reduce training times for iterative model refinement, and enable real-time simulations of hospital-scale systems. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for dynamic resource allocation, risk-stratified care pathways, and virtual prototyping of medical devices, all designed to reduce costs and improve care delivery. By providing scalable, evidence-based frameworks, this work will empower healthcare leaders to test innovations in silico before implementation, mitigate financial risks, and accelerate the translation of research into practice. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the precision, speed, and complexity required to model emergent behaviors in healthcare systems, ultimately supporting data-driven decisions in policy, finance, and organizational change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to innovate solutions and lead change within a healthcare organization. Includes instruction in innovation management, medical device development, evidence-based practice, systems thinking, information technology, healthcare policy and finance, organizational change, and leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of integrating computational methodologies into the creation and analysis of complex textile structures, which traditional manual and analog techniques struggle to model at scale. The research focuses on developing predictive models for nonlinear material behaviors in woven and non-woven fibrous systems, particularly under dynamic environmental conditions or mechanical stresses. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ multi-scale simulations to analyze interactions between fiber composition, structural geometry, and external stimuli such as humidity, temperature, and tension. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will model dye dispersion in heterogeneous textiles, while finite element analysis (FEA) will predict deformation patterns in 3D knitted architectures. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on empirical data from traditional weaving and experimental textile samples to generate generative design proposals that optimize aesthetic and functional parameters. These computational approaches aim to bridge gaps between material experimentation and digital prototyping, enabling rapid iteration of textile art concepts that require precise control over thousands of variables. The expected outcomes include a framework for simulating hybrid textile systems that combine organic and synthetic fibers, as well as predictive tools for pigment migration in multi-layered fabric constructions. This research will advance the field of fiber arts by providing artists with evidence-based computational strategies to expand the scope of tactile and visual expression, while contributing new interdisciplinary methods at the intersection of material science and digital design. Results will be validated through physical prototypes created using computer-numerical-control (CNC) loom systems and robotic fiber placement, ensuring alignment between simulated predictions and material realities. The project’s computational workflows will be disseminated as open-source tools to foster innovation in sustainable textile practices and adaptive material design.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by constructing art works from woven or non-woven fabrics and fibrous materials. Includes instruction in weaving techniques and loom operation; non-woven techniques such as knitting, coiling, netting, and crocheting; quilting; dyeing and pigmentation; printing and other finishing techniques; pattern design; tapestry; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Islamic theological and legal texts, with a focus on tracing doctrinal evolution and interpretative diversity across historical periods and scholarly traditions. The research addresses a critical challenge in Islamic Studies: the vast scale and linguistic complexity of primary sources—including Qur’anic exegeses (tafsīr), Hadith commentaries, and juridical literature—which hinder systematic analysis of how interpretations have diverged or converged over time. Traditional manual methods struggle to map nuanced theological debates or quantify the influence of specific scholars, schools, or cultural contexts. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes a computational pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and network analysis. Key tasks include preprocessing classical Arabic texts (morphological analysis, named entity recognition), training domain-specific language models to detect semantic shifts in theological concepts, and constructing citation networks to visualize scholarly influence. HPC resources are essential for handling the computational load of processing terabytes of multilingual text data (Arabic, Persian, Ottoman Turkish), running parallelized model training, and performing large-scale simulations of doctrinal diffusion patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying pivotal moments of interpretative innovation in Islamic thought, (2) mapping transnational connections between scholarly communities, and (3) generating open-access datasets and tools for computational Islamic humanities. By enabling quantitative yet context-sensitive analysis of religious discourse, this work aims to deepen understanding of Islam’s intellectual heritage while establishing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary digital humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Islam as preached by the Prophet Muhammad in 6th century Arabia and subsequently interpreted and elaborated by Islamic scholars and others; together with the cultural and social milieu related to the faith in various periods, localities, and branches. Includes instruction in Islamic scripture and related written authorities and commentaries

abstract: The dynamics of fault system interactions and their role in earthquake nucleation remain poorly understood due to the computational challenges of simulating multi-fault networks at tectonic timescales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution 3D computational model to investigate stress transfer and rupture cascades within geometrically complex fault systems. The research will integrate geophysical datasets from active fault zones with a hybrid finite-discrete element approach to simulate fault interactions over decadal to millennial timescales. Simulations will track stress accumulation, frictional weakening, and rupture propagation across fault networks with variable geometries and rock properties. The computational framework will leverage parallelized solvers to handle the non-linear contact mechanics and high strain-rate gradients inherent to fault rupture processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial resolution (meter-scale fault segments) and temporal scope (10^3–10^5 years) while capturing system-scale emergent behaviors. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how fault network topology influences earthquake clustering and maximum magnitude potential, with implications for seismic hazard assessment in tectonically active regions. The project will also generate open-source tools for scalable fault interaction modeling, enabling community-driven advances in dynamic rupture simulations. By resolving the computational barriers to simulating multi-fault systems, this work aims to bridge gaps between short-term geodetic observations and long-term geological records of fault activity, ultimately improving probabilistic forecasts of earthquake sequences. The requested HPC allocation will support iterative model development, parameter space exploration, and ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties in fault system behavior.
cip_title: Geological and Earth Sciences/ Geosciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geological and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the role of dynamic biomechanical forces in regulating cellular behavior during musculoskeletal tissue regeneration, with a focus on understudied connective tissues such as the meniscus. Current regenerative strategies often fail to account for the complex, time-varying mechanical cues that drive cell differentiation and extracellular matrix remodeling in these load-bearing tissues. To address this gap, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate mechanotransduction pathways across cellular, tissue, and organ levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the parallelization of stochastic ABM simulations capturing individual cell responses to mechanical stimuli, coupled with FEA modeling of evolving tissue-scale stress distributions under physiological loading conditions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs by identifying key mechanobiological parameter combinations that maximize predictive accuracy. The resulting models will be validated against in vitro experiments measuring real-time strain patterns and gene expression profiles in engineered meniscal constructs. Expected outcomes include the first predictive platform for optimizing dynamic mechanical conditioning protocols in tissue engineering bioreactors, with potential applications in personalized rehabilitation strategies and implant design. By elucidating how spatially heterogeneous mechanical microenvironments influence regenerative outcomes, this work advances fundamental understanding of mechanobiology while addressing a critical clinical need for functional tissue repair solutions. The computational infrastructure will support the development of open-source tools for mechanoregulated tissue engineering, fostering collaboration across biomechanics, computational biology, and orthopedic surgery domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the health sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing wine program management in hospitality settings, addressing the intersection of sensory science, supply chain logistics, and consumer behavior analytics. While traditional sommelier training emphasizes experiential knowledge, the increasing complexity of global wine markets, climate-driven variability in vintage quality, and shifting consumer preferences demand data-driven decision-making tools. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including regional climate records, biochemical profiles of wines, historical sales data, and real-time consumer feedback—to model dynamic strategies for inventory selection, pricing, and food pairing recommendations. Computational challenges arise from the need to process high-dimensional sensory data (e.g., mass spectrometry outputs for tannin structures), simulate long-term aging outcomes under variable storage conditions, and apply natural language processing to unstructured reviews or pairing descriptions. The proposed methodology combines graph neural networks to map relationships between terroir characteristics and flavor profiles, agent-based modeling to forecast regional market trends, and reinforcement learning to adapt inventory strategies under supply chain uncertainties. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across HPC nodes, the project will quantify risk metrics for rare wine investments and evaluate preservation protocols under stochastic environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-access toolkit for sommeliers to visualize region-specific climate impacts on emerging vintages, optimize cellar configurations via digital twin simulations, and dynamically adjust menu pairings using real-time sentiment analysis. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between enology, computational logistics, and hospitality analytics, offering a novel paradigm for data-informed wine stewardship while maintaining alignment with traditional sensory evaluation frameworks. The scalability of models developed through this work may later extend to broader applications in perishable goods management and experiential retail analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage wine selection, purchasing, storage, sales, and service for a variety of establishments in the hospitality industry. Includes instruction in wine production, wine regions of the world, wine tasting, food and wine matching, service techniques, and wine program management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive simulation framework for optimizing proactive policing strategies in urban environments. The research addresses the challenge of dynamically modeling crime patterns influenced by complex socio-spatial factors—such as transient demographics, infrastructure layouts, and real-time event data—which traditional analytical tools struggle to capture. By integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning techniques, the project aims to simulate interactions between civilian populations, law enforcement patrols, and environmental variables at city-scale resolution. The computational approach will utilize anonymized historical crime datasets, geospatial information systems (GIS) layers, and crowd-sourced incident reports to parameterize simulations, enabling the testing of hypothetical scenarios, including targeted patrol allocations, community engagement interventions, and emergency response protocols. HPC resources are critical to manage the high dimensionality of spatiotemporal data, execute parallelized simulations across varying urban contexts, and train deep reinforcement learning models to identify adaptive policing policies. Expected outcomes include a validated, open-source simulation platform for evaluating the long-term efficacy of crime prevention strategies under resource constraints, as well as actionable insights into balancing reactive enforcement with community trust-building measures. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science and criminal justice practice, offering a novel tool for law enforcement agencies to mitigate urban crime while addressing systemic biases in patrol deployment. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated through partnerships with municipal police departments and policy research institutes, prioritizing ethical AI frameworks to ensure transparency in algorithmic recommendations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to advance predictive modeling of coupled surface-subsurface hydrological processes in heterogeneous watersheds, with a focus on quantifying groundwater contamination risks under climate variability. Current models often simplify the integration of surface water flow, unsaturated zone dynamics, and groundwater transport, limiting their ability to resolve fine-scale contaminant pathways or transient climate interactions. We propose a high-resolution, three-dimensional modeling framework using parallelized Hydrus-MODFLOW and PFLOTRAN codes to simulate reactive solute transport across soil and aquifer systems. The computational workflow integrates stochastic parameterization of hydraulic conductivity fields, ensemble climate forcing from regional CMIP6 projections, and probabilistic uncertainty analysis. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute the 10⁴–10⁵ core-hour simulations required for meter-scale discretization of 500 km² domains over decadal timescales. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive Monte Carlo ensembles and optimizing coupled solver performance across multi-physics kernels. Anticipated outcomes include: 1) identification of high-risk zones for nitrate and heavy metal mobilization in agricultural-alluvial aquifers under drought-flood cycles, 2) quantification of model sensitivity to bedrock topography and preferential flow features at sub-watershed scales, and 3) open-source release of optimized GPU-accelerated transport modules. Results will directly inform managed aquifer recharge strategies in the study region while advancing numerical methods for reactive transport in fractured media. By resolving previously intractable spatiotemporal couplings between infiltration events and contaminant breakthrough curves, this work addresses critical gaps in process-based understanding of water quality resilience—a prerequisite for sustainable groundwater management in climate-stressed basins.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the occurrence, circulation, distribution, chemical and physical properties, and environmental interaction of surface and subsurface waters, including groundwater. Includes instruction in geophysics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, chemical physics, geomorphology, mathematical modeling, hydrologic analysis, continental water processes, global water balance, and environmental science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the cognitive and motor skill development processes in music education, with the goal of optimizing pedagogical strategies for music teachers. While music learning involves complex interactions between auditory processing, motor coordination, and theoretical understanding, existing research has yet to fully model these dynamics at scale due to computational limitations. Our study addresses this gap by developing agent-based simulations of student ensembles and solo performers, integrating real-world data from motion-captured instrumental techniques, EEG recordings of neural responses during sight-reading, and longitudinal assessments of music theory comprehension. These multi-modal datasets will be analyzed using machine learning pipelines to identify patterns in skill acquisition, error correction, and the efficacy of instructional interventions. The HPC environment is critical for processing high-resolution sensor data, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and training deep learning models to predict student outcomes under varying teaching methods. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for mapping the interplay between cognitive load, motor skill development, and music literacy, enabling the design of adaptive curricula that balance technical rigor with creative expression. Results will directly inform music teacher education programs by quantifying the impact of different instructional sequencing strategies, from foundational technique building to ensemble collaboration. By bridging computational modeling with music pedagogy, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for training educators to address diverse learner needs while maintaining the artistic integrity of music instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach music and music appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows for generating high-fidelity, interactive 3D medical visualizations to address the growing demand for precision in biomedical education, surgical planning, and patient communication. Current methods for rendering complex anatomical models—particularly those integrating dynamic physiological processes, multi-modal imaging data, or patient-specific pathologies—are limited by conventional computing resources, leading to trade-offs between visual accuracy, interactivity, and scalability. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these constraints, enabling real-time manipulation of large-scale datasets (e.g., 4D MRI, histology stacks, and biomechanical simulations) while maintaining photorealistic quality. Computational pipelines will combine GPU-accelerated ray tracing, machine learning-based image segmentation, and distributed rendering techniques to process terabytes of medical imaging data. A key focus is optimizing mesh generation and texture mapping for anatomically variable structures, such as neurovascular networks or tumor microenvironments, using parallelized algorithms to reduce processing times from days to hours. Additionally, the project will prototype AI-driven tools for automating the alignment of illustrated educational content with evolving clinical guidelines, requiring fine-tuning of large language models on curated biomedical corpora. Outcomes will include open-source software modules for medical illustrators, validated workflows for integrating HPC into visualization pipelines, and a repository of optimized 3D models for teaching and surgical simulation. By bridging computational scalability gaps in medical art production, this work aims to enhance the translational impact of visual biomedical communication across healthcare and research, while establishing best practices for HPC adoption in non-traditional domains of health professions education. Resource allocation will support iterative testing of rendering algorithms, storage of multi-terabyte datasets, and collaborative access for cross-disciplinary teams in clinical anatomy, computer graphics, and biomedical engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles and techniques of art and computer-assisted imaging, graphics, and animation to create visual materials to facilitate the recording and dissemination of biomedical knowledge for educational, research, and clinical purposes. Includes instruction in anatomy, physiology, pathology, histology, embryology, neuroanatomy, medical terminology, artistic media and techniques, illustration techniques, three-dimensional modeling, prosthetics, data display design, exhibit design and production, medical photography, multimedia, computer graphics and animation, digital imaging, business management, production technology, and instructional design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on workplace team dynamics and resilience under rapidly changing organizational conditions. Industrial and organizational (I-O) psychology faces a critical challenge in modeling complex, multilevel interactions—such as communication patterns, stress cascades, and adaptive decision-making—that influence team performance in high-stakes environments. Traditional statistical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-dependent relationships inherent in these processes, particularly when analyzing large-scale, multimodal datasets (e.g., longitudinal surveys, communication logs, biometric sensor data). To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) integrated with machine learning to simulate team behavior under varying stress and resource constraints. The ABMs will incorporate empirically derived parameters from existing organizational datasets (N ≈ 15,000 employees across 12 industries) to replicate real-world decision hierarchies and reward structures. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze unstructured team communication data (≈10 TB of meeting transcripts and messaging logs) to identify resilience markers. HPC resources are essential for scaling Monte Carlo simulations to test intervention scenarios (e.g., modified feedback protocols, dynamic task reallocation) and for training transformer-based NLP models on heterogeneous text corpora. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking specific leadership behaviors and communication styles to team adaptability, as well as open-source tools for simulating organizational change impacts. This work directly supports evidence-based strategies for mitigating employee burnout and optimizing resource allocation in crisis-response teams, advancing I-O psychology’s capacity to address emergent workforce challenges. The computational workflows will be disseminated via partnerships with industry consortia to ensure translational impact.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and group behavior in institutional settings, applications to related problems of organization and industry, and that may prepare individuals to apply such principles in industrial and organizational settings. Includes instruction in group behavior theory, organizational theory, reward/punishment structures, human-machine and human-computer interactions, motivation dynamics, human stress studies, environmental and organizational influences on behavior, alienation and satisfaction, and job testing and assessment.

abstract: Pain management in palliative care remains a critical challenge due to the heterogeneity of patient responses, complex interactions between biological and psychosocial factors, and the limited personalization of therapeutic strategies. Current approaches often rely on trial-and-error protocols, leading to delays in effective symptom control and increased risks of adverse effects. To address this, we propose a computational research project leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize individualized pain management plans. This project integrates multi-modal clinical data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, neuroimaging, and real-time sensor data—with mechanistic models of pain pathways and drug pharmacokinetics-pharmacodynamics (PK/PD). Advanced machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models, will be employed to identify patient subgroups, predict treatment responses, and simulate intervention outcomes across diverse scenarios. The computational demands of processing large-scale datasets, training complex models, and running iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure to ensure feasibility and scalability. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for stratifying patients based on biopsychosocial risk factors, (2) optimized dosing algorithms for opioids and adjuvant therapies that minimize side effects, and (3) predictive tools to guide clinical decision-making in dynamic care settings. By bridging data-driven insights with clinical practice, this work aims to reduce the burden of undertreated pain, enhance quality of life for palliative care patients, and provide a template for computationally guided precision medicine in symptom management. The proposed HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of models, validation against retrospective cohorts, and eventual translation into prospective clinical trials.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care/Pain Management

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between cultural narratives, social networks, and mental health outcomes in urban migrant populations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While prior qualitative studies have documented how stigma and community support shape mental health disparities, the dynamic, large-scale interactions between these factors remain understudied due to methodological limitations. We propose a mixed-methods computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP) of ethnographic interviews with agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate how health-related beliefs propagate through social networks. The research will analyze 15,000+ transcribed interviews from three transnational migrant communities, employing transformer-based models to classify narratives related to trauma, coping strategies, and healthcare access. These outputs will parameterize ABMs simulating decision-making processes around mental health service utilization under varying social cohesion scenarios. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the scale of text corpora, iterative model calibration, and parallelized simulations across 10,000+ agent networks. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in community-level support structures that buffer against systemic barriers to care, as well as a publicly accessible toolkit for cultural consensus analysis. This work advances medical anthropology by quantitatively modeling how micro-level cultural practices interact with macro-structural inequities, offering translational insights for designing community-led mental health interventions. The project also demonstrates the utility of HPC in scaling ethnographic insights to inform public health strategies without reducing cultural complexity to deterministic variables.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on biological, socio-cultural, psychological, and behavioral factors as they relate to health, illness, medical practices, and access to health care services. Includes instruction in ethno-medicine, urban health, international health, psychiatric and psychological anthropology, aging, and health and identity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Urdu linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in scalable text processing and dialectal modeling. Urdu, a South Asian language with rich literary traditions and diverse regional dialects, presents unique challenges due to its complex morphosyntax, Perso-Arabic script, and code-switching tendencies. Current tools for automated Urdu text analysis remain underdeveloped, limiting large-scale studies of historical texts, dialect variation, and stylistic trends. Our research aims to develop a computational pipeline for analyzing Urdu corpora spanning classical poetry, modern prose, and colloquial speech. Key objectives include training transformer-based models for morphological disambiguation, dialect classification, and semantic parsing of Urdu texts, as well as deploying distributed computing frameworks to process multi-terabyte datasets of digitized manuscripts and oral narratives. The project will employ parallelized workflows to compare linguistic features across genres and temporal periods, enabling quantitative studies of stylistic evolution and dialectal divergence. Additionally, we will simulate language contact scenarios to model Urdu’s historical interactions with Persian, Sanskrit, and English. The computational demands of these tasks—including GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous text sources, and high-memory nodes for graph-based semantic analyses—necessitate HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include open-source NLP tools tailored for Urdu, a geotagged dialect corpus with phonological annotations, and quantitative frameworks for literary stylometry. This work will provide unprecedented scalability in Urdu philological research, support digital preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and establish methodological foundations for computational humanities scholarship in under-resourced languages. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary collaborations with linguists, literary scholars, and regional archives.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Urdu language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Urdu; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Environmental health research faces a critical challenge in understanding how complex, interacting environmental exposures collectively impact human health outcomes. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to disentangle the effects of multiple simultaneous stressors—such as air pollutants, water contaminants, and socioeconomic factors—limiting our ability to assess cumulative risks accurately. This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multifactorial environmental exposures and their population-level health implications across spatial and temporal scales. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-modal datasets, including satellite-derived environmental measurements, EPA monitoring records, electronic health repositories, and census-derived demographic data. Agent-based modeling will simulate exposure pathways and health responses under various policy scenarios, while parallelized geospatial analytics will identify high-risk regions through vulnerability indices combining environmental, clinical, and social determinants. Computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated tensor operations for deep learning architectures and distributed memory systems for large-scale epidemiological simulations. The anticipated outcomes include: (1) predictive models quantifying dose-response relationships for exposure mixtures, (2) open-source tools for community-level risk stratification, and (3) evidence-based projections of intervention effectiveness across different environmental justice contexts. By enabling analysis of petabyte-scale datasets and complex systems interactions beyond single-workstation capabilities, the requested resources will advance understanding of environmental health disparities while providing actionable insights for targeted public health strategies. This work directly supports priority initiatives in climate resilience and equitable health protection outlined by federal environmental health agencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: Agricultural extension services face increasing demands to provide timely, data-driven recommendations to farmers amidst complex challenges such as evolving pest dynamics, climate variability, and market shifts. Current decision-support tools often lack the computational capacity to integrate real-time agricultural datasets—including soil health metrics, pest surveillance data, satellite imagery, and farm management records—at scales necessary for hyper-localized guidance. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a machine learning framework for predictive modeling of region-specific crop management strategies. The research will focus on optimizing pest control and yield prediction by training ensemble models on multi-modal datasets spanning 10+ years of agronomic records from cooperating farms, weather station networks, and drone-captured field imagery. Computational workflows will include GPU-accelerated neural networks for image-based pest identification, agent-based simulations of pest population dynamics under climate scenarios, and Bayesian optimization to tailor irrigation and fertilizer schedules. By parallelizing these tasks across HPC nodes, the project aims to reduce model training times from weeks to days, enabling iterative testing of management strategies against stochastic variables. Outcomes will include open-source tools for extension agents to generate dynamic recommendations via user-friendly dashboards, validated through on-farm trials in collaboration with regional producer networks. This work addresses critical gaps in scalable, adaptive precision agriculture tools, with potential to enhance the responsiveness of extension services to localized agricultural challenges while reducing economic and environmental risks for stakeholders. The computational infrastructure will also support future integration of real-time sensor data streams, fostering long-term innovation in agricultural education and decision-support systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide referral, consulting, technical assistance, and educational services to gardeners, farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and other organizations. Includes instruction in basic agricultural sciences, agricultural business operations, pest control, adult education methods, public relations, applicable state laws and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling in landscape architecture, focusing on the dynamic interplay between ecological systems, human-designed landscapes, and climate variability. Traditional design methods often rely on static environmental datasets or simplified simulations, limiting the ability to predict long-term ecological performance under stochastic climate conditions. This project addresses this gap by developing a multi-agent simulation framework that integrates real-time hydrological data, vegetative growth algorithms, and human behavioral patterns to model landscape resilience at urban scales. The computational approach combines geospatial analysis, machine learning for predictive scenario generation, and agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between soil erosion, plant communities, and pedestrian movement in high-density urban green spaces. Key challenges include processing high-resolution LiDAR and satellite imagery to parameterize micro-scale terrain variations, as well as optimizing parallelized simulations for diverse climate scenarios (e.g., extreme precipitation events, drought cycles). The HPC infrastructure will enable iterative testing of design interventions across 10,000+ stochastic climate realizations, providing probabilistic assessments of landscape durability and ecosystem service delivery. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive landscape design, validated against case studies in flood-prone coastal cities, and novel metrics quantifying the economic value of ecological redundancy in public spaces. By bridging computational ecology with design practice, this work aims to establish evidence-based standards for climate-responsive landscapes while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-STEM design disciplines. The results will directly inform municipal resilience planning and offer a replicable methodology for integrating complex systems science into landscape architecture education and professional workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of landscape architecture and research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in geology and hydrology; soils, groundcovers, and horticultural elements; project and site planning; landscape design, history, and theory; environmental design; applicable law and regulations; and professional responsibilities and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in educational assessment by developing advanced computational models to analyze complex, multidimensional assessment data at scale. Traditional psychometric methods often struggle to account for dynamic learning processes, contextual biases, and high-dimensional interaction patterns inherent in modern digital learning platforms and adaptive testing systems. The research will employ machine learning architectures and Bayesian hierarchical models to (1) detect latent skill trajectories across heterogeneous student populations, (2) quantify differential item functioning in culturally diverse contexts, and (3) optimize automated scoring systems for constructed-response assessments. High-performance computing resources are essential for training transformer-based models on longitudinal response data from 2.5 million learners across 14 state assessment systems, conducting Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate measurement invariance, and implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms for large-scale item response theory parameter estimation. Computational challenges include managing sparse, nested data structures across multiple assessment modalities (e.g., game-based tasks, multimedia stimuli) while maintaining interpretability for educational decision-making. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for real-time diagnostic assessment analytics, improved detection of biased test items through neural network attribution methods, and optimized algorithms for adaptive test assembly that reduce computational latency by 40% compared to current industry standards. By enhancing the scalability and precision of measurement models, this work will directly inform the design of fairer, more responsive assessment systems while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of psychometrics and computational education research.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for designing, developing, implementing and evaluating tests and other mechanisms used to measure learning, evaluate student progress, and assess the performance of specific teaching tools, strategies and curricula. Includes instruction in psychometric measurement, instrument design, test implementation techniques, research evaluation, data reporting requirements, and data analysis and interpretation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational workflows in architectural design, specifically addressing the integration of generative algorithms, real-time simulation, and multi-objective optimization within immersive digital design environments. Contemporary architectural practice faces a critical challenge in balancing design innovation, material efficiency, and environmental performance, particularly as projects grow in scale and complexity. While parametric modeling and digital fabrication have transformed design possibilities, existing tools struggle to synthesize real-time feedback across structural, thermal, and occupant-centric datasets during iterative design exploration. This research proposes a computational framework that unifies physics-based simulations, machine learning-assisted topology optimization, and augmented reality (AR) interfaces to enable architects to interactively explore high-dimensional design spaces. The HPC infrastructure will support parallelized evaluation of thousands of design variants through finite element analysis (FEA) for structural performance, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for microclimate modeling, and reinforcement learning agents trained to propose material-efficient geometries. A novel aspect involves developing distributed computing pipelines to bridge discrete architectural software ecosystems (e.g., BIM platforms, game engines) with scientific simulation tools, requiring customized containerization and GPU-accelerated rendering for AR visualization. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source middleware prototype for cross-platform interoperability, validated through case studies on adaptive reuse projects requiring rapid performance evaluation of heritage structures under climate stress scenarios. By reducing latency between design iteration and performance feedback from days to minutes, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for computationally augmented decision-making in architecture, with broader implications for resource-efficient urban retrofitting strategies. The requested resources will enable scaling from single-building analyses to district-level simulations, addressing critical gaps in tools for sustainable architectural practice.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: Advances in oncology pharmacy require precise integration of pharmacogenomic, clinical, and molecular data to optimize therapeutic strategies for cancer patients. A critical barrier in this field is the computational complexity of modeling multi-omics datasets to predict patient-specific drug responses, particularly in heterogeneous malignancies. This project proposes the development of a scalable machine learning framework to analyze high-dimensional genomic, transcriptomic, and pharmacokinetic data, coupled with real-world clinical outcomes, to identify predictive biomarkers and personalize treatment regimens. The research will employ ensemble learning algorithms, neural networks, and Bayesian inference models to integrate sparse, multi-modal datasets while accounting for tumor evolution and drug resistance mechanisms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative training of models on terabyte-scale datasets, perform parallelized molecular dynamics simulations of drug-target interactions, and conduct sensitivity analyses across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for chemotherapy and targeted therapy response in solid tumors, (2) identification of novel combinatorial drug targets to overcome resistance pathways, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive therapy optimization. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid processing of whole-exome sequencing data from 2,000+ patients (retrospective cohort) and real-time analysis of prospective data from ongoing clinical trials. By leveraging distributed computing for large-scale parameter optimization and cross-validation, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks that currently limit clinical translation. The results will directly inform precision dosing protocols, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and minimize adverse drug events in oncology practice. This project bridges computational innovation with clinical pharmacy by providing a template for resource-efficient, data-driven decision support in cancer care.
cip_definition: Research focused on oncology pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation in decentralized communication networks, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale interactions across hybrid digital platforms. As emerging communication technologies—such as federated social networks, encrypted messaging systems, and AI-mediated content tools—reshape information ecosystems, traditional analytical frameworks struggle to capture the nonlinear, cross-platform behaviors driving misinformation spread. The research problem centers on identifying critical thresholds at which localized misinformation events escalate into systemic crises, particularly in contexts where algorithmic moderation and human intervention interact unpredictably. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will integrate network science simulations with natural language processing (NLP) of multi-platform communication traces (e.g., social media posts, encrypted chat metadata, and synthetic media shares). Computational workflows will employ graph neural networks to model cross-platform influence cascades, coupled with agent-based simulations of user communities adapting to evolving content policies. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets spanning six communication platforms, training transformer-based NLP models on multilingual misinformation corpora, and running Monte Carlo iterations of crisis escalation scenarios with over 10^6 simulated agents. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for assessing platform-interconnected risks, quantitative metrics for resilience benchmarking, and visual analytics tools to support policymakers in designing adaptive content governance strategies. By mapping the computational affordances of modern communication technologies to their societal impacts, this work aims to advance both scholarly understanding of decentralized information systems and practical interventions for maintaining epistemic security in journalism-adjacent digital spaces.
cip_title: Communications Technologies and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications technologies and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of South Asian languages, with a focus on under-resourced and historically significant languages such as Prakrit, Pali, and early modern vernaculars. The research problem centers on the computational modeling of morphosyntactic and semantic structures in these languages, which exhibit complex agglutination, non-linear script representations, and dialectal variations that challenge conventional natural language processing (NLP) tools. Current methods, often optimized for Indo-European languages with digital corpora, fail to capture the unique linguistic features of South Asian languages, limiting scholarly access to textual analysis at scale. This project proposes the development of parallelized computational workflows to process and annotate multilingual corpora spanning 10+ South Asian languages, including digitized manuscripts, inscriptions, and oral narratives. Key computational methods include graph-based morphological parsers trained on finite-state transducers, transformer models adapted for low-resource language settings, and distributed semantic role labeling pipelines. These tools will be deployed on HPC clusters to enable batch processing of terabyte-scale textual data, iterative model training across GPU nodes, and comparative linguistic analyses through high-throughput simulations. The expected outcomes include open-access annotated corpora, reusable NLP models for historical and contemporary South Asian languages, and novel insights into syntactic evolution across literary traditions. By enabling large-scale, cross-linguistic studies, this work will advance computational methodologies in philology, support endangered language preservation efforts, and provide infrastructure for interdisciplinary research on South Asia’s literary heritage. The requested HPC resources are essential given the computational intensity of training multilingual models, the need for parallel processing of heterogenous text formats, and the scale of diachronic data spanning eight centuries.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of the Indian subcontinent and associated borderlands and island groups.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of climate-driven hydrological changes and their cascading impacts on terrestrial ecosystem resilience and biogeochemical cycles. As shifting precipitation patterns and intensified drought regimes increasingly stress regional water resources, predicting feedbacks between surface hydrology, vegetation dynamics, and soil carbon-nutrient cycling remains a critical challenge. To address this, we propose developing a high-resolution, process-based model integrating surface-subsurface hydrology, plant-soil interactions, and soil biogeochemistry.
