The model will leverage parallel computing architectures to simulate coupled water-carbon-nitrogen dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes at unprecedented spatial resolutions (100 m scale) over decadal timescales. Satellite remote sensing data (Sentinel-2, Landsat, GRACE-FO) will be assimilated to constrain soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and vegetation productivity, while machine learning techniques will optimize parameterization of subgrid-scale processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational load of multi-year ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios and to process large geospatial datasets. Expected outcomes include identifying regions at risk of hydrological regime shifts, quantifying thresholds for ecosystem transitions (e.g., forest to grassland), and mapping hotspots of soil carbon vulnerability under altered moisture regimes. The results will directly inform water resource management strategies and climate adaptation planning for agricultural and natural landscapes. By elucidating terrestrial system responses to hydroclimatic stressors, this work will contribute foundational knowledge to Earth system models while providing scalable computational frameworks for regional resilience assessments. The requested allocation supports iterative model development, large-scale data assimilation, and scenario analysis critical for addressing interlinked water, ecosystem, and climate challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interaction of the Earth's oceanographic, atmospheric, and terrestrial systems. Includes instruction in biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize personalized nutrition interventions using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between individual metabolic variability, gut microbiome dynamics, and dietary components. Dietetic technicians frequently encounter challenges in tailoring nutrition plans for patients with metabolic disorders (e.g., diabetes, obesity) due to the multifactorial nature of nutrient processing, which varies significantly across individuals. Current clinical tools lack the granularity to predict how specific foods or meal compositions interact with a patient’s unique microbial ecology and metabolic pathways, leading to trial-and-error approaches that delay effective care. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that integrates multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic) with real-time dietary intake records to simulate personalized nutrient-microbiome-host interactions. The project will leverage HPC resources to run large-scale simulations using mechanistic models of microbial metabolism (e.g., constraint-based reconstruction) coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on clinical datasets. These models will predict postprandial metabolic responses (e.g., glucose fluctuations, short-chain fatty acid production) to diverse meal compositions, accounting for interindividual differences in microbiome diversity and host genetics. By parallelizing simulations across thousands of dietary scenarios, we aim to identify optimal nutrient profiles for specific patient subgroups, reducing the need for iterative dietary adjustments in clinical practice. The outcomes will include an open-access tool for dietetic technicians to generate data-driven meal plans and a repository of simulated metabolic response datasets. This work bridges computational biology and clinical nutrition, advancing precision dietetics while providing a scalable platform to explore emergent questions in microbiome-nutrient interactions. Successful implementation will enhance the efficacy of dietary interventions, particularly for populations with complex metabolic needs underserved by conventional nutritional frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of registered dietitians and nutritionists, to implement nutritional and dietetic plans and provide direct client and patient services. Includes instruction in human nutrition, client interviewing and record keeping, dietary planning, food preparation and safety, food worker supervision, food service establishment monitoring and inspection, and applicable procedures and regulations.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations is a resource-intensive process, often hindered by the empirical nature of traditional trial-and-error experimentation. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling approaches for predicting the physicochemical behavior of complex drug delivery systems and cosmetic emulsions. The research will focus on overcoming challenges in preformulation evaluation, stability testing, and product reformulation by integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven quantitative structure-property relationship (QSPR) models, and finite element analysis (FEA) of multi-phase systems. Key objectives include simulating API-excipient interactions under varied thermodynamic conditions, optimizing emulsion droplet size distributions through computational fluid dynamics, and predicting degradation pathways for small molecules in topical formulations. The computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated MD packages (e.g., GROMACS) for nanoscale system characterization and distributed ML frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow) to analyze structure-stability correlations across large formulation datasets. By enabling rapid in silico screening of prototype formulations, this approach aims to reduce experimental iterations in physical stability testing by an estimated 40-60%, while providing mechanistic insights into failure modes observed during accelerated aging studies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-throughput simulations required to model complex semi-solid matrices and for training neural networks on historical formulation data spanning multiple product categories. Outcomes will directly inform industrial formulation strategies, enhance predictive capabilities in pharmaceutical development, and establish computational workflows that align with quality-by-design (QbD) principles for regulatory submissions. This work bridges critical gaps between computational pharmaceutics and real-world formulation challenges, offering transformative potential for both industrial pharmacy operations and cosmetic science innovation.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: Healthcare systems face escalating demands for efficient resource allocation amidst dynamic patient needs, workforce variability, and financial constraints. Traditional decision-making frameworks often rely on static models, which inadequately capture the complexity and uncertainty inherent in healthcare operations. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation and optimization platform to model multi-faceted healthcare delivery systems, with the goal of improving resource allocation strategies across hospitals and integrated care networks. The research will integrate agent-based modeling to simulate patient flow, staff scheduling, equipment utilization, and facility operations under diverse scenarios, including surge events and policy changes. Reinforcement learning algorithms will be employed to dynamically optimize real-time decisions, such as bed allocation, elective surgery scheduling, and cross-facility resource sharing, while accounting for financial viability and regulatory compliance. The computational framework will process large-scale datasets, including electronic health records, staffing logs, and cost structures, to identify inefficiencies and predict outcomes of intervention strategies. By leveraging parallel computing, the project will scale simulations to regional healthcare networks, enabling system-level analysis of trade-offs between cost, wait times, and clinical outcomes. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for administrators to balance operational budgets with service quality, evidence-based policy recommendations for crisis resource management, and open-source algorithmic modules adaptable to diverse healthcare settings. This work addresses critical gaps in computational health management by providing data-driven methodologies to enhance equity, resilience, and sustainability in healthcare delivery systems, directly supporting the program’s focus on operational excellence in health administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, plan, and manage health care operations and services within health care facilities and across health care systems. Includes instruction in planning, business management, financial management, public relations, human resources management, health care systems operation and management, health care resource allocation and policy making, health law and regulations, and applications to specific types of health care services.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of endocrine signaling dysregulation in tumor microenvironment adaptation and therapy resistance, with a focus on hormone-sensitive cancers. Despite advances in endocrine therapies, many tumors develop resistance through poorly understood mechanisms involving dynamic crosstalk between cancer cells and stromal components. The research problem centers on identifying how endocrine-driven cellular communication networks evolve during treatment, altering metabolic and secretory profiles to promote survival. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze spatially resolved transcriptomic and proteomic datasets from patient-derived xenograft models of breast and prostate cancer, capturing temporal changes in endocrine signaling pathways during therapy. Computational models will integrate single-cell RNA sequencing data with secreted protein profiles to reconstruct paracrine interaction networks between epithelial cells and fibroblasts. Agent-based simulations will map how hormone receptor activation dynamics influence collective survival behaviors under therapeutic pressure. A custom computational pipeline will employ Bayesian network inference to identify master regulatory nodes coordinating endocrine and stress-response pathways, validated through in silico perturbation experiments. Expected outcomes include predictive models of resistance-associated secretory phenotypes and candidate targets for disrupting adaptive endocrine-stromal crosstalk. This work will advance understanding of microenvironment-mediated therapy evasion while providing a computational framework to optimize combination therapies targeting both endocrine and compensatory signaling axes. The scale of multi-omic integration and need for high-resolution spatial-temporal modeling necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing of large-scale datasets (>50 TB) and iterative simulation of complex cellular systems. Outcomes will directly inform preclinical studies in hormone-driven cancers, bridging critical gaps between endocrine physiology and translational oncology.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition, manufacture, and secretion of protein compounds by cells and glands and the role of endocrine substances in bodily processes. Includes instruction in protein chemistry, protein secretion, membrane biogenesis and transfer methods, cellular communication, gene and cell regulation, cytochemistry, fractionation, radioautography, and applications such as neuroendocrinology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare data ecosystems, driven by advances in interoperable health information exchange and artificial intelligence applications, has amplified vulnerabilities in patient privacy protection. Existing anonymization frameworks often fail to account for combinatorial re-identification risks arising from multimodal data integration across distributed networks. This project seeks to develop and validate a dynamic privacy-risk assessment platform capable of simulating large-scale healthcare data linkage attacks while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct a synthetic health data environment mirroring real-world patient demographics, clinical variables, and socio-geographic markers across 50 million simulated patient records. Computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks to model potential adversarial inference pathways and probabilistic re-identification surfaces across heterogeneous data types, including genomic markers, wearable device outputs, and longitudinal electronic health record data. The parallelized architecture will enable simultaneous evaluation of multiple attack vectors under varying threat models while preserving differential privacy constraints through GPU-accelerated cryptographic computations. Validation phases will benchmark performance against current de-identification standards using federated learning approaches across simulated healthcare institutions. Expected outcomes include a risk stratification framework that quantifies re-identification probabilities in emerging data-sharing contexts and an open-source toolkit for adaptive anonymization policy testing. This work addresses critical gaps in healthcare information security by providing computational tools to proactively identify privacy erosion points in next-generation health data infrastructures, ultimately supporting the development of more robust patient privacy preservation strategies in complex, interconnected care environments.
cip_title: Healthcare Information Privacy Assurance and Security
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers in designing, implementing, and administering comprehensive privacy and security protection programs in all types of healthcare organizations. Includes instruction in health information ethics, healthcare information privacy and security, healthcare compliance, healthcare information security and disaster recovery, and healthcare privacy law.

abstract: The sustainable management of natural resources under accelerating climate change and anthropogenic pressures requires advanced predictive modeling to inform conservation strategies. This project addresses critical gaps in understanding how complex, large-scale interactions between climate variables, hydrological systems, and terrestrial ecosystems influence biodiversity patterns and resource availability at regional scales. Current models often oversimplify spatial heterogeneity or fail to integrate multi-temporal datasets spanning decades, limiting their utility for adaptive management. We propose to develop a high-resolution computational framework leveraging remotely sensed data (30m resolution), historical climate records, and species occurrence databases to simulate ecosystem responses under multiple climate scenarios (RCP 4.5, 6.0, 8.5). The research employs coupled hydrodynamic and species distribution models (SDMs) with machine learning techniques to predict shifts in habitat suitability for 200+ keystone species and quantify cascading impacts on watershed health. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process 80TB of multispectral imagery, run ensemble microclimate simulations at 1km² granularity, and optimize neural networks for ecological pattern recognition. Parallelized workflows using MPI will accelerate Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses assessing uncertainty in soil-carbon feedback loops and precipitation regime changes. Expected outcomes include: (1) spatially explicit vulnerability maps identifying conservation priority zones in critical biomes; (2) open-source algorithms for real-time drought-flood risk assessment integrating USGS streamflow data; and (3) predictive metrics quantifying trade-offs between forest carbon sequestration capacity and water resource sustainability. By enabling unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution in coupled human-natural system modeling, this work will directly support state agencies in revising habitat conservation plans and allocating climate resilience funding. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a replicable framework for interdisciplinary resource management studies across diverse ecological regions.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the studies and activities relating to the natural environment and its conservation, use, and improvement. Includes instruction in subjects such as climate, air, soil, water, land, fish and wildlife, and plant resources; in the basic principles of environmental science and natural resources management; and the recreational and economic uses of renewable and nonrenewable natural resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict the evolution of transnational terrorist networks and their operational strategies, with a focus on emerging cyberterrorism tactics and the use of encrypted communications. Current counterterrorism models often lack the granularity to capture the adaptive behaviors of decentralized groups, particularly their financial networks and online recruitment activities. To address this, we propose integrating multi-source intelligence data—including dark web transaction records, social media metadata, and intercepted communications—into a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation environment. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will be employed to simulate decision-making processes within terrorist cells under varying counterterrorism scenarios, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will analyze dynamic network relationships across temporal and spatial dimensions. The computational workflow requires processing petabytes of structured and unstructured data, necessitating GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines and distributed memory architectures for real-time pattern detection. Expected outcomes include a predictive analytics toolkit capable of identifying emerging threat vectors, estimating resource mobilization timelines for terrorist operations, and evaluating the cascading impacts of cyber-physical attacks on critical infrastructure. This research will advance the field by enabling three-dimensional visualization of threat networks, probabilistic risk assessments for weaponized AI systems, and evidence-based strategies for disrupting terrorist financing channels. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling our prototype to global threat landscapes, reducing simulation wall-clock times from weeks to hours, and maintaining compliance with privacy-preserving federated learning protocols when handling classified data subsets. Results will directly inform joint operations planning frameworks and enhance adaptive resilience models for homeland security agencies.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the study of terrorism as a global and national threat and the methods for analyzing and countering it. Includes instruction in psychology, cultural studies, terrorist history and organization, terrorist capabilities, terrorist finance and international money-laundering, threat assessment, intelligence operations, incident command systems, border security, emergency response, joint operations, surveillance and communications systems, cyberterrorism, weapons of mass destruction, counterterrorist operations, and applications to specific terrorist organizations and threats.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational modeling of multifactorial ophthalmic diseases, with a focus on optimizing diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for conditions such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration. Current clinical decision-making often relies on static, population-level data, which inadequately captures the dynamic interplay of genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors driving disease progression. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multi-omics integration and personalized risk prediction. The research will leverage federated learning architectures to aggregate anonymized patient data from collaborating optometric clinics, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) images, visual field tests, and longitudinal electronic health records. Computational workflows will combine deep learning models for image segmentation (e.g., retinal layer thickness quantification) with mechanistic modeling of intraocular pressure dynamics and vascular perfusion metrics. A key innovation involves implementing hybrid graph neural networks to map patient-specific biomarker interactions across temporal and spatial scales. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter optimization for these models while maintaining compliance with healthcare data privacy standards through containerized processing environments. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for disease progression trajectories and a cloud-based decision support tool prototype for clinicians. This resource will directly enhance the precision of optometric care delivery while establishing a scalable computational paradigm for ophthalmic research. The project’s open-source tools and de-identified datasets will be disseminated through partnerships with professional associations, creating infrastructure to advance computational optometry education and practice standards. By bridging HPC capabilities with clinical optometric workflows, this work aims to reduce preventable vision loss through earlier, more individualized interventions.
cip_title: Ophthalmic and Optometric Support Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ophthalmic and optometric support services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Public health education and promotion efforts face significant challenges in designing interventions that effectively account for the dynamic interplay of social, behavioral, and environmental factors influencing health outcomes. Current approaches often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the complexity of population-level interactions, limiting their predictive accuracy and real-world applicability. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to simulate the spread of health-related behaviors and evaluate the efficacy of targeted educational campaigns under diverse sociodemographic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate granular data on individual health literacy, social networks, environmental constraints, and cultural norms. These models will simulate intervention scenarios across synthetic populations calibrated to real-world census and health survey data, enabling the exploration of "what-if" strategies for promoting preventive measures (e.g., vaccination uptake, chronic disease management). Computational demands arise from the need to model populations exceeding 10 million agents, incorporate adaptive learning algorithms for behavior change processes, and perform multi-dimensional sensitivity analyses across intervention parameters. The HPC environment will facilitate parallelized simulations to assess spatial-temporal variations in intervention effectiveness and identify optimal resource allocation strategies for underserved communities. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible toolkit for predicting the population-level impacts of health education programs, evidence-based guidelines for tailoring communications to specific subpopulations, and quantitative frameworks for evaluating equity in health promotion efforts. This work directly addresses critical gaps in translational public health research by providing decision-makers with scalable, data-driven methods to maximize the reach and sustainability of preventive health initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of educational and communications principles and methods to the promotion of preventive health measures and the education of targeted populations on health issues, and prepares individuals to function as public health educators and health promotion specialists. Includes instruction in human development, health issues across the life span, population-specific health issues, principles and methods of public health education, administration of health education campaigns and programs, evaluation methods, public communications, and applications to specific public health subjects and issues.

abstract: Climate change and escalating anthropogenic pressures necessitate robust economic strategies to optimize conservation efforts and sustainable resource management. However, existing approaches often fail to account for the dynamic, non-linear interactions between ecological systems and socioeconomic factors, leading to suboptimal policy outcomes. This project addresses this gap by developing an integrated computational framework to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of conservation policies under environmental and market uncertainties. The research employs high-performance computing (HPC) to implement a spatially explicit, dynamic stochastic model that combines agent-based simulations of resource user behavior with biophysical models of ecosystem services. Key computational tasks include Bayesian calibration of ecological-economic parameters, Monte Carlo simulations to assess climate scenario uncertainties, and parallelized optimization algorithms to identify Pareto-efficient resource allocation strategies across heterogeneous landscapes. The model integrates high-resolution datasets on land use, biodiversity, and regional economic indicators, requiring large-scale data processing and real-time sensitivity analyses. By quantifying trade-offs between conservation investments, agricultural productivity, and long-term ecosystem resilience, this project aims to generate actionable insights for designing adaptive management policies. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for policymakers to prioritize interventions in critical habitats while balancing equity and efficiency goals. The computational framework will also advance methodological innovation in environmental economics by enabling granular, systems-level analysis of coupled human-natural systems, which is infeasible with conventional computing resources. This work directly contributes to global sustainability targets by bridging gaps between economic theory, ecological complexity, and computational scalability.
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resource Economics (NATURAL RESOURCES/ CONSERVATION SCIENCES)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: The emergence of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to global health, driven in part by the horizontal transfer of mobile genetic elements (MGEs) such as plasmids and transposons. While the molecular mechanisms underlying MGE transfer are broadly characterized, the regulatory networks and host-pathogen interactions governing their stability and propagation in diverse bacterial populations remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating large-scale comparative genomics with mechanistic modeling to identify conserved genetic and epigenetic factors influencing MGE dynamics in clinically relevant Gram-negative bacteria. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the analysis of over 50,000 bacterial genomes to map structural variations, recombination hotspots, and regulatory motifs associated with MGE maintenance. Custom sequence alignment pipelines will be optimized for distributed-memory architectures to process terabyte-scale datasets. Mechanistic simulations using agent-based models will explore how population heterogeneity, nutrient stress, and phage predation modulate conjugation efficiency and plasmid fitness. These models will incorporate empirical data from publicly available transcriptomic and chromatin conformation capture (Hi-C) datasets to parameterize host-MGE interactions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking genetic architecture to MGE dissemination patterns, with applications for designing targeted strategies to disrupt resistance gene spread. The computational workflows developed will be modular and scalable, facilitating future integration of single-cell omics data. By elucidating principles of genetic stability and transfer in bacterial populations, this work will advance foundational knowledge in molecular genetics while addressing an urgent public health challenge. The requested resources are critical for managing memory-intensive genomic analyses and stochastic simulations across parameter spaces infeasible on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: Turfgrass systems are critical components of agricultural and recreational landscapes, yet optimizing their sustainability and resilience under increasing environmental stressors remains a significant challenge. This project seeks to address key knowledge gaps in turfgrass genetics, physiology, and adaptive management by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex genotype-environment-management interactions. The research problem centers on identifying genetic markers and management practices that enhance drought tolerance, disease resistance, and nutrient-use efficiency in cool-season turfgrasses, which are economically vital but face mounting pressures from climate variability. Current experimental approaches are limited in scalability and predictive power due to the multivariate nature of these systems. We propose a computational framework integrating machine learning, genomic prediction models, and process-based ecophysiological simulations to analyze multi-omics datasets (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) and long-term turf performance data from controlled and field environments. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of Bayesian genome-wide association studies (GWAS), neural network training on hyperspectral imaging data, and stochastic optimization of irrigation-fertilization regimes under diverse climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes linked to stress tolerance, predictive models for turfgrass response to abiotic and biotic stressors, and data-driven recommendations for precision management. By elucidating the molecular and environmental drivers of turfgrass resilience, this work will directly inform breeding programs and operational practices, reducing water and chemical inputs while maintaining turf quality. The computational pipeline developed will also serve as a template for integrative analyses in other perennial grass systems, advancing methodological synergies between agricultural science and computational biology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on turfgrasses and related groundcover plants and prepares individuals to develop ornamental or recreational grasses and related products; plant, transplant, and manage grassed areas; and to produce and store turf used for transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable plant sciences, genetics of grasses, turf science, use analysis, turf management, and related economics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing hyper-localized sales and distribution networks in volatile consumer markets. The research problem centers on the inefficiencies of traditional static distribution models in adapting to real-time demand fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, and spatially heterogeneous consumer behavior—challenges amplified by climate-related logistics uncertainties and shifting purchasing patterns in post-pandemic economies. We propose an agent-based simulation platform that integrates real-time sales data, geospatial weather patterns, and dynamic inventory constraints to model multi-echelon distribution networks at street-level granularity. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic demand forecasting with graph neural networks to optimize routing and inventory allocation across interdependent nodes, while accounting for competitive pricing feedback loops. A unique innovation involves embedding generative AI to simulate synthetic consumer cohorts exhibiting non-linear responses to micro-targeted promotions, enabling stress-testing of resilience strategies under 10,000+ scenario variations. The project will validate models against proprietary data from a partner network of 350+ urban retail outlets, requiring parallelized computation of high-dimensional decision spaces. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive distribution planning, with preliminary results demonstrating a 15–20% reduction in perishable goods waste in pilot food distribution systems. The work bridges computational economics, operations research, and spatial analytics, advancing business methodology for resource allocation in climate-vulnerable markets while establishing benchmarks for AI-driven sales channel optimization. HPC resources are critical for handling the terabyte-scale integration of IoT sensor data, satellite weather feeds, and transaction records across simulated temporal horizons exceeding 18 months.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous biological datasets to uncover dynamic patterns in protein interaction networks and their role in cellular signaling processes. Current methods for network analysis struggle with scalability and precision when handling high-dimensional data from diverse sources, such as proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and structural interactome databases. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-optimized pipeline integrating graph neural networks (GNNs) and parallelized Monte Carlo simulations. The pipeline will model time-resolved protein interaction dynamics, predict context-specific signaling pathways, and quantify uncertainty in network inferences. By leveraging distributed computing frameworks (e.g., Dask and MPI) and GPU-accelerated GNN training, the approach will efficiently process datasets spanning millions of interactions across multiple experimental conditions. Key outcomes include (1) novel algorithms for scalable network topology optimization, (2) probabilistic models of signaling crosstalk, and (3) an open-source software package for community use. The computational demands—including memory-intensive graph operations, thousands of parallel simulation trials, and hyperparameter optimization—necessitate dedicated HPC resources. Successful implementation will enable unprecedented resolution of signaling network plasticity, with applications to therapeutic target identification and precision medicine. This work directly advances bioinformatics methodologies by bridging gaps between network theory, statistical learning, and systems biology, while providing infrastructure for future large-scale omics integration studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer-based technologies and services to biological, biomedical, and biotechnology research. Includes instruction in algorithms, network architecture, principles of software design, human interface design, usability studies, search strategies, database management and data mining, digital image processing, computer graphics and animation, CAD, computer programming, and applications to experimental design and analysis and to specific quantitative, modeling, and analytical studies in the various biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of dynamic cognitive load modulation in virtual learning environments (VLEs) through computational modeling and real-time simulation. As digital education tools become increasingly complex, learners face challenges in managing cognitive resources effectively, leading to disparities in engagement and knowledge retention. Traditional pedagogical models struggle to adapt to individual cognitive thresholds, particularly in heterogeneous or large-scale virtual classrooms. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity neural network framework that simulates learner-environment interactions under varying cognitive load conditions. The model will integrate psychometric data, eye-tracking patterns, and physiological response datasets to predict optimal load thresholds for different learning modalities (e.g., immersive VR vs. 2D interfaces). High-performance computing resources are essential to process multimodal data streams concurrently, train reinforcement learning agents that adapt content delivery in simulated environments, and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations assessing scalability across diverse demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for educators to design cognitively sustainable VLEs and evidence-based thresholds for adaptive content pacing algorithms. This work bridges educational psychology, computational neuroscience, and human-computer interaction, offering a novel framework to address equity in digital learning by computationally modeling the biological and environmental constraints of cognitive capacity. Results will be validated against empirical classroom studies, with open-source code and simulation templates disseminated to support personalized learning infrastructure development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory and practice of learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how large-scale computational analysis can advance understanding of genre evolution in digital writing environments, particularly as traditional text-based genres adapt to multimodal, interactive formats. While existing scholarship has qualitatively examined shifts in genres like blogs, podcasts, and interactive narratives, the scale and complexity of digital writing across platforms necessitate quantitative approaches to identify patterns in rhetorical strategies, structural innovation, and audience engagement. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning to analyze a corpus of 30,000 digital texts spanning 2010–2023, sourced from open-access repositories, social media, and web archives. Computational methods will include semantic network analysis to map rhetorical moves, transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) to classify hybrid genre features, and sentiment analysis to correlate stylistic choices with reader feedback metrics. High-performance computing resources are critical for training custom NLP models on heterogeneous data (text, metadata, hyperlinks) and processing multimodal elements, including embedded images and dynamic content, which require parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated feature extraction. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of emergent digital genres based on computational rhetorical analysis, (2) models predicting successful genre adaptation strategies across contexts, and (3) open-access tools for writers to visualize genre conventions and audience expectations. By bridging computational methods with writing studies, this project will provide empirically grounded insights into how digital technologies reshape compositional practices, offering practical applications for writing pedagogy, professional communication, and inclusive design in public-facing genres.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the personalization of educational interventions for students with disabilities, addressing the challenge of efficiently tailoring evidence-based strategies to highly heterogeneous learning needs. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual data analysis and generalized frameworks, which can limit scalability and precision in dynamic classroom settings. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from K-12 special education programs, including longitudinal academic performance metrics, behavioral logs, teacher annotations, and physiological sensor data from attention-monitoring tools. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns in student responses to specific interventions under varying conditions, such as classroom configurations, task types, and instructor scaffolding techniques. Computational simulations will test hypothetical intervention combinations across synthetic cohorts representing diverse disability profiles (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, and developmental delays), enabling rapid iteration of strategies that maximize predicted learning gains while minimizing educator workload. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated clustering algorithms to categorize emergent student archetypes and reinforcement learning to model adaptive teaching sequences. Outcomes will include an open-source framework for generating data-driven IEP recommendations and a sensitivity analysis toolkit to evaluate intervention robustness across demographic and disability severity factors. By enabling real-time processing of complex, high-dimensional educational data, this work aims to reduce disparities in special education outcomes through computationally optimized teaching strategies while preserving the critical role of human educator judgment. The requested resources will support the parallel processing demands of training transformer-based models on sensitive, de-identified student records (≥100 TB) and running multi-agent simulations of classroom dynamics at scale.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of spiritual resilience in digital religious communities through computational text and network analysis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale, unstructured datasets. As virtual faith-based spaces—such as prayer forums, grief support groups, and crisis counseling channels—grow in prominence, their role in shaping individual and collective spiritual well-being remains underexplored. The research problem centers on identifying linguistic, relational, and behavioral patterns that correlate with measurable outcomes in pastoral care efficacy, particularly in contexts where traditional in-person ministry is inaccessible. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) to analyze sentiment, thematic clusters, and narrative structures in anonymized text corpora from moderated interfaith support platforms (spanning 2015–2023), alongside temporal network analysis to model participant engagement and community cohesion. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to detect subtle markers of spiritual distress or growth, while graph algorithms will map the diffusion of coping strategies and social support across decentralized networks. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale (estimated 15TB of text and metadata) and complexity of these analyses, particularly for fine-tuning large language models on domain-specific theological and counseling terminology, and for running iterative simulations of community resilience under varying sociotechnical conditions. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying pastoral impact in digital ministry contexts, actionable insights for optimizing virtual care protocols, and open-source tools tailored to ethical analysis of sensitive spiritual communication data. This work bridges computational social science, pastoral theology, and digital humanities, offering methodological innovations for studying emergent forms of religious practice while addressing urgent practical challenges in scalable, culturally competent spiritual care.
cip_title: Pastoral Counseling and Specialized Ministries, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pastoral counseling and specialized ministries, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Black cultural production across the 20th-century United States and Caribbean, with a focus on interdisciplinary connections between literature, visual art, and music. While existing scholarship has documented key movements like the Harlem Renaissance or Negritude, significant gaps remain in mapping large-scale patterns of creative exchange, thematic recurrence, and diasporic influence due to the scale and complexity of archival materials. Our research will employ computational text analysis, image recognition, and network modeling to process digitized collections of novels, paintings, oral histories, and musical recordings from 1900–1999. Using natural language processing (NLP) tools fine-tuned for African-American Vernacular English and Creole languages, we will identify linguistic motifs in literary works alongside parallel visual patterns in contemporaneous artworks. Audio analysis algorithms will cross-reference musical structures with textual/visual datasets to trace transmedia cultural signatures. Graph neural networks will then model spatial and temporal diffusion of creative themes across geographic nodes (e.g., New York, New Orleans, Port-au-Prince). This approach requires HPC capabilities to manage heterogeneous data (10TB+ of text, images, audio) and run multi-modal machine learning pipelines. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously understudied connections between regional artistic movements, 2) visualization of how specific aesthetic strategies persisted or transformed through migration and political change, and 3) an open-access computational framework for analyzing diasporic cultural production. By enabling systematic study of cross-disciplinary creative practices at scale, this project aims to reshape understandings of Black cultural innovation while developing methodologies that center African-American Studies’ unique archival challenges and opportunities.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of the North American peoples descended from the African diaspora; focusing on the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean, but also including reference to Latin American elements of the diaspora.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-echelon parts warehousing networks through the development of a high-fidelity computational framework that integrates real-time inventory tracking, predictive demand modeling, and autonomous replenishment algorithms. The core challenge lies in balancing competing operational constraints—including spatial limitations in storage facilities, heterogeneous part perishability rates, and stochastic supplier lead times—while maintaining service-level agreements for diverse customer segments. Current heuristic-based approaches fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these variables at enterprise scale, particularly when managing millions of SKUs across distributed fulfillment centers. The proposed solution leverages high-performance computing resources to implement a hybrid simulation-optimization architecture combining discrete-event modeling of warehouse operations with reinforcement learning agents trained on historical transaction data. Key computational components include: 1) GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for risk propagation across supply chain tiers, 2) graph neural networks to model part substitution patterns and counter service interactions, and 3) distributed optimization solvers for simultaneous capacity allocation across network nodes. The research will validate the framework using a novel dataset comprising IoT sensor streams from automated storage systems, supplier quality metrics, and technician repair histories. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system capable of generating adaptive replenishment policies that reduce excess inventory holdings by ≥18% while maintaining 99.5% same-day fulfillment rates, along with open-source tools for simulating cascading stockout scenarios in critical parts distribution networks. This work bridges gaps between operations research, industrial engineering, and computational logistics, offering methodological advances in handling time-dependent constraints within large-scale inventory systems.
cip_title: Parts, Warehousing, and Inventory Management Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide administrative, technical, and managerial support in the operation of warehouses, control of inventory, parts identification, and the performance of counter services for customers. Includes instruction in record-keeping, equipment operation, database entry, supply logistics, shop operations and math, and customer and supplier relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a machine learning framework to optimize the design of individualized education plans (IEPs) for elementary students with disabilities, addressing the challenge of efficiently integrating heterogeneous data to personalize instruction. Current IEP development relies heavily on manual analysis of student performance, behavioral observations, and diagnostic assessments—a process that strains educator capacity and may overlook subtle patterns in multisource data. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multimodal deep learning models on structured and unstructured data from 5,000+ anonymized IEPs, longitudinal academic records, and sensor-based engagement metrics (e.g., eye-tracking, response latency) collected across 15 special education classrooms. Computational workflows will process natural language notes, time-series behavioral logs, and curriculum-aligned assessment scores to identify cross-modal predictors of skill acquisition rates. A transformer-based architecture will then recommend targeted accommodations, scaffolded objectives, and intervention strategies tailored to individual learner profiles. Validation will involve simulating IEP efficacy across synthetic cohorts representing diverse disabilities, socioeconomic factors, and classroom contexts. By automating data synthesis and pattern detection, this approach aims to reduce IEP preparation time by 30–50% while improving the granularity of skill progression targets, as measured by post-implementation student growth metrics. The resulting open-source toolkit will provide educators with real-time decision support, dynamically adjusting recommendations based on ongoing student data. This work directly addresses critical gaps in special education practice by enhancing the scalability of evidence-based personalization, ultimately fostering more equitable outcomes for neurodiverse learners. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets, training complex models with cross-validation, and running large-scale simulations to ensure robustness across educational settings.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Elementary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the elementary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for elementary special education; and teaching elementary education subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to advance sustainable pulp and paper manufacturing by optimizing the energy-intensive pulping and bleaching processes through high-fidelity computational modeling. Current industrial methods rely on empirical correlations that inadequately capture the complex, multiscale interactions between lignocellulosic fibers, chemical reagents, and process parameters. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of lignin depolymerization, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modeling of reactor-scale transport phenomena, and machine learning (ML)-driven surrogate models for process optimization. The MD component will simulate solvent-lignin interactions at the atomic scale using reactive force fields (ReaxFF) to identify catalytic pathways for reducing thermal degradation energy barriers. Concurrently, CFD simulations will resolve turbulent flow, heat transfer, and chemical diffusion in industrial digesters, enabling the design of spatially optimized reagent distribution systems. These high-resolution models will inform ML training datasets to develop real-time predictive controllers for minimizing chlorine dioxide usage in bleaching stages while maintaining product brightness specifications. The computational workload demands high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the need for large-scale parallel MD simulations (10^6+ atoms), transient multiphase CFD with adaptive meshing, and distributed hyperparameter tuning for neural networks. Expected outcomes include a 15-20% reduction in energy consumption for kraft pulping, a 30% decrease in bleaching chemical demand, and predictive models transferable to biorefinery operations. By elucidating fundamental process-structure-property relationships across scales, this work will provide a computational toolkit for transitioning the pulp and paper industry toward carbon-neutral manufacturing paradigms. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for MD/ML workloads and high-memory CPUs for large-domain CFD simulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and manufacturing of pulp and paper products. Includes instruction in pulp and paper science, pulping and bleaching processes, paper structure and processes, pulp and paper manufacturing, coating technology, surface and colloid science, and fibers.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving regulatory landscape of insurance law, focusing on the intersection of legal doctrine, actuarial risk models, and algorithmic decision-making in underwriting. The research addresses a critical gap in computational legal studies: the lack of scalable frameworks to model how heterogeneous state and federal insurance regulations interact with dynamic risk environments, particularly in emerging areas such as cyber liability, climate-related coverage gaps, and AI-driven claims adjudication. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) to parse legal texts (statutes, case law, and regulatory guidance) with stochastic simulations of insurance market behaviors, the project aims to quantify the systemic impacts of regulatory fragmentation on market stability and consumer protection. Key computational challenges include training transformer-based models on domain-specific legal corpora to identify latent patterns in regulatory divergence, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate insurer and policyholder decision-making under varying regulatory constraints. The HPC environment is essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter space of these simulations, which involve millions of interdependent agents across jurisdictional boundaries and multi-year risk horizons. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for predicting regulatory arbitrage hotspots, optimizing compliance strategies for insurers, and informing evidence-based policymaking. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, advancing methodologies for large-scale legal system analysis while addressing pressing questions about equity and resilience in insurance markets. By situating insurance law within a computational paradigm, the project establishes a novel interdisciplinary niche that transcends traditional doctrinal analysis, offering scalable solutions to 21st-century regulatory challenges.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive framework for optimizing grant-seeking strategies in mission-driven organizations, with a focus on computational grantsmanship—an emerging interdisciplinary niche integrating business analytics, behavioral economics, and natural language processing. The research addresses the critical challenge of resource allocation in competitive funding environments, where organizations often lack data-driven methods to prioritize grant opportunities, align proposals with funder priorities, and predict success probabilities. Current approaches rely on manual processes and heuristic decision-making, resulting in inefficiencies and suboptimal outcomes. The project will employ machine learning models trained on heterogeneous datasets, including historical grant awards, funder mission statements, proposal text corpora, and economic indicators. Computational experiments will utilize agent-based simulations to model funder-organization interactions under varying resource allocation scenarios, while transformer-based architectures will analyze semantic patterns in successful proposals. Key technical challenges include scaling graph neural networks to map evolving funder networks and processing multi-modal data streams in real time. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for probabilistic grant opportunity scoring, dynamic budget allocation optimization algorithms, and a generative AI assistant for proposal tailoring. These deliverables aim to reduce the cost-per-award ratio by an estimated 30-40% for nonprofit and social enterprise users while advancing computational methods for ethical AI in resource-constrained business contexts. The research will contribute novel insights into the behavioral dynamics of philanthropic markets and establish benchmarks for data-driven grantsmanship, with implications for emerging fields such as altruism analytics and impact finance. HPC resources are essential for training large language models on proprietary grant databases, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of funding ecosystems, and maintaining secure, auditable workflows for sensitive organizational data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and write grant proposals to support an organization or cause. Includes instruction in identifying grant opportunities, developing an effective proposal, budget justifications, and developing a working relationship with the funder.

abstract: This project seeks to address the scalability and accuracy challenges inherent in automating real-time accounting processes for multinational enterprises, where traditional software systems struggle with high-volume, heterogeneous transaction data across diverse regulatory environments. The rapid digitization of global financial systems, coupled with increasing transaction velocities and compliance demands, necessitates computational frameworks capable of dynamically reconciling ledgers, detecting anomalies, and enforcing jurisdiction-specific rules at scale. We propose developing a hybrid architecture combining graph-based transaction modeling, federated learning for localized compliance pattern recognition, and parallelized blockchain-inspired consensus mechanisms to enable secure, auditable record-keeping across distributed entities. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate enterprise-scale transaction environments (10^8+ daily events) with varying tax regimes and reporting standards, training machine learning models on synthetically generated financial data while maintaining data isolation constraints. Computational experiments will focus on optimizing distributed ledger sharding techniques for real-time balance sheet synchronization and stress-testing anomaly detection algorithms under peak load scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive accounting system design, quantitative benchmarks for transaction throughput versus auditability tradeoffs in multi-jurisdictional contexts, and novel metrics for measuring algorithmic fairness in automated compliance decisions. By advancing the computational infrastructure underlying next-generation accounting technologies, this work aims to reduce latency in financial reporting cycles by 40-60% for large organizations while maintaining sub-0.1% error rates in automated regulatory adherence—a critical capability as real-time fiscal transparency becomes central to global business operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: This project seeks to advance voice writing technology by addressing critical gaps in real-time transcription accuracy and adaptability across diverse linguistic and acoustic environments. Voice writing systems—essential for live captioning, media accessibility, and transcription services—often struggle with variability in speech patterns, background noise, speaker accents, and domain-specific terminology, leading to errors that hinder communication access. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to train and optimize adaptive neural speech recognition models capable of processing multimodal inputs (audio, contextual metadata, and user corrections) while maintaining low latency for real-time applications. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and dynamic acoustic adaptation algorithms, to improve contextual awareness and robustness. Large-scale datasets of spoken shorthand, live event recordings, and annotated corrections will be used to simulate challenging real-world conditions, enabling iterative model refinement. Computational workflows will prioritize parallel processing to reduce training times for resource-intensive tasks such as noise-invariant feature extraction and speaker diarization. Expected outcomes include a scalable, open-source voice writing toolkit with enhanced accuracy (targeting <5% word error rate in noisy environments) and adaptive personalization features for professional captioners and journalists. This work will directly benefit accessibility initiatives, media production workflows, and remote communication platforms by reducing barriers to high-quality transcription. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume (estimated at 50TB of audio-text pairs) and computational demands, enabling rapid experimentation with model architectures that would otherwise be infeasible on local infrastructure. By bridging computational linguistics with user-centered design, this project aims to set new benchmarks for equitable access to voice-driven communication technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to use voice writing computer software and speak a verbal shorthand language to create transcripts and screen captioning of live or recorded events intended for the public or a specific audience in a variety of media (e.g., digital, film, print, television) as well as for conferences, conversations, interviews, and meetings. Includes instruction in screen captioning, speed building, spoken shorthand, transcription, and voice input writing.

abstract: Marine transportation systems face increasing complexity due to evolving environmental regulations, dynamic operational demands, and the need for sustainable practices. This project seeks to optimize vessel routing and energy efficiency in heterogeneous maritime networks by integrating high-resolution environmental data, real-time vessel performance metrics, and port operation constraints. Current analytical methods struggle to account for the multivariate, nonlinear interactions between hydrodynamic forces, propulsion systems, and logistical requirements at scale. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The approach combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of vessel hydrodynamics with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal routing strategies that minimize fuel consumption and emissions while meeting operational schedules. Nested mesoscale oceanographic models will provide localized wave and current forecasts, while graph neural networks will model port congestion dynamics. The computational workflow requires parallel execution of multiple CFD instances across varying environmental conditions, coupled with iterative optimization cycles that demand significant memory bandwidth and GPU-accelerated machine learning training. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for maritime operators, quantitative assessments of energy-saving potential under climate variability scenarios, and novel methodologies for coupled physical-AI modeling in transportation systems. This work will directly contribute to the International Maritime Organization's decarbonization targets while advancing computational techniques applicable to complex transportation networks. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving sufficient spatial resolution in hydrodynamic simulations (10^8 grid cells per vessel configuration) and for training deep reinforcement learning models on petascale datasets spanning global shipping routes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in water transportation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociotechnical dynamics of AI-driven urban surveillance systems through a computational lens, integrating policy analysis, ethical frameworks, and large-scale behavioral simulations. As cities globally adopt artificial intelligence for public safety and infrastructure management, the interplay between algorithmic decision-making, civic trust, and regulatory efficacy remains understudied. The research problem centers on modeling how heterogeneous sociopolitical values—embedded in urban populations—interact with automated surveillance architectures, potentially amplifying biases or eroding public consent. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop agent-based models simulating multi-stakeholder decision networks (citizens, municipal authorities, AI developers) across diverse demographic and governance contexts. These models will incorporate real-world datasets on policy adoption rates, anonymized mobility patterns, and public sentiment metrics derived from social media. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess emergent outcomes under varying ethical constraint parameters (e.g., transparency thresholds, accountability mechanisms) to quantify trade-offs between surveillance efficacy and societal equity. The computational framework will enable sensitivity analyses at unprecedented scale, testing how localized cultural norms and legacy infrastructures mediate the global proliferation of surveillance technologies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of scenario projections to inform adaptive governance frameworks, alongside novel metrics for evaluating "algorithmic accountability thresholds" in urban policy contexts. By bridging computational social science with Science and Technology Studies, this work aims to establish predictive tools for anticipating second-order societal impacts of intelligent systems while advancing methodological integration across technical and humanistic domains.
detailed_field: History/ philosophy of science, technology, and society
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the contemporary social and public policy ramifications of science and technology, the interrelationship of science and engineering with the public policy process, and the social and ethical dimensions of scientific and technological enterprises.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of ethical reasoning in complex, large-scale moral dilemmas, particularly those arising in emerging technologies and sociotechnical systems. While traditional ethical analysis relies on qualitative, case-based methods, the increasing scale and interconnectivity of modern moral problems—such as algorithmic bias, climate justice, or biomedical AI—demand tools capable of modeling dynamic interactions between ethical principles, contextual variables, and stakeholder priorities. The research problem centers on developing computational frameworks to systematically analyze how competing ethical theories (e.g., utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics) resolve conflicts in high-dimensional scenarios where outcomes depend on non-linear relationships and probabilistic uncertainties. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, Bayesian networks, and constrained optimization techniques to simulate decision landscapes under diverse ethical paradigms. Agent behaviors will be encoded with rule sets derived from philosophical literature, while environmental variables will incorporate empirical data from case studies in technology ethics and policy. HPC resources are essential for iteratively testing model robustness across parameter spaces encompassing millions of potential scenario configurations and ethical weighting schemes. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible library of simulated moral dilemmas annotated with ethical trade-offs, (2) quantitative metrics for comparing theoretical approaches’ coherence under scalability pressures, and (3) visualizations of how hybrid ethical frameworks might address gaps in traditional theories when applied to systemic challenges. By bridging formal ethics with computational social science methods, this work aims to provide philosophers and policymakers with evidence-based tools for navigating morally pluralistic, rapidly evolving problem domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the theory of moral good and its application to various theoretical and practical problems. Includes instruction in ethical theory, history of ethics, belief and value systems, ethical constructs, and applications to specific topics, issues and problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dialectal variation and historical linguistic shifts in Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian (BSH) languages using advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The research addresses a critical gap in BSH studies: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to systematically map dialect continua, track lexical and morphosyntactic changes across time, and quantify mutual intelligibility between regional varieties. Current methodologies rely heavily on manual analysis of limited text samples, which restricts the scope and reproducibility of findings. To overcome these limitations, we propose training transformer-based language models on a curated corpus of over 10 million words spanning contemporary and historical texts (19th–21st centuries), including novels, newspapers, oral histories, and social media. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing this heterogeneous dataset, which requires distributed training across multiple GPU nodes to handle memory-intensive tasks such as contextual embedding generation and diachronic semantic shift detection. Computational experiments will include dialect classification using attention mechanisms, phonetic alignment of regional speech variants, and graph-based network analysis to model lexical borrowing patterns. The project will also develop open-source tools for low-resource Slavic language processing, including a BSH-specific tokenizer and a web interface for visualizing dialect boundaries. Expected outcomes include new insights into the dynamic interplay between standard languages and regional varieties in post-Yugoslav contexts, with applications in language preservation, educational resource development, and cross-cultural NLP systems. By leveraging parallel computing architectures to manage the computational complexity of multilingual and multidialectal modeling, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for computational humanities research in understudied language communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian Languages and Literatures
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bosnian, Serbian and/or Croatian languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and optical interactions governing corneal deformation under varying intraocular pressure (IOP) and mechanical stress, a critical factor in conditions such as keratoconus and post-refractive surgery ectasia. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individual susceptibility to vision-threatening deformations due to the cornea’s complex, anisotropic microstructure and dynamic response to physiological forces. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with ray-tracing simulations. The FEA component will simulate stress-strain distributions across corneal lamellae using patient-specific data from corneal topography, optical coherence tomography, and tonometry. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated ray-tracing will model light propagation through the deformed corneal geometry to quantify aberrations and visual quality degradation. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-resolution 3D corneal meshes (∼10^6 elements per simulation), solving nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive equations, and iteratively coupling biomechanical and optical outputs across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform correlating microstructural anomalies with macroscopic optical deficits, enabling early diagnosis of subclinical keratoconus and personalized refractive surgery planning. By elucidating how regional variations in collagen fibril orientation modulate both mechanical stability and optical performance, this work will advance therapeutic strategies for preserving visual function in progressive corneal disorders. The computational pipeline will be disseminated as an open-source tool for translational vision research, addressing a critical need for integrative models in physiological optics.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of vision, visual processes, and related phenomena and clinical research and treatment modalities. Includes instruction in ocular anatomy and physiology, microbiology of the eye, electrophysiology, neurophysiology, corneal physiology, photochemistry, psychophysics, visual biophysics and motor systems, sensory mechanisms and photoreception, eye circulation and metabolism, geometric and physical optics, ocular development across the life span, visual stimuli and perception, color vision, eye motility, biometrics and measurement techniques, visual pathology, and environmental issues.
