abstract: Vocational sales and marketing education faces a critical challenge in bridging theoretical knowledge with dynamic, real-world applications. Current pedagogical approaches often lack scalable methods to simulate complex market environments or analyze large-scale student performance data, limiting educators’ ability to personalize instruction and predict learner outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and deploy computational models that enhance the design and delivery of marketing and distribution teacher education programs. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating agent-based simulations of market ecosystems to model consumer behavior, supply chain dynamics, and competitive scenarios for use in classroom training, and (2) implementing machine learning algorithms to analyze longitudinal datasets tracking student engagement, skill acquisition, and career progression. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, the simulations will incorporate multi-agent interactions across diverse economic conditions, enabling pre-service teachers to experiment with pedagogical strategies in risk-free virtual environments. Concurrently, natural language processing techniques will be applied to qualitative feedback from teaching portfolios, while recurrent neural networks will identify patterns in quantitative performance metrics. These computational approaches will allow for the identification of optimal instructional interventions tailored to varying learner profiles. The anticipated outcomes include an open-source simulation platform adaptable to regional market contexts, predictive models for student success in certification programs, and evidence-based frameworks for competency assessment in distributive education. By integrating computational modeling with teacher training methodologies, this work aims to advance the preparation of marketing educators, ultimately strengthening the pipeline of skilled professionals in sales and distribution fields. The requested HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets and maintaining low-latency performance during concurrent simulation runs, capabilities unattainable with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_title: Sales and Marketing Operations/ Marketing and Distribution Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational sales and marketing operations/marketing and distributive education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neural and biomechanical underpinnings of apraxia of speech (AOS), a motor planning disorder characterized by impaired speech production. Current diagnostic frameworks for AOS rely heavily on subjective clinical assessments, leading to variability in diagnosis and treatment. To address this, we propose an interdisciplinary approach integrating neuroimaging, computational biomechanics, and machine learning to develop objective biomarkers for AOS. The research will utilize multimodal datasets, including high-resolution functional MRI (fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and 3D vocal tract kinematics captured during speech tasks. Computational challenges arise from the need to model dynamic interactions between cortical activation patterns, white matter connectivity, and articulatory muscle coordination—a process requiring real-time processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative simulations of neural-mechanical coupling. HPC resources will enable the deployment of graph neural networks (GNNs) to map disrupted network topology in speech-related brain regions and finite element models (FEMs) to simulate vocal tract dynamics under varying neuromotor constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model linking specific neural circuit abnormalities to articulatory kinematics, (2) automated classification algorithms to differentiate AOS from related disorders, and (3) open-source tools for optimizing speech motor rehabilitation protocols. By bridging gaps between computational neuroscience and speech motor control theory, this work aims to establish a novel framework for precision assessment of motor speech disorders, with potential applications in neurorehabilitation technology and adaptive therapeutic interfaces. The scale of data integration and the complexity of real-time biomechanical simulations necessitate the parallel processing and GPU-accelerated workflows uniquely afforded by HPC infrastructure.
cip_title: Communication Disorders Sciences and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communications disorders sciences and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic evolution in American literature from the Colonial Era to the 20th century. Traditional literary scholarship often relies on close reading of select texts, limiting the scope of analysis to curated corpora. This research addresses the challenge of systematically tracing patterns across vast, heterogeneous collections of U.S. literary works—including novels, essays, and oral tradition transcriptions—to identify understudied connections between regional dialects, genre conventions, and sociocultural shifts. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques, including transformer-based models for semantic role labeling, dynamic topic modeling, and stylometric clustering. These methods will process digitized texts from repositories such as the HathiTrust Digital Library and the American Antiquarian Society’s archives, requiring parallelized workflows to handle ~50TB of unstructured data. Key tasks include training custom word embeddings to capture historical linguistic nuances, deploying distributed algorithms for network analysis of intertextual influence, and applying neural architectures to map sentiment trajectories in response to events like the Civil War or industrialization. HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, reducing runtime for iterative model training, and enabling scalable storage solutions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts with metadata on stylistic features and thematic tags, as well as visualizations of literary trends across time and geography. The project aims to reveal how marginalized voices (e.g., Indigenous oral traditions, early African American narratives) influenced canonical literary movements—a question difficult to address at this scale without computational support. By bridging digital humanities and American literary studies, this work will provide a replicable framework for data-driven inquiry into cultural production, offering new empirical foundations for theoretical debates about nationalism, regionalism, and identity in U.S. literature.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the literature and literary development, both formal and folkloric, of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and regional and oral traditions.

abstract: The development of advanced structural materials with tailored mechanical properties requires a fundamental understanding of defect dynamics at atomic and microstructural scales. Current experimental techniques face limitations in resolving real-time evolution of dislocations, grain boundaries, and voids under complex thermo-mechanical loads, particularly in multi-phase systems. This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate defect-mediated deformation mechanisms in polycrystalline alloys, integrating atomistic and mesoscale models to bridge critical gaps in predicting failure initiation. Using large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we will quantify dislocation nucleation and interaction energies in heterogeneous microstructures with explicit grain boundaries, while phase-field models will capture longer-term coarsening and crack propagation behaviors. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated LAMMPS for MD and in-house phase-field solvers optimized for adaptive mesh refinement, enabling concurrent multi-scale simulations across 10^6–10^9 atom ensembles and millimeter-scale microstructures. Key challenges include managing memory constraints during cross-scale data transfer and achieving strong scaling for iterative solute diffusion calculations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework correlating local defect configurations with macroscopic yield strength and fatigue resistance in titanium-aluminide composites. The resource request targets 250,000 node-hours on a GPU-equipped cluster, with 2 TB of high-speed storage for trajectory analysis. Results will inform the design of next-generation high-temperature alloys for aerospace applications, directly addressing the materials science community’s need for predictive tools that bypass trial-and-error prototyping. By resolving the spatiotemporal limits of existing models, this work aims to establish computational protocols for defect engineering in additive manufacturing processes, with open-source release of optimized simulation workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of the characteristics and behavior of solids, including internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, compound materials, and research on industrial applications of specific materials.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision metal working by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize advanced manufacturing processes. Precision metal fabrication techniques, such as laser cutting, micro-machining, and additive manufacturing, require tight control over thermal, mechanical, and metallurgical variables to minimize defects and ensure dimensional accuracy. However, existing empirical methods struggle to predict complex phenomena like residual stress formation, microstructural evolution, and tool wear under dynamic conditions, leading to costly trial-and-error approaches. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a computational framework integrating multi-physics simulations, machine learning (ML), and large-scale data analytics. Finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate thermo-mechanical interactions during metal processing at micron-scale resolutions, while ML algorithms will identify optimal parameter sets (e.g., laser power, feed rates, cooling strategies) to mitigate defects. The HPC environment is essential for resolving spatially heterogeneous material behaviors and coupling multiphase phenomena—tasks infeasible with conventional computing due to their high memory and processing demands. Expected outcomes include predictive models for defect-free fabrication, validated against experimental data from partner manufacturing facilities, and an open-access dataset of simulated process-performance correlations. This work will advance the scalability of precision metalworking technologies for high-value aerospace and medical components, reduce material waste, and provide training resources to bridge HPC literacy gaps in technical education. By integrating computational rigor with industrial practice, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for smart manufacturing in technology-driven metalworking fields.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision metal work, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The variability in patient responses to pharmacotherapy poses a significant challenge in clinical, hospital, and managed care settings, where optimized drug regimens are critical to outcomes. Current approaches to dose individualization often rely on population averages or limited patient-specific data, leading to suboptimal efficacy or toxicity risks. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-resolution computational models of drug pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) tailored to diverse patient populations. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multi-scale data, including electronic health records, genomic biomarkers, and real-world drug monitoring results, into predictive frameworks. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to identify nonlinear relationships between patient covariates (e.g., renal/hepatic function, pharmacogenomic profiles) and drug behavior. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model drug-receptor interactions under physiological conditions, incorporating genetic variants affecting protein structure. These computational workflows will be validated against clinical trial data from oncology and psychiatric pharmacy cohorts, where narrow therapeutic indices demand precise dosing. The HPC environment is essential for managing the iterative parameter estimation required for population PK/PD modeling, parallel processing of genomic data, and large-scale sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models enabling dynamic dose adjustments for drugs with high interpatient variability, such as immunosuppressants and chemotherapeutics, and (2) a decision-support framework to guide therapeutic drug monitoring in real-time clinical workflows. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on advancing evidence-based, patient-specific care through computational innovation, with potential applications in antimicrobial stewardship, transplant pharmacy, and chronic disease management. By bridging mechanistic pharmacology with clinical informatics, the project aims to reduce adverse drug events and improve therapeutic outcomes in complex care environments.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Clinical, Hospital, and Managed Care Pharmacy
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to deliver specialized pharmacy services and produce pharmaceutical products in clinical settings in conjunction with other health care professionals. Includes instruction in biostatistics; clinical pharmacokinetics; biopharmaceutics; neuropharmacology; pharmacodynamics; drug metabolism; clinical sampling and research design; drug delivery systems; chemotherapy; pharmacotherapy; clinical pharmacy management; medical and research ethics; and applications to nuclear, nutrition support, oncology, psychiatric, and therapeutic pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the adaptive strategies of multidenominational religious institutions in navigating evolving legal and administrative landscapes, particularly in contexts where secular regulations intersect with doctrinal principles. The research problem centers on understanding how such institutions reconcile compliance with legal frameworks—such as data privacy laws, labor regulations, and nonprofit governance standards—while maintaining theological integrity and operational coherence. Existing scholarship often addresses doctrinal or historical dimensions of religious institutions but lacks systematic analysis of their administrative decision-making under legal constraints. To address this gap, the project employs a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling (ABM). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing large corpora of legal documents, institutional policies, and archival records, enabling semantic analysis of regulatory texts and comparative mapping of policy adaptations across denominations. ABM simulations will model decision-making dynamics within administrative bodies, incorporating variables such as doctrinal rigidity, stakeholder influence, and legal risk tolerance. The integration of these methods aims to identify patterns in institutional adaptability and predict responses to emerging regulatory challenges. Expected outcomes include a framework for assessing policy alignment between religious and legal norms, predictive tools for institutional compliance planning, and a publicly accessible dataset of annotated legal-religious policy interactions. This research holds significance for both academic and practical domains, offering interdisciplinary insights into governance at the intersection of law and religion while providing actionable guidance for religious institutions operating in pluralistic legal environments.
cip_title: Religious Institution Administration and Law, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in religious institution administration and law, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Respiratory care management for patients with acute or chronic pulmonary conditions relies heavily on optimizing ventilator settings and therapeutic interventions. However, current clinical protocols often depend on generalized guidelines that may not account for individual patient variability in lung mechanics, disease progression, or response to treatment. This project seeks to address this gap by developing patient-specific computational models to simulate respiratory mechanics and predict optimal ventilator parameters. The research problem centers on the lack of personalized, data-driven tools to guide respiratory therapists in dynamically adjusting care plans, particularly in critical care settings where rapid decision-making is essential. By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to create multi-scale models integrating clinical data—such as airflow resistance, lung compliance, and gas exchange metrics—with biomechanical simulations of pulmonary function. These models will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to analyze airway pressure gradients and machine learning algorithms to correlate real-time patient monitoring data with historical outcomes. The computational workflow will require parallel processing to handle large datasets from electronic health records and high-resolution imaging, as well as iterative simulations to test hypothetical interventions. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for identifying patient-specific ventilation strategies that minimize barotrauma and hypoxia risks while improving weaning success rates. This project will also generate open-source tools for respiratory therapy education, enabling technicians to explore simulated clinical scenarios. The results have the potential to enhance evidence-based practice, reduce trial-and-error in ventilator management, and improve care quality for patients with respiratory failure. Successful implementation of this research hinges on access to HPC resources capable of managing complex simulations and large-scale data integration within clinically relevant timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer general respiratory care procedures under the supervision of respiratory therapists in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in patient data collection and monitoring, airway management, installation of nebulizers and other respiratory assistance devices, application and monitoring of breathing gases, equipment operation and maintenance, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize private security operations through advanced computational modeling, addressing gaps in proactive threat mitigation for Security and Loss Prevention Services. Current security strategies often rely on reactive measures, historical incident data, and static patrol patterns, which struggle to adapt to dynamic, real-world environments. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous data streams—including geospatial crime trends, IoT sensor inputs from secured sites, and behavioral anomaly detection from surveillance systems—into a unified model capable of forecasting high-risk scenarios and recommending adaptive resource allocation. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal relationships between threat factors, reinforcement learning to simulate patrol route optimization under uncertainty, and agent-based modeling to stress-test security protocols against synthetic threat scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets spanning urban crime records, client-site sensor logs, and simulated adversarial behavior, while enabling real-time parameter tuning for evolving threat landscapes. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating risk heatmaps, dynamic scheduling algorithms for security personnel, and probabilistic forecasts of asset vulnerability under varying conditions. The project bridges computational criminology, operations research, and IoT analytics, offering private security providers a scalable method to transition from generalized patrols to intelligence-driven deployment. By leveraging HPC to handle the combinatorial complexity of threat variables, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in loss prevention, reducing response latency by 30-50% in simulated environments while maintaining compliance with privacy-preserving data governance standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine inspection, patrol and crime prevention services for private clients. Includes instruction in the provision of personal protection as well as property security.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between neural plasticity and cognitive flexibility using computational models that integrate neuroimaging data, behavioral experiments, and artificial neural networks. While cognitive flexibility—the ability to adapt thinking and behavior to novel stimuli—is critical to human intelligence, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Traditional approaches in neuroscience or psychology alone struggle to disentangle the multiscale interactions between synaptic-level changes, network-level dynamics, and behavioral outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a hybrid computational framework that couples spiking neural network models with reinforcement learning algorithms, calibrated against functional MRI (fMRI) and electroencephalography (EEG) data from human subjects performing cognitive flexibility tasks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large-scale networks with biophysically realistic neuron models, optimize parameters via evolutionary algorithms, and perform Bayesian inference on hierarchical models linking neural activity to behavioral metrics. The proposed work will generate novel predictions about how neurotransmitter systems (e.g., dopamine, acetylcholine) modulate plasticity-flexibility trade-offs across developmental stages. Expected outcomes include a publicly shared toolbox for simulating cognitive flexibility impairments in neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., autism spectrum disorder) and actionable insights for designing adaptive AI systems that mimic human-like learning transitions. By bridging computational neuroscience, machine learning, and cognitive psychology, this research advances a unified theory of adaptive intelligence while providing scalable methods for cross-domain data integration—a critical need in multidisciplinary cognitive science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the mind and the nature of intelligence from the interdisciplinary perspectives of computer science, philosophy, mathematics, psychology, neuroscience, and other disciplines. Includes instruction in mathematics and logic, cognitive process modeling, dynamic systems, learning theories, brain and cognition, neural networking, programming, and applications to topics such as language acquisition, computer systems, and perception and behavior.

abstract: Emergency medicine research faces critical challenges in integrating heterogeneous clinical data to improve time-sensitive decision-making. This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework for acute care outcomes by leveraging high-dimensional electronic health records (EHRs), real-time physiological waveforms, and multimodal imaging data from trauma and sepsis patients. Current models lack the computational capacity to process temporal-spatial relationships in waveform data while simultaneously analyzing structured EHR variables, limiting their clinical utility in emergency departments (EDs). We propose a hybrid machine learning architecture combining transformer-based temporal modeling for physiological signals (e.g., ECG, arterial line waveforms) with graph neural networks to represent complex interactions between clinical variables. The computational workflow requires distributed training of deep learning models across multi-GPU nodes, integration of 10+ terabytes of anonymized patient data from six regional EDs, and real-time simulation of clinical decision pathways through Monte Carlo methods. High-performance computing resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) parallel processing of raw waveform data at scale using GPU-accelerated signal decomposition, (2) federated learning across institutional datasets while maintaining privacy constraints, and (3) validation through agent-based modeling of ED workflows under different prediction scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated risk stratification system for septic shock progression within 24 hours of ED admission and a resource allocation model optimizing critical care transitions. This work will establish computational infrastructure for future emergency medicine studies requiring rapid analysis of complex clinical data streams, with immediate applications for improving mortality prediction in undifferentiated critically ill patients. The developed models and pipelines will be disseminated through an open-source platform adaptable to diverse emergency care settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular and biomechanical mechanisms underlying impaired osseointegration of dental implants in patients with metabolic bone disorders, a critical yet understudied intersection of oral biology, bioengineering, and computational systems biology. While implant failure rates remain elevated in populations with osteoporosis, diabetes, or rare skeletal dysplasias, current diagnostic tools lack predictive power at the microstructural and cellular levels. We propose to develop multiscale computational models integrating patient-specific bone microarchitecture data (μCT scans), single-cell RNA sequencing of peri-implant osteoprogenitor cells, and dynamic finite element analysis to simulate mechanobiological responses during early implant healing. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-terabyte histomorphometric datasets, machine learning-driven pattern recognition in bone remodeling trajectories, and agent-based modeling of osteoclast-osteoblast coupling under pathological metabolic conditions. The computational framework will be validated against longitudinal clinical cohorts with matched imaging and biopsy data. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for implant success probability based on subclinical bone quality parameters, identification of mechanosensitive gene networks amenable to therapeutic targeting, and optimized implant surface designs informed by simulated load distribution patterns in compromised bone. This interdisciplinary approach bridges gaps between clinical oral pathology and computational mechanobiology, offering novel strategies to personalize implant dentistry while advancing fundamental understanding of craniofacial bone adaptation in systemic disease states.
cip_title: Oral Biology and Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the growth, development, diseases, healing properties, and neurological components of the oral cavity, related tissues and organs, and associated craniofacial areas. Includes instruction in oral microbiology microanatomy, craniofacial pain, humoral aspects of disease, etiology and histology of caries, plaque ecology, wound healing, oral disease epidemiology, oral manifestations of systemic disease, lesions, normal and pathologic physiology, and related molecular and physical studies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex, interconnected challenges in urban sustainability and community resilience through a multidisciplinary lens. Urban systems are inherently dynamic, involving feedback loops between socioeconomic factors, environmental stressors, and infrastructure demands. Traditional analytical tools often fail to capture these nonlinear interactions at scale, particularly when integrating heterogeneous datasets spanning demographics, climate projections, and real-time sensor networks. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to model urban systems as adaptive networks, enabling policymakers to test intervention strategies under diverse scenarios. The proposed approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-driven optimization to simulate decision-making processes across individual, institutional, and infrastructural actors. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations that account for variable climate patterns, population growth trajectories, and resource allocation policies. Key computational challenges include managing sparse matrix operations for large-scale network analysis and training graph neural networks on temporally evolving urban datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of identifying leverage points for sustainable urban transitions, with specific applications to energy equity and flood resilience planning. The project’s significance lies in its integration of computational social science, environmental informatics, and complex systems theory—a convergence unique to interdisciplinary general studies. By creating transferable methodologies for coupling qualitative social dynamics with quantitative environmental data, this work will provide actionable insights for cities facing compound crises. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at unprecedented resolution, directly supporting graduate student training in transdisciplinary computational research while fostering collaborations between urban planners, data scientists, and community stakeholders. Results will be disseminated through interactive data visualizations and policy briefs alongside traditional academic publications.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing radar system performance in contested electromagnetic environments, where adversarial signal degradation, spectrum congestion, and emerging electronic warfare tactics threaten operational effectiveness. Current radar resource management strategies struggle to adapt to dynamic, multi-threat scenarios due to computational limitations in real-time signal processing and decision-making algorithms. Our research proposes the development of a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex radar-environment interactions across tactical networks. The computational approach integrates physics-based radar propagation models with machine learning techniques to predict and mitigate interference patterns, while testing adaptive waveform allocation strategies under varying threat conditions. By simulating large-scale scenarios involving coordinated radar networks, mobile platforms, and adversarial countermeasures, the project aims to identify optimal resource allocation protocols that balance detection accuracy, spectral efficiency, and anti-jamming resilience. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic spectrum sharing, improved signal classification architectures resistant to deception techniques, and quantifiable performance benchmarks for next-generation radar systems operating in multi-domain battle spaces. This work bridges the gap between traditional radar engineering and modern computational warfare requirements, offering actionable insights for maintaining electromagnetic superiority without requiring hardware modifications. The requested computing resources will enable parametric studies across 10^6+ scenario variations, dramatically accelerating the development cycle for tactical radar enhancements while maintaining operational security constraints inherent to military research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: The structural integrity and operational safety of steam boilers are critical concerns in industrial and energy systems, where failures due to thermal fatigue, pressure fluctuations, and material degradation can lead to catastrophic consequences. Current industry standards for boiler design and maintenance rely heavily on empirical data and simplified analytical models, which often fail to capture the complex, multiphysics interactions occurring in real-world operating conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate the thermo-mechanical behavior of boiler components under dynamic loads. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to conduct large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to map stress distributions, thermal gradients, and material responses across welded joints, riveted seams, and critical interfaces. These simulations will integrate multi-physics couplings, including heat transfer, fluid-structure interaction, and cyclic plasticity, to predict failure mechanisms such as crack initiation and creep deformation. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be employed to optimize material selection and welding parameters by correlating simulation outputs with experimental data from tensile testing and non-destructive evaluation. The computational demands of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of high-resolution meshes and iterative optimization workflows—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Outcomes from this research will provide actionable insights for revising boiler design codes, improving maintenance protocols, and extending component lifespans. By bridging advanced computational modeling with boilermaking practices, this project aims to enhance the safety and efficiency of steam-powered systems while fostering new interdisciplinary training opportunities for students in computational materials science and applied engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and repair steam boiler components. Includes instruction in principles of steam power, material selection, welding, riveting, sealing materials, pressure testing, pipefitting, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize mineral extraction processes in underground mining environments, with a focus on improving efficiency while minimizing environmental disruption. A critical challenge in modern mining is balancing economic viability with ecological sustainability, particularly in complex geological settings where traditional methods struggle to predict dynamic rock behavior, ore distribution, and groundwater interactions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-physics simulations integrating geomechanical modeling, computational fluid dynamics, and machine learning-driven ore grade prediction. The computational approach will utilize finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress redistribution during excavation, coupled with discrete fracture network models to map fluid flow through fractured rock systems. Concurrently, convolutional neural networks will process historical drilling data and real-time sensor inputs to refine resource estimation accuracy. These interdependent models require parallelized computing architectures to handle the terabyte-scale datasets typical of mine-scale simulations, including 3D lithological maps and continuous monitoring data streams. The HPC infrastructure will enable parameter sweeps across safety thresholds, extraction sequences, and equipment configurations that are computationally prohibitive on local clusters. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying optimal cut-and-fill sequences, real-time risk assessment modules for mine collapse prevention, and dynamic resource allocation strategies that reduce waste by 15–20% compared to conventional methods. By creating a digital twin capability for mining operations, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainable resource extraction, directly supporting the program’s mission to advance technical solutions in mineral development. The resulting open-source framework will be validated against case studies from copper and rare earth element mines, with implications for reducing energy consumption and water usage across the mining sector.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing clinical workflows and patient outcomes through advanced computational modeling of multi-modal health data. Despite the growing availability of electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, and genomic datasets, healthcare systems struggle to integrate these heterogeneous data sources for real-time decision support. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to improve resource allocation in clinical settings, reduce diagnostic delays, and personalize care pathways for patients with complex chronic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, machine learning techniques—including graph neural networks and transformer architectures—will be applied to de-identified EHR data from [Institution/Partner Network] to identify patterns in care delivery bottlenecks and comorbidities. Second, discrete-event simulation models will be developed to test interventions for clinic scheduling, staff deployment, and equipment utilization under varying patient volumes. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including time-series vital sign data, radiology reports, and administrative operation logs. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for simulating clinic operations under different resource constraints, predictive models for early identification of high-risk patients, and evidence-based recommendations for balancing clinical efficiency with care quality. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on medical management and clinical specialization by creating scalable tools to enhance both administrative decision-making and patient-facing care coordination. The requested HPC resources will enable rapid iteration of complex models that cannot run efficiently on local clinical systems, particularly for Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of operational scenarios. Results will be disseminated through healthcare informatics conferences and adapted into training modules for clinical assistant education programs.
cip_title: Medical/ Health Management and Clinical Assistant/ Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, nurses, or other health care professionals, to perform medical office or facilities management services and perform one or more clinical allied health specialties. Includes instruction in health care management; medical office administration; medical law and regulations; training in one or more diagnostic, treatment, therapy, or laboratory specialties at the assistant level or above; and applicable professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing mineral extraction and processing systems through advanced computational modeling, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations of traditional empirical methods. The research focuses on developing multiscale, multiphysics simulations to model complex interactions in ore fragmentation, mineral liberation, and slurry transport—processes central to efficient resource recovery. Current methods struggle to integrate micro-scale mineralogical heterogeneity with macro-scale operational parameters, leading to inefficiencies in energy use, material recovery, and waste management. By implementing coupled discrete element method (DEM) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) frameworks, we aim to resolve particle-scale breakage dynamics and fluid-particle interactions in processing equipment such as crushers, mills, and flotation cells. These simulations will be validated against experimental data from sensor-equipped pilot-scale systems. Additionally, machine learning models will be trained on HPC-processed geospatial and operational datasets to predict ore variability and optimize real-time decision-making in mine planning. The computational demands of these tasks—including high-resolution 3D meshing, parallelized solver algorithms, and large-scale parameter space exploration—necessitate access to HPC resources for feasible execution. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing energy consumption in comminution, improving mineral recovery rates by 10–15%, and reducing tailings waste through optimized separation thresholds. The project will provide open-source simulation modules to advance collaborative research in sustainable mining practices, directly supporting industry priorities in decarbonization and circular resource economies. By bridging computational innovation with mineral engineering fundamentals, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven, environmentally conscious mineral resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resilient supply chain networks in high-uncertainty environments, integrating stochastic operational dynamics with multi-objective decision-making under disruptive scenarios. Traditional supply chain models often fail to account for real-time disruptions such as geopolitical shifts, resource shortages, or sudden demand fluctuations, leading to systemic vulnerabilities. The research addresses this gap by combining large-scale discrete-event simulation, machine learning (ML)-driven risk prediction, and distributed optimization algorithms to model adaptive reconfiguration of production-distribution systems. The computational approach leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to manage the combinatorial complexity of multi-echelon networks, where millions of potential scenarios—spanning supplier failures, transportation delays, and demand spikes—are evaluated concurrently. Custom ML models will predict disruption probabilities from heterogeneous data streams (e.g., logistics APIs, economic indices), while mixed-integer programming and graph-based resilience metrics will guide re-routing and inventory buffering strategies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for parallelizing scenario analyses, training deep reinforcement learning agents for dynamic resource allocation, and solving high-dimensional optimization problems with latency constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-aware supply chain resilience, validated against real-world data from automotive and pharmaceutical manufacturing partners. This work will advance industrial management practices by enabling computationally tractable, real-time decision support systems that balance cost, sustainability, and robustness in volatile markets. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed memory processing for large-scale optimizations, and high-throughput data pipelines to handle global supply chain datasets. Success in this project will provide a template for integrating HPC-driven analytics into operational risk management frameworks, fostering more agile and fault-tolerant industrial ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of nonequilibrium quantum many-body dynamics in strongly correlated systems, a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics. While experimental advances have enabled precise manipulation of quantum systems, theoretical progress remains limited by the exponential scaling of computational complexity with system size. Traditional methods, such as exact diagonalization or mean-field approximations, fail to capture emergent phenomena in large-scale systems under time-dependent perturbations. To address this gap, we propose leveraging tensor network algorithms, specifically matrix product states (MPS) and time-dependent variational principles (TDVP), to simulate the real-time evolution of one-dimensional quantum spin chains and fermionic lattices. The research will employ hybrid CPU-GPU architectures on high-performance computing clusters to optimize the contraction and renormalization steps critical for maintaining numerical precision in large bond-dimension simulations. Key objectives include characterizing thermalization dynamics in disordered Heisenberg models, identifying prethermalization plateaus in Floquet-driven systems, and quantifying entanglement growth near critical points. The computational framework will incorporate adaptive time-stepping and distributed memory parallelism to scale simulations to system sizes of ~100 lattice sites, exceeding the capabilities of existing single-node implementations. Expected outcomes include predictive insights into the stability of quantum memory in near-term quantum devices and universal scaling laws for information scrambling in nonintegrable systems. Results will be validated against ultrafast quantum simulator data from collaborating experimental groups. By providing open-source implementations of optimized tensor network libraries, this work will enhance the broader community’s capacity to model quantum matter under extreme nonequilibrium conditions, with implications for quantum computing, sensing, and the fundamental limits of statistical mechanics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the major topics, concepts, processes, and interrelationships of physical phenomena as studied in any combination of physical science disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian hierarchical models for high-dimensional spatiotemporal data, addressing computational bottlenecks in uncertainty quantification for complex statistical inference. Modern applications in epidemiology, environmental monitoring, and public policy increasingly demand models that integrate large, heterogeneous datasets with spatially and temporally varying parameters. However, conventional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied to such high-dimensional settings, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with distributed variational inference, optimized for parallelization on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. The approach leverages GPU-accelerated tensor operations for gradient calculations and implements domain decomposition strategies to partition spatial grids across nodes, reducing memory constraints. A key innovation involves adaptive tuning of proposal distributions using stochastic optimization, which minimizes convergence time in hierarchical models with thousands of latent variables. The computational workflow will be validated on synthetic data with known ground truth and applied to a case study analyzing climate-driven disease spread across urban networks, integrating satellite-derived environmental variables and anonymized health records. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for efficient Bayesian inference on spatiotemporal problems, (2) benchmarks comparing computational scalability across HPC architectures, and (3) novel statistical insights into uncertainty propagation in multi-scale epidemiological models. By enabling faster convergence and lower memory overhead than existing MCMC toolkits, this work will advance the practical feasibility of fully Bayesian approaches for large-scale public health interventions. The requested computing resources are critical for testing distributed memory configurations and optimizing load balancing across up to 256 nodes, given the project’s emphasis on weak scaling to terabyte-scale datasets.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to analyze the impacts of climate variability and policy interventions on agricultural resource allocation and productivity across heterogeneous regions. A critical challenge in agricultural economics is modeling spatially explicit decision-making under uncertainty, particularly as climate change exacerbates risks for producers and complicates policy design. Current approaches often rely on aggregated data or simplified assumptions, limiting their capacity to capture localized interactions between environmental conditions, market dynamics, and farmer behavior. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale agent-based model (ABM) integrated with econometric estimation techniques, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate decision processes across millions of individual agents and diverse geographies. The ABM will incorporate historical climate data, crop yield projections, and real-world policy scenarios (e.g., subsidy structures, carbon pricing) to evaluate how resource allocation efficiency and regional resilience evolve under stochastic shocks. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations and machine learning-based parameter optimization to account for uncertainty in climate forecasts and market responses. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for training neural networks on high-dimensional agricultural survey datasets and CPU clusters for large-scale equilibrium simulations. Expected outcomes include policy-relevant insights into the cost-effectiveness of adaptive interventions, such as crop insurance schemes or precision agriculture incentives, across differing agroecological zones. By enabling granular analysis of nonlinear system behaviors, this work aims to advance methodological tools for agricultural economics while directly informing strategies to enhance sustainability and equity in resource use. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of iteratively solving dynamic stochastic models at fine spatial resolutions, a task infeasible with standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics to the analysis of resource allocation, productivity, investment, and trends in the agricultural sector, both domestically and internationally. Includes instruction in economics and related subfields as well as applicable agricultural fields.

abstract: The sustainable scaling of microbial bioenergy systems is hindered by inefficiencies in bioprocessing and gaps in understanding how microbial consortia interact dynamically under industrial conditions. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multi-scale complexity of these systems, which span genetic regulation, metabolic fluxes, and large-scale bioreactor hydrodynamics. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an integrated computational framework that bridges genome-scale metabolic modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and life cycle assessment (LCA) for the optimization of lignocellulosic biofuel production. Using genome-resolved metagenomic data from pilot-scale anaerobic digesters, we will parameterize agent-based models to simulate microbial community responses to fluctuating feedstock compositions and reactor conditions. These models will be coupled with CFD simulations of industrial-scale bioreactors to predict how hydrodynamic stressors and nutrient gradients influence microbial metabolism and overall conversion efficiency. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal operational parameters and microbial consortia configurations to maximize ethanol yield while minimizing energy inputs. The computational pipeline will further integrate techno-economic and environmental impact assessments to evaluate scalability and sustainability trade-offs. By simulating thousands of design permutations across spatial and temporal scales, this HPC-driven approach will bypass costly iterative experimentation, accelerating the translation of lab-scale findings to commercial applications. Expected outcomes include predictive models of microbial resilience in heterogeneous bioreactor environments, validated strategies for feedstock flexibility, and a publicly accessible database linking microbial traits to process performance metrics. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation biorefineries, advancing the economic viability and ecological sustainability of bioenergy systems within resource-constrained agricultural landscapes.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of health data, including electronic health records (EHRs), wearable device outputs, and genomic datasets, present significant challenges for efficient management, analysis, and secure utilization in clinical and administrative settings. Existing computational tools often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data types at scale, perform real-time analytics, or ensure compliance with evolving privacy regulations. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a scalable framework for multi-modal health data integration, predictive modeling, and privacy-preserving data sharing. The research will focus on three computational objectives: (1) designing parallelized pipelines for harmonizing structured and unstructured health data across distributed sources, (2) training deep learning models to predict patient outcomes and administrative bottlenecks using longitudinal EHR data, and (3) implementing GPU-accelerated simulations of cryptographic protocols for secure cross-institutional data exchange. The HPC environment will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from partner healthcare networks, including 10+ years of de-identified patient records and real-time streaming data from IoT medical devices. Computational experiments will compare distributed computing architectures (e.g., Spark vs. Dask) for optimal resource utilization in clinical workflows and evaluate transformer-based neural networks against traditional machine learning approaches for predictive accuracy. Privacy-preserving techniques, including homomorphic encryption and federated learning frameworks, will be benchmarked for computational overhead and compliance with HIPAA and GDPR standards. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for health information administrators to manage large-scale data assets, validated predictive models for clinical deterioration and resource allocation, and quantitative guidelines for balancing computational costs with data utility in privacy-sensitive scenarios. This work will directly enhance the operational efficiency of healthcare organizations while advancing methodological innovations at the intersection of health informatics and high-performance computing.
cip_title: Health Information/ Medical Records Administration/ Administrator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage systems, processes, and facilities used to collect, store, secure, retrieve, analyze, and transmit medical records and other health information used by clinical professionals and health care organizations. Includes instruction in the principles and basic content of the biomedical and clinical sciences, information technology and applications, data and database management, clinical research methodologies, health information resources and systems, office management, legal requirements, and professional standards.

abstract: Emerging infectious diseases in agricultural livestock pose significant threats to food security, animal welfare, and public health. Current disease transmission models often lack the resolution to integrate multi-scale data—such as host-pathogen interactions, genomic variability in disease resistance, and dynamic environmental factors—limiting their predictive accuracy. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-agent computational framework to simulate disease spread within heterogeneous animal populations and evaluate targeted intervention strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement spatially explicit agent-based models that incorporate individual animal movement, contact networks, and environmental pathogen persistence. These models will integrate genomic datasets to explore correlations between genetic markers and disease susceptibility in cattle populations, alongside machine learning algorithms trained on historical outbreak data to identify high-risk transmission scenarios. By simulating millions of agent interactions across diverse herd configurations and environmental conditions, the project aims to optimize vaccination protocols, biosecurity measures, and culling strategies while minimizing economic losses. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for predicting outbreak trajectories under climate variability, genetic profiles associated with resilience to common pathogens, and data-driven guidelines for regional disease management. The results will directly inform livestock health policies, enhance the precision of veterinary interventions, and reduce reliance on broad-spectrum antimicrobials, advancing sustainable agricultural practices. This work requires HPC capabilities due to the parallel processing demands of large-scale simulations, the need for rapid parameter optimization across complex biological datasets, and the analysis of high-dimensional genomic-environmental interactions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological and chemical principles to the study, prevention, and control of diseases in agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in environmental science, pharmacology, animal population studies, genetics, animal physiology and diet, disease prevention, treatment methodologies, and laboratory and testing procedures.

abstract: Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain significant global health challenges, particularly among preterm infants and those with complex perinatal conditions. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying neonatal sepsis and respiratory failure, two leading causes of adverse outcomes in this population. Current limitations in integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with high-resolution clinical datasets hinder the development of predictive models for early diagnosis and personalized interventions. We propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze longitudinal multi-omics profiles from 500 neonates in combination with real-time physiological monitoring data (heart rate variability, oxygen saturation patterns) and maternal-fetal health records. Machine learning approaches, including recurrent neural networks and graph-based models, will be employed to identify dynamic biomarker signatures predictive of sepsis onset and respiratory deterioration. Parallelized computational fluid dynamics simulations will model pulmonary mechanics in preterm infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia, incorporating patient-specific CT-derived airway geometries and ventilator parameters. The scale of data integration (≥10 TB heterogeneous datasets) and complexity of multi-scale modeling necessitate HPC resources for distributed memory processing, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of novel predictive biomarkers for neonatal sepsis 24-48 hours prior to clinical manifestation, (2) development of individualized ventilation strategy simulations to reduce ventilator-induced lung injury, and (3) creation of open-source computational tools for real-time analysis of neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) datasets. This research directly addresses the program's focus on pathophysiology and clinical management of sick newborns, with potential to transform risk stratification protocols and inform NICUs’ integration of precision medicine approaches. The requested computing resources will enable processing timelines impossible with institutional cluster capacities, particularly for time-sensitive analyses correlating acute clinical events with multi-omics cascades.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time data integration and processing for small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) leveraging office automation systems. While modern businesses increasingly rely on tools for data entry, spreadsheet management, and reporting, fragmented workflows often lead to latency, errors, and scalability challenges—particularly when merging unstructured data (e.g., emails, documents) with structured transactional datasets. Traditional automation software struggles to dynamically prioritize tasks or adapt to fluctuating workloads, creating bottlenecks in high-volume environments. This project proposes the development of an adaptive computational framework that combines graph-based workflow modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize end-to-end data processing pipelines. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training RL agents on simulated office automation scenarios, which involve multi-agent coordination across heterogeneous tasks (e.g., invoice parsing, inventory updates, report generation). The framework will employ distributed computing to parallelize data ingestion and preprocessing, while graph neural networks will model interdependencies between tasks to minimize idle time and resource contention. A key innovation lies in dynamically adjusting computational priorities based on real-time business metrics (e.g., order fulfillment deadlines, cash flow projections). The research will validate the system using synthetic datasets mirroring SME operational scales (10^4–10^6 daily transactions) and benchmark against existing tools like robotic process automation (RPA) platforms. Expected outcomes include a 30–50% reduction in processing latency for complex workflows, improved error detection in cross-system data transfers, and quantifiable metrics for resource allocation in hybrid human-AI office environments. Results will provide a foundation for scalable, self-optimizing office automation architectures, directly enhancing SMEs’ capacity to leverage data-driven decision-making without costly infrastructure overhauls.
cip_title: Business/ Office Automation/ Technology/ Data Entry
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to support business information operations by using computer equipment to enter, process, and retrieve data for a wide variety of administrative purposes. Includes instruction in using basic business software and hardware, business computer networking, principles of desktop publishing, preparing mass mailings, compiling and editing spreadsheets, list maintenance, preparing tables and graphs, receipt control, and preparing business performance reports.

abstract: Chronic pain remains a poorly understood condition with heterogeneous treatment responses, often necessitating trial-and-error approaches that prolong patient suffering. This project seeks to address this challenge by integrating multimodal neurobiological data to develop predictive computational models of pain perception and treatment efficacy. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will analyze large-scale datasets spanning functional neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG), transcriptomic profiles of peripheral nociceptors, and longitudinal electronic health records from diverse chronic pain cohorts. Machine learning pipelines will be optimized to identify neural circuit signatures and genetic markers associated with pain phenotypes, while mechanistic simulations of neurotransmitter dynamics will model interactions between pharmacological agents and patient-specific neurophysiology. A key innovation involves federated learning frameworks to securely aggregate data across institutions, addressing sample size limitations while preserving privacy. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning for image analysis, parallelized genomic association studies, and agent-based modeling of neural network plasticity. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated classifier for predicting opioid vs. non-opioid therapy success based on baseline biomarkers, (2) dynamic maps of pain-related brain connectivity alterations under different interventions, and (3) open-source tools for simulating patient-specific drug effects on pain pathways. By bridging clinical pain neuroscience with advanced computational methods, this work aims to establish a foundation for precision pain medicine, reducing reliance on empirical treatment strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing petascale neuroimaging datasets, running comparative analyses across 10,000+ genomic loci, and maintaining iterative model training pipelines requiring months of compute time on conventional systems.
cip_definition: A post-residency program of study that prepares physicians in the diagnosis, management, and treatment of acute and chronic pain. Includes instruction in anesthesiology, pain assessment, pain classification and diagnosis, pain neuroscience, palliative and end-of-life care, physical medicine and rehabilitation, psychiatry of pain, pain pharmacology, public policy, and legal issues of pain management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding and optimization of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) protocols and decompression illness management through high-performance computing (HPC)-driven modeling of physiological and biochemical processes. Current treatment guidelines for conditions such as decompression sickness, carbon monoxide poisoning, and radiation-induced tissue damage rely on generalized empirical models, which often fail to account for patient-specific variables, including comorbidities, metabolic heterogeneity, and dynamic gas exchange kinetics. These limitations can lead to suboptimal clinical outcomes, prolonged recovery, or complications. To address this, we propose to develop high-fidelity computational models integrating multi-physics simulations of gas diffusion, tissue oxygenation, and vascular dynamics under hyperbaric conditions. These models will leverage patient-derived data, including real-time biomarker profiles, imaging-based tissue perfusion maps, and hyperbaric chamber operational parameters. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of finite element analyses for simulating gas bubble formation/resolution in decompression sickness, as well as machine learning-driven optimization of HBOT dosing regimens across diverse pathologies. Additionally, we will employ agent-based modeling to assess risk stratification for divers and occupational workers in altered atmospheric environments, incorporating factors such as microbubble nucleation thresholds and oxidative stress responses. The computational framework will be validated against clinical datasets from hyperbaric treatment centers and diving incident registries. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for personalized HBOT scheduling, real-time decompression risk monitoring algorithms, and evidence-based revisions to chamber operation guidelines. This work directly supports the program’s mission to enhance therapeutic efficacy, reduce disability in high-risk populations, and establish precision medicine approaches in undersea and hyperbaric clinical practice. The scale of required simulations—spanning molecular-scale gas-tissue interactions to system-level hemodynamics—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive multiscale modeling workflows.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat decompression illness and diving accident cases; to use hyperbaric oxygen therapy treatment for conditions such as carbon monoxide poisoning, gas gangrene, non-healing wounds, tissue damage from radiation and burns, and bone infections; to serve as consultant in all aspects of hyperbaric chamber operations; and to assess risks and apply appropriate standards to prevent disease and disability in divers and other persons working in altered atmospheric conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize workflow efficiency and client communication in veterinary reception environments through the analysis of large-scale operational data. Veterinary receptionists manage complex, dynamic workflows involving patient intake, client interactions, and administrative coordination, yet existing tools for workflow analysis in this niche field remain underdeveloped. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in appointment scheduling bottlenecks, client wait-time dissatisfaction, and miscommunication risks arising from inconsistent terminology use in client-facing interactions. Using anonymized datasets from 15 veterinary clinics—including timestamps, service codes, free-text client communications, and staff activity logs—we will employ natural language processing (NLP) to analyze communication efficacy and graph-based network modeling to simulate workflow scenarios. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing multi-terabyte datasets and running iterative agent-based simulations that test the impact of proposed interventions, such as dynamic scheduling algorithms or standardized communication templates. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for identifying high-risk workflow configurations, (2) a veterinary-specific NLP toolkit to assess clarity in client-staff exchanges, and (3) open-source simulation software tailored to small-animal practice logistics. By integrating computational social science methods with veterinary administrative practices, this work aims to establish evidence-based protocols that reduce operational inefficiencies while maintaining compliance with animal care regulations. The project bridges a gap in applied computational research for non-clinical veterinary support systems, offering scalable tools adaptable to diverse practice environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, veterinary technicians, or veterinarians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in veterinary office and animal care facility procedures, veterinary terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in communication arts and literature pedagogy through large-scale analysis of student writing and discourse patterns. A critical challenge in teacher education is understanding how diverse instructional techniques—such as peer feedback, multimodal composition, or culturally responsive writing interventions—impact language development across varied student populations. Traditional qualitative methods, while valuable, struggle to systematically analyze the linguistic complexity, semantic coherence, and rhetorical strategies present in thousands of student texts or classroom dialogue transcripts. This project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and graph-based discourse analysis, to evaluate longitudinal datasets comprising student essays, discussion forums, and multimedia projects from partner K-12 districts. Computational workflows will be designed to identify patterns in syntactic maturity, genre adaptation, and argumentation quality, while clustering algorithms will map how instructional scaffolds correlate with measurable improvements in writing and critical communication skills. HPC resources are essential for training custom NLP models on domain-specific educational corpora, processing terabytes of unstructured text and speech data, and simulating adaptive feedback mechanisms via reinforcement learning. Anticipated outcomes include (1) evidence-based frameworks for tailoring writing instruction to learners’ linguistic and cultural backgrounds, (2) automated tools to help pre-service teachers diagnose rhetorical strengths/gaps in student work, and (3) multimodal datasets annotated with pedagogical strategies for integration into teacher training curricula. By bridging computational linguistics and classroom practice, this work aims to equip future educators with data-driven insights to foster equitable, effective communication arts instruction.
cip_title: Communication Arts and Literature Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to teach oral expression, literature, and writing to students at various education levels. Includes instruction in interpersonal communication, intercultural communication, language learning, listening instructional techniques, public speaking, reading instructional techniques, writing instructional techniques, and practical teaching experience.

abstract: Operational oceanography in military contexts requires the integration of high-resolution environmental data with dynamic modeling to support tactical decision-making in complex, contested maritime environments. Existing oceanographic models often lack the granularity and computational efficiency needed to predict localized phenomena—such as nearshore turbulence, acoustic propagation anomalies, or rapid thermocline shifts—that directly impact mission success. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a multi-scale, adaptive modeling framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The research will focus on three interconnected challenges: (1) real-time assimilation of heterogeneous data streams (satellite, autonomous sensors, and legacy hydrographic datasets) into predictive models, (2) coupling hydrodynamic and acoustic propagation models at tactically relevant spatiotemporal scales (meters to kilometers, minutes to hours), and (3) quantifying uncertainty in rapidly evolving littoral zones. Computational methods will leverage parallelized finite-element solvers for non-linear wave equations, machine learning techniques for parameterizing subgrid-scale processes, and ensemble-based data assimilation to improve forecast reliability. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce latency in operational predictions by 40–60% compared to current operational systems while maintaining sub-kilometer resolution. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for adaptive oceanographic forecasting, validated against field measurements from recent naval exercises in the Indo-Pacific region.
