The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring petascale processing capabilities and high-bandwidth memory—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. Successful implementation will provide military operators with enhanced situational awareness in dynamic coastal environments, directly informing mission planning related to mine countermeasures, antisubmarine warfare, and amphibious operations. This work bridges oceanographic science and defense priorities, advancing computational methods for time-sensitive, security-critical applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of physical oceanography as applied to the naval tactical and strategic environment and the support of military operations. Includes instruction in atmospheric thermodynamics and radiation propagation, air-ocean fluid dynamics, ocean waves, nearshore environments and processes, ocean acoustics, ocean analysis, tactical oceanography, prediction, and related quantitative and experimental methods.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of electrocardiographic (ECG) signal analysis through advanced computational modeling, addressing limitations in traditional methods for detecting cardiac arrhythmias and abnormalities. Despite the widespread use of ECG technology, challenges persist in analyzing high-volume, noisy datasets from ambulatory monitoring systems and wearable devices, particularly in distinguishing subtle pathological patterns from artifacts or benign variations. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing machine learning (ML) algorithms trained on large-scale, heterogeneous ECG datasets to improve automated rhythm classification and anomaly detection. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabytes of multi-lead ECG recordings, including publicly available databases and de-identified clinical data from partner institutions. Deep learning architectures, such as convolutional and transformer-based networks, will be optimized for parallelized training on GPU clusters to identify temporal and spatial features indicative of arrhythmias, ischemic events, and conduction disorders. Signal preprocessing pipelines will integrate noise reduction techniques and domain adaptation strategies to enhance model generalizability across diverse patient populations and recording devices. The project will further simulate cardiac electrical activity using finite-element modeling to generate synthetic ECG waveforms for augmenting training data and validating detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time ECG analysis, validated against expert clinician interpretations, with potential integration into clinical workflows and educational platforms. By improving diagnostic precision and reducing latency in identifying critical cardiac events, this research aims to directly support patient care and advance training in electrocardiograph technology. The scalability of these computational methods will also provide a foundation for future innovations in personalized cardiovascular monitoring, aligning with broader goals of improving health outcomes through technology-driven clinical decision support.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and nurses, to administer EKG and ECG diagnostic examinations and report results to the treatment team. Includes instruction in basic anatomy and physiology, the cardiovascular system, medical terminology, cardiovascular medications and effects, patient care, EKG and ECG administration, equipment operation and maintenance, interpretation of cardiac rhythm, patient record management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Behavioral disorders in companion animals present complex challenges that often involve interactions between medical, environmental, and neurophysiological factors. Current approaches to diagnosing and treating these disorders rely heavily on observational assessments and trial-and-error interventions, which lack predictive power and scalability. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational models to predict individual animal responses to behavior modification therapies and pharmacological treatments. The research will integrate multi-modal data, including electronic health records, behavioral phenotyping datasets (e.g., motion tracking, vocalization patterns), owner-reported environmental factors, and physiological biomarkers (e.g., cortisol levels, neuroimaging data). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process and analyze these large, heterogeneous datasets, which span terabytes of structured and unstructured data. Machine learning frameworks, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify latent patterns linking medical conditions (e.g., endocrine dysfunction, chronic pain) to specific behavioral phenotypes. Agent-based modeling will simulate dynamic interactions between animals, owners, and environments to test hypotheses about intervention efficacy under diverse scenarios. Additionally, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) simulations will model drug metabolism variability across species and breeds to optimize dosing protocols for psychoactive medications. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized workflows for feature extraction, model training, and sensitivity analyses, requiring access to GPU clusters and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to stratify animals by probable treatment outcomes, (2) evidence-based guidelines for integrating medication with behavior modification plans, and (3) open-source software for veterinary behaviorists to simulate intervention impacts in silico. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by reducing reliance on reactive, one-size-fits-all approaches, ultimately improving outcomes for animals with treatment-resistant behavioral pathologies and mitigating risks of euthanasia due to unresolved behavioral issues.
cip_definition: Research on how to understand and treat the behavioral problems of animals, primarily through the application of behavior modification techniques to companion animals; may also involve diagnosis of medical conditions that can affect a pet's behavior, and the use of medication in conjunction with behavior modification therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for next-generation wireless communication networks, addressing the challenge of dynamically balancing spectral efficiency, energy consumption, and latency in dense urban environments. Existing resource allocation models struggle to adapt to real-time network conditions, particularly in scenarios with high user mobility, interference, and heterogeneous device requirements. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to model network topologies and optimize resource distribution. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep learning architectures on large-scale network simulations generated via stochastic geometry and ray-tracing propagation models. Key computational tasks include parallel Monte Carlo simulations of 5G/6G channel access protocols, distributed training of GNNs across multiple GPU nodes, and real-time optimization benchmarking under varying traffic loads. The proposed methods will be validated against standardized 3GPP scenarios and open-source network datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel MORL framework for adaptive subchannel/power allocation in non-stationary environments, (2) quantitative comparisons of computational efficiency between conventional optimization and machine learning-driven approaches, and (3) open-source simulation tools for massive MIMO network prototyping. This work directly supports communications engineering research by enabling complex trade-off analyses that exceed the capabilities of single-node computing environments, particularly in parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 dimensions. Successful implementation will provide methodological advances for network optimization under uncertainty while informing practical deployments of energy-aware communication systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling memory-intensive network graph operations and achieving statistically significant results across diverse urban configurations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of communications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in communications networks and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance diagnostic accuracy and workflow efficiency in medical sonography by developing advanced computational tools for real-time ultrasound image analysis. Current clinical practice relies heavily on manual interpretation of sonographic data, which is time-intensive and subject to interoperator variability, particularly when detecting subtle pathologies such as early-stage tumors or microvascular abnormalities. To address these challenges, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of automating image segmentation, anomaly detection, and quantitative biomarker extraction from dynamic ultrasound datasets. The computational workflow will involve processing high-resolution 3D/4D ultrasound volumes and Doppler血流 data using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers optimized for temporal-spatial feature recognition. These models will be trained on a multi-institutional dataset of annotated cases spanning hepatic, cardiac, and obstetric applications, with federated learning techniques to maintain patient privacy. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of this data (estimated at 250 TB), enabling rapid hyperparameter optimization, and simulating real-time inference scenarios across diverse clinical hardware. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive sonographic analysis, validated against ground-truth diagnostic findings, that reduces manual measurement errors by ≥30% in pilot trials. The project will further generate benchmark datasets for rare pathologies, addressing a gap in sonography AI research. By integrating computational advances with clinical workflows, this work aims to standardize diagnostic criteria, improve early disease detection, and provide ultrasound technicians with decision-support tools that complement their expertise—ultimately enhancing patient care quality in resource-constrained settings.
cip_title: Diagnostic Medical Sonography/ Sonographer and Ultrasound Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to utilize medical ultrasound techniques to gather sonographic data used to diagnose a variety of conditions and diseases. Includes instruction in obtaining, reviewing, and integrating patient histories and data; patient instruction and care; anatomic, physiologic and pathologic data recording; sonographic data processing; sonography equipment operation; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation medicine faces significant challenges in predicting and optimizing treatment outcomes for children and young adults with congenital or childhood-onset physical impairments. Current clinical models often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data types—such as electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, wearable sensor outputs, and psychosocial assessments—into unified frameworks for personalized care. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to model multifactorial interactions influencing functional outcomes. The research will focus on two core aims: (1) creating predictive algorithms to identify optimal rehabilitation pathways using longitudinal EHR data and motion-capture biomechanical datasets, and (2) simulating neurodevelopmental trajectories through whole-brain computational models derived from diffusion tensor imaging and functional MRI. Machine learning approaches, including graph neural networks and multimodal transformers, will be deployed to analyze temporal patterns in rehabilitation progress while accounting for individual variability in musculoskeletal development, cognitive profiles, and environmental factors. The computational workflow will require large-scale parallel processing for parameter optimization in patient-specific biomechanical simulations and Bayesian inference frameworks for treatment effect estimation. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, the team will perform iterative analyses across multi-terabyte datasets encompassing >5,000 historical cases from collaborating children’s hospitals. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for gross motor function improvement in cerebral palsy cohorts and a computational toolset for simulating intervention impacts on neural plasticity. This resource-intensive approach aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in pediatric rehabilitation, with potential to reduce trial-and-error treatment strategies while addressing critical gaps in understanding lifespan implications of childhood interventions. The resulting infrastructure will be shared as open-source modules to support reproducibility in rehabilitation science.
cip_definition: Research on how to use an interdisciplinary approach to prevent, diagnose, treat, and manage congenital and childhood-onset physical impairments in children and young adults, including related medical, physical, functional, psychosocial, and vocational limitations or conditions.

abstract: Healthcare administrative systems face growing complexity due to increasing patient volumes, evolving care models, and resource constraints. This project seeks to optimize operational decision-making in hospital networks by developing predictive models for patient flow, staff scheduling, and resource utilization. The research addresses a critical gap in scalable, real-time computational tools capable of integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records, staffing logs, and equipment inventories—to dynamically balance efficiency and care quality. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization framework combining discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and reinforcement learning to capture multi-scale interactions between administrative policies and clinical outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale historical operational datasets, train deep neural networks on patient admission patterns, and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing intervention scenarios. Initial pilot studies using single-node architectures achieved 82% accuracy in predicting emergency department bottlenecks but lacked the temporal resolution needed for proactive adjustments. The requested allocation will enable large-scale parameter space exploration across 12 hospital sites, each modeled with site-specific constraints and demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for adaptive capacity planning, (2) validated thresholds for critical resource reallocation during demand surges, and (3) predictive metrics linking administrative decisions to 30-day readmission risks. By quantifying how computational resource allocation impacts both operational and clinical endpoints, this work will provide novel evidence to guide investments in healthcare infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through the National Association of Healthcare Access Management and integrated into graduate health administration curricula, directly advancing workforce training in data-driven medical operations.
cip_title: Health and Medical Administrative Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical administrative services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale digital humanities investigation into the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in Ukraine, with emphasis on underrepresented regional and gender perspectives. The research problem centers on analyzing vast, unstructured datasets—including digitized folklore archives, Soviet-era periodicals, post-independence media, and contemporary social media—to identify patterns in how cultural symbols, linguistic markers, and collective memory have been negotiated across Ukraine’s contested historical landscapes. Current methodologies in cultural studies lack scalable tools to systematically process multimodal Ukrainian-language materials spanning five centuries while accounting for dialectal diversity, shifting political terminologies, and erasures in archival records. Our computational approach integrates transformer-based language models fine-tuned on historical Ukrainian texts, geospatial network analysis of cultural production centers, and semi-supervised clustering algorithms to map discursive continuities and fractures across time, space, and sociocultural groups. The workflow requires parallelized processing of 12TB of text and image data, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for graph-based analyses of regional cultural networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of persistent subnational narrative frameworks in border regions like Slobozhanshchyna and Bukovyna; (2) quantitative models tracing the impact of 20th-century state policies on gendered representations in folk traditions; (3) an open-access annotated corpus of Ukrainian cultural discourse from 1600–2023. By enabling computationally intensive analysis at unprecedented temporal and geographical granularity, this project will provide new empirical foundations for understanding cultural resilience and adaptation in Ukraine while developing transferable pipelines for non-Anglocentric digital humanities research. The requested resources directly address the computational barriers that have historically constrained large-scope cultural studies in under-resourced linguistic contexts.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the Ukraine and its inhabitants, and related border regions, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Latin textual corpora spanning classical, medieval, and ecclesiastical periods. A central challenge in Latin philology lies in systematically tracing linguistic evolution, syntactic variation, and lexical shifts across eras, dialects, and genres—tasks complicated by the scale and diversity of surviving texts. Traditional manual methods struggle to process the growing digitized corpus, which includes inscriptions, classical literature, medieval manuscripts, and liturgical documents, often with fragmentary or contested authorship. This research proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) techniques with historical linguistic frameworks to model diachronic and synchronic patterns in Latin usage. Key objectives include training domain-specific language models on curated datasets of classical and post-classical Latin; developing algorithms to detect stylistic and grammatical features indicative of period, genre, or regional influence; and applying graph-based methods to analyze intertextual networks in medieval theological works. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of multilingual manuscripts (e.g., Latin-Greek comparative analysis), high-dimensional clustering of syntactic structures, and simulation of dialectal convergence in Italic languages. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital toolkit for Latin philological analysis, quantitative maps of linguistic change across transitional periods (e.g., Late Antiquity to Carolingian Latin), and improved attribution models for anonymous ecclesiastical texts. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic scholarship, this project aims to deepen understanding of Latin’s sociolinguistic dynamics while establishing scalable methods for interdisciplinary textual research. The requested resources are critical to handling memory-intensive tasks, such as training transformer models on non-standard orthographies and optimizing optical character recognition (OCR) pipelines for digitized pre-modern manuscripts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Latin language and literature from its origins through its decline and its current ecclesiastical usage, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, related Italic dialects, Late Roman and Medieval Latin, and modern Church Latin.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing school-based interventions for enhancing social-emotional learning (SEL) and academic engagement in K–12 students. A critical challenge in educational psychology is modeling the dynamic, multi-level interactions between student traits, instructional practices, and intervention components that collectively shape learning outcomes. Traditional statistical methods often oversimplify these interdependencies, limiting the ability to predict how interventions perform across diverse classroom contexts. To address this, we propose developing computational models that integrate agent-based simulations with longitudinal educational datasets. The agent-based framework will represent students, teachers, and school environments as interactive entities, parameterized using empirical data on developmental trajectories, behavioral patterns, and intervention response metrics from 15 regional school districts. Machine learning pipelines will then analyze simulated and real-world data to identify context-sensitive predictors of intervention efficacy. HPC resources are essential for scaling these computationally intensive tasks: parallelized simulations will explore thousands of scenarios varying classroom compositions, intervention timing, and implementation fidelity, while deep learning architectures will process multimodal data (e.g., academic records, behavioral surveys, teacher reports). Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model linking intervention design to context-dependent student outcomes and (2) actionable guidelines for tailoring counseling strategies and SEL programs to specific school environments. This work directly supports the program’s mission to improve educational processes through psychological research, offering novel tools to bridge the gap between individualized counseling principles and systemic educational practices. By elucidating how interventions interact with classroom ecosystems, the project aims to empower educators with evidence-based strategies for fostering equitable student development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychology to the study of the behavior of individuals in the roles of teacher and learner, the nature and effects of learning environments, and the psychological effects of methods, resources, organization and non-school experience on the educational process. Includes instruction in learning theory, human growth and development, research methods, and psychological evaluation.

abstract: Chiropractic care, rooted in the relationship between spinal alignment and nervous system function, lacks a comprehensive biomechanical and neurophysiological understanding of how specific adjustments influence systemic health. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multi-scale computational model to simulate the immediate and cascading effects of spinal manipulations on neural signaling, musculoskeletal dynamics, and autonomic regulation. Current clinical studies and in vitro experiments are limited in resolving real-time, system-wide interactions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate heterogeneous data—including MRI-derived spinal geometries, neural activity datasets, and biomechanical force profiles—into a unified simulation framework. The research will employ finite element modeling to simulate vertebral segment mechanics under adjustment forces, coupled with dynamic neural network models to predict central nervous system (CNS) responses. Machine learning algorithms will analyze simulated and clinical data to identify patterns linking adjustment parameters (e.g., force vector, velocity) to physiological outcomes such as pain modulation, inflammatory marker changes, or autonomic balance. HPC resources are critical for managing the computational intensity of iterative simulations across variable patient anatomies and for training predictive models on multi-terabyte datasets encompassing retrospective clinical records and motion-capture biomechanics. Expected outcomes include a validated in silico platform for optimizing adjustment protocols, a mechanistic framework explaining how localized biomechanical interventions propagate systemic effects, and predictive tools for personalizing chiropractic care based on patient-specific spinal kinematics and neural responsiveness. This work aims to advance chiropractic science from an empirically guided practice to a quantitatively grounded discipline, bridging biomechanics, neuroscience, and clinical therapeutics. By elucidating the biophysical underpinnings of spinal adjustments, the project will inform safer, more effective treatment strategies and foster interdisciplinary collaborations to position chiropractic within integrative healthcare models.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of chiropractic, a health care and healing system based on the application of non-invasive treatments and spinal adjustments to alleviate health problems caused by vertebral misalignments affecting bodily function as derived from the philosophy of Daniel Palmer. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, chiropractic theory and science, postural and spinal analysis, diagnostic radiology and ultrasound, adjustment technique, patient counseling, professional standards and ethics, and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the computational modeling of hypersonic flow-structure-thermal interactions in next-generation aerospace vehicles, a critical challenge in high-speed flight systems. Current predictive tools struggle to resolve the coupled physics of turbulent boundary layers, aerodynamic heating, and thermoelastic material responses at Mach 10+ conditions, limiting the design of reliable thermal protection systems and reusable spacecraft. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation framework combining adaptive mesh refinement, implicit large-eddy turbulence modeling, and partitioned fluid-structure-thermal coupling algorithms. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for compressible Navier-Stokes equations integrated with nonlinear finite-element analysis of anisotropic composite materials. Our approach requires petascale high-performance computing resources to resolve multiscale phenomena across spatial scales (boundary layer vortices to global vehicle deformation) and temporal scales (microsecond shock oscillations to minute-long aerodynamic heating). Initial validation will focus on experimental data from arc-jet wind tunnels and published flight test measurements. Expected outcomes include new insight into transition regimes between laminar and turbulent hypersonic flows, quantified uncertainty bounds for coupled ablation-erosion processes, and optimized material architectures for sharp leading-edge components. These results will directly inform ongoing NASA and Department of Defense initiatives on crewed Mars reentry systems and responsive hypersonic platforms. The resource request supports 18 months of simulations across 20M core-hours on parallel architectures, enabling parametric studies at unprecedented resolution. Deliverables will include open-source solver modules for the computational aerospace community and datasets to accelerate machine learning surrogate models for real-time hypersonic design applications.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their system. Combines instruction in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and functional integration of implantable biosensors for real-time monitoring of physiological biomarkers. A critical challenge in biomedical device engineering lies in balancing sensor sensitivity, biocompatibility, and long-term stability within dynamic biological environments. Current experimental approaches are limited in resolving multiscale interactions between sensor materials, biofluids, and host tissue responses. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to model sensor-tissue interfaces across spatial and temporal scales. MD will simulate atomic-level interactions between sensor coatings and proteins to predict fouling risks, while FEA will model mechanical strain distributions and electrochemical signal stability under physiological conditions. A neural network trained on these datasets will identify optimal sensor geometries and material compositions. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the need for parallelized MD trajectories (10⁶–10⁷ atoms) over microsecond timescales, coupled with multiphysics FEA simulations incorporating fluid-structure interactions and diffusion-reaction kinetics. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking sensor design parameters to in vivo performance metrics, validated against experimental data from collaborator labs. This work will establish an open-source toolkit for accelerated biosensor prototyping, reducing iterative animal trials and enabling patient-specific device customization. By addressing computational bottlenecks in multiscale biointerface modeling, the project aims to advance translational biomedical engineering while fostering HPC-enabled innovation in medical technology development.
detailed_field: Biological/ biosystems engineering and biomedical technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing biological or medical systems and products. Includes instruction in instrument calibration, design and installation testing, system safety and maintenance procedures, procurement and installation procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Clinical nurse leaders (CNLs) face complex challenges in optimizing patient outcomes through evidence-based interventions, particularly when managing dynamic care environments with high-acuity patients. A critical barrier is the inability to rapidly analyze large-scale, heterogeneous clinical datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), real-time biosensor data, and longitudinal care coordination metrics—to inform decision-making. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that identify early risk factors for preventable adverse events (e.g., sepsis, medication errors) and simulate intervention strategies for CNL-led teams. Leveraging a de-identified dataset of 250,000+ patient encounters from three tertiary care centers, we will employ parallelized machine learning (ML) frameworks, including ensemble classifiers and recurrent neural networks, to model temporal patterns in patient deterioration and care process inefficiencies. Computational workflows will integrate structured EHR data, unstructured nursing notes (processed via natural language processing), and high-frequency vital sign streams. Sensitivity analyses will evaluate how staffing ratios, care pathway adjustments, and interdisciplinary communication protocols affect outcomes in agent-based simulations. HPC resources are essential for training ML models on multi-terabyte datasets, running computationally intensive simulations across diverse scenarios, and enabling real-time model validation. Expected outcomes include (1) risk prediction tools with ≥85% accuracy for adverse events, integrated into CNL workflows via a dashboard; (2) evidence-based recommendations for care team configurations under varying clinical demands; and (3) an open-source computational framework for nursing researchers to simulate care delivery models. By bridging high-performance analytics with frontline nursing practice, this work will empower CNLs to proactively mitigate risks, allocate resources efficiently, and demonstrate the translational impact of computational nursing science on patient safety.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses for careers as clinical nurse leaders in which they work as part of an interdisciplinary team that provides direct medical care for patients based on evidence-based practice and research. Includes instruction in pharmacology, pathophysiology, epidemiology, research in nursing methods, advanced health assessment, statistics, and clinical practice management.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing personalized ophthalmic lens and frame design using advanced computational modeling to improve visual outcomes and patient comfort in populations with complex anatomical or optical needs. Current methods for fitting corrective eyewear rely on generalized measurements and manual adjustments, which may fail to account for subtle variations in facial asymmetry, tissue biomechanics, or dynamic interactions between lenses, frames, and anatomical structures during prolonged wear. We propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity biomechanical simulations of facial soft tissue deformation, optical ray-tracing models, and machine learning to predict optimal lens positioning and frame geometry tailored to individual patients. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the execution of finite element analysis (FEA) models incorporating anatomically accurate 3D facial scans, material properties of frame components, and lens prescriptions to simulate pressure distribution, slippage patterns, and optical performance under real-world conditions. Concurrently, a deep neural network trained on a synthetic dataset of virtual fittings will accelerate the identification of design parameters that minimize visual distortion while maintaining comfort. The project will validate predictions against clinical data from 200 patients with challenging fitting requirements, including post-surgical craniofacial anatomy and high-prescription myopia with astigmatism. Outcomes will include an open-source computational toolkit for opticians to simulate and visualize fitting outcomes prior to fabrication, reducing iterative adjustments and material waste. By bridging ophthalmic optics, soft tissue biomechanics, and computational engineering, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in precision opticianry, enhancing both clinical efficiency and patient-specific optical correction. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space and multi-physics simulations inherent to this personalized approach.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to adapt and fit corrective eyewear, including eyeglasses and contact lenses, as prescribed by ophthalmologists or optometrists; to assist patients in selecting appropriate frames; and to prepare work orders for ophthalmic laboratory technicians. Includes instruction in geometrical optics, ophthalmic optics, anatomy of the eye, optical instrumentation, use and maintenance of adjustment and cleaning tools, prescription interpretation, contact lens adaptation and fitting, prosthesis fitting, facial and eye measuring, pathology identification, record-keeping, and patient and business administrative tasks.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern diesel engines, coupled with stringent emissions regulations and demands for higher fuel efficiency, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize engine design, diagnostics, and maintenance strategies. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate diesel engine combustion dynamics, emissions formation, and component wear under diverse operating conditions. Current experimental approaches are limited by cost, scalability, and the inability to isolate variables in real-world systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address these gaps through large-scale parametric studies of fuel injection patterns, turbocharger performance, and aftertreatment system interactions. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will leverage open-source solvers (e.g., OpenFOAM) to model multiphase combustion processes, while machine learning frameworks will analyze sensor data from engine testbeds to predict failure modes in critical components like fuel injectors and piston rings. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of core-hours, integrating 3D engine geometries and real-world duty-cycle data from industrial partners. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimizing combustion efficiency under transient loads, digital twins for proactive maintenance of fleet vehicles, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated engine performance scenarios. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in Diesel Mechanics Technology programs by providing students with exposure to computational diagnostics tools, bridging traditional hands-on training with Industry 4.0 methodologies. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for diesel technicians and collaborations with manufacturers to validate models against engine dynamometer tests. The project addresses a critical need for data-driven decision-making in diesel engine maintenance and design, with potential impacts on reducing operational downtime, lowering emissions, and extending engine service life in transportation and energy sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the acoustical properties of woodwind instruments, with a focus on optimizing performance techniques and instrument design. While traditional pedagogical methods for woodwind performance emphasize empirical practice and subjective feedback, the complex interactions between airflow, mechanical resonance, and player biomechanics remain poorly quantified. Current challenges include predicting how subtle variations in embouchure, finger technique, or instrument geometry affect tonal quality, intonation, and dynamic control. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate air-column vibrations, pressure distributions, and energy transfer within instrument bodies under performance conditions. High-resolution 3D scans of instruments (e.g., clarinet, oboe) will inform geometrically accurate models, while motion-capture data of performer interactions will parameterize boundary conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then identify patterns linking computational outputs to perceptual audio metrics derived from professional performance recordings. The scale of these simulations—requiring millions of mesh elements and iterative solvers for transient multiphysics problems—necessitates parallelized HPC workflows. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models to guide pedagogical strategies for embouchure development, quantitative frameworks for evaluating instrument modifications, and data-driven insights into historical performance practices. By bridging computational engineering and performing arts, this work aims to establish reproducible methodologies for studying woodwind acoustics, offering conservatories and instrument makers tools to enhance artistic training and design innovation. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated computations, large-scale data storage for time-series simulations, and collaborative visualization platforms for interdisciplinary analysis.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a woodwind instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: Pediatric rheumatic diseases, such as juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and pediatric collagen disorders, present significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their clinical heterogeneity, complex pathophysiology, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches to risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making rely on limited biomarkers and subjective clinical assessments, often leading to delayed or suboptimal care. This project aims to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-modal datasets—including genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, and longitudinal clinical data—and develop predictive models for disease progression and treatment outcomes. A key focus is identifying molecular signatures and biomechanical risk factors associated with treatment-resistant phenotypes in JIA and pediatric lupus. Computational workflows will include large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS), dynamic network modeling of immune pathways, and machine learning algorithms (e.g., graph neural networks, ensemble classifiers) to analyze high-dimensional datasets from multicenter cohorts. Additionally, biomechanical simulations of joint tissue stress in pediatric patients will be performed using finite element analysis to evaluate injury susceptibility and inform rehabilitation protocols. These computationally intensive tasks require parallelized processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU acceleration to manage datasets exceeding 100 TB and execute iterative modeling frameworks. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for early identification of high-risk patients, (2) mechanistic insights into treatment resistance pathways, and (3) open-source computational tools for pediatric rheumatology biomarker discovery. By enabling rapid, data-driven stratification of patients, this work has the potential to reduce irreversible joint damage, optimize biologic therapy selection, and improve quality of life for children with chronic musculoskeletal conditions. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s scale and complexity, which exceed the capabilities of local clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research on how to diagnose and treat diseases of joints, muscle, bones, and tendons in children and young adults, including arthritis, back pain, muscle strains, common athletic injuries, and collagen diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research focused on modeling the evolution of judicial reasoning in common law systems. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing how legal principles adapt over time through appellate court decisions, particularly in areas where statutory frameworks are sparse or ambiguous. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case analysis, which limits scalability and obscures macro-level patterns in judicial decision-making. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), graph theory, and temporal network analysis to map doctrinal shifts across large corpora of judicial opinions from U.S. federal appellate courts. The methodology involves training transformer-based models to identify latent legal concepts and their relational dynamics within case texts, followed by the construction of time-evolving knowledge graphs to trace precedent influence and conceptual divergence. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured legal text, optimizing neural architectures for domain-specific language, and simulating longitudinal network behavior. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for quantifying doctrinal stability and innovation in case law, 2) identification of understudied inflection points in judicial reasoning across civil rights and intellectual property domains, and 3) open-source tools to assist legal researchers in visualizing citation networks and predicting conceptual trajectories. By integrating computational social science methods with legal theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for empirical jurisprudence, offering insights into the sociotechnical forces shaping legal evolution. The results could inform judicial education, legislative drafting, and the development of AI-assisted legal research platforms, bridging gaps between traditional doctrinal analysis and data-driven policy design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of law, for taking state and national bar examinations, and for advanced research in jurisprudence. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of the legal system, including the statutory, administrative, and judicial components of civil and criminal law.

abstract: The integration of multi-omics data and advanced computational modeling in chemical pathology has the potential to revolutionize diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making. However, current workflows face challenges in processing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., metabolomic, proteomic, and lipidomic profiles) and linking them to clinical outcomes due to limitations in computational power and algorithmic scalability. This project seeks to address these bottlenecks by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for disease stratification and laboratory test optimization. The research focuses on two interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to identify novel biomarkers for metabolic disorders, such as diabetes and inborn errors of metabolism, by analyzing multi-scale chemical pathology data from retrospective cohorts, and (2) simulating dynamic biochemical pathway perturbations using systems biology models to predict patient-specific responses to therapeutic interventions. Computational workflows will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures (e.g., graph neural networks for metabolite interaction mapping) and parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in diagnostic thresholds. By unifying heterogeneous datasets—including mass spectrometry outputs, electronic health records, and real-time sensor data from laboratory instrumentation—this approach aims to reduce diagnostic latency and improve the precision of chemical test interpretation. The outcomes will directly inform clinical protocols for laboratory test prioritization and resource allocation in pathology departments, while the open-source tools developed will enable reproducible analysis pipelines for the broader community. This work underscores the critical role of HPC in bridging gaps between high-throughput analytical chemistry and actionable clinical insights, ultimately advancing personalized medicine in chemical pathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use and interpretation of chemical analyses, chemical diagnoses and management, and the supervision of chemical pathology laboratories. May included related research in basic and applied analytical chemical pathology; instrumentation data processing and chemical laboratory management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing executive coaching strategies in complex organizational ecosystems. While executive coaching is a critical tool for leadership development and organizational change, current methodologies often rely on qualitative, anecdotal approaches that struggle to account for the dynamic interplay of individual behaviors, team dynamics, and systemic organizational variables. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven models to predict how tailored coaching interventions propagate through hierarchical and cross-functional networks, particularly in large, geographically dispersed organizations. To address this gap, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate multi-level organizational interactions, integrating behavioral datasets (e.g., psychometric assessments, 360-degree feedback) with real-time communication metadata (e.g., email, Slack networks) to map decision-making cascades. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of thousands of scenario simulations, varying parameters such as leadership styles, communication latency, and team cohesion thresholds. Machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks, will be applied to identify latent patterns in coaching efficacy across diverse organizational cultures. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for quantifying the second-order effects of coaching interventions, such as their impact on innovation cycles or conflict resolution pathways. This work aims to establish a novel, computationally rigorous paradigm for designing adaptive coaching protocols that balance individual executive growth with enterprise-wide strategic objectives. By bridging computational social science with leadership development, the project will provide actionable insights for optimizing human capital investments in rapidly evolving business environments, with potential applications in merger integration, digital transformation initiatives, and crisis leadership preparedness.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in warehouse operations and maintenance through advanced computational modeling and optimization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enhance decision-making in inventory management, equipment maintenance, and workflow design. Traditional methods for optimizing warehousing systems often rely on static models or simplified heuristics, which fail to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating demand, equipment degradation, or real-time supply chain disruptions. The research problem centers on developing adaptive, data-driven frameworks capable of simulating large-scale warehouse environments and predicting operational bottlenecks with high fidelity. Using agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation, this project will replicate complex interactions between personnel, automated systems, and inventory flows under diverse scenarios. Parallelized optimization algorithms, including genetic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning, will be employed to iteratively refine maintenance schedules, inventory placement strategies, and equipment utilization protocols. High-performance computing is critical to process multi-terabyte datasets from IoT sensors, historical maintenance logs, and enterprise resource planning systems, enabling real-time anomaly detection in equipment performance and predictive failure analysis. The computational workflows will integrate graph neural networks to model dependencies between warehouse subsystems and stochastic optimization techniques to account for uncertainty in supply chain variables. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for warehouse operations, predictive maintenance algorithms with quantified error margins, and evidence-based resource allocation guidelines to minimize downtime. By enabling hyperparametric tuning of simulation models and reducing computational latency in optimization loops, HPC resources will directly contribute to operational cost reductions of 15–25% in simulated test cases. The resulting tools aim to set new benchmarks for resilience in warehousing systems while providing open-source computational frameworks for workforce training in maintenance technology programs.
cip_title: Parts and Warehousing Operations and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain inventory control, care for inventory, and make minor repairs to warehouse equipment.

abstract: Athletic injuries to the musculoskeletal system present complex biomechanical and physiological challenges, with prevention and rehabilitation strategies often limited by incomplete understanding of injury mechanisms across diverse populations. This project seeks to develop multiscale computational models integrating tissue-level biomechanics, athlete-specific motion patterns, and biological healing processes to predict injury risks and optimize rehabilitation protocols. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process large datasets from wearable sensors, 3D motion capture, and medical imaging (MRI, ultrasound) of 500+ athletes, alongside mechanistic simulations of load distribution in bone, muscle, and connective tissues. Machine learning pipelines will analyze movement patterns associated with common injuries (e.g., ACL tears, rotator cuff strains), while finite element modeling will simulate tissue stress responses under dynamic sporting loads. A novel agent-based model will further explore cellular-level healing timelines post-injury, incorporating individual variability in inflammation markers and genetic profiles. The computational workflow demands parallel processing for real-time parameter optimization in athlete-specific models and probabilistic risk assessments across heterogeneous cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for injury susceptibility, validated against prospective clinical data from three collegiate sports programs, and personalized rehabilitation guidelines informed by simulated healing trajectories. This work directly addresses critical gaps in evidence-based injury prevention by quantifying interactions between biomechanical forces, biological recovery processes, and athlete-specific factors at unprecedented resolution. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for clinical researchers and partnerships with sports medicine providers to reduce reinjury rates and improve return-to-play decision-making.
cip_definition: Research on how to prevent and manage athletic injuries and to provide appropriate care for all structures of the musculoskeletal system directly affected by participation in sporting activity.

abstract: Current methods for fitting contact lenses often rely on empirical adjustments and static anatomical measurements, which may not account for dynamic physiological interactions between the lens, corneal surface, and tear film. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model these interactions at the micron scale, enabling personalized lens parameter optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement multi-physics simulations combining finite element analysis of lens deformation, computational fluid dynamics of tear film stability, and biomechanical corneal response under varying environmental conditions. Patient-specific data from corneal topography, blink patterns, and meibomian gland function will inform boundary conditions. Machine learning algorithms will then identify optimal lens curvature, material elasticity, and edge design parameters that minimize interfacial stress while maintaining optical performance. The proposed simulations require parallel processing capabilities to handle 3D meshes with >10^7 elements and iterative solvers for coupled differential equations across temporal scales. Successful validation against clinical outcomes from 200 retrospective cases will establish model accuracy. This approach aims to reduce fitting time by 40% and improve wearer comfort metrics by 30% compared to standard protocols. By integrating optometric practice with computational engineering, this project advances precision eye care tools while providing a scalable platform for investigating ocular surface disorders. The resource allocation will support critical developments at the intersection of clinical optometry and high-fidelity biomechanical modeling, fostering innovation in a specialized health sciences niche.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist optometrists in providing patient care, administering examinations and treatments, and performing office administrative functions. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology of the eye, visual testing, patient communication, patient preparation, medications and administration, dispensing and fitting of eyeglasses and contact lenses, record-keeping, and office management skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing resource allocation in heterogeneous computing architectures, which integrate diverse components such as CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs to meet escalating computational demands in real-world applications. As systems grow more complex, traditional static allocation strategies struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and hardware utilization, particularly in dynamic workloads common to cloud computing, edge environments, and AI-driven applications. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of adaptive resource management frameworks that leverage machine learning (ML) and real-time system telemetry. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train ML models on large-scale, multi-node simulations of heterogeneous systems under varying workloads, while also enabling the evaluation of dynamic allocation algorithms across diverse hardware configurations. The computational approach includes creating modular simulation environments using containerized workloads, profiling tools for hardware-software interaction analysis, and reinforcement learning models to predict optimal resource distribution. Expected outcomes include novel allocation strategies that reduce latency by 15–20% in mixed CPU-GPU workflows, improve energy efficiency by 10–15% through predictive power management, and provide generalized guidelines for architecture-aware resource partitioning. The resulting frameworks will be validated against industry-standard benchmarks and open-source compute orchestration tools, with findings disseminated as reusable optimization modules for system administrators and developers. By advancing adaptive resource management techniques, this work aims to lower barriers to efficient heterogeneous system deployment in sectors reliant on scalable computing infrastructure, including autonomous systems, distributed AI training, and real-time data processing pipelines. The requested HPC resources will directly support large-scale parallelism in simulations, iterative model training, and comparative analysis across thousands of hardware-software permutations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and biophysical mechanisms underlying Asian Bodywork Therapy (ABT) modalities, such as acupressure and Tui na, through computational modeling and simulation. Despite widespread clinical use, the physiological effects of ABT techniques—particularly their interactions with tissue dynamics, neural signaling, and systemic energy pathways (e.g., Qi flow)—remain poorly quantified. Traditional studies rely on small-scale empirical data or subjective outcomes, limiting reproducibility and mechanistic insight. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical models, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and optimize ABT interventions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution medical imaging data, model tissue deformation and fluid dynamics during pressure application, and analyze multiscale physiological responses across diverse populations. Simulations will incorporate variable parameters such as force magnitude, direction, and duration, as well as individualized anatomical variations (e.g., muscle density, vascular networks). Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify patterns in existing clinical datasets linking ABT techniques to biomarkers of pain modulation, inflammation, and autonomic nervous system activity. The integration of FEA and ML outputs aims to generate predictive models of therapy efficacy, enabling personalized treatment protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational pipeline for mapping ABT biomechanics, (2) quantitative evidence of dose-response relationships in pressure-based therapies, and (3) open-access tools for practitioners to refine techniques using simulated scenarios. By bridging traditional practices with computational biophysics, this work will establish a foundation for evidence-based optimization of ABT, enhancing its integration into multidisciplinary care and informing regulatory standards for training and safety. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for parallelized simulations of heterogeneous tissue interactions and large-scale ML training—necessitate HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant resolution and scalability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide relief and improved health and well-being based on Chinese medical principles through one or more of the traditional bodywork therapies of Asia. Includes instruction in acupressure, AMMA(r) Therapy, Chi Nei Tsang, Five Element Shiatsu, Integrative Eclectic Shiatsu, Japanese Shiatsu, Jin Shin Do(r) Bodymind Acupressure(tm), Macrobiotic Shiatsu, Anma Therapy, Thai massage, Tui na, Zen Shiatsu, Qigong, Okazaki(r) Restorative Massage, principles of Western and Chinese medicine, patient counseling and observation, practice management, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize radiation dose and image quality in diagnostic radiologic imaging, addressing the critical challenge of balancing patient safety with diagnostic efficacy. Current protocols for x-ray, CT, and hybrid imaging systems often rely on generalized parameters, which may not account for patient-specific anatomical variability or emerging technologies such as photon-counting detectors. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate radiation transport using Monte Carlo methods, model iterative image reconstruction algorithms, and train deep learning networks for protocol optimization. Multiscale simulations will be conducted to quantify dose deposition across heterogeneous tissues and evaluate noise-resolution trade-offs under varying acquisition parameters. A key innovation involves integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize realistic patient-specific phantoms, enabling large-scale virtual trials without exposing individuals to excess radiation. Additionally, reinforcement learning frameworks will be implemented to dynamically adapt imaging parameters based on real-time feedback from simulated scans. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing of large-scale datasets (>100 TB), including voxelized phantom libraries and raw sensor data from digital radiography and MRI systems. Expected outcomes include validated models for personalized protocol optimization, open-source tools for dose prediction, and quantitative guidelines for emerging technologies like low-dose spectral CT. This work will directly inform clinical practice by establishing data-driven methods to reduce population radiation exposure while maintaining diagnostic accuracy, with particular relevance to pediatric and high-risk populations. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the required spatial and temporal resolution in simulations, as well as for training complex neural networks on heterogeneous imaging data. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed platforms and integrated into residency training programs, advancing both radiologic physics research and translational safety initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnostic applications of x-rays, gamma rays from sealed sources, ultrasonic radiation, and magnetic resonance; and in the use of equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing administrative workflow efficiency in dynamic office environments, with a focus on mitigating bottlenecks in document management, communication scheduling, and task prioritization. Administrative professionals in secretarial and assistant roles increasingly face complex, data-dense workflows due to the proliferation of digital communication tools and hybrid work models. Traditional time-management strategies often fail to account for real-time variables such as shifting priorities, multi-channel requests, and document versioning conflicts. This project addresses the computational challenge of modeling these variables to generate adaptive workflow recommendations. Using anonymized datasets of email threads, calendar interactions, and document-editing histories from corporate environments, we will train transformer-based models to predict task-critical paths and simulate resource allocation scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallel processing of temporal graphs representing workflow dependencies, coupled with reinforcement learning to iteratively refine scheduling policies. Expected outcomes include a prototype system capable of dynamically reprioritizing tasks based on real-time input streams, reducing latency in document processing cycles, and automating conflict resolution in multi-stakeholder requests. This work bridges computational scalability gaps in office management research, offering a quantitative framework to enhance decision-making in administrative roles. By integrating NLP for request parsing and graph neural networks for workflow modeling, the project advances interdisciplinary intersections between business communication theory and computational logistics. Results will provide actionable insights for developing next-generation office management tools, with potential applications in training AI-augmented administrative systems and redefining productivity metrics for hybrid work environments.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: The sustainable production of bioenergy from plant and microbial feedstocks requires resolving complex trade-offs between environmental impacts, resource efficiency, and economic viability. Current challenges include optimizing microbial consortia for lignocellulosic biomass conversion, predicting feedstock suitability under variable hydrological and soil conditions, and scaling bioprocess designs to minimize energy-intensive separations. This project seeks advanced computing resources to develop multi-scale models integrating genomic, metabolic, and ecosystem-level data for bioenergy systems. High-performance computing (HPC) will enable genome-resolved simulations of microbial community interactions during anaerobic digestion, dynamic flux balance analysis of engineered metabolic pathways for enhanced biofuel yields, and spatially explicit assessments of region-specific feedstock viability. Coupled machine learning approaches will identify optimal microbial strains, pretreatment strategies, and harvest cycles that maximize energy output while minimizing water and nutrient use. The computational framework will incorporate regional hydrology datasets, soil carbon dynamics, and life-cycle inventory data to evaluate trade-offs between bioenergy production and natural resource conservation. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide the design of low-impact biorefineries, maps of optimal feedstock zones under climate uncertainty, and open-source tools for real-time bioprocess optimization. By quantifying linkages between microbial efficiency, ecosystem services, and supply-chain logistics, this work aims to advance scalable bioenergy solutions that align decarbonization goals with sustainable land and water management. Access to HPC resources is critical for resolving the high-dimensional parameter spaces and stochasticity inherent in biological and environmental systems, which cannot be feasibly addressed with conventional computing infrastructure. The results will directly inform policy frameworks and industrial practices aimed at achieving net-zero bioenergy systems within planetary boundaries.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize patient flow and administrative efficiency in medical reception workflows through advanced computational modeling and predictive analytics. Medical receptionists are critical frontline personnel managing patient intake, scheduling, and communication, yet current practices often rely on static protocols ill-suited for dynamic clinical environments. The research problem centers on mitigating bottlenecks and inefficiencies in high-volume settings (e.g., emergency departments, multispecialty clinics) by developing adaptive, real-time decision-support tools. We propose a two-phase computational approach: first, constructing a discrete-event simulation model of patient-staff interactions using historical electronic health record (EHR) data, including arrival patterns, service times, and resource utilization; second, integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict workflow disruptions and recommend optimal staffing or scheduling adjustments. The simulation will incorporate variables such as patient acuity, seasonal demand fluctuations, and interruptive tasks (e.g., urgent calls, walk-ins), requiring parallelized computation to evaluate millions of scenario permutations. HPC resources will enable training of ensemble ML models on multimodal data (structured EHR entries, free-text triage notes, timestamps) to forecast congestion points and automate adaptive responses. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source framework for clinic workflow optimization, reducing average patient wait times by 20-30% in pilot simulations, and actionable insights into task prioritization strategies for receptionists. This interdisciplinary work bridges health operations research, human-computer interaction, and applied data science, offering a novel computational lens to enhance a traditionally understudied yet vital component of healthcare delivery. The tools developed could be generalized to improve resource allocation in diverse clinical administrative settings, directly supporting workforce effectiveness and patient satisfaction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, nurses, or physicians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in medical office and health care facility procedures, medical terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize individualized educational strategies for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Current approaches to designing personalized learning plans rely heavily on qualitative observations and trial-and-error adjustments, which can delay effective interventions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from classroom settings, including behavioral recordings, sensory response metrics, and longitudinal academic performance data. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns linking specific instructional methods, environmental adjustments, and communication supports to measurable improvements in engagement, skill acquisition, and emotional regulation. A key innovation involves agent-based simulations of student-teacher interactions, which will test hypothetical teaching strategies under diverse virtual scenarios before real-world implementation. These simulations will incorporate dynamic variables such as sensory sensitivities, communication preferences, and task complexity. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of high-resolution video data (for nonverbal behavior analysis) and real-time optimization of adaptive learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to guide educators in selecting evidence-based strategies during individualized education program (IEP) development, (2) quantified thresholds for environmental adaptations (e.g., lighting, noise levels) that maximize student focus, and (3) open-source tools for simulating ASD learning profiles to enhance teacher training programs. By bridging computational analytics with special education pedagogy, this research aims to empower teachers with data-driven decision-making tools while preserving the human-centric values of autism education. The HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s multimodal data integration, large-scale parameter space exploration, and rapid iteration of simulation models.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Cancer treatment resistance remains a critical barrier to improving patient outcomes, with tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and dynamic molecular adaptations driving therapeutic failure. While multi-omics profiling provides unprecedented insights into these mechanisms, integrating genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic datasets at scale remains computationally intractable for conventional systems. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable the development of predictive models of treatment resistance in solid tumors, leveraging machine learning and spatial transcriptomics to map tumor microenvironmental dynamics. We propose a computational workflow combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from metastatic melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer cohorts with longitudinal clinical outcomes. Graph neural networks will model cell-cell interaction networks within tumor-immune ecosystems, while Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify the emergence of resistance-associated mutations under therapeutic pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural impacts of novel resistance mutations in kinase domains identified through these analyses. The HPC environment is essential for processing >50 TB of raw sequencing data, training deep learning architectures with hyperparameter optimization, and running large-scale parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of microenvironmental signatures predictive of early resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, (2) a ranked catalog of high-risk adaptive mutations in targeted therapy pathways, and (3) open-source tools for real-time resistance monitoring using liquid biopsy data. This work directly addresses the NCI’s priority of translating complex tumor dynamics into clinically actionable biomarkers, with potential to guide adaptive therapy protocols and combination treatment strategies. By centralizing computational toxicology and evolutionary modeling within a clinical oncology framework, the project bridges critical gaps between cancer systems biology and precision medicine implementation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of cancer and other benign and malignant tumors; this includes deciding on and administering therapy for these malignancies, as well as consulting with surgeons and radiotherapists on other treatments for cancer.

abstract: Agricultural education faces critical challenges in preparing teachers to address evolving agricultural systems, climate resilience, and technological advancements. Current vocational curricula often lack integration of real-time environmental data, predictive modeling, and adaptive pedagogical strategies, limiting educators’ capacity to equip students with skills for sustainable agriculture.
