This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and analyze large-scale simulations of agricultural ecosystems, coupled with machine learning-driven assessments of teaching efficacy. The research problem centers on bridging the gap between data-driven agricultural science and practical teacher training by modeling complex interactions between environmental variables, educational interventions, and student outcomes. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics, geospatial analysis of regional agricultural trends, and ensemble machine learning algorithms to evaluate the impact of curriculum components on student competency development. These approaches require parallel processing capabilities to handle multidimensional datasets spanning climate projections, soil health metrics, and longitudinal educational performance data. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to optimize agricultural curricula for regional climate adaptation, (2) AI-driven tools for personalized teacher training modules, and (3) scalable models linking STEM pedagogy to agricultural workforce readiness. By synthesizing agricultural science, computational analytics, and educational theory, this work aims to establish a replicable pipeline for enhancing vocational training through evidence-based resource allocation. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from USDA reports, IoT-enabled farm networks, and statewide student assessments, which are computationally prohibitive on local infrastructure. Results will directly inform the design of adaptive teaching resources, strengthening the integration of precision agriculture and climate-smart practices into teacher education programs. This project advances the broader mission of agricultural education by fostering data-literate educators capable of addressing 21st-century food systems challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational agricultural programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance precision medicine in pediatric gastroenterology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multi-modal datasets from children with digestive disorders. Chronic abdominal pain, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and biliary atresia represent significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their heterogeneous presentations, poorly understood molecular mechanisms, and variable treatment responses. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, underscoring the need for patient-specific predictive models. This project will integrate genomic, metabolomic, microbiome, and electronic health record data from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 patients to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Computational challenges include processing whole-genome sequencing data, resolving high-dimensional interactions between host genetics and gut microbial communities, and training machine learning models to predict disease progression or complications like stricturing Crohn’s disease. HPC resources will enable genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with gene-environment interaction terms, longitudinal microbiome trajectory modeling via Bayesian hierarchical frameworks, and dynamic simulations of mucosal immune-metabolic networks. A key innovation involves developing federated learning pipelines to preserve patient privacy while aggregating data across institutions. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for stratifying patients into molecularly defined subgroups, (2) validated predictive algorithms for treatment response (e.g., anti-TNF therapy in IBD), and (3) mechanistic insights into microbiome-host crosstalk in biliary atresia pathogenesis. By addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in multi-omics integration, this work will directly inform the design of targeted clinical trials and personalized monitoring strategies, ultimately reducing diagnostic delays and improving outcomes for children with complex gastrointestinal conditions. The requested resources will support containerized workflows for scalable data processing, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale parameter sweeps for mechanistic model optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the digestive systems of infants, children, and adolescents; includes treatment of conditions such as abdominal pain, ulcers, diarrhea, cancer, and jaundice, and performance of complex diagnostic and therapeutic procedures using lighted scopes to see internal organs.

abstract: Acute care medicine requires rapid, data-driven decision-making to optimize patient outcomes in critical settings. However, current predictive models for clinical deterioration, treatment response, and resource allocation in acute care lack the granularity and speed needed for real-time application. This project proposes to develop machine learning frameworks capable of integrating high-dimensional clinical data—including electronic health records, real-time biosensor streams, and imaging biomarkers—to predict patient trajectories and guide interventions. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks that limit model scalability, latency, and generalizability across diverse acute care populations. We will employ distributed deep learning architectures and ensemble methods to process multimodal datasets at scale, with iterative model validation against prospective clinical outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to train complex neural networks on >100 TB of curated critical care data, simulate clinical scenarios through agent-based modeling, and perform hyperparameter optimization across thousands of parallelized trials. Expected outcomes include validated prediction tools for sepsis progression, acute respiratory failure subtypes, and trauma resuscitation outcomes, all optimized for integration into clinical workflows via low-latency inference engines. The computational pipelines developed will enable dynamic risk stratification using time-varying data, addressing a critical gap in acute care informatics. By leveraging HPC capabilities for federated learning across institutions, this work will also establish privacy-preserving frameworks for multicenter model validation. Successful implementation has the potential to reduce diagnostic delays, personalize resuscitation strategies, and improve resource allocation in emergency departments and intensive care units. This project bridges translational gaps in acute care research by delivering computationally intensive, clinically actionable tools that traditional single-node systems cannot feasibly produce.
cip_definition: Research focused on Acute Care Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven pedagogical frameworks for K-12 teacher education. A critical challenge in modern teacher preparation is designing instruction that equitably addresses the diverse cognitive, cultural, and linguistic needs of students while integrating emerging technologies. Current approaches often rely on static models of classroom interaction, which fail to account for the dynamic, multivariate nature of learning environments. To address this gap, we propose building a computational platform that simulates classroom ecosystems through agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML). The ABM component will parameterize student agents using empirical data on learning behaviors, developmental stages, and sociocultural contexts, while ML algorithms will analyze real-world classroom interaction datasets to identify patterns in teacher responsiveness and student engagement. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to thousands of virtual classrooms, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios across demographic variables, instructional strategies, and technology integration models. The computational outputs will inform the design of a teacher training module focused on adaptive decision-making, with an emphasis on culturally sustaining practices and AI-augmented teaching tools. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated classroom interaction data, (2) evidence-based guidelines for embedding computational thinking into teacher education curricula, and (3) predictive models linking specific teaching strategies to equity-oriented learning outcomes. By bridging computational analytics with pedagogical theory, this work aims to equip educators with dynamic, scalable tools to navigate the complexities of 21st-century classrooms, ultimately contributing to more personalized and inclusive educational experiences.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education that prepares individuals to be effective educators or trainers. Includes instruction in school reform and design; arts and technology in the classroom; theories of teaching and learning; adult and adolescent development; race, class, and gender dynamics; and the history and future of education in America.

abstract: This project seeks to advance teacher professional development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize adaptive learning environments for diverse classroom scenarios. A critical challenge in teacher education is preparing educators to design instruction that responds dynamically to variations in student needs, cultural contexts, and resource constraints. Traditional training methods often rely on static case studies or limited live simulations, which lack the scalability and granularity needed to explore complex, real-time decision-making processes. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates multidimensional classroom interactions, integrating variables such as student prior knowledge, engagement patterns, language barriers, and differentiated pedagogical strategies. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to replicate student-teacher dynamics, using empirical data from classroom observations and anonymized student performance metrics to parameterize agents. Machine learning techniques, including reinforcement learning, will then be applied to iteratively refine instructional strategies within these simulations. HPC resources are essential to support large-scale parallelization of simulations across diverse demographic and socioeconomic contexts, enabling the exploration of "what-if" scenarios at a resolution impractical on standard computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated suite of simulation tools for training pre-service and in-service teachers in adaptive pedagogy, (2) data-driven insights into high-impact teaching practices under resource-limited conditions, and (3) open-source visualization modules demonstrating optimal decision pathways for common classroom challenges. By bridging computational modeling with teacher education, this work aims to create scalable, evidence-based professional development resources that enhance instructional equity and effectiveness across heterogeneous learning environments.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale literary corpora, advancing methodological innovations in computational literary studies. While traditional close reading remains foundational to literary analysis, the scale and complexity of available digitized texts—spanning centuries, genres, and cultural contexts—present challenges for manual examination. This research addresses the need for scalable, systematic approaches to identify macro-level patterns in literary production, such as shifts in narrative structure, thematic recurrence, or stylistic evolution across time. The primary computational focus involves developing and refining natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to process and analyze heterogeneous literary datasets, including novels, poetry, and drama from the 18th century to the present. Key tasks include training transformer-based models for context-aware semantic analysis, implementing graph-based algorithms to map intertextual networks, and applying unsupervised clustering techniques to detect latent stylistic or thematic groupings. A pilot study on 19th-century British novels demonstrated preliminary success in tracing the diffusion of Gothic tropes, but scaling this to multi-genre, transnational corpora requires HPC capabilities for distributed storage, parallel processing, and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include (1) a reusable computational framework for diachronic literary analysis, (2) empirical insights into genre hybridity and canon formation, and (3) public datasets annotated with computational metadata to support reproducibility. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to bridge methodological divides in literary scholarship, offering new tools to interrogate the relationships between form, content, and cultural change at scale. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale text collections, reduce runtime for iterative model training, and facilitate high-dimensional visualization of literary networks—tasks infeasible on standard institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on literature from one or more genres, cultures or traditions. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, and studies of various types of literary text.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the detection and classification of precancerous and malignant cellular anomalies in cytological samples, addressing critical bottlenecks in manual screening processes. Current cytotechnological methods rely heavily on labor-intensive microscopic evaluation by trained professionals, which can lead to variability in diagnostic accuracy, particularly in early-stage or borderline cases. To mitigate these challenges, we propose a machine learning-driven approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze high-resolution digitized cytology slides. The research will focus on creating deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs), trained on multi-institutional datasets of cervical, thyroid, and urinary tract cytology samples. These models will be optimized to identify subtle cellular and nuclear features—such as hyperchromasia, chromatin patterns, and nuclear membrane irregularities—that correlate with dysplastic or malignant transformations. Computational workflows will include preprocessing pipelines for stain normalization and artifact removal, followed by multi-scale feature extraction and ensemble classification. HPC resources are essential to manage the terabyte-scale image datasets, accelerate model training through parallelized GPU computing, and validate results against gold-standard pathologist annotations. Successfully validating these models is expected to yield three outcomes: (1) a reproducible open-source tool for augmenting cytotechnologists’ workflow by prioritizing high-risk cases, (2) quantitative benchmarks linking computational predictions to diagnostic confidence metrics, and (3) insights into understudied morphological precursors of malignancy. By integrating computational pathology with traditional cytotechnology, this work aims to reduce diagnostic turnaround times, improve inter-observer consistency, and ultimately support earlier intervention for patients with neoplastic diseases. The scalability of the proposed methods will also provide a foundation for adapting the framework to other cytological subfields.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work with pathologists to detect changes in body cells that may indicate, and permit diagnosis of, the early development of cancers and other diseases. Includes instruction in biochemistry, microbiology, applied mathematics, microscopy, slide preparation, identification of cellular structures and abnormalities, and laboratory procedures and safety.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the biomechanical interactions between barbering tools and human tissue, with the goal of reducing occupational injuries and improving ergonomic tool design. Barbers experience disproportionately high rates of musculoskeletal disorders due to repetitive motions, static postures, and suboptimal tool ergonomics, yet current solutions remain anecdotal rather than data-driven. The project will develop computational simulations of hand-tool-tissue dynamics during common barbering tasks (e.g., precision scissor work, razor shaving) using finite element analysis and multibody dynamics frameworks. High-resolution 3D models of tools, hands, and facial/neck anatomy will be constructed from MRI and motion-capture data, incorporating material properties of skin, muscle, and hair. HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across tool geometries, grip angles, and force profiles to quantify tissue stress distributions and joint loading patterns under varying conditions. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal tool modifications and handling techniques to minimize biomechanical strain. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking tool design to injury risk, (2) prototype specifications for ergonomic tools tailored to diverse hand morphologies, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for technique adjustments. By bridging barbering practice with computational biomechanics, this work addresses a critical gap in vocational health research while demonstrating how HPC can advance safety and innovation in non-traditional technical fields. The resulting frameworks may also inform tool design paradigms for other manual professions lacking quantitative ergonomic standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to shave and trim facial/neck hair and beards, cut and dress hair, fit hairpieces, give facial and scalp massages, apply cosmetic treatments, and to prepare for licensure as professional barbers at various levels.  Includes instruction in facial shaving; beard and mustache shaping and trimming; shampooing; hair cutting; hair styles and styling art; facial treatments and massage; chemical applications; hair and scalp anatomy and physiology; hairpiece and toupee fitting; equipment operation; health and safety; customer service; and shop business practices.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) represent a critical public health challenge, with treatment outcomes often hindered by the complex interplay of genetic, neurobiological, and socioenvironmental factors. Current approaches to predicting treatment response and optimizing intervention strategies lack the computational power to integrate multi-dimensional datasets, limiting personalized care. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that bridge these gaps, enhancing precision in addiction counseling. We propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze large-scale datasets, including genomic data, electronic health records, and real-time behavioral data from wearable devices. ML algorithms will identify biomarkers and psychosocial predictors of treatment adherence and relapse, while ABM simulations will model population-level dynamics of substance use spread and recovery within social networks. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-resolution neuroimaging data, running parallelized simulations of intervention scenarios, and training deep learning models on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel risk stratification profiles, optimized intervention timing strategies, and dynamic models of counselor-client interactions that improve therapeutic outcomes. By integrating computational psychiatry with clinical counseling frameworks, this research will provide actionable insights for tailoring evidence-based interventions, training counselors in data-informed decision-making, and allocating community resources efficiently. The project aligns with the program’s mission to advance addiction science through interdisciplinary innovation, directly contributing to reduced relapse rates and enhanced quality of life for individuals and families affected by SUDs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: Wilderness medicine addresses critical challenges in delivering healthcare under environmental stressors with limited resources, such as extreme temperatures, altitude, or isolation. A significant gap exists in predicting patient deterioration or optimizing interventions in these dynamic settings, where environmental factors directly interact with physiological responses. This project proposes to develop computational models of human physiology under environmental stress to simulate clinical scenarios, predict outcomes, and inform evidence-based protocols for austere care. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the complexity of these models, which integrate real-world environmental data, multi-scale physiological systems, and stochastic resource constraints. The research will first aggregate and analyze existing clinical datasets from wilderness and disaster settings to identify key variables influencing outcomes. Agent-based modeling and finite element analysis will then simulate interactions between environmental parameters (e.g., hypothermia, hypoxia) and patient-specific factors (e.g., comorbidities, injuries). Machine learning approaches will optimize model accuracy by training on outcomes from field case reports and controlled experimental data. Finally, Monte Carlo methods will evaluate the robustness of proposed treatment strategies across variable resource availability and environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide triage, intervention timing, and resource allocation in austere environments, as well as generalized frameworks for adapting clinical guidelines to novel environmental insults. This work will directly support the development of scalable, context-specific protocols for wilderness medicine practitioners, from prehospital providers to disaster response teams. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process high-dimensional data and run computationally intensive simulations, the project aims to reduce preventable morbidity in resource-limited settings while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of clinical medicine and environmental systems modeling.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: Health professions education faces increasing demands to optimize training strategies that balance clinical competency, adaptive learning, and equitable outcomes across diverse populations. Current approaches to curriculum design and evaluation often rely on limited datasets or simplified models that inadequately capture the complexity of clinical learning environments, interprofessional dynamics, and longitudinal skill development. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets and simulate large-scale training scenarios. The research will integrate anonymized student performance metrics, clinical simulation logs, preceptor evaluations, and demographic data from a multi-institutional consortium of health professions programs. Machine learning models will be developed to predict trajectories of clinical reasoning development, identify hidden biases in assessment tools, and simulate the impact of adaptive curricula on learner outcomes under variable resource constraints. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing to analyze qualitative feedback, graph-based algorithms to map interprofessional collaboration patterns, and agent-based modeling to test interventions in virtual clinical training ecosystems. The project requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize iterative model training, and run high-fidelity simulations of educational scenarios involving thousands of virtual learners and instructors. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for optimizing competency-based curricula, evidence-based strategies to reduce disparities in clinical skill acquisition, and open-source tools for simulating health professions education systems. These computational advances will empower educators to make data-driven decisions in curriculum design, resource allocation, and adaptive assessment strategies at scale, ultimately strengthening the pipeline of clinical educators equipped to address evolving healthcare challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on education and administration leadership skills for clinical educators across health professions and specialties. Includes instruction in academic leadership, assessment, clinical decision making, curriculum development, ethics, primary care education, program evaluation, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of dynamic resource optimization in large-scale, multi-venue event ecosystems using computational modeling and simulation. While traditional event planning relies on static schedules and heuristic vendor allocation, modern hybrid and decentralized events—such as conferences spanning physical venues, virtual platforms, and satellite hubs—require real-time coordination of interdependent variables, including attendee flow, vendor capacity, energy consumption, and emergency response logistics. The project will develop a high-fidelity agent-based model (ABM) integrated with stochastic optimization algorithms to simulate scenarios involving 50,000+ concurrent participants across heterogeneous event nodes. The computational approach combines graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal dependencies between venues, Monte Carlo methods to assess risk propagation in supply chain disruptions, and reinforcement learning to optimize vendor routing under capacity constraints. High-performance computing resources are critical for parameter sensitivity analysis across 10^6 possible configurations and real-time scenario testing during model training. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of recommending adaptive resource allocation strategies that reduce operational costs by 15-25% in simulated events while maintaining attendee satisfaction metrics. The framework will also quantify cascading failure risks in event ecosystems—a novel contribution to hospitality risk management literature. By bridging computational social science with event operations, this work establishes a methodological foundation for data-driven resilience planning in an industry increasingly shaped by complex, technology-mediated participant experiences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, budget, and implement conferences, meetings, and other special events in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in principles of meeting and event planning; special event management; budgets and finance; site selection; contracts, vendors, and negotiations; marketing and promotions; food and beverage management; audio-visual basics and meeting technology; and hospitality law.

abstract: Aerospace systems operating in hypersonic regimes face extreme aerothermal loads that challenge conventional design methodologies, particularly in predicting coupled fluid-thermal-structural behavior. Current simulations often rely on simplified models or decoupled analyses, limiting their ability to resolve the multiscale, multiphysics interactions inherent in high-speed flows. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework for coupled aerothermal-structural analysis, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage large-eddy simulation (LES) for turbulence modeling, coupled with finite element methods (FEM) for transient thermal-structural response, to simulate hypersonic flow over deformable vehicle surfaces. These simulations will resolve boundary layer transitions, shock-wave interactions, and material ablation phenomena at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. The computational approach requires distributed-memory parallelism and GPU-accelerated solvers to manage the high dimensionality of the problem, with meshes exceeding 100 million cells and iterative solver stability across tightly coupled physics domains. Validation will utilize experimental data from wind tunnel tests and prior flight campaigns. The outcomes aim to advance predictive capabilities for thermal protection system (TPS) design, reduce reliance on costly physical testing, and inform material selection for next-generation reusable hypersonic vehicles. By quantifying the interplay between aerodynamic heating, structural deformation, and material degradation, this work will directly support the development of safer, more efficient aerospace systems capable of sustained operation in extreme environments. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieve the necessary scale and fidelity, as local computing infrastructure cannot support the memory and processing demands of these multidisciplinary simulations.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing aircraft, spacecraft and their systems. Includes instruction in aircraft/spacecraft systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The development of efficient hydrocarbon recovery strategies in complex reservoirs requires high-fidelity simulations to address subsurface heterogeneities, multiphase flow dynamics, and coupled thermal-hydro-mechanical processes. Conventional reservoir modeling approaches often rely on coarse grid resolutions or simplified physics due to computational limitations, leading to inaccuracies in predicting fluid behavior and optimizing extraction processes. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance reservoir simulation capabilities through large-scale, three-dimensional modeling of fractured unconventional reservoirs with dynamic fracture propagation and multiphase flow interactions. The research will employ parallelized finite element methods coupled with discrete fracture network models to resolve fine-scale features, including stress-dependent fracture apertures, proppant transport, and non-Darcy flow effects. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to calibrate model parameters using historical production data and microseismic monitoring results, enabling adaptive grid refinement in critical regions. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory architectures to simulate reservoir domains exceeding 10^8 grid cells, capturing high-resolution interactions between hydraulic fractures, natural fracture networks, and matrix permeability. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize fracture spacing, fluid injection schedules, and well placement under geomechanical constraints, directly addressing challenges in enhancing recovery rates in low-permeability shale and tight oil reservoirs. The results will provide novel insights into the role of fracture connectivity and stress shadowing on long-term production performance, with applications to sustainable reservoir management and reduced environmental footprint. By utilizing HPC resources, this work aims to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale experimental data and field-scale operational decision-making, offering a computational framework to maximize hydrocarbon recovery while minimizing water usage and greenhouse gas emissions associated with hydraulic fracturing operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for locating, extracting, processing and refining crude petroleum and natural gas, including prospecting instruments and equipment, mining and drilling systems, processing and refining systems and facilities, storage facilities, transportation systems, and related environmental and safety systems.

abstract: Forensic pathology faces growing challenges in synthesizing complex, multi-modal datasets to resolve ambiguous causes of death and support legal accountability. Current workflows for integrating histopathology, toxicology, genetic analyses, and crime scene reconstructions rely on manual correlation, which is time-intensive, prone to human error, and ill-suited for large-scale data. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to automate and enhance the analysis of forensic evidence through high-performance computing (HPC). The primary research problem involves creating predictive models that reconcile heterogeneous data—such as 3D postmortem imaging, mass spectrometry outputs, and genomic sequences—to identify subtle patterns indicative of trauma, poisoning, or natural disease. A hybrid machine learning approach will be employed, combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image-based feature extraction (e.g., tissue injury quantification in autopsy photographs) with graph-based algorithms to map temporal and spatial relationships in crime scene data. Natural language processing (NLP) tools will parse autopsy reports and legal documents to extract contextual variables for model training. These components will be integrated into an HPC-optimized pipeline using parallelized workflows (MPI and CUDA) to manage terabyte-scale datasets. The project will validate the framework using retrospective cases with known ground truths, assessing accuracy gains over conventional methods. Anticipated outcomes include a reproducible, open-source platform for forensic data fusion, capable of identifying latent biomarkers (e.g., gene-environment interactions in drug-related deaths) and generating probabilistic reports to clarify pathologists’ legal testimony. By enabling rapid, evidence-based reconciliation of conflicting findings, this work aims to reduce diagnostic uncertainties in high-stakes forensic investigations and strengthen the scientific rigor of death certification processes in public health systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on the performance of medical autopsies, the analysis of human remains and crime scenes, and the legal follow-up and responsibilities of public pathologists.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biochemical and genetic data in the diagnosis of inherited metabolic disorders presents a critical challenge in clinical biochemical genetics. Current methods for interpreting multi-omics datasets—including metabolomic, proteomic, and genomic profiles—often lack the computational power to integrate heterogeneous data streams or model dynamic biochemical pathways at scale. This limitation hinders the identification of novel biomarkers, the prediction of variant pathogenicity in enzymes and transporters, and the personalization of therapeutic strategies. To address this, we propose a computational project leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of metabolic dysfunction in rare genetic diseases. The research will focus on three aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to integrate multi-omics data and prioritize pathogenic variants disrupting metabolic networks, (2) simulating enzyme kinetics and substrate flux alterations using genome-scale metabolic models parameterized with patient-derived data, and (3) establishing a cloud-accessible platform for real-time analysis of biochemical assays linked to genetic findings. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of molecular dynamics simulations to assess structural impacts of missense variants on enzyme function, as well as Bayesian inference methods to quantify uncertainty in pathway predictions. The computational workflows will be validated against clinical datasets from 500 patients with confirmed or suspected inborn errors of metabolism. Expected outcomes include improved classification of variants of uncertain significance, dynamic models linking genotype to biochemical phenotype in disorders such as mitochondrial diseases and lysosomal storage disorders, and open-source tools for clinical laboratories to interpret complex datasets. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy, refine therapeutic monitoring, and inform the development of targeted metabolic interventions, bridging gaps between computational innovation and clinical application in the management of genetic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to perform and interpret biochemical analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases, and to serve as a consultant regarding laboratory diagnosis of a broad range of inherited disorders.

abstract: The increasing complexity of human-technology interactions necessitates computational frameworks capable of modeling diverse behavioral patterns and societal impacts. Current systems often fail to account for the dynamic interplay between individual cognitive processes, cultural contexts, and adaptive interface requirements, resulting in technologies that may perpetuate accessibility barriers or unintended social consequences. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance simulation environment that integrates cognitive modeling, machine learning, and large-scale user behavior analysis. Leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, we will implement agent-based models simulating 10,000+ heterogeneous users interacting with adaptive interfaces under varying sociotechnical conditions. These models incorporate cognitive architectures derived from experimental psychology data and real-world interaction logs from partnered assistive technology organizations. Concurrently, deep reinforcement learning pipelines will train interface adaptation policies on multimodal datasets encompassing eye-tracking, physiological signals, and interaction metadata. The computational demands of simultaneously running thousands of parallel simulations, processing terabyte-scale behavioral datasets, and optimizing neural networks with over 100 million parameters necessitate dedicated high-performance computing resources. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source framework for ethical interface personalization that respects cognitive diversity, 2) predictive models of technology adoption disparities across demographic groups, and 3) evidence-based design guidelines to mitigate emergent societal risks in AI-driven interaction systems. By bridging computational scalability with human-centered validation, this work aims to establish new methodologies for responsible innovation in human-computer interaction research.
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of the interaction between people and technology and how that technology impacts society, and combines disciplines within the fields of computing and information science (information systems, software engineering, artificial intelligence and design), engineering, and the behavior sciences (cognitive science, cognitive psychology, sociology, organizational psychology, and social psychology). Includes instruction in information technology, cognitive and behavioral sciences, and systems design.

abstract: This project seeks to advance computational photography techniques for commercial applications by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in processing ultra-high-resolution visual data. Commercial photography increasingly relies on workflows involving 4K/8K video, gigapixel image composites, and AI-driven post-processing, which demand intensive computational resources. Current consumer-grade systems struggle with processing latency, memory constraints, and scalability when handling multi-layered projects common in advertising, product visualization, and archival documentation. The research will develop optimized pipelines for neural rendering, real-time HDR fusion, and AI-assisted color grading using distributed computing frameworks. Key methodologies include parallelized processing of image stacks across GPU clusters, training domain-specific generative models for texture synthesis, and implementing physics-based light transport simulations to enhance digital scene reconstruction accuracy. The project will utilize containerized environments to standardize workflows while maintaining compatibility with industry-standard software suites. Outcomes aim to reduce render times for complex composites by 60-80%, enable interactive editing of 100+ layer projects, and improve fidelity in virtual product photography simulations. This work will directly benefit commercial photography education by creating open-source tools for managing computational workflows, while advancing research at the intersection of artistic practice and computational imaging. Successful implementation will demonstrate how HPC resources can democratize access to advanced digital production techniques typically limited to large studios, fostering innovation in visual storytelling for small-to-medium enterprises. The computational frameworks developed will be validated through case studies in automotive advertising photography and cultural heritage digitization, with performance benchmarks published to guide future resource allocation in arts computing initiatives.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences, and recording events and people, via digital, film, still and video photography. Includes instruction in specialized camera and equipment operation and maintenance, applications to commercial and industrial needs, and photography business operations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nursing care delivery and workforce optimization by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulation frameworks tailored to practical nursing contexts. Despite advancements in healthcare technology, nursing professionals—particularly in vocational and assistant roles—face persistent barriers in managing complex patient loads, preventing adverse events, and adapting to dynamic clinical environments. Current approaches to workforce planning and patient risk stratification often rely on static guidelines, which fail to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff skill mix, and resource availability. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to analyze multi-source clinical datasets, including electronic health records, staffing logs, and patient outcome metrics. HPC resources will enable large-scale training of ML algorithms to identify patterns predictive of patient deterioration or readmission risks, while ABM simulations will model nurse-patient interactions under varying staffing ratios and workflow conditions. The computational pipeline will process terabytes of structured and unstructured data, requiring parallelized workflows for feature extraction, model validation, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to prioritize at-risk patients for early intervention, (2) evidence-based staffing recommendations to balance clinical efficiency with nurse workload sustainability, and (3) open-source simulation platforms for nursing education programs to train students in resource-constrained decision-making. By quantifying relationships between nursing interventions and patient outcomes at unprecedented granularity, this research aims to inform policy reforms, optimize care delivery models, and reduce preventable complications in diverse healthcare settings. The scalability of these computational tools will support translational applications across nursing education and practice, ultimately enhancing both workforce preparedness and patient safety.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying stress-induced decision-making deficits through computational modeling of cortico-limbic circuit dynamics. While acute stress is known to impair prefrontal cortex (PFC) function and amplify amygdala activity, the precise spatiotemporal interactions between these regions during value-based decision tasks remain poorly quantified. We propose to develop biophysically detailed neural network models incorporating stress hormone dynamics, synaptic plasticity rules, and region-specific connectivity derived from primate and rodent tract-tracing studies. These models will simulate population-level activity across PFC subregions (e.g., dorsolateral vs. orbitofrontal cortex) and amygdala nuclei under varying stress intensities, using experimentally validated parameters from published electrophysiological and behavioral datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and run large-scale simulations capturing 1) millisecond-scale neural dynamics across >100,000 conductance-based neurons, 2) stochastic neurotransmitter release effects, and 3) long-term potentiation/depression processes over decision-making timescales. Parallelized parameter optimization will employ evolutionary algorithms to identify circuit configurations that reproduce empirical patterns of stress-induced choice biases. Resulting models will be analyzed through dimensionality reduction techniques to extract phase-space representations of decision trajectories. Expected outcomes include a computational taxonomy of stress effects on decision circuits, predictive models of behavioral vulnerability phenotypes, and openly shared simulation libraries for testing pharmacological interventions. This work addresses critical gaps in psychobiological theories of stress cognition while demonstrating how HPC-enabled neurocomputational approaches can advance mechanistic understanding of adaptive behavior. The requested resources will support 15,000+ core-hours for model exploration and 50TB of storage for raw simulation outputs and processed network analysis files.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the biological bases of behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the stability and transfer of heritable information in bacteriophage populations under environmental stress. While phage genomes are highly compact, their ability to rapidly acquire mutations or horizontally transferred genetic elements contributes to adaptability, yet the regulatory processes that balance genome stability with plasticity remain poorly understood. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze large-scale genomic datasets from phage populations subjected to mutagenic conditions (e.g., UV exposure, chemical mutagens) to identify conserved regulatory motifs and mutation hotspots. Computational models will simulate the dynamics of DNA replication and repair processes under varying stress intensities, integrating empirical data on mutation rates, recombination frequency, and gene expression. These simulations will employ parallelized algorithms to track probabilistic outcomes of replication errors and repair pathway efficacy across millions of simulated generations. Additionally, network analysis tools will map interactions between phage-encoded stability factors (e.g., terminases, integrases) and host machinery to pinpoint evolutionary constraints on genome architecture. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking specific genetic elements to mutation tolerance, insights into selective pressures driving horizontal gene transfer in viral populations, and mechanistic explanations for stress-induced genomic instability. This work will advance foundational knowledge in molecular genetics by elucidating how phage genomes maintain functional integrity despite rapid evolution, with broader implications for understanding genetic adaptation in pathogenic viruses. The scale of genomic data and complexity of stochastic modeling necessitate HPC resources to achieve statistically robust, high-resolution analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing industrial-scale additive manufacturing (AM) processes through advanced computational modeling and simulation. While AM technologies offer transformative potential for customized production and rapid prototyping, inconsistent part quality due to thermal stress, material anisotropy, and process parameter variability remains a significant barrier to reliable adoption. Current experimental approaches to parameter optimization are resource-intensive and lack the resolution needed to predict localized defects. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate coupled thermal-structural phenomena during metal powder bed fusion processes. The project will implement finite element analysis (FEA) at the macroscale, discrete element method (DEM) for powder dynamics, and phase-field modeling at the microstructural level, with adaptive meshing techniques to bridge scale-dependent interactions. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to identify defect-correlated process signatures and enable real-time parameter optimization. By utilizing parallel computing architectures, we aim to reduce simulation times for complex geometries by 60-70% compared to existing single-scale approaches, while achieving micron-scale resolution in critical regions. The resulting open-source computational toolkit will provide manufacturers with predictive capabilities to minimize post-processing and material waste, directly supporting sustainable manufacturing objectives. Successful implementation will advance fundamental understanding of multi-physics interactions in AM systems while delivering practical frameworks for quality assurance in aerospace tooling, medical device production, and other high-value applications. This work requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for machine learning integration and large-memory systems to handle multi-terabyte datasets from coupled simulations.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and development necessitates advanced computational tools to model molecular interactions, optimize pharmacokinetic properties, and predict therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address the challenge of identifying multi-target inhibitors for neurodegenerative diseases, where traditional experimental approaches are time-intensive and limited in exploring vast chemical and conformational spaces. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a hybrid computational strategy integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven virtual screening, and free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to systematically evaluate candidate molecules. The research will utilize GPU-accelerated MD simulations to characterize dynamic binding mechanisms of lead compounds with amyloid-beta and tau protein targets implicated in Alzheimer’s disease. Concurrently, an ensemble ML model trained on structural and physicochemical descriptors will screen a curated library of 1.2 million small molecules to prioritize candidates with optimal polypharmacological profiles. FEP workflows will then refine binding affinity predictions for top candidates, enabling atomistic resolution of ligand-target interactions. This computationally intensive pipeline requires parallelized processing of terabytes of simulation data, necessitating access to HPC clusters with high-memory nodes and scalable GPU architectures. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel dual-target inhibitors with enhanced blood-brain barrier permeability and reduced off-target effects, accelerating preclinical development. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated protein-ligand trajectories and ML models tailored for neurodegenerative drug discovery. By integrating computational biophysics and cheminformatics, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for rational polypharmacology design, directly addressing critical gaps in pharmaceutical sciences for complex neurological disorders.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_title: Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, and Administration, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in real-time data integration and analysis across heterogeneous medical devices within clinical office environments, a challenge exacerbated by proprietary software architectures and variable data formats. While modern medical offices rely on interconnected devices for diagnostics, monitoring, and record-keeping, latency and interoperability limitations often delay critical decision-making. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing an adaptive middleware framework optimized via high-performance computing (HPC) to enable seamless, low-latency data synthesis from diverse sources such as imaging systems, wearable sensors, and electronic health records (EHRs). The computational approach will involve parallelized data normalization algorithms to harmonize structured and unstructured inputs, coupled with machine learning models trained on simulated clinical workflows to predict and mitigate system bottlenecks. HPC resources will be critical for both training these models on large-scale synthetic datasets (emulating multi-device environments) and for deploying containerized microservices that dynamically allocate computational workloads based on real-time demand. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in data processing latency compared to existing commercial solutions, validated through benchmarking against simulated patient care scenarios. The project will further produce open-source modules for edge-device communication protocols, designed to comply with HIPAA security standards and adaptable to legacy systems. By enhancing the speed and reliability of cross-platform data integration, this work aims to improve clinical operational efficiency, reduce software maintenance costs, and support timely diagnostic interventions in resource-constrained medical offices. Success metrics will prioritize scalability across small-to-medium practices, with iterative feedback from partner clinics guiding usability refinements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply computer programming, troubleshooting, and information technology skills to the installation, maintenance, and upgrade of standard, customized, or proprietary medical software and associated hardware. Includes instruction in computer programming, systems analysis, networking, telecommunications, medical records and informatics software applications, information technology, systems administration, computer security, and applicable regulations and certifications or licenses.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize culturally-responsive pedagogical strategies for International Baccalaureate (IB) classrooms through advanced computational modeling of classroom dynamics. A critical challenge in international education is designing teaching practices that equitably engage students from diverse cultural, linguistic, and cognitive backgrounds. While qualitative studies have identified key principles of cross-cultural pedagogy, there remains a gap in systematically predicting how specific instructional choices interact with classroom heterogeneity to affect learning outcomes. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating student-teacher interactions in virtual IB classrooms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize thousands of agents with culturally variable traits (e.g., communication styles, prior knowledge frameworks) and test pedagogical interventions under diverse demographic configurations. The model will integrate empirical data from IB teacher surveys, student performance metrics, and classroom observation studies to ground agent behaviors in real-world patterns. Computational experiments will evaluate how variations in lesson pacing, multimodal instruction, and formative assessment strategies influence equitable participation and concept mastery across student subgroups. Sensitivity analyses will identify which cultural or developmental factors most significantly mediate instructional efficacy. Outcomes will inform a scalable framework for IB teacher training, highlighting adaptive practices that maximize inclusivity in heterogeneous classrooms. By leveraging HPC to simulate complex sociocognitive processes, this work bridges educational theory and practical implementation, offering data-driven insights to refine culturally attuned pedagogy. The resulting models and code will be shared as open-access resources for educators and researchers, fostering collaborative innovation in international teacher preparation.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach in schools that are implementing or proposing to implement the International Baccalaureate curriculum. Includes instruction in culturally-responsive classrooms, cross-cultural awareness, foundations of international education, human learning, human development, international teaching and learning, and pedagogy.

abstract: This project seeks to address gaps in understanding the evolution of Western polyphonic compositional practices between the 14th and 16th centuries by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale musical datasets. While historical musicology has traditionally relied on manual score analysis, the sheer volume of surviving manuscripts—coupled with complex intertextual relationships between works—has hindered systematic study of stylistic transitions, regional influences, and theoretical innovations. Our research will computationally process digitized musical corpora, including the Digital Image Archive of Medieval Music and the Josquin Research Project, using optical music recognition (OMR) adapted for early notation systems. Converted symbolic data will undergo feature extraction for harmonic progressions, contrapuntal patterns, and cadential structures through custom Python pipelines integrating music21 and librosa. Machine learning models (LSTMs, transformer networks) will then identify temporal and geographic patterns in compositional techniques, trained on metadata-rich subsets before scaling to full corpora. HPC resources are critical for managing storage demands (50+ TB of high-resolution manuscript images), parallel processing of OMR workflows, and training complex models across thousands of scores. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of analyzed works, quantitative maps of stylistic diffusion across Europe, and detection of previously unrecognized theoretical treatise influences on compositional practice. By bridging computational methods with musicological expertise, this work will enable novel insights into Renaissance musical networks while establishing reproducible frameworks for computational music analysis. Results will directly inform ongoing debates about the transmission of musical knowledge and the technological constraints shaping early modern composition.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical evolution of music as a social and intellectual phenomenon, the development of musical instruments and techniques, and the analysis and criticism of musical literature. Includes instruction in music history research methods, aesthetic analysis of musical compositions, history of musical writing and notation, the development of musical instruments, the development of music theory, and the study of specific periods, cultural traditions, styles, and themes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in optimizing microbial cell factories for sustainable bioproduction. Despite advances in synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, inefficiencies in pathway regulation, substrate utilization, and product toxicity often limit the yield and scalability of engineered microbial systems. Traditional experimental approaches to troubleshoot these bottlenecks are time-intensive and costly, particularly when exploring complex genotype-phenotype relationships or screening vast combinatorial libraries of genetic modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose an integrated computational pipeline combining genome-scale metabolic modeling (GEM), machine learning (ML)-guided strain optimization, and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. GEMs of target organisms (e.g., Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae) will be refined using constraint-based algorithms (e.g., flux balance analysis) to predict metabolic fluxes under varying genetic and environmental conditions. Parallelized ML models will iteratively identify optimal gene knockout/overexpression candidates and regulatory circuit designs by training on multi-omics datasets and prior experimental results. For critical enzymatic bottlenecks, MD simulations will probe structural dynamics and substrate-binding mechanisms to inform rational enzyme engineering. The computational workflow demands HPC capabilities to manage large-scale parameter sweeps, stochastic simulations of genetic circuits, and energy calculations for protein-ligand interactions. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-efficiency strain designs for producing biofuels, therapeutic proteins, and platform chemicals, validated through subsequent wet-lab experiments. This work will establish a scalable framework for in silico bioprocess optimization, reducing experimental trial-and-error while advancing fundamental understanding of microbial metabolism. The requested resources will directly support the development of open-source tools for the biotechnology community, enabling faster translation of lab-scale discoveries to industrial applications in renewable energy and biomanufacturing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of biologists and biotechnologists in research, industrial, and government settings. Includes instruction in fermentation technology, cell culturing, protein purification, biologic synthesis, assaying and testing, quality control, industrial microbiology, bioprocessing, chromatography and bioseparation, genetic technology, laboratory and hazardous materials safety, and computer applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address methodological challenges in analyzing large-scale, high-dimensional educational datasets, such as national assessment results and longitudinal student performance records, which are critical for evaluating educational interventions and policy impacts. Current approaches for modeling these data often rely on simplified statistical assumptions or underspecified computational models, limiting their ability to account for complex interactions, non-linear trajectories, and nested data structures inherent in educational systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing and validating a suite of computationally intensive methods, including Bayesian hierarchical models with adaptive shrinkage priors, ensemble machine learning techniques for causal inference, and high-dimensional optimization algorithms for latent variable modeling. These methods will be applied to investigate how multi-level factors—such as classroom practices, district-level resource allocation, and socioeconomic covariates—interact to influence disparities in STEM achievement outcomes across diverse student populations. The computational demands of this work necessitate high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the scale of datasets (millions of observations with thousands of features), the need for parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling across hundreds of nodes, and iterative cross-validation procedures for model comparison. Expected outcomes include (1) optimized open-source software tools for educational data science, implemented in R/Python with GPU acceleration support; (2) methodological advances in handling missing data and selection bias in quasi-experimental education research; and (3) evidence-based insights into scalable intervention strategies for reducing achievement gaps. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge the gap between modern computational statistics and applied education research, providing robust analytical frameworks that can inform equitable policy decisions while advancing the methodological rigor of quantitative educational research.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the analysis and solution of educational research problems, and the development of technical designs for research studies. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, research design, computer applications, instrument design, research methodologies, and applications to research problems in specific education subjects.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural evolution of U.S. constitutional jurisprudence through large-scale computational legal analytics. The core problem addressed is the lack of systematic, data-driven methodologies for mapping how doctrinal shifts in constitutional law emerge and propagate across judicial hierarchies and temporal scales. Traditional legal scholarship relies on manual case analysis, limiting the scope and granularity of insights into complex, system-wide patterns. This project proposes a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and temporal graph modeling to process over 250,000 federal and state court decisions spanning 1789–2023. Custom transformer-based models will be developed to classify legal reasoning patterns, detect citation network dynamics, and quantify semantic drift in key constitutional concepts (e.g., "due process," "equal protection"). The HPC environment is critical for training domain-specific legal language models, executing parallelized network simulations, and storing multidimensional embeddings of judicial discourse. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for identifying latent dependencies between Supreme Court doctrine and lower court adoption rates, 2) predictive models of jurisprudential change under varying sociolegal conditions, and 3) interactive visualizations of constitutional law’s conceptual topology. By bridging computational social science and legal theory, this work aims to establish new methodologies for studying law as a complex adaptive system, with implications for judicial education, policymaking, and public understanding of constitutional governance. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale legal text corpora, GPU-accelerated model training, and real-time simulation of hypothetical doctrinal scenarios—capabilities unfeasible without HPC infrastructure.
cip_title: American/ US Law/ Legal Studies/ Jurisprudence
cip_definition: An advanced, professional program of the U.S. legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning models that enhance the accessibility of STEM educational materials for K–12 students with visual impairments. Current methods for converting visual content (e.g., graphs, diagrams, spatial concepts) into tactile, auditory, or multimodal formats are labor-intensive and lack personalization, limiting equitable access to complex curricula. The research problem centers on addressing the computational demands of automating the adaptation of visual materials into accessible formats while tailoring outputs to individual learners’ needs. Proposed work includes training multimodal neural networks on datasets of tactile graphics, Braille annotations, and user interaction logs to predict optimal adaptations of visual content. Computational workflows will integrate computer vision for analyzing source materials, natural language processing for generating contextual descriptions, and reinforcement learning to refine outputs based on simulated student feedback. HPC resources are critical for scaling model training across diverse educational content types (e.g., mathematics, biology diagrams) and iterating on hyperparameters to balance accuracy, latency, and interpretability. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for educators to rapidly generate customized accessible materials, reducing the preparation burden on teachers of students with visual impairments. The project also aims to publish benchmark datasets and validation metrics for evaluating AI-generated adaptations against human-expert standards. By accelerating the creation of tailored, high-quality accessible resources, this work has the potential to improve engagement and learning outcomes for students with visual disabilities while advancing computational applications in specialized teacher education.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Vision Impairments Including Blindness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with visual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with visual impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising blind or visually handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing high-fidelity virtual cinematography environments, addressing the growing demand for scalable, real-time rendering solutions in film production. Traditional methods for creating complex visual scenes—particularly those involving dynamic lighting, particle effects, and physics-based interactions—are computationally prohibitive for low-budget or independent filmmakers, limiting creative experimentation. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize rendering workflows, train machine learning models for adaptive scene optimization, and simulate photorealistic environments at resolutions up to 8K. The research will employ a hybrid approach: (1) using distributed rendering frameworks to process large-scale scene datasets across GPU clusters, reducing latency in preview generation; (2) implementing neural networks to predict lighting and texture outcomes under variable parameters, enabling rapid iterative design; and (3) integrating fluid dynamics and rigid-body simulations to automate physically accurate visual effects, such as smoke or debris interactions. By decentralizing computationally intensive tasks to HPC infrastructure, this project aims to democratize access to advanced cinematographic tools, allowing creators to prototype scenes in near real-time without sacrificing artistic intent. Expected outcomes include open-source software modules for optimized asset management, a benchmark dataset for training domain-specific AI models, and case studies demonstrating reduced production timelines for short films. The work bridges gaps between computational imaging research and applied media arts, offering scalable solutions that could redefine workflows in both academic training and industry practice. Results will be disseminated through film festivals, conferences on media technology, and partnerships with independent studios to evaluate real-world efficacy.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to communicate dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through the making and producing of films and videos. Includes instruction in theory of film, film technology and equipment operation, film production, film directing, film editing, cinematographic art, film audio, techniques for making specific types of films and/or videos, media technologies, computer image making, multi-media production, and the planning and management of film/video operations.

abstract: Soil microbiomes play a critical role in agricultural productivity through nutrient cycling, plant-microbe interactions, and resilience to environmental stressors. However, predicting and managing these complex microbial communities remains challenging due to the scale of genomic diversity, nonlinear dynamics of microbial networks, and context-dependent responses to soil management practices. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of soil microbial community assembly and function under varying agricultural management regimes. We will integrate genome-resolved metagenomics, biogeochemical data, and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial interactions at micrometer-to-meter scales across soil matrices. Computational workflows will include (1) large-scale metagenomic assembly and annotation of soil microbiomes from long-read sequencing data, (2) dynamic flux balance analysis to predict metabolic interactions in rhizosphere communities, and (3) spatially explicit simulations of microbial dispersal and nutrient exchange in soil aggregates. These analyses require parallelized processing of multi-terabyte sequencing datasets, iterative optimization of genome-scale metabolic models, and high-resolution 3D simulations of soil microenvironments—tasks infeasible without dedicated HPC infrastructure. The resulting models will be validated against experimental data from controlled mesocosm studies and field trials evaluating cover cropping, tillage, and organic amendment strategies. By resolving how management practices alter microbial functional traits and community stability, this work will advance our ability to design soil health interventions that optimize crop productivity while reducing synthetic fertilizer inputs. The computational frameworks developed will provide scalable tools for linking microbial ecology to agroecosystem outcomes, addressing a critical gap in sustainable agriculture research. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the project’s goal of translating soil microbiome complexity into actionable management principles for agricultural systems.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on application of microbiological theory and methods to the study of the organismic properties of soils, soil-plant and soil-animal interactions, and the biological components and effects of soil management strategies. Includes instruction in microbiology and related biological sciences, applicable animal and plant sciences, soil chemistry and physics as related to biological characteristics, and environmental science.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the long-term evolution of political decision-making patterns and their relationship to historical crises through the computational analysis of multi-century, cross-regional archival datasets. Combining methods from computational history, network science, and political institutionalism, we propose to analyze structured records of legislative votes, treaty formations, and policy responses to environmental/economic shocks across three geopolitical regions (Europe, Southeast Asia, and South America) from 1600–1950. The central research problem addresses how path dependencies in governance systems emerge from crisis responses, and whether these patterns exhibit measurable similarities across distinct cultural-historical contexts. Current manual historiography struggles to systematically compare such complex, longitudinal processes, particularly when analyzing interactions between formal institutions and informal power networks. Our computational approach employs transformer-based language models fine-tuned on multilingual historical documents to extract structured event data, coupled with temporal network analysis to model institutional relationships.
