Key innovations include the development of a novel graph neural network architecture capable of processing temporally discontinuous historical records and a counterfactual simulation framework for testing institutional resilience hypotheses. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage three core challenges: 1) processing over 15 million pages of digitized primary sources across six languages, 2) training multi-modal models that integrate textual, spatial, and socioeconomic data, and 3) running ensemble simulations of political system evolution under varying historical constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-access knowledge graph tracing institutional adaptations across case studies, quantitative frameworks for assessing historical contingency in political development, and methodological advances in computational historical analysis. This work aims to provide policymakers and historians with new analytical tools for understanding the systemic impacts of crisis responses while establishing computational social science infrastructure for transhistorical comparative research.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of history and political science or a specialization which draws from history and political science. Includes instruction in comparative government and politics, historiography, historical research methods, political science, political theory, records administration, and systematic study of political institutions and behavior.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of task allocation and workflow efficiency in clerical environments through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on mitigating cognitive and ergonomic strain in hybrid office settings. As organizations increasingly adopt digital tools and hybrid work models, clerical workers face fragmented workflows, uneven task loads, and poorly integrated human-technology interfaces, leading to productivity loss and increased occupational health risks. Current studies lack granular simulations of how micro-level decisions—such as document routing prioritization, interruptive task management, and ergonomic workspace configurations—collectively impact operational outcomes. The project will develop an agent-based model integrating behavioral data from motion capture studies, productivity logs, and environmental sensors to simulate clerical ecosystems at unprecedented resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multimodal datasets spanning 12+ months of observational data from participating organizations, train machine learning classifiers for real-time task complexity estimation, and run parallelized simulations testing 50,000+ workflow permutations. Computational experiments will evaluate interventions including dynamic task redistribution algorithms, adaptive interface designs, and posture-aware scheduling systems. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for balancing efficiency metrics with physiological strain indicators, validated against biometric wearables data from 150 clerical workers. Results will inform the development of open-source tools for small-to-medium enterprises to optimize administrative ecosystems without specialized HR infrastructure. By bridging operations research, occupational health, and human-computer interaction, this work addresses a critical gap in evidence-based strategies for sustainable clerical work design in digitally transformed environments.
cip_title: General Office Occupations and Clerical Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide basic administrative support under the supervision of office managers, administrative assistants, secretaries, and other office personnel. Includes instruction in typing, keyboarding, filing, general business correspondence, office equipment operation, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive, high-dimensional data visualization framework to address the challenge of interpreting complex, heterogeneous datasets emerging from cross-domain scientific collaborations. As interdisciplinary research increasingly integrates diverse data types—from spatially resolved environmental sensor streams to temporally dynamic genomic or social network data—existing visualization tools struggle to balance computational efficiency with perceptual effectiveness. Our work focuses on creating a scalable pipeline that couples topological data analysis with perceptually optimized rendering, enabling researchers to identify latent patterns across disparate data modalities. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated dimension reduction algorithms, dynamic graph processing, and cognitive load-aware visual encoding strategies, all orchestrated through a distributed workflow manager. High-performance computing resources will be critical for three components: (1) parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets using persistent homology calculations to extract multi-scale features, (2) real-time rendering of 3D/4D visualizations with adaptive level-of-detail adjustments based on user interaction patterns, and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of visual parameter spaces through large-scale A/B testing of perceptual efficacy. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that reduces interpretative bias in multidisciplinary science by maintaining mathematical rigor while respecting human visual cognition constraints. The resource will be validated through case studies in climate-epidemiology modeling and materials science-biointerface research, where it will enable discovery of cross-domain correlations previously obscured by disciplinary visualization conventions. This work bridges gaps between computational topology, perceptual psychology, and domain sciences, advancing the capacity for visual analytics to drive convergence research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and derive meaning from data by using visual presentation tools and techniques. Includes instruction in cognitive science, computer programming, data management, data visualization theory, graphic design, infographics, perceptual psychology, statistics, and visual design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive educational tools and intervention strategies for students with multiple disabilities. Current approaches to designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual analysis of behavioral, sensory, and academic data, which limits the scalability and personalization of interventions for learners with complex, co-occurring needs. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing multimodal datasets—such as eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and communication device logs—to model student engagement and predict optimal instructional pathways. The project will employ machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, to analyze heterogeneous data streams from classroom observations and assistive technology use. These models will be trained to identify patterns in student responsiveness to specific interventions, accounting for variables like sensory processing profiles, motor limitations, and communication modalities. By parallelizing large-scale simulations of hypothetical IEP scenarios on HPC clusters, the team will iteratively refine adaptive learning algorithms that dynamically adjust content delivery, pacing, and sensory supports. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational framework for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated through collaboration with special education teachers. This framework aims to reduce trial-and-error in intervention design while maintaining alignment with legal and pedagogical requirements for students with multiple disabilities. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume (estimated at 50+ TB of annotated video and sensor data) and enabling real-time analysis during classroom pilot studies. Successful implementation could transform how educators individualize instruction for this population, bridging gaps between assistive technology innovation and practical teaching workflows.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between social network structures and demographic behaviors using large-scale computational simulations. The research problem centers on understanding how evolving social ties—such as kinship, friendship, and professional connections—influence population-level outcomes like migration patterns, fertility decisions, and household formation. Traditional survey-based methods struggle to capture the recursive feedback between individual agency and structural constraints at scale, particularly across heterogeneous populations. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) that simulates life-course decisions within dynamic, multi-layered social networks. The model will integrate demographic microdata, longitudinal social tie metrics, and empirically derived behavioral rules to explore emergent phenomena under varying policy and environmental scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the computational demands of simulating millions of interacting agents across decadal time horizons, while maintaining granular detail in network evolution and decision pathways. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallel processing for network topology updates, implementing adaptive sampling techniques for rare demographic events, and validating model outputs against census and panel study benchmarks. Expected outcomes include novel insights into how localized network disruptions (e.g., workforce automation, climate migration) propagate through social systems to alter demographic trajectories. The results will advance theoretical frameworks in computational sociology while providing actionable evidence for policymakers addressing population aging and spatial inequality. By open-sourcing the optimized ABM framework, this work will also create a reusable resource for studying complex social systems across disciplines.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sociology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Agricultural supply chains face growing challenges from market volatility, climate variability, and logistical inefficiencies, which complicate inventory management, procurement, and distribution for retailers and wholesalers. Traditional analytical tools struggle to integrate real-time data across spatial and temporal scales, limiting adaptive decision-making. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to model and optimize agricultural supply chain networks, with a focus on dynamic resource allocation under uncertainty. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate interactions among producers, distributors, retailers, and consumers, incorporating heterogeneous datasets such as historical sales, weather forecasts, transportation costs, and crop yield predictions. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to forecast regional demand fluctuations and supply disruptions, while mixed-integer linear programming techniques will optimize distribution routes and inventory thresholds. Computational workflows will leverage parallel processing to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, assessing trade-offs between cost, resilience, and sustainability metrics. By enabling granular, data-driven insights into procurement timing, warehouse placement, and pricing strategies, this project aims to reduce operational waste, minimize stockouts, and improve profit margins for agricultural suppliers. The resulting models will be validated against case studies from midwestern U.S. grain and livestock supply chains, with scalability assessments for global applications. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools for supply chain analytics and evidence-based policy recommendations to stabilize market access for small-scale agricultural retailers. This work bridges computational innovation with practical agribusiness management, advancing the resilience of agricultural economies in the face of compounding stressors.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale computational analysis of diachronic and synchronic variations in the Japanese language, with a focus on philological evolution, dialectal diversity, and sociolinguistic applications. A central challenge in Japanese linguistics lies in systematically tracing linguistic shifts across historical periods (Ancient, Medieval, Modern) and geographically dispersed dialects, processes that require parsing complex, non-standardized textual and audio datasets. Traditional manual methods struggle to manage the scale of corpora needed to robustly analyze morphological, syntactic, and semantic changes or to model dialectal continua across Japan’s regional speech communities. This project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models and phonetic alignment algorithms, to process digitized classical texts, modern regional speech recordings, and mixed-mode corpora spanning pre-modern to contemporary sources. Computational workflows will be designed to identify patterns in language change, quantify dialect boundaries using phonological and lexical features, and simulate contact-induced shifts in specialized contexts (e.g., technology-related terminology adoption). HPC resources are critical for training custom tokenizers for historical Japanese orthography, running parallelized analyses across multi-century text corpora, and processing high-resolution audio data for dialect mapping. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible diachronic corpus of annotated Japanese texts with computational linguistic metadata; (2) probabilistic models of regional dialect classification informed by sociogeographic variables; and (3) frameworks for predicting semantic drift in technical lexicon, with applications for cross-cultural communication and pedagogy. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this research aims to establish scalable methods for preserving linguistic heritage and addressing contemporary challenges in Japanese language standardization, education, and technology-driven lexical innovation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Japanese language. Includes instruction in philology; Ancient, Medieval, and Modern Japanese; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Aircraft armament systems represent a critical component of modern military operations, requiring precise integration of mechanical, electronic, and computational subsystems. However, current maintenance and operational protocols for these systems rely heavily on static schedules and reactive diagnostics, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation, unplanned downtime, and potential safety risks. This project proposes the development of a dynamic, data-driven predictive maintenance framework using high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize the lifecycle management of aircraft weapon systems. The research addresses the challenge of processing heterogeneous datasets—including real-time sensor telemetry, historical maintenance logs, environmental corrosion metrics, and component wear simulations—to predict failure modes and prioritize maintenance interventions. Computational methods will integrate machine learning models (e.g., graph neural networks to map interdependencies among subsystems) with physics-informed digital twins that simulate stress propagation in composite weapon materials under operational conditions. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate probabilistic failure scenarios across diverse climatic and operational contexts, as well as parallelized optimization algorithms to balance mission readiness with maintenance costs. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing unplanned maintenance events by 30–40%, extending component lifespans through corrosion-mitigation strategies, and improving safety compliance by identifying latent risks in aging armament systems. The project’s computational workflows will be designed for interoperability with existing military logistics platforms, ensuring direct applicability to operational environments. By bridging advanced analytics with domain-specific constraints of military technology, this work advances a novel paradigm for sustainment of critical defense infrastructure while aligning with emerging priorities in predictive operational analytics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of aircraft weapons systems and associated peripherals. Includes instruction in basic science and quantitative methods, computer science, electronics, engineering graphics, fluid power, heavy equipment operation, armament systems, weapon materials and processes, weapon safety, corrosion control, aircraft systems maintenance, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to advance teacher professional development by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the efficacy of adaptive instructional strategies in diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in teacher education is the lack of scalable, data-driven frameworks to evaluate how nuanced teaching behaviors—such as real-time feedback, differentiated instruction, and culturally responsive practices—impact student engagement and learning outcomes. Traditional observational studies are constrained by small sample sizes, manual coding, and limited generalizability. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate classroom dynamics under varied pedagogical strategies. Large-scale datasets of teacher-student interactions (video, audio, and text transcripts from K-12 classrooms) will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to identify behavioral patterns. These patterns will inform the parameterization of ABMs, which will simulate how modifications to teacher strategies propagate through student networks, affecting collective learning. HPC resources are essential to train deep learning models on multimodal data (requiring GPU-accelerated processing) and to run thousands of parallelized ABM iterations, enabling robust sensitivity analyses across demographic and contextual variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational framework linking specific teaching practices to equity-focused student outcomes, (2) open-access tools for teacher educators to visualize and test strategy adaptations in virtual environments, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for personalized professional development programs. By quantifying the systemic impacts of teaching methods at scale, this work aims to transform how teacher preparation programs design clinical training and support data-informed instructional decision-making.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Levels and Methods, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education and professional development, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the detection and analysis of fraudulent activities among government contractors and grantees, focusing on suspension and debarment investigations. Current investigative methods struggle to efficiently process the scale and complexity of multi-modal data—including financial records, procurement histories, legal documents, and communication logs—which often contain patterns indicative of fraud, collusion, or non-compliance. The research problem centers on creating scalable tools to identify hidden relationships, anomalies, and procedural deviations across heterogeneous datasets while adhering to legal and administrative constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will deploy machine learning models to analyze structured transactional data and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract actionable insights from unstructured text, such as contracts, emails, and audit reports. Graph-based algorithms will map networks of entities, subcontractors, and financial flows to detect collusion or money laundering schemes. Computational experiments will simulate decision pathways for administrative actions, incorporating jurisdictional rules and historical case outcomes to model equitable solutions. The proposed framework will also integrate privacy-preserving methods to handle sensitive data securely. Outcomes include a prototype system capable of flagging high-risk cases, prioritizing investigative leads, and quantifying evidence thresholds for administrative proceedings. By automating labor-intensive data triage and pattern recognition tasks, this work aims to reduce case resolution timelines, improve consistency in debarment decisions, and strengthen safeguards against systemic procurement risks. The scalability of the computational approach will be validated using anonymized case repositories from federal and state agencies, with results informing best practices for integrating advanced analytics into legally constrained investigative workflows. This project bridges gaps between forensic accounting, legal informatics, and public accountability, offering a model for data-driven oversight in non-procurement contexts.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques for investigating criminal behavior among government contractors and grantees at different levels. Includes instruction in financial fraud and money-laundering, auditing, computer investigations, legal concepts and applications, procurement law, non-procurement debarment, jurisdiction and lead agency, analytical methods, suspension, parallel proceedings, evidence protection, equitable considerations, investigative techniques, administrative and global solutions, case management and preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize automated defect detection and lifecycle management in building construction finishing processes. Current inspection practices rely heavily on manual assessments, which are time-consuming, subjective, and prone to human error, leading to costly delays and safety risks. To address this, we propose a machine learning-driven approach using high-resolution 3D scans, thermal imaging datasets, and real-time sensor data from construction sites. The core challenge lies in processing multi-modal data streams at scale to identify subtle material defects (e.g., cracks, moisture ingress, improper insulation) while accounting for dynamic environmental factors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep convolutional neural networks on terabyte-scale image datasets and running finite element analysis simulations to model defect propagation under varying stress conditions. Parallelized workflows will integrate computer vision algorithms for anomaly detection with probabilistic models to predict failure risks across building systems. A key innovation involves developing a digital twin platform that maps defect signatures to maintenance protocols, enabling proactive resource allocation for repairs. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline capable of reducing inspection time by 40-60% while improving defect classification accuracy to >95% compared to manual methods. The project will generate open-source tools for construction managers to prioritize high-risk zones in finishing workflows and extend asset lifespans. By bridging computational engineering with construction management, this work aims to establish new standards for data-driven quality control in the built environment, with potential applications in regulatory compliance and sustainable resource utilization.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Railway transportation systems face increasing demands for efficiency, safety, and sustainability, necessitating advanced computational tools to model complex operational dynamics. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing rail network operations under variable constraints, including fluctuating freight demand, heterogeneous traffic flows, and dynamic environmental conditions. The core research problem lies in resolving inefficiencies caused by conflicting priorities between freight scheduling, passenger service reliability, and infrastructure maintenance cycles. Current analytical methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors at scale, particularly when incorporating real-time sensor data from trackside IoT devices and onboard train systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and reinforcement learning algorithms. The framework will integrate historical operational data from Class I railroads with live telemetry streams to create adaptive decision-support tools for dispatchers and network planners. High-performance computing resources are essential for executing parallelized simulations of continental-scale rail networks, training deep neural networks on multimodal sensor data, and performing sensitivity analyses across probabilistic weather and demand scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for congestion mitigation, data-driven recommendations for capacity allocation, and quantitative safety assessments for novel routing protocols involving hazardous materials. By enabling near-real-time optimization of resource deployment across rail yards and mainline corridors, this research aims to reduce systemic delays by an estimated 12-18% in benchmark scenarios while maintaining compliance with Federal Railroad Administration safety standards. The computational infrastructure developed through this project will serve as a shared resource for subsequent studies in railway energy efficiency and automated inspection systems, fostering cross-institutional collaboration in transportation technology innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the operation of railroads and other aspects of the railway industry, including railroad and railyard service. Includes instruction in railway culture, operating skills, General Code of Operation rules, conductor service, signal systems, switching, transportation of hazardous materials, safety, and railway telecommunications systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize grooming protocols for domestic animals by modeling the biomechanical and physiological interactions between grooming tools, animal anatomy, and coat characteristics. Current grooming practices rely on generalized guidelines, which often fail to account for individual variations in species, breed-specific skin elasticity, fur density, or stress responses. The lack of data-driven, personalized protocols can lead to suboptimal outcomes, including skin irritation, incomplete coat maintenance, or undue animal stress. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate grooming processes across a diverse array of biological and tool-based parameters. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model tool-skin interactions under varying pressure, motion, and temperature conditions, while agent-based simulations will predict stress responses in animals based on physiological metrics such as heart rate variability and thermal regulation. Machine learning algorithms will integrate empirical data from veterinary studies, groomer-reported outcomes, and sensor-derived biometrics (collected via wearable devices during grooming sessions) to generate adaptive, breed-specific grooming recommendations. The computational pipeline will also evaluate the efficacy of novel grooming tool designs through virtual prototyping, reducing reliance on iterative physical testing. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of simulated grooming scenarios, predictive models for stress-minimized workflows, and evidence-based guidelines for tool selection and maintenance. By bridging computational biomechanics, ethology, and cosmetology, this work aims to advance animal welfare standards while supporting innovation in a historically practice-driven industry. The scale of multi-parametric simulations and real-time data assimilation necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve the resolution required for actionable insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide cosmetic services for household pets, show animals, work animals and animal athletes. Includes instruction in skin, coat, and pelt grooming and styling; skin care; hoof, nail, and claw care; animal massage; minor first aid and veterinary referral; animal grooming products and applications; health and safety; and applicable regulations.

abstract: Play therapy is a critical intervention for addressing childhood psychological and developmental challenges, yet the field lacks robust computational tools to quantify therapeutic interactions and predict outcomes. Current methods rely heavily on subjective observational coding, limiting scalability and reproducibility. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop machine learning models capable of analyzing multimodal play therapy datasets, including video recordings, physiological sensor data (e.g., heart rate variability), and therapist annotations. The primary research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in child-therapist interactions that correlate with clinical improvements, particularly in children with trauma-related disorders or neurodevelopmental conditions. The computational approach involves training transformer-based architectures on temporally aligned sequences of play behavior, vocal prosody, and physiological signals to model dyadic synchrony—a hypothesized mechanism of change in play therapy. Additionally, reinforcement learning frameworks will be tested to simulate personalized play scenarios for optimizing therapist decision-making. By processing petabytes of video and sensor data across diverse demographic groups, the HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale validation of these models while maintaining necessary privacy protections via federated learning protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational taxonomy of play therapy microprocesses, (2) predictive biomarkers of treatment response, and (3) open-source tools for real-time interaction analysis to guide therapist training. This work bridges developmental neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and clinical psychology, establishing a novel paradigm for data-driven refinement of play therapy protocols. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, secure data storage, and complex simulation workflows that exceed local computing capabilities, ultimately advancing evidence-based practices in this specialized mental health domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be a Registered Play Therapist (RPT) or a School Based-Registered Play Therapist (SB-RPT). Includes instruction in child development, theories of personality, psychotherapy, child and adolescent psychopathology, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the escalating complexity of regulatory ecosystems in compliance law, where traditional legal analysis struggles to keep pace with dynamic, high-volume, and interdependent policy frameworks. The research focuses on developing computational models to automate the identification of latent compliance risks, predict regulatory conflicts, and simulate the operational impacts of emerging legislation. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, we aim to process multilingual legal texts, supranational regulatory databases, and real-time legislative updates at scale. Key computational challenges include training domain-specific transformer models on heterogeneous legal corpora, constructing dynamic knowledge graphs to map cross-jurisdictional regulatory overlaps, and running agent-based simulations to stress-test organizational compliance protocols under hypothetical policy shifts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized processing of terabyte-scale legal datasets, iterative fine-tuning of deep learning architectures, and Monte Carlo simulations assessing risk propagation in multi-stakeholder compliance networks. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for compliance risk prediction, a framework for quantifying regulatory ambiguity in textual sources, and evidence-based recommendations for harmonizing conflicting compliance standards. This work bridges computational law and operational risk management, offering novel methodologies to enhance decision-making in corporate governance, regulatory technology (RegTech), and cross-border policy analysis. By formalizing the interaction between legal semantics and systemic risk, the project aims to advance computational literacy in compliance practice while establishing benchmarks for scalable, ethics-aware regulatory analytics.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate quantum many-body dynamics in strongly correlated fermionic systems using advanced computational methods. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding non-equilibrium behavior and thermalization processes in systems with high entanglement, which are inaccessible to analytical solutions or classical simulation techniques. The central challenge lies in simulating large-scale quantum systems with sufficient accuracy to resolve emergent phenomena, such as many-body localization and quantum phase transitions, which govern the interplay between disorder, interactions, and quantum coherence. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining tensor network algorithms—specifically matrix product states (MPS) and projected entangled pair states (PEPS)—with stochastic variational Monte Carlo methods. These techniques will be optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures to handle the exponential scaling of Hilbert space dimensions, enabling simulations of 2D lattices with up to 100 sites and long-time evolution under realistic interaction parameters. The computational workload will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for tensor contractions and parallel CPU clusters for stochastic sampling, with adaptive memory management to reduce overhead. Expected outcomes include the identification of universal signatures of thermalization in disordered fermionic systems, quantitative predictions of critical exponents near quantum phase transitions, and validation of proposed effective field theories. These results will provide foundational insights into the robustness of quantum coherence in engineered systems, with implications for quantum information science and the design of next-generation quantum simulators. The project’s success hinges on access to HPC resources capable of sustaining petascale operations, including multi-node GPU allocations and high-memory nodes for storing large tensors. By bridging theoretical predictions with numerical benchmarks, this work will advance the understanding of quantum matter and establish scalable computational protocols for future studies of complex quantum systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the theories that explain the fundamental structure of our world and the universe and which draws from physics and astronomy. Includes instruction in astronomy, calculus, cosmology, differential equations, electricity, magnetism, data analysis, physics, quantum mechanics, space science, spectroscopy, and thermal physics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize real-time adaptive control systems for distributed ecological monitoring networks, a niche intersecting environmental informatics, edge computing, and programmable sensor architectures. Current approaches struggle to balance high-frequency data assimilation from heterogeneous field devices (acoustic, visual, and chemical sensors) with dynamic resource constraints, leading to latency or data loss in critical environmental scenarios. We propose a hybrid computational architecture leveraging hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) to autonomously allocate processing tasks across edge nodes, fog layers, and cloud backends while maintaining strict energy budgets. The core innovation lies in training multi-objective HRL agents that simultaneously optimize data fidelity, transmission efficiency, and hardware longevity under fluctuating field conditions. High-performance computing resources are essential to simulate large-scale sensor networks (10,000+ nodes) across diverse ecological topologies, train ensemble models incorporating real-world noise profiles, and validate control policies against extreme event datasets (e.g., wildfire precursors, pollutant spills). Computational workflows will combine discrete-event simulations for network dynamics, PyTorch-based RL training with curriculum learning, and thermodynamic modeling of embedded system constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive environmental control systems, empirically validated scaling laws for edge-fog-cloud hierarchies in ecological applications, and novel convergence strategies for multi-agent RL in resource-constrained distributed systems. This work directly addresses interoperability challenges in the growing domain of environmental cyber-physical systems while advancing computational methods for autonomous resource allocation in non-stationary, real-world deployments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of general computer programming to the solution of specific operational problems and customization requirements presented by individual software users and organizational users. Includes training in specific types of software and its installation and maintenance.

abstract: Dental caries and periodontal diseases remain prevalent global health challenges, driven by complex microbial biofilm communities in the oral cavity. Traditional experimental approaches to studying these biofilms face limitations in resolving spatial-temporal dynamics, interspecies interactions, and substrate adhesion mechanisms at micron and sub-second scales. This project proposes a computational framework to model oral biofilm formation, structural evolution, and response to antimicrobial agents using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will employ hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to capture multiscale processes, from molecular-level interactions between bacterial adhesins and tooth enamel hydroxyapatite to population-level biofilm expansion under varying oral environments. The ABM component will integrate empirical data from microbial culturing assays to parameterize species-specific growth rates, metabolic cooperation, and quorum sensing behaviors, while MD simulations will elucidate atomic-scale binding affinities critical for early biofilm adhesion. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of parallelized simulations across thousands of microbial agents and billions of molecular interactions, particularly when modeling clinically relevant timeframes (24-72 hours) at high spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include identification of key molecular targets for disrupting biofilm initiation, predictive models of pH-dependent antimicrobial efficacy, and optimization of topical treatment delivery kinetics. These results will directly inform preclinical studies in caries prevention strategies and provide a computational platform for testing novel biomaterials in restorative dentistry. By bridging gaps between molecular mechanisms and ecological biofilm behavior, this work aims to advance personalized preventive dentistry frameworks while demonstrating how computational modeling can accelerate translational research in oral health.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in dentistry.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between multigenerational family communication patterns and emerging adult identity development using computational social science methods. While prior work in family systems has emphasized qualitative or survey-based approaches, this study addresses a critical gap by modeling how nonlinear, time-dependent interactions within family networks (e.g., parent-child-grandparent triads) influence psychosocial outcomes. The research problem centers on identifying computational signatures of adaptive versus maladaptive identity formation processes through analysis of longitudinal interaction data from 300 families, including multimodal behavioral (video-recorded discussions), linguistic (transcribed narratives), and physiological (heart rate variability) datasets. A high-performance computing (HPC) resource allocation is essential to implement agent-based models that simulate family communication dynamics across developmental timescales, integrating reinforcement learning architectures to capture how interpersonal feedback loops shape self-concept. Computational challenges include real-time natural language processing of dyadic emotional tone, network analysis of cross-generational influence hierarchies, and Bayesian inference models quantifying uncertainty in developmental trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for predicting identity coherence scores based on simulated family interaction patterns, (2) identification of computational biomarkers indicating resilience to intergenerational conflict, and (3) open-source tools for visualizing developmental cascades in family systems. By bridging developmental psychology with complex systems science, this work advances theoretical understanding of how micro-level interpersonal processes macro-scale identity outcomes, while providing methodological innovations for studying relational dynamics in HDFS research. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of >10TB of multimodal data and parallelized simulation of 50,000+ family interaction scenarios with varying cultural and socioeconomic parameters.
cip_title: Human Development and Family Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on basic human developmental and behavioral characteristics of the individual within the context of the family. Includes instruction in the conditions that influence human growth and development; strategies that promote growth and development across the life span; and the study of family systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators teaching students with hearing impairments, including deafness. A critical challenge in this field is the high variability in students’ auditory processing abilities, communication modalities (e.g., sign language, speechreading, cochlear implants), and language acquisition trajectories, which complicates the design of individualized instructional strategies. Traditional approaches rely on static lesson plans or generalized assessments, often failing to account for real-time student engagement or dynamic learning needs. To address this, the research will employ machine learning (ML) models trained on multimodal classroom datasets—including visual sign language recognition, speech-to-text accuracy metrics, and eye-tracking patterns—to predict optimal instructional adjustments. Computational simulations will model how different teaching interventions (e.g., visual scaffolding techniques, pacing adjustments) interact with student-specific sensory and cognitive profiles. HPC resources are essential for processing high-resolution video data of sign language interactions, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and optimizing ML architectures for real-time feedback. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating personalized lesson recommendations and a simulation platform to train educators in adapting instruction for diverse auditory and language profiles. By quantifying the impact of specific teaching strategies on learning outcomes, this work aims to bridge gaps in evidence-based practices for deaf and hard-of-hearing education, directly supporting teacher preparation programs in aligning pedagogical training with the heterogeneous needs of this student population.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Hearing Impairments Including Deafness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with hearing impairments including deafness which adversely affect their educational performance, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with hearing impairments, including deafness, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising hearing-impaired students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent collective phenomena in driven-dissipative quantum spin systems using large-scale numerical simulations. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how non-equilibrium quantum systems stabilize under competing interactions, external drives, and environmental dissipation—a fundamental challenge in modern condensed matter physics. Current analytical methods struggle to capture the complex interplay of quantum coherence, many-body interactions, and non-Markovian dissipation in these systems, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose to employ tensor network methods combined with variational quantum algorithms to simulate spin-1/2 lattices with time-dependent Hamiltonian drives and spatially inhomogeneous dissipation. The computational framework will leverage hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to optimize matrix product operator (MPO) contractions and time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) routines, enabling the study of system sizes beyond current numerical capabilities (up to N=100 spins). Key objectives include characterizing phase transitions between dynamically stabilized quantum states, identifying signatures of dissipative time-crystalline order, and quantifying entanglement scaling in non-equilibrium steady states. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parameter space exploration across multiple energy scales and dissipation regimes while maintaining the numerical precision required for quantum trajectory sampling. This work will provide new insights into the control of quantum coherence in open systems, with potential applications in quantum information storage and noise-resilient quantum simulation. Results will be disseminated through open-source code packages for the broader physics community, establishing computational tools for future studies of driven-dissipative quantum matter.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced optimization frameworks for dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, stochastic operational systems, with applications in healthcare logistics and supply chain management. Traditional methods for such problems often struggle with computational intractability when addressing high-dimensional state spaces, time-dependent constraints, and uncertainty propagation—particularly in systems requiring frequent human-in-the-loop decision-making. We propose a hybrid computational methodology integrating stochastic mixed-integer programming, parallelized approximate dynamic programming, and distributed simulation-optimization techniques. The core innovation involves decomposing complex multistage optimization problems through scenario reduction algorithms and implementing asynchronous value iteration across high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. This approach will leverage GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo tree search for real-time adaptive decision policies and employ variance reduction techniques to enhance convergence rates in stochastic dual dynamic programming. The computational demands are substantial, requiring tera-scale memory bandwidth for branch-and-bound tree traversals in mixed-integer formulations, distributed storage for scenario trees with >10^6 nodes, and parallel processing capabilities for ensemble simulations evaluating policy robustness. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly available software toolkit for stochastic resource allocation, benchmarked against industrial-scale problem instances; (2) novel convergence guarantees for parallel decomposition algorithms in partially observable Markov decision processes; and (3) case studies demonstrating 20-40% efficiency improvements in hospital bed allocation and cross-dock logistics systems compared to current industry practices. The HPC resources will enable parameter sensitivity analyses across 10^4+ simulation replications and real-time optimization of systems with >10^5 interdependent decision variables—capabilities critical for bridging theoretical operations research with practical implementation challenges in human-centered operational systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems. These programs have a mathematical focus.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural and intellectual exchange across medieval and Renaissance Europe through the computational analysis of fragmented historical datasets. Traditional scholarship in this domain has been constrained by the manual processing of disparate sources—including digitized manuscripts, archival records, art inventories, and archaeological reports—limiting the scale at which patterns of transmission can be identified. The proposed research will integrate natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning to systematically analyze multilingual textual corpora, artistic iconography, and material culture data spanning the 12th to 16th centuries. Key objectives include modeling the diffusion of literary motifs, reconstructing trade and pilgrimage routes using geospatial datasets, and identifying socio-cultural hubs through dynamic network simulations. HPC resources are critical to process terabytes of high-resolution manuscript images, optimize OCR accuracy for archaic scripts, and train neural networks to detect stylistic correlations in art and architecture. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated datasets, interactive maps visualizing transnational exchange networks, and computational models that quantify the impact of specific institutions (e.g., monastic scriptoria, merchant guilds) on cultural dissemination. By bridging gaps between textual, artistic, and archaeological evidence, this project aims to reveal previously unrecognized pathways of influence, enriching scholarly debates on regional identity formation and the transmission of knowledge. The tools and methodologies developed will establish a scalable framework for computational humanities research, enabling future studies to interrogate large, heterogeneous datasets with greater precision. This work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in addressing complex historical questions that transcend disciplinary boundaries.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the Medieval and/or Renaissance periods in European and circum-Mediterranean history from the perspective of various disciplines in the humanities and social sciences, including history and archeology, as well as studies of period art and music.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in producing high-resolution, dynamic illustrations that integrate real-time interactivity and complex visual effects, which are increasingly demanded in fields such as digital publishing, augmented reality (AR), and interactive media. Current workflows for illustrators are constrained by the limitations of consumer-grade hardware, particularly when rendering intricate 3D models, simulating physical materials (e.g., fabric, lighting), or applying machine learning (ML) techniques to automate stylistic adaptations across multi-platform deliverables. The research problem centers on scaling artistic workflows to accommodate large datasets—such as 3D-scanned environments or generative asset libraries—while maintaining the precision and aesthetic nuance required in professional illustration. To overcome these barriers, the project proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources for distributed rendering, parallelized simulation of material behaviors, and training ML models for style transfer and asset generation. Custom pipelines will be developed to optimize tasks like batch-processing thousands of high-fidelity frames for animated illustrations or dynamically adjusting vector-based designs for cross-media formatting. The use of GPU-accelerated nodes will enable real-time collaboration tools for artists working on shared virtual canvases, reducing latency in iterative design processes. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for illustrators, benchmarks for HPC-driven artistic workflows, and case studies demonstrating scalable solutions for client-driven projects, such as interactive children’s books or AR-enhanced fashion catalogs. By bridging the gap between computational scalability and artistic practice, this work aims to expand the technical possibilities for illustrators, reduce production bottlenecks, and establish new standards for computationally intensive creative workflows in the visual arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze systemic disparities in criminal case outcomes through advanced computational modeling of legal text data. The study focuses on identifying latent biases and procedural inefficiencies within criminal law by examining large-scale datasets of judicial opinions, plea agreements, sentencing memoranda, and appellate records. A core challenge lies in processing unstructured legal texts at scale to detect patterns in judicial decision-making, statutory interpretation, and the application of procedural rules across jurisdictions. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal corpora—with network analysis to map citation patterns and evolutionary trends in criminal procedure. Custom machine learning pipelines will be developed to classify case outcomes, predict procedural delays, and quantify disparities tied to demographic or jurisdictional factors. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models on terabytes of legal documents and running parallelized simulations of alternative procedural frameworks. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible framework for analyzing bias in criminal case processing, 2) evidence-based recommendations for procedural rule modifications, and 3) novel metrics for evaluating the equitable application of criminal laws. By bridging computational methods with legal theory, this work aims to establish reproducible techniques for large-scale legal analytics while addressing pressing questions about fairness and efficiency in criminal justice systems. The project demonstrates how HPC capabilities can advance sociolegal research in ways traditional doctrinal analysis cannot, offering transformative potential for both academic inquiry and policy reform.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting criminal law and trial procedures.

abstract: Dental materials must meet stringent biomechanical, biochemical, and biocompatibility requirements to ensure long-term functionality and safety in the dynamic oral environment. However, optimizing these materials—such as resin composites, ceramics, and bioactive coatings—remains challenging due to the complex interplay between their physicochemical properties, mechanical performance under cyclic loads, and interactions with oral tissues and microbial biofilms. This project seeks to address these challenges by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to model and predict the behavior of next-generation dental materials at multiple scales. Specifically, the research will focus on (1) simulating the molecular dynamics of polymer-ceramic interfacial bonding in resin composites to reduce failure rates in restorative procedures, (2) analyzing stress distribution and fatigue behavior in zirconia-based prostheses using finite element modeling under occlusal loading conditions, and (3) predicting the degradation kinetics and ion release profiles of bioactive glass coatings designed to inhibit secondary caries. Atomistic simulations will elucidate interfacial adhesion mechanisms between filler particles and resin matrices, while mesoscale models will correlate microstructural heterogeneity with crack propagation resistance. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms trained on existing experimental datasets will accelerate the discovery of material compositions with optimal mechanical and antimicrobial properties. The computational workflows will integrate multi-physics simulations to account for thermal, chemical, and mechanical stressors encountered in vivo. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to overcome the limitations of traditional trial-and-error approaches, enabling rapid virtual screening of material designs. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for material longevity, data-driven design guidelines for improved prostheses, and foundational insights into material-tissue interactions that could reduce postoperative complications. The results will advance the development of durable, bioactive dental materials while establishing a computational framework translatable to other biomedical material challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biomaterials and inert and active compounds used in dental procedures; the development of dental materials; and their effects on the living tissues of the oral cavity and systemic bodily health. Includes instruction in materials science, dental bioengineering, biocompatibility of materials, physics and mechanics of dental materials, elastic and plastic deformation, surface bonding, and applications to fixed and removable prostheses and restorative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resilient construction materials and adaptive project scheduling in large-scale infrastructure systems, addressing the critical need for infrastructure that can withstand increasing environmental stressors and supply chain disruptions. The research problem centers on the complexity of modeling multi-physics interactions in novel composite materials (e.g., fiber-reinforced polymers, self-healing concretes) while simultaneously coordinating dynamic construction workflows under uncertainty. Current methods struggle to integrate real-time material performance data with stochastic scheduling variables such as equipment availability, labor productivity, and weather disruptions at the scale of city-level projects. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid high-performance computing (HPC) approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) for material behavior prediction, discrete-event simulation for construction process modeling, and machine learning to identify risk-mitigation patterns from historical project data. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized multi-scale modeling to resolve interactions between microstructural material properties and macro-scale structural performance, coupled with agent-based simulations of construction site operations. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system capable of recommending optimal material-formulation-to-construction-sequence pairings, validated through case studies on bridge rehabilitation and high-rise construction projects. The HPC resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets from IoT sensors, lidar scans, and materials testing archives while maintaining computational feasibility for scenario ensembles. This work aims to advance sustainable construction practices by reducing material waste through precision simulations and improving project resilience metrics by 20-30% in modeled scenarios. Results will contribute open-source modules for construction process optimization, bridging a critical gap between civil engineering materials science and operations management in the AEC (architecture, engineering, construction) industry.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific, mathematical, and management principles to the planning, design, and building of facilities and structures. Includes instruction in civil engineering, structural principles, site analysis, computer-assisted design, geology, evaluation and testing, materials, contracting, project management, graphic communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in mathematical logic—specifically in model theory and computability theory—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address problems intractable to classical analytical methods. A core challenge in modern logic involves analyzing the structural complexity of uncountable models, classifying degrees of unsolvability in recursion-theoretic hierarchies, and resolving open questions about the consistency and independence of axiomatic systems. Such problems require the systematic exploration of vast solution spaces, verification of combinatorial or infinitary constructions, and iterative testing of conjectures across parameterized scenarios, all of which exceed the computational limits of standard workstations. The proposed work will employ custom algorithms to automate the generation and analysis of mathematical structures, including fine-structure models of set theory, non-well-founded trees for independence proofs, and priority argument simulations for degree-theoretic classifications. These algorithms will integrate symbolic computation, parallelized search heuristics, and proof-assistant frameworks (e.g., Lean 4 or Coq) to ensure formal correctness. HPC resources will enable large-scale Monte Carlo simulations for stochastic model construction, distributed computation of consistency thresholds in forcing extensions, and efficient SAT-solving for propositional encodings of logical satisfiability problems. Expected outcomes include resolving conjectures in the stability hierarchy of infinitary theories, characterizing the computational density of Turing degrees below 0', and producing open-access datasets of axiomatic consistency results. By bridging proof-theoretic rigor with computational scalability, this project aims to expand the methodological toolkit of pure logic research while contributing foundational insights to areas such as algorithmic meta-mathematics and the philosophy of mathematical practice. The requested resources will directly support the parallelization of memory-intensive tasks, with an estimated need for 50,000 core-hours and 2 TB of distributed memory to accommodate iterative model-checking and proof-tree generation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: Liver transplantation remains a life-saving intervention for end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges persist in predicting graft survival, optimizing immunosuppression regimens, and managing post-transplant complications. Current clinical models often rely on static, single-modality data, limiting their ability to account for dynamic interactions between donor-recipient immune compatibility, multi-omics profiles, and evolving clinical variables. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled predictive framework to integrate longitudinal multi-modal data—including genomics, proteomics, radiomics, and electronic health records—from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 liver transplant recipients. Using machine learning approaches such as transformer-based neural networks and ensemble models, we will simulate immune-mediated graft injury pathways, predict early and late rejection events, and identify biomarkers of tolerance. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated model training and large-scale parallel simulations to analyze spatial transcriptomic data from graft biopsies, coupled with time-series clinical variables. Validation will involve retrospective prediction of known outcomes and prospective correlation with real-world transplant registry data. This resource-intensive approach is necessary due to the high dimensionality of multi-omics datasets, the temporal complexity of post-transplant immune responses, and the need for real-time adaptive modeling in clinical decision support tools. Expected outcomes include the creation of a validated predictive model for graft survival with superior accuracy to existing clinical scores, a computational platform for personalized immunosuppression dosing, and open-source tools for dynamic risk stratification. The project directly addresses unmet needs in transplant hepatology by enabling data-driven precision in pre- and post-transplant care, with potential to reduce rejection rates, improve long-term patient outcomes, and lower healthcare costs through optimized resource allocation.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge and the skill required of a gastroenterologist to care for patients prior to and following hepatic transplantation that spans all phases of liver transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate a computational framework to enhance the design and evaluation of competency-based training modules in Trade and Industrial Teacher Education (TITE). A critical challenge in vocational education is ensuring that instructional strategies align with the dynamic technical and pedagogical demands of modern industrial environments. While existing curricula emphasize hands-on skill development, there is a lack of scalable tools to simulate complex trade scenarios, model learner progression, and optimize teaching methods for diverse student cohorts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build adaptive simulation environments and predictive analytics models. The research will focus on three interconnected computational tasks: (1) developing physics-based simulations of industrial tasks (e.g., mechatronic systems troubleshooting, precision machining) using finite element analysis and discrete event modeling; (2) training machine learning classifiers to identify patterns in learner performance data from virtual labs; and (3) implementing multi-agent reinforcement learning systems to model classroom interactions and pedagogical decision-making. These methods require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale datasets of student interactions, high-fidelity equipment simulations, and stochastic modeling of educational outcomes. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of training scenarios across variables such as class size, skill heterogeneity, and resource availability. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for generating evidence-based teaching recommendations, predictive models of skill acquisition timelines, and optimized virtual training environments that mirror real-world trade workplaces. By computationally bridging the gap between industrial practice and teacher preparation, this work aims to elevate the precision and scalability of vocational educator training while maintaining strict alignment with industry standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach specific vocational trades and industries programs at various educational levels.

abstract: In the rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, nursing professionals face increasing demands to deliver high-quality care while managing complex patient needs. This project seeks to address critical challenges in clinical decision-making and patient outcome optimization through advanced computational modeling. The research focuses on developing predictive analytics tools to identify patients at risk of adverse events, such as sepsis or falls, using large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multidimensional data—including vital signs, medication histories, and nursing notes—in real time. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models capable of processing heterogeneous data streams with high dimensionality. Our methodology includes the development of ensemble learning frameworks and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) tailored to temporal clinical data. These models will be validated against retrospective EHR data from diverse healthcare settings, ensuring generalizability across populations. The computational workflow will utilize distributed computing paradigms for feature extraction, model training, and real-time inference, requiring significant memory and processing capabilities provided by HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include deployable risk prediction tools that empower nursing staff to prioritize interventions proactively, potentially reducing hospital-acquired complications by 15–20%. Furthermore, this research will establish scalable computational pipelines adaptable to emerging healthcare technologies, strengthening the integration of data-driven decision support in nursing education and practice. By bridging gaps between clinical expertise and advanced analytics, this project aims to enhance both patient outcomes and nursing workforce efficiency in acute care environments.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolutionary and neurophysiological underpinnings of cross-species social learning strategies using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral data analysis. Social learning—critical for survival in many species—varies in complexity across taxa, but the mechanisms driving these differences remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental methods face limitations in scaling species comparisons, integrating neural data with behavioral outcomes, and simulating evolutionary trajectories under dynamic ecological pressures. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, agent-based models will simulate social learning dynamics across virtual populations of primates, corvids, and cetaceans, incorporating neurophysiological constraints (e.g., memory capacity, neural connectivity) derived from empirical datasets. Second, machine learning pipelines will analyze over 50TB of existing species-specific behavioral video archives and electrophysiology recordings to identify conserved and divergent neural-behavioral correlates. Third, phylogenetic comparative models will integrate these results with evolutionary trees to test hypotheses about the emergence of complex social learning strategies. HPC resources are essential for optimizing deep reinforcement learning architectures, running parallelized evolutionary simulations across parameter spaces, and processing high-dimensional neural data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking neuroanatomical adaptations to social learning diversity, validated against empirical data from collaborating primate cognition labs. This work will advance comparative psychology by bridging micro-scale neural mechanisms and macro-scale evolutionary patterns, with broader implications for understanding cognitive evolution and designing biologically inspired AI systems. The requested computing allocation will enable iterative model refinement and large-scale synthetic experiments impractical on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the behavior of members of particular species or groups and the relationship of the behaviors of the species or group to their evolutionary origins. Includes instruction in differential psychology, experimental and physiological psychology, psychopharmacology, psychology of individual differences, reinforcement theory, and neurophysiology.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in predicting multi-organ toxicity caused by environmental and pharmaceutical agents, a challenge complicated by the dynamic interplay between toxin pharmacokinetics, tissue-specific susceptibility, and delayed pathophysiological outcomes. Current experimental models struggle to resolve these complex, system-wide interactions, particularly for toxins with non-linear dose-response relationships or those requiring metabolic activation. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multi-scale computational models integrating molecular toxicokinetic data with organ-level physiological networks. Agent-based modeling will simulate toxin distribution and metabolism across hepatic, renal, and nervous systems, parameterized by existing in vitro and in vivo datasets on priority chemicals such as halogenated hydrocarbons and organophosphate derivatives. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess inter-individual variability in detoxification capacity, incorporating polymorphisms in cytochrome P450 enzymes and membrane transporter proteins. A second computational arm will apply molecular dynamics simulations to predict structural interactions between reactive toxin metabolites and critical biomolecules, including albumin, glutathione, and extracellular matrix components, to identify sequestration or bioactivation hotspots. These simulations will utilize GPU-optimized force fields calibrated against crystallographic data from toxin-adducted proteins. The integration of these approaches aims to generate predictive maps of toxin fate and injury propagation across biological scales, enabling identification of early biomarkers and countermeasure targets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational framework for simulating multi-organ toxicity scenarios, validated against clinical and toxicological databases. This work will directly inform the design of safer chemicals, improve antidote development strategies, and reduce reliance on animal testing for systemic toxicity assessments. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the high-dimensional parameter spaces, iterative model optimization, and large-scale sensitivity analyses required to achieve these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of poisons and other biohazards; their interactions with organisms and their food and respiratory systems; and their prevention, management, and counteraction. Includes instruction in toxicological biochemistry, toxic agents and transporters, toxin fate, toxicokinetics and metabolism, toxin classification, molecular toxic mechanisms, extracellular matrices and cell function, bacterial pathogenesis and mutagenesis, pathophysiology and apoptosis, cell stress and injury, studies of specific toxins, and studies of specific organ systems and physiological functions in relation to toxicological problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methods for analyzing high-dimensional, sparse biological datasets commonly encountered in agricultural and natural resource studies.
