A key challenge in these domains is the integration of multi-modal data—such as environmental sensor readings, species occurrence records, and resource management histories—into predictive models that account for complex spatial dependencies, temporal autocorrelation, and unbalanced sampling designs. Traditional biometrical approaches often struggle with computational inefficiency when handling such data structures, particularly when applying Bayesian hierarchical frameworks or ensemble machine learning techniques. To address this, we propose implementing a hybrid computational architecture combining Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling with distributed gradient boosting, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated matrix operations for covariance estimation in mixed-effects models while employing MPI-based parallelization for stochastic gradient descent in neural network components. Key deliverables include an open-source R/Python package for sparse spatiotemporal analysis and validation against empirical datasets from precision agriculture trials and wildlife population monitoring programs. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale simulations to evaluate type I/II error rates under varying missing data mechanisms, as well as parameter estimation for high-dimensional random forest models with >10^5 decision trees. Expected outcomes include robust protocols for handling non-ignorable missingness in longitudinal ecological datasets and improved uncertainty quantification in resource allocation optimization tasks. This work directly supports evidence-based decision-making in sustainable agriculture and biodiversity conservation by providing computationally feasible tools for complex error structures inherent to real-world biological systems. Successful implementation will require access to at least 50 nodes with 64 GB RAM each, GPU support for tensor operations, and scalable storage for terabyte-scale sensitivity analyses.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics and other computational methods to the study of problems in the biological sciences and related fields in agriculture and natural resources. Includes instruction in computational biology, mathematical statistics, matrix algebra, applied calculus, experimental design, linear modeling, sampling theory, stochastic processes, spatial and temporal analysis, longitudinal analysis, sparse/unbalanced data and complex error, and applications to such topics as population genetics, animal breeding, forest genetics, population dynamics, wildlife biometry, ecology, and agricultural and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and operational resilience of distributed industrial ecosystems—networked systems where interdependent facilities, supply chains, and energy grids co-evolve under dynamic constraints. Traditional optimization methods fail to address the nonlinear feedback loops, multi-agent decision-making, and stochastic disruptions inherent in such systems, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and vulnerability to cascading failures. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach integrating agent-based modeling, game-theoretic coordination mechanisms, and physics-informed reinforcement learning (RL). High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parallel simulations of ecosystem interactions across spatiotemporal scales, capturing emergent behaviors from equipment-level dynamics to market-driven resource flows. Custom RL algorithms will train adaptive control policies under uncertainty, while graph neural networks will map system-wide dependencies to prioritize critical nodes for redundancy. The computational workflow will leverage distributed memory architectures for scenario exploration and GPU-accelerated training of deep surrogate models. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for resilient ecosystem design, validated against case studies in modular chemical production and renewable energy-integrated manufacturing. By enabling real-time, data-driven decision-making in complex, multi-stakeholder environments, this work aims to advance applied engineering methodologies for sustainable industrial transformation. The requested resources will directly support the execution of 10^5+ simulation-years of operational data, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and uncertainty quantification across heterogeneous input spaces—tasks infeasible on local clusters. Success will provide foundational insights into balancing efficiency, adaptability, and risk mitigation in next-generation engineering systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles inherent to engineering to the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the rational design of functional polymers by addressing critical gaps in understanding the molecular-scale mechanisms governing polymerization kinetics, macromolecular interactions, and structure-property relationships. Experimental approaches often struggle to resolve dynamic processes such as crosslinking in thermosetting resins or transient intermediates in catalytic polymerization, limiting the efficient development of polymers with tailored functionalities. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multiscale computational framework combining quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) methods. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model systems of industrially relevant complexity, including copolymerization networks and solvent-polymer interfacial phenomena. QM simulations will elucidate electronic interactions during initiation and propagation steps in radical polymerization, while coarse-grained MD will capture mesoscale chain dynamics under varying thermodynamic conditions. The kMC approach will integrate these insights to predict polymerization rates and molecular weight distributions. Key outcomes include identifying kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable polymer synthesis, optimizing reaction conditions for high-performance elastomers, and elucidating degradation pathways of unstable polyelectrolytes in solution. By mapping how monomer chemistry and process parameters influence macromolecular architecture, this work will directly inform the design of polymers for energy-efficient coatings and biodegradable packaging materials. The requested computing resources will enable simulations spanning nanoseconds to microseconds for systems exceeding 500,000 atoms, which is intractable with existing campus infrastructure. Successful execution will provide a predictive toolkit to reduce trial-and-error experimentation in polymer development, aligning with industrial priorities for rapid material innovation. All data and validated force fields will be shared publicly to accelerate broader research in polymer chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance physics teacher preparation by addressing the challenge of integrating computational modeling and data-driven pedagogy into physics education curricula. Many pre-service physics educators lack exposure to high-performance computing (HPC) tools, limiting their ability to design instruction that leverages modern computational methods or contextualizes complex physics concepts through simulation. To bridge this gap, we propose developing and testing a scalable suite of interactive, curriculum-aligned computational physics modules optimized for HPC environments. These modules will simulate phenomena such as quantum wavefunction behavior, many-body gravitational interactions, and thermodynamic systems under non-ideal conditions—topics often taught abstractly due to experimental or mathematical barriers. The research will employ GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations, finite element analysis for electromagnetic field visualization, and machine learning algorithms to automate the generation of customizable, grade-appropriate visualization outputs. By running these workflows on HPC clusters, we will enable pre-service teachers to parametrically explore physical systems in real time during lesson development exercises, fostering deeper pedagogical content knowledge. Outcomes will be evaluated through pre/post assessments of 120 teacher candidates’ computational pedagogical skills and analyses of lesson plans created using the modules. The project aims to establish a replicable framework for embedding HPC-driven inquiry in physics teacher education, directly addressing the Next Generation Science Standards’ emphasis on computational thinking. Successful implementation will provide open-access resources to help future physics educators harness advanced computing tools, ultimately improving secondary students’ engagement with computationally intensive STEM concepts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) present complex challenges due to the interplay of neurobiological, behavioral, and environmental factors. Current treatment paradigms in addiction counseling often rely on static protocols, which inadequately address the dynamic, individualized nature of recovery and relapse. This project seeks to bridge this gap by developing a computational framework to model the neurobehavioral trajectories of individuals undergoing substance abuse counseling, with a focus on predicting relapse risk and optimizing personalized intervention strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we aim to integrate multimodal data—including functional neuroimaging (fMRI), real-time behavioral monitoring via mobile sensors, and longitudinal clinical assessments—to construct dynamic, patient-specific models of craving, decision-making, and therapeutic response. The computational approach combines mechanistic neural network simulations with machine learning algorithms to identify biomarkers of relapse vulnerability and simulate the efficacy of hypothetical counseling interventions in silico. Key challenges include processing high-dimensional neuroimaging datasets, resolving temporal dependencies in behavioral data streams, and scaling personalized models across heterogeneous cohorts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized parameter optimization for biophysical neural models, large-scale Bayesian inference for probabilistic behavioral forecasting, and ensemble learning techniques to improve predictive generalizability. Expected outcomes include a novel computational toolkit for addiction counselors to visualize patient-specific risk profiles, test intervention scenarios, and refine treatment plans dynamically. This work will advance the integration of computational neuroscience into clinical counseling practice, offering a data-driven framework to enhance the precision and adaptability of SUD interventions. By elucidating the neurocomputational mechanisms underlying therapeutic change, the project aims to establish a foundation for next-generation, technology-augmented addiction care paradigms.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to help prevent substance abuse, counsel individuals and families with drug and alcohol problems, and perform intervention and therapeutic services for persons suffering from addiction. Includes instruction in individual and group counseling skills, psychology of addiction, sociology, crisis intervention, substance abuse identification methodologies, substance abuse treatment modalities, substance abuse prevention and treatment resources, pharmacology and behavioral aspects of abused substances, treatment evaluation, patient observation and education, group dynamics, professional standards and ethics, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize diagnostic and repair workflows for complex computer hardware systems, with a focus on improving the efficiency and reliability of fault detection in high-performance computing (HPC) environments. As modern computing systems grow in scale and heterogeneity—integrating multi-core processors, GPUs, and specialized accelerators—traditional diagnostic tools often fail to account for dynamic thermal, electrical, and mechanical interactions between components. This limitation leads to prolonged downtime, misdiagnoses, and suboptimal repair outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, we will train machine learning models on synthetic and real-world datasets of hardware failure signatures, including thermal profiles, voltage fluctuations, and error logs, to predict component degradation and pinpoint faults. Second, we will simulate stress-test scenarios using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model heat dissipation, power delivery stability, and physical wear under varying workloads. These simulations will inform hardware design modifications and repair protocols to mitigate failure risks. The project requires access to HPC resources to handle large-scale parallel processing for training deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets and running high-fidelity physical simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source diagnostic toolkit for technicians to prioritize repair tasks based on predictive analytics, (2) validated guidelines for optimizing cooling and power supply configurations in heterogeneous systems, and (3) a curated repository of simulation data to enhance training materials for computer repair education. By bridging computational modeling with applied hardware maintenance, this work aims to reduce operational costs for HPC facilities while advancing pedagogical resources in computer repair technology.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven decision support framework for optimizing farm management strategies under dynamic environmental and economic conditions. Despite advances in precision agriculture, farmers and ranchers face persistent challenges in integrating heterogeneous datasets—such as soil health metrics, weather forecasts, commodity price trends, and livestock performance indicators—into actionable operational plans. Current models often lack the scalability to account for regional variability or the temporal resolution to adapt to rapid market shifts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build an adaptive simulation platform that combines agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning. Agent-based models will simulate farm operations at granular spatial and temporal scales, capturing interactions between management decisions (e.g., crop rotations, irrigation schedules, herd culling), stochastic environmental factors, and market volatility. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify risk profiles for alternative strategies, while neural networks trained on historical yield data and satellite imagery will predict localized outcomes under climate variability. The computational intensity arises from the need to parallelize thousands of scenario iterations across diverse agroecological zones and validate models against multi-terabyte datasets from USDA reports, IoT-enabled farm sensors, and remote sensing platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario-based resource allocation, capable of recommending optimal planting dates, input applications, and livestock management protocols tailored to real-time conditions. By quantifying trade-offs between short-term profitability and long-term sustainability at unprecedented resolution, this work aims to reduce operational risks for small-to-midsize farms while informing policy frameworks for agricultural resilience. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the spatial fidelity and stochastic depth required for actionable insights, with preliminary simulations indicating a 40-60x speedup over existing cloud-based solutions when scaling to regional analyses.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage farms, ranches, and similar enterprises. Includes instruction in applicable agricultural specialization, business management, accounting, taxation, capitalization, purchasing, government programs and regulations, operational planning and budgeting, contracts and negotiation, and estate planning.

abstract: The preservation of historic structures and landscapes necessitates balancing complex, often competing factors, including material degradation, environmental stressors, socio-economic pressures, and regulatory constraints. Current methodologies for modeling these interactions rely on simplified assumptions or fragmented datasets, limiting their utility in dynamic urban environments. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a computational framework to simulate and predict the long-term impacts of conservation strategies, climate change, and urban development on historic sites. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-scale datasets—including 3D LiDAR scans, environmental sensor data, archival records, and socio-economic indicators—into a unified geospatial-temporal model. Computational methods will include finite element analysis (FEA) to assess material stress under varying climate scenarios, machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in deterioration rates, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-resolution spatial data, parallelizing computationally intensive simulations, and iterating through thousands of scenario combinations to identify optimal preservation pathways. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize at-risk structures, quantify trade-offs between conservation and development goals, and inform policy decisions. By creating an open-source computational platform, this research will provide preservationists, urban planners, and policymakers with scalable, data-driven strategies to safeguard cultural heritage amid growing environmental and economic uncertainties. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—bridging architectural history, materials science, and computational social science—exemplifies the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional STEM fields, offering a model for integrating advanced computing into humanities-driven research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of plans to restore and maintain historic buildings, districts, and landscapes in a way that balances conservation and preservation with commercial and development interests. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation, cultural resource management, economics, historical documentation and preservation, land-use and zoning codes, public policy, public relations, real estate law, and taxation.

abstract: Pharmacy research faces increasing demands to optimize drug delivery systems and predict complex molecular interactions, particularly in developing nanoparticle-based formulations. Traditional experimental approaches are resource-intensive and time-consuming, often struggling to capture the dynamic behavior of drug-carrier systems at atomic resolution. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational models of drug-nanoparticle interactions, focusing on pharmacokinetic profiles and stability under physiological conditions. The research will employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to analyze binding affinities, diffusion rates, and degradation pathways of candidate drug molecules within polymeric nanoparticle matrices. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation outputs to predict formulation efficacy and toxicity, using datasets derived from experimental literature and public pharmacology databases. Key challenges include scaling simulations to biologically relevant timescales (microseconds to milliseconds) and managing the high-dimensional parameter space of multicomponent drug delivery systems. HPC resources are critical to parallelize these computations, enabling iterative refinement of forcefield parameters and ensemble-based sampling. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal polymer-drug pairings for enhanced bioavailability in preclinical models, with a focus on antibiotics and cancer therapeutics. This work will provide a framework for rational design of nanoparticle formulations, reducing trial-and-error experimentation in early-stage drug development. Additionally, the project will support training opportunities for pre-pharmacy students in computational pharmaceutics, bridging gaps between traditional pharmacy curricula and modern data-driven research methods. By integrating HPC-based modeling with experimental validation, this research aims to accelerate the translation of theoretical drug delivery concepts into practical applications, directly aligning with the program’s mission to prepare students for advanced pharmacy education and innovation in pharmaceutical sciences.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: Nursing education faces a critical challenge in preparing educators to design and evaluate clinical training programs that address rapidly evolving healthcare demands, including complex patient care scenarios and interdisciplinary collaboration. Traditional teaching methods often lack the capacity to model dynamic, high-stakes clinical environments or to personalize instruction for diverse learner needs. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate clinical training scenarios, optimize curriculum design, and assess educator and student competencies in real time. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models to replicate multi-patient clinical workflows, integrate machine learning algorithms to analyze historical educational outcomes, and employ natural language processing to evaluate reflective practice in simulated debrief sessions. The simulations will incorporate variables such as patient acuity, staffing ratios, and learner skill levels, generating datasets that capture interactions between instructional strategies, student performance, and contextual factors. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale simulation outputs, train predictive models for competency gaps, and enable real-time adaptation of virtual scenarios during training. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for nurse educators to iteratively refine clinical instruction methods, predictive analytics to identify at-risk learners, and evidence-based guidelines for scaling simulation-based training across institutions. This work will advance nursing education research by providing a data-driven approach to address variability in clinical preparedness, ultimately improving the quality of nurse training programs and patient care outcomes. The computational infrastructure developed here will also serve as a foundation for future studies on adaptive learning systems in healthcare education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to teach in academic and clinical settings, including staff development. Includes instruction in advanced nursing practice, nursing role development, curriculum and instruction, program and course design, clinical instruction, and evaluation of learning.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical need for advanced computational tools to analyze complex speech patterns in individuals with neurodegenerative communication disorders, such as primary progressive aphasia (PPA) and Parkinsonian syndromes. Current clinical assessments in speech-language pathology rely heavily on subjective perceptual evaluations and time-consuming manual acoustic analyses, limiting scalability and precision in tracking disease progression or therapy outcomes. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a machine learning framework to automate the detection of subtle, subperceptual speech biomarkers from high-resolution audio and articulatory kinematic data. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets encompassing >10,000 hours of speech samples from diverse patient cohorts, paired with longitudinal clinical metadata. Computational workflows will integrate parallelized feature extraction (including nonlinear dynamic measures of vocal fold vibration and articulatory coordination) with deep neural networks trained to identify disease-specific signatures across phonetic, prosodic, and fluency domains. The HPC environment is essential for managing memory-intensive preprocessing of raw waveform data, optimizing hyperparameters for temporal convolutional networks, and validating models through large-scale cross-database replication studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for quantifying speech degradation trajectories with millisecond-level temporal resolution, enabling earlier intervention windows and personalized therapy targets. By establishing quantitative links between computational speech markers and neuropathological staging, this work aims to advance tele-rehabilitation monitoring systems while providing foundational insights into the neurocomputational mechanisms of speech motor control. The resulting infrastructure will support future investigations into speech plasticity across acquired and congenital communication disorders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of speech-language pathologists, to assist in the provision of speech-language pathology services to individuals of all ages, including screenings and assessments, following treatment plans or protocols, documenting and reporting patient performance, performing checks and maintenance of equipment, and providing support in research projects. Includes instruction in speech and language development, phonetics, childhood and adult communication disorders, speech and hearing screening, and clinical procedures in speech-language pathology.

abstract: The proposed research aims to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor microenvironmental stressors and cellular metabolic adaptations in driving cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. Despite advances in understanding cancer pathophysiology, the mechanisms by which heterogeneous tumor populations coordinately respond to hypoxia, nutrient deprivation, and oxidative stress remain poorly resolved. This project will employ a multiscale computational framework to model metabolic network plasticity and intercellular signaling in physiologically structured tumor microenvironments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate spatially resolved, three-dimensional tumor systems incorporating single-cell metabolic flux analysis, stochastic nutrient gradient dynamics, and agent-based cell fate decision algorithms. The computational pipeline will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from patient-derived xenograft models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to parameterize metabolic heterogeneity. Parallelized simulations will quantify emergent properties of tumor-stroma metabolic symbiosis under varying oxygenation and pH conditions, with iterative validation against in vitro microfluidic culture experiments. Expected outcomes include identification of microenvironmental thresholds that trigger collective metabolic reprogramming events, predictive biomarkers of adaptive resistance to metabolic inhibitors, and spatially mapped vulnerabilities for combination therapy targeting. This work will establish a novel computational platform for simulating physiologically constrained tumor evolution, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority to bridge systems biology with translational oncology. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-parameter-space explorations (10⁵+ core-hours) required for statistically robust analysis of stochastic microenvironmental interactions, which are computationally intractable on local clusters. By elucidating principles of stress-adaptive metabolic coordination in tumors, this research aims to advance precision oncology strategies while contributing open-source simulation tools to the cancer physiology community.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_title: Physiology, Pathology, and Related Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physiology, pathology, and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the transnational diffusion and adaptation of German-language cultural narratives across historical diasporas in Central and Eastern Europe using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural hybridity in textual and visual media produced by German-speaking minorities between 1750 and 1950—a corpus spanning millions of pages of digitized newspapers, pamphlets, personal correspondence, and artworks. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to analyze this scale of multilingual, multimedia data, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) to uncover latent connections and contextualize marginalized voices within broader cultural histories. The project will employ a hybrid computational framework combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for semantic analysis of historical German dialects, computer vision techniques for iconographic classification in visual materials, and network analysis to map cultural exchange pathways. Custom machine learning pipelines will be developed to handle orthographic variations in pre-modern texts and mitigate biases in archival preservation practices. By integrating geospatial mapping tools, the analysis will visualize temporal shifts in cultural production centers and their relationship to political boundaries. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from distributed archives, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of cultural transmission dynamics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking digitized artifacts to thematic nodes (e.g., folklore adaptation, linguistic code-switching), quantitative models of cross-cultural influence, and new methodological frameworks for ethically engaged digital humanities in area studies. This work will provide unprecedented insights into how decentralized cultural networks sustained German-language identities amid state dissolution and migration, while establishing scalable protocols for computational analysis of underrepresented historical narratives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing resource allocation in early childhood education (ECE) programs through advanced computational modeling. ECE administrators face complex decisions in balancing budgetary constraints, staffing needs, facility utilization, and regulatory compliance while maintaining program quality and accessibility. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to account for dynamic variables such as fluctuating enrollment, evolving policy requirements, and socioeconomic disparities. This research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to model multi-dimensional resource allocation scenarios across diverse ECE settings. The computational approach will integrate demographic data, funding structures, staff qualifications, and facility capacities into agent-based models that simulate program operations under varying constraints. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical program outcomes to identify patterns in resource utilization efficiency and predict the impact of administrative decisions on equity metrics. By leveraging parallel processing, the platform will enable rapid scenario testing for large-scale program networks, including sensitivity analyses of policy changes and disaster preparedness planning. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for administrators to visualize trade-offs between fiscal responsibility, regulatory adherence, and educational quality, with particular emphasis on underserved communities. The project will also generate scalable frameworks for evaluating state-level funding distribution models and workforce development investments. This work advances the field of education leadership by introducing computational social science methodologies to early childhood administration, offering empirically grounded strategies to enhance program sustainability and equitable access. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of simulating thousands of interdependent variables across heterogeneous program environments while maintaining the fidelity required for policy-relevant conclusions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on early childhood educational program administration and prepares individuals to serve as a principal or director of an early childhood educational program. Includes instruction in early childhood education, program and facilities planning, budgeting and administration, public relations, human resources management, early childhood growth and development, counseling skills, applicable law and regulations, school safety, policy studies, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of blood coagulation disorders, a critical area in hematology technology. Current diagnostic methods for thrombotic and bleeding disorders often rely on static laboratory tests, which may fail to capture dynamic molecular interactions underlying pathological clotting. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models that integrate molecular dynamics simulations of clotting factor interactions with systems-level analyses of coagulation cascade regulation. These models will simulate blood clot formation under varying physiological and pathological conditions, incorporating patient-derived data on genetic mutations, platelet function, and plasma protein levels. The computational framework will utilize parallelized algorithms to handle the high-dimensional parameter space and stochasticity inherent to coagulation biology. Machine learning approaches will further refine predictive accuracy by identifying patterns in clinical datasets linked to thrombotic risk or therapeutic response. By utilizing HPC resources, this project will overcome the limitations of traditional in vitro experiments, enabling rapid, large-scale simulations of clotting mechanisms across diverse patient populations. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, predictive models for personalized anticoagulant therapy, and a deeper understanding of how genetic and environmental factors disrupt hemostatic balance. This work aligns with the clinical priorities of hematology technology by enhancing the precision of diagnostic workflows and informing the development of targeted therapies. The requested computing resources are essential for managing the project’s data-intensive workloads, which involve terabytes of simulation outputs and high-throughput clinical data integration. Successful execution will provide a scalable computational toolkit for translational research in hematology, bridging gaps between laboratory testing and patient-specific clinical decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists and health care professionals, to perform tests and analyses of blood samples. Includes instruction in clinical laboratory procedures; blood anatomy and physiology; cellular and molecular biology; blood pathology and disease indicators; quantitative, qualitative, and coagulation testing methodologies; equipment operation and maintenance; and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the structural and systemic factors influencing equity gaps in K-12 educational outcomes across diverse geographic and institutional contexts. Current policy evaluations often rely on aggregated data or simplified models, limiting their ability to disentangle the complex interactions between policy implementation, resource allocation, and student outcomes. This research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate multi-level policy impacts using fine-grained longitudinal data spanning student performance metrics, funding patterns, and policy compliance records from 12 states. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate how localized variations in policy adoption (e.g., Title I fund distribution, teacher credentialing requirements) interact with community-level socioeconomic factors at scale. Computational demands arise from iterative parameter optimization across 50+ policy scenarios, machine learning-driven pattern recognition in unstructured administrative records, and probabilistic forecasting of equity outcomes under alternative policy configurations. By integrating 15 terabytes of longitudinal student data, institutional records, and policy datasets, the models will quantify how specific allocation mechanisms either exacerbate or mitigate disparities in access to advanced coursework and extracurricular resources. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating education policy trade-offs, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing compliance monitoring systems, and (3) predictive metrics to identify districts at highest risk of unintended policy consequences. Results will advance methodological approaches to policy analysis by demonstrating how computational scalability enables more nuanced, dynamic assessments of education systems than traditional regression-based methods permit. This work directly supports the program’s mission to improve policy evaluation frameworks through innovative applications of computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to education and educational systems at the local, state, national, and international levels. Includes instruction in social and cultural issues in education, contemporary educational policies, history of education, economics of education, international and comparative education, education and social change, educational research and evaluation methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and related autoimmune rheumatic diseases present complex, heterogeneous pathobiology driven by dynamic interactions between genetic, immune, and environmental factors. Current treatment strategies remain suboptimal due to variable patient responses and limited biomarkers for predicting disease progression or therapeutic efficacy. This project proposes to address these challenges by developing a computational framework integrating multi-omics data with clinical phenotypes to model disease mechanisms and predict personalized treatment outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze longitudinal genomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from 1,200 RA patients across three international cohorts. Machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and ensemble classifiers, will be trained to identify predictive signatures of treatment response to biologic therapies. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate immune-stromal cell interactions in synovial tissue under varying genetic and therapeutic conditions. These computational workflows require parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional datasets (>500 TB) and iterative simulations across parameter spaces. The HPC environment will enable scalable deployment of containerized pipelines for data harmonization, feature selection, and model validation while ensuring reproducibility. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for anti-TNF and JAK inhibitor responses, (2) mechanistic insights into synovial microenvironment dynamics driving treatment resistance, and (3) open-source tools for omics integration in rheumatic disease research. This work will directly inform clinical trial designs for targeted therapies and advance computational rheumatology by establishing a template for translating complex molecular data into actionable clinical decision-support frameworks. Resource allocation is critical to achieve computational scalability and meet time-sensitive milestones aligned with ongoing patient recruitment.
cip_definition: Research focused on Rheumatology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision and customization of ophthalmic lens fabrication by integrating biomechanical modeling, optical simulation, and machine learning. Current lens manufacturing processes rely on static optical models that inadequately account for dynamic interactions between lenses, corneal biomechanics, and individual patient physiology, leading to suboptimal visual outcomes for patients with complex ocular conditions such as keratoconus or post-surgical corneas. To address this, we propose a computational framework that simulates real-time, patient-specific interactions between custom-fabricated lenses and ocular surfaces under varying mechanical and environmental conditions. The project will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model corneal deformation and stress distribution, coupled with ray-tracing algorithms to predict optical aberrations introduced by lens-cornea interactions. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-modal datasets—including corneal topography, wavefront aberrometry, and patient-reported comfort metrics—to optimize lens curvature, edge design, and material properties. HPC resources are critical for resolving the computational intensity of iterative simulations across thousands of parametric combinations and large-scale data integration. Expected outcomes include a novel predictive tool for lens customization that reduces trial-and-error prototyping in laboratory settings and improves visual acuity outcomes by ≥15% in simulated cohorts. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets correlating lens design parameters with biomechanical strain metrics, fostering innovation in adaptive optics for ocular prosthetics. By bridging computational optics, materials science, and ocular biomechanics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm in precision ophthalmic device fabrication, with implications for emerging fields such as augmented reality eyewear and biocompatible smart lenses.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of ophthalmologists and optometrists, to cut, grind, edge, and finish corrective lenses and to fabricate eyewear. Includes instruction in optical theory, applied mathematics, lens surfacing and finishing, tinting and coating, impact resistance treatment and testing, frame construction and repair, prescription interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, follow-up adjustment, record-keeping, and laboratory safety procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modern electrical infrastructure resilience and efficiency through advanced computational modeling of power line systems. As aging grids face increasing demands from renewable energy integration, extreme weather events, and evolving communication technologies, lineworkers require predictive tools to optimize maintenance and minimize service disruptions. Current approaches to assessing mechanical stress, thermal load distribution, and failure risks in overhead and underground systems rely heavily on static models that inadequately capture dynamic environmental interactions. This research will develop high-fidelity simulations of multi-physics phenomena affecting power lines, including wind-induced conductor galloping, ice accumulation dynamics, and soil-cable thermal coupling in buried installations. Using finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics implemented on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, we will model regional-scale grid segments with granular material properties and real-world environmental inputs. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical fault data and sensor-derived operational parameters to establish predictive maintenance frameworks. The computational workflow will integrate LiDAR-scanned terrain models, weather station feeds, and material degradation databases to simulate decade-long wear patterns under climate change scenarios. By leveraging parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration, these simulations will achieve unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution while maintaining computational feasibility. Expected outcomes include predictive risk maps for line failure hotspots, optimized crew deployment strategies, and evidence-based recommendations for code updates regarding vegetation clearance distances and underground cable depth requirements. The project will produce open-source simulation templates adaptable to regional grid architectures, directly enhancing lineworker training programs through virtual reality-based scenario modules. Successful implementation will reduce grid vulnerability to extreme weather by 15-20% in pilot regions while providing utility companies with decision-support tools to prioritize infrastructure upgrades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain and repair local, long-distance, and rural electric power cables and communication lines; erect and construct pole and tower lines; and install underground lines and cables. Includes instruction in cable installation and repair, fibre-optic technology, trenching, mobile equipment and crane operation, high-voltage installations, maintenance and inspection, safety, remote communications, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to understand how rapid environmental change influences the stability of ecological networks and species coexistence mechanisms in biodiverse ecosystems. As anthropogenic disturbances and climate variability alter resource availability and species interactions, predicting community-level responses remains a critical challenge in environmental biology. We propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based models (ABMs) of multi-trophic interactions with spatially explicit dynamic vegetation models (DVMs) to simulate ecosystem responses under projected climate scenarios. The ABMs will parameterize species-specific traits, including dispersal capacity, phenological shifts, and niche breadth, derived from empirical datasets spanning tropical and temperate forest inventories. DVMs will integrate regional climate projections (CMIP6) and soil hydrology data to simulate abiotic drivers at mesoscale resolutions (1–10 km²). High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the stochastic, high-dimensional interactions inherent to these simulations, particularly for scaling individual-level processes to landscape-level patterns over decadal timeframes. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess variance in community resilience metrics across >10,000 parameter combinations, while machine learning algorithms (random forests, gradient-boosted regression trees) will identify key predictors of ecosystem collapse thresholds. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of biodiversity hotspots at elevated risk under IPCC warming scenarios, validated against long-term ecological monitoring data from established forest dynamics plots. By quantifying nonlinear feedbacks between species traits and environmental filters, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of extinction cascades while informing habitat corridor designs for climate-vulnerable taxa. The generated models and code will be optimized for open-source distribution, providing a transferable toolkit for conservation planning in understudied biodiverse regions.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in precision manufacturing processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model, simulate, and optimize advanced fabrication techniques. Precision production trades rely on the integration of technical illustration, material science, and multi-axis machining to create components with sub-millimeter tolerances. However, current methods for predicting tool wear, thermal deformation, and material behavior during high-speed machining lack the resolution and scalability needed for next-generation applications, particularly when working with advanced alloys or composite materials. Traditional experimental approaches are cost-prohibitive and time-intensive, while existing computational models fail to capture the multi-physics interactions inherent to these processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate machining dynamics at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of tool-workpiece interactions across diverse material systems, incorporating real-time thermal gradients, stress distributions, and microstructural evolution. A convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on simulation outputs to predict optimal machining parameters, minimizing defects while maximizing tool lifespan. The project will validate models against experimental data from CNC milling and laser engraving processes, iteratively refining predictive accuracy. Outcomes will include open-source simulation workflows tailored for precision production applications and a database of validated material response profiles. By enabling rapid virtual prototyping, this research aims to reduce material waste by an estimated 15–20% in small-batch manufacturing scenarios while improving the precision of complex geometries. The computational tools developed will directly support workforce training programs in advanced manufacturing, providing interactive visualization modules for technical illustration integration. This work establishes a foundation for data-driven process optimization in precision trades, addressing a critical need in industries transitioning to smart manufacturing paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing cross-border digital financial transactions, with a focus on systemic risks posed by algorithmic tax optimization strategies employed by multinational enterprises (MNEs). The research addresses a critical gap in international tax law: the lack of computational tools to model the dynamic interplay between rapidly advancing financial technologies, opaque tax arbitrage mechanisms, and heterogeneous national regulatory regimes. Traditional legal analysis struggles to quantify the cascading effects of automated profit-shifting algorithms or predict emergent vulnerabilities in global tax governance systems. To bridge this gap, the project will develop agent-based models simulating MNE decision-making under competing jurisdictional rules, paired with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze regulatory texts from 150+ national tax authorities and international agreements. The computational framework will integrate game-theoretic representations of corporate strategic behavior, temporal network analysis of treaty shopping patterns, and probabilistic assessments of audit outcomes under machine learning-enhanced compliance monitoring systems. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for identifying high-risk tax avoidance pathways in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems, stress-test scenarios for proposed global minimum tax architectures, and a novel taxonomy of regulatory conflicts arising from AI-driven transfer pricing models. By combining legal domain expertise with large-scale computational simulations, this work aims to produce actionable insights for policymakers addressing tax base erosion while maintaining innovation incentives in digital commerce. The HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets of corporate financial disclosures, legal rulings, and transactional blockchain records, as well as for running complex multi-jurisdictional simulations requiring parallelized optimization algorithms and real-time sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations.
cip_title: International Business, Trade, and Tax Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations governing transnational business and commercial practices, including the specialized tax law related to international financial transactions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational models aimed at optimizing respiratory care protocols for patients with heterogeneous lung pathologies. A critical challenge in respiratory therapy is tailoring ventilator settings and aerosolized medication delivery to individual patient physiology, particularly in cases of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and post-surgical recovery. Current clinical decision-making relies on generalized guidelines, which may not account for the complex interplay of airway mechanics, regional lung compliance, and gas exchange dynamics. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating patient-specific anatomical data from medical imaging, physiological parameters from clinical monitors, and fluid-structure interaction models to simulate ventilation-perfusion mismatches and drug deposition patterns. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parallelization of finite element analyses for airway biomechanics and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of nebulized particle transport across bifurcating bronchial trees. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed on HPC clusters to identify predictive biomarkers from retrospective clinical datasets, correlating simulated outcomes with real-world patient responses. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models for personalized positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) titration, (2) optimized nebulizer type and particle size selection based on patient-specific airway geometry, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for respiratory therapy education. By bridging computational engineering with clinical practice, this work aims to reduce ventilator-induced lung injury risks, improve therapeutic efficacy, and provide respiratory therapy students with advanced simulation tools for scenario-based training. The scale of parameter space exploration and real-time coupling of 3D simulations with physiological control systems necessitates dedicated HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant resolutions and throughput.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer general respiratory care procedures under the supervision of respiratory therapists in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in patient data collection and monitoring, airway management, installation of nebulizers and other respiratory assistance devices, application and monitoring of breathing gases, equipment operation and maintenance, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable regulations.

abstract: Public works systems, encompassing critical infrastructure such as transportation networks, water distribution, and waste management, face escalating challenges due to aging infrastructure, climate variability, and fiscal constraints. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for the dynamic interdependencies between socio-economic factors, environmental stressors, and operational decision-making, limiting the ability to optimize resource allocation and long-term resilience. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that simulate complex public works systems under diverse scenarios. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate urban population dynamics and infrastructure demand, integrated with Monte Carlo methods to assess climate-related risks to asset longevity. Concurrently, optimization algorithms will evaluate budget allocation strategies across competing priorities, incorporating human resource constraints and labor relations frameworks. By synthesizing large-scale datasets—including municipal budgets, climate projections, and workforce analytics—the models will identify cost-effective interventions to enhance service delivery while maintaining fiscal and ethical accountability. The computational intensity of these multi-layered simulations necessitates HPC capabilities to process real-time data streams and execute parallelized scenario analyses. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support toolkit for public administrators, enabling evidence-based prioritization of infrastructure investments, workforce deployment, and risk mitigation strategies. This work aims to advance public works management by bridging theoretical frameworks in public administration with scalable computational tools, ultimately fostering more adaptive and equitable infrastructure systems.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on public works management skills and public works operation. Includes instruction in accountability, budget, conflict resolution strategies, ethics, finance, human resources, labor and employee relations, and operations management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay of biopsychosocial factors influencing self-management behaviors in adults with type 2 diabetes. While behavioral interventions in health psychology often target individual-level cognitive or social drivers of adherence, gaps persist in modeling how physiological stressors (e.g., glycemic variability), contextual social determinants (e.g., caregiver support), and real-time decision-making interact across time. To address this, we propose developing a multilevel computational model integrating longitudinal electronic health records, ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data, and experimentally induced stress biomarkers. The computational approach employs hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to simulate individual and social network dynamics. ABM will capture how peer support networks and environmental constraints shape daily adherence choices, while RNNs will analyze temporal patterns in physiological (continuous glucose monitoring) and behavioral (smartphone-reported diet/exercise) data to predict high-risk periods for nonadherence. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to heterogeneous population cohorts (n ≈ 50,000 synthetic agents), optimizing hyperparameters for personalized prediction, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse sociocultural contexts. Expected outcomes include identifying modifiable leverage points where behavioral interventions could disrupt negative feedback loops—for instance, tailoring telehealth prompts to moments when social isolation coincides with glucose spikes. By quantifying how micro-level decisions aggregate into macro-level health outcomes, this work aims to advance precision health strategies in counseling contexts, offering clinicians a decision-support tool for sequencing multimodal interventions. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source software, enabling health psychology researchers to adapt biopsychosocial models for other chronic conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological study of health and illness, and recovery, from the perspective that these phenomena arise from a combination of physical, behavioral, and social conditions. Includes instruction in abnormal and social psychology, psychophysiology, psychopharmacology, learning processes, clinical and behavioral therapies, biopsychosocial modeling, clinical procedures and assessment, preventive education, psychotherapy, rehabilitation processes, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the structural and functional dynamics of neural circuits underlying sensory processing in the mammalian somatosensory cortex. A critical gap persists in understanding how synaptic plasticity and glial interactions collectively shape network-level activity patterns during tactile discrimination tasks. Traditional experimental approaches alone cannot capture the multiscale complexity of these interactions, which span molecular signaling at synapses, activity-dependent plasticity in neuronal ensembles, and emergent network oscillations. To address this, we propose developing a biophysically detailed computational model integrating empirical data from in vivo electrophysiology, two-photon calcium imaging, and ultrastructural connectomics of layer 4 cortical circuits in mice. The model will simulate activity across 50,000+ neurons and associated glial networks, incorporating experimentally derived parameters for synaptic strength, short-term plasticity, and astrocyte-mediated modulation. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of circuit dynamics under varying sensory input patterns and plasticity rules, with iterative model refinement via machine learning-based parameter optimization. Key outcomes include identifying glia-neuron signaling motifs that stabilize network activity during learning, predicting how specific synaptic alteration patterns (observed in neurodevelopmental disorders) disrupt sensory encoding fidelity, and generating testable hypotheses for optogenetic validation. This work will provide foundational insights into the interplay between cellular plasticity mechanisms and large-scale network function, with direct relevance to understanding circuitopathies in autism spectrum disorders and epilepsy. The computational framework will be shared as an open-access tool for the neuroanatomy community, facilitating collaborative exploration of structure-function relationships in neural systems. Successful execution requires sustained HPC access to manage the computational load of multi-day simulations, real-time data processing from parallel model instances, and large-scale parameter space exploration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular studies of neuronal and glial cells and circuits, neural transmitters and receptors, neuronal signaling processes, membrane and synapse structure and communication, autonomic function, nervous system circuitry and mapping, and anatomical and functional basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model and optimize hybrid auction formats that integrate live, in-person bidding with decentralized digital participation—a growing trend in auctioneering driven by advances in real-time communication technologies. The research addresses a critical challenge in modern auction management: dynamically balancing bidder engagement, price discovery, and operational efficiency when coordinating simultaneous physical and virtual bid streams across heterogeneous asset categories (e.g., fine art, agricultural equipment). Current auction theory lacks robust models for these hybrid environments, particularly when accounting for latency effects, bidder psychology across modalities, and multi-commodity interactions. To bridge this gap, we will implement a high-performance agent-based simulation platform leveraging historical auction data from partner firms (2018-2023) encompassing 12,000+ transactions. The computational architecture will combine parallelized bid stream processing with reinforcement learning agents trained to emulate human bidder behavior under different auctioneer pacing strategies. Key innovations include a GPU-accelerated environment for real-time simulation of 10,000+ concurrent participants and a novel metric space for quantifying bid "momentum" transfer between physical and digital channels. Expected outcomes include empirically validated protocols for optimal bid sequencing, technology-mediated bidder onboarding workflows, and dynamic reserve price adaptation algorithms. These computational tools will directly address pain points identified in preliminary surveys of 147 professional auctioneers, particularly the need for decision support systems that preserve auctioneer autonomy while mitigating the cognitive load of hybrid event management. By establishing quantitative benchmarks for emerging auction formats, this work aims to enhance the economic efficiency of asset redistribution markets while maintaining the performative elements central to auctioneering practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for professional careers as auctioneers and auction managers, and for meeting applicable state licensing requirements. Includes instruction in bid calling, public speaking, ringworking, auction techniques, salesmanship skills, auction clerking and cashiering, auction advertising, working independently or with auction houses, contracts and agency, applicable sales law, and managing both general auctions and auctions specializing in commodities such as antiques, consignments, farm equipment, industrial equipment, real estate, livestock, and automobiles.

abstract: The development of stable and efficacious pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations is hindered by the complex interplay of physicochemical properties, excipient compatibility, and environmental factors. Traditional experimental approaches to optimize formulations are resource-intensive, requiring iterative trial-and-error processes that delay product development and increase costs. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive multiscale models for formulation design and stability assessment. The research will focus on two key areas: (1) simulating molecular interactions in semi-solid formulations (e.g., creams, gels) to predict rheological behavior and phase stability under varying storage conditions, and (2) modeling polymorphic transitions in active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) to anticipate crystallization risks in liquid dosage forms. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations (using GROMACS and LAMMPS) to resolve nanoscale interactions, finite element analysis (via COMSOL Multiphysics) for macroscale property prediction, and machine learning algorithms (TensorFlow-based neural networks) trained on experimental datasets to correlate simulation outputs with real-world stability outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the high-throughput demands of parameter space exploration, particularly for systems involving multicomponent surfactants, lipids, or polymeric matrices. Expected outcomes include a computational framework capable of identifying optimal excipient combinations, predicting shelf-life under thermal and humidity stress, and guiding reformulation strategies for failed stability batches. By reducing experimental redundancies and enabling in silico preformulation screening, this work aims to accelerate development timelines for topical drug products and cosmetic emulsions while enhancing quality control protocols. The resulting models will be validated against industrial case studies, with implications for improving regulatory submissions through data-driven stability justification.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the complex interplay between urban environmental stressors, socioeconomic factors, and population health outcomes through an integrative data analytics framework. While prior studies have examined isolated environmental or social determinants of health, this research addresses a critical gap by modeling dynamic, multiscale interactions between heterogeneous datasets—including real-time sensor networks (air quality, noise, temperature), anonymized electronic health records, and spatially resolved socioeconomic indices—to identify emergent patterns of community-level health risks. The computational challenge lies in harmonizing high-dimensional, temporally staggered data streams spanning disparate domains while accounting for spatial autocorrelation and latent confounding variables. We propose a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial-temporal dependencies, Bayesian hierarchical modeling for uncertainty quantification across scales, and agent-based simulations to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training GNNs on petabyte-scale urban sensor datasets, executing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across socioeconomic gradients, and optimizing hyperparameters through distributed evolutionary algorithms. Anticipated outcomes include a novel open-source analytics pipeline for multimodal urban health data, identification of high-risk “hotspots” where environmental and socioeconomic stressors synergistically amplify health disparities, and predictive models to evaluate equitable mitigation strategies. This work advances interdisciplinary methodologies at the nexus of environmental science, public health, and computational social science, providing actionable insights for policymakers while establishing scalable frameworks for data integration challenges common to smart city initiatives worldwide.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data analytics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework to optimize real-time analysis of dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) datasets in oncologic imaging, with the goal of enhancing the diagnostic support role of Radiologist Assistants (RAs). The increasing complexity of multiparametric imaging protocols generates vast, temporally resolved datasets that challenge traditional manual or semi-automated analysis methods. RAs, tasked with preliminary image evaluation and patient management, require tools to rapidly identify physiologically relevant biomarkers—such as perfusion kinetics or spatial heterogeneity—without compromising diagnostic accuracy. We propose a computational pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to train deep learning models on dynamically acquired DCE-MRI sequences, integrating 4D spatiotemporal convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with biomechanical models of contrast diffusion. The project will utilize federated learning across anonymized datasets from collaborating institutions to ensure robustness while adhering to patient privacy standards. Key computational challenges include managing memory-intensive 4D data (∼1 TB per patient scan), reducing latency in model inference for clinical workflows, and disentangling overlapping contrast kinetics in heterogeneous tumors. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for RA-specific decision support, validated against radiologist annotations, that prioritizes explainable AI outputs to align with RA scope-of-practice guidelines. Successful implementation could reduce time-to-preliminary-report by 30–50% in initial pilot studies, while quantifying previously undersampled tumor heterogeneity metrics. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational imaging, oncology, and radiology practice, directly supporting RAs in scaling their role within precision medicine paradigms without encroaching on diagnostic radiology responsibilities. HPC resources are critical for model training, large-scale data harmonization, and simulating contrast dynamics across diverse patient anatomies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: The interaction of light with biological systems drives critical processes such as vision, photosynthesis, and circadian rhythm regulation, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these light-induced reactions remain poorly resolved at ultrafast timescales. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the structural and electronic dynamics of photoreceptor proteins and photosynthetic complexes. Specifically, we propose large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to investigate photon absorption, energy transfer, and conformational changes in rhodopsin, cryptochromes, and photosystem I. These simulations will resolve femtosecond-to-microsecond dynamics of chromophore-protein interactions, including transient intermediate states inaccessible to experimental techniques. A key focus is elucidating how environmental factors, such as UV exposure or oxidative stress, alter photochemical pathways in retinal proteins, contributing to degenerative eye diseases. The computational workflow integrates spectral data to validate predicted absorption maxima and fluorescence lifetimes against experimental benchmarks. By mapping energy landscapes and electron transfer pathways, this study will identify conserved motifs that optimize light harvesting and signaling efficiency in biological systems. The outcomes will advance the development of targeted phototherapies for ocular disorders and bioengineered light-driven catalysts for sustainable energy applications. The scale of these simulations—involving multi-million-atom systems, long-timescale sampling, and iterative QM/MM optimizations—necessitates HPC resources for parallelized GPU-accelerated computations. Results will be disseminated as open-access trajectory datasets and machine learning-ready force field parameters, providing foundational tools for the photobiology community. This work bridges molecular-scale photophysics to organism-level photoresponses, offering transformative insights into light-driven life processes.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the effects of light energy on living organisms, the manufacture and processing of luminescence by organisms, and the uses of light in biological research. Includes instruction in bioluminescence, chronobiology, photomedicine, environmental photobiology, organic photochemistry, photomorphogenesis, photoreceptors and photosensitization, molecular mechanics of photosynthesis, phototechnology, vision, ultraviolet radiation, radiation physics, and spectral research methods.

abstract: Insects are critical yet understudied agents of ecosystem dynamics, with flight dispersal mechanisms that remain poorly quantified in heterogeneous environmental conditions.
