This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model micro-scale atmospheric interactions governing insect flight trajectories, leveraging entomological data to predict population-scale dispersal under climate variability. Current models oversimplify fluid-insect biomechanics, neglecting turbulence effects on species-specific morphology, such as wingbeat kinematics and body mass distributions. We propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with agent-based modeling (ABM) to resolve how localized wind patterns, thermal gradients, and precipitation interact with insect physiology to shape dispersal outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10⁶–10⁷ agent insects across dynamic 3D atmospheric fields derived from remote-sensing datasets. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on CFD-ABM outputs to accelerate parameter space exploration, targeting species of agricultural and epidemiological concern (e.g., migratory pests, disease vectors). Validation will utilize entomological radar datasets and mark-release-recapture field trials for select Lepidoptera and Diptera species. Expected outcomes include the first open-source platform for probabilistic insect dispersal forecasting at meter-scale resolution, directly addressing gaps in precision agriculture and vector-borne disease management. By quantifying how extreme weather events and habitat fragmentation modulate dispersal efficiency, this work will inform resilience strategies for pollination networks and invasive species containment. The computational framework will prioritize scalability for global change scenarios, with generated datasets bridging entomology, atmospheric science, and environmental policy. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and public dissemination of models via an interactive portal for stakeholder-driven scenario testing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of insect species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to address the growing challenges of decrypting and analyzing encrypted communications used by terrorist organizations, which increasingly leverage sophisticated cryptographic methods and obfuscation techniques to evade detection. Current forensic tools struggle to process large-scale digital evidence efficiently, particularly when dealing with fragmented data, multi-layered encryption, and covert channels embedded in network traffic. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized brute-force decryption, machine learning-driven pattern recognition, and large-scale network traffic simulation. The project will focus on three computational objectives: (1) optimizing distributed algorithms to accelerate password cracking and cryptographic key recovery for common encryption protocols identified in counterterrorism cases; (2) training deep learning models on HPC clusters to detect anomalies in partially reconstructed data sets, including metadata patterns indicative of covert messaging; and (3) simulating terrorist cyber-attack scenarios using virtualized network environments to identify vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure systems. By utilizing GPU-accelerated computing and scalable memory architectures, this approach will significantly reduce the time required to process terabyte-scale forensic images and network packet captures. Anticipated outcomes include a novel framework for prioritizing forensic artifacts in large datasets, improved decryption success rates for law enforcement agencies, and actionable intelligence about emerging cyberterrorism tactics. The computational workflows developed will be validated against real-world case data from partner agencies, with results contributing to open-source forensic toolkits. This research directly supports national security priorities by enhancing the technical capabilities of investigators to disrupt terrorist activities in compliance with legal and procedural standards.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques used to identify, search, seize and analyze digital media and to conduct cyber investigations against criminal and terrorist activity. Includes instruction in computer boot processes and drives, jumper setting, file access and reconstruction, hacking, network systems, cryptography, programming, investigative techniques, forensic imagery, web-based investigation methods, cyberterrorism, and applicable laws and administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern graphic communications workflows by developing predictive models to optimize material usage, energy consumption, and production quality across hybrid print-digital processes. Current industry practices rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and heuristic adjustments, particularly for complex jobs involving variable data printing, specialty substrates, or multi-stage finishing. These methods incur significant time, cost, and environmental impacts that limit scalability for small-to-medium enterprises. We propose a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA) for substrate behavior modeling, machine learning (ML) to predict ink-substrate interactions under diverse press conditions, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess process variability. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training ML models on heterogeneous datasets spanning spectrophotometric measurements, substrate tensile properties, and environmental sensor data from press operations. The simulations will parameterize variables including humidity, temperature, and mechanical stress across lithographic, digital, and screen printing subsystems. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool that recommends optimal press configurations for given substrate-ink pairs, reducing waste by an estimated 15-30% in test scenarios. This research bridges gaps between empirical print production knowledge and computational engineering approaches, offering a pathway to democratize advanced process optimization for non-industrial users. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter sweeps for FEA simulations, and storage for terabyte-scale print quality image analysis. Results will be validated against physical press trials conducted in our graphic communications lab, with open-source release of non-proprietary models to benefit academic programs and industry partners transitioning to sustainable production practices.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the manufacture and distribution or transmission of graphic communications products. Includes instruction in the prepress, press, and postpress phases of production operations and processes such as offset lithography, flexography, gravure, letterpress, screen printing, foil stamping, digital imaging, and other reproduction methods.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model wildfire propagation and suppression dynamics, addressing critical gaps in current fire behavior prediction systems. Wildfires present a growing threat to ecosystems, infrastructure, and public safety, exacerbated by climate change and urban expansion into wildland interfaces. Existing models often lack the spatial granularity and integration of real-time environmental variables necessary to predict fire spread in complex terrains or under rapidly shifting weather conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled atmosphere-fire numerical model that integrates computational fluid dynamics (CFD), fuel moisture dynamics, and stochastic ignition scenarios at meter-scale resolution. The framework will utilize parallelized simulations to account for multi-scale interactions between fireline behavior, localized wind patterns, and fuel heterogeneity, validated against historical fire perimeter data and controlled burn experiments. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to identify high-risk ignition zones and optimize resource deployment strategies. By enabling near-real-time scenario testing for fire departments and land managers, this research aims to improve tactical decision-making during active fire incidents and long-term risk mitigation planning. Expected outcomes include an open-source modeling toolkit for fire agencies, enhanced predictive accuracy for fire spread under extreme weather conditions, and data-driven recommendations for fuel management prioritization. The computational demands of resolving fine-scale physics and running ensemble forecasts for probabilistic risk assessment necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and large memory capacity. This work will directly support firefighter safety, community resilience, and evidence-based policy in wildfire-prone regions, while advancing computational methodologies for fire science within the homeland security domain.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in fire protection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of sustainable, high-performance textiles through multiscale computational modeling of bio-derived polymer systems. Traditional textile science relies heavily on empirical experimentation to optimize fiber properties, dye interactions, and finishing processes, which is time-intensive and limited in its capacity to predict complex material behaviors at molecular and mesoscopic scales. The research addresses this gap by integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, coarse-grained modeling, and machine learning (ML) to decode the relationships between molecular structures of bio-based polymers (e.g., cellulose derivatives, chitin composites) and their macroscopic performance in textile applications. Key objectives include simulating the self-assembly of novel fiber-forming polymers under varying thermal and mechanical conditions, predicting dye adsorption kinetics on functionalized surfaces, and optimizing enzymatic finishing processes for reduced environmental impact. The computational workflows will involve large-scale parallelized simulations using GROMACS and LAMMPS, coupled with ML-driven surrogate models to accelerate parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for designing biodegradable fibers with tailored mechanical strength, colorfastness, and moisture-wicking capabilities, directly addressing industry demands for eco-conscious textiles. By elucidating fundamental structure-property relationships in bio-polymer systems, this work will establish computational textile science as a critical tool for sustainable material innovation, reducing reliance on trial-and-error methods. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-throughput simulations and datasets required to model heterogeneous polymer-dye interactions at experimentally relevant scales, enabling advancements unattainable with conventional laboratory techniques.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties and processing of fibers, yarns, whole fabrics, dyes, and finishes, both natural and synthetic. Includes instruction in the chemical and physical properties of textile materials; end-use analysis; interior furnishing applications; and industrial applications.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the mechanisms underlying vascular remodeling in diabetic cardiovascular complications, a leading contributor to morbidity in patients with type 2 diabetes. Despite clinical evidence linking hyperglycemia and hemodynamic stress to pathological vascular changes, the integrated effects of metabolic dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and altered mechanical forces on arterial wall dynamics remain poorly understood. We propose a multi-scale computational framework to model vascular adaptation in diabetes, combining hemodynamic simulations with cellular-scale representations of endothelial and smooth muscle cell behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve spatially heterogeneous blood flow patterns in patient-specific arterial geometries derived from clinical imaging, while simultaneously simulating mechanotransduction pathways and redox signaling in vascular cells. The computational model will integrate physiological data from in vitro studies of human vascular cells exposed to diabetic conditions, including glucose variability and oxidative stress, to parameterize cellular responses to biomechanical cues. Using finite element methods and agent-based modeling, we will predict how localized alterations in wall shear stress and circumferential strain drive maladaptive remodeling in coronary and renal arteries. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds in glucose levels, blood pressure, and inflammatory markers that exacerbate vascular stiffening and luminal narrowing. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform to map disease progression under varying metabolic and hemodynamic conditions, as well as candidate mechanobiological targets to mitigate remodeling. This work will advance translational strategies for diabetic cardiovascular complications by elucidating how systemic metabolic disturbances converge with localized mechanical forces to drive tissue-level pathology, directly supporting the development of personalized interventions for high-risk patients.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: The optimization of large-scale bioprocessing systems for sustainable chemical production remains a critical challenge in biochemical engineering, particularly in balancing reaction kinetics, mass transfer limitations, and enzyme stability under industrial conditions. This project seeks to develop multiscale computational models to predict the performance of immobilized enzyme reactors for continuous bioconversion processes, with specific application to biofuel precursor synthesis. Current experimental approaches struggle to resolve spatiotemporal heterogeneities in substrate-enzyme interactions at industrially relevant scales, leading to suboptimal reactor designs and costly trial-and-error optimization. We propose an integrated computational framework combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of enzyme-substrate binding energetics with computational fluid dynamics (CDM) modeling of multiphase flow through porous catalyst supports. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the 10^6-atom MD systems required to capture allosteric effects in industrially robust enzymes, coupled with lattice Boltzmann methods simulating fluid transport across micrometer-scale reactor geometries. The workflow will employ hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization to efficiently scale across multiple nodes, leveraging GPU acceleration for the MD component using AMBER and OpenFOAM for CDM simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating enzyme mutation patterns with optimal reactor operating parameters, validated against experimental data from collaborating labs. This resource request directly supports the creation of open-source simulation tools that will enable rational design of continuous bioprocessing systems, potentially reducing process development timelines by 40% for emerging biomanufacturing applications. The computational insights gained will advance fundamental understanding of scale-dependent phenomena in heterogeneous biocatalysis while providing actionable strategies to improve energy efficiency in sustainable chemical production pipelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the study of biochemical processes in living organisms, properties of biological materials, and processes using biochemical agents such as cells, enzymes, and antibodies. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, bioprocesses, and chemical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing digital heritage preservation through advanced computational methods in library science. As libraries and archives increasingly manage dynamic, multimedia-rich collections—including born-digital content, interactive media, and decentralized community archives—traditional cataloging and preservation frameworks struggle to scale. Existing tools lack the capacity to analyze complex relationships between heterogeneous data types (text, audio, video, 3D models) or to model degradation risks for evolving digital formats. This research proposes the development of an AI-driven semantic mapping and preservation prioritization system, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process petabytes of unstructured data across distributed repositories. Computational methods will include graph neural networks to model content interdependencies, transformer-based models for cross-format metadata alignment, and probabilistic simulations to forecast preservation urgency under multiple resource constraints. The workflow will integrate library-specific ontologies with machine learning to automate metadata enhancement while preserving curatorial nuance. By parallelizing ingestion pipelines and training custom embeddings on HPC clusters, the system aims to reduce metadata latency by 60-75% compared to current standards while improving semantic search accuracy. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for scalable digital collection analysis, predictive models for preservation resource allocation, and a benchmark dataset documenting format-specific decay patterns. This work bridges computational scalability challenges with emerging needs in digital stewardship, offering libraries a pathway to sustainable management of 21st-century collections. Successful implementation will directly support 15 partner institutions managing at-risk digital holdings while establishing reproducible methods for interdisciplinary collaboration between library science and computational research.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing real-time decision-making in high-stress military operational environments, leveraging advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. Traditional decision-support systems often struggle to account for the dynamic interplay of human cognitive limitations, environmental unpredictability, and mission-critical constraints. Our research addresses this gap by modeling complex scenarios—such as urban reconnaissance or contested logistics operations—where rapid adaptation to emergent threats and resource limitations is paramount. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based simulations that integrate behavioral data from military training exercises with real-time sensor inputs, environmental variables, and adversarial action-reaction dynamics. These simulations will train reinforcement learning models to identify optimal decision pathways under uncertainty while minimizing cognitive overload for personnel. Key computational challenges include scaling neural architecture searches for time-sensitive predictions, parallelizing scenario variations to cover low-probability/high-impact events, and validating models against classified operational datasets in secure virtual environments. The expected outcomes include a prototype decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive contingency plans with quantified risk profiles, as well as generalized insights into human-machine collaboration under stress. This work bridges military operational theory, cognitive science, and computational systems engineering, offering a novel approach to enhancing mission resilience in asymmetric conflict environments. By utilizing HPC resources to simulate thousands of interdependent variables across operational timelines, the project aims to advance both applied military readiness and interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and human factors analysis.
cip_title: Military Technologies and Applied Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in military technologies and applied sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in funeral service and mortuary science, specifically addressing the optimization of postmortem logistical processes and environmental impact mitigation. The funeral service industry faces growing challenges in balancing operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and ecological sustainability, particularly in urban environments with limited burial space and evolving public health requirements. Traditional methods for managing interment logistics, embalming chemical dispersion modeling, and cemetery land-use planning remain largely manual or reliant on oversimplified heuristics, resulting in suboptimal resource allocation and environmental strain. This research proposes the development of computational models to simulate mortuary workflows, burial site utilization patterns, and chemical transport in soil systems under varying demographic and climatic scenarios. Agent-based modeling will map multi-stakeholder decision-making processes in funeral home operations, while finite element analysis will quantify groundwater contamination risks from embalming fluids. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical burial records and geographic information system (GIS) data to predict long-term cemetery capacity constraints. The computational intensity of these parallelizable simulations—particularly the three-dimensional hydrogeological modeling and large-scale optimization of burial space allocation—necessitates HPC infrastructure for parameter space exploration and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing funeral service carbon footprints, evidence-based guidelines for sustainable thanatopraxy practices, and open-source frameworks for cemetery spatial planning. By integrating computational science with mortuary science, this work aims to establish quantitative decision-support systems for an industry critical to public health and cultural practices, while creating novel methodologies applicable to other non-traditional HPC domains. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary partnerships with funeral service associations and environmental regulatory bodies.
cip_title: Funeral Service and Mortuary Science, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in funeral service and mortuary science not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning models that enhance personalized educational interventions for students with developmental delays. A critical challenge in special education is designing individualized learning plans that adapt to the heterogeneous cognitive, social, and emotional profiles of these students. Traditional methods for creating such plans often rely on manual, time-intensive assessments and static curricula, which struggle to integrate real-time behavioral data, longitudinal performance metrics, and multimodal inputs (e.g., sensor-based engagement tracking, speech patterns, or fine motor skill evaluations). To address this, we propose a computational approach using deep reinforcement learning and ensemble models to dynamically predict student needs and recommend tailored instructional strategies. The project will train these models on aggregated, de-identified datasets spanning video-recorded classroom interactions, standardized assessment scores, and individualized education program (IEP) outcomes. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these datasets, which include high-dimensional temporal sequences and require parallel processing for hyperparameter optimization and cross-validation. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom scenarios to test intervention efficacy under varying constraints. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for generating adaptive lesson plans and a framework for integrating predictive analytics into teacher training programs. By enabling rapid iteration of data-driven strategies, this work aims to reduce educators’ administrative burdens while improving the precision of interventions for developmentally delayed learners, ultimately advancing equity in special education. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with local school districts and workshops for special education teachers.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals Who are Developmentally Delayed
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who exhibit slow social, physical, cognitive, or emotional growth patterns related to age, or a combination of such factors that affect learning, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identification of developmental delay patterns, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising developmentally delayed students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in computational resources for advancing research in Punjabi language and literature, particularly in analyzing its dialectal diversity and historical textual corpora. Punjabi, a widely spoken yet under-resourced language in computational linguistics, presents unique challenges due to its regional variations, evolving orthography, and limited digitized materials. The research aims to develop a scalable computational framework to analyze syntactic, morphological, and semantic patterns across Punjabi dialects and historical texts, enabling systematic comparisons and philological insights. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale textual datasets—including digitized classical literature, modern prose, and oral narratives—and to train machine learning models for dialect classification, automated transliteration between scripts (Gurmukhi, Shahmukhi), and semantic annotation. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) tools adapted for Punjabi’s agglutinative morphology and code-switching tendencies, leveraging parallel processing to manage heterogeneous data. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of Punjabi texts, computational models for dialect mapping, and tools for syntactic parsing tailored to regional variants. These resources will empower scholars to investigate linguistic evolution, sociolinguistic dynamics, and intertextual connections in Punjabi literature with unprecedented granularity. The project will also facilitate applications in language preservation, pedagogy, and technology development, such as improving OCR accuracy for historical manuscripts and supporting NLP tools for Punjabi in educational and commercial contexts. By bridging computational and humanistic methodologies, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven research in Punjabi studies while contributing to equitable language technology development for underrepresented linguistic communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying drug-receptor interactions, with a focus on G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and their associated signaling pathways. Despite their prominence as therapeutic targets, the dynamic conformational changes governing ligand specificity, biased signaling, and allosteric modulation remain poorly resolved at atomistic scales. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the transient, heterogeneous states of these membrane-embedded systems, limiting rational drug design. This project will employ advanced molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model GPCR-ligand complexes in physiologically relevant lipid environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to achieve the timescales (microsecond-to-millisecond) and system sizes (>200,000 atoms) required for robust sampling. Simulations will integrate free energy perturbation calculations to quantify binding affinities and machine learning-driven analysis to classify metastable receptor states. A parallel workflow will apply coarse-grained methods to screen ligand-induced membrane remodeling effects linked to downstream signaling outcomes. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from collaborative studies on adenosine A2A and adrenergic β2 receptors. By resolving state-specific pharmacophore features and membrane-mediated signaling biases, this work aims to identify novel allosteric sites and optimize polypharmacology profiles for drugs targeting neuropsychiatric and cardiovascular disorders. The requested HPC allocation will enable the generation of a publicly accessible database of GPCR conformational ensembles, accelerating structure-guided drug discovery. Outcomes are expected to advance therapeutic strategies for diseases with complex signaling etiologies while establishing computational frameworks adaptable to other membrane receptor families.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the biochemical and biophysical characteristics of drugs at the molecular level and their interaction with, and effects on, biological macromolecules and cellular structures and processes. Includes instruction in molecular biology and biophysics; pharmacology of signal transduction, transmitters, and protein synthesis and release; receptors, protein interaction and binding; drug discovery and recognition; molecular toxicology; drug design; pharmacodynamics; developmental genetics; and studies of therapeutic strategies.

abstract: Athletic injuries present a critical challenge in sports medicine, with existing prevention and management strategies often limited by insufficient personalization and mechanistic understanding of injury pathways. This project proposes a computational approach to model the multifactorial dynamics of musculoskeletal injuries, integrating biomechanical, physiological, and clinical data to advance injury prediction and care. The research will focus on two high-impact problems: (1) identifying biomechanical risk factors for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears during dynamic movements and (2) optimizing post-injury rehabilitation protocols to mitigate reinjury risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the development of multiscale finite element models simulating tissue stress distributions under sport-specific loads, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on multi-modal datasets. These datasets include 3D motion capture, wearable sensor outputs, MRI-derived musculoskeletal geometries, and longitudinal patient outcomes from collegiate and professional athlete cohorts. The computational pipeline will require parallelized processing of high-resolution imaging data, real-time optimization of neural networks for pattern detection in movement kinematics, and probabilistic risk stratification across diverse populations. By quantifying interactions between biomechanical forces, tissue adaptation, and rehabilitation adherence, the models aim to generate actionable thresholds for injury prevention and personalized recovery timelines. Anticipated outcomes include open-access tools for clinicians to simulate injury scenarios and evaluate intervention efficacy in silico, reducing trial-and-error approaches in treatment planning. This work will establish a scalable computational framework to address gaps in sports injury research, with translational potential to improve return-to-play decision-making and reduce the burden of musculoskeletal disorders in athletic populations.
cip_definition: Research on how to prevent and manage athletic injuries and to provide appropriate care for all structures of the musculoskeletal system directly affected by participation in sporting activity.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of persuasive communication in digital media environments through large-scale computational analysis of multimodal discourse. As digital platforms increasingly shape public opinion, understanding how rhetorical strategies—such as argumentation frameworks, emotional appeals, and nonverbal cues—interact across text, audio, and visual modalities remains a critical challenge. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and complexity of modern communication ecosystems, necessitating advanced computational tools. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze a corpus of 10 million social media posts, political speeches, and multimedia content from diverse cultural contexts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models to detect rhetorical patterns, sentiment trajectories, and cross-modal coherence at scale, while maintaining sensitivity to contextual factors like audience demographics and platform-specific norms. Parallel processing will enable real-time simulation of information diffusion networks to model how persuasive messages evolve through user interactions. Expected outcomes include (1) a taxonomy of effective multimodal rhetorical strategies in digital persuasion, (2) predictive models linking specific communication patterns to audience engagement metrics, and (3) open-source tools for ethical discourse analysis. These contributions will advance rhetorical theory by quantitatively testing classical frameworks against contemporary digital practices while providing evidence-based guidance for communication professionals addressing societal challenges like misinformation and polarization. The project’s scale—requiring simultaneous analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, complex neural network architectures, and dynamic network simulations—fundamentally depends on HPC capabilities for distributed processing, GPU-accelerated model training, and high-memory data handling beyond conventional computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific, humanistic, and critical study of human communication in a variety of formats, media, and contexts. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of interpersonal, group, organizational, professional, and intercultural communication; speaking and listening; verbal and nonverbal interaction; rhetorical theory and criticism; performance studies; argumentation and persuasion; technologically mediated communication; popular culture; and various contextual applications.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized motor rehabilitation frameworks for individuals with neurological impairments, a critical focus area within pre-occupational therapy education and practice. Current rehabilitation protocols often adopt generalized approaches, which fail to account for the heterogeneity in neural recovery patterns, sensorimotor deficits, and patient-specific environmental contexts. To address this gap, we propose a computational study integrating multimodal neuroimaging, biomechanical movement data, and machine learning to model patient-specific motor learning processes. The research will analyze high-resolution functional MRI (fMRI) and motion capture datasets from stroke survivors to identify neural correlates of motor adaptation, combined with biomechanical simulations of upper-limb task performance under varying environmental constraints. Deep reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on these datasets to predict optimal therapeutic task progressions tailored to individual neurophysiological profiles and functional goals. The computational workflow demands significant parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization in biomechanical simulations, as well as GPU-accelerated training of neural networks on heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework that maps neuroplasticity dynamics to personalized rehabilitation strategies, thereby informing clinical decision-making and enhancing pre-occupational therapy curricula with data-driven approaches to intervention design. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational neuroscience, rehabilitation engineering, and occupational therapy, offering a novel paradigm for optimizing motor recovery while aligning with emerging trends in precision rehabilitation. The project’s success hinges on HPC capabilities to manage computationally intensive simulations and machine learning workflows, which are infeasible on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an immersive, generative multimedia installation that integrates real-time sensor data, machine learning (ML), and high-fidelity visual and spatial audio rendering to explore dynamic human-environment interactions. The research addresses the challenge of processing and synthesizing heterogeneous data streams—including motion, biometrics, and environmental inputs—into cohesive, responsive artistic outputs. Current tools for real-time multimedia synthesis struggle with scalability when managing simultaneous high-resolution visual, auditory, and interactive components, particularly when integrating latency-sensitive ML models. To overcome these limitations, the project requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize rendering tasks, train generative adversarial networks (GANs) for adaptive visual texture synthesis, and optimize fluid dynamics simulations for particle-based audio-visual effects. Computational methods will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks such as Unity’s High-Definition Render Pipeline and PyTorch for ML inference, alongside custom CUDA kernels for real-time data fusion. A key innovation involves distributed computing to decouple sensor data processing (via IoT middleware) from rendering pipelines, ensuring stability during large-scale audience interactions. Expected outcomes include a publicly exhibited installation that dynamically evolves based on participant behavior and environmental conditions, alongside an open-source toolkit for scalable multimedia synthesis. This work bridges computational art and human-computer interaction, offering new methods for resource-efficient, data-driven artistic practice. The HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the necessary frame rates (≥60 fps) and audio latency (<20 ms) for immersive experiences while handling terabyte-scale datasets from multi-sensor arrays. Results will advance interdisciplinary discourse in computational aesthetics and provide a framework for future artists working at the intersection of real-time media and emergent technologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive instructional tools for students with diverse learning needs in special education. A critical challenge in the field is the efficient personalization of learning interventions, which requires real-time analysis of complex, multimodal datasets (e.g., behavioral logs, academic performance metrics, and physiological sensor data) to detect patterns in student engagement and learning barriers. Traditional methods for analyzing these datasets are limited by computational bottlenecks, restricting the scalability and responsiveness of adaptive systems. This project proposes a computational approach using machine learning (ML) models, including transformer-based architectures and reinforcement learning, to process and interpret heterogeneous educational data streams. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training of deep learning models on large-scale datasets spanning anonymized student records, eye-tracking data, and interaction logs from digital learning platforms. Key objectives include (1) developing predictive models to identify optimal intervention strategies for individual learners based on dynamic profiles, (2) simulating the longitudinal impacts of personalized interventions through agent-based modeling, and (3) generating synthetic datasets to address privacy-preserving model training challenges in educational contexts. The outcomes will yield open-source tools for educators to design data-driven Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and real-time feedback systems. By accelerating the analysis of high-dimensional educational data, this work aims to bridge gaps between special education research and classroom practice, empowering teachers with scalable computational resources to address variability in learning disabilities. The requested HPC allocation will directly support GPU-intensive tasks, hyperparameter optimization, and large-scale simulations critical to achieving robust, generalizable models for equitable special education delivery.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing sustainable architectural design in Pre-Architecture Studies. Traditional design processes often rely on iterative manual adjustments to balance environmental performance, structural efficiency, and human-centric spatial quality, a method that is time-intensive and limited in handling complex, multivariate scenarios. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by integrating generative design algorithms, climate-responsive simulations, and ergonomic analysis into a unified computational workflow. Using parametric modeling tools and machine learning, the project will automate the exploration of design permutations that minimize energy consumption while maximizing spatial functionality and aesthetic coherence. Key computational methods include finite element analysis for structural stress testing, agent-based modeling to simulate human movement and interaction within virtual environments, and dynamic thermal simulations to predict building performance under diverse climatic conditions. These processes demand significant parallel processing capabilities to manage large-scale datasets and real-time feedback loops between design parameters and performance metrics. The anticipated outcomes include a scalable, open-source toolkit for pre-architecture education and practice, enabling students to rapidly prototype designs that align with decarbonization goals and adaptive reuse principles. By bridging architectural theory, environmental ethics, and computational innovation, this project aims to advance pedagogical approaches in Pre-Architecture Studies while contributing methodological frameworks for sustainable design in non-science disciplines. The HPC resources will facilitate the analysis of thousands of design iterations, reducing computational bottlenecks and fostering data-driven decision-making in early-stage architectural ideation.
cip_definition: A program of study that is a precursor to an advanced degree in architecture. Includes instruction in architectural design, architectural graphics, architectural history, architectural technology, architectural theory and criticism, building technology, calculus, design studio, human factors, environmental architecture, geometry and trigonometry, physics, and technical drawing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools for real-time spatial audio synthesis and interactive music systems, addressing the challenge of creating immersive, dynamically adaptive soundscapes for virtual/augmented reality (VR/AR) and live performance contexts. Current methods for 3D audio rendering struggle to balance high spatial precision with low latency, particularly in environments requiring real-time interaction or adaptive acoustic responses. To overcome these limitations, the research will implement parallelized physical modeling algorithms and machine learning-driven sound propagation simulations optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations for room acoustics, neural networks trained on spectral impulse response datasets, and distributed processing of multichannel audio streams. The project will leverage large-scale parameter sweeps to optimize hybrid models combining physics-based and data-driven approaches, enabling efficient synthesis of spatially complex auditory environments. Expected outcomes include open-source software frameworks for real-time spatial audio manipulation and novel metrics for evaluating perceptual accuracy in dynamic 3D sound fields. These tools will directly benefit music technology research by enabling new forms of computational composition and performance while advancing interdisciplinary applications in VR/AR development. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the memory-intensive wave equation simulations and large neural network architectures required to model high-frequency audio interactions at scale, tasks infeasible on standard workstations. By bridging music cognition research with computational acoustics, this work aims to establish new best practices for technology-mediated musical expression and interactive audio design.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the creative aspects of the blending of music and technology; and that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the composition, recording, synthesis, and performance of music; audio-visual production; scoring for film and multimedia; and software and multimedia development. Includes instruction in music theory, music history, composition, acoustics, recording technology, computer composition, electronic music synthesis, technology-based performance, 3D sound and spatial audio, and music business and law.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing plant health and landscape sustainability in managed green spaces through advanced computational modeling of dynamic plant-environment interactions. Current landscaping practices rely heavily on generalized guidelines for irrigation, nutrient application, and pest management, which often fail to account for micro-scale variations in soil composition, microclimate, and plant phenology. We propose to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating agent-based modeling of plant growth with real-time environmental data assimilation to predict outcomes under diverse management scenarios. The computational approach will couple process-based models of turfgrass and ornamental species physiology with machine learning algorithms trained on hyperspectral imaging data and IoT sensor feeds from experimental plots. High-performance computing resources are essential to parameterize species-specific responses across heterogeneous landscapes, simulate water-nutrient dynamics at sub-meter scales, and conduct Monte Carlo analyses of long-term management strategies under climate uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of prescribing spatially variable irrigation schedules, fertilizer application rates, and species selection matrices that minimize resource use while maintaining aesthetic and functional requirements. By enabling precision landscaping at scale, this research will provide commercial groundskeeping operations and urban planners with evidence-based tools to reduce water consumption by an estimated 15-25%, decrease chemical inputs, and enhance climate resilience in designed landscapes. The proposed work directly advances the agricultural sciences through novel applications of computational agroinformatics to ornamental horticulture, while maintaining strict exclusion of natural ecosystem conservation aspects to align with program scope.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and maintain indoor and/or outdoor ornamental and recreational plants and groundcovers and related conceptual designs established by landscape architects, interior designers, enterprise owners or managers, and individual clients. Includes instruction in applicable principles of horticulture, gardening, plant and soil irrigation and nutrition, turf maintenance, plant maintenance, equipment operation and maintenance, personnel supervision, and purchasing.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of analyzing large-scale economic and business datasets in journalism, where traditional computational tools are increasingly inadequate for real-time, data-driven storytelling. Business and economic journalists face challenges in efficiently processing heterogeneous data—such as global financial markets data, corporate disclosures, social media sentiment, and macroeconomic indicators—while maintaining analytical rigor and meeting tight deadlines. This research proposes the development of a scalable computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and analysis workflows for investigative and explanatory reporting. The methodology integrates natural language processing (NLP) to extract insights from unstructured text (e.g., earnings calls, regulatory filings), machine learning models to detect patterns in market trends and corporate behavior, and interactive visualization tools to communicate findings across multimedia platforms. Key computational tasks include parallel processing of terabyte-scale historical financial datasets, sentiment analysis of news archives, and real-time simulation of economic policy impacts using agent-based models. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated computing for training deep learning models on textual corpora and deploy containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated business data journalism, case studies demonstrating HPC-enabled investigative reporting techniques, and pedagogical resources for training journalists in computational storytelling. By enhancing the capacity to synthesize complex economic information rapidly, this work aims to elevate the precision and impact of business journalism while fostering public understanding of economic systems. The requested HPC resources are critical to overcoming latency and scalability barriers inherent in analyzing cross-sectoral, high-velocity data, thereby bridging the gap between academic research tools and industry-grade journalism practices.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: Healthcare-associated adverse events remain a significant public health challenge, contributing to preventable patient harm and systemic inefficiencies. This project seeks to develop predictive models for identifying latent risks in clinical workflows and evaluating large-scale intervention strategies using advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on the limitations of current risk assessment tools, which often fail to account for complex interactions between human factors, organizational dynamics, and evolving care protocols in modern healthcare systems. We propose a multi-modal computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinical notes, and incident reporting system data from 23 affiliated hospitals (n≈4.1 million encounters). Deep learning architectures will be implemented to model temporal patterns in adverse event trajectories, while natural language processing techniques will extract critical contextual features from clinician narratives. Agent-based modeling simulations will test the theoretical impact of safety interventions across heterogeneous care environments, requiring parallelized computation of >10,000 scenario permutations. The computational workflow demands significant GPU-accelerated processing for training transformer-based models on multi-site EHR data and running real-time sensitivity analyses on intervention parameters. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive framework for anticipating preventable harm events with temporal-spatial granularity, (2) quantitative evidence for optimizing resource allocation in safety initiatives, and (3) open-source tools for simulating care pathway modifications under different risk profiles. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for reducing preventable medical errors through data-driven approaches, with particular significance for health systems managing competing safety and operational demands. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the scale and complexity of multimodal healthcare data while maintaining necessary computational throughput for iterative model development and validation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of transformative mechanisms and evidence-based protocols to reduce preventable patient harm and improve clinical outcomes. Includes instruction in healthcare quality, patient safety, research methods, program evaluation, epidemiology, legal and regulatory compliance, systems thinking, human factors engineering, and risk management.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable water management systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize wastewater treatment and recycling processes. Current challenges include accurately modeling complex biological and chemical interactions within treatment systems, predicting contaminant removal efficiency under variable operational conditions, and scaling laboratory-derived process parameters to full-scale implementations. This project proposes to develop a multi-scale computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges through three primary objectives: (1) simulating hydrodynamic behavior and mass transfer in membrane filtration systems using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with adaptive mesh refinement, (2) parameterizing biofilm growth and nutrient degradation kinetics in bioreactors via agent-based modeling coupled with machine learning optimization, and (3) validating predictive models for emerging contaminant removal through ensemble molecular dynamics simulations of adsorption processes. The computational workflow will integrate open-source solvers (OpenFOAM, LAMMPS) with custom Python-based analytics pipelines to process terabyte-scale simulation outputs. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution for capturing microscale biofilm dynamics (μm-scale over 100+ hours) while maintaining system-scale predictive capability. Expected outcomes include optimized membrane module designs reducing energy consumption by 15-20%, validated operational thresholds for biofilm-based nutrient recovery systems, and predictive tools for selecting adsorbent materials targeting pharmaceutical residues in recycled water. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation treatment plants with enhanced recycling capacity, addressing critical gaps in water scarcity mitigation. The developed models and datasets will be made available through a public repository to support workforce training in computational water quality management.
cip_title: Water Quality and Wastewater Treatment Management and Recycling Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using water storage, waterpower, and wastewater treatment systems. Includes instruction in water storage, power and/or treatment systems and equipment; testing and inspection procedures; system maintenance procedures; and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize radiation therapy treatment planning while minimizing secondary cancer risks associated with stray radiation exposure—a critical public health concern in medical physics. Current protocols prioritize tumor targeting but lack robust models to predict long-term carcinogenic effects on healthy tissues, particularly for pediatric and genetically susceptible populations. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating Monte Carlo radiation transport modeling with patient-specific genomic and radiobiological data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute parallelized simulations of radiation dose deposition at sub-millimeter resolution across heterogeneous anatomical phantoms, coupled with probabilistic risk models informed by population-level epidemiological datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on these outputs to identify dose-distribution patterns that balance therapeutic efficacy with lifetime risk thresholds. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for rapid Monte Carlo iterations and CPU clusters for large-scale parameter sweeps across radiation types, energy levels, and patient demographics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide clinical decision-making, reduce secondary malignancy rates, and inform public health guidelines on radiation safety. By openly sharing optimized codebases and risk-assessment modules, this work will empower broader research into radiation-related health disparities. The project’s scale—requiring ~200,000 core-hours for sensitivity analyses of 10+ cancer types and 3D dose reconstructions from historical treatment data—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation. Results will advance precision radiology while addressing a systemic challenge in public health: mitigating unintended consequences of life-saving medical technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics, nuclear science, and engineering physics to diagnostic, treatment, and therapeutic processes and public health protection. Includes instruction in radiation biophysics, biophysics, health effects of natural and artificially induced radiation, hazard evaluation, environmental radioactivity, nuclear physics, engineering physics, radiobiology, medical radiology, calibration and dosage theory, computer applications and medical informatics, and specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the multilevel determinants of demographic change in rapidly aging societies, with a focus on modeling the complex interdependencies between migration patterns, fertility transitions, and mortality dynamics. Traditional demographic methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops and spatial-temporal heterogeneities inherent in these processes, particularly when scaling to national or transnational populations. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with Bayesian hierarchical inference, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate population dynamics at scale. The ABM will incorporate individual-level decision-making rules, household structures, and macro-level policy environments, calibrated using longitudinal census data, vital registration systems, and cross-national survey datasets. A key innovation involves coupling this model with spatially explicit environmental and economic covariates to project localized demographic pressures under varying climate change and urbanization scenarios. The computational demands are substantial: stochastic simulations across parameter spaces require millions of CPU-hours, while Bayesian parameter estimation via Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods necessitates parallelized processing of high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical leverage points in demographic systems that could inform targeted policy interventions, (2) probabilistic projections of population aging trajectories under alternative migration and fertility assumptions, and (3) open-source tools for scalable demographic simulation. By elucidating how micro-level behaviors aggregate to macro-level trends, this work will advance methodological integration in population studies while providing actionable insights for governments managing aging populations. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome memory and processing constraints encountered in pilot studies, enabling the first globally scalable application of this hybrid modeling approach.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in demography, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and validation of computational models for optimizing personalized counseling interventions in diverse populations. Counseling psychology faces a critical challenge in tailoring therapeutic strategies to individual clients’ dynamic needs, particularly when addressing complex, overlapping distress symptoms (e.g., anxiety, relational conflicts, identity-related stressors) that vary across cultural and socioeconomic contexts. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to model the nonlinear interactions between client characteristics, intervention techniques, and longitudinal outcomes. To address this, we propose building machine learning (ML) frameworks trained on multimodal datasets, including anonymized clinical session transcripts, client self-report metrics, and demographic data from supervised counseling practice archives. These models will integrate natural language processing (NLP) to analyze therapeutic dialogue patterns, graph neural networks to map symptom interdependencies, and reinforcement learning to simulate intervention adaptation over time. The scale of data (projected at 50,000+ session records) and complexity of modeling temporal, textual, and relational variables necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized training and large-scale hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive tools to identify client subgroups most likely to benefit from specific counseling modalities, (2) a computational framework for simulating the longitudinal impacts of culturally adapted interventions, and (3) open-source algorithms to help practitioners refine case conceptualizations. By bridging counseling psychology’s human-centered ethos with computational rigor, this work aims to enhance equitable access to effective mental health support while maintaining ethical alignment with client autonomy and therapeutic relationship principles. The requested resources will enable iterative model development, including sensitivity analyses to mitigate algorithmic bias and ensure interpretability for clinical utility.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of psychological counseling, involving the rendering of therapeutic services to individuals and groups experiencing psychological problems and exhibiting distress symptoms. Includes instruction in counseling theory, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient/counselor relationships, testing and assessment methods and procedures, group therapy, marital and family therapy, child and adolescent therapy, supervised counseling practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational challenges in advancing jewelry design innovation and material optimization. Traditional jewelry arts rely on labor-intensive experimentation to balance aesthetic intent with material constraints, such as metal fatigue, gemstone structural integrity, and thermal behavior during casting or enameling. However, the complex interplay of physical forces, microstructural evolution, and geometric variables in these processes limits the scalability of empirical methods. This project proposes a computational framework combining finite element analysis (FEA), molecular dynamics simulations, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to model material responses, predict fabrication outcomes, and explore design spaces. HPC resources will enable multi-physics simulations of metalforming techniques (e.g., electroforming current distribution, stress gradients in lapidary work) at micron-scale resolutions, coupled with machine learning-driven optimization of stone-cutting angles for light refraction efficiency. A parallel focus involves training GANs on historical and contemporary jewelry corpora to generate culturally informed, structurally feasible design variants while minimizing material waste. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating process parameters (e.g., alloy composition, annealing schedules) with mechanical and aesthetic properties, reducing trial-and-error cycles in studio practice. The integration of computational materials science with generative design aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainable jewelry production, preserving craft traditions while expanding creative possibilities through digital innovation. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for jewelry educators and workshops demonstrating computational workflows, fostering interdisciplinary dialogue between artisanal practices and computational research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by fashioning jewelry from gems, other stones, and precious metals. Includes instruction in design concepts, electroforming, enameling, gemology, lapidary technique and art, metal and non-metal casting and molding, metal coloring, metalsmithing and finishing, personal style development, photo etching, and stone cutting and polishing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary investigation into the dynamics of cultural and intellectual exchange across premodern Afro-Eurasian societies. The research problem centers on analyzing fragmented, multilingual textual and material records (e.g., trade logs, religious manuscripts, artistic motifs) to trace the diffusion of ideas, technologies, and social practices between 500–1500 CE. Existing scholarship lacks systematic computational frameworks to integrate these heterogeneous datasets, which span archaeology, linguistics, and historiography. The project will develop scalable natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to parse and align digitized texts in Arabic, Sanskrit, and classical Chinese, combined with network analysis models to map connectivity patterns across trade routes and urban hubs. Computational challenges include handling non-Latin scripts, fragmentary or damaged source materials, and spatial-temporal data normalization across disparate scholarly corpora. The HPC environment is critical for training transformer-based models on low-resource historical languages, running agent-based simulations of cultural transmission, and visualizing multilayer networks at continental scales. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access digital repository of annotated, cross-referenced primary sources; (2) quantitative metrics for assessing the role of environmental factors versus institutional actors in shaping intercultural exchange; and (3) methodological frameworks for reconciling humanistic interpretations with computational pattern detection. By bridging computational social science and digital humanities approaches, this work aims to redefine narratives about globalization’s antecedents while demonstrating how HPC can catalyze resource-intensive, multidisciplinary inquiry in liberal arts contexts. The results will inform curriculum development in global history and computational humanities programs, emphasizing data-driven perspectives on cultural complexity.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences/ Liberal Studies
cip_definition: A program that is a structured combination of the arts, biological and physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities, emphasizing breadth of study. Includes instruction in independently designed, individualized, or regular programs.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance and novel viral pathogens in animal populations presents significant challenges to veterinary medicine and public health. Traditional laboratory techniques often lack the resolution to unravel complex host-microbe interactions at scale, necessitating advanced computational approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underpinning pathogen virulence, transmission dynamics, and host immune evasion in agriculturally and companionally relevant species. Using multi-omics integration, we will analyze genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from clinically significant bacterial and viral pathogens, including avian influenza strains and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural variations in key virulence factors under selective pressure from antimicrobial agents. Epidemiological modeling powered by agent-based frameworks will simulate outbreak scenarios across diverse animal populations. The computational pipeline will employ machine learning algorithms to identify conserved antigenic epitopes for vaccine development and predict resistance gene transfer probabilities. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, improved risk assessment models for zoonotic spillover events, and optimized vaccination protocols tailored to specific livestock production systems. By integrating large-scale data analytics with mechanistic modeling, this research aims to advance translational veterinary medicine while informing One Health initiatives at the animal-human-environment interface. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of sequencing data, executing computationally intensive simulations, and training predictive models—tasks infeasible with standard laboratory infrastructure. This work will directly contribute to mitigating antimicrobial resistance, enhancing animal welfare, and reducing economic losses in agricultural systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on clinical applications of research on harmful microorganisms, including viruses, and of the disease processes they induce in animals.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between urban environmental stimuli and dynamic cognitive load modulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model how multisensory input patterns influence decision-making efficiency in pedestrian navigation contexts. While prior psychology research has examined environmental stressors or cognitive load in isolation, this work integrates real-world spatial-auditory-visual datasets with individualized cognitive resource allocation models to predict adaptive behavior in complex, noisy environments—a novel intersection of environmental psychology, cognitive neuroscience, and computational urban science. The core challenge lies in simulating high-dimensional interactions between fluctuating environmental parameters (e.g., crowd density metrics, acoustic signatures, architectural affordances) and neural resource competition processes at millisecond timescales. We propose developing hybrid neural networks that combine biologically constrained cortical column models with transformer architectures to process geospatial-temporal data streams from 12 global cities. These models will be trained on both experimental data (360-degree VR navigation tasks with EEG/fNIRS monitoring) and synthetic environments generated through procedural urban space algorithms. The HPC infrastructure is critical for three components: 1) Parallel processing of petascale urban sensor datasets, 2) Evolutionary optimization of cognitive architecture hyperparameters across 50,000+ simulated agents, and 3) Real-time ray tracing for psychoacoustic and visual clutter simulations in Unity-based experimental paradigms. Anticipated outcomes include the first predictive framework mapping nonlinear relationships between environmental complexity gradients and cognitive performance thresholds, with applications for adaptive urban design and spatial cognition-aware navigation systems. This work establishes a computational psychology paradigm for studying embodied cognition in built environments while advancing methods for coupling neural dynamical systems with large-scale environmental simulations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the critical challenge of personalized dietary intervention optimization by investigating the complex interplay between host metabolism, gut microbiota dynamics, and nutritional inputs. Current clinical nutrition frameworks often rely on population-level recommendations, which fail to account for individual variations in microbial community structure, metabolic pathways, and nutrient processing efficiency. We propose to develop a computational platform integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and proteomic profiles) with physiological parameters to model personalized nutrient-microbiome-host interactions. The research will employ machine learning algorithms to identify predictive biomarkers of dietary response variability and agent-based modeling to simulate microbial community shifts under different nutritional regimes. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (>10 TB of multi-omics data from clinical cohorts), training deep neural networks to recognize nonlinear relationships between dietary components and metabolic outcomes, and running parallelized simulations of gut ecosystem dynamics across diverse virtual patient profiles. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-source predictive tool for optimizing clinical nutrition strategies in metabolic disorders, identification of microbial taxa associated with differential nutrient absorption efficiency, and novel insights into temporal patterns of microbiome-mediated food compound transformation. This work bridges computational biology, systems nutrition, and clinical dietetics, offering a transformative approach to precision nutrition that could inform therapeutic dietary interventions for conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and micronutrient deficiency syndromes. The computational framework developed will enable real-time adjustment of dietary recommendations based on individual microbial and metabolic signatures, advancing the field beyond current one-size-fits-all paradigms in clinical nutrition practice.
cip_title: Dietetics and Clinical Nutrition Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dietetics and clinical nutrition services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational workflows to optimize the design and simulation of complex mechanical systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Mechanical drafting and CAD/CADD workflows increasingly require high-fidelity simulations to validate designs for manufacturability, structural integrity, and operational efficiency. However, traditional CAD tools struggle with the computational demands of multi-physics simulations (e.g., thermal-stress coupling, fluid-structure interactions) and large-scale parametric studies, particularly when applied to intricate assemblies or high-resolution geometries. This bottleneck limits the ability to explore design spaces efficiently and delays iterative improvements. To address this, the proposed research will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers tailored for mechanical drafting applications.
