Key computational challenges include managing large-scale optimization of routing strategies under uncertainty, resolving conflicts in multi-agent systems, and simulating energy consumption patterns across heterogeneous vehicle types. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for urban mobility planning, quantitative benchmarks for fleet deployment scenarios, and energy-optimal control strategies adaptable to diverse city layouts. The work will directly support municipal transportation agencies and vehicle manufacturers in evaluating system-level impacts of autonomous technologies while advancing computational methods for real-time traffic optimization. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project aims to overcome current limitations in simulation fidelity and scale, enabling analysis of city-wide networks with sub-second temporal granularity—an essential requirement for operationalizing autonomous fleets in complex urban environments. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and collaborative workshops with industry partners to accelerate adoption of data-driven transportation solutions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle and equipment operation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic spatial organization of cellular components during tissue morphogenesis, a fundamental yet poorly understood process in developmental anatomy. A critical gap persists in modeling how mechanical forces and intracellular signaling pathways collectively drive the emergence of three-dimensional tissue architecture. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with continuum mechanics to simulate multicellular systems at subcellular resolution. The ABM component will represent individual cells as discrete entities with rule-based behaviors, while finite element methods will model stress propagation across extracellular matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the scale of these simulations, which require tracking >10^5 interacting cellular agents with micrometer-level spatial precision over developmental timescales (48-72 simulated hours). Parallelized code will leverage GPU acceleration to optimize force calculations and matrix solvers. Experimental validation will utilize time-lapse microscopy datasets of avian limb bud development, with machine learning pipelines (deployed on HPC clusters) quantifying cytoskeletal dynamics and strain patterns from 4D imaging data. Expected outcomes include: 1) identification of critical force thresholds regulating epithelial folding patterns, 2) predictive models of tissue buckling under genetic perturbation scenarios, and 3) open-source simulation tools for visualizing mechanochemical coupling in developing tissues. This work will advance our mechanistic understanding of how cellular-scale processes generate anatomical form, with implications for congenital defect research and bioengineered tissue design. The requested computing allocation (500,000 CPU-core hours, 2 TB RAM allocation, and GPU node access) will enable parameter space exploration across physiologically relevant mechanical regimes currently inaccessible through conventional computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_title: Cell/ Cellular Biology and Anatomical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cell/cellular biology and anatomical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis of Jewish philosophical and religious manuscripts, with a focus on tracing the evolution of hermeneutical and ethical frameworks across diasporic contexts. The central research problem lies in the fragmented and multilingual nature of Jewish textual traditions, which span Hebrew, Aramaic, Judeo-Arabic, and other languages, often embedded in commentaries spanning centuries. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically analyze conceptual shifts, intertextual dependencies, or geographic-cultural variations at scale. Our computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques optimized for Semitic languages, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on rabbinic corpora, to map philosophical argumentation structures, semantic networks, and citation patterns across digitized manuscripts. Key datasets include the Bar-Ilan Responsa Project, the Sefaria Library, and newly digitized Kabbalistic works from the 13th–18th centuries. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these texts, training multilingual embeddings to detect latent theological or ethical concepts, and network analysis of intellectual influence across temporal and spatial axes (e.g., comparing Sephardic and Ashkenazi interpretive traditions). Expected outcomes include (1) identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal synergies or tensions between philosophical schools, (2) quantitative models of how legal-ethical reasoning adapted to diaspora conditions, and (3) an open-access computational toolkit for Jewish textual analysis. This work will provide novel insights into Judaism’s intellectual adaptability while demonstrating how HPC can address enduring challenges in religious studies, such as analyzing multilayered commentary traditions or reconciling normative texts with lived ethical practice. The project bridges computational humanities and Judaic studies, offering methodological frameworks applicable to other religious traditions with complex textual histories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. Includes instruction in Jewish religious heritage, sacred texts, and law; Jewish philosophy and intellectual history; Jewish life and culture, both in Israel and the Jewish Diaspora; historical Jewish minority cultures such as the Yiddish, Sephardic, and other; anti-Semitism, gentile relations and Shoa; Zionism; and modern developments within Judaism.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of under-documented and typologically diverse languages, focusing on cross-linguistic patterns in morphological and syntactic structures. While advances in natural language processing (NLP) have transformed research on high-resource languages, many languages—particularly those with complex agglutinative or polysynthetic morphologies—remain understudied due to a lack of tailored computational tools and scalable resources. Our research aims to develop and apply high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled methods to analyze large-scale multilingual corpora, including historical texts, transcribed oral narratives, and modern digital communications from under-resourced language communities. Key computational tasks include parallelized morphological parsing, automated alignment of dialectal variants, and probabilistic modeling of syntactic change over time. These methods will leverage GPU-accelerated machine learning frameworks to train transformer-based models on distributed datasets spanning multiple language families, enabling efficient handling of non-linear morphological rules and low-resource training scenarios. The project will also employ agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about language contact dynamics and the diffusion of grammatical features. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philological analysis, this work will generate novel insights into universal and language-specific structural constraints, while contributing open-source tools for processing morphologically rich languages. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of annotated corpora, optimized NLP pipelines for under-documented languages, and interdisciplinary frameworks for modeling linguistic diversity. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the iterative training of large language models, process terabyte-scale text and audio datasets, and run computationally intensive simulations. This research will advance both theoretical linguistics and computational methodologies, offering scalable solutions to challenges in language preservation, typological classification, and the study of linguistic evolution.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Foreign Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational study of cross-cultural religious textual traditions, addressing gaps in scalability and analytical depth within current digital humanities methodologies. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing patterns in religious thought, symbolism, and narrative structures across vast, multilingual corpora, including Buddhist sutras, Abrahamic scriptures, and Indigenous oral tradition transcriptions. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to identify latent thematic connections or quantify doctrinal evolution at scale, particularly when examining understudied textual interactions between major and minor religious traditions. To address this, we propose a multi-modal computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning classification. The workflow will process digitized primary texts in original languages (Sanskrit, Pali, Classical Arabic, etc.) and translations using transformer-based models fine-tuned for historical religious language, enabling semantic similarity mapping and motif tracking across traditions. Network models will then visualize the diffusion of cosmological concepts and ritual practices, while clustering algorithms will identify statistically significant variations in ethical frameworks. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, managing terabyte-scale textual datasets, and running iterative simulations of hypothetical transmission pathways. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping interreligious conceptual exchanges in South Asian and Mediterranean contexts between 200 BCE–500 CE, 2) quantitative models challenging assumptions about doctrinal boundaries in syncretic traditions, and 3) open-source tools for automated comparative analysis of ritual narratives. By enabling systematic large-scale comparison, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how religious ideas hybridize across cultural contexts while establishing computational methods as central to future phenomenological studies in religion. The requested resources directly support the development of reproducible, data-driven frameworks for analyzing religious pluralism—a pressing need in interdisciplinary humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature of religious belief and specific religious and quasi-religious systems. Includes instruction in phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature and art of religion; mythology; scriptural and textual studies; religious history and politics; and specific studies of particular faith communities and their behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms driving antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens and their interactions with host immune responses. A critical challenge in infectious disease management is the rapid evolution of multidrug-resistant pathogens, which undermines therapeutic efficacy and complicates global health interventions. Current gaps in understanding how microbial communities adapt to antimicrobial pressures—and how these adaptations modulate host-pathogen interactions—limit the development of targeted treatments. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and machine learning (ML) to model bacterial protein-ligand interactions under selective drug pressure, alongside agent-based simulations of microbial population dynamics in host environments. MD simulations will focus on key resistance-conferring enzymes (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps) to map structural and energetic changes associated with resistance mutations. Concurrently, agent-based models will simulate polymicrobial community behaviors under varying immune conditions, incorporating data on phagocyte activity and cytokine signaling. ML algorithms will analyze genomic and transcriptomic datasets from clinical isolates to identify predictive markers of emergent resistance. By utilizing HPC resources, these computationally intensive workflows will enable large-scale, parallelized simulations and high-dimensional data integration. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into resistance evolution, immune evasion strategies, and community-level microbial resilience. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation antimicrobials and immunotherapies, while providing a framework to anticipate resistance trends in clinical and environmental settings. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the resolution and throughput required for these analyses, which are infeasible with standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, social, and behavioral factors contributing to the cause and spread of infectious diseases. Includes instruction in research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, disease mechanisms, antimicrobial resistance, immunology, and bioterrorism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent patterns in biological systems through large-scale simulations of organismal interactions, aiming to uncover fundamental principles underlying collective behaviors in diverse taxa. While collective phenomena—such as flocking, swarming, or synchronized signaling—are observed across biological scales, the general rules driving these behaviors remain poorly understood, particularly in non-model organisms and under variable environmental conditions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling with empirical data on movement, communication, and resource utilization from field studies of arthropods, avian groups, and marine invertebrates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating populations of >10^5 agents across parameter spaces that capture habitat heterogeneity, stochastic disturbances, and interspecific variability. Each agent will follow dynamically updated rules informed by species-specific biological constraints (e.g., sensory thresholds, energy budgets), with parallelized simulations running on GPU clusters to optimize scaling. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved interaction motifs that promote robust collective outcomes despite phylogenetic and ecological differences, and (2) predictive models of how environmental stressors disrupt or amplify self-organization. By focusing on cross-taxa principles rather than molecular or ecosystem-level mechanisms, this work bridges gaps between subdisciplines in general biology while avoiding domain-specific assumptions. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will enable researchers to test hypotheses about behavioral adaptation and resilience in biologically realistic virtual environments, advancing our capacity to study complexity in underexplored species. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential given the iterative nature of parameter optimization and the need for high-resolution, multi-generational simulations across proposed scenarios.
cip_definition: A general program of biology at the introductory, basic level or a program in biology or the biological sciences that is undifferentiated as to title or content. Includes instruction in general biology and programs covering a variety of biological specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cross-cultural trade networks in premodern Asia (c. 1200–1800 CE), with a focus on integrating fragmented textual, archaeological, and geospatial datasets. The research problem centers on reconstructing dynamic economic and cultural exchanges across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and East Asia, where surviving records—including merchant logs, port registries, and multilingual epigraphic materials—are dispersed, heterogeneous, and computationally demanding to process at scale. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to systematically correlate these sources or model large-scale patterns of interaction over time. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for classical Chinese, Arabic, and Sanskrit texts to extract named entities, transaction records, and route descriptions. These outputs will feed into spatial network models built using graph databases and agent-based simulations to map shifting trade corridors, quantify commodity flows, and assess the impact of political events on regional connectivity. A parallel workflow will apply computer vision techniques to LiDAR-derived archaeological site data from maritime entrepôts, automating the identification of infrastructure patterns linked to commercial activity. By synthesizing these computational approaches on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to resolve longstanding debates about the role of monsoon seasonality, imperial policies, and transregional institutions in shaping Asia’s economic integration. Expected outcomes include an open-access geotemporal database of trade nodes and routes, scalable tools for multilingual historical text analysis, and quantitative frameworks for evaluating connectivity’s influence on cultural exchange. This work will provide a replicable model for data-driven historical inquiry while advancing scholarly understanding of Asia’s premodern globalization, with implications for contemporary discussions about regional interdependence.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the Asian Continent from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: Early childhood education is foundational to cognitive and socioemotional development, yet optimizing instructional strategies for diverse learners remains a challenge. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling individualized learning trajectories in preschool settings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal educational data at scale. The research problem centers on the dynamic interplay between instructional methods, child-specific factors (e.g., attention span, language exposure), and learning outcomes—a complex system requiring fine-grained temporal analysis. Current approaches in teacher education often rely on aggregated classroom-level metrics, limiting personalization. To address this, we propose a machine learning pipeline integrating classroom video recordings (processed via computer vision), audio transcripts of teacher-student interactions (analyzed through NLP), and longitudinal assessments of skill acquisition. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets from 50+ classrooms, coupled with agent-based simulations to test how variations in pedagogical strategies propagate through heterogeneous learner populations. The computational models will quantify the efficacy of differentiated instruction patterns under varying resource constraints and student ability distributions. Expected outcomes include (1) probabilistic mappings between teachable moments and concept mastery rates, (2) generative AI tools to help educators anticipate individual needs during lesson planning, and (3) open-source code for simulating inclusive classroom environments. By bridging developmental theory with computational precision, this work aims to equip preschool teacher training programs with evidence-based, scalable strategies for addressing variability in early learning. The requested resources are critical for handling the temporal resolution required (sub-second behavioral coding across months of observation) and the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of plausible intervention scenarios. Results will directly inform competency frameworks in early childhood teacher education while maintaining strict privacy standards through on-premises HPC deployment.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in formal settings prior to beginning regular elementary school, usually ranging in age from three to six years (or grade one), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: The sustainable management of natural resources under escalating environmental change requires advanced predictive tools to evaluate complex ecological and socio-economic interactions. Current models often lack the spatial resolution, temporal scope, or integration of dynamic feedbacks necessary to inform adaptive policy frameworks. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution, agent-based modeling (ABM) platform to simulate coupled human-natural systems in critical watershed ecosystems. The ABM will integrate multi-scale datasets, including remote sensing-derived land-use patterns, hydrologic flow regimes, climate projections, and stakeholder decision-making behaviors, to quantify trade-offs between conservation targets, resource extraction, and climate resilience. Computational demands are significant due to the need for fine-grained spatial representation (≤100m resolution), stochastic uncertainty analyses across decadal timescales, and real-time calibration against ecological monitoring data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized model ensembles, machine learning-assisted parameter optimization, and sensitivity analyses across 10^4+ permutations. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of leverage points for policy interventions that balance biodiversity conservation with sustainable resource use under multiple climate scenarios, (2) probabilistic risk maps of habitat degradation hotspots, and (3) open-source tools for participatory scenario planning with stakeholders. The computational framework will advance capacity to anticipate cascading impacts of management decisions—a critical gap in current natural resource governance. By scaling spatially explicit simulations across heterogeneous landscapes, this work directly supports evidence-based policymaking in line with international biodiversity commitments while avoiding reliance on agricultural or veterinary science approaches. Resource allocation will prioritize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for large geospatial dataset processing.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, develop, manage, and evaluate programs to protect and regulate natural habitats and renewable natural resources. Includes instruction in the principles of wildlife and conservation biology, environmental science, animal population surveying, natural resource economics, management techniques for various habitats, applicable law and policy, administrative and communications skills, and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to model the dynamics of intergroup conflict escalation and resolution in fragile sociopolitical environments, integrating computational social science, behavioral psychology, and network theory. While traditional peace studies rely on qualitative case analyses or simplified quantitative models, this research addresses the critical gap in simulating complex, adaptive systems where nonlinear interactions between cultural narratives, economic disparities, and communication patterns drive conflict. The core computational challenge lies in scaling agent-based models (ABMs) to incorporate millions of heterogeneous agents—representing individuals, institutions, and external actors—operating across temporal, spatial, and sociocultural dimensions. These agents will be programmed with empirically derived behavioral rules informed by field data from post-conflict regions, including decision-making biases, trust thresholds, and coalition-formation heuristics. The HPC framework will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore probabilistic pathways of conflict diffusion under varying policy interventions, such as resource redistribution or mediated dialogue protocols. Key innovations include coupling graph neural networks with ABMs to capture evolving alliance structures and deploying natural language processing to analyze sentiment shifts in simulated discourse. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for predicting tipping points in communal tensions and optimizing conflict mitigation strategies. By quantifying the systemic effects of socioeconomic variables and intervention timing, this work aims to provide actionable insights for peacebuilding organizations while advancing computational methods for interdisciplinary conflict science. The scale of required simulations—necessitating terabyte-scale memory management and GPU-accelerated parameter sweeps—makes HPC resources indispensable for achieving statistically robust, generalizable results.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of international and inter-group conflicts. Includes instruction in peace research methods and related social scientific and psychological knowledge bases.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to assess the impacts of climate variability on critical watershed systems, addressing gaps in predicting how dynamic hydrological and ecological interactions influence water security and biodiversity conservation. Current models often lack the spatial resolution or computational capacity to capture nonlinear feedbacks between precipitation shifts, land cover changes, and species habitat viability at regional scales. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a coupled hydrologic-ecological model at unprecedented resolution (1 km² grid cells) across a 50,000 km² study area encompassing threatened montane and lowland ecosystems. The framework integrates satellite-derived land use data, downscaled climate projections (CMIP6), and agent-based simulations of species dispersal under habitat fragmentation. Machine learning algorithms will optimize parameter calibration across heterogeneous terrain, while parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in drought and flood scenarios under varying emission pathways. By simulating 100+ years of daily hydrological fluxes and habitat connectivity metrics, the project will identify tipping points in water availability and ecosystem resilience. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of climate refugia for endemic species, prioritized zones for watershed restoration, and open-access tools for adaptive management. The computational demands—10 TB of input data, iterative ensemble runs, and real-time visualization of multi-dimensional outputs—necessitate HPC infrastructure for memory-intensive workloads and GPU-accelerated model training. Results will directly inform regional conservation planning, providing a scalable template for assessing climate risks to natural resources in data-limited regions. This work advances computational ecology by bridging gap between process-based modeling and decision-relevant conservation analytics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in natural resources and conservation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of quantum-coherent processes in photosynthetic protein complexes under non-equilibrium conditions, integrating principles from quantum biophysics, photochemistry, and condensed matter physics. While quantum effects in biological systems have been studied in isolated contexts, the interplay between coherent energy transfer, environmental decoherence, and protein conformational fluctuations remains poorly understood. The central challenge lies in modeling these multiscale interactions across temporal (femtoseconds to milliseconds) and spatial (angstroms to micrometers) scales, requiring unprecedented computational synthesis of quantum dynamics, molecular mechanics, and mesoscale environmental perturbations. The research will employ hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations combined with tensor network algorithms optimized for photosynthetic exciton systems, executed on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to achieve the necessary parallelization of multidimensional parameter spaces. Key innovations include adaptive sampling protocols to track rare conformational states influencing coherence lifetimes and machine learning-driven dimensionality reduction for analyzing simulation trajectories. Expected outcomes include predictive models of how specific protein architectures protect quantum coherence under physiological noise, with implications for bio-inspired quantum material design and synthetic biology applications. The computational framework will also enable exploration of nonequilibrium control strategies using tailored electromagnetic fields to enhance coherent energy transport—a potential gateway to novel photonic technologies. By bridging quantum physics with structural biology and nonlinear dynamics, this work addresses a critical gap in understanding life’s potential exploitation of quantum phenomena while establishing scalable computational methodologies for studying complexity across biological and quantum systems. Resource allocation is essential for handling the project’s teraflop-scale demands, particularly for GPU-accelerated quantum dynamical calculations and large-scale Monte Carlo sampling of conformational landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that is either a general synthesis of one or more of the biological and physical sciences, or a specialization which draws from the biological and physical sciences.

abstract: This research project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies and inaccuracies in medical insurance coding processes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven predictive framework. Medical coding, a critical interface between clinical care and billing systems, faces challenges due to the complexity of evolving code sets (e.g., ICD-11, CPT), heterogeneous electronic health record (EHR) data structures, and human error in code assignment. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) and deep learning architectures to analyze multi-modal clinical documentation—including provider notes, imaging reports, and procedural summaries—to predict optimal code combinations. By training transformer-based models on de-identified datasets spanning 10 million patient encounters from diverse healthcare systems, the computational approach will focus on semantic context extraction, code conflict resolution, and real-time compliance checks against Medicare and third-party payer policies. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, hyperparameter optimization for ensemble models, and simulation of coding scenarios under varying regulatory constraints. Expected outcomes include a validated AI-assisted coding tool that reduces claim denials by ≥25%, identifies documentation gaps contributing to coding ambiguities, and dynamically adapts to annual coding updates. This work bridges health informatics, computational linguistics, and reimbursement policy analysis, offering a novel pathway to enhance financial sustainability for healthcare institutions while maintaining coding education relevance in an increasingly automated landscape. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, secure data storage compliant with HIPAA and HITECH standards, and scalable deployment architecture for integration with existing coding software ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized data entry, classification, and record-keeping procedures related to medical diagnostic, treatment, billing, and insurance documentation. Includes instruction in medical records and insurance software applications, basic anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, fundamentals of medical science and treatment procedures, data classification and coding, data entry skills, and regulations relating to Medicare and insurance documentation.

abstract: The integration of telemedicine into clinical practice has the potential to revolutionize healthcare delivery, particularly in underserved populations. However, scaling telemedicine platforms to handle real-time, multimodal patient data—including high-resolution imaging, continuous biosensor streams, and electronic health records—requires computational resources capable of processing and analyzing large datasets with low latency. Current systems often struggle with the volume and heterogeneity of data, leading to delays in clinical decision-making and suboptimal resource allocation. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a scalable, AI-driven telemedicine framework for dynamic patient monitoring and predictive intervention. The research will focus on three computational aims: (1) creating federated machine learning models to predict patient deterioration using distributed datasets while preserving privacy, (2) optimizing real-time video and sensor data processing through parallelized algorithms and GPU acceleration, and (3) simulating resource allocation strategies for telemedicine networks via agent-based modeling to balance clinical demand with infrastructure constraints. The HPC environment will enable training on diverse, multi-institutional datasets (>500 TB), reduce inference latency to sub-second thresholds for critical alerts, and model large-scale healthcare delivery scenarios involving thousands of virtual patients and providers. Expected outcomes include an open-source telemedicine analytics pipeline validated across three chronic disease use cases (diabetes, heart failure, COPD), a resource optimization toolkit for health systems, and novel benchmarks for computational efficiency in real-time clinical AI. By addressing the computational bottlenecks in telemedicine infrastructure, this work aims to enhance the reliability of remote care delivery, reduce clinician workload through automated prioritization, and provide a template for data-driven healthcare scalability. Results will be disseminated through clinical informatics conferences and collaborations with telehealth platform developers to ensure translational impact.
cip_definition: Research on how to bring together technology and clinical medicine to enhance the overall delivery of medical care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of multiscale computational models for optimizing the design and functional integration of neural interface systems. Neural interfaces, such as brain-machine interfaces (BMIs) and peripheral nerve stimulators, face critical challenges in balancing biocompatibility, signal resolution, and long-term stability due to the dynamic interplay between engineered materials and biological tissues. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of bioelectrical, mechanical, and biochemical interactions at the neural-tissue-device interface. To address this, we propose a coupled computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of microscale electrode-tissue mechanics, agent-based simulations of neuroinflammatory responses, and machine learning-driven optimization of device geometries. The FEM module will resolve mechanical strain distributions and ion transport dynamics under physiological motion, while the agent-based model will simulate immune cell recruitment and oxidative stress patterns over weeks-long timelines. A reinforcement learning algorithm will iteratively adjust electrode topology and surface coatings to minimize predicted inflammatory cascades without sacrificing electrical performance. This computationally intensive workflow requires parallelized solvers, large-scale parameter sweeps, and high-throughput data integration, necessitating HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and GPU-accelerated training of neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for chronic neural interface performance and optimized design guidelines for next-generation electrodes, reducing reliance on iterative animal testing. The results will directly inform ongoing experimental collaborations focused on minimally invasive neuromodulation devices for treating Parkinson’s disease and neuropathic pain. By bridging molecular-scale biological responses to macroscale device functionality, this work aims to establish a computational pipeline for accelerating the translation of bioengineered neural technologies into clinical practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: Substance use disorders (SUDs) and co-occurring psychiatric conditions represent a critical public health challenge, with existing treatments often yielding suboptimal outcomes due to heterogeneous biological, psychological, and social underpinnings. This project seeks to address gaps in predictive modeling of treatment response and disease trajectories by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multi-modal datasets, including neuroimaging, genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and real-time behavioral data. A key challenge lies in integrating these high-dimensional datasets to identify biomarkers of addiction severity, relapse risk, and differential responses to pharmacotherapy or behavioral interventions. The computational approach employs machine learning frameworks, such as graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformer architectures, to model interactions between neurocircuitry alterations, genetic polymorphisms, and environmental factors. Dynamic computational simulations will further explore how individual-level data scales to population-level outcomes, incorporating agent-based models to simulate the impact of novel interventions on long-term recovery rates. HPC resources are essential for training these models on clustered GPU nodes, enabling parallel processing of neuroimaging voxels, genome-wide association study (GWAS) data, and temporal EHR features. Expected outcomes include the development of a scalable computational platform for personalized treatment matching and the identification of neurocognitive targets for interventions in dual-diagnosis populations. By optimizing resource allocation for computationally intensive tasks—such as permutation testing for multivariate associations or Bayesian network inference—this work will advance translational insights into SUD mechanisms while providing a template for data integration in psychiatric research. The proposed tools aim to reduce trial-and-error in clinical practice, ultimately improving patient outcomes through computationally derived precision psychiatry approaches.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation and treatment of individuals with alcohol, drug, or other substance-related disorders, and of individuals with the dual diagnosis of substance-related and other psychiatric disorders.

abstract: The physics of polymer systems in melt, solution, and solid states presents unresolved challenges in understanding how multi-scale structural evolution governs macroscopic material behavior. Existing coarse-grained models often fail to capture the interplay between entropic driving forces, topological constraints, and long-range correlations that dictate phenomena such as non-Newtonian flow, glass transition dynamics, and strain-induced crystallization. This project seeks to address these gaps through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid Monte Carlo-MD simulations of model polymer systems under varied thermodynamic and deformation conditions. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) quantifying the role of chain entanglement density in governing viscoelastic response during nonlinear shear flows, (2) characterizing the coupling between segmental mobility and collective rearrangements near the glass transition, and (3) mapping free energy landscapes for stress-induced crystallization in semi-flexible polymers. Simulations will employ modified Kremer-Grest bead-spring models with tunable persistence lengths and interaction potentials, scaled to system sizes exceeding 10^6 particles to ensure proper representation of long-chain dynamics. Parallel tempering methods will enhance sampling efficiency for glassy systems. High-performance computing resources are essential to achieve the required spatial and temporal resolution, particularly for resolving sub-diffusive motion in entangled melts (10^5-10^7 τ Lennard-Jones time units) and capturing rare nucleation events during crystallization. Expected outcomes include predictive relationships between molecular architecture and bulk rheological properties, validation of mode-coupling theory extensions for polymer glasses, and quantitative criteria for strain-induced phase transitions. The generated datasets will establish structure-property connections at previously inaccessible scales, advancing fundamental physics frameworks for non-equilibrium polymer behavior. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and a public repository of validated force field parameters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes for hydrocarbon upgrading is hindered by the multiscale nature of reaction networks, which span molecular interactions to reactor-scale hydrodynamics. Current computational models struggle to integrate these scales due to prohibitive resource demands, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable coupled molecular dynamics (MD) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of catalytic systems under industrially relevant conditions. By employing hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization, we will resolve atomic-scale surface reactions while capturing macroscale transport phenomena in multiphase reactor environments. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate parameter estimation for rate constants and adsorption equilibria, informed by quantum mechanics calculations on key intermediates. The resulting multiscale framework will predict catalyst performance metrics (e.g., selectivity, deactivation) and optimize reactor configurations for methane pyrolysis—a promising pathway to low-carbon hydrogen production. Successful implementation will provide a validated computational toolkit for accelerating the design of intensified chemical processes, directly supporting energy transition goals through reduced computational trial-and-error. Access to GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory architectures is critical for managing the 10^6-core-hour requirements of cross-scale simulations spanning nanoseconds to process timescales. This work bridges a critical gap in process systems engineering by enabling first-principles prediction of catalytic reactor behavior, with potential applications in petrochemicals, carbon capture, and renewable fuel synthesis.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in chemical engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The genetic basis of many rare developmental disorders remains unexplained, particularly for cases linked to non-coding genomic regions. Traditional sequencing approaches often focus on exonic variants, leaving regulatory and structural elements underexplored. This project seeks to identify pathogenic non-coding variants associated with congenital neurogenetic disorders using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 5,000 trios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will perform genome-wide association analyses integrating chromatin conformation data, epigenetic annotations, and machine learning-based variant prioritization. Computational challenges include processing >1 petabyte of raw sequencing data, running complex haplotype phasing algorithms, and training deep neural networks to predict variant pathogenicity across 3D genomic contexts. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel execution of these tasks, reducing analysis time from months to weeks. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel regulatory variants impacting neurodevelopmental genes, characterization of their mechanistic roles in gene dysregulation, and validation through CRISPR screening in cellular models. This work will advance understanding of non-coding contributions to genetic diseases, directly informing clinical diagnostic pipelines and therapeutic target development. By resolving previously undiagnosed cases, the project aligns with precision medicine initiatives while demonstrating scalable computational frameworks for analyzing non-coding variation at population scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze and model the socio-spiritual dynamics of urban communities, focusing on the optimization of ministry interventions in rapidly changing metropolitan environments. Urban ministry practitioners face complex challenges, including transient populations, systemic inequality, and fragmented community networks, which hinder the efficacy of traditional outreach and support strategies. Current approaches often rely on qualitative assessments or small-scale surveys, limiting the ability to predict emergent needs or evaluate systemic impacts of interventions. This project addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as demographic records, public health metrics, geospatial activity patterns, and anonymized community engagement logs—into predictive models of urban spiritual and social needs. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between individuals, ministry organizations, and urban infrastructures to test hypothetical interventions, while natural language processing (NLP) will analyze historical sermon texts, community feedback, and social media discourse to identify patterns in spiritual concerns across demographic groups. Graph-based network analysis will map relational ties within urban populations to optimize resource allocation and collaborative partnerships. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process large-scale datasets (spanning multiple cities and decades) and run iterative, high-resolution simulations that account for variables like migration flows, economic shifts, and crisis events. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for urban ministry leaders, offering evidence-based strategies for adaptive community engagement, crisis response, and long-term resilience-building. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science, theology, and urban studies, advancing methodological innovation in humanities research while addressing pressing practical challenges in under-resourced urban contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize tax compliance strategies for multinational enterprises (MNEs) operating in dynamically evolving regulatory environments. The computational challenge arises from the complexity of modern tax systems, where overlapping jurisdictions, transient bilateral agreements, and real-time economic data create a high-dimensional optimization problem. Traditional analytical methods fail to account for stochastic variables—such as fluctuating exchange rates, sudden policy shifts, or supply chain disruptions—that significantly impact tax liabilities. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to simulate MNE decision-making under uncertainty. The ABM will represent MNEs, tax authorities, and regulatory bodies as autonomous agents interacting within a multi-jurisdictional environment, while RL will train adaptive strategies for tax-efficient resource allocation. HPC resources are critical to manage the combinatorial explosion of scenarios, particularly when modeling cascading effects of tax policy changes across global networks spanning 100+ jurisdictions. Computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic outcomes of tax planning strategies, incorporating real-world datasets on cross-border transactions, treaty networks, and historical audit outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of identifying robust tax strategies that minimize compliance risks while adhering to evolving OECD guidelines and local regulations. This work aims to advance computational taxation as an interdisciplinary field, bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and legal informatics. By quantifying the systemic impacts of tax optimization, the project will provide policymakers with evidence-based insights into unintended consequences of regulatory frameworks, while helping businesses navigate volatile fiscal landscapes efficiently.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide tax advice and management services to individuals and corporations. Includes instruction in tax law and regulations, tax record systems, individual and corporate income taxation, tax planning, partnerships and fiduciary relationships, estates and trusts, property depreciation, capital gains and losses, dispositions, transfers, liquidity, valuation, and applications to specific tax problems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making in juvenile corrections systems by modeling the dynamic interplay of behavioral, environmental, and institutional factors influencing rehabilitation outcomes. Despite advances in correctional practices, juvenile facilities often rely on static risk-assessment tools that fail to account for real-time behavioral data, situational stressors, or the heterogeneous needs of youth populations. This gap limits the ability to allocate resources effectively or predict the long-term impacts of intervention strategies. To address this, we propose an agent-based simulation platform that integrates individual-level psychological profiles, facility-specific operational constraints, and longitudinal recidivism data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the stochasticity and scalability required for these simulations, which will model thousands of synthetic agents across diverse demographic and behavioral categories. Machine learning techniques will be applied to calibration and validation datasets derived from anonymized records of 15,000 juvenile cases, including behavioral logs, educational progress metrics, and post-release outcomes. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about the efficacy of targeted staffing allocations, therapeutic programming schedules, and crisis response protocols under varying resource constraints. The resulting models aim to identify cost-effective policy adjustments that reduce recidivism while maintaining facility safety. By bridging computational social science with correctional practice, this work will provide juvenile justice administrators with evidence-based tools to prioritize interventions for high-need individuals and simulate the systemic effects of resource reallocation before implementation. Anticipated outcomes include open-source simulation software adaptable to regional correctional contexts and a policy whiteboard outlining computational best practices for non-specialist stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to specialize in the provision of correction services to underage minor populations. Includes instruction in corrections, juvenile delinquency, juvenile development and psychology, juvenile law and justice administration, social services, record-keeping procedures, and communication skills.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data presents a critical challenge in clinical genetics, where integrating cytogenetic and molecular findings is essential for accurate diagnosis of genetic disorders. Current analytical pipelines struggle to harmonize heterogeneous data types—such as chromosomal microarray, next-generation sequencing, and epigenetic profiles—while scaling to population-level datasets. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing an integrative computational framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve ambiguities in variant interpretation and uncover novel genotype-phenotype relationships. We will process multi-modal genomic data from 10,000 retrospectively collected clinical cases, including unresolved diagnoses of developmental disorders and hereditary cancers, using graph-based genome representations to unify structural variants, single-nucleotide variations, and copy-number alterations. Deep learning models trained on HPC clusters will predict variant pathogenicity by incorporating 3D chromatin architecture data and functional genomic annotations, enabling context-aware prioritization of candidate variants. Additionally, we will implement distributed algorithms to detect cryptic chromosomal rearrangements from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing, reducing reliance on resource-intensive traditional cytogenetics. The HPC environment is indispensable for managing petabyte-scale data storage, parallelizing genome-wide association analyses across millions of loci, and optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble models through iterative GPU-accelerated workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source platform for unified cytogenomic analysis, a curated repository of reclassified variants of uncertain significance, and improved diagnostic yield for complex cases. By bridging computational scalability gaps in multi-omics integration, this work will advance precision diagnostics and inform guidelines for clinical reporting of intertwined cytogenetic and molecular findings, directly enhancing management strategies for patients with rare genetic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in art historical analysis and conservation through advanced computational methods. The research focuses on two interconnected problems: (1) the large-scale analysis of stylistic and material patterns in understudied medieval manuscript collections, and (2) modeling environmental degradation effects on organic pigments in pre-modern paintings. Current manual methods for comparative stylistic analysis and conservation risk assessment are time-intensive, lack scalability, and struggle to account for multivariate degradation factors. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid computational workflow. First, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will be trained on multi-spectral imaging data from digitized manuscripts to detect subtle stylistic variations and workshop attributions across 15,000 folios from dispersed collections. Parallelly, molecular dynamics simulations will model the interaction of temperature, humidity, and light exposure on nine organic pigment binders, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations to predict degradation pathways. The HPC environment is essential for processing terabyte-scale cultural heritage datasets, running ensemble simulation models across multiple parameter combinations, and training deep learning architectures with sufficient granularity to capture micro-features in high-resolution conservation imaging. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible attribution framework for manuscript studies, predictive risk matrices for pigment conservation, and open-source tools for material culture analysis. By integrating computational science with art historical expertise, this work aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing cultural heritage at scale while advancing preventive conservation strategies for fragile collections. The requested resources will enable processing timelines impossible on local clusters, particularly for the DFT simulations requiring weeks of sustained computation across multiple nodes.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical development of art as social and intellectual phenomenon, the analysis of works of art, and art conservation. Includes instruction in the theory of art, art history research methods, connoisseurship, the preservation and conservation of works of art, and the study of specific periods, cultures, styles, and themes.

abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to global public health, yet the genetic and molecular mechanisms driving resistance adaptation in clinically relevant species remain incompletely characterized. This project seeks to identify high-confidence genomic and structural predictors of antibiotic resistance evolution in priority pathogens, including methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* (MRSA) and carbapenemase-producing *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating bacterial whole-genome sequencing datasets with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to resolve how specific mutations in penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and efflux pump regulators enable resistance phenotypes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabyte-scale genomic data from public repositories (NCBI Pathogen Detection, CARD) and clinical isolates, followed by variant annotation, phylogenetic clustering, and pan-genome-wide association studies (pan-GWAS) to prioritize resistance-linked loci. Concurrently, all-atom MD simulations will model mutant PBP structures under ligand-binding conditions to quantify conformational changes impacting beta-lactam antibiotic affinity. These simulations require sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for millisecond-scale sampling. Expected outcomes include (1) a ranked catalog of genomic signatures predictive of resistance emergence in hospital-associated bacterial lineages, (2) dynamic structural maps identifying key residues governing antibiotic-target interactions, and (3) open-access machine learning models trained on integrated genomic and biophysical data to forecast resistance risks from emerging strains. By bridging population-level genomic trends with atomistic mechanisms, this work will advance actionable frameworks for resistance surveillance and inform the development of next-generation antimicrobials targeting adaptive vulnerabilities in pathogenic bacteria.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of pathogenic bacteria that are significant factors in causing or facilitating human disease. Includes instruction in the pathogenesis of bacterial diseases, bacterial genetics and physiology, bacterial anatomy and structure, antigens, bacterial reproduction, bacterial adhesion, phagocytes, and the identification of new or mutated bacteria and bacterial agents.

abstract: This project proposes a computational investigation of cross-regional cultural narratives in premodern and early modern Asia, focusing on the transmission of gendered archetypes and their evolution in literary and visual sources. While textual and artistic records from 1000–1800 CE reflect dynamic exchanges of cultural ideals across Asian societies, systematic analysis of these narratives remains fragmented due to the multilingual, multimodal, and geographically dispersed nature of primary materials. Leveraging high-performance computing, this study will process a curated corpus of 15,000+ digitized texts (poetry, folktales, religious commentaries) and 8,000+ visual works (scroll paintings, temple reliefs, illustrated manuscripts) from Chinese, Japanese, Persian, and Sanskrit traditions. A hybrid pipeline combining multilingual transformer models (for text) and graph neural networks (for iconographic relationships) will be developed to trace the adaptation of gender-related motifs—such as fertility symbols, warrior ideals, and cosmological pairings—across linguistic and artistic contexts. Spatial-temporal analysis modules will map regional variations in narrative prominence against historical trade routes and religious networks. The computational workflow addresses challenges in cross-modal alignment, requiring parallel processing of text-image pairs from heterogeneous digitization standards. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously unrecognized intercultural pathways in gendered symbol transmission, 2) quantitative models correlating narrative shifts with documented sociopolitical transformations, and 3) public visualization tools for exploring motif trajectories. This work advances Asian cultural studies by enabling macroscale comparative analysis of identity constructs while developing methodologies for ethically engaged computational humanities. The scale of data integration and need for simultaneous training of multimodal architectures necessitates HPC resources beyond local cluster capabilities, particularly for memory-intensive graph processing and low-latency cross-repository data federation.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Asian Continent, including the study of the Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on syntactic and semantic patterns in premodern East Asian texts, with a focus on Classical Chinese and its influence on early Japanese and Korean literary traditions. A key challenge in analyzing these texts lies in their linguistic complexity, non-standardized orthographies, and the scarcity of digitized corpora with robust philological annotations. Traditional manual analysis struggles to address the scale of data required to trace diachronic shifts in grammatical structures or quantify cross-regional lexical borrowing. The proposed computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models, to automate the parsing of syntactic dependencies and semantic role labeling across heterogeneous text sources. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle variant characters, scribal abbreviations, and multilingual glosses prevalent in historical manuscripts. HPC resources will enable large-scale training of domain-specific language models using distributed deep learning frameworks, as well as the alignment of parallel texts across Chinese, Japanese, and Korean to map transcultural literary exchanges. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of 10,000+ pages of digitized manuscripts, quantitative frameworks for tracking morphosyntactic evolution in premodern East Asia, and improved OCR models tailored to understudied script variants. This work will provide novel insights into how linguistic contact shaped literary production across the region, while developing computational tools to bridge gaps between traditional philology and digital humanities methodologies. The requested resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks such as training multilingual embeddings and conducting Monte Carlo simulations of language change dynamics across millisecond-scale historical intervals.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: East Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the languages of East Asia, including, but not limited to, the Sino-Tibetan, Japanese, and Korean languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Palliative care research faces significant challenges in predicting patient trajectories and optimizing individualized care plans due to the complex interplay of biological, psychosocial, and clinical factors influencing outcomes. Current approaches often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic symptom evolution, treatment responses, and heterogeneous patient needs. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to integrate multimodal data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, real-time symptom reports, and social determinants of health—into predictive models for personalized palliative care. The research will employ machine learning techniques such as recurrent neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze longitudinal datasets from 15,000+ patients across six palliative care cohorts. These models will identify critical predictors of symptom burden, quality-of-life trajectories, and end-of-life decision-making patterns while accounting for missing data and temporal dependencies. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for model training, stochastic simulations of care pathways, and sensitivity analyses across demographic subgroups. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of complex algorithms that would be infeasible with standard clinical computing resources. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools to guide early interventions for high-risk patients, dynamic decision-support systems for clinicians, and stratification frameworks for clinical trial enrollment. By elucidating modifiable factors in palliative care outcomes, this work aims to reduce preventable suffering, optimize resource allocation, and establish scalable computational methodologies for future research in patient-centered care. The proposed models and pipelines will be disseminated through open-source platforms to foster collaboration across palliative care research networks.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern recreational vehicles (RVs) necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize system performance, safety, and reliability. Current industry practices rely heavily on physical prototyping and empirical testing to address failures in interconnected RV subsystems (e.g., electrical, propane, hydraulic, structural), leading to high costs, extended development cycles, and limited predictive capacity. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-physics simulation framework that models the dynamic interactions between RV mechanical, thermal, and electrical systems under real-world operating conditions. The research will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) to assess structural integrity in chassis and frame components, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model propane flow and combustion in appliance systems, and machine learning (ML) to predict failure modes in brake and towing systems based on sensor-derived stress and wear data. Additionally, the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate human-technician interactions during repair scenarios, enabling the optimization of service workflows and training protocols. By coupling these computational approaches, the framework will identify design vulnerabilities, recommend material or procedural improvements, and generate synthetic datasets to train AI-assisted diagnostic tools. The outcomes will directly support RV manufacturers and service technicians by reducing maintenance downtime, enhancing safety standards, and enabling data-driven decision-making. The HPC environment is critical to handling the scale of concurrent simulations—particularly for modeling transient thermal-electrical interactions in compact RV environments and processing high-resolution 3D scans of corroded or fatigued components. This work bridges a gap in technical education by providing open-source simulation tools tailored to RV systems, fostering innovation in a sector traditionally reliant on manual expertise. Anticipated impacts include a 15–20% reduction in critical system failures during stress testing and a scalable computational model adaptable to emerging RV technologies, such as hybrid power systems and smart IoT-enabled appliances.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to build, test, inspect, repair, service and maintain recreational vehicles, systems, and interior and exterior components. Includes instruction in brake, hydraulic, and towing systems; electrical systems; propane systems and propane and electric appliances; carpentry; plumbing; welding; and structural frames.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the nonlinear acoustics and performance dynamics of woodwind instruments, with a focus on optimizing pedagogical frameworks and performance outcomes. While traditional methods in woodwind pedagogy emphasize empirical observation and qualitative feedback, the complex interplay of airflow, reed vibration, and resonator behavior in instruments such as clarinets, oboes, and saxophones remains insufficiently modeled at high temporal resolutions. Current computational tools struggle to simulate the multiphysics interactions governing timbre, intonation, and articulation with the fidelity required to inform advanced performance strategies. This research aims to address this gap by developing a coupled fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model to simulate reed response and bore acoustics under varied performance conditions, including dynamic embouchure adjustments and articulation techniques. The computational approach will utilize finite element analysis (FEA) and lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) to resolve transient airflow and pressure waves within instrument bores, validated against experimental sensor data from instrument-mounted pressure transducers and motion-capture systems. Machine learning algorithms will then analyze simulated and empirical datasets to identify patterns linking physiological control parameters (e.g., lip pressure, breath velocity) to acoustic outputs. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, the project will achieve the necessary scale to model performance scenarios in real-time equivalence. Anticipated outcomes include a computational framework for diagnosing performance inefficiencies, predictive tools for timbral customization, and evidence-based guidelines for technical exercises targeting acoustically critical parameters. This work will advance the intersection of computational physics and performing arts, offering novel resources for both educators and performers to refine technical mastery through data-driven insights.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master a woodwind instrument and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in playing and personal style development.

abstract: Maritime law enforcement faces unique challenges in detecting and responding to illicit activities across vast, dynamic ocean environments. Traditional methods for monitoring piracy, smuggling, and illegal fishing often rely on fragmented data streams, manual analysis, and reactive strategies, leading to inefficiencies in resource deployment and delayed interventions. This project proposes the development of an integrated computational framework to optimize maritime surveillance and enforcement operations through advanced predictive analytics, real-time sensor fusion, and multi-agent simulation. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, automatic identification system (AIS) trajectories, historical incident reports, and environmental sensor networks—using machine learning models to identify anomalous vessel behavior and forecast high-risk zones. Agent-based modeling will simulate interdiction scenarios, incorporating variables such as patrol vessel dynamics, weather conditions, and adversarial tactics to evaluate response protocols and resource allocation strategies. A key innovation lies in coupling hydrodynamic simulations with reinforcement learning algorithms to model vessel pursuit dynamics under varying sea states, enabling the design of adaptive interception pathways. The computational demands of training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and running parallelized, stochastic simulations necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for real-time threat prioritization, a risk-based patrol optimization engine, and a scenario-testing platform for training personnel in emergent threat environments. By bridging computational science and maritime operational requirements, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for enhancing situational awareness, reducing response times, and improving the cost-effectiveness of maritime law enforcement agencies globally.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement and security principles and procedures to the marine environment. Includes instruction in criminal and nautical law, nautical terminology, seamanship and vessel operation, vessel maintenance, navigation and navigation systems, meteorology, vessel and passenger safety, radar and remote sensing systems, communications systems, vessel pursuit and stop, boarding and arrest techniques, investigative and evidence techniques, weaponry and applications to specific situations such as piracy, drug trafficking and smuggling.

abstract: The brewing industry faces critical challenges in optimizing fermentation processes, which are central to beer quality, consistency, and production efficiency. Microbial dynamics during fermentation involve complex interactions between yeast strains, metabolic byproducts, and environmental variables, yet current predictive models lack the resolution to account for strain-specific genetic variability, substrate utilization patterns, and stress responses under industrial-scale conditions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop multiscale simulations of Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolism and population behavior during wort fermentation. Agent-based modeling frameworks will integrate genomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets from lab-scale fermentations to simulate yeast cell heterogeneity, nutrient gradients, and metabolic flux at the bioreactor scale. Parallelized parameter sweeps will explore the effects of temperature, pH, oxygen levels, and sugar composition on fermentation kinetics and off-flavor compound formation. Genome-scale metabolic reconstructions of industrial yeast strains will be coupled with machine learning classifiers to predict strain performance under novel brewing conditions. By iteratively validating simulations against experimental fermentation data, the models will identify genetic and process engineering targets to minimize batch variability and spoilage risks. The computational workflows will require large-scale memory nodes for population-level simulations and GPU acceleration for deep learning components. Outcomes will advance precision brewing methodologies, reduce resource waste in fermentation trials, and provide open-source tools for strain optimization. This work aligns with agricultural science priorities by enhancing the efficiency of microbial biomass utilization in value-added food production systems, directly supporting the brewing industry’s need for sustainable, data-driven process innovations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of beer brewing operations. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, malting, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the biomechanical and chemical interactions between permanent cosmetic pigments and human skin tissues, with the goal of improving safety, longevity, and aesthetic outcomes in cosmetic tattooing.
