Despite the growing demand for permanent makeup and medical tattooing (e.g., scar camouflage, areola restoration), there remains a critical gap in understanding how pigment composition, particle size, and application techniques influence long-term stability and biocompatibility. Current industry standards rely on anecdotal evidence, with limited quantitative modeling of pigment migration, degradation kinetics, or inflammatory responses. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of pigment-skin interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) of dermal stress during needle insertion, and machine learning (ML) models trained on longitudinal clinical data. MD simulations will map binding affinities between common organic/inorganic pigments and collagen/elastin networks, while FEA models will quantify tissue trauma under varying needle geometries and motor speeds. Concurrently, ML algorithms will correlate these computational outputs with real-world outcomes using a dataset of 5,000+ anonymized client cases (provided by collaborating clinics) to identify risk factors for pigment fading or granuloma formation. The HPC environment is essential for handling the high-resolution 3D skin models, parallelized simulation workflows, and large-scale data integration required. Anticipated outcomes include evidence-based guidelines for pigment selection, needle configurations, and aftercare protocols, as well as a predictive tool for artists to customize techniques based on individual skin typology. By bridging cosmetic art with computational biomedicine, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for safer, more durable aesthetic outcomes while advancing regulatory science in an understudied domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to prepare and apply permanent markings, color, and cosmetic products to the face and body for aesthetic or clinical purposes; to remove unwanted markings; and to function as licensed permanent makeup artists and tattooists.  Includes instruction in client consultation; sterilization and sanitation; skin anatomy, diseases, and disorders; skin preparation and anesthetics; color theory; machine theory and operation; needle selection; applications such as eyebrows, eyeliners, lips, lipliners, beauty marks, and blemish/mark removal; after care; laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of personalized learning plans (PLPs) for students with developmental delays by leveraging machine learning (ML) and large-scale educational datasets. A critical challenge in special education is efficiently tailoring interventions to students’ heterogeneous cognitive, social, and emotional needs while adhering to resource constraints. Current methods for creating PLPs rely heavily on manual, time-intensive processes by educators, often leading to delays in implementation and suboptimal alignment with individual student trajectories. To address this, we propose training ensemble ML models on multimodal data—including longitudinal academic performance records, behavioral observation logs, and demographic factors—to predict intervention efficacy and recommend adaptive teaching strategies. The computational workload involves high-dimensional clustering of student profiles, multi-objective optimization of resource allocation, and real-time simulation of learning outcomes under varying instructional scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of anonymized student data from partnered school districts, run parallelized model training for diverse developmental delay subtypes, and validate predictions against experimental classroom pilot studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool that assists educators in rapidly generating evidence-based PLPs, reducing the planning-to-implementation cycle by an estimated 40–60%. The models will also quantify trade-offs between individualized pacing and classroom resource limitations, providing policymakers with scalable frameworks for equitable special education practices. By integrating computational analytics with pedagogical expertise, this work aims to advance teacher training in data-driven decision-making while directly addressing the acute need for precision in supporting developmentally delayed learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals Who are Developmentally Delayed
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who exhibit slow social, physical, cognitive, or emotional growth patterns related to age, or a combination of such factors that affect learning, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identification of developmental delay patterns, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising developmentally delayed students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of industrial-scale chemical production processes, with a focus on enhancing energy efficiency and reducing environmental impacts. Current challenges in Chemical Engineering Technology include the computational limitations of simulating multiphase reactor dynamics, heterogeneous catalysis, and real-time process control under variable industrial conditions. These limitations hinder the development of scalable, sustainable chemical manufacturing systems. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for reactor-scale flow and heat transfer analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate catalyst-surface interactions, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to optimize process parameters. The CFD models will resolve turbulent fluid behavior and species transport in large-scale reactors, while MD simulations will probe atomic-scale mechanisms of catalytic activity and degradation. ML frameworks will integrate these datasets to predict optimal operating conditions, such as temperature gradients and feedstock ratios, balancing production efficiency with emissions control. The HPC environment is critical for managing the high dimensionality of these simulations, particularly the parallel processing demands of coupled CFD-MD workflows and the training of deep neural networks on terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include validated models for industrial reactor design, actionable insights into catalyst longevity, and adaptive control strategies for minimizing energy consumption in continuous chemical processes. This work aligns with the Chemical Engineering Technology program’s emphasis on applied industrial problem-solving, offering transferable computational tools for educators and industry partners. Successful implementation will directly support curriculum development in process simulation and provide a foundation for collaborative research on sustainable chemical manufacturing, addressing pressing needs in environmental compliance and operational cost reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the production and utilization of chemicals on an industrial scale. Includes instruction in organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, industrial processes, instrumental analysis, sampling and monitoring, and chemical and environmental safety.

abstract: The proliferation of dynamic, user-centric web applications demands increasingly sophisticated methods to optimize real-time content delivery while balancing computational efficiency and user experience. This project addresses the challenge of adaptive resource allocation for personalized multimedia streaming in large-scale, heterogeneous web environments. Traditional server-side optimization frameworks struggle to dynamically reconcile fluctuating user demand patterns, device-specific rendering constraints, and quality-of-service requirements—particularly when operating across distributed edge computing architectures. We propose a hybrid computational strategy combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to model complex dependencies between user behavior, network topology, and media encoding parameters. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to 1) train GNNs on terabyte-scale clickstream datasets augmented with synthetic edge network topologies, 2) simulate MORL decision-making processes across millions of concurrent user sessions under varying latency constraints, and 3) validate optimization policies through discrete-event modeling of content delivery networks. Key innovations include the development of a novel attention mechanism for cross-modal feature alignment between user interaction sequences and media asset metadata, as well as a distributed training framework for MORL agents operating in partially observable network environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source optimization engine capable of reducing median page load times by 15-20% while maintaining adaptive video quality thresholds, alongside fundamental insights into computational tradeoffs in edge-based web resource management. This work bridges critical gaps between information systems design, distributed computing, and human-centered web architecture, advancing capabilities for next-generation webmaster tools in an era of exponentially growing multimedia demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and maintain web servers and the hosted web pages at one or a group of web sites, and to function as designated webmasters. Includes instruction in computer systems and networks, server installation and maintenance, web page design and editing, information resources management, web policy and procedures, Internet applications of information systems security, user interfacing and usability research, and relevant management and communications skills.

abstract: Chronic pain is a multidimensional health challenge with complex interactions between neurophysiological, psychological, and sociocultural factors. Current treatment paradigms often rely on generalized protocols that fail to account for individual variability in pain perception, treatment response, and psychosocial comorbidities. This project proposes to develop a multiscale computational framework integrating neuroimaging, genomic, and electronic health record (EHR) data to model patient-specific pain pathways and predict optimized therapeutic strategies. The research problem centers on overcoming the limitations of reductionist approaches by establishing dynamic, personalized models of pain modulation that reflect the interplay of biological systems and clinical outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets, including functional MRI time series, single-nucleotide polymorphism arrays, and longitudinal treatment histories from 10,000+ patients. Computational methods will involve machine learning-driven feature extraction to identify biomarkers of pain chronification, coupled with mechanistic simulations of neurotransmitter dynamics and drug-receptor interactions. Graph neural networks will map functional connectivity alterations in pain-processing brain regions, while pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models will simulate individualized responses to analgesic combinations. The project will leverage distributed computing frameworks to perform real-time optimization of treatment parameters through in silico clinical trials, iteratively refining predictions using federated learning across collaborating institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for precision pain management that stratifies patients into mechanistically defined subgroups, predicts adverse event risks, and recommends tailored interventions. By bridging neurobiological insights with clinical decision-making, this work aims to reduce reliance on trial-and-error prescribing, mitigate opioid misuse, and improve functional outcomes in refractory pain populations. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a template for integrating heterogeneous health data into actionable clinical models, advancing interdisciplinary collaboration in pain neuroscience and systems medicine.
cip_definition: A post-residency program of study that prepares physicians in the diagnosis, management, and treatment of acute and chronic pain. Includes instruction in anesthesiology, pain assessment, pain classification and diagnosis, pain neuroscience, palliative and end-of-life care, physical medicine and rehabilitation, psychiatry of pain, pain pharmacology, public policy, and legal issues of pain management.

abstract: The safe and efficient use of nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies relies on precise modeling of radiation interactions with materials and systems. Current challenges include optimizing radiation shielding designs, predicting material degradation under prolonged exposure, and improving real-time monitoring algorithms for complex environments. These problems demand high-fidelity simulations that account for multi-physics phenomena, such as coupled radiation transport, thermal effects, and structural deformation, which exceed the capabilities of standard computing resources. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for radiation-matter interaction studies. The research will employ Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations using Geant4 and MCNP frameworks, integrated with finite element analysis for thermo-mechanical modeling. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization for shielding materials and automate anomaly detection in radiation sensor networks. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized particle transport calculations and CPU clusters for coupled multiphysics simulations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting radiation-induced material behavior in next-generation nuclear reactors, optimized shielding configurations for industrial radiography devices, and AI-enhanced protocols for radiation safety monitoring. These results will directly support the development of safer, more efficient radiologic technologies in energy production, nondestructive testing, and medical applications. The project will also produce open-source tools to streamline radiation simulation workflows, fostering collaboration across the science-related technologies community. By addressing critical computational bottlenecks, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models and real-world implementation in radiation-dependent industries.
cip_title: Nuclear and Industrial Radiologic Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Telemedicine has emerged as a critical tool for expanding equitable access to medical care, yet integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging, wearable devices, and patient-reported outcomes—into actionable clinical insights remains a significant challenge. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to process multimodal datasets in real time, limiting their utility for dynamic decision-making in remote care settings. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multimodal data integration and predictive analytics in telemedicine. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating scalable pipelines to harmonize structured and unstructured data from diverse sources, (2) training machine learning models to predict clinical deterioration in chronic disease patients monitored remotely, and (3) optimizing real-time processing of streaming physiological data from wearable sensors. Computational methods will include federated learning architectures to preserve patient privacy while leveraging distributed datasets, transformer-based models for temporal EHR analysis, and GPU-accelerated signal processing algorithms for continuous vital sign interpretation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization, validation across multi-site datasets (>100,000 patient records), and simulation of telemedicine workflows under varying network latency conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for telemedicine analytics, validated predictive models for early intervention in conditions such as heart failure and diabetes, and performance benchmarks for real-time data processing in resource-constrained settings. This work will directly advance the clinical utility of telemedicine by providing computationally robust methods to synthesize complex data streams, ultimately supporting more precise, proactive, and personalized remote care delivery. By addressing both technical and translational challenges, the project aims to establish a foundation for scalable, evidence-based telemedicine systems that improve outcomes while reducing disparities in healthcare access.
cip_definition: Research on how to bring together technology and clinical medicine to enhance the overall delivery of medical care.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model dynamic household financial decision-making under economic uncertainty, with a focus on identifying patterns of resilience and vulnerability across diverse demographic groups. The research addresses a critical gap in family and consumer economics: traditional static models inadequately capture the interdependencies between real-time market fluctuations, behavioral biases, and heterogeneous household priorities (e.g., intergenerational caregiving, education savings, or debt management). By leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to implement a large-scale agent-based model that simulates decision pathways across 100,000+ synthetic households parameterized using merged microdata from financial surveys, census records, and behavioral experiments. The model will integrate machine learning classifiers to predict tipping points at which households transition between stable and unstable financial states when exposed to simulated economic shocks, such as inflationary periods or abrupt policy changes. Computational challenges include optimizing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing and training neural networks on imbalanced temporal datasets representing rare but consequential financial events (e.g., medical bankruptcies). Outcomes will yield a publicly accessible toolkit for policymakers to evaluate how localized economic interventions might differentially affect households based on asset portfolios, cultural norms around resource sharing, and access to financial literacy resources. This work bridges computational social science with consumer economics, offering novel methodologies to analyze complex, adaptive decision-making processes that defy reduction to conventional economic assumptions.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Economics and Related Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer economics and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrative computational framework to model emergent dynamics in urban heat resilience, combining climate science, social vulnerability metrics, and infrastructure systems analysis. Urban heat islands (UHIs) disproportionately impact marginalized communities during extreme heat events, yet existing models inadequately capture the feedback loops between microclimatic conditions, human behavioral adaptation, and aging energy grids. Our research addresses this gap by constructing a multi-layered agent-based model (ABM) coupled with high-resolution atmospheric simulations and real-time socioeconomic datasets. The ABM will simulate individual and institutional decision-making under thermal stress, while nested weather research and forecasting (WRF) models parameterize localized heat flux dynamics at street-canyon scales. Machine learning surrogates will bridge these components, enabling sensitivity analyses of policy interventions such as green infrastructure deployment or emergency cooling center allocation. The computational demands are substantial: ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios (RCP 4.5/8.5) require parallelized execution of 10^5 agent interactions per km² at hourly temporal resolution over decadal horizons. We request GPU-accelerated nodes for WRF downscaling and CPU clusters for ABM calibration using Bayesian optimization. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital twin platform for cities to stress-test heat mitigation strategies through virtual experimentation. This work advances systems science methodology by formalizing cross-domain couplings between biophysical processes and social inequity drivers, while delivering actionable insights for climate adaptation planning. Successful implementation will demonstrate how computationally intensive, multidisciplinary integration can address pressing societal challenges at the human-environment-technology interface.
cip_definition: A program with a multidisciplinary approach to the analysis and solution of complex problems, requiring a combined approach using data and models from the natural, social, technological, behavioral and life sciences, and other specialized fields.

abstract: This project addresses the pressing need to optimize agroecosystem management by resolving critical knowledge gaps in the multi-scale interactions between crops, soils, microbial communities, and climate variables. Current empirical and modeling approaches struggle to capture the dynamic, nonlinear feedbacks governing nutrient cycling, pest resilience, and crop productivity under climate variability, limiting the design of scalable, context-specific sustainable practices. To overcome these barriers, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and high-resolution climate data assimilation. The ABM will simulate spatially explicit agroecosystem dynamics at the field-to-landscape scale, incorporating microbial metabolic processes, root-soil interactions, and pollinator behavior. ML algorithms will parameterize models using heterogeneous datasets, including multi-omics data from soil microbiomes, remote sensing imagery, and historical yield records. Climate resilience assessments will integrate regional CMIP6 projections to evaluate management strategies under diverse emission scenarios. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing of large-scale simulations and real-time ML training—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources to achieve biologically meaningful spatiotemporal resolutions. Expected outcomes include identifying crop rotation sequences that enhance soil carbon sequestration, optimizing cover crop mixtures for pest suppression and water retention, and quantifying trade-offs between yield stability and input reduction across agroclimatic zones. By bridging molecular-scale processes to landscape-level outcomes, this work will provide actionable insights for farmers and policymakers, advancing the dual goals of climate resilience and food security. The resulting open-source tools will empower stakeholders to simulate site-specific management scenarios, fostering adoption of practices that align ecological integrity with socioeconomic viability. This project thus directly supports the program’s mission to develop agricultural systems that are productive, resource-efficient, and socially equitable.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the diachronic and synchronic dynamics of Romance language evolution, with a focus on identifying patterns of syntactic and morphological change across geographically dispersed dialects. The study addresses a critical gap in computational Romance linguistics: modeling how contact phenomena (e.g., bilingualism, language shift) and sociolinguistic variables drive structural divergence in languages such as Occitan, Sardinian, and Galician, which exist in dynamic contact with dominant state languages. Current methodologies lack the computational power to process large-scale, multi-modal corpora—including historical texts, sociolinguistic interviews, and dialectal audio recordings—while accounting for the nonlinear interactions between linguistic variables. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) with transformer-based natural language processing (NLP). The ABM framework will simulate language contact scenarios over centuries, parameterized by demographic data and attested sound laws, while fine-tuned NLP models (e.g., BERT variants trained on historical Romance texts) will analyze morphosyntactic variation across 15th–21st century corpora. HPC resources are essential for three components: (1) parallelized ABM simulations across thousands of parameter combinations to model probabilistic language change; (2) training domain-specific language models on terabyte-scale textual and phonetic datasets; and (3) real-time alignment of simulation outputs with empirical data using GPU-accelerated phylogenetic algorithms. Expected outcomes include the first probabilistic maps of syntactic convergence risks for endangered Romance varieties, a publicly accessible database of annotated dialectal features, and methodological frameworks for scalable diachronic linguistic analysis. This work will directly inform language revitalization efforts and enhance computational tools for minority language education, while advancing interdisciplinary connections between Romance linguistics and computational social science.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Romance languages of Western, Central, and Southern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project investigates the resilience of decentralized information ecosystems under cascading disruptions caused by climate-driven environmental stressors. As global infrastructural and ecological systems become increasingly interdependent, understanding how localized failures propagate through information networks—particularly those reliant on hybrid human-machine decision-making—is critical. The research integrates computational social science, network theory, and environmental informatics to model multi-layer networks that couple physical sensor arrays, community reporting platforms, and institutional data-sharing protocols. Using agent-based modeling and temporal graph neural networks, we will simulate how distributed information systems adapt (or collapse) when facing compound events such as simultaneous power grid failures, communication outages, and population displacement. The computational approach requires high-performance resources to handle three core challenges: 1) scaling discrete-event simulations across heterogeneous network topologies with >10^6 dynamic nodes, 2) training attention-based models on sparse, multi-modal data streams (satellite imagery, crowdsourced text, IoT sensor logs), and 3) optimizing parameter space exploration for resilience metrics under uncertainty bounds derived from climate projection ensembles. Expected outcomes include a framework for quantifying information criticality thresholds in coupled human-technical systems, novel protocols for dynamic network rerouting in resource-constrained environments, and open-source tools enabling communities to stress-test local information infrastructures against climate scenarios. By bridging gaps between disaster informatics, participatory sensing, and adaptive systems theory, this work advances predictive capabilities for information continuity in crisis contexts while informing policy on equitable resource allocation for climate-resilient communication architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory, organization, and process of information collection, transmission, and utilization in traditional and electronic forms. Includes instruction in information classification and organization; information storage and processing; transmission, transfer, and signaling; communications and networking; systems planning and design; human interfacing and use analysis; database development; information policy analysis; and related aspects of hardware, software, economics, social factors, and capacity.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a data-driven decision-support framework for optimizing resource allocation in collegiate athletic departments, with a focus on balancing financial sustainability, athlete performance, and fan engagement. Current challenges in sport management include siloed data systems, dynamic scheduling constraints, and the need for real-time responsiveness to variables such as ticket demand, athlete health metrics, and facility utilization. Traditional analytical tools struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets—spanning ticket sales, wearable device outputs, social media sentiment, and operational logistics—into cohesive models. The proposed research will employ agent-based modeling and hybrid machine learning architectures to simulate multi-stakeholder interactions (e.g., fan behavior, athlete load management, venue operations) under varying scenarios. HPC resources will enable parallelized optimization of scheduling algorithms, Monte Carlo simulations for financial risk assessment, and natural language processing of fan engagement data across large-scale social media corpora. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for predictive resource allocation, such as dynamic ticket pricing models sensitive to athlete rest cycles, or energy-efficient facility scheduling that aligns event calendars with real-time maintenance needs. By addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in processing high-dimensional, temporally sensitive data, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in sport administration while establishing methodological benchmarks for integrating operational, physiological, and business analytics in a non-STEM disciplinary context. The resulting tools will be validated through partnerships with NCAA Division I programs, with potential applications to community sports organizations seeking cost-effective strategies for sustainable management.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply business, coaching and physical education principles to the organization, administration and management of athletic programs and teams, fitness/rehabilitation facilities and health clubs, sport recreation services, and related services. Includes instruction in program planning and development; business and financial management principles; sales, marketing and recruitment; event promotion, scheduling and management; facilities management; public relations; legal aspects of sports; and applicable health and safety standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of leadership decision-making under complex organizational constraints using computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. A critical challenge in organizational leadership is understanding how leaders balance competing priorities—such as financial efficiency, team cohesion, and stakeholder demands—in rapidly evolving environments. Existing studies often rely on qualitative case analyses or simplified simulations, limiting generalizability and scalability. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate multi-level organizational interactions under varying leadership strategies, resource allocations, and crisis scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize these models with real-world organizational datasets (e.g., communication logs, performance metrics, and employee surveys) and to execute thousands of parallel simulations. The computational framework will integrate machine learning techniques to identify patterns in leadership effectiveness across diverse virtual scenarios, including supply chain disruptions, workforce restructuring, and cross-cultural team conflicts. Expected outcomes include a taxonomy of adaptive leadership behaviors correlated with organizational resilience, quantified metrics for resource allocation trade-offs, and predictive tools to assess intervention impacts before implementation. This work will advance scholarly understanding of leadership as a dynamic, data-driven process while providing actionable insights for training programs and policy design. The requested computing resources will enable handling of sensitive, large-scale organizational datasets securely, support real-time visualization of network-level decision cascades, and reduce simulation runtime from weeks to days. By bridging computational social science with leadership theory, this project aims to establish a replicable methodology for evidence-based leadership development in business and non-profit sectors.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on leadership skills that can be applied to a business, government, non-profit, or educational setting. Includes instruction in organizational planning, dynamics of leadership, finance, team building, conflict resolution and mediation, communication and other management skills.

abstract: Soil systems are complex, heterogeneous environments where physical, chemical, and biological processes interact across spatial and temporal scales, influencing nutrient cycling, water retention, and carbon dynamics. However, predicting these interactions—particularly under changing environmental conditions—remains a critical challenge due to limitations in resolving multiscale phenomena experimentally. This project seeks to advance understanding of soil biogeochemical processes through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling. We propose to develop and validate a coupled reactive transport framework integrating molecular-scale simulations of mineral-organic interactions, pore-scale fluid dynamics, and field-scale soil hydrology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will parameterize free energy landscapes for ion exchange and organic matter adsorption on clay surfaces, while finite element models resolve pore network geometry and reactive transport. These outputs will inform macroscale hydrological models incorporating soil structure heterogeneity and microbial activity. The computational demand arises from the need to simulate thousands of stochastic pore-scale domains, perform ensemble MD runs across mineralogical compositions, and iteratively optimize parameters using machine learning. By leveraging GPU-accelerated HPC resources, we aim to quantify how microscale processes propagate to observable soil behavior, such as nutrient leaching or carbon stabilization. Outcomes will provide predictive tools for optimizing soil management practices, including precision fertilizer application and soil amendment strategies under climate variability. This work directly supports agricultural sustainability by bridging molecular mechanisms to field-scale outcomes, addressing urgent needs in food security and climate-resilient soil systems. The resulting open-source models will enable researchers to explore soil chemistry-physics interactions at unprecedented resolution, fostering innovation in soil health monitoring and intervention design.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical and physical principles to research and analysis concerning the nature and properties of soils and the conservation and management of soils. Includes instruction in soil and fluid mechanics, mineralogy, sedimentology, thermodynamics, geomorphology, environmental systems, analytical methods, and organic and inorganic chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and sociolinguistic mechanisms underlying second language (L2) acquisition through advanced computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. A critical challenge in the field is understanding how individual differences—such as prior linguistic knowledge, cognitive load, and social context—interact with instructional interventions to shape language learning trajectories. Existing studies often rely on small datasets or simplified models, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic, nonlinear processes inherent in L2 development. To address this gap, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal datasets (e.g., learner corpora, eye-tracking data, and longitudinal proficiency assessments) and simulate complex acquisition processes. Computational methods will include deep learning models to identify patterns in language production across proficiency levels, agent-based simulations to explore social network effects on L2 retention, and Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify variability in learning outcomes. These approaches require parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of annotated linguistic data and iterative parameter tuning for cognitive models. The expected outcomes include (1) novel insights into how neurocognitive constraints and social interactions co-determine L2 mastery, (2) predictive frameworks for personalizing language pedagogy based on learner profiles, and (3) open-source tools for scalable analysis of multilingual datasets. By integrating psycholinguistic theory with computational rigor, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for language education while establishing a methodological bridge between humanities-driven SLA research and data-intensive computational science. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the project’s scope, enabling rapid experimentation with high-dimensional models and reproducibility across diverse learner populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development, use, and maintenance of second languages. Includes instruction in language pedagogy, use, analysis and processes.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing project efficiency, cost management, and risk mitigation, particularly as projects grow in scale and complexity. Traditional methods for planning and managing multi-phase construction processes—such as structural analysis, material logistics, and labor allocation—often rely on static models that fail to account for dynamic variables like weather disruptions, supply chain variability, and real-time structural performance data. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a computational framework for simulating and optimizing construction workflows through high-performance computing (HPC). The research will focus on integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessment, discrete-event simulation for supply chain and labor scheduling, and machine learning models to predict and adapt to real-time project risks. By leveraging HPC resources, the team will execute large-scale parametric studies to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, including material substitutions, equipment configurations, and regulatory constraints, under varying environmental and operational conditions. Key outcomes will include a validated digital twin platform capable of simulating construction processes at high fidelity, predictive tools for identifying cost and schedule risks, and data-driven recommendations for resilient project designs. The computational demands of this work—particularly the parallel processing requirements for FEA-coupled simulations and the training of deep reinforcement learning models on heterogeneous datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. This research will advance the integration of computational modeling into construction engineering practice, offering a pathway to reduce material waste, improve compliance with safety standards, and enhance the adaptability of construction projects in response to unforeseen disruptions. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools and case studies, providing actionable insights for industry stakeholders and academic researchers focused on smart construction technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers, engineering contractors and other professionals engaged in the construction of buildings and related structures. Includes instruction in basic structural engineering principles and construction techniques, building site inspection, site supervision, construction personnel supervision, plan and specification interpretation, supply logistics and procurement, applicable building codes, and report preparation.

abstract: The spread of entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) as biocontrol agents against agricultural pests is constrained by limited understanding of their tri-trophic interactions with insect hosts and plant rhizospheres under dynamic environmental conditions. This project seeks to model the molecular and ecological drivers of EPN-host-plant signaling cascades using a multi-scale computational framework. We aim to resolve how soil temperature gradients, root exudate chemistry, and insect immune responses collectively modulate nematode foraging efficiency and infection success. High-performance computing resources will enable spatially explicit agent-based simulations of nematode population dynamics in heterogeneous soil matrices, integrated with genome-scale metabolic network models of symbiotic bacteria (Xenorhabdus spp.) to predict toxin production thresholds under nutrient stress. Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will analyze hyperspectral imaging datasets from host plants exposed to EPN infestations, identifying spectral signatures linked to induced systemic resistance. The computational workflow will be validated against empirical data from microcosm experiments tracking Steinernema carpocapsae infections in fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) larvae across varying soil moisture regimes. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing EPN field persistence, novel biomarkers for non-destructive monitoring of rhizosphere interactions, and genotype-environment mapping of bacterial symbiont resilience under drought scenarios. By bridging nematode behavioral ecology, microbial systems biology, and plant phenomics, this work addresses a critical gap in developing climate-adaptive biocontrol strategies while advancing computational methods for analyzing soil-borne multipartite symbioses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive decision-making in large-scale construction projects under dynamic uncertainty, integrating real-time data from IoT-enabled job sites with stochastic resource allocation models. Construction management faces persistent challenges in mitigating delays and cost overruns caused by volatile material prices, labor shortages, and environmental disruptions, yet existing planning tools rely on static schedules that fail to adapt to evolving conditions. The research will combine agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and multi-objective optimization to create a dynamic decision-support system capable of reallocating labor, equipment, and materials in response to real-time sensor data and predictive risk analytics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabyte-scale datasets from IoT devices (e.g., RFID trackers, drone surveys, equipment telemetry) while running parallelized simulations of alternative resource allocation strategies across thousands of probabilistic scenarios. The computational architecture will employ graph neural networks to model interdependencies between project phases and reinforcement learning to optimize trade-offs between cost, timeline, and carbon footprint metrics. Expected outcomes include a novel resilience metric for quantifying project vulnerability to supply chain shocks and climate-related delays, as well as open-source algorithms for scenario-aware resource scheduling. By enabling proactive adaptation to emergent risks in complex construction ecosystems, this work aims to reduce average project overruns by 15-20% in simulated environments while establishing computational benchmarks for sustainable infrastructure development. The HPC implementation will specifically target GPU-accelerated mixed-integer programming solvers and distributed memory systems to manage the combinatorial complexity of multi-stakeholder coordination problems inherent in megaproject management.
cip_definition: Any program in construction management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Higher education institutions face growing challenges in optimizing resource allocation amidst evolving enrollment patterns, financial constraints, and competing institutional priorities. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex, dynamic interactions between academic, operational, and financial variables at scale. This project seeks to develop a computational modeling platform to simulate and evaluate resource allocation strategies across multi-campus university systems. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML), the research will analyze how decentralized budget decisions, faculty hiring policies, and infrastructure investments interact with student demand and institutional performance metrics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support large-scale simulations incorporating heterogeneous datasets—including historical enrollment records, budget archives, and facilities utilization metrics—across a network of anonymized partner institutions. The ABM framework will parameterize institutional actors (e.g., departments, administrative units) as autonomous agents operating under policy constraints, while ML techniques will identify latent patterns in cross-institutional outcomes. Expected outputs include predictive models to assess trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., faculty workload equity vs. program expansion) and sensitivity analyses of funding allocation scenarios under demographic or economic shifts. By enabling real-time simulation of system-wide impacts from localized decisions, this work aims to advance data-driven leadership practices in higher education administration. The computational tools developed will provide actionable insights for administrators balancing strategic planning with operational sustainability, while contributing methodological innovations to the emerging field of computational organizational studies in academia. Successful validation against historical data from three public university systems will establish proof-of-concept for scaling the platform to broader institutional contexts.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project addresses the challenge of automating real-time auditing processes in large-scale financial systems, a critical need in modern accounting that demands integration with advanced computational methods. Traditional auditing frameworks struggle to efficiently analyze high-volume transactional data streams, particularly in decentralized or blockchain-based environments, leading to latency in anomaly detection and compliance risks. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a hybrid machine learning and cryptographic verification system optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The research will implement distributed graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex transactional networks across terabyte-scale datasets while leveraging zero-knowledge proofs for privacy-preserving validation of suspicious patterns. Computational workflows will be parallelized across GPU clusters to enable sub-second analysis intervals, with iterative model training incorporating adversarial samples to improve robustness against evolving financial fraud tactics. The project will further design a novel consensus mechanism tailored for auditing smart contracts, requiring large-scale simulations of Byzantine fault tolerance scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework that reduces false positive rates in anomaly detection by at least 40% compared to existing tools while maintaining interpretability for regulatory compliance. This work will advance interdisciplinary methodologies at the accounting-computer science interface by establishing scalable benchmarks for real-time audit automation and contributing optimized tensor operations for financial graph processing. The resulting infrastructure will directly benefit both academic researchers studying decentralized finance and enterprises requiring auditable, low-latency transaction systems.
cip_definition: A program that combines accounting with computer science and/or computer studies.

abstract: Adolescence is marked by dynamic neurobiological and psychosocial changes that shape cognitive and emotional development, yet the mechanisms through which these interacting systems influence decision-making and behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. This project seeks to model the multilevel interactions between neurodevelopmental trajectories, environmental contexts, and social learning processes during adolescence using computational approaches that require high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current limitations in analyzing high-dimensional longitudinal datasets—integrating neuroimaging, ecological momentary assessments, and social network data—hinder the field’s ability to capture real-time developmental processes. We propose a hybrid methodology combining dynamical systems modeling, graph-based network analyses, and reinforcement learning frameworks to simulate how individual differences in pubertal timing interact with peer influence dynamics to predict risk-taking behaviors. Agent-based models will parameterize decision-making processes under varying social reward contingencies, while Bayesian hierarchical models will assess longitudinal heterogeneity in developmental pathways. These computationally intensive methods demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, stochastic optimization across parameter spaces, and iterative model validation—tasks exceeding the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of critical neurosocial tipping points in adolescent risk behavior trajectories, (2) development of open-source tools for multilevel developmental systems modeling, and (3) empirically grounded frameworks for predicting individual differences in adaptive vs. maladaptive developmental outcomes. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to advance computational developmental science through scalable models that bridge biological, cognitive, and social domains, ultimately informing targeted prevention strategies and theoretical innovations in adolescent psychology research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical and synchronic phonetic variation across North Germanic languages using high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale acoustic and textual datasets. The research focuses on resolving ambiguities in the phonological evolution of Scandinavian languages, particularly the divergence of regional dialects in Norway, Sweden, and Denmark, and their relationship to insular Nordic varieties (e.g., Icelandic, Faroese). Current scholarship lacks comprehensive models of how vowel shifts and consonant gradation patterns propagated across these communities, partly due to computational limitations in processing heterogeneous data spanning medieval runic inscriptions, modern speech corpora, and digitized historical texts. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow. First, we will employ neural networks trained on parallelized phonetic data to detect subtle acoustic patterns in contemporary and archival speech recordings. Second, phylogenetic algorithms, adapted from computational biology, will model language diversification timelines, integrating textual evidence from Old Norse manuscripts and dialect maps. Finally, agent-based simulations will test sociolinguistic hypotheses about contact-driven changes in coastal versus inland regions. The project requires HPC resources to manage the scale of data (∼50 TB of audio, annotated texts, and metadata) and the complexity of simulations involving thousands of linguistic variables. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Nordic phonetic features, refined models of language change applicable to understudied minority varieties (e.g., Elfdalian), and methodological frameworks for cross-disciplinary computational linguistics. This work will advance the digital humanities in Scandinavian studies by enabling resource-intensive analyses previously constrained by local computing infrastructure, while contributing to broader linguistic theories of language contact and divergence.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on one or more of the languages, literatures, and linguistics of the peoples of Scandinavia and associated Northern European island groups. Programs may involve multiple languages and language families, not be specific as to the name of the language(s) studied, or be otherwise undifferentiated.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-institutional datasets on college student mental health and counseling outcomes. While student counseling services are critical for academic success and well-being, resource allocation decisions often rely on fragmented or localized data, limiting the generalizability of insights. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in intervention efficacy, demographic disparities in service utilization, and longitudinal outcomes across diverse student populations. Current approaches, constrained by conventional computing, struggle to process complex, high-dimensional datasets (e.g., multi-year counseling records, linked academic performance metrics, and demographic variables) at scale. This project will employ machine learning techniques, including deep learning and ensemble methods, to model student outcomes and simulate the impact of hypothetical counseling strategies. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) of anonymized counselor notes, clustering algorithms to subgroup students by risk profiles, and agent-based modeling to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for training predictive models on terabytes of heterogeneous data, optimizing hyperparameters via parallelized grid searches, and running computationally intensive simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting at-risk student populations, validating equity-centered counseling practices, and informing data-driven resource distribution (e.g., staffing, program types). Results will be disseminated through open-access predictive tools and visualizations to support evidence-based decision-making in student affairs. By bridging computational advances with counseling research, this work aims to enhance institutional capacity to address mental health crises and reduce attrition among marginalized students.
cip_title: College Student Counseling and Personnel Services
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the organization and provision of counseling, referral, assistance and administrative services to students in postsecondary educational institutions and adult education facilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as professional counselors in such settings. Includes instruction in applicable laws and policies, residential counseling and services, vocational counseling and placement services, remedial skills counseling, and therapeutic counselor intervention.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of healthcare environments by integrating spatial analytics, behavioral dynamics, and environmental health data. Current architectural practices for healthcare settings often rely on static guidelines that inadequately address the complex interplay between spatial configurations, occupant behavior, and health outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven approach combining generative design algorithms, agent-based modeling (ABM), and high-fidelity simulations of environmental variables (e.g., airflow, acoustics, light exposure) to predict how design choices influence infection transmission rates, patient recovery times, and caregiver efficiency. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run large-scale parametric simulations, iterating over thousands of spatial layouts while incorporating real-world datasets from hospital motion-tracking systems, microbial sampling, and patient health records. Machine learning models will be trained to identify design features that correlate with improved health metrics, enabling the generation of adaptive, context-specific design recommendations. Key computational challenges include scaling ABM to simulate occupant interactions in multi-story facilities, coupling computational fluid dynamics with epidemiological models, and optimizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) for 3D spatial synthesis. Outcomes will include an open-source simulation toolkit for evidence-based healthcare design, predictive models linking spatial parameters to health risks, and a framework for dynamically updating architectural guidelines in response to emerging public health threats. This work aims to advance interdisciplinary collaboration between computational sciences, architecture, and public health by establishing a methodological bridge between data-driven design and clinical outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the impact of design and architecture on the health of individuals and larger populations, and how to create settings that promote health, healing, and well-being. Includes instruction in architecture, interior design, human health services, communication studies, medical and clinical innovations, behavioral and engineering sciences, hospitals and health systems, and environmental conditions that influence health.

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in correctional facility resource allocation through advanced computational modeling, with the goal of optimizing rehabilitation outcomes while reducing operational costs. Despite evidence-based practices in corrections administration, facilities struggle to dynamically align staffing, programming, and infrastructure with fluctuating inmate populations and complex behavioral needs. Current decision-making relies on static protocols ill-suited to real-time operational demands, contributing to suboptimal rehabilitation rates and recidivism. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to simulate facility operations under variable constraints, integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of inmate behavior, system dynamics models of institutional workflows, and machine learning-driven risk prediction. The ABM component will simulate individual and group interactions influenced by program participation, staff-inmate ratios, and environmental stressors, while system dynamics models will map resource flows across educational, therapeutic, and custodial functions. Machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized historical data—including inmate demographics, program completion rates, and post-release outcomes—will identify critical leverage points for intervention. By deploying these models on HPC infrastructure, we will perform multi-scale optimization analyses to test hypothetical scenarios, such as adaptive scheduling of cognitive behavioral therapy sessions or reallocation of security personnel during program hours. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of forecasting the cascading impacts of resource allocation choices on safety, rehabilitation metrics, and budgetary outcomes. This work bridges correctional theory with computational social science, offering a novel paradigm for data-driven facility management. Successful implementation could inform policy frameworks for dynamic resource distribution in correctional systems, potentially reducing recidivism by 10-15% in modeled scenarios while maintaining operational safety standards. The computational architecture developed will be scalable to diverse facility types, establishing a template for evidence-based corrections administration in an era of constrained resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in quantum dynamical systems, where traditional numerical methods fail due to exponential scaling with dimensionality. Current approaches, such as finite element or spectral methods, become intractable beyond moderate dimensions, limiting progress in understanding complex quantum phenomena. To overcome this, we propose a novel hybrid algorithm combining stochastic gradient descent with adaptive sparse grid collocation, designed to exploit low-rank structures in solution manifolds while mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The method integrates deterministic solvers for localized features and probabilistic sampling for global behavior, enabling scalable approximations in phase space. Implementing this framework requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the iterative nature of the algorithm, the need for parallelized linear algebra operations on distributed sparse matrices, and large-scale parameter optimization. Key computational steps include GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition, dynamic load balancing for irregular grid refinements, and ensemble simulations to quantify numerical uncertainty. The project will leverage MPI for inter-node communication and CUDA for fine-grained parallelism, with validation against exact solutions in lower dimensions and benchmark quantum systems. Successful implementation will yield a publicly available software toolkit for high-dimensional PDEs, advancing mathematical tools for quantum mechanics and nonlinear wave propagation. Outcomes will demonstrate the feasibility of resolving 8-10 dimensional quantum systems with sub-exponential computational costs, providing a pathway to study entanglement dynamics and decoherence in scalable settings. This work bridges theoretical numerical analysis and practical HPC innovations, offering broadly applicable strategies for dimensionality reduction in computational mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of theoretical and applied mathematics to the solution of functional problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, numerical statistics, optimization, operational research, signal analysis, wavelets, image processing, fuzzy sets, spline, stochastic analysis, integral equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in modern printing operations by developing data-driven optimization models for resource allocation, production scheduling, and quality control in commercial printing workflows. Despite advances in digital printing technologies, many facilities struggle with balancing cost, speed, and environmental impact due to complex variables including substrate diversity, ink chemistry constraints, and fluctuating client demands. Current analytical tools often fail to account for real-time process interdependencies or the scale of multi-stage production systems. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate plant-wide operations through discrete-event simulation frameworks enhanced by machine learning algorithms trained on historical production data. Computational experiments will focus on three key areas: 1) dynamic scheduling under equipment failure scenarios, 2) waste reduction through predictive ink viscosity modeling, and 3) energy consumption optimization across hybrid analog/digital workflows. Large-scale parallelization will enable simultaneous evaluation of thousands of parameter combinations through Monte Carlo methods, while neural networks trained on GPU clusters will identify nonlinear relationships between press configurations and output quality metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit for printing managers, validated through industry partnerships with three regional commercial printers. The computational approach will advance sustainable practices in graphic communications by reducing material waste by an estimated 15-20% in test scenarios and improving equipment utilization rates. By applying HPC capabilities to traditionally non-technical domains, this work bridges critical gaps between operational research and practical printing management challenges while establishing computational reproducibility standards for the graphic arts industry.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical and managerial knowledge and skills to the processes and procedures of managing printing operations from initial design through finished product distribution. Includes instruction in the principles of graphic communications design and production; quality control; printing operations management; computerization; printing plant management; business finance and marketing; logistics and distribution; personnel supervision and leadership; and professional standards in the graphic communications industry.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to sustainable power generation, yet their efficiency and reliability are challenged by dynamic environmental conditions, aging infrastructure, and the integration of modern control systems. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model, simulate, and optimize hydroelectric turbine performance and maintenance protocols under variable operational scenarios. Current analytical tools lack the resolution to capture complex fluid-structure interactions, sediment erosion patterns, and real-time stress distributions in turbines, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and energy losses. To overcome these limitations, the proposed research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate multiphysics interactions within hydroelectric systems at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict component degradation and failure risks using historical sensor data and simulated wear patterns. The HPC environment is essential to process terabytes of sensor data, execute parallelized simulations of turbine clusters, and train predictive models with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for hydroelectric turbines, predictive maintenance algorithms to reduce unplanned downtime, and optimized turbine designs that enhance energy output by 10–15% under low-flow conditions. These advancements will directly inform technician training programs, equipping future professionals with data-driven repair strategies and system diagnostics. By bridging computational modeling with applied hydroelectric technology, this project aims to strengthen the resilience of renewable energy infrastructure while reducing operational costs and environmental impacts.
cip_title: Hydroelectric Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of patient care outcomes in practical nursing settings. A critical challenge in nursing practice is optimizing staffing workflows and clinical decision-making under dynamic, resource-constrained conditions. Traditional methods for predicting patient deterioration or allocating nursing staff often rely on static protocols, which may not account for real-time variables such as fluctuating patient acuity, staff availability, or emerging health data from wearable sensors. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework trained on multimodal datasets, including electronic health records (EHRs), nurse-patient interaction logs, and real-time biometric monitoring data. The computational workload involves processing terabytes of temporally structured, heterogeneous data to train deep learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures and time-series forecasting networks) capable of predicting short-term patient risks and recommending adaptive staffing adjustments. HPC resources are essential for parallelized hyperparameter tuning, large-scale simulation of care scenarios, and validation across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive tool to assist nurse managers in proactive resource allocation and a validated model for early detection of patient decompensation in vocational nursing contexts. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with nursing expertise, this work aims to reduce preventable adverse events, improve nurse workload equity, and establish scalable computational methods for personalized care planning in non-hospital settings. The results will directly inform competency-based training frameworks for nursing assistants and contribute novel computational strategies to the nursing science literature.
cip_title: Practical Nursing, Vocational Nursing and Nursing Assistants, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in practical nursing, vocational nursing, and nursing assistants, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Herbalism has long relied on empirical knowledge of plant-derived compounds for therapeutic applications, yet systematic validation of multi-compound interactions, bioavailability, and mechanisms of action remains a critical gap. This project seeks to computationally model the polypharmacological effects of traditional herbal formulations used in Western and Indigenous herbal medicine traditions, focusing on their modulation of neuroinflammatory pathways implicated in chronic pain and age-related cognitive decline. Current limitations in predicting synergistic or antagonistic interactions among hundreds of phytochemicals—particularly when combined with modern pharmaceuticals—require advanced computational approaches to address safety and efficacy concerns. We propose a multi-scale modeling framework integrating molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-driven metabolomic network analysis, and agent-based models of blood-brain barrier permeation. High-performance computing resources will enable the analysis of 50+ herbal species from the Appalachian materia medica tradition, each represented by 200-500 phytochemicals, against multi-omic datasets of neuroinflammatory targets. This will involve parallelized docking simulations (AutoDock-GPU, OpenMM), dynamic pharmacophore refinement, and ensemble learning to predict herb-drug interaction risks. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for identifying high-priority herbal candidates for experimental validation, (2) quantitative safety profiles for traditional formulations in common clinical use, and (3) an open-access database mapping 10,000+ phytochemicals to neuroinflammatory pathway targets. By establishing computational workflows tailored to herbalism's unique polycompound challenges, this research aims to bridge traditional ecological knowledge with contemporary systems pharmacology, addressing critical gaps in evidence-based integration of herbal therapies into mainstream healthcare. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated simulations and large-scale data integration tasks impractical on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to utilize the materia medica and clinical practices of Western, Native American, African, Australasian, and other herbal medicine traditions to prevent and cure illness and temporary physical disorders. Includes instruction in basic anatomy, physiology, pathology, and toxicology; nutrition; terminology and materia medica; therapeutic herbalism; herbal pharmacy; botanicals and ethnobotany; wildcrafting and harvesting; labeling and dispensing phytotherapy; counterindications; practice management; consultation skills; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-source social datasets for understanding how structural inequalities shape community resilience during environmental crises. As climate-related disasters intensify, marginalized populations face disproportionate risks, yet existing sociological models often lack the granularity and computational capacity to simulate dynamic interactions between institutional policies, demographic shifts, and localized adaptive behaviors. The research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate census microdata, geospatial risk assessments, and qualitative community survey data to simulate decision-making processes in urban and rural contexts under varying disaster scenarios. Computational workflows will employ parallel processing to handle heterogeneous data inputs, including NLP-driven analysis of interview transcripts and social media narratives, paired with demographic simulations of migration patterns and resource access. By scaling these models to regional populations (n ≈ 10^6 agents), the project aims to identify policy-relevant thresholds where targeted interventions—such as equitable infrastructure investments or participatory disaster planning—could mitigate cascading inequalities. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for applied sociologists, validated against case studies from three U.S. regions undergoing rapid environmental and demographic change. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive simulations, iterative parameter testing, and sensitivity analyses across diverse socioeconomic scenarios. Results will advance methodological integration of computational social science with public sociology, offering evidence-based frameworks for policymakers to prioritize equity in climate adaptation strategies. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on applied sociological research by bridging theoretical insights on structural inequality with actionable models for real-world intervention.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of sociological theory, methods, skills, and research to resolve particular issues in real-world settings. Includes instruction in data collection, group and organizational dynamics, participatory action research, program evaluation, sociological research methods, and sociological theory.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the integration of generative design and real-time environmental simulation within architectural technology.
