Current policy evaluation tools struggle to incorporate real-time threat intelligence or simulate multi-vector attacks across distributed networks, limiting their utility for strategic planning. To address this, we propose a multi-layered computational framework combining agent-based modeling, graph-theoretic network analysis, and machine learning techniques to simulate threat propagation, policy interventions, and cascading systemic impacts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations of nation-state and non-state actor behaviors, analyzing petabyte-scale datasets of historical cyber incidents, and training neural networks to predict policy outcomes under uncertainty. The computational architecture will integrate game-theoretic adversarial models with probabilistic risk assessment algorithms, enabling policymakers to stress-test defense strategies against emergent attack patterns. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible repository of validated policy simulation templates, quantitative metrics for cyber resiliency across critical infrastructure sectors, and adaptive policy recommendations informed by scenario-based sensitivity analyses. This work aims to advance cybersecurity governance by establishing a methodological foundation for evidence-based defense strategy formulation, directly supporting the development of standards for proactive vulnerability reduction and post-incident recovery. The requested resources will enable unprecedented granularity in modeling the socio-technical dimensions of cyber conflicts, ultimately contributing to more robust, agile, and empirically grounded defense policies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: Geothermal energy systems offer a sustainable pathway to meet growing energy demands, yet their deployment is hindered by challenges in predicting subsurface thermal behavior and optimizing energy extraction. Current models struggle to account for heterogeneous geological formations, dynamic fluid-rock interactions, and long-term reservoir performance, leading to uncertainties in system efficiency and economic viability. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced simulations of geothermal reservoirs, enabling precise characterization of subsurface processes and informed engineering decisions. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) creating multi-physics models that integrate heat transfer, fluid flow, and geomechanical deformation across varying spatial and temporal scales; (2) employing machine learning algorithms to calibrate models using field data from existing geothermal sites; and (3) optimizing well placement and operational parameters to maximize energy output while minimizing environmental impacts. Computational methods will include finite element analysis for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical simulations, parallelized Monte Carlo techniques for uncertainty quantification, and neural networks for pattern recognition in heterogeneous rock strata. The HPC resources will enable computationally intensive tasks such as 3D reservoir modeling at meter-scale resolution and ensemble runs to assess scenario-based risks. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting reservoir longevity, a publicly accessible database of synthetic geothermal reservoir datasets, and guidelines for adaptive management of geothermal systems. By advancing predictive capabilities, this work will directly support the design of next-generation geothermal technologies, reduce exploration costs, and accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy infrastructure. The computational tools developed will be shared with the geothermal research community, fostering collaboration and innovation in renewable energy engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing geothermal energy systems. Includes instruction in geothermal energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Plants dynamically adjust their circadian rhythms to synchronize with environmental cycles, a process critical for optimizing photosynthesis, nutrient allocation, and stress resilience. While the core circadian clock components in model plants are well characterized, the molecular mechanisms enabling plasticity in clock-regulated metabolic networks under fluctuating abiotic stresses—such as drought-heat synergies—remain unresolved. This project seeks to elucidate how post-translational modifications (PTMs) of clock-associated proteins rewire plant metabolic pathways under combinatorial stress. We will employ a multi-omics approach, integrating time-resolved phosphoproteomics, ubiquitinomics, and metabolomics data from *Sorghum bicolor*—a C4 crop with exceptional stress tolerance—exposed to concurrent drought and high-temperature regimes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three computational tasks: (1) Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to predict stress-induced conformational changes in key circadian kinases (e.g., CASEIN KINASE 1-like proteins) that alter substrate specificity; (2) Bayesian network inference to map condition-dependent PTM-metabolite causal relationships across diurnal cycles; and (3) Agent-based modeling of organelle-specific redox states influencing clock-protein stability. By resolving how stress-responsive PTMs reconfigure circadian-metabolic crosstalk, this work will establish predictive frameworks for engineering crops with maintained productivity under climate volatility. The computational pipelines developed will be adaptable to other C4 species, addressing a critical gap in translating molecular chronobiology to agricultural resilience.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to the study of biomolecular structures, functions, and processes specific to plants and plant substances. Includes instruction in the biochemistry of plant cells, nuclear-cytoplasmic interactions, molecular cytostructures, photosynthesis, plant molecular genetics, and the molecular biology of plant diseases.

abstract: Sleep disorders, such as obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), insomnia, and circadian rhythm dysregulation, are pervasive yet mechanistically complex conditions with poorly understood interactions between genetic, neurological, and physiological factors. Current diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks often rely on phenotypic classifications that inadequately capture heterogeneity, limiting personalized interventions. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including polysomnography (PSG) time series, genomic profiles, and electronic health records (EHRs) from a cohort of 15,000 patients. The primary research problem focuses on identifying latent biomarkers and causal pathways underlying sleep disorder subtypes using computational methods that require intensive parallel processing. A hybrid approach integrating deep neural networks (DNNs) and Bayesian hierarchical modeling will be employed to disentangle temporal dependencies in PSG signals, correlate them with genetic variants, and predict treatment responses. Additionally, computational simulations of neural circuit dynamics will model interactions between orexinergic pathways and sleep-wake transitions, utilizing differential equations solved over high-dimensional parameter spaces. These analyses demand significant memory allocation (~2 TB RAM), multi-node GPU clusters for DNN training, and scalable storage for iterative model validation. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel subtype-specific biomarkers, predictive algorithms for therapeutic efficacy, and mechanistic insights into neurotransmitter dysregulation in sleep disorders. The computational workflows will be open-sourced to enable reproducibility, and results will directly inform three ongoing clinical trials targeting genotype-guided interventions for OSA. By enabling the integration of heterogeneous data at unprecedented scale, this project aims to advance precision sleep medicine, reduce trial-and-error treatment paradigms, and provide a template for computationally driven clinical research in resource-constrained healthcare settings.
cip_definition: Research focused on Sleep Medicine

abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic landscape modifications are rapidly altering habitat suitability for aquatic and terrestrial species, necessitating advanced predictive models to inform adaptive management strategies. This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit, multi-species simulation framework to assess climate resilience and habitat connectivity across freshwater and coastal ecosystems in the Pacific Northwest. The research integrates high-resolution remote sensing data, species occurrence records, and hydrodynamic models to quantify how shifting temperature regimes, hydrologic patterns, and land-use changes affect critical life history stages for anadromous fish populations and their associated riparian predators. Computational challenges arise from the need to process petabyte-scale environmental datasets, implement individual-based movement models across heterogeneous landscapes, and run ensemble climate projections at 10m spatial resolution. We request allocation of high-performance computing resources to parallelize three core components: (1) machine learning classification of LiDAR and multispectral imagery to map microhabitat features, (2) hydrodynamic simulations of stream networks under variable snowpack and precipitation scenarios, and (3) Bayesian network analysis of species-environment interactions across temporal scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU acceleration for convolutional neural networks and distributed memory processing for landscape genetic analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of climate refugia, prioritized corridors for habitat restoration, and open-source tools for optimizing protected area networks under multiple climate futures. This work directly supports state and tribal wildlife agencies in implementing climate-adaptive management plans while advancing computational ecology methods for coupled human-natural systems. By quantifying threshold responses in critical ecosystems, the project aims to reduce uncertainty in conservation decision-making under rapid environmental change.
cip_title: Wildlife, Fish and Wildlands Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conserve and manage wilderness areas and the flora, marine and aquatic life therein, and manage wildlife reservations and zoological/aquarium facilities for recreational, commercial, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in wildlife biology, marine/aquatic biology, environmental science, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, natural resources management and policy, outdoor recreation and parks management, the design and operation of natural and artificial wildlife habitats, applicable law and regulations, and related administrative and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in nurse anesthesia by modeling patient-specific responses to anesthetic agents. A critical challenge in anesthesia practice is the variability in drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics across individuals, which contributes to adverse events such as intraoperative awareness, postoperative delirium, or hemodynamic instability. Current dosing protocols rely on population averages, but factors like genetic polymorphisms, comorbidities, and polypharmacy necessitate personalized approaches. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and physiological simulations to predict individualized anesthetic requirements. The project will develop machine learning models trained on retrospective EHRs from 50,000+ surgical cases, including anesthesia records, vital sign trajectories, and postoperative outcomes. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will characterize how genetic variants in drug-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP2B6, CYP3A4) influence propofol and opioid metabolism. These components will be unified in a multiscale model optimized via HPC-enabled parameter sweeps to account for interactions between genetic, physiological, and clinical variables. The computational workflow will require parallel processing for large-scale genomic simulations, distributed training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous clinical data, and sensitivity analyses across simulated patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include predictive models for optimal anesthetic dosing and real-time risk stratification tools deployable in perioperative settings. Successful validation against prospective clinical data could transform anesthesia practice by reducing trial-and-error dosing and mitigating adverse events. This work will also establish a scalable infrastructure for integrating -omics data into nurse anesthesia research, addressing a critical gap in the field. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of multiscale modeling and enable rapid iteration of predictive algorithms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between cellular adhesion mechanisms and cytoskeletal reorganization during collective cell migration, a critical yet poorly understood process in tissue repair and morphogenesis. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the multiscale complexity of cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, particularly in heterogeneous microenvironments. We propose an integrated computational-experimental framework to model and simulate the spatiotemporal coordination of adhesion receptor clustering, actomyosin contractility, and force transmission across epithelial cell sheets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale agent-based simulations of individual cell behaviors coupled with continuum-scale finite element modeling of tissue-level mechanical stresses. The computational model will integrate live-cell imaging data from fluorescence microscopy (e.g., vinculin dynamics, traction force microscopy) and perturbation experiments targeting focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and Rho GTPase signaling pathways. Key computational challenges include parameter optimization across multiple spatial scales (molecular clusters to tissue domains) and real-time simulation of stochastic adhesion complex assembly/disassembly events in 3D extracellular matrix environments. Expected outcomes include predictive models of collective migration patterns under varying matrix stiffness and adhesion ligand density conditions, identification of critical regulatory nodes in mechanochemical signaling networks, and quantitative frameworks for interpreting emergent tissue-scale behaviors from subcellular events. The requested resources will directly support parallelized computation of parameter space explorations, machine learning-assisted analysis of high-dimensional simulation outputs, and visualization of terabyte-scale dynamic datasets. This work will advance fundamental understanding of how cells collectively interpret mechanical cues during tissue reorganization while establishing computational tools for probing multiscale cellular behaviors that are inaccessible to purely experimental approaches.
detailed_field: Cell/ cellular biology and anatomy nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure, function, and regulation of cells as individual units and as components of larger systems. Includes instruction in cell chemistry, cellular dynamics, cellular replication and reproduction, cell anatomy, membrane function, organelles, cell adhesion and extracellular matrices, cell dynamics and motility, meiosis and mytosis, signal transduction, regulation, recognition and defense mechanisms, the cell cycle, cell metabolism and respiration, gene expression, and studies of cell types and characteristics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the capabilities of 3-D modeling and design workflows through high-fidelity simulations and resource-intensive computational analyses, enabled by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current 3-D modeling tools face limitations in efficiently processing complex geometries, simulating multi-physics interactions (e.g., thermal, structural), and optimizing designs for additive manufacturing. These challenges are exacerbated when working with high-resolution datasets from 3-D scanning or large-scale parametric models, where conventional computing infrastructure struggles with memory constraints and processing latency. To address this, the proposed research will leverage HPC resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) workflows, accelerate topology optimization algorithms, and enable real-time rendering of intricate 3-D models. Computational methods will include GPU-accelerated solvers for stress-strain simulations in CAD environments, machine learning-driven mesh refinement for 3-D scanned data, and distributed computing frameworks to manage iterative design-test cycles for additive manufacturing parameter optimization. The project will validate these approaches using case studies in architectural component design and industrial tooling, where precision and material efficiency are critical. Expected outcomes include reduced computational bottlenecks in handling billion-element meshes, improved accuracy in predicting material behavior during 3-D printing, and scalable workflows for integrating multi-sensor scan data into unified models. By enhancing the speed and resolution of 3-D modeling processes, this work aims to bridge gaps between digital design and physical fabrication, directly benefiting industries reliant on rapid prototyping and customized manufacturing. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required scale of computation, enabling iterative exploration of design spaces that are currently infeasible with departmental-level hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurocognitive and psychosomatic mechanisms underlying transpersonal counseling interventions, with a focus on therapeutic trance and meditative practices, to advance evidence-based frameworks for spiritual psychology. Despite growing interest in integrating spiritual systems into counseling, there remains a critical gap in understanding how these practices modulate consciousness, emotional regulation, and somatic responses at scale. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal datasets, including electroencephalography (EEG), heart rate variability (HRV), and qualitative self-report data from participants engaged in guided therapeutic trance and mindfulness-based rituals. Agent-based modeling will simulate collective consciousness dynamics in group healing practices, while machine learning pipelines will identify patterns linking specific interventions to psychospiritual outcomes (e.g., transcendent experiences, emotional integration). A novel computational framework will be developed to map transient states of altered consciousness during rituals, correlating neural oscillations with phenomenological reports. The project’s computational demands arise from processing high-resolution temporal neurophysiological data (≈10 TB across 200 participants), running parallelized simulations of consciousness networks, and training transformer models on qualitative narratives to decode spiritual meaning-making. Expected outcomes include predictive models of intervention efficacy, optimized protocols for personalized transpersonal counseling, and a publicly accessible database of annotated spiritual practice biomarkers. By bridging first-person experiential data with third-person computational analysis, this work aims to establish empirical foundations for spiritual psychology while respecting its phenomenological complexity, ultimately enhancing the rigor and accessibility of transpersonal approaches in applied counseling contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to pursue spiritual and psychological practices for counseling. Includes instruction in emotional intelligence, expressive movement, healing practices and rituals, human consciousness, movement and meditation, psychosomatic connection, spiritual systems and wellness, transpersonal counseling, and therapeutic trance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized home furnishing design and installation processes through advanced simulation, machine learning, and generative modeling. Current methods for space planning, material selection, and aesthetic coordination rely heavily on manual iteration, limiting scalability and adaptability to diverse client needs, spatial constraints, and sustainability goals. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these challenges by training deep neural networks on multimodal datasets—including 3D room scans, textile performance metrics, client preference surveys, and environmental impact profiles—to predict optimal furniture layouts, material pairings, and decorative configurations. Agent-based models will simulate long-term wear patterns and ergonomic interactions across upholstery materials, while finite element analysis will assess stress distributions in custom-built furnishings. A parallelized workflow will integrate these components into a real-time visualization tool, enabling installers to test thousands of design permutations against client-specific criteria. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support system that reduces material waste by 15-20% through predictive sustainability analytics, improves client satisfaction via adaptive personalization algorithms, and establishes quantitative metrics for evaluating aesthetic coherence in hybrid physical-digital design spaces. The computational infrastructure will also enable the creation of an open-access repository of simulated home environments, advancing research in human-centered spatial interaction beyond traditional empirical methods. By bridging computational design, behavioral analytics, and material science within the home furnishings domain, this project aims to redefine industry standards for efficiency, customization, and ecological responsibility in residential spaces.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in home furnishings and decorations. Includes instruction in selecting, purchasing, and designing home furnishings, decorations, and equipment; floral design; accessory construction; textiles; and upholstery.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the drivers of phylogenetic discordance and biogeographic patterns in a hyper-diverse clade of tropical angiosperms, integrating large-scale molecular, morphological, and ecological datasets to resolve longstanding uncertainties in evolutionary relationships and diversification processes. A major challenge in systematic biology is reconciling conflicting phylogenetic signals arising from incomplete lineage sorting, hybridization, and convergent trait evolution, particularly in lineages with rapid radiations. To address this, we will employ a computational pipeline combining Bayesian species-tree inference, divergence-time estimation, and comparative methods to analyze genome-scale sequence data (targeted enrichment sequencing), fossil-calibrated trait matrices, and historical biogeographic reconstructions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the project’s scope: datasets include ~2,000 loci across 500+ species, 10,000+ morphological character states, and probabilistic biogeographic models requiring iterative likelihood calculations across millions of tree topologies. Key computational steps include parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for multilocus coalescent models, machine learning-assisted morphological homology assessments, and likelihood-based tests for trait-dependent diversification. The requested resources will enable efficient processing of these analyses, which are otherwise computationally intractable on standard laboratory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a robust, time-calibrated phylogeny resolving contentious nodes in the focal clade, (2) identification of ecological and biogeographic factors correlated with diversification rate shifts, and (3) novel protocols for integrating high-dimensional morphological data into phylogenomic frameworks. This work will advance systematic theory by clarifying how heterogeneous evolutionary processes shape taxonomic diversity in tropical hotspots, while providing open-access computational workflows and a curated database of phenotypic characters to support future studies. Results will directly inform conservation prioritization by identifying evolutionarily distinct lineages in threatened ecosystems.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical and empirical study of the principles and processes underlying the origin and maintenance of biological taxonomic diversity; related biogeographical and evolutionary patterns; and studies of the origin, diversification, distribution, and extinction of species and lineages. Includes instruction in phylogenetic analysis, structural development and molecular evolution, classification and taxonomic theory, biological nomenclature, taxonomic assignment, evolutionary theory, biological surveys and inventories, computer modeling, and database building.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing personalized counseling interventions for postsecondary students facing academic and psychosocial challenges. Current counseling practices often rely on generalized frameworks that may not adequately account for the complex, dynamic interactions between individual student characteristics, institutional contexts, and intervention outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational model integrating longitudinal student data—including academic performance, mental health surveys, and counselor session transcripts—to identify patterns in intervention efficacy across diverse student subgroups. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze unstructured counseling session data, combined with multilevel Bayesian network modeling to map relationships between intervention types, student traits, and longitudinal outcomes. Computational demands include training transformer-based NLP models on anonymized session transcripts (estimated 50,000+ documents) and running iterative simulations to test intervention scenarios across synthetic student cohorts. HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive NLP tasks and enabling rapid parameter space exploration in Bayesian networks. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive framework for matching students to optimal counseling strategies based on their profiles, 2) identification of underrecognized risk/protective factors in student persistence, and 3) open-source tools for dynamic intervention planning. Results will directly inform evidence-based practices in student support services while advancing methodological integration of computational social science approaches in education research. This work addresses a critical need for scalable, data-driven decision-making tools in student counseling—a field historically constrained by small-sample qualitative methods—and demonstrates how HPC can catalyze innovation in personalized education support systems.
cip_title: Student Counseling and Personnel Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in student counseling and personnel services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on Turkish language evolution and dialectal variation across historical and modern contexts. The primary research problem centers on the challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous text corpora spanning pre-modern Ottoman Turkish (using Perso-Arabic script) and modern Turkish (Latin script), which exhibit significant grammatical, lexical, and orthographic shifts. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for identifying patterns in phonology, morphology, and semantic change across these variants, particularly when analyzing understudied dialects or non-standard texts from regional archives. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for cross-script alignment, neural machine translation for historical text normalization, and graph-based algorithms to map dialectal features. Computational philological workflows will be developed to automate the analysis of morphological segmentation in agglutinative structures and detect loanword integration from Arabic, Persian, and European languages. HPC resources are critical for training deep learning models on multi-terabyte corpora, parallelizing comparative analyses across temporal and geographic axes, and running computationally intensive simulations of language change. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for Ottoman Turkish NLP, a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic features, and quantitative models tracing syntactic simplification trends from the 15th to 21st centuries. These resources will enable novel research on language contact phenomena in Anatolian dialects and accelerate the digitization of endangered vernacular texts. By bridging computational methods with Turkological scholarship, this project aims to establish a scalable framework for studying lesser-resourced languages with complex historical trajectories, while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations in digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Turkish language in either or both of its pre-modern and modern variants. Includes instruction in philology; Ottoman Turkish; Modern Turkish; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Palliative care and pain management require personalized treatment strategies to address the complex interplay of biological, psychological, and social factors influencing patient outcomes. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may fail to account for individual variability in pain perception, treatment response, and disease progression. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating multimodal patient data—including electronic health records, genomic profiles, and longitudinal symptom reports—to identify predictive biomarkers and optimize dynamic treatment regimens. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational challenges of analyzing high-dimensional, heterogeneous datasets while preserving clinical interpretability. To address this, we will implement machine learning models (e.g., Bayesian hierarchical clustering, recurrent neural networks) and causal inference methods to model temporal relationships between interventions and outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on a cohort of 15,000+ palliative care patients, enabling parallel processing of genomic association studies, real-time simulation of treatment pathways, and sensitivity analyses across diverse demographic subgroups. Key computational steps include dimensionality reduction of multi-omics data, reinforcement learning for adaptive treatment recommendation systems, and validation through in silico clinical trials. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for opioid response phenotypes, (2) dynamic decision-support tools for titrating multimodal therapies, and (3) mechanistic insights into neuroimmune pathways influencing refractory pain. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle complex interactions at scale, this work aims to advance precision palliative care, reduce trial-and-error prescribing, and establish a computational infrastructure for translating large-scale clinical data into actionable treatment protocols. The results will directly inform the design of a forthcoming multicenter clinical trial evaluating algorithm-guided pain management strategies.
cip_definition: Research focused on Palliative Care/Pain Management

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in mineral extraction efficiency and mine safety through advanced computational modeling and simulation. A key research problem in mining technology is the inability of conventional methods to accurately predict geomechanical instabilities in complex geological formations or optimize mineral processing workflows under dynamic environmental constraints. Current approaches often rely on oversimplified analytical models or limited-scale experimental data, leading to suboptimal resource recovery and elevated risks of structural failures. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FE), discrete element method (DEM), and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model rock fracturing, granular material flow, and slurry transport processes at unprecedented resolution. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of mine-scale geometries with heterogeneous material properties, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on historical sensor data from operational mines to refine predictive accuracy. Key deliverables include GPU-accelerated simulations of stress redistribution during excavation, real-time predictive models for equipment wear in processing plants, and probabilistic risk assessments for collapse scenarios under varying mineralogical conditions. The computational workflow will utilize open-source platforms like OpenFOAM and LAMMPS, optimized for distributed-memory architectures to handle terabytes of spatially resolved geological data. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for adaptive drilling strategies, improved tailings management systems, and digital twins for mine ventilation networks. By integrating HPC-driven insights with field operations, this research aims to reduce energy consumption in mineral processing by 15–20%, enhance worker safety through early hazard detection systems, and extend the operational lifespan of aging mines. Results will be disseminated as open-access simulation toolkits tailored for mining engineers, fostering broader adoption of data-driven decision-making in resource-intensive industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: The integration of personalized immunotherapy into clinical oncology remains hindered by the dynamic complexity of immune-tumor interactions and interpatient variability. Current computational models lack the resolution to simulate these interactions at scale, limiting their utility in predicting patient-specific therapeutic outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, agent-based modeling framework to simulate immune cell behavior within the tumor microenvironment, informed by multi-omics data from individual patients. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale simulations capturing spatial and temporal dynamics of immune cell infiltration, tumor antigen presentation, and cytokine signaling networks. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze simulation outputs, identify predictive biomarkers of response, and optimize combinatorial therapeutic strategies. Key computational challenges include managing the stochasticity of cell-cell interactions, scaling models to accommodate single-cell omics data, and ensuring real-time adaptability for clinical integration. By correlating simulated outcomes with longitudinal clinical data from patients undergoing immunotherapy, the project aims to validate model accuracy and refine predictive capabilities. Successful implementation of this framework could transform therapeutic decision-making by enabling clinicians to test virtual treatment scenarios, prioritize high-efficacy regimens, and minimize off-target effects. The requested HPC resources are critical to handle the computational load of parallelized simulations, which involve millions of interacting agents and parameter combinations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for immuno-oncology research and clinically actionable insights into patient-specific resistance mechanisms. This interdisciplinary approach bridges systems biology, clinical oncology, and computational science, advancing precision medicine while operating squarely within the domain of medical therapeutic innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of medicine, involving the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illnesses, injuries, and other disorders of the human body. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, clinical medicine, examination and diagnosis, patient communications, medical ethics and law, professional standards, and rotations in specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, orthopedics, neurology, ophthalmology, radiology, clinical pathology, anesthesiology, family medicine, and psychiatry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-agent business ecosystems under uncertainty, integrating stochastic modeling, behavioral economics, and distributed machine learning. Contemporary enterprises operate in environments characterized by rapidly shifting consumer preferences, competitive actions, and supply chain disruptions, yet existing analytical tools often fail to capture the emergent complexity arising from interdependent stakeholder interactions. The research will create agent-based simulation architectures that model strategic decision pathways across three scales: individual consumer micro-behaviors, organizational resource allocation patterns, and macroeconomic shock propagation. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore decision trees across 10^6+ possible state configurations, coupled with evolutionary algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal strategies balancing risk and innovation. A novel feature involves embedding transformer-based neural networks within simulation agents to enable adaptive learning from real-time streaming data on market sentiment and competitor actions. Computational challenges include managing asynchronous updates across heterogeneous agents, optimizing memory allocation for high-dimensional state representations, and ensuring numerical stability in gradient-based strategy updates. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for scenario stress-testing in strategic planning, validated through case studies in cross-industry partnerships facing climate transition risks. The resource request targets GPU-accelerated nodes for deep reinforcement learning components and high-memory nodes for large-scale sensitivity analyses. By bridging discrete optimization, behavioral simulation, and enterprise-scale analytics, this work aims to advance decision theory while providing practical frameworks for resilient business adaptation in volatile markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply data science to solve business challenges. Includes instruction in machine learning, optimization methods, computer algorithms, probability and stochastic models, information economics, logistics, strategy, consumer behavior, marketing, and visual analytics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for public sector entities facing climate-related fiscal risks. As governments increasingly confront budgetary pressures from extreme weather events, shifting regulatory landscapes, and transitional climate policies, traditional static budget models fail to capture the complex interdependencies between environmental volatility, infrastructure investments, and long-term fiscal health. The project will create a high-resolution simulation platform integrating stochastic climate projections, heterogeneous agent-based modeling of municipal stakeholders, and machine learning-driven vulnerability assessments. Using historical fiscal data from coastal municipalities and climate scenario outputs from IPCC reports, we will parameterize a multi-objective optimization model that balances short-term service delivery obligations against long-term resilience investments. The computational approach leverages parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate thousands of budget pathway permutations under variable carbon pricing regimes, disaster frequency distributions, and intergovernmental funding constraints. By implementing this framework on high-performance computing infrastructure, we aim to overcome current limitations in temporal granularity and system complexity that restrict conventional econometric tools. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of real-time sensitivity analysis for public finance officers, novel metrics for climate-adjusted municipal bond risk assessment, and policy recommendations for adaptive capital budgeting processes. This work bridges computational sustainability science with public financial management, addressing a critical gap in fiscal policy tools for climate-vulnerable jurisdictions while advancing methodological innovations in resource allocation modeling under deep uncertainty.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the financial assets and budgets of public sector organizations. Includes instruction in public trusts and investments; the laws and procedures used to plan, prepare and administer public agency budgets; and the preparation and analysis of public budget projections and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize care delivery workflows and reduce adverse patient outcomes in settings reliant on nursing assistants and patient care aides. Nursing aides are critical frontline providers in long-term and acute care facilities, yet high patient-to-staff ratios, time-sensitive tasks, and variability in patient deterioration patterns create challenges in prioritizing care. Current protocols often rely on static schedules or reactive interventions, which may delay response to emerging risks such as falls, pressure injuries, or sepsis. To address this, we propose a machine learning approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal patient data—including electronic health records, real-time vital signs, and mobility metrics—to dynamically predict patient risk states and recommend task prioritization. A hybrid neural network architecture will integrate temporal (e.g., hourly vital trends) and contextual (e.g., medication schedules, mobility limitations) data streams, trained on retrospective datasets from partnered healthcare facilities. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, optimize hyperparameters across parallelized simulations, and validate models against diverse clinical scenarios through in silico trials. Expected outcomes include a real-time decision support tool that identifies high-risk patients and suggests context-aware task sequences for nursing aides, balancing acuity needs with workflow efficiency. Successful implementation could reduce preventable adverse events by 15–25% in pilot facilities while providing empirical insights into workload distribution patterns. This work directly aligns with nursing science priorities to enhance auxiliary staff effectiveness through scalable computational tools, ultimately improving patient safety in resource-constrained environments.
cip_title: Nursing Assistant/ Aide and Patient Care Assistant/ Aide
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine nursing-related services to patients in hospitals or long-term care facilities, under the training and supervision of a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive workplace design in response to dynamic organizational needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between spatial configurations, occupant behavior, and operational efficiency. Traditional facility planning methods rely on static benchmarks or heuristic evaluations, which struggle to account for real-time variables such as fluctuating occupancy patterns, evolving health and safety protocols, and heterogeneous employee preferences. The research problem centers on creating predictive models that integrate environmental psychology principles, real-time sensor data, and multi-objective optimization to generate workspace layouts that balance productivity, well-being, and resource efficiency. Using agent-based modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, the project will analyze how spatial parameters (e.g., desk density, circulation pathways, shared amenities) interact with human factors (e.g., collaboration frequency, noise sensitivity) and environmental conditions (e.g., air quality, thermal comfort). HPC resources are critical to scaling these simulations across thousands of hypothetical scenarios, enabling probabilistic assessments of design resilience under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., energy use vs. social connectivity) and identifies Pareto-optimal solutions for facility managers. This work bridges gaps between data science, behavioral economics, and architectural design, offering a novel methodology for post-pandemic workspace strategy. By advancing computational approaches to facility planning, the project aims to establish evidence-based standards for adaptive environments while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional, policy-adjacent domains. Results will be validated against empirical data from partner organizations, with open-source model components to encourage broader adoption in workplace innovation research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on strategic workplace and facility planning and that prepares individuals to function as facility and event managers and workplace consultants. Includes instruction in the principles of aesthetic and functional design, environmental psychology and organizational behavior, real estate planning, principles of occupational health and safety, event planning and management, operations management, and applicable regulatory and policy issues.

abstract:
Modern office environments are complex systems requiring dynamic coordination of personnel, resources, and spatial configurations. Traditional management approaches often rely on static models or heuristic decision-making, which may not adequately address interdependencies between variables such as workforce scheduling, real-time space utilization, and evolving operational demands. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop data-driven optimization frameworks for office management and supervision. The research will focus on two interconnected challenges: (1) modeling the impact of hybrid work arrangements on team productivity and resource allocation, and (2) optimizing office layouts and workflows under fluctuating operational priorities.  

The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning techniques to analyze multidimensional datasets encompassing employee mobility patterns, task completion rates, and facility usage metrics. Large-scale simulations will evaluate thousands of potential scheduling scenarios, workspace configurations, and technology deployment strategies while accounting for constraints such as budget limitations, equipment availability, and workplace safety regulations. Machine learning models will be trained on historical operational data and real-time IoT sensor inputs to predict workflow bottlenecks and recommend adaptive management strategies.  

This research requires HPC resources to manage the computational intensity of parallelized simulations and iterative model training processes. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for minimizing workflow disruptions, evidence-based strategies for hybrid workspace design, and dynamic decision-support systems for supervisors. The project will advance academic understanding of computational approaches to organizational management while delivering practical solutions that enhance operational efficiency, reduce overhead costs, and improve employee satisfaction in business administration contexts. Results will be disseminated through open-source optimization frameworks and case studies demonstrating measurable improvements in office management outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise and manage the operations and personnel of business offices and management-level divisions. Includes instruction in employee supervision, management, and labor relations; budgeting; scheduling and coordination; office systems operation and maintenance; office records management, organization, and security; office facilities design and space management; preparation and evaluation of business management data; and public relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced optimization frameworks for next-generation wireless communication systems, with a focus on enhancing spectral efficiency and reliability in densely deployed 5G/6G networks and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. The proliferation of heterogeneous devices, dynamic traffic patterns, and stringent quality-of-service requirements in modern telecommunications infrastructure necessitates computationally intensive modeling to address challenges in interference mitigation, resource allocation, and adaptive beamforming. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating machine learning-driven channel estimation, large-scale optimization of massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) configurations, and stochastic modeling of millimeter-wave propagation in urban environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for executing parallelized electromagnetic simulations using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, training deep neural networks for real-time signal processing, and solving non-convex optimization problems across distributed antenna systems. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of channel state information and network traffic logs collected from experimental testbeds. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic spectrum sharing, optimized precoding matrices for reduced inter-cell interference, and validated models for energy-efficient beam alignment in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted networks. These advancements will directly inform the design of scalable, low-latency communication protocols for smart city applications and industrial IoT deployments. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of network topology variations and physical-layer configurations that are infeasible with existing campus cluster capabilities, significantly accelerating the translation of theoretical models into practical implementation guidelines for telecom operators and standards bodies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of telecommunications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in telecommunications, computer networking, communications networks and systems, signals, circuits, fiber optics, and wireless systems and technology.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies for multi-venue hospitality ecosystems using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, real-time interactions between traveler behavior, seasonal demand fluctuations, and operational constraints. Current pricing models in hospitality management often operate in silos, failing to account for cross-sector dependencies (e.g., how concert events impact hotel occupancy and restaurant demand) or hyperlocal externalities like transportation disruptions. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including tourist mobility patterns, event calendars, and competitive market pricing—to simulate decision-making scenarios across interconnected hospitality services. The computational model will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate pricing strategies under stochastic demand conditions, coupled with graph neural networks to capture spatial-temporal relationships between venues. By leveraging HPC resources, we aim to process multi-terabyte datasets encompassing five years of tourism records, weather data, and social media sentiment across 12 major global destinations. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for revenue resilience during demand shocks and a novel metric for "hospitality ecosystem saturation" to guide capacity planning. This work bridges computational economics and operations research, advancing decision-making in tourism-dependent economies while addressing scalability challenges in legacy hospitality management systems. The proposed models will be validated against real-world data from a pilot partnership with a multinational resort operator, with iterative refinements enabled by GPU-accelerated optimization loops. Results will provide actionable insights for coordinating pricing, staffing, and inventory decisions across spatially distributed service networks, particularly in emerging markets where tourism infrastructure growth outpaces existing analytical capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing turfgrass health and playability on golf courses while minimizing environmental impact and operational costs through advanced computational modeling. Traditional grounds management relies on generalized agronomic practices, which often lead to over-application of water, fertilizers, and pesticides, contributing to ecological strain and financial inefficiency. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-resolution, multi-scale simulation framework integrating site-specific variables such as microclimate data, soil hydrology, turfgrass genetics, and pest dynamics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled irrigation systems, drones, and soil probes, enabling dynamic modeling of turf responses under diverse scenarios. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical and synthetic datasets to predict localized stress factors (e.g., drought, disease outbreaks) and recommend precision interventions. By parallelizing complex agent-based models of root-zone microbial communities and nutrient cycling, the simulations will quantify trade-offs between turf quality, resource use, and ecosystem health at unprecedented spatial granularity. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support tool for groundskeepers, optimized irrigation and pest management protocols, and a validated sustainability index for golf course certification programs. The computational framework will advance the integration of precision agriculture techniques into recreational land management, offering scalable solutions for an industry under increasing pressure to adopt environmentally responsible practices. This work bridges agronomy, data science, and environmental management, establishing a novel interdisciplinary niche within golf course operations research.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Golf Course Operation and Grounds Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operation of golf courses. Includes instruction in turf grass science and management, golf course design and construction, grounds equipment and operation, pest control, and grounds management.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the challenge of optimizing drug delivery systems for poorly soluble therapeutics, a critical barrier in pharmaceutical development. Many promising drug candidates exhibit low bioavailability due to solubility limitations, necessitating advanced formulation strategies. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and simulate nanostructured drug carriers, including lipid nanoparticles and polymeric micelles, at atomic and mesoscopic scales. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using GROMACS and coarse-grained models will elucidate molecular interactions governing drug encapsulation, stability, and release kinetics under physiological conditions. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict carrier performance across diverse chemical spaces, reducing experimental trial-and-error. The computational workflow will involve large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate carrier designs under varied pH, temperature, and concentration gradients, generating multi-terabyte datasets. HPC resources are essential to achieve sufficient sampling timescales (microsecond-range simulations) and to process high-dimensional data from 10,000+ simulated formulation variants. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal carrier compositions for three model therapeutics with documented solubility challenges, as well as predictive frameworks linking molecular descriptors to release profiles. This work will advance rational design principles for nanomedicine platforms while providing open-access simulation protocols to the pharmaceutical sciences community. Successful implementation could shorten preclinical development timelines by 30-50% for insoluble drugs, with direct applications in oncology and infectious disease treatment. The requested computing allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, parallelized data analysis, and storage of reference datasets for reproducibility.
cip_title: Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, and Administration, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of polypharmacology-driven drug interactions and their implications for therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. A critical challenge in pharmacology is predicting how drugs with multi-target effects—particularly those used in combination therapies—interact dynamically with biological systems to produce synergistic, additive, or antagonistic outcomes. Traditional experimental methods are limited in scalability and temporal resolution, especially when evaluating complex pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) relationships across diverse physiological conditions. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning (ML) to map the behavior of multi-target drugs in heterogeneous biological environments. PBPK models will simulate drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) across virtual patient populations, while MD simulations will resolve atomistic interactions between drugs and off-target proteins implicated in adverse effects. ML algorithms, trained on curated datasets of drug-target affinities and clinical toxicity reports, will predict high-risk drug combinations and optimize dosing regimens. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale of simulations, which involve millions of atomic trajectories, and to process high-dimensional PK-PD datasets spanning genetic, metabolic, and demographic variables. Expected outcomes include predictive models for drug-drug and drug-protein interactions, identification of repurposable drugs with minimized polypharmacological risks, and actionable insights into personalized dosing strategies. This work will directly inform preclinical drug development and clinical trial design, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches in therapeutic optimization. By prioritizing computational toxicology and pharmacodynamic profiling, the project aligns with the program’s focus on drug safety and mechanistic pharmacology while avoiding overlap with excluded biological subfields.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of drug interactions on biological systems and organisms and the sources, chemical properties, biological effects, and therapeutic uses of drugs. Includes instruction in pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, drug therapeutics, drug action, bodily responses to drug events, biochemical proliferation and differentiation, apoptosis, cell biology, medicinal chemistry, and studies of specific drugs and drug interactions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate community-level interventions addressing systemic inequities in access to social services, with a focus on housing instability and mental health disparities. Social work research faces unique challenges in evaluating multi-agency interventions due to the dynamic interactions between individuals, institutions, and policies. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture nonlinear feedback loops, resource allocation trade-offs, and emergent outcomes in complex social systems. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build large-scale simulations that integrate anonymized administrative data from public health departments, homeless shelters, and community mental health providers. The ABM will model decision-making processes of individuals navigating service systems alongside organizational behaviors under varying policy constraints. Computational demands arise from the need to simulate heterogeneous populations (N ≈ 100,000 agents) with detailed interaction rules, longitudinal time horizons (10+ simulated years), and sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations. The model will be implemented using Python-based Mesa frameworks optimized for parallel processing, with validation against longitudinal outcomes data from three urban counties. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for improving service coordination, quantifying threshold effects in resource allocation, and generating policy test scenarios for crisis response systems. This work directly supports evidence-based decision-making in public administration by creating a virtual laboratory to assess equity impacts of proposed interventions before implementation. The requested computing resources are essential given the memory-intensive nature of tracking multidimensional disadvantage indicators across large populations and the need for rapid iteration with community partners.
cip_definition: Any program providing instruction in social work and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in Korean dialectology and historical linguistics, with a focus on analyzing phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variations across regional and temporal Korean language datasets. The primary research problem lies in the computational limitations of processing large-scale, multi-modal corpora—including textual archives, spoken dialect recordings, and historical manuscripts—that are critical for tracing language evolution and mapping dialect boundaries. Current methods for analyzing these datasets are constrained by the volume of unstructured data, the complexity of training cross-dialectal models, and the need for real-time processing of acoustic features in speech corpora. To address this, the project will employ neural network architectures, including transformer-based models for text analysis and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for speech signal processing, optimized for parallel computation on HPC clusters. Key tasks include automated phonetic alignment of non-standard dialect recordings, diachronic semantic vector modeling to track lexical shifts in pre-modern texts, and geospatial clustering of syntactic features. The computational pipeline will integrate existing NLP tools adapted for Korean’s agglutinative morphology and honorific systems, while novel codebases will be developed to handle historical orthographies and low-resource dialect variants. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Korean dialect variation, open-access models for dialect classification, and datasets annotating syntactic changes from Middle Korean to modern forms. These resources will directly support pedagogical tools for heritage language preservation and inform policy on standardized language education in multilingual communities. The project’s scale—processing over 10 TB of text and audio data, with iterative model training requiring thousands of GPU hours—necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve feasible runtime and precision. By bridging computational linguistics with Korean philology, this work aims to set a methodological precedent for resource-intensive humanities research while addressing critical gaps in understanding Korea’s linguistic diversity.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Korean language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of robotic systems in industrial applications demands advanced computational tools to optimize design, control, and operational efficiency. Current robotics technologies face challenges in real-time adaptive decision-making, multi-sensor data fusion, and dynamic environment interaction, particularly in unstructured settings such as flexible manufacturing or logistics automation. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-fidelity simulation frameworks and machine learning models to enhance robotic autonomy and performance. The research will focus on creating scalable algorithms for robotic path planning, collision avoidance, and task optimization under variable constraints. A key computational challenge lies in managing the high-dimensional state spaces inherent to multi-joint robotic systems and stochastic environments, which require iterative simulations and large-scale parameter sweeps. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to accelerate the training of reinforcement learning agents, parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for system reliability analysis, and validate hybrid control strategies that integrate vision-based sensing with actuator dynamics. The proposed workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks for neural network training and distributed computing for real-time simulation of multi-robot coordination scenarios. Expected outcomes include optimized control algorithms for energy-efficient robotic operations, probabilistic models for failure prediction in complex tasks, and open-source simulation tools tailored for industrial robotics applications. These results will directly benefit collaborative robotics research and provide actionable insights for deploying adaptable robotic systems in small-to-medium enterprises. By utilizing HPC resources, this project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical control strategies and practical implementation, advancing the scalability of robotics solutions in non-standardized industrial environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using robots. Includes instruction in the principles of robotics, design and operational testing, system maintenance and repair procedures, robot computer systems and control language, specific system types and applications to specific industrial tasks, and report preparation.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of analyzing high-dimensional longitudinal data in clinical trials, where traditional statistical methods face computational limitations due to increasing data complexity and scale. Clinical trials increasingly incorporate frequent measurements of biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, and digital health metrics, generating datasets with high temporal resolution and numerous covariates. Existing software and algorithms struggle with the computational demands of fitting mixed-effects models or performing variable selection in such settings, leading to oversimplified analyses or impractical runtime. This project aims to develop a scalable, parallelized computational framework for Bayesian hierarchical models that efficiently handle high-dimensional longitudinal data. The approach will leverage Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling techniques, optimized for graphics processing unit (GPU) architectures, to accelerate posterior inference. Key innovations include adaptive preconditioning strategies for ill-conditioned covariance matrices and sparse matrix operations to reduce memory overhead. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to benchmark the method against existing approaches using simulated datasets with varying dimensionality (10³–10⁶ observations, 10²–10⁴ covariates) and to apply the framework to an ongoing Phase III trial evaluating a novel immunotherapy for autoimmune diseases. The trial’s data include weekly multi-omics measurements, electronic health record covariates, and irregularly sampled patient-generated health data. Successful implementation will provide the biostatistics community with open-source software optimized for distributed HPC environments, enabling rigorous analysis of complex trial data without resorting to dimensionality reduction. Anticipated outcomes include improved identification of treatment-effect heterogeneity, more accurate characterization of temporal biomarker trajectories, and actionable insights for adaptive trial designs. This work directly addresses NIH priorities for advancing computational infrastructure in clinical research and has broad applicability to precision medicine initiatives requiring real-time analysis of high-resolution biomedical data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of descriptive and inferential statistics to biomedical research and clinical, public health, and industrial issues related to human populations. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, modeling, clinical trials methodology, disease and survival analysis, longitudinal analysis, missing data analysis, spatial analysis, computer tomography, biostatistics consulting, and applications to such topics as genetics, oncology, pharmacokinetics, physiology, neurobiology, and biophysics.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to livestock health and food security. This project addresses the urgent need to model host-pathogen-antibiotic interactions in veterinary-relevant bacteria, including *Salmonella enterica* and *Escherichia coli*, to predict AMR evolution and optimize therapeutic strategies. Current limitations in experimental approaches hinder systematic analysis of microbial genomic plasticity, immune evasion mechanisms, and antibiotic pressure dynamics in complex biological systems. We propose an integrated computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to 1) analyze longitudinal metagenomic datasets from cattle infection trials, 2) simulate molecular interactions between bacterial surface antigens and host immune proteins, and 3) model population-level AMR selection pressures under varying treatment regimens. Machine learning pipelines will process multi-terabyte sequencing datasets to identify conserved resistance loci and antigenic variation patterns, while molecular dynamics simulations (GROMACS, AMBER) will characterize binding affinities between pathogen-associated molecular patterns and bovine Toll-like receptors. Agent-based models will simulate microbial community responses to different antibiotic dosing protocols. This resource request supports GPU-accelerated computations for large-scale molecular simulations and parallel processing of heterogeneous biological datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models of AMR emergence in veterinary pathogens, identification of conserved immunogenic targets for vaccine development, and data-driven treatment protocols to extend antimicrobial efficacy. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented resolution of host-microbe-drug interactions directly relevant to bovine respiratory disease complex and mastitis—two economically devastating conditions in global agriculture. By bridging microbial genomics, immunobiology, and computational modeling, this work aims to transform empirical approaches to veterinary infectious disease management while maintaining alignment with sustainable agricultural practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microbial causation and immunologic processes related to animal disease, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in bacteriology, mycology, virology, immune response mechanisms, humoral and cell function, cancer defenses, immune system dysfunction, immunologic diseases, parasitology, pathogenesis, and disease vectors.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel framework for adaptive human-computer symbiosis in microtask-driven data workflows, addressing inefficiencies in traditional data entry systems that rely on rigid, error-prone manual input. Current approaches in microcomputer applications often fail to dynamically integrate user behavior patterns, environmental context, or real-time quality metrics, leading to high cognitive load and error rates in specialized domains such as clinical data curation or multilingual archival digitization. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train ensemble models that combine eye-tracking analytics, keystroke dynamics, and contextual semantic validation. These models will power an adaptive interface capable of predicting user intent, pre-filling context-aware templates, and flagging inconsistencies during data entry sessions. Computational workflows will leverage distributed GPU-accelerated architectures to process multimodal interaction data at millisecond latency, while federated learning techniques will preserve privacy when aggregating patterns across institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in task completion time and a 60% decrease in post-processing correction needs across pilot deployments in healthcare transcription and cultural heritage digitization. The project will yield open-source libraries for real-time microtask optimization, advancing the understudied intersection of cognitive ergonomics and edge computing in microcomputer applications. By establishing scalable methods for human-in-the-loop adaptation, this work aims to redefine data entry systems as collaborative processes rather than static transactional interfaces, with implications for workforce training, accessibility design, and low-resource language preservation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in data entry/microcomputer applications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance equitable educational assessment practices by analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets to identify systemic biases in learning outcome evaluations. Traditional statistical methods struggle to model complex, nonlinear interactions in multimillion-row datasets spanning standardized test results, demographic surveys, and digital learning platform logs.
