We propose developing machine learning architectures to 1) detect latent bias patterns in assessment instruments across diverse student subgroups and 2) simulate how modified evaluation frameworks could reduce observed disparities. The computational workflow integrates natural language processing (NLP) to analyze open-response items, graph neural networks to map relationships between institutional policies and localized achievement gaps, and Bayesian hierarchical models to account for nested data structures (e.g., district-school-classroom hierarchies). High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on text responses from 12 million K-12 assessments, conducting Monte Carlo simulations of alternative grading rubrics, and running sensitivity analyses across 150+ demographic cross-sections. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source bias detection toolkit for assessment designers, 2) empirically validated thresholds for differential item functioning in AI-assisted grading systems, and 3) policy recommendations for weighting socioeconomic covariates in accountability frameworks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory parallelism, this work will overcome current limitations in handling sparse, high-dimensional education data while maintaining interpretability constraints required for ethical AI in assessment contexts. The results will directly inform state-level reforms in competency modeling and help institutions audit assessment equity under proposed Title IX regulatory changes.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_title: Educational Assessment, Evaluation, and Research, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in educational evaluation, research and statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of enzyme-responsive biomaterials for targeted drug delivery, addressing the challenge of achieving precise spatiotemporal control in therapeutic release. Current experimental approaches to engineer these systems are limited by the complexity of modeling enzyme-substrate interactions, molecular-level assembly dynamics, and degradation kinetics under physiological conditions. We propose to integrate atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with coarse-grained kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) methods to bridge time- and length-scale gaps inherent in traditional modeling approaches. The MD simulations will characterize interfacial binding energetics and conformational changes in protease-sensitive peptide linkers, while the kMC framework will predict bulk degradation behavior of polymeric nanoparticles as a function of linker chemistry and matrix topology. Machine learning models will be trained on simulation data to identify design rules linking molecular descriptors to release profiles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the >10^6-atom systems in explicit solvent, microsecond-scale MD trajectories, and parameterization of multi-fidelity models across 10^4+ combinatorial material variants. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for rational biomaterial design, reducing costly iterative experimentation in drug carrier development. The computational pipeline will be generalized to other enzyme-driven systems, advancing applications in personalized cancer therapeutics and programmable biomanufacturing. This work aligns with the molecular biotechnology focus of chemical engineering by connecting nanoscale phenomena to process-relevant performance metrics, with broader impacts on biopharmaceutical innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems at the interface of chemical engineering and biology, with an emphasis at the molecular level, such as biopharmaceutical processes, protein engineering, metabolic engineering, gene therapy, biomaterials, cell and tissue engineering, and drug delivery. Includes instruction in chemical engineering, thermodynamics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, momentum and heat transfer, cellular and molecular biotechnology, process design, and chemical reactor design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving role of digital communication in non-ordained Women’s Ministry programs, a specialized niche within Humanities that intersects gender studies, theology, and social dynamics. While Women’s Ministry programs prioritize spiritual and leadership development for women in faith-based communities, there is limited quantitative research on how digital platforms—such as virtual Bible studies, online counseling sessions, and social media outreach—shape theological discourse, community formation, and leadership efficacy. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in digital engagement that correlate with measurable outcomes in spiritual growth, leadership retention, and intergenerational mentorship, particularly in underrepresented cultural contexts. Using computational text analysis, network modeling, and machine learning, this study will process unstructured data from ministry forums, sermon transcripts, and anonymized counseling logs (spanning 15+ years and multiple denominations) to map theological themes, communication hierarchies, and sentiment trends. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models to classify nuanced theological arguments, simulating network resilience under varying leadership structures, and conducting large-scale sentiment analysis across multilingual datasets. Expected outcomes include a framework for optimizing digital ministry strategies, predictive tools for identifying at-risk participants, and open-access datasets illuminating the interplay between gender, technology, and spiritual practice. By integrating computational methods with qualitative insights, this project aims to advance evidence-based practices in Women’s Ministry while contributing to broader Humanities discourse on technology’s role in marginalized community-building.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained women to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to other women in local churches, parachurch organizations, and other settings. Includes instruction in foundations of women's ministry, women's ministry in the local church, spiritual formation, women's evangelism and discipleship, bible study and theology, homiletics, lay counseling, women's issues, and leadership training.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber-physical attacks targeting industrial control systems (ICS) necessitates novel methods to audit and fortify embedded device security without disrupting operational continuity. Traditional vulnerability assessments in ICS environments rely on static protocol analyses or passive network monitoring, which fail to capture dynamic adversarial interactions in hybrid digital-physical workflows. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, agent-based simulation framework to model attack-defense scenarios in ICS networks, explicitly integrating device firmware behavior, process-aware threat vectors, and real-time safety constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the framework will execute massively parallel simulations of compromised operational technology (OT) nodes under varying threat models, including stealthy code injection, sensor spoofing, and cascading process failures. Computational experiments will employ containerized device emulation, discrete-event process modeling, and evolutionary optimization algorithms to iteratively identify critical security gaps in simulated water treatment and energy distribution testbeds. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—requiring synchronized execution of thousands of virtualized Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), physics-based process models, and adaptive penetration testing agents—demands distributed memory architectures and GPU-accelerated compute nodes. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly available benchmark dataset of ICS attack trajectories, quantitative metrics for resilience auditing in safety-critical infrastructure, and prescriptive guidelines for deploying runtime attestation mechanisms in heterogeneous OT environments. By bridging cybersecurity auditing with industrial process modeling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive risk assessment in cyber-physical systems, directly supporting the development of next-generation industrial security standards.
cip_title: Computer and Information Systems Security/ Auditing/ Information Assurance
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assess the security needs of computer and network systems, recommend safeguard solutions, and manage the implementation, auditing, and maintenance of security devices, systems, and procedures. Includes instruction in computer architecture, programming, and systems analysis; networking; telecommunications; cryptography; security system auditing and design; applicable law and regulations; risk assessment and policy analysis; contingency planning; user access issues; investigation techniques; and troubleshooting.

abstract: The emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in veterinary pathogens presents a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current experimental approaches to characterize resistance mechanisms and develop targeted therapies are limited by the complexity of host-pathogen interactions and the vast genomic diversity of veterinary pathogens. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of AMR dynamics in bacterial pathogens affecting livestock, with a focus on multidrug-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* and *Escherichia coli* strains. We propose an integrative approach combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-enabled genomic analysis, and virtual drug screening to identify novel therapeutic targets and compounds. MD simulations will model conformational changes in key resistance-associated proteins (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps) under varying ligand-binding conditions, requiring millisecond-scale sampling enabled by GPU-accelerated nodes. Concurrently, ML algorithms will analyze multi-omic datasets (whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomics) from clinical veterinary isolates to predict resistance genotypes and epistatic interactions. A virtual compound library will be screened against prioritized targets using docking simulations and free-energy perturbation calculations. The scale of these analyses—involving >50,000 GPU core-hours and large-scale parallelization of genomic data processing—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic resolution maps of resistance protein dynamics, (2) predictive models linking genomic signatures to phenotypic resistance in veterinary isolates, and (3) a shortlist of lead compounds with validated binding affinities. This work will directly inform the development of narrow-spectrum antimicrobials tailored to veterinary pathogens, reducing reliance on broad-spectrum antibiotics in agriculture. By bridging computational biology and veterinary clinical science, the project aims to establish a framework for rapid, cost-effective AMR mitigation strategies while advancing computational methodologies for veterinary biomedical research.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Biomedical and Clinical Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in veterinary biomedical and clinical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the integrative physiological mechanisms underlying extreme thermoregulatory adaptations in heterothermic mammals, with a focus on hibernating species and their capacity to survive prolonged hypometabolic states. While mammalian thermoregulation is well-studied under normative conditions, the dynamic interplay between neural regulation, metabolic scaling, and organ-specific thermal responses during torpor-arousal cycles remains poorly resolved. This gap limits translational applications for improving organ preservation in transplant medicine or mitigating hypothermic injuries in humans. To address this, we propose a computational physiology framework combining species-specific biophysical models with whole-organism metabolic network analyses. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the integration of multiscale datasets, including infrared thermographic maps of heat distribution, in vivo electrophysiological recordings of hypothalamic regulation, and mitochondrial efficiency metrics across tissues. Machine learning algorithms will parameterize a novel reaction-diffusion model capturing spatiotemporal thermal gradients in vital organs during rapid rewarming phases. Comparative analyses will contrast obligate hibernators (e.g., ground squirrels) with facultative species (e.g., bears) to identify conserved versus specialized adaptations. The computational pipeline will iteratively refine models using empirical data from collaborator labs, incorporating phylogenetic constraints and allometric relationships. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform for simulating interspecific resilience to metabolic instability, identification of critical thresholds for organ viability during hypothermia, and biomarkers of thermoregulatory plasticity. This work bridges comparative animal physiology with computational thermodynamics—an underexplored niche—to advance both fundamental understanding of heterothermy evolution and biomedical strategies for targeted temperature management in critical care. The requested HPC allocation will directly support the complex numerical simulations and high-dimensional data integration required to resolve these nonlinear physiological dynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of function, morphology, regulation, and intercellular communications and dynamics within vertebrate and invertebrate in animal species, with comparative applications to homo sapiens and its relatives and antecedents. Includes instruction in reproduction, growth, lactation, digestion, performance, behavioral adaptation, sensory perception, motor action, phylogenetics, biotic and abiotic function, membrane biology, and related aspects of biochemistry and biophysics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of interactive narrative systems in modern video games demands computational approaches capable of dynamically adapting storylines while maintaining coherence, emotional resonance, and player agency. Traditional procedural content generation methods often prioritize efficiency over narrative depth, resulting in formulaic or disjointed storytelling experiences. This project proposes the development of a hybrid AI-driven narrative framework that integrates large language models (LLMs), affective computing, and real-time player behavior analysis to generate contextually rich, emotionally adaptive story arcs. The research addresses the computational challenge of balancing low-latency narrative adjustments during gameplay with the high-dimensional optimization required for multi-character plot consistency across extended play sessions. A multi-stage architecture will be implemented, combining transformer-based dialogue systems, graph neural networks for plot state tracking, and reinforcement learning agents trained to maximize narrative novelty while preserving causal logic. High-performance computing resources are essential for training ensemble models on heterogeneous datasets encompassing literary structures, player interaction logs, and psycholinguistic annotations. GPU-accelerated simulations will test dynamic narrative branching under variable player decision densities, while distributed computing will enable large-scale A/B testing of emotional valence predictions across diverse demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for emotion-aware narrative generation, quantitative metrics for evaluating interactive story coherence, and novel techniques for real-time constraint satisfaction in branching narrative systems. This work bridges gaps between computational creativity, affective human-computer interaction, and game design, offering foundational methods for next-generation storytelling in games and immersive media.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: Clinical cytogenetics faces growing challenges in analyzing complex genomic and cytogenetic data to diagnose genetic disorders, guide organ transplant compatibility, and optimize cancer treatment strategies. Current methodologies, including karyotyping, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), and molecular genetic profiling, generate vast multi-modal datasets—such as high-resolution chromosomal images, spatial gene expression maps, and sequencing outputs—that demand advanced computational resources for integration and interpretation. Traditional analysis pipelines lack the scalability to process these data efficiently, limiting the resolution of structural variants, mosaic anomalies, and epigenetic interactions critical for clinical decision-making. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a unified computational framework for large-scale cytogenetic data analysis. The proposed workflow will deploy machine learning models to automate the detection of chromosomal aberrations in karyotype and FISH images, integrate these findings with whole-genome sequencing and transcriptomic data via graph-based algorithms, and simulate spatial chromatin dynamics in cancer cells to predict clonal evolution. HPC capabilities are essential for training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale imaging repositories, performing parallelized genomic variant calling across thousands of samples, and running molecular dynamics simulations of chromosomal rearrangements. Expected outcomes include a scalable pipeline for identifying diagnostic biomarkers of transplant rejection risk, subclonal cancer populations, and rare constitutional abnormalities with higher sensitivity than current clinical standards. The resource will also enable real-time photomicrography analysis during time-sensitive procedures like hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. By bridging computational bottlenecks in multi-omics data synthesis, this project aims to establish new standards for precision in genetic disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and transplant compatibility assessment, directly impacting patient outcomes in leukemia, solid tumors, and congenital disorders. All tools will be containerized for clinical deployment, ensuring translation of HPC-driven insights into routine diagnostic workflows.
cip_definition: The clinical research and diagnosis of genetic diseases and defects, in preparation for organ transplants, and in support of treatments for cancers and leukemias. Includes chromosome analysis, fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), molecular genetic techniques, cytotechnology, and photomicrography.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in business and economic journalism by addressing the challenges of analyzing large-scale, dynamic datasets in real time. Business journalists increasingly confront complex financial markets, global supply chain disruptions, and rapidly evolving economic indicators, yet traditional analytical tools often lack the capacity to process heterogeneous data streams—including structured financial records, unstructured corporate disclosures, and social media sentiment—at the speed and scale required for timely reporting. The research problem centers on developing computational workflows that integrate machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis to identify trends, anomalies, and narratives within these datasets. Proposed methods include training transformer-based models to extract semantic patterns from earnings calls and regulatory filings, applying graph algorithms to map interdependencies in global trade networks, and deploying ensemble forecasting techniques to predict market reactions to geopolitical events. These workflows will be optimized for parallel processing and GPU acceleration to handle terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for journalistic investigations, enabling faster identification of underreported economic stories (e.g., supply chain vulnerabilities, regulatory arbitrage) and democratizing access to advanced analytics for newsrooms with limited technical infrastructure. The project also aims to produce methodological frameworks for ethically integrating automated insights into reporting processes, addressing concerns around algorithmic bias and transparency. By enhancing the computational rigor of business journalism, this work will strengthen public understanding of economic systems while maintaining the discipline’s emphasis on accuracy, context, and accountability. Resource requests include GPU nodes for model training, high-memory nodes for large-scale NLP tasks, and scalable storage for curating annotated datasets spanning financial, corporate, and media sources.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a large-scale computational framework to analyze stylistic evolution in English literary texts across distinct historical periods, with a focus on identifying patterns of linguistic innovation and intertextual influence. While traditional literary scholarship has relied on manual close reading, the sheer volume of extant texts—from Early Modern pamphlets to 20th-century novels—necessitates scalable computational methods to detect subtle, systemic shifts in language use and narrative structure. The research will employ natural language processing techniques, including transformer-based language models fine-tuned on period-specific corpora, to quantify syntactic complexity, semantic field distributions, and metaphor density across a curated dataset of 30,000 primary texts. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: parallel processing of heterogeneous archival formats (TEI XML, OCR-scanned texts), training domain-specific word embeddings using dynamic temporal contexts, and implementing graph neural networks to map citation networks and thematic diffusion. By correlating linguistic features with sociocultural metadata, the analysis will test hypotheses about how major events like the Industrial Revolution or suffrage movements influenced literary expression. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital repository of annotated texts, visualization tools for diachronic stylistic trends, and statistical models quantifying the relationship between lexical innovation and canon formation. This work will advance methodological debates in digital humanities by demonstrating how computational approaches can complement qualitative interpretation, while providing new empirical evidence for longstanding theoretical claims about literary periodization. The resource demands—particularly GPU-intensive model training and large-scale graph traversal—require dedicated HPC allocation to ensure feasible processing times for terabyte-scale textual data.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the English language, including its history, structure and related communications skills; and the literature and culture of English-speaking peoples.

abstract: Environmental health research faces significant challenges in understanding the complex interactions between multiple environmental stressors and their cumulative impacts on human populations. Current risk assessment frameworks often rely on simplified models that analyze single pollutants or pathways, limiting their ability to predict real-world outcomes where exposures to air pollutants, heavy metals, organic contaminants, and climate-related factors co-occur. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model multi-stressor exposure dynamics, dose-response relationships, and population-level health outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate spatially resolved environmental monitoring data, toxicokinetic/toxicodynamic (TK/TD) models, and machine learning algorithms to simulate exposure scenarios across diverse urban and rural landscapes. The computational workflow will couple Bayesian inference methods with mechanistic models to quantify uncertainty in exposure sources, bioavailability, and biomarker trajectories while accounting for demographic variability. Key objectives include (1) simulating synergistic effects of particulate matter (PM2.5) and heavy metal exposures on cardiovascular outcomes using multi-scale atmospheric transport models, (2) predicting groundwater contamination risks from emerging contaminants under climate-driven hydrological changes, and (3) optimizing intervention strategies through probabilistic cost-benefit analysis. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale geospatial datasets, running parallelized toxicity simulations, and training neural networks on cohort health records. Expected outcomes include novel risk prediction tools capable of informing adaptive public health policies, prioritized remediation targets for environmental regulators, and open-source computational models for assessing environmental justice disparities. By advancing methodologies for complex mixture analysis, this research will directly support evidence-based decision-making in environmental health practice while providing a scalable framework for future studies on emerging contaminants and climate-health interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of environmental sciences, public health, the biomedical sciences, and environmental toxicology to the study of environmental factors affecting human health, safety, and related ecological issues, and prepares individuals to function as professional environmental health specialists. Includes instruction in epidemiology, biostatistics, toxicology, public policy analysis, public management, risk assessment, communications, environmental law, occupational health and safety emergency response, and applications such as air quality, food protection, radiation protection, solid and hazardous waste management, water quality, soil quality, noise abatement, housing quality, and environmental control of recreational areas.

abstract: Agroecological systems require the integration of complex biological, environmental, and socioeconomic factors to optimize sustainability and productivity. However, current modeling frameworks often lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between crop genotypes, soil microbiomes, and management practices at scale, limiting their utility for predicting system outcomes under climate variability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model to simulate agroecosystem dynamics, with a focus on crop-soil-microbe interactions and their response to diverse agricultural management strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate process-based crop models, microbial community metagenomic data, and spatially explicit soil health metrics to predict nutrient cycling efficiency, pest resilience, and yield stability across heterogeneous landscapes. Machine learning methods will be applied to parameterize models using multi-year field datasets from experimental agroecological plots, including crop rotations, cover cropping, and reduced tillage systems. The computational workflow will employ parallelized simulations to evaluate thousands of management scenarios under projected climate conditions, quantifying trade-offs between productivity, soil carbon sequestration, and input use efficiency. By coupling genomic, edaphic, and agronomic data at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales, this work will advance understanding of resilience mechanisms in diversified farming systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable modeling toolkit for optimizing management decisions, identification of genotype-by-management combinations that enhance sustainability, and open-access datasets to support broader agroecological research. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the high dimensionality of ecological datasets, running iterative simulations, and enabling real-time analytics for stakeholder-driven scenario testing. This project directly aligns with the program’s mission to develop computationally informed, ecologically sound solutions for agricultural challenges while prioritizing economic viability and resource efficiency.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of hybrid edge-cloud infrastructures demands adaptive resource management strategies that transcend traditional static allocation models. This project addresses the challenge of optimizing computational and network resource distribution in dynamic, heterogeneous environments where IoT devices, edge nodes, and cloud systems operate under fluctuating workloads and strict latency constraints. Current approaches in network and system administration often rely on reactive scaling or oversimplified predictive models, leading to suboptimal utilization rates and service degradation during demand spikes. We propose developing an autonomous resource orchestration framework that integrates graph-based network topology analysis with real-time telemetry from distributed systems. The computational methodology combines temporal graph neural networks to model evolving device dependencies with multi-agent reinforcement learning for decentralized decision-making. This approach requires high-performance computing resources to simulate large-scale network environments (10,000+ nodes) while training machine learning models on parallelized workflows. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for neural network training and distributed memory systems for network emulation at operational scales. Expected outcomes include a novel resource allocation algorithm capable of maintaining sub-100ms decision latency in simulated smart city deployments, dynamic storage tiering strategies that reduce redundant data transfers by 30-40%, and failure prediction models that improve fault tolerance through proactive resource reservation. Success metrics will be validated against industrial IoT and emergency response communication scenarios, providing system administrators with concrete benchmarks for next-generation infrastructure management. The developed tools will be released as open-source modules for integration with existing network monitoring platforms, advancing capabilities in adaptive system administration while establishing performance baselines for AI-driven resource management in critical infrastructure applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the computer operations and control the system configurations emanating from a specific site or network hub. Includes instruction in computer hardware and software and applications; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) networking; principles of information systems security; disk space and traffic load monitoring; data backup; resource allocation; and setup and takedown procedures.

abstract: The discovery and optimization of natural product-derived therapeutics are hindered by the structural complexity of bioactive compounds and the computational demands of analyzing their interactions with biological targets. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the identification and mechanistic characterization of natural products with pharmacological potential. A key challenge lies in efficiently modeling the dynamic behavior of structurally diverse compounds—such as alkaloids, terpenoids, and polyketides—within complex biosynthetic pathways and protein-binding environments. We propose an integrated computational workflow combining molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and machine learning (ML)-guided virtual screening to predict bioactivity, metabolic stability, and target engagement. MD simulations will map conformational landscapes of lead compounds interacting with therapeutic targets (e.g., kinase enzymes, GPCRs), while DFT will optimize reaction coordinates for enzymatic modifications of natural product scaffolds. Concurrently, a neural network trained on ethnobotanical databases and biophysical assay data will prioritize compounds for experimental validation. The scale of these analyses—requiring millions of CPU-core hours for ensemble simulations and quantum mechanical computations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of three candidate compounds with enhanced binding affinity to inflammation and oncology-related targets, (2) predictive models linking structural motifs to pharmacokinetic properties, and (3) a publicly accessible database of annotated natural product conformers. This work bridges traditional pharmacognosy with computational innovation, accelerating the translation of bioactive natural products into preclinical candidates while reducing reliance on resource-intensive screening. By elucidating structure-activity relationships at unprecedented resolution, the project will advance methodological frameworks for natural product drug discovery within pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of biologically active compounds found in naturally occurring sources such as plants, animals, and microbes and their use and/or modification as medicinal substances. Includes instruction in medicinal chemistry, organic medicinals, pharmacological therapeutics, pharmacokinetics, molecular biology, structural chemistry, enzymes, nucleic acids, economic botany, ethnobotany, bioprospecting, bioassay, compound identification and isolation, mass spectrometry, and analytical instrumentation and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Bengali linguistics and literary analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to enable large-scale text processing, dialect classification, and syntactic pattern recognition. Despite Bengali’s status as the seventh most spoken language globally, computational tools for its analysis remain underdeveloped compared to Indo-European languages with more extensive digital infrastructure. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, annotated corpora and models capable of capturing regional dialect variations, historical linguistic shifts, and stylistic features in Bengali literature. To address this, we propose building a multi-dialectal corpus of Bengali texts spanning pre-modern to contemporary eras, integrating philological annotations, and training machine learning models to analyze linguistic evolution and literary trends. Computational methods will include neural network-based dialect classifiers, transformer models for syntactic parsing, and geospatial mapping of phonetic variations using distributed computing frameworks. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of textual data, optimize parallelized training of language models, and run iterative simulations for dialect boundary identification. Expected outcomes include (1) the first open-access, computationally annotated corpus of Bengali texts with metadata on regional and historical context, (2) quantitative frameworks for tracking syntactic simplification in modern literary Bengali, and (3) dialect classification models with applications in education, speech technology, and cultural preservation. By bridging computational linguistics with Bengali philology, this work will empower interdisciplinary scholarship while developing replicable methods for under-resourced languages. The requested resources will directly support data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and large-scale text rendering for visual analytics, enabling breakthroughs in both theoretical linguistics and applied language technologies for Bengali.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the optimization of casino table game dealing techniques through computational modeling of real-time decision-making and biomechanical efficiency. The research problem centers on the lack of empirical frameworks for training dealers in high-pressure, dynamic gaming environments, where split-second accuracy, ergonomic precision, and adaptive crowd management directly influence operational outcomes. Current pedagogical approaches rely on experiential repetition without robust quantitative analysis of performance variables. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based models simulating multi-player table interactions across Blackjack, Craps, and Roulette, incorporating stochastic event chains (e.g., irregular bet placements, rule disputes, and dealer error recovery). High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of 10,000+ gameplay scenarios, capturing probabilistic distributions of dealer response latencies, motion trajectories, and cognitive load under varying casino floor conditions. Custom physics engines will model biomechanical efficiency in chip handling, card distribution, and wheel operation, integrating motion capture data from professional dealers. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework identifying critical thresholds for dealer error rates relative to game complexity and player density, (2) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive training modules targeting situational stress resilience, and (3) generative algorithms proposing optimized table layouts to minimize repetitive motion injuries. By bridging computational ergonomics, behavioral modeling, and gaming operations, this work aims to establish a novel research niche at the intersection of hospitality technology and human performance analytics, offering translational benefits for both vocational education standards and casino operational integrity protocols.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to apply technical skills and knowledge to become table games dealers in casinos or other recreational settings. Includes instruction in dealing techniques for Baccarat, Blackjack, Carnival Games, Craps, Poker, and Roulette.

abstract: Palliative care nursing requires integrating complex clinical, psychosocial, and patient-reported data to optimize care for individuals with life-threatening illnesses. However, current approaches to symptom management and care planning often rely on generalized protocols or small-scale studies, limiting personalization and timeliness. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets from palliative care populations, including electronic health records, longitudinal symptom assessments, and qualitative patient/family narratives. The research problem centers on identifying dynamic patterns in symptom trajectories, treatment responses, and psychosocial outcomes to inform real-time clinical decision-making. Computational methods will include machine learning models to predict individualized pain and symptom escalation risks, natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract themes from unstructured narrative data, and agent-based simulations to model care delivery workflows under varying resource constraints. These analyses require HPC capabilities due to the volume of longitudinal patient data (>50,000 anonymized records), the need for parallel processing to train predictive models across diverse demographic subgroups, and the computational intensity of simulating multi-agent care scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to prioritize high-risk patients for early intervention, (2) a framework for quantifying the impact of palliative nursing interventions on caregiver burden and patient quality of life, and (3) open-source tools to visualize symptom trajectories for clinical use. By elucidating the interplay between biological, psychological, and social factors in end-of-life care, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in palliative nursing while establishing scalable computational methodologies for future research in supportive care domains. The requested resources will directly enable the processing and integration of heterogeneous datasets that are currently underutilized due to technical limitations in existing clinical analytics infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide a combination of active and compassionate therapies intended to comfort and support patients and their families who are living with life-threatening illness. Includes instruction in pathophysiology, palliative care processes, pain management, pharmacology, loss, grief, death, and bereavement.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Thai linguistics and literature, addressing critical gaps in scalable analysis of the Thai language’s structural and historical complexity. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of processing Thai’s unique orthographic system, dialectal diversity, and understudied literary corpora. Traditional methods struggle to efficiently analyze large-scale textual data, particularly when modeling phonetic shifts across regional dialects, parsing archaic scripts in historical manuscripts, or identifying stylistic patterns in classical literature. This project proposes a multi-phase computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and corpus linguistics. First, HPC resources will enable the training of transformer-based models on digitized Thai texts—including Sukhothai-era inscriptions, Rattanakosin literary works, and contemporary social media data—to automate script normalization and dialect classification. Second, parallelized algorithms will map phonetic and semantic evolution across Thai dialects using phylogenetic models, requiring iterative simulations of language change. Third, graph-based network analysis will trace intertextual influences in classical poetry and prose, correlating stylistic features with historical context. These methods demand significant memory and processing capacity due to the non-Latin script’s tokenization complexity, the need for fine-grained acoustic modeling in dialect studies, and the high dimensionality of literary metadata. Expected outcomes include the first open-access computational toolkit for Thai dialectometry, a diachronic corpus annotated for linguistic and literary features, and publicly deployable models for automated Thai script analysis. The project will directly support Thailand’s efforts to preserve endangered regional dialects, enhance digital humanities pedagogy, and improve NLP tools for low-resource languages. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to establish a methodological framework for future interdisciplinary studies in Southeast Asian languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Thai languages. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize supply chain resilience and inventory management strategies for agricultural retailers and wholesalers, with a focus on mitigating disruptions caused by climate variability and fluctuating input costs. Agricultural supply chains face increasing pressure from unpredictable weather patterns, shifting pest and disease pressures, and volatile global markets for fertilizers, seeds, and equipment. Existing inventory models often fail to account for the complex interdependencies between agronomic variables, seasonal demand cycles, and multi-tier supplier networks. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and stochastic programming to analyze dynamic decision-making across agricultural supply networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to model region-specific climate scenarios (e.g., drought probabilities, extreme weather events) alongside economic variables such as commodity price fluctuations and transportation costs. The computational workflow will leverage historical sales data, climate projection datasets, and supplier lead time records to train predictive models for input demand forecasting. Parallelized optimization routines will identify robust inventory policies that balance service-level targets with risk mitigation across decentralized distribution networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit for agricultural suppliers, validated through case studies with farm cooperatives in drought-prone regions. This work will advance computational methodologies for agricultural supply chain management while directly addressing operational challenges faced by retailers and wholesalers in maintaining affordable, timely access to critical farm inputs. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive simulations of multi-echelon distribution networks and computationally demanding scenario analyses at spatial resolutions relevant to regional agricultural economies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of multi-scale neural network models that bridge cellular-level dynamics with systems-level cognitive functions. A critical challenge in computational neuroscience is simulating large-scale, biologically realistic neural circuits while capturing the nonlinear interactions between synaptic plasticity, neuromodulation, and emergent network behavior. Current models either oversimplify biophysical detail or lack the scalability to investigate brain-wide phenomena, limiting their utility for probing mechanisms underlying disorders such as Parkinson’s disease or epilepsy. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating spiking neural networks (SNNs) with mean-field approximations, optimized for parallelized GPU-accelerated architectures. The SNN component will model microcircuits with Hodgkin-Huxley dynamics and calcium-mediated plasticity, while mean-field reductions will enable efficient simulation of macro-scale network interactions. This approach requires iterative parameter sweeps across millions of neurons and trillions of synapses, necessitating HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and parameter optimization via evolutionary algorithms. Validation will utilize electrophysiological datasets from collaborating labs, including in vivo recordings during decision-making tasks. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) mechanistic insights into how dopaminergic modulation stabilizes or destabilizes cortical-basal ganglia circuits, (2) open-source tools for scalable multi-scale modeling, and (3) predictive biomarkers for deep brain stimulation protocols. The computational demands—terabyte-scale data generation per simulation, real-time spike sorting across distributed nodes, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses—exceed the capabilities of local cluster infrastructure. Allocated resources will directly support parameter space exploration, enable validation against experimental benchmarks, and accelerate the translation of theoretical models to clinical applications in neurotechnology. This work aligns with national priorities in understanding neural computation and advancing brain-inspired artificial intelligence.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply advanced computational methods and analysis to the nervous system and neuroscience-related technologies. Includes instruction in neural network modeling, neural dynamics, sensory, motor, and cognitive modeling, statistical modeling, sensory prosthesis, brain-machine interfaces, neuroinformatics, neuromorphic engineering, and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model the biomechanical and acoustic interactions inherent in advanced instrumental performance practices. While traditional music performance research has relied on qualitative or small-scale empirical studies, the complexity of real-time gesture-sound relationships in solo and ensemble contexts demands computational approaches capable of processing high-dimensional data. The core research problem centers on quantifying how subtle variations in performer biomechanics—such as embouchure adjustments in wind players, bowing techniques in string instruments, or percussive strike kinematics—affect acoustic output and perceived expressivity. To address this, motion-capture data, audio recordings, and physiological sensor inputs from professional musicians will be integrated into machine learning models trained to identify patterns across temporal, spectral, and spatial domains. HPC resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-modal datasets at scale, including real-time simulations of acoustic environments for ensemble balance analysis and GPU-accelerated neural networks for gesture classification. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking technical execution to acoustic consequences, which will be disseminated as open-source tools for performance analysis. These resources will provide empirical frameworks for pedagogues to diagnose technical challenges, inform injury-prevention strategies through movement efficiency analysis, and expand understanding of how virtuosic techniques emerge from coordinated physiological systems. By bridging computational methodologies with performance praxis, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven music research while preserving the artistic integrity of instrumental traditions.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to master musical instruments and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers. Includes instruction on one or more specific instruments from various instrumental groupings.

abstract: The increasing complexity of healthcare workflows and communication demands in inpatient units has highlighted critical inefficiencies in traditional Health Unit Coordinator (HUC) practices, particularly in managing real-time data streams, prioritizing interdisciplinary communications, and mitigating errors during high-stress periods. This project proposes a computational approach to model, analyze, and optimize HUC workflows by integrating electronic health record (EHR) metadata, interdepartmental communication logs, and sensor-derived patient flow data. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop agent-based simulations to map decision-making patterns under varying clinical loads and apply natural language processing (NLP) to classify communication urgency in transcribed orders and messages. A machine learning pipeline will identify predictors of workflow bottlenecks and latent risks in task sequencing, using federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across participating hospital systems. The computational framework will be validated against observational datasets from six acute care units, encompassing over 200,000 discrete HUC interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for dynamic task prioritization, a risk-aware alert system for order transcription errors, and generative AI tools to simulate training scenarios for emergent care contexts. By quantifying the relationship between administrative efficiency and patient throughput, this research aims to establish evidence-based standards for HUC training programs while providing scalable computational tools to reduce cognitive load and improve care coordination. The project bridges healthcare operations research, human factors engineering, and clinical informatics, offering a novel pathway to enhance the resilience of frontline administrative roles in modern healthcare systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nurses or ward supervisors, to perform routine administrative and reception duties in a patient care unit within a hospital or other health care facility. Includes instruction in receiving and directing visitors, transcribing medical and nursing orders, preparing requisition forms, scheduling patient appointments and procedures, monitoring patients and personnel, and interpersonal skills.

abstract: Pediatric clinical research faces critical challenges in understanding complex, multifactorial diseases due to the dynamic interplay of developmental biology, environmental factors, and heterogeneous patient responses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches for pediatric sepsis, a leading cause of mortality in critically ill children. Current risk stratification and treatment protocols lack personalization, contributing to variable outcomes. We propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic), electronic health records, and longitudinal immune profiling from a multicenter cohort of 2,500 pediatric sepsis patients. Machine learning models, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression, organ dysfunction, and therapeutic response. Bayesian hierarchical modeling will account for developmental age-specific variations in immune and metabolic pathways, while mechanistic simulations of host-pathogen interactions will explore causal drivers of clinical heterogeneity. The scale of data (≈150 TB) and complexity of models necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized data processing, distributed hyperparameter optimization, and large-memory nodes for genome-wide association studies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated risk stratification tool for early identification of high-risk patients, (2) computational biomarkers to guide immunomodulatory therapy selection, and (3) open-source pipelines for pediatric multi-omics integration. By enabling rapid analysis of developmental trajectories and rare patient subgroups, this HPC-driven approach will address fundamental gaps in understanding sepsis pathophysiology across maturing biological systems. Results will be disseminated through clinician-facing decision support tools and a public cloud repository for pediatric sepsis datasets, fostering translational applications in critical care.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for early detection and personalized treatment of complex ophthalmic diseases, including diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, and glaucoma. Current diagnostic methods often rely on static clinical imaging and manual feature extraction, which lack the capacity to integrate dynamic, multimodal data or model disease progression at scale. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining deep learning with large-scale biomechanical simulations to analyze longitudinal optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus imaging, and patient-specific genetic datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution 3D retinal scans (>10,000 images) and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify novel biomarkers. Finite element modeling of intraocular pressure dynamics and retinal tissue stress will be optimized using GPU-accelerated solvers to simulate disease pathways under varying physiological conditions. Recurrent neural networks will then integrate these multimodal outputs to predict individual patient trajectories and optimize intervention strategies. The computational workload demands significant memory allocation (~1 TB RAM) and multi-node GPU clusters due to the scale of image processing and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for early risk stratification, a generative model of disease progression for surgical planning, and open-source tools for automated analysis of ophthalmic imaging data. This work will directly enhance clinical decision-making in ocular pathology management and provide a template for computationally driven precision medicine in ophthalmology. By allocating these resources, the project aims to reduce diagnostic delays for sight-threatening conditions and improve the cost-effectiveness of vision-preserving therapies.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, prevention treatment of ophthalmic diseases and disorders, and ocular pathology procedures. May included related research in eye surgery.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between transnational educational policy diffusion and student outcome disparities across diverse socioeconomic contexts using large-scale, multi-country datasets. A critical challenge in comparative education research lies in analyzing complex, heterogeneous data—such as national assessment results, policy documents, and student mobility records—while accounting for cultural, linguistic, and institutional variability. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), multilevel statistical modeling, and geospatial network analysis. The research will process multilingual policy texts (e.g., UNESCO reports, national education strategies) using transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for cross-cultural semantic alignment. Longitudinal student performance data from international assessments (PISA, TIMSS) will be analyzed through Bayesian hierarchical models to identify policy-associated outcome patterns. Migration and exchange program data will be modeled as dynamic networks to quantify educational mobility trends. The computational intensity of simultaneously training multiple deep learning architectures on terabyte-scale datasets, coupled with the need for real-time sensitivity analyses across 50+ national contexts, necessitates high-performance computing resources. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel open-access repository of computationally harmonized education policy indicators, 2) evidence-based insights into how policy adaptation processes correlate with equity gaps in different regions, and 3) predictive models of student migration flows under varying global education scenarios. This work will advance methodological paradigms in comparative education by enabling systematic integration of unstructured policy data with quantitative outcome metrics while addressing scale limitations inherent in traditional case-study approaches. The requested resources will directly support 12 months of computational experiments, with results informing ongoing collaborations with UNESCO’s Global Education Monitoring Report team and the OECD’s Education Policy Committee.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the educational phenomena, practices, and institutions within different societies and states in a comparative perspective, and the study of international educational issues. Includes instruction in comparative research methods, country- or area-specific studies, cross-national studies of learning and teaching styles, international educational policy and development, and analyses of educational migration patterns and experiences.

abstract: Intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) is critical for preventing neurological injury during surgeries, yet existing systems face challenges in real-time processing of complex neurophysiological data and predictive modeling of adverse events. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced computational tools to enhance the speed, accuracy, and interpretability of IONM systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to analyze multimodal data streams—including high-density EEG, EMG, and somatosensory evoked potentials—to detect subtle neural changes indicative of surgical risk. The computational approach integrates parallelized signal processing algorithms for noise reduction and feature extraction, coupled with machine learning models trained on retrospective surgical datasets to predict intraoperative neurological compromise. A key innovation involves simulating real-world surgical scenarios using finite element modeling to map how mechanical or ischemic perturbations propagate through neural networks, enabling the creation of patient-specific risk profiles. The HPC environment is essential for managing the scale of data (terabytes per case), optimizing deep learning architectures via distributed training, and reducing latency in real-time analytics to sub-second thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive IONM signal interpretation, validated against clinical outcomes from 500+ historical cases, and a predictive dashboard to guide surgical decision-making. This work will establish computational benchmarks for neuromonitoring accuracy, directly addressing gaps in current clinical practice where delayed or ambiguous interpretations contribute to preventable complications. By enabling rapid, data-driven insights, the project aims to improve surgical safety standards and provide a scalable platform for training future neuromonitoring professionals in computational methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to become neuromonitoring technicians who analyze, monitor, and record nervous system function to promote the effective treatment of pathological conditions. Includes instruction in EEG technology, EMG technology, anatomy, and neuroanatomy.

abstract: Radiation therapy efficacy is critically dependent on the precise delivery of tumoricidal doses while sparing adjacent healthy tissues, a challenge exacerbated by dynamic anatomical changes (e.g., organ motion, tumor shrinkage) during treatment. Current adaptive radiotherapy workflows, which adjust plans using periodic imaging, are limited by computational bottlenecks in processing high-resolution, real-time imaging data and rapidly recalculating optimized dose distributions. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for real-time adaptive radiation therapy (RT-ART) in Medical Radiologic Technology. The research problem centers on integrating continuous MRI-guided imaging with instantaneous dose recalculation, enabling submillimeter accuracy in targeting moving tumors. The computational approach combines GPU-accelerated deformable image registration algorithms, Monte Carlo dose simulation, and machine learning models trained to predict short-term anatomical shifts from time-resolved 4D-MRI data. These models will be iteratively refined using retrospective clinical datasets from thoracic and abdominal radiotherapy patients, with HPC resources enabling parallel processing of multi-terabyte imaging repositories. Key technical challenges include reducing latency in dose optimization loops to under 10 seconds and validating computational predictions against physical phantom measurements. Expected outcomes include a scalable RT-ART pipeline capable of dynamically adjusting beam parameters during treatment delivery, potentially reducing planning target volume margins by 30–50% and lowering radiation-induced toxicity risks. The project’s significance lies in bridging a critical gap between emerging imaging technologies and their clinical translation, offering a foundation for personalized, motion-robust radiotherapy. Successful implementation will require access to HPC clusters with high-memory nodes, multi-GPU configurations, and fast interconnects to handle concurrent image analysis, dose computation, and uncertainty modeling tasks.
cip_title: Medical Radiologic Technology/ Science - Radiation Therapist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to administer prescribed courses of radiation treatment, manage patients undergoing radiation therapy, and maintain pertinent records. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, oncologic pathology, radiation biology, radiation oncology procedures and techniques, radiation dosimetry, tumor localization, treatment planning, patient communication and management, data collection, record-keeping, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for optimizing large-scale, stochastic industrial systems, with applications to supply chain resilience and production scheduling under uncertainty. Industrial systems increasingly face disruptions from geopolitical, environmental, and market volatility, necessitating real-time adaptive decision-making. However, existing optimization frameworks struggle with combinatorial complexity when modeling multi-echelon networks or high-dimensional uncertainty spaces, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture integrating distributed stochastic optimization, parallelized Monte Carlo simulation, and graph-based machine learning. The methodology leverages high-performance computing (HPC) resources to decompose problems across temporal and spatial dimensions while maintaining coordination through asynchronous consensus algorithms. Key innovations include GPU-accelerated scenario generation for non-stationary disruption risks and memory-efficient graph neural networks to predict cascading failures in interconnected production networks. Computational experiments will evaluate system performance under synthetic and real-world datasets spanning semiconductor manufacturing logistics and hospital resource allocation networks. The project requires HPC resources to manage terabyte-scale optimization models, parallelize millions of scenario evaluations, and train deep reinforcement learning agents on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source algorithmic frameworks for stochastic industrial system optimization, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational scalability against commercial solvers, and (3) case studies demonstrating 15-30% improvements in recovery time and resource utilization under disruption scenarios. By enabling rapid analysis of complex trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and risk, this work will provide foundational tools for next-generation resilient systems engineering. Results will be disseminated through the INFORMS Journal on Computing and collaborations with industry partners in advanced manufacturing and healthcare operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Includes instruction in applied mathematics, physical sciences, the social sciences, engineering analysis, systems design, computer applications, and forecasting and evaluation methodology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of next-generation hypersonic aerospace vehicles through advanced computational modeling of aerothermal-structural interactions. Current limitations in predicting turbulent boundary layer behavior, shock-wave interactions, and thermal protection system performance under extreme Mach number regimes (Mach 5–20) hinder progress toward reliable, efficient vehicles capable of sustained atmospheric flight. The research will employ high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with thermo-structural finite element analysis to resolve multi-physics phenomena across disparate temporal and spatial scales. Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) and wall-modeled Large Eddy Simulation (LES) approaches will be implemented to capture turbulence-chemistry interactions in high-enthalpy flows, while adaptive mesh refinement techniques will optimize resource allocation for localized phenomena such as boundary layer transition and shock impingement. The computational framework will integrate open-source solvers (e.g., SU2, OpenFOAM) with custom-developed algorithms for conjugate heat transfer and material ablation modeling. Access to high-performance computing resources is essential to achieve the required spatial resolution (sub-millimeter scale) and temporal sampling across multi-second flight trajectories, with anticipated simulations exceeding 10 million core-hours. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for surface heat flux distribution, boundary layer stability criteria, and thermally induced structural deformation, directly informing the design of actively cooled leading edges and scramjet combustor configurations. Results will advance fundamental understanding of hypersonic flow physics while providing industry-applicable tools to reduce reliance on empirical correlations and costly experimental testing. The developed workflows will also contribute scalable parallelization strategies for exascale-ready aerospace simulations, benefiting broader scientific efforts in multi-physics modeling.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aeronautics/ Aviation/ Aerospace Science and Technology, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of aviation and the aviation industry, including in-flight and ground support operations. Includes instruction in the technical, business, and general aspects of air transportation systems.

abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) face escalating challenges due to increasing patient volumes, resource constraints, and the critical need for rapid, data-driven decision-making. A key unmet need is the ability to predict patient outcomes and optimize care pathways in real time, particularly for high-acuity conditions such as sepsis, traumatic injury, and acute cardiovascular events. Existing predictive models often lack the granularity, scalability, or computational efficiency required for dynamic ED environments. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing and validating machine learning (ML) models to predict clinical deterioration, prioritize resource allocation, and personalize treatment strategies using multimodal data from electronic health records (EHRs), real-time vital sign streams, and imaging studies. The computational complexity of integrating heterogeneous data sources—spanning structured EHR entries, free-text clinical notes, and high-resolution physiological waveforms—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a hybrid deep learning framework combining transformer-based natural language processing for clinical text, convolutional networks for imaging analysis, and temporal models for continuous vital sign interpretation. These components will be integrated via ensemble methods to generate risk scores updated in real time. HPC infrastructure is critical for training these models on retrospective datasets (>500,000 ED encounters) and simulating operational workflows under varying patient influx scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include validated prediction tools for sepsis onset within 1–3 hours of triage, mortality risk stratification for trauma patients, and optimized bed assignment algorithms to reduce ED boarding times. Successful implementation will provide a scalable computational framework to enhance clinical decision-making, reduce preventable morbidity, and improve resource utilization in emergency care. The requested resources will enable processing of terabytes of multimodal data, parallelized hyperparameter optimization, and deployment of low-latency inference pipelines, which are infeasible with standard clinical computing systems. This work aligns with national priorities to integrate advanced analytics into emergency medicine, offering a template for data-driven acute care innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: The diagnosis and management of neurological disorders in pediatric populations remain challenging due to the heterogeneity of genetic, metabolic, and environmental factors contributing to conditions such as epileptic encephalopathies, neonatal hypoxic-ischemic injury, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multimodal datasets at scale, hindering the identification of biomarkers and personalized therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, neuroimaging, and clinical datasets from a cohort of 2,000 pediatric patients with undiagnosed or treatment-resistant neurological disorders. Using whole-genome sequencing data, longitudinal MRI/DTI imaging, and electronic health records, we will implement machine learning pipelines to identify pathogenic genetic variants, map structural and functional neural network abnormalities, and correlate these findings with clinical outcomes. Computational workflows will include variant prioritization via deep learning models trained on multi-omic databases, graph-based analyses of brain connectivity, and survival models to predict disease progression. The scale of data integration—spanning terabytes of imaging and genomic data—necessitates distributed computing frameworks for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include the discovery of novel genotype-phenotype associations, predictive algorithms for early intervention in high-risk neonates, and a publicly accessible computational toolkit for pediatric neurology research. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and developmental trajectories, this work aims to advance precision medicine approaches, reduce diagnostic odysseys, and improve functional outcomes for children with neurological disorders. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving these goals, enabling analyses that are infeasible with standard clinical computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of neurologic disorders of the neonatal period, infancy, early childhood, and adolescence. Requires training in neurology with additional training in child neurology.

abstract: Nuclear radiology relies on precise imaging and quantification of radionuclide biodistribution to diagnose diseases such as cancer, neurological disorders, and cardiovascular conditions. However, current methods for reconstructing tomographic images and modeling radiotracer kinetics face limitations in accuracy and resolution, particularly in heterogeneous tissues or dynamic physiological conditions. These challenges stem from computational constraints in handling complex photon transport physics, noise reduction, and the integration of multi-modal patient data. This project proposes to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for optimizing nuclear imaging protocols and predictive biodistribution models. The research will focus on two aims: (1) creating patient-specific Monte Carlo simulations of photon interactions in hybrid SPECT/CT and PET/MRI systems to improve image reconstruction accuracy, and (2) training deep learning models to predict radiotracer kinetics using spatially resolved, time-dependent datasets from clinical studies. The simulations will account for tissue heterogeneity, scatter effects, and motion artifacts, while the machine learning component will integrate imaging data with genomic and metabolic profiles to identify biomarkers of abnormal tracer uptake. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, parallel processing of high-resolution voxelized phantoms, and iterative training of neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for reducing radiation dose without compromising diagnostic quality, predictive models linking biodistribution patterns to molecular subtypes of disease, and open-source tools for reproducible analysis of nuclear radiology data. This work has direct translational implications for personalizing diagnostic workflows, enhancing early detection of treatment-resistant malignancies, and improving the safety of longitudinal imaging in vulnerable populations.
