By bridging computational innovation with clinical nuclear radiology, the project aims to establish a scalable framework for advancing precision medicine in radionuclide-based diagnostics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the imaging by external detection of radionuclides and/or biodistribution by external detection of radionuclides for diagnosis of disease. Requires prior partial completion of a residency program in diagnostic radiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Tamil philology and dialectology, addressing critical gaps in the analysis of Tamil’s historical evolution and regional variations. While Classical and Modern Tamil have been extensively studied through traditional methods, the computational modeling of linguistic shifts, dialectal divergence, and sociolinguistic influences remains underdeveloped due to the scale and complexity of datasets. The research problem centers on analyzing large, multi-regional corpora spanning 2,000 years, including digitized palm-leaf manuscripts, modern literary texts, and oral recordings, to map phonetic, syntactic, and semantic changes across time and geography. Key challenges include processing non-standardized orthographies, managing code-switching phenomena in texts, and detecting subtle dialectal features in audio data. The proposed computational approach integrates neural language models trained on Tamil-specific corpora, phonetic alignment algorithms for cross-dialect comparisons, and graph-based methods to trace lexical diffusion pathways. HPC resources will enable the parallelization of these tasks, particularly for transformer-based models fine-tuned to handle archaic Tamil forms, and the storage of intermediate outputs from terabyte-scale text and speech datasets. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated Tamil linguistic variants, predictive models of dialectal intelligibility, and tools for automated dating of undetermined historical texts. These results will directly support philological research, language preservation initiatives, and educational applications, such as dialect-aware pedagogical tools. By bridging computational linguistics with Tamil scholarship, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for under-resourced Dravidian languages while advancing interdisciplinary connections between humanities research and high-performance computing.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Tamil language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Classical and Modern Tamil; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Diabetes mellitus represents a complex, multifactorial disorder with profound global health impacts, yet the mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Current therapeutic strategies often fail to account for individual variability in disease progression, treatment response, and complication risk, highlighting the need for integrative approaches to unravel its pathophysiological complexity. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal clinical, genomic, and metabolomic datasets from a longitudinal cohort of 15,000 patients with type 2 diabetes. The research will develop machine learning models to identify subtype-specific biomarkers and predict individualized risks of microvascular complications. Computational challenges include integrating high-dimensional datasets (whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal HbA1c measurements, and serum metabolomics) while addressing missing data and temporal dependencies. A hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for biological network integration and transformer-based architectures for temporal pattern recognition will be implemented. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate candidate protein-metabolite interactions implicated in subtype-specific pathways. The scale of data processing (~2 PB) and the iterative nature of deep learning model training necessitate HPC capabilities for parallelized workflows, GPU-accelerated computations, and large-memory nodes. Expected outcomes include (1) a clinically actionable stratification framework for diabetes subtyping, (2) predictive models for complication risks with validated accuracy (>85% AUC), and (3) mechanistic insights into dysregulated pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting. By bridging large-scale data science with clinical translation, this work aims to advance precision medicine paradigms in diabetes care, potentially reducing trial-and-error treatment approaches and complication-related healthcare burdens. The requested computing resources are critical to achieving the project’s resolution of complex interactions across biological scales within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Diabetes

abstract: Hematological disorders, including leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and coagulation abnormalities, present complex molecular mechanisms that challenge conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Current limitations in integrating multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with dynamic models of hematopoiesis and coagulation hinder the identification of predictive biomarkers and personalized treatment strategies. This project proposes a computational framework to model disease mechanisms, optimize laboratory workflows, and predict clinical outcomes in hematologic pathologies. The primary research challenge lies in processing high-dimensional datasets and simulating multi-scale biological systems, which require substantial computational resources beyond the capacity of standard laboratory infrastructure. To address this, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to execute large-scale machine learning pipelines for integrating heterogeneous clinical and omics data, molecular dynamics simulations of coagulation factor interactions, and agent-based models of hematopoietic stem cell differentiation. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks to classify leukemia subtypes from single-cell RNA-seq data, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of thrombotic risk under varying coagulation parameters, and ensemble modeling of clonal evolution in myeloid malignancies. These analyses demand terabytes of memory, thousands of CPU core-hours per simulation, and specialized GPU nodes for matrix operations. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking genetic variants to coagulation lab test anomalies, optimized algorithms for flow cytometry data interpretation, and digital twins of bone marrow niches to test therapeutic interventions *in silico*. The resource-intensive nature of these workflows necessitates access to HPC clusters with high-throughput storage, scalable node architectures, and GPU acceleration capabilities. Successful implementation will advance precision diagnostics, reduce turnaround times for complex hematopathology testing, and provide a computational foundation for virtual clinical trials in rare hematologic disorders. This work bridges critical gaps between experimental hematology and clinical translation, with direct implications for laboratory management and evidence-based guideline development.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory and analytical procedures for studying all facets of hematologic and coagulation disorders. May included related research in the management of hematology laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in large-scale procurement decision-making under dynamic market conditions, where traditional optimization models fail to account for real-time supply chain volatility, multi-tiered vendor dependencies, and regulatory constraints. Current approaches to contract lifecycle management often rely on static cost models or heuristic methods, leaving organizations vulnerable to disruptions and suboptimal resource allocation. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates stochastic optimization, agent-based supply chain simulations, and natural language processing (NLP) for automated contract analysis. The computational model will process real-world datasets spanning historical procurement transactions, supplier risk profiles, geopolitical event logs, and contractual obligation structures. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will evaluate probabilistic scenarios for cost overruns, while graph neural networks will map interdependencies across tiered supplier networks. A novel NLP pipeline will extract penalty clauses, delivery terms, and compliance requirements from unstructured contract texts to inform constraint matrices. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these computations across millions of scenario permutations and terabyte-scale procurement databases, enabling near-real-time prescriptive analytics. Expected outcomes include a decision support system capable of recommending optimal contract structures under uncertainty, predicting supplier failure risks with 85%+ accuracy, and dynamically adjusting procurement strategies based on simulated market shocks. This research will advance computational methods in contract management by establishing quantifiable metrics for agile procurement in high-risk sectors such as defense logistics and critical infrastructure development. Results will be validated through partnerships with federal contracting agencies and multinational corporations, with implementation guidelines disseminated through the National Contract Management Association. The requested computing resources will directly support 12-18 month benchmark studies comparing model performance against industry-standard procurement optimization tools.
cip_title: Purchasing, Procurement/ Acquisitions and Contracts Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage and/or administer the processes by which a firm or organization contracts for goods and services to support its operations, as well as contracts it to sell to other firms or organizations. Includes instruction in contract law, negotiations, buying procedures, government contracting, cost and price analysis, vendor relations, contract administration, auditing and inspection, relations with other firm departments, and applications to special areas such as high-technology systems, international purchasing, and construction.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate complex household decision-making dynamics under economic stress, a critical yet underexplored area within Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Traditional studies in FCS rely on survey-based or qualitative methods, which struggle to model the nonlinear interactions of financial, social, and psychological factors shaping resource allocation decisions in families. The research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate multi-agent household systems, integrating behavioral economics, psychosocial stressors, and real-world economic datasets. The primary objective is to model how households prioritize competing needs—such as healthcare, education, nutrition, and debt management—during prolonged economic instability, such as that induced by global crises or localized recessions. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques, the project will simulate decision trees influenced by variables including income volatility, cultural norms, policy interventions, and intergenerational resource transfer. HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, parallelize simulations across diverse demographic profiles, and validate models against longitudinal datasets from public health and economic databases. Expected outcomes include identifying resilience strategies adopted by households in different socioeconomic contexts, quantifying the cascading effects of delayed financial decisions, and generating predictive insights into crisis-driven behavioral shifts. The results will inform policymakers and FCS practitioners in designing targeted interventions to mitigate economic vulnerability. Additionally, the project aims to establish a scalable computational methodology for human sciences, bridging gaps between empirical social research and data-driven systems modeling. By advancing the use of HPC in non-traditional domains, this work will demonstrate the transformative potential of computational social science in addressing real-world challenges at the intersection of family well-being and economic sustainability.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurocognitive and behavioral correlates of contemplative practices using advanced computational modeling to bridge gaps between subjective experiential reports and objective physiological data. While prior research has established basic neural signatures of meditation and mindfulness, fundamental questions remain about how individual differences in cognitive traits, cultural context, and practice modalities shape the dynamic interplay between conscious experience, attention regulation, and autonomic nervous system responses. The study will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets—including high-density EEG recordings, heart rate variability metrics, and first-person phenomenological annotations—collected from 200 participants engaged in diverse contemplative protocols. A novel computational pipeline will integrate dynamical systems modeling to characterize phase transitions in attentional states, machine learning classifiers to map neural patterns to self-reported experiential qualities, and network neuroscience approaches to identify practice-specific functional connectivity profiles. Crucially, the HPC environment will enable large-scale simulations testing theoretical frameworks about metacognitive resource allocation during sustained introspection, as well as Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify cross-cultural variations in contemplative efficacy. Expected outcomes include a validated computational ontology for classifying contemplative states, predictive models linking neurophysiological markers to training outcomes, and open-source tools for real-time biofeedback in contemplative interventions. By synthesizing methods from computational neuroscience, anthropology of consciousness, and cognitive phenomenology, this work aims to establish a rigorous empirical foundation for understanding how contemplative practices modulate human cognition—a critical step toward developing personalized mental health interventions and advancing interdisciplinary dialogue between science and contemplative traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophical, psychological, and scientific bases of human contemplative experience. Includes instruction in cognitive science, meditation, mindfulness, neuroscience, philosophy, psychology, and religion.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of dynamic social network evolution in shaping health disparities among aging populations, leveraging computational social science frameworks to model longitudinal interactions between social connectivity and biological aging. While gerontology traditionally emphasizes biomedical or public health approaches, this work integrates complex systems theory, network science, and computational linguistics to analyze how shifting social ties—mediated by retirement, caregiving demands, and digital communication patterns—influence trajectories of cognitive decline and multimorbidity. The research problem centers on identifying critical transition points where social network fragmentation accelerates health deterioration, particularly in understudied rural aging populations. Using anonymized longitudinal data from health surveys, electronic health records, and natural language processing of community forum interactions (spanning 15 years across 3 regions), we will develop agent-based models simulating network-aging feedback loops. High-performance computing resources are required to handle three computational challenges: 1) Bayesian inference for missing data imputation across heterogeneous sources, 2) multiscale network simulations incorporating individual-level biomarker data and community-level resource maps, and 3) sensitivity analyses quantifying policy intervention impacts through counterfactual scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel metric of "social frailty" that predicts vulnerability thresholds more accurately than existing clinical tools, along with an open-source simulation platform for testing community support strategies. By computationally modeling the entanglement of social dynamics and biological aging processes, this work aims to advance predictive frameworks for aging equity while establishing methodological bridges between computational social science and lifespan health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized therapeutic exercise protocols for patients with mobility impairments due to neurological or musculoskeletal conditions. Current rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized guidelines, which may not account for individual variability in biomechanics, physiology, and pathology. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create patient-specific simulations that model the biomechanical and physiological effects of therapeutic exercises. The research problem centers on identifying how individualized parameters—such as joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns, and tissue load distribution—interact during rehabilitation, and how these factors influence functional recovery outcomes. The computational approach integrates musculoskeletal modeling, machine learning, and dynamic simulations to predict optimal exercise intensity, duration, and modality for diverse patient profiles. Multiscale models will simulate neuromuscular responses to therapeutic movements using open-source biomechanics software (e.g., OpenSim), while machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets (e.g., gait analysis, electromyography, and patient-reported outcomes) to identify predictive biomarkers of rehabilitation success. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large patient cohorts and high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool to guide kinesiotherapists in designing adaptive, evidence-based interventions for conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, and osteoarthritis. This work will advance precision rehabilitation by bridging gaps between clinical practice and computational biomechanics, potentially reducing trial-and-error in therapy design and improving patient adherence. The resulting open-access models and datasets will serve as a resource for interdisciplinary research in rehabilitation science, motor control, and assistive technology development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the direction of physicians, to treat the effects of disease, injury, and congenital disorders through therapeutic exercise and education. Includes instruction in human anatomy, human physiology, kinesiology, biomechanics, therapeutic exercise and adapted physical education, human growth and development, motor learning and performance, testing and measurement, first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, psychology, rehabilitation procedures, patient assessment and management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: Geriatric patients often present with complex, multifactorial health conditions that require integration of diverse clinical, genomic, and sensor-derived data to optimize care. Current approaches to analyzing these datasets are limited by conventional computing resources, which struggle to manage the scale, heterogeneity, and temporal resolution of geriatric health data. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of geriatric health outcomes and adverse drug events, with a focus on polypharmacy risks and age-related physiological decline. The research will aggregate electronic health records, wearable device metrics, and genomic data from a longitudinal cohort of 2,500 patients aged 65+ receiving care through partner clinical sites. Machine learning pipelines will be implemented to identify multidimensional risk profiles for falls, delirium, and medication-related hospitalizations, while mechanistic models of pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic interactions will simulate age-related changes in drug metabolism. Agent-based modeling will further explore how nurse-led interventions can mitigate risks in different care settings. Computational challenges include federated learning across distributed clinical datasets, real-time processing of continuous vital sign streams, and parameter optimization for physiologically based pharmacokinetic models. Outcomes will include validated predictive algorithms for geriatric syndromes, open-source tools for personalized medication reconciliation, and simulation frameworks to test care coordination strategies. By enabling large-scale integration of multimodal geriatric data, this work aims to advance precision nursing interventions, reduce preventable complications in aging populations, and inform clinical decision-support systems tailored to gerontological nursing practice. The requested HPC resources are essential for training deep learning architectures, running parallelized simulations, and maintaining secure data processing pipelines in compliance with healthcare privacy standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care to aging and elderly patients. Includes instruction in geriatric primary care, geriatric diagnosis, mental health and aging, primary care management, geriatric acute and chronic illness, advanced nursing practices for geriatric patients, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of marine propulsion and energy systems, driven by global demands for operational efficiency and stringent environmental regulations, necessitates advanced computational tools to model, optimize, and predict system behavior. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for hybrid marine propulsion systems integrating diesel engines, electrical storage, and waste-heat recovery technologies. A critical challenge lies in balancing real-time energy demands, thermal management, and emissions control under dynamic operational conditions, such as variable loads and harsh marine environments. Traditional analytical methods and low-resolution simulations fail to capture the multi-physics interactions between mechanical, electrical, and thermal subsystems, limiting predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, coupled simulations of fluid dynamics, combustion processes, and electromechanical systems. Agent-based modeling will simulate component interactions, while machine learning algorithms will optimize control strategies using real-world operational data. The HPC environment is essential for resolving microsecond-scale combustion events, turbulent flow in heat exchangers, and system-wide energy transfers simultaneously, which would otherwise be computationally intractable. Expected outcomes include predictive models for hybrid system performance under diverse scenarios, validated against experimental data from lab-scale marine engine testbeds. These models will inform the design of adaptive control systems to reduce fuel consumption by 10–15% and nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions by 20% compared to conventional configurations. The project will also generate open-access datasets and modular code libraries to support future research in marine energy systems. By advancing computational capabilities in marine engineering, this work aims to accelerate the adoption of sustainable technologies in maritime industries, aligning with global decarbonization goals while maintaining operational reliability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in shipboard mechanical and electrical engineering and the maintenance and operation of marine engines, including gas, diesel, and steam engines. Includes instruction in automation, diesel-powered systems, electrical circuits and systems, engine performance, hydraulics, manufacturing, motor-powered systems, refrigeration and air-conditioning, steam-powered systems, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework to optimize the detection and classification of rare hematologic disorders through advanced computational analysis of high-dimensional blood sample data. Current diagnostic workflows in hematology technology face challenges in identifying subtle, heterogeneous patterns in blood morphology and molecular biomarkers, particularly in cases of understudied or overlapping conditions such as clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) or atypical myelodysplastic syndromes. Traditional manual microscopy and single-analyte assays lack the resolution to capture complex cellular dynamics and multi-omics interactions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process terabyte-scale datasets comprising hyperspectral cellular imagery, single-cell RNA sequencing, and longitudinal patient metadata. A hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) and graph neural network (GNN) architecture will be trained to identify spatial, temporal, and molecular relationships across these multimodal datasets. Computational workflows will integrate open-source tools for digital pathology image analysis (QuPath, CellProfiler) with custom PyTorch models optimized for GPU-accelerated environments. Key innovations include the development of synthetic data augmentation pipelines to address class imbalances in rare disease cohorts and the implementation of explainable AI techniques to map decision pathways for clinical validation. Anticipated outcomes include a validated computational platform capable of differentiating between 15+ hematologic conditions with ≥92% accuracy in retrospective validation studies, alongside novel biomarkers for early disease detection. This work will directly enhance diagnostic precision in hematology laboratories while establishing scalable computational methods for analyzing emerging multi-omics datasets in blood-based diagnostics. The requested HPC resources will enable simultaneous training of multiple model variants, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and comparative benchmarking against existing clinical decision support systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of clinical laboratory scientists and health care professionals, to perform tests and analyses of blood samples. Includes instruction in clinical laboratory procedures; blood anatomy and physiology; cellular and molecular biology; blood pathology and disease indicators; quantitative, qualitative, and coagulation testing methodologies; equipment operation and maintenance; and record-keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of next-generation parametric design workflows in architectural technology, with a focus on optimizing building performance and construction efficiency. Traditional architectural design processes often rely on iterative, manual adjustments to balance aesthetic, structural, and environmental criteria—a time-intensive approach that limits exploration of complex design spaces. The proposed research addresses this bottleneck by integrating real-time physics-based simulations, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and multi-objective optimization algorithms into a unified computational framework. Key challenges include the need for parallelized evaluation of thousands of design variants under dynamic environmental conditions, as well as the training of AI models on heterogeneous datasets spanning material properties, climate profiles, and historical architectural precedents. The computational workflow will utilize distributed computing architectures to simultaneously analyze structural integrity (via finite element methods), energy efficiency (through computational fluid dynamics), and constructability (using automated rule-based systems) at urban-scale resolutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for AI-assisted architectural design that reduces simulation time by orders of magnitude compared to conventional software, enabling rapid prototyping of sustainable building solutions. This work bridges gaps between architectural practice, computational geometry, and environmental informatics, offering novel methodologies for data-driven design decision-making while maintaining fidelity to architectural intent. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive 3D model processing, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the integration of real-world sensor data from smart building systems into generative design pipelines. By democratizing access to advanced simulation capabilities typically restricted to engineering domains, this project aims to redefine technological workflows in architectural practice and education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist architects in developing plans and related documentation and in performing architectural office services. Includes instruction in architectural drafting, computer-assisted drafting and design, construction methods and materials, environmental systems, building codes and standards, structural principles, cost estimation, planning documentation, visual communication skills, display production, and architectural office management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop adaptive, real-time procedural content generation (PCG) systems for interactive game environments by integrating player behavior modeling with high-fidelity physics simulations. While procedural techniques are widely used to automate game asset creation, existing methods often lack dynamic responsiveness to individual player interactions, resulting in environments that feel static or disconnected from gameplay. This research addresses the challenge of balancing computational efficiency with real-time adaptability, particularly in complex 3D environments where player actions influence terrain deformation, object interactions, and non-player character (NPC) behaviors. The core computational methodology combines deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for player preference prediction with parallelized fluid dynamics and granular material simulations. High-performance computing resources will enable the simultaneous execution of multiple physics engines alongside DRL training cycles, allowing iterative optimization of environment generation algorithms under varying player interaction scenarios. Key technical hurdles include minimizing latency between player input and environmental response while maintaining visual fidelity, as well as ensuring scalable synchronization between discrete simulation modules. The project will validate outcomes through automated playtesting frameworks that measure emergent player engagement metrics across generated environments. Successful implementation could establish new paradigms for responsive PCG systems, reducing development costs for open-world games while enhancing player immersion through environments that evolve meaningfully in response to individual playstyles. This work bridges gaps between computational creativity, human-computer interaction, and real-time physics simulation—advancing game design capabilities through tightly integrated applications of machine learning and high-performance computational modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the knowledge and skills of design and computer programming to the development of computer games. Includes training in character and story development, computer programming, computer graphics, game design, game physics, human-computer interaction, human-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address computational bottlenecks in simulating complex mechanical systems for advanced Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CAD/CADD) applications. Current workflows in mechanical drafting often rely on iterative physical prototyping and simplified computational models to predict system behavior, leading to prolonged development cycles, material waste, and suboptimal designs under multifactorial stress conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven topology optimization to model high-fidelity mechanical assemblies. The project will focus on optimizing parametric designs for industrial machinery components subject to dynamic thermal, vibrational, and structural loads. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across thousands of design permutations, coupled with real-time visualization of deformation patterns and failure modes at micron-scale resolutions. Key computational challenges include managing multi-physics couplings in GPU-accelerated environments, automating geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) validation through distributed computing, and training neural networks on terabyte-scale simulation datasets to predict optimal material distributions. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in computational runtime compared to current workstation-based workflows, enabling rapid iteration of ASME Y14.5-compliant designs. The research will produce open-source tools for automated blueprint generation and stress analysis visualization, directly enhancing technical communication in cross-disciplinary engineering teams. By integrating HPC capabilities into mechanical drafting pedagogy, this project aims to bridge the gap between traditional CAD techniques and Industry 4.0 demands, equipping students with skills in large-scale simulation and data-driven design optimization. Results will be validated against physical prototypes in collaboration with regional manufacturing partners, with potential applications in renewable energy systems and precision aerospace components.
cip_title: Mechanical Drafting and Mechanical Drafting CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations in support of mechanical and industrial engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in manufacturing materials and processes, mechanical drafting, electrode-mechanical drafting, basic metallurgy, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, blueprint reading, and technical communication.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how rapid environmental change disrupts coevolutionary dynamics between interacting species, with implications for biodiversity loss and ecosystem resilience. A key challenge in evolutionary ecology lies in scaling mechanistic insights from pairwise species interactions—such as predator-prey or host-parasite systems—to complex ecological networks while accounting for shifting abiotic conditions. To address this, we propose developing spatially explicit, individual-based models that integrate ecological interactions, trait evolution, and environmental stochasticity. These models will simulate multi-species communities across realistic landscapes, parameterized using empirical data on species traits, interaction strengths, and climate projections. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of evolving interaction networks, track fine-scale adaptive trajectories across populations, and perform sensitivity analyses under diverse climate scenarios. Parallelized simulations will quantify how thermal tolerance, phenological shifts, and dispersal capacity modulate extinction cascades and evolutionary rescue events. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in environmental change rates beyond which coevolutionary feedbacks fail to maintain stability, as well as predicting which functional traits and network structures confer resilience. Results will advance theoretical frameworks for eco-evolutionary dynamics under global change and inform conservation strategies prioritizing species interactions at risk of rapid decoupling. The scale of parameter exploration (10^4–10^5 simulated communities) and the need for real-time integration of high-resolution climate data necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for memory-intensive tasks and efficient parallel processing. This work bridges population ecology and evolutionary theory, directly aligning with the program’s focus on biodiversity dynamics across biological hierarchies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the relationships and interactions across levels of biological organization--genes and genomes, organisms, species, and ecosystems--and how these change over time, including the origins and history of species, the processes by which biodiversity has evolved, and the ecological context in which this evolution takes place. Includes instruction in animal, plant, population, functional, evolutionary, and ecosystem ecology; ecological and evolutionary genetics; molecular evolution; population and conservation biology; animal and plant diversity; biometry; and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory management in multi-location restaurant franchises, a critical yet underexplored challenge at the intersection of food services operations, computational economics, and real-time data analytics. Traditional pricing and inventory models fail to account for the hyper-localized variability in demand drivers—such as seasonal tourism patterns, regional supply chain disruptions, and localized competitor activity—that impact perishable food inventory across geographically dispersed franchises. The project proposes a novel computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate spatially distributed consumer behavior, supplier networks, and cross-location inventory transfers. By deploying parallelized simulations across HPC clusters, the model will iteratively optimize pricing and redistribution strategies for perishable goods under constraints including shelf life, transportation costs, and franchise-specific profit-sharing agreements. The computational workflow will process real-time sales data, weather forecasts, and social media sentiment metrics to dynamically adjust parameters, requiring distributed memory architectures for low-latency updates across thousands of simulated franchise nodes. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of reducing food waste by 12–18% and improving margin resilience during supply shocks, as validated against historical data from a participating franchise network. This work advances computational methods in food services by formalizing the interdependencies between micro-localized demand signals and macro-scale inventory logistics, offering a transferable paradigm for perishable goods industries. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the granularity, speed, and parallelization required for both training RL policies and operationalizing real-time recommendations across complex, multi-stakeholder systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market restaurants, food services in hospitality establishments, food service chains and franchise networks, and restaurant supply operations. Includes instruction in hospitality administration, food services management, wholesale logistics and distribution, franchise operations, business networking, personnel management, culinary arts, business planning and capitalization, food industry operations, marketing and retailing, business law and regulations, finance, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and estimate high-dimensional econometric models to analyze the dynamic interdependencies between macroeconomic variables, financial markets, and policy shocks in a global context. Traditional econometric methods face computational limitations when scaling to systems with hundreds of interdependent time series, particularly when incorporating latent factors, structural breaks, and nonlinearities inherent to modern economic systems. The research problem centers on overcoming these barriers through advanced computational strategies, enabling robust analysis of complex economic networks and their stability under various shock scenarios. The project will employ Bayesian vector autoregressive (BVAR) frameworks with hierarchical priors, combined with stochastic volatility models and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling techniques adapted for distributed computing architectures. These methods require iterative estimation of high-dimensional parameter spaces and repeated simulation of counterfactual scenarios, necessitating parallelized computation and large-scale memory management. The requested high-performance computing resources will support 1) the calibration of models using historical datasets spanning national accounts, asset prices, and central bank policies across 50+ economies; 2) real-time nowcasting experiments integrating unstructured data sources; and 3) stress-testing exercises evaluating systemic risk propagation. Expected outcomes include new computational workflows for economic forecasting under parameter uncertainty, open-source tools for massive-scale econometric estimation, and empirically grounded insights into the resilience characteristics of interconnected economic systems. By enabling analysis at previously impractical scales, this work aims to advance quantitative economics through methodological innovation while providing policymakers with enhanced frameworks for evaluating macroeconomic stability. The resource-intensive nature of these computations—particularly the need for multi-node GPU acceleration and petabyte-scale data handling—makes high-performance computing infrastructure essential to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of mathematical and statistical analysis of economic phenomena and problems. Includes instruction in economic statistics, optimization theory, cost/benefit analysis, price theory, economic modeling, and economic forecasting and evaluation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of morphosyntactic and phonological patterns in Classical Sanskrit and Prakrit texts, with a focus on tracing diachronic developments in early Indo-Aryan languages. A central challenge in historical linguistics research on these languages lies in systematically analyzing vast corpora of digitized texts to identify subtle linguistic shifts, such as the evolution of case-marking systems or metrical innovations across genres and periods. Traditional manual methods are constrained by the scale and complexity of these texts, which include thousands of verses spanning Vedic, Epic, and Classical Sanskrit, as well as Prakrit dialects like Pali and Ardhamagadhi. To address this, we propose developing a hybrid computational pipeline integrating rule-based morphological parsers, machine learning models for syntactic annotation, and phylogenetic algorithms to model language change. The pipeline will process digitized critical editions from repositories like the Kyoto-Harvard Sanskrit Corpus and the Gandhari Prakrit Digital Archive, requiring HPC resources for parallelized text processing, training transformer-based models on classical language data, and running Bayesian comparative analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for annotating syntactic and metrical features in under-resourced ancient Indo-Aryan languages, (2) quantitative models of linguistic variation across literary, ritual, and grammatical texts, and (3) open-access datasets mapping phonological and morphological innovations between Vedic Sanskrit and later Prakrits. By enabling large-scale pattern detection across centuries of textual production, this work will provide new empirical foundations for debates about language contact, standardization processes, and the interplay between oral composition and grammatical formalization in South Asia. The computational tools developed will also benefit philological studies of related Indo-European languages by establishing transferable methods for analyzing non-Latin-script historical corpora.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Sanskrit and Classical Indian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Sanskrit and related ancient and classical Indo-Aryan languages. Includes instruction in Vedic and Classical Sanskrit, Pali and other Prakrits, and the historical development of Indo-Aryan languages and their relation to Indo-European languages such as Greek, Latin and the Baltic languages.

abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has transformative potential for rapid prototyping and customized production, but current methods for selecting process parameters rely heavily on empirical trial-and-error, leading to material inefficiencies and suboptimal mechanical properties. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiphysics interactions during AM processes and predict optimal printing parameters for diverse materials and geometries. The research will employ coupled finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics models to resolve thermal gradients, residual stresses, and microstructure evolution at high spatial and temporal resolutions. Machine learning techniques will be integrated to correlate simulated behaviors with experimental defect data, enabling adaptive parameter optimization. By utilizing HPC resources, the team will scale simulations across thousands of core-hours to capture complex interactions in industrial-scale components, validated through synchronized physical experiments. The anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for AM parameter prediction, reducing material waste by an estimated 30–50% in pilot studies, and enhancing mechanical performance through microstructure control. This work addresses a critical bottleneck in AM adoption by providing a systematic, computationally driven approach to process design, with broad implications for manufacturing sectors reliant on high-precision, low-waste production methodologies. The requested computing resources will enable the high-fidelity modeling required to bridge the gap between laboratory-scale AM research and industrial implementation, directly advancing engineering technologies in scalable digital manufacturing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between skeletal morphology and environmental stressors in hominin evolution using advanced computational modeling. A persistent challenge in physical anthropology lies in quantifying how biomechanical demands—such as locomotion patterns, tool use, or dietary shifts—shaped skeletal adaptations in fossil hominins. Current analyses rely heavily on static morphological comparisons, limiting our ability to model dynamic responses to evolutionary pressures. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating micro-CT data from fossil specimens, finite element analysis (FEA), and agent-based evolutionary simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D skeletal models (5–10 µm/voxel), run iterative FEA under simulated biomechanical loads, and model long-term adaptive trajectories across parameterized landscapes. The workflow will first reconstruct strain distributions in hominin fossil elements (e.g., femoral necks, mandibular rami) during hypothesized behaviors, then use these mechanical profiles to inform evolutionary algorithms that simulate morphological change over generational timescales. This approach will be validated against known evolutionary sequences in the hominin fossil record before being applied to contested adaptations, such as the emergence of bipedal femoral morphology in early Australopithecus. Expected outcomes include a validated computational pipeline for testing evolutionary hypotheses, quantitative benchmarks for skeletal adaptation thresholds, and novel insights into how developmental plasticity interacted with natural selection during key transitions. The requested resources will enable processing of terabyte-scale micro-CT datasets, parallelized FEA computations across 10,000+ core-hours, and evolutionary simulations tracking 50+ morphological variables over 100,000 generations. By bridging empirical paleoanthropology with computational biomechanics, this work aims to establish new methods for testing evolutionary hypotheses that are inaccessible to traditional comparative techniques.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and anthropology to the study of the adaptations, variability, and the evolution of human beings and their living and fossil relatives. Includes instructions in anthropology, human and mammalian anatomy, cell biology, paleontology, human culture and behavior, neuroscience, forensic anthropology, anatomical reconstruction, comparative anatomy, and laboratory science and methods.

abstract: The increasing complexity of information technology (IT) projects, characterized by dynamic stakeholder requirements, distributed teams, and evolving security threats, demands novel approaches to optimize resource allocation under uncertainty. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating multi-objective IT project scenarios, with a focus on modeling interdependencies between human, technical, and temporal variables in large-scale deployments. Leveraging agent-based modeling and discrete-event simulation techniques, the research will quantify how adaptive resource allocation strategies impact project outcomes such as delivery timelines, risk exposure, and team productivity. Computational experiments will integrate real-world datasets from cloud migration initiatives and cybersecurity upgrade projects, incorporating stochastic elements to represent requirements volatility and workforce availability constraints. The framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate millions of scenario permutations, identifying robust allocation policies that balance competing priorities across technical debt reduction, security compliance, and agile delivery targets. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for stress-testing IT project plans under diverse constraints, along with predictive models that correlate resource flexibility metrics with project success probabilities. By enabling data-driven analysis of tradeoffs between parallel development workflows, contingency reserves, and specialized skill deployment, this work aims to advance decision-support capabilities for IT project managers operating in high-uncertainty environments. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and resolution in modeling complex project ecosystems, particularly when analyzing emergent behaviors in projects spanning hybrid cloud infrastructures and geographically distributed development teams.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, develop, and manage information technology projects in a variety of companies and organizations. Includes instruction in principles of project management, risk management, procurement and contract management, information security management, software management, organizational principles and behavior, communications, quality assurance, financial analysis, leadership, and team effectiveness.

abstract: Understanding the mechanisms governing earthquake nucleation and propagation remains a critical challenge in geophysics, with significant implications for seismic hazard assessment. Current models struggle to resolve the multi-scale physics of fault zones, where granular interactions at micrometer scales influence kilometer-scale stress accumulation and rupture dynamics. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing high-resolution, three-dimensional simulations of fault systems using advanced computational methods. The research will focus on the San Andreas Fault system, integrating geodetic, seismologic, and laboratory-derived friction data to constrain models of stress transfer and rupture propagation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the non-linear coupling of thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes across spatial scales (nanometers to kilometers) and temporal scales (seconds to millennia). Numerical methods will include adaptive mesh refinement finite element modeling to capture localized deformation and machine learning algorithms to optimize parameter space exploration. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized solvers and GPU acceleration to manage the high dimensionality of the problem. Expected outcomes include new insights into the role of fluid-rock interactions in modulating earthquake recurrence intervals and the identification of precursory stress patterns detectable through geodetic monitoring. By bridging laboratory-scale friction laws with field-scale fault behavior, this work will advance physics-based seismic hazard models, directly informing infrastructure resilience planning. The requested computing resources will enable ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainties, a critical step toward operational earthquake forecasting. This project underscores the necessity of HPC in modern geophysical research, where data-intensive, multi-physics simulations are indispensable for decoding Earth’s complex mechanical systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physics of solids and its application to the study of the earth and other planets. Includes instruction in gravimetric, seismology, earthquake forecasting, magnetrometry, electrical properties of solid bodies, plate tectonics, active deformation, thermodynamics, remote sensing, geodesy, and laboratory simulations of geological processes.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, multi-stakeholder decision-making in decentralized business ecosystems enabled by blockchain-based smart contracts. As organizations increasingly adopt distributed ledger technologies for supply chain coordination, dynamic pricing, and cross-institutional governance, existing computational models struggle to scale to the complexity of continuously evolving, trustless networks with conflicting stakeholder incentives. The project will develop agent-based simulation frameworks to model emergent behaviors in these systems, incorporating game-theoretic reward mechanisms, stochastic market dynamics, and privacy-preserving data-sharing protocols. Computational demands arise from the need to simulate thousands of autonomous agents operating under Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus rules while maintaining cryptographic audit trails. Proposed methods include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing, evolutionary algorithms to optimize incentive structures, and graph neural networks to predict network congestion patterns. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for designing resilient decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) and quantified metrics for trade-offs between transaction finality speeds, incentive alignment costs, and system vulnerability surfaces. By advancing computational modeling capabilities at the intersection of distributed systems theory and operational business processes, this work aims to establish performance benchmarks for next-generation enterprise blockchain implementations while informing protocol standardization efforts. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations of large-scale networks (>10^4 nodes) and enabling rapid iteration cycles for machine learning components trained on synthetic transaction graphs.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatial dynamics of informal knowledge networks in urban food systems and their resilience to climate-induced disruptions, leveraging computational geography to address gaps in socio-environmental systems research. While urbanization intensifies, informal food networks—such as community gardens, street vendors, and localized barter systems—remain critical yet understudied components of urban resilience. The research problem centers on how these networks adapt to climate stressors (e.g., extreme heat, flooding) and how their spatial configurations influence equity in resource access. Current models often neglect the fine-grained, dynamic interactions between human agency, infrastructure, and environmental variability. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a multi-agent simulation framework integrating high-resolution geospatial data (satellite imagery, Lidar), climate projections, and agent-based behavioral models derived from participatory mapping surveys. Computational workflows will parallelize spatial network analysis to model cascading disruptions across temporal scales (daily interactions to decadal climate trends) and spatial scales (neighborhood to metropolitan regions). Machine learning methods will identify emergent patterns in network adaptability, while geostatistical models will quantify disparities in access under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational toolkit for simulating socio-spatial resilience, predictive maps of vulnerability hotspots, and policy-relevant insights into infrastructure investments that bolster equitable food security. By bridging computational geography with social practice theory, this work advances methodological innovation in modeling human-environment interactions while contributing empirical knowledge to nascent interdisciplinary research on informal urban systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling large raster datasets, optimizing complex network algorithms, and running ensemble simulations to capture uncertainty in socio-environmental feedbacks.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the spatial distribution and interrelationships of people, natural resources, plant and animal life. Includes instruction in historical and political geography, cultural geography, economic and physical geography, regional science, cartographic methods, remote sensing, spatial analysis, and applications to areas such as land-use planning, development studies, and analyses of specific countries, regions, and resources.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between urban built environments and psychological well-being, with a focus on loneliness, stress, and restorative experiences in densely populated regions. While prior studies highlight correlations between environmental features (e.g., green spaces, communal areas) and mental health outcomes, the dynamic mechanisms underlying these relationships—particularly across diverse sociocultural groups—remain poorly quantified. To address this gap, we propose a computational modeling framework integrating agent-based simulations (ABS) with machine learning-driven analysis of multi-modal datasets, including geospatial records, anonymized mobile device mobility traces, and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data from 5,000 participants across 15 global cities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale ABS scenarios that simulate daily routines, social interactions, and environmental exposures for synthetic populations calibrated to real-world demographic and psychological profiles. Concurrently, graph neural networks will analyze temporal patterns in mobility and self-reported well-being data to identify context-dependent predictors of environmental stress buffering. The computational pipeline will leverage parallelized processing for (1) parameter space exploration in ABS experiments testing urban design interventions and (2) training of attention-based models to detect subtle environment-behavior linkages across subgroups. Outcomes will yield a validated predictive toolkit for assessing how spatially embedded stressors and resources interact with individual differences to shape mental health trajectories. This work directly supports applied environmental psychology goals by enabling evidence-based recommendations for equitable urban planning and personalized therapeutic landscape design. The requested resources will overcome current limitations in modeling complex person-environment systems at scale, advancing translational applications in community counseling and preventive mental health infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of behavioral interactions between human beings and the environment in individual and group contexts, and ways to improve them. Includes instruction in contextual theory; statistics; physiological, social, and psychological responses to natural and technological hazards and disease; environmental perception and cognition; loneliness and stress; and psychological aspects of environmental design and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of German-language cultural narratives across digital archives spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in the representation of regional identities, migration, and transnational cultural exchange within German-speaking Europe, as reflected in digitized literature, periodicals, and ephemera. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to address the scale and complexity of these materials, which include over 500,000 multilingual texts from repositories such as the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek and Europeana, alongside understudied diasporic publications from North America and Eastern Europe. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and geospatial analysis to trace semantic shifts, intertextual networks, and the diffusion of motifs across time and borders. Custom transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to handle historical German orthographic variations and code-switching in minority-language contexts, while graph algorithms will map connections between authors, publishers, and thematic clusters. The workflow requires distributed training of multilingual embeddings, large-scale topic modeling across GPU-accelerated frameworks, and high-memory processing of georeferenced metadata. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas visualizing cultural transmission pathways, as well as new methodologies for computational literary studies that address the unique challenges of Central European multilingual corpora. By revealing how regional identities were negotiated in transnational contexts, this work will provide German Studies scholars with data-driven insights into the historical roots of contemporary cultural debates, while demonstrating the value of HPC infrastructure for humanities research reliant on heterogeneous, temporally layered datasets.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: The integration of dynamic market simulations into vocational sales and marketing teacher education remains underdeveloped, limiting instructors’ ability to prepare learners for real-world complexities. Current pedagogical tools often rely on static case studies or simplified scenarios, which fail to capture the high-dimensional, rapidly evolving nature of modern consumer markets. This project seeks to address this gap by developing and validating computational models of market ecosystems for use in distributive education classrooms. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques to simulate heterogeneous consumer behaviors, competitive interactions, and multi-channel marketing dynamics at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) training deep reinforcement learning agents to emulate realistic buyer decision processes using historical sales data, (2) running large-scale parameter sweeps to model diverse market conditions across geographical and demographic contexts, and (3) optimizing parallelized ABM simulations that capture emergent market phenomena through millions of agent interactions. The computational framework will be validated against real-world marketing campaign data from industry partners, with statistical verification of model fidelity. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform that enables vocational educators to generate adaptive, data-driven marketing scenarios for classroom use. This resource will directly enhance the pedagogical capacity of marketing operations instructors by providing interactive tools that bridge theoretical concepts with applied decision-making under uncertainty. Successful implementation will be measured through pilot deployments in teacher education programs, assessing both instructor adoption rates and improvements in student competency metrics related to market analysis and strategy development. The project contributes to the advancement of vocational education by establishing scalable computational methods for workforce-relevant skill development in marketing and distribution.
cip_title: Sales and Marketing Operations/ Marketing and Distribution Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational sales and marketing operations/marketing and distributive education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Veterinary toxicology faces a critical challenge in predicting and mitigating adverse health effects caused by synthetic and naturally occurring chemical exposures in animals. Current approaches to risk assessment rely heavily on time-consuming in vivo studies and limited mechanistic data, which fail to account for the vast chemical diversity and complex interactions affecting toxicity outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model chemical interactions with biological targets and predict species-specific toxicological responses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize toxin-receptor binding dynamics across veterinary-relevant species, including companion animals and livestock, with machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets (transcriptomic, metabolomic) from clinical toxicology cases. Key objectives include mapping structural determinants of toxin affinity for neural, hepatic, and reproductive system targets; simulating dose-response relationships under varying physiological conditions; and identifying genetic susceptibility markers for adverse outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of MD simulations across diverse chemical classes (e.g., pesticides, mycotoxins, pharmaceuticals) and support the training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets encompassing 50,000+ historical exposure records. Expected outcomes include predictive models for acute and chronic toxicity thresholds, a computational biomarker panel for rapid clinical risk stratification, and mechanistic insights into interspecies variability in chemical sensitivity. This work will directly inform evidence-based treatment protocols, regulatory guidelines for veterinary drug residues, and targeted antidote development, addressing critical gaps in clinical veterinary toxicology while reducing reliance on animal testing. By bridging computational chemistry with clinical data science, the project establishes a scalable paradigm for precision toxicology in veterinary medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical application of research on the nature and extent of adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals. May included related research in chemical mechanisms and the specialties of reproductive, developmental, genetic, forensic, inhalation and neurobehavioral toxicology.

abstract: The hospitality industry faces increasing pressure to optimize dining operations amidst fluctuating customer demands, labor shortages, and the need for personalized service. Traditional approaches to dining room management often rely on static protocols and experiential intuition, which may inadequately address real-time variables such as dynamic seating patterns, staff-task coordination, and customer satisfaction metrics. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven simulation framework to model and optimize multi-dimensional aspects of restaurant service systems. The research will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate guest behavior, staff workflows, and table turnover rates under varying scenarios, coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to predict customer preferences and service bottlenecks. By leveraging HPC resources, the framework will process large-scale datasets—including historical service times, menu popularity, and real-time IoT sensor inputs from dining environments—to generate adaptive staffing and seating strategies. Key computational challenges include parallelizing ABM simulations to account for thousands of concurrent agents (guests, staff) and training ML models on heterogeneous data streams (e.g., reservation logs, motion-tracking data). The outcomes will provide a decision-support tool for dynamically allocating resources—such as adjusting server assignments or reconfiguring table layouts—to minimize wait times, reduce operational costs, and enhance guest experience. This work bridges computational analytics and hospitality management, offering a novel methodology for data-driven service optimization. The resulting open-source tools will empower small-to-medium restaurants to adopt scalable, AI-enhanced management practices, fostering resilience in a post-pandemic economy. Successful implementation will demonstrate the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional domains, encouraging interdisciplinary innovation at the intersection of service industries and computational science.
cip_title: Food Service, Waiter/Waitress, and Dining Room Management/Manager.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve food to customers in formal or informal settings.  Includes instruction in the nutritional, sensory, and functional properties of food and its ingredients; food services principles; table and counter services; dining room operations and procedures; service personnel supervision and management; communication skills; business math; safety; and sanitation.

abstract: Sleep disorders, affecting millions globally, present complex diagnostic challenges due to the multidimensional nature of polysomnographic (PSG) data, which includes electroencephalography, electromyography, respiratory signals, and oximetry. Traditional analysis methods rely on manual scoring and linear statistical approaches, limiting the ability to detect subtle, nonlinear patterns predictive of disorders such as obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy, or insomnia. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a scalable computational framework to automate and enhance PSG analysis through machine learning (ML) and high-dimensional signal processing. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on a retrospective dataset of 10,000+ de-identified PSG studies, integrating time-series biosignals with clinical metadata. Key computational challenges include parallel processing of multi-channel signals at scale, optimizing hyperparameters for temporal convolutional networks, and implementing federated learning protocols to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. The project will validate models against expert-annotated hypnograms and clinical outcomes, assessing accuracy in sleep stage classification, event detection (e.g., apneas, limb movements), and disorder prediction. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for automated PSG scoring, reducing inter-rater variability and clinician workload. Additionally, the discovery of novel electrophysiological biomarkers could advance personalized interventions. HPC resources are critical to manage the dataset’s size (>50 TB), enable rapid iteration of complex models, and support real-time inference simulations for eventual clinical integration. This work aligns with national priorities to improve sleep health infrastructure and demonstrates how computational innovation can transform diagnostic paradigms in allied health professions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to work under the supervision of a physician to provide comprehensive evaluation and treatment of sleep disorders. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, polysomnographic technology, polysomnography scoring, neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of sleep, sleep disorders, and medical terminology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, safety, and maintenance protocols of recreational vehicle (RV) systems, with a focus on integrating multi-physics simulations to address complex engineering challenges. RVs are subject to dynamic mechanical, thermal, and environmental stresses during operation, yet traditional testing methods for critical systems—such as hydraulic braking, electrical networks, propane distribution, and structural frames—are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict failure modes under real-world conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate interactions between mechanical, electrical, and fluid systems under diverse operating scenarios. Key objectives include modeling stress distribution in welded joints during towing, predicting thermal profiles of propane appliances under extreme temperatures, and analyzing corrosion propagation in aluminum frames exposed to road salts. These simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and parallelized workflows to handle large-scale datasets spanning material properties, environmental conditions, and usage patterns. The outcomes will inform the development of predictive maintenance algorithms and design guidelines to enhance component longevity and safety. Additionally, the project will generate open-access training modules to introduce RV technicians to computational diagnostics, bridging gaps between traditional hands-on repair practices and data-driven decision-making. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing, this work aims to reduce reliance on physical prototypes, lower R&D costs for manufacturers, and advance technical education in the RV service sector. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required resolution for multi-system simulations and ensuring scalable, reproducible results across heterogeneous RV configurations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to build, test, inspect, repair, service and maintain recreational vehicles, systems, and interior and exterior components. Includes instruction in brake, hydraulic, and towing systems; electrical systems; propane systems and propane and electric appliances; carpentry; plumbing; welding; and structural frames.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize personalized culinary experiences through the integration of sensory science, consumer behavior analytics, and molecular gastronomy. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to predict how individualized dietary preferences, cultural contexts, and physiological responses interact to shape culinary satisfaction. Current approaches rely heavily on generalized surveys or small-scale experiments, which fail to capture the dynamic, multidimensional variables influencing taste perception, texture preferences, and emotional engagement with food. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex networks of consumer-food interactions using agent-based modeling, machine learning, and multiscale sensory datasets. Computational models will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including biochemical properties of ingredients, real-time biometric feedback (e.g., salivary response, neuroimaging correlates of flavor perception), and sociodemographic variables—to generate predictive profiles of personalized culinary outcomes.
