The project will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures to analyze high-resolution spectral data from food matrices, coupled with natural language processing of consumer reviews and cultural narratives. Validation will involve iterative comparisons between simulated outcomes and empirical data from controlled culinary trials. Anticipated outcomes include a novel decision-support tool for chefs and food service providers to design hyper-personalized menus, reducing waste and enhancing consumer engagement. This work will establish a foundation for computational gastronomy as an interdisciplinary field, bridging gaps between data science, cultural studies, and culinary arts. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s large-scale datasets, real-time simulations of multi-agent interactions, and computationally intensive optimization algorithms, which cannot feasibly be executed on local infrastructure. By advancing predictive analytics in culinary personalization, this research aims to transform hospitality services while contributing methodological innovations to non-STEM domains.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats in military operations necessitates advanced computational tools to model, predict, and counter adversarial tactics in real time. This project seeks to develop a dynamic, AI-driven simulation framework for analyzing multi-vector cyber-physical attacks on military networks, with a focus on adversarial behavior patterns that exploit vulnerabilities across integrated command, control, and communications (C3) systems. Current threat assessment models lack the granularity to evaluate cascading failures in hybrid environments where cyber operations intersect with electronic warfare (EW) capabilities, such as jamming, spoofing, and electromagnetic spectrum manipulation. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale, adaptive attack scenarios incorporating machine learning (ML)-based adversarial agents, probabilistic failure propagation models, and real-time defensive response algorithms. Computational methods will include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to assess system resilience under stochastic threat conditions, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map interdependencies between cyber and electronic warfare nodes, and evolutionary optimization techniques to iteratively harden defense postures. The framework will integrate classified threat intelligence datasets with synthetic data generation to balance operational security requirements with model fidelity. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for identifying critical vulnerabilities in next-generation C3 architectures, metrics for quantifying mission degradation under coordinated cyber-EW attacks, and actionable recommendations for adaptive resource allocation in contested environments. By enabling multi-domain threat modeling at unprecedented scale and speed, this work aims to directly inform doctrine development and capability investments for modern electronic warfare and cyber operations. The proposed HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of simulating nation-state-level adversarial tactics while maintaining the low-latency processing required for operational relevance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the technological and operation aspects of information warfare, including cyber attack and cyber defense. Includes instruction in computer and network security, cryptography, computer forensics, systems security engineering, software applications, threat and vulnerability assessment, wireless networks and satellite communications, tactical and strategic planning, legal and ethical issues, and cyber warfare systems development and acquisition.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a real-time adaptive control system for next-generation neuroprosthetic devices that integrate bidirectional neural interfaces with wearable robotic exoskeletons. Current systems face critical limitations in dynamically interpreting user intent while delivering proprioceptive feedback, particularly during complex locomotor tasks. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in decoding high-dimensional neural data (ECoG, EMG) and synthesizing responsive mechanical assistance within physiologically relevant latencies (<50ms). We propose a hybrid computational architecture leveraging federated learning for personalized intent recognition models and physics-informed neural networks for predictive gait optimization. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel training of patient-specific neural decoders across multiple GPU nodes while simultaneously simulating musculoskeletal dynamics and exoskeleton interaction forces through multibody finite element analysis. The computational workflow will integrate heterogeneous data streams from our partner rehabilitation center, including motion capture, embedded force sensors, and chronic neural recordings from ongoing clinical trials. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for co-adaptive neuro-mechanical control that maintains synchronization across timescales spanning milliseconds (neural processing) to seconds (gait adaptation). Successful implementation could demonstrate clinically significant improvements in stair negotiation and obstacle avoidance tasks for lower-limb prosthesis users, measured through validated mobility metrics. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and rehabilitation robotics by addressing the temporal hierarchy of sensorimotor integration—a prerequisite for restoring naturalistic movement patterns in patients with spinal cord injuries or stroke-related mobility impairments. The requested resources directly support large-scale parameter optimization and validation of our novel control paradigm against existing clinical datasets.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function. Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize AI-driven workflow automation tools for administrative support roles by analyzing complex, unstructured communication patterns in hybrid office environments. The proliferation of asynchronous communication platforms (email, chat systems, collaborative documents) has created bottlenecks in task prioritization and delegation, particularly when managing cross-departmental requests with conflicting urgency signals. Current rule-based automation systems fail to adequately interpret contextual nuances in stakeholder communications, leading to inefficient resource allocation in calendaring, document routing, and meeting coordination. This study proposes developing a multimodal natural language processing (NLP) framework trained on anonymized organizational datasets—including email threads, project management logs, and meeting transcripts—to predict optimal task handling pathways. The computational approach combines transformer-based language models with temporal graph neural networks to map request-response patterns across communication channels while preserving confidentiality through differential privacy techniques. High-performance computing resources are required for three critical phases: 1) Parallel processing of terabyte-scale historical communication data to establish baseline interaction patterns, 2) Federated learning across simulated departmental knowledge domains, and 3) Real-time optimization testing through discrete event simulations modeling 10,000+ concurrent workflow scenarios. Expected outcomes include a probabilistic decision-support system that reduces administrative latency in complex request handling by 35-50% compared to current industry-standard tools, as measured through simulated stress tests and validated against human expert benchmarks. The research bridges computational linguistics with organizational behavior theory, offering novel insights into human-AI collaboration dynamics in modern administrative ecosystems. Successful implementation could redefine competency frameworks for administrative professionals by introducing evidence-based metrics for evaluating automation-assisted workflow efficiency.
cip_title: Administrative Assistant and Secretarial Science, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform the duties of administrative assistants and/or secretaries and stenographers. Includes instruction in business communications, principles of business law, word processing and data entry, office machines operation and maintenance, office procedures, public relations, secretarial accounting, filing systems and records management, and report preparation.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop computational frameworks for optimizing quantum-enhanced sensing networks (QESNs), an emerging interdisciplinary domain merging quantum physics, distributed systems engineering, and machine learning. Current quantum sensing technologies face scalability challenges when deployed in networked configurations, limiting their real-world utility in applications such as precision navigation, infrastructure health monitoring, or distributed environmental sensing. The project addresses the critical engineering challenge of modeling and optimizing QESNs under realistic noise, latency, and resource constraints—a problem requiring high-dimensional parameter space exploration beyond the capabilities of classical computing resources. The computational approach combines quantum circuit simulations using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) methods with graph-based network optimization algorithms accelerated by GPU-parallelized Monte Carlo sampling. A custom HPC workflow will integrate existing quantum simulation libraries (e.g., QuTiP) with novel topology optimization routines designed for heterogeneous quantum-classical networks. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for QESN performance prediction under dynamic operating conditions, (2) machine learning-derived heuristics for resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical sensor arrays, and (3) benchmark data correlating network topology with metrological gain in multi-parameter estimation tasks. The research will advance engineering methodologies for distributed quantum systems, providing foundational insights for future hardware implementations while maintaining compatibility with classical sensor infrastructures. By leveraging high-performance computing to bridge quantum theory and network engineering constraints, this work aims to establish scalable design principles for next-generation sensing systems that transcend the limitations of standalone quantum devices. Successful implementation will directly benefit engineering education initiatives by generating case studies and modular codebases for pre-engineering curricula focused on emerging technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of pharmacological mechanisms underlying traditional Chinese herbal formulae, with a focus on multi-component interactions and their systemic effects on human physiology. While Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has long utilized complex herbal combinations to treat diseases holistically, the molecular basis of their efficacy remains underexplored due to the combinatorial complexity of bioactive compounds and the lack of scalable computational frameworks. Current limitations in processing power and algorithmic efficiency hinder systematic analysis of herb-herb and herb-protein interactions at the scale required for clinically relevant formulae. To address this, we propose a multi-stage computational workflow integrating cheminformatics, molecular docking, and machine learning to model the polypharmacology of classical TCM prescriptions. Molecular dynamics simulations will be employed to study dynamic interactions between herbal compounds and target proteins implicated in immune regulation, metabolic homeostasis, and inflammation—key pathways in TCM diagnostic frameworks. Network pharmacology approaches will map multi-target effects, while generative AI models will predict synergistic herb combinations based on historical texts and modern pharmacopeia. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental data from collaborator labs, including metabolomic and proteomic studies of patient samples. By enabling large-scale virtual screening of herbal libraries and dynamic modeling of formula-body interactions, this work aims to identify novel bioactive candidates, elucidate synergistic principles of herbal配伍 (compatibility), and establish predictive frameworks for optimizing personalized TCM treatments. Outcomes will bridge empirical TCM knowledge with modern systems biology, providing a foundation for evidence-based herbology and fostering innovation in integrative medicine. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the terabytes of simulation data, training deep learning models on compound-target networks, and iterating complex multi-scale analyses within project timelines.
cip_title: Traditional Chinese Medicine and Chinese Herbology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Chinese herbal medicine, a system based on the use of nutrition, natural products, and prescribed medical formulae to treat imbalances in the state of bodily health as defined in the Nei Ching Su Wen and other authorities. Includes instruction in the basic Western medical sciences, history and theory of Chinese medicine, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbology, herbal prescription preparation, herbal patent medicine, herbal pharmacology, Chinese internal medicine and gynecology, febrile diseases, food therapy, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision horticulture by modeling genotype-environment interactions in high-value crops under variable climatic conditions. A critical challenge in applied horticulture is optimizing plant performance while minimizing resource inputs, particularly as growers face increasing pressure from climate variability, water scarcity, and market demands for sustainable practices. Traditional field trials for evaluating plant responses to environmental stressors are time-intensive, spatially limited, and cost-prohibitive at scale. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating hyperspectral imaging data, genomic datasets, and dynamic environmental variables to predict phenotypic outcomes in real-world production systems. Using machine learning architectures (convolutional neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees), we will analyze multi-terabyte datasets capturing plant physiology, soil moisture dynamics, and microclimate variations across diverse growing environments. Agent-based modeling will simulate crop growth under projected climate scenarios, while parallelized genome-wide association studies (GWAS) will identify genetic markers linked to stress resilience. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing sensor-derived irrigation metrics, LiDAR-generated canopy structures, and high-resolution weather models at scale. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for irrigation scheduling, genotype-specific cultivation recommendations, and a publicly accessible database correlating genomic traits with environmental adaptability. By quantifying trade-offs between yield, water use efficiency, and nutrient uptake, this work will directly inform commercial growers’ operational decisions and breeding programs targeting climate-resilient cultivars. The computational pipeline developed here will establish a replicable framework for data-driven horticultural management, bridging the gap between genomic potential and field-scale agricultural performance.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general production and processing of domesticated plants, shrubs, flowers, foliage, trees, groundcovers, and related plant materials; the management of technical and business operations connected with horticultural services; and the basic scientific principles needed to understand plants and their management and care.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the historical transmission and adaptation of medical knowledge across global networks during the 19th and early 20th centuries, with a focus on how socio-economic disparities influenced the adoption of biomedical technologies. The study addresses a critical gap in the historiography of medicine by systematically analyzing large-scale, multilingual archival materials—including medical journals, institutional records, and correspondence—to trace the diffusion of surgical practices, diagnostic tools, and public health policies between colonial powers and colonized regions. A key challenge lies in processing heterogeneous, unstructured historical data spanning multiple languages and geographic contexts, which requires advanced computational methods. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract semantic patterns from digitized texts, network analysis to map knowledge exchange pathways, and geospatial modeling to visualize regional disparities in medical resource distribution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on historical medical terminology, conducting large-scale sentiment and thematic analyses across temporal scales, and running iterative simulations of knowledge diffusion under varying socio-economic parameters. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously undocumented epistemic hierarchies in colonial medicine, quantitative evidence linking infrastructure investments to therapeutic outcomes, and an open-access digital repository of annotated historical datasets. By integrating computational social science methods with traditional historiographic approaches, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for data-driven historical inquiry while contributing new perspectives on the relationship between medical globalization and health inequities. The requested computing resources will enable processing of over 500,000 pages of primary source materials and support the development of customizable analysis pipelines for future interdisciplinary studies in the history of medicine.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical evolution and socio-economic context of medical theories, education, practices, and technologies; and on the history of diseases, therapeutics, patients, and healers. Includes instruction in the concepts and methods of the historiography of medicine; the history of science, medicine, and technology; and of research methods in the history of medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural underpinnings of cognitive-communication disorders (CCD) in individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI) using advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC). CCD—characterized by deficits in attention, memory, and discourse coherence—arises from diffuse axonal injury and disrupted network connectivity, yet the dynamic interplay between structural damage, functional reorganization, and behavioral outcomes remains poorly understood. Current clinical assessments lack precision in predicting recovery trajectories, and rehabilitation strategies are often generalized rather than personalized. To address this gap, we propose integrating multimodal neuroimaging (diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state fMRI) with behavioral data from 150 TBI patients to construct patient-specific computational models of large-scale brain networks. These models will simulate neural dynamics under varying degrees of structural disruption and test hypotheses about compensatory mechanisms. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of imaging data, running parallelized simulations of whole-brain network activity using biologically informed neural mass models, and applying machine learning to identify biomarkers of CCD severity. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework linking TBI-induced structural damage to functional communication deficits, (2) predictive models of recovery patterns based on early post-injury network characteristics, and (3) prototype algorithms for optimizing non-invasive neuromodulation protocols tailored to individual network profiles. By elucidating how distributed neural systems adapt to injury, this work will advance the development of biologically grounded interventions for CCD, directly addressing the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders’ priority of integrating basic neuroscience with clinical translation. The requested computing resources will enable scaling beyond pilot studies, fostering innovation in neurorehabilitation for an understudied population with chronic communication challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biomedical, psychological, and physical principles to the study of the scientific bases, development, and treatment of speech, language, hearing, and cognitive communication problems caused by disease, injury, or disability. Includes instruction in language science, hearing science, speech and voice science, biology of communication, behavioral linguistics, psychology, and applications to the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative strategies and technologies.

abstract: Pediatric dental caries remains a leading chronic disease in children, with disparities in prevalence linked to complex interactions between microbial, genetic, environmental, and behavioral factors. Current clinical risk-assessment tools lack precision in predicting caries progression, particularly in diverse populations, due to oversimplified models that fail to capture nonlinear dynamics. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to model caries etiology and progression in pediatric populations, integrating longitudinal clinical data, microbial metagenomics, and socio-environmental variables. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate spatial-temporal interactions within oral biofilms under varying dietary and hygiene conditions, coupled with machine learning (ML) to identify critical risk thresholds and optimize personalized prevention strategies. The ABM will incorporate strain-level microbial genomic data from pediatric saliva samples (n=1,200) to simulate pH dynamics, biofilm maturation, and enamel demineralization processes. Parallelized ML pipelines will analyze multi-omic datasets (16S rRNA sequencing, host transcriptomics, geospatial data) to stratify patients by risk trajectories. Computational demands include large-scale parameter space exploration (>10,000 simulated patient-years), real-time adaptation of ML models to heterogeneous data streams, and validation against a 5-year clinical cohort. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive tool for early caries intervention, mechanistic insights into resilience phenotypes in high-risk populations, and optimized preventive protocols tailored to genetic and socioeconomic profiles. This work will advance precision pedodontics by bridging gaps between microbial ecology, behavioral science, and clinical decision-making, with direct implications for reducing oral health disparities. The computational infrastructure will also establish a scalable platform for future studies on pulp therapy outcomes and dental trauma management in pediatric populations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the therapeutic and preventive care of the oral health of children from birth through adolescence, and the care of adults with physical, mental, and emotional disabilities. Includes instruction in developmental oral biology, preventive medicine, diet therapy and counseling, patient management, pediatric restorative procedures, pulp therapy, trauma management, anesthesia, treatment planning, and the treatment of handicapped patients.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of intergenerational decision-making in household resource allocation under economic uncertainty, a topic situated at the intersection of human development, behavioral economics, and computational social science. While existing studies in Family and Consumer Sciences often rely on survey-based or qualitative methods, this research addresses a critical gap by modeling complex, nonlinear interactions between cultural norms, cognitive biases, and financial stressors that influence family systems. The computational challenge arises from simulating millions of agent-based household scenarios with heterogeneous parameters, including varying income volatility, multi-generational cohabitation patterns, and culturally embedded risk perceptions. A hybrid modeling approach will integrate adaptive network architectures (to capture evolving family structures) with reinforcement learning frameworks (to simulate decision-making heuristics), validated against longitudinal datasets from transnational demographic surveys. The HPC environment is essential for parallel processing of stochastic simulations across parameter spaces and for training deep learning models to identify latent patterns in high-dimensional behavioral data. Expected outcomes include predictive models of resilience strategies adopted by households facing economic shocks, visualized through interactive decision trees accessible to policymakers and financial literacy educators. This work will establish a novel computational methodology for human sciences research, enabling granular analysis of socio-economic behaviors while preserving the contextual complexity often lost in traditional disciplinary approaches. By bridging agent-based modeling with family systems theory, the project contributes to evidence-based interventions aimed at improving household financial stability in demographically diverse communities.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the dynamic mechanisms underlying neural circuit plasticity in response to multisensory integration, a process critical for adaptive behavior but poorly understood at the network level. Current limitations in modeling large-scale, biologically realistic neural networks hinder the exploration of how synaptic and circuit-level interactions drive reorganization during sensory processing. To address this gap, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate spiking neural network models incorporating anatomically constrained connectivity derived from mammalian sensory cortices. These models will integrate biophysical parameters governing short-term plasticity, dendritic computation, and neuromodulatory effects, enabling the study of emergent network states under varying sensory input conditions. Simulations will leverage parallelized NEURON and Nest simulations across GPU-accelerated nodes to achieve the scale required for whole-circuit analysis (>100,000 neurons with 10^8 adaptive synapses). Computational experiments will systematically perturb cross-modal input timing and intensity while tracking spike-timing-dependent plasticity rules and population coding fidelity. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of critical windows for circuit reorganization during multisensory conflict resolution, 2) predictive models of plasticity thresholds that prevent maladaptive rewiring, and 3) data-driven hypotheses about cortical layer-specific contributions to dynamic integration. The HPC implementation will enable parameter space exploration at scales unachievable with standard computing infrastructure, directly advancing our understanding of neural adaptability. Resulting datasets and optimized simulation workflows will be shared via community platforms to accelerate research in computational neuroscience. This work bridges systems-level neurobiology with computational theory, with potential implications for developing targeted interventions in sensory processing disorders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in neurobiology and neurosciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The apparel and textile industry faces mounting challenges in predicting consumer preferences and optimizing marketing strategies due to the rapid evolution of trends, sustainability demands, and global supply chain complexities. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between cultural, economic, and design-driven variables that shape purchasing behavior. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model dynamic consumer-textile-market ecosystems, integrating heterogeneous datasets such as social media sentiment, historical sales patterns, real-time retail analytics, and textile material performance metrics. By leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to map relationships between microtrends and macro-market shifts, coupled with agent-based modeling to simulate decision cascades across consumer demographics, the research aims to predict emergent fashion trends with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. The computational workflow will require parallel processing of multi-modal data (text, images, transactional records) to train deep learning architectures optimized for trend forecasting accuracy. Key deliverables include an open-source toolkit for adaptive marketing campaign simulation, capable of evaluating sustainability trade-offs between fast-fashion cycles and circular economy principles. The project’s outcomes will advance data-driven decision-making in apparel marketing by quantifying how localized design innovations propagate through global markets, ultimately reducing overproduction waste and enhancing cultural responsiveness in product launches. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, marketing analytics, and textile lifecycle management, establishing a novel methodology for resource allocation in industries where aesthetic and functional value propositions intersect.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the neural and behavioral mechanisms underlying hypnotherapy’s efficacy in modulating pain perception and emotional regulation. Despite growing clinical interest in hypnotherapy as a non-pharmacological intervention, the neurocomputational basis of its therapeutic effects remains poorly understood. Current limitations include insufficient resolution in modeling dynamic brain-state transitions during trance induction and a lack of scalable frameworks to simulate individualized therapeutic protocols. To address this, we propose a multi-modal computational approach integrating functional neuroimaging (fMRI, EEG) with behavioral data from clinical hypnotherapy sessions. HPC resources will enable the development of a biophysical neural network model optimized to simulate cortical-subcortical interactions during hypnosis, incorporating real-time feedback mechanisms and variability across patient phenotypes. Machine learning pipelines will be deployed to analyze high-dimensional datasets (spanning neural oscillations, autonomic responses, and self-reported symptom profiles) and identify predictive biomarkers of therapeutic response. Additionally, agent-based modeling will explore how therapist-client interactions influence trance depth and treatment outcomes. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across GPU clusters, we aim to generate the first large-scale, dynamic simulations of hypnotherapy processes, bridging gaps between neurobiology and clinical practice. Expected outcomes include validated computational biomarkers for optimizing hypnotic suggestion protocols, a predictive framework for personalizing interventions in chronic pain and anxiety disorders, and open-source tools for simulating neurobehavioral responses to hypnosis. This work will establish a foundation for data-driven hypnotherapy research, advancing its integration into precision health paradigms while addressing critical gaps in mechanistic understanding. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the scale, speed, and complexity of modeling brain-behavior dynamics in real-time therapeutic contexts, which cannot feasibly be achieved with standard computational resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to employ the controlled inducement of altered states of consciousness, or trance, to reduce pain, resolve emotional conflicts, and enhance communications as part of diagnostic and treatment programs. Includes instruction in the principles of hypnosis and suggestion, induction and deepening, post-hypnotic suggestion, awakening techniques, regression, pacing and leading, resistance transformation, client testing and management, practice management and regulation, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing large-scale, stochastic industrial systems under dynamic constraints, with applications in supply chain resilience and process integration. The research addresses the challenge of designing adaptive systems capable of responding to disruptions such as material shortages, demand fluctuations, and energy variability. Current analytical models struggle to balance real-time decision-making with long-term strategic planning, particularly when handling high-dimensional uncertainty or nonlinear interactions between subsystems. The proposed work combines mixed-integer programming, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to model multi-echelon networks, integrating production scheduling, inventory management, and logistics coordination. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to solve these computationally intensive problems within practical timeframes. Parallelized algorithms will be implemented to accelerate scenario-based optimization, leveraging distributed computing frameworks for Monte Carlo simulations of disruption scenarios. A key innovation involves embedding graph neural networks within decomposition methods to predict bottleneck propagation across interconnected systems. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision support tool that identifies robust resource allocation policies and quantifies trade-offs between efficiency and resilience metrics. The results will advance fundamental methodologies in operations research by addressing state-space explosion in stochastic optimization, with direct applications to semiconductor manufacturing and pharmaceutical distribution case studies. By enabling rapid evaluation of mitigation strategies for systemic risks, this work aims to reduce operational downtime costs by an estimated 15–25% in modeled systems. The computational infrastructure will also support open-source code development for reproducible industrial engineering research, fostering collaboration on complex system optimization challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific and mathematical principles to the design, development, improvement, and installation of integrated systems of people, material, information, and energy. Combines instruction in industrial and systems engineering.

abstract: Vascular diseases of the nervous system, including ischemic stroke and intracranial hemorrhage, represent leading causes of global morbidity and mortality. Current clinical management strategies remain limited by incomplete understanding of disease heterogeneity, dynamic pathophysiological processes, and variable treatment responses. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of cerebrovascular disease progression and optimize individualized therapeutic interventions. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) developing multiscale computational models integrating hemodynamic, thromboembolic, and tissue injury dynamics to simulate stroke pathophysiology across spatial and temporal scales, and (2) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze high-dimensional clinical datasets, including neuroimaging, biomarker profiles, and electronic health records. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model cerebral blood flow alterations in patient-specific vascular geometries derived from angiographic data, while finite element analyses will predict tissue-level responses to ischemia-reperfusion injury. Parallelized deep learning architectures will process multimodal datasets to identify prognostic signatures and predict treatment outcomes. These approaches require HPC capabilities due to the scale of 4D neuroimaging analyses (>10 TB/cohort), real-time coupling of differential equation systems in multiscale models, and hyperparameter optimization across neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for hemorrhagic transformation risk post-thrombolysis, optimized clot retrieval strategies for large-vessel occlusion, and dynamic biomarkers of penumbral tissue viability. By enabling complex simulations of neurovascular pathophysiology that are infeasible on standard computing infrastructure, this research will directly inform clinical trial design and bedside decision-making. The resulting computational tools aim to reduce disability-adjusted life years through precision neurology approaches, addressing a critical need in cerebrovascular care. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated workflows, large-scale data storage for longitudinal cohort analyses, and high-throughput processing of real-world clinical data streams.
cip_definition: Research focused on the evaluation, prevention, treatment, and recovery from vascular diseases of the nervous system resulting from a large number of causes, such as ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, spinal cord ischemia, and spinal cord hemorrhage.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in predictive maintenance strategies for complex vehicle systems through advanced computational modeling and machine learning. Traditional diagnostic methods in vehicle maintenance often rely on reactive or rule-based approaches, leading to unplanned downtime, costly repairs, and suboptimal resource allocation. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-fidelity simulation framework to model wear patterns, failure modes, and component interactions across diverse vehicle subsystems, including hybrid/electric powertrains, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and legacy combustion systems. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte datasets comprising real-world telemetry, sensor logs, maintenance records, and material degradation metrics. Computational methods will include finite element analysis for structural fatigue modeling, computational fluid dynamics for thermal management systems, and graph neural networks to map interdependencies between components. Parallelized training of ensemble machine learning models will enable probabilistic failure forecasting at scale, while sensitivity analyses will identify critical maintenance thresholds. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive maintenance toolkit optimized for commercial repair workflows, validated through partnerships with fleet operators and dealerships. The project aims to reduce diagnostic errors by 25–40% in pilot studies and establish computational benchmarks for lifecycle assessment of emerging vehicle technologies. By integrating HPC-driven insights with technician training modules, this work bridges gaps between data science and hands-on repair practices, fostering innovation in a traditionally hardware-focused field. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and the development of adaptive digital twins for next-generation vehicle architectures.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in vehicle maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The development of advanced synthetic fibers with tailored mechanical, thermal, and functional properties requires a fundamental understanding of how polymer molecular architecture and processing conditions influence hierarchical structure formation. Current experimental approaches face limitations in resolving dynamic, multiscale phenomena—such as stress-induced crystallization during fiber spinning or interfacial interactions between polymers and functional additives like dyes or flame retardants—at atomistic or mesoscopic scales. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and coarse-grained simulations that bridge these gaps. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) modeling the alignment and phase transitions of semi-crystalline polymer chains under shear and elongational flow during fiber extrusion, and (2) characterizing the molecular-scale interactions between cellulose-derived fibers and bio-based dye molecules under varying thermal and pH conditions. Simulations will employ optimized force fields validated against experimental X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy data, with adaptive sampling techniques to accelerate rare event exploration. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks linking processing parameters to fiber morphology and mechanical performance, as well as design rules for enhancing dye uptake in sustainable textile systems. The computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated codes (e.g., LAMMPS, GROMACS) for efficient sampling of 100,000+ atom systems over microsecond timescales. By elucidating structure-property relationships inaccessible through experimentation alone, this work aims to advance the rational design of high-performance fibers for biomedical and environmental applications while reducing reliance on empirical trial-and-error approaches. The requested resources will directly support parameterization efforts requiring 200,000+ core-hours annually for ensemble simulations and machine learning-assisted analysis of multidimensional datasets.
detailed_field: Materials chemistry and materials sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the synthesis, structure and properties of polymers with an emphasis on fibers. Includes instruction in polymer chemistry and synthesis, fiber and polymer physics and physical chemistry, the production, processing and properties of fibrous materials, and chemistry of dyes, finishes, and their processes.

abstract: The rapid evolution of computing demands necessitates innovative approaches to optimize hardware architectures for performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Current challenges in computer hardware design—such as mitigating thermal bottlenecks, enhancing parallelism in multi-core processors, and improving reliability in emerging memory technologies—require computationally intensive modeling and simulation that surpass the capabilities of standard laboratory resources. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in next-generation computer hardware design, focusing on the development and validation of novel architectures for heterogeneous computing systems. The research will employ large-scale finite-element simulations to model thermal and electrical behaviors in advanced processor designs, coupled with discrete-event simulations to evaluate system-level performance under varying workloads. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be integrated to automate design optimization, enabling rapid exploration of parameter spaces for components such as cache hierarchies, interconnect fabrics, and near-memory computing units. The computational workflows will leverage parallel computing frameworks (e.g., MPI and OpenCL) to maximize resource utilization. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal configurations for reducing power consumption in high-density server processors, predictive models for failure rates in non-volatile memory systems, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated hardware benchmarks. These results will directly inform the design of energy-efficient data center infrastructure and edge computing devices, addressing critical gaps in sustainable technology development. By enabling large-scale, multi-physics simulations, the requested HPC allocation will accelerate the prototyping cycle for hardware innovations while reducing reliance on physical fabrication during early design stages. The project aligns with industry priorities for scalable computing solutions and will provide foundational insights for academic curricula in computer architecture and embedded systems engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills to support engineers in designing computer hardware and peripheral systems. Includes instruction in computer systems design, computer architecture, computer electronics, processors, peripherals, testing equipment, and computer manufacturing processes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of precolonial African social and political networks through large-scale spatial and temporal analysis of fragmented historical data. While Africa’s precolonial history is richly documented in diverse sources—including oral traditions, archaeological findings, traveler accounts, and colonial records—these materials remain dispersed, heterogeneous, and challenging to synthesize at continental scales. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to systematically analyze patterns of state formation, trade dynamics, or cultural diffusion across such vast, interconnected geographies and timeframes. This project addresses this gap by developing computational models to integrate and visualize multi-source data, enabling the identification of macrohistorical trends and localized interactions. Using geospatial analysis, network modeling, and machine learning techniques, we will map shifting political boundaries, trade routes, and cultural exchange networks across West and Central Africa from 1000–1800 CE. Key tasks include processing unstructured textual data (e.g., Arabic manuscripts, Portuguese colonial records) via NLP tools, georeferencing archaeological site data, and simulating trade network resilience under environmental stressors. HPC resources are critical for handling the scale of geospatial datasets, running agent-based simulations of social interactions, and training transformer models to detect linguistic and thematic patterns in multilingual corpora. Expected outcomes include an open-access interactive atlas of precolonial African polities, a repository of computationally enhanced historical datasets, and new insights into the longue durée impacts of trans-Saharan and intra-African exchange systems. By bridging computational methods with African historiographic scholarship, this project aims to reshape understandings of precolonial statecraft, mobility, and connectivity while centering African agency in global historical narratives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of one or more peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara (and including the African diasporas overseas) from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to optimize operational efficiency and emissions control in fossil fuel and nuclear power plants, with a focus on addressing thermal stress dynamics in turbine systems and real-time pollutant mitigation. Power plant operations require precise balancing of energy output, equipment longevity, and regulatory compliance, yet existing models often oversimplify transient thermal gradients in turbine blades or rely on static assumptions about combustion byproduct dispersion. The research will employ multiphysics simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning-driven optimization to characterize heat transfer, material fatigue, and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system performance under variable load conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolve 3D transient simulations of turbine blade erosion patterns, coupled with reactor core thermal-hydraulic interactions in nuclear systems, at timescales spanning milliseconds to operational cycles. A parallelized workflow will combine OpenFOAM for turbulent flow modeling, MOOSE Framework for thermomechanical stress analysis, and custom Python-based optimizers to identify operating thresholds that minimize NOx/SOx emissions while maintaining grid stability. Datasets from three operational power plants will validate model outputs. Anticipated outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms for turbine assemblies, dynamic SCR control templates to reduce reagent waste by 15-20%, and generalized thermal stress mitigation protocols applicable to next-generation reactor designs. This work directly supports workforce training in power plant instrumentation and industrial controls by generating open-access simulation case studies for academic use. The requested computing allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10,000+ core-hour simulations, which are infeasible on local clusters due to memory-intensive meshing requirements for rotating machinery geometries. Results will advance scalable computational tools for power generation infrastructure, aligning with national priorities for grid reliability and emissions reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: Critical infrastructure systems, such as power grids, transportation networks, and communication systems, face escalating threats from adversarial cyber-physical attacks and cascading failures exacerbated by interdependencies. Current risk assessment models often oversimplify these interdependencies or lack the computational capacity to simulate large-scale, dynamic scenarios, limiting their utility in real-world mitigation planning. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model and analyze multi-sector infrastructure vulnerabilities under hybrid cyber-physical threat scenarios. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, network dynamics simulations, and machine learning techniques to capture the nonlinear interactions between physical infrastructure components, cyber control systems, and human operator responses. Computational workflows will simulate coordinated attacks on interdependent systems, incorporating stochastic threat vectors, adaptive adversary behaviors, and cascading failure pathways. The HPC environment will enable parallelized scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations, including climate stressors, infrastructure age profiles, and regional interdependency configurations. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for quantifying systemic risks, identifying critical failure cascades, and evaluating the resilience of redundancy configurations. The project will also produce AI-driven threat detection modules capable of processing real-time operational data streams from supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems. By leveraging HPC resources to overcome scale limitations in existing methods, this work aims to advance evidence-based infrastructure protection strategies, providing policymakers and operators with actionable insights for hardening nationally significant assets. The resulting computational framework will be adaptable to emerging threat landscapes and support the development of standardized resilience metrics for cross-sector infrastructure governance.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the design, planning and management of systems and procedures for protecting critical national physical and cyber infrastructure from external threats, including terrorism. Includes instruction in homeland security policy, critical infrastructure policy, information security, matrix vulnerability assessment, threat assessment, physical security, personnel security, operational security, contingency planning, case analyses of specific industries and systems, redundancy planning, emergency and disaster planning, security systems, and intelligence operations.

abstract: Agroecological systems are critical for addressing global food security and environmental sustainability, yet optimizing these systems under dynamic climatic and socioeconomic conditions remains a formidable challenge. Current empirical approaches often fail to capture the complex interactions between crop physiology, soil biogeochemistry, pest dynamics, and farm management decisions at relevant spatiotemporal scales. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to simulate and optimize multifunctional agroecosystems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We will integrate process-based crop models (e.g., APSIM), soil nutrient cycling algorithms, and agent-based representations of pest populations within a unified simulation environment. Machine learning techniques will be applied to parameterize models using heterogeneous datasets spanning long-term field trials, remote sensing products, and IoT sensor networks from experimental farms. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations across diverse climate scenarios (CMIP6 projections) and management regimes to identify robust strategies that balance yield stability, nitrogen use efficiency, and carbon sequestration potential. A novel multi-agent system will simulate farmer decision-making processes under evolving market and policy constraints. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of tradeoffs between regenerative practices and short-term productivity, (2) spatially explicit recommendations for cover crop integration and pest suppression planting schedules, and (3) open-source tools for participatory design of climate-resilient polycultures. By resolving nonlinear interactions between biophysical and human dimensions at unprecedented scales, this work will advance computational agroecology while directly supporting extension programs aimed at reducing synthetic input dependency in row-crop systems. The requested computing resources are essential for managing petabyte-scale simulation outputs and implementing genetic optimization algorithms across high-dimensional parameter spaces.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on agricultural principles and practices that, over the long term, enhance environmental quality, make efficient use of nonrenewable resources, integrate natural biological cycles and controls, and are economically viable and socially responsible; and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of agricultural and environmental problems. Includes instruction in principles of agroecology, crop and soil sciences, entomology, horticulture, animal science, weed science and management, soil fertility and nutrient cycling, applied ecology, agricultural economics, and rangeland ecology and watershed management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing high-performance composite materials for extreme environments by leveraging advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current experimental approaches to designing materials with tailored thermal stability, mechanical strength, and corrosion resistance are limited by the cost and time required to test combinatorial variations in composition, microstructure, and processing conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and phase-field modeling to predict the evolution of material properties under coupled thermal-mechanical-chemical loads. The HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of atomic-scale defect interactions in metal-ceramic interfaces, mesoscale modeling of grain boundary dynamics in polycrystalline alloys, and parametric studies of processing parameters such as sintering temperatures and cooling rates. These simulations will generate datasets linking synthesis conditions to microstructure-property relationships, which will inform machine learning models to accelerate materials discovery. The outcomes will directly support experimental efforts to develop next-generation composites for energy storage systems and high-temperature industrial applications, reducing reliance on trial-and-error approaches. By resolving atomic-scale mechanisms of interfacial degradation and phase transformations, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of materials behavior in aggressive environments while providing actionable design guidelines for industry partners. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the high computational cost of ab initio calculations across multiple alloy systems, the memory demands of 3D phase-field simulations at experimentally relevant scales, and the parallel processing required for sensitivity analyses across thousands of parameter combinations. Successful completion of this project will establish a validated computational pipeline for accelerated materials development, with potential applications in sustainable manufacturing and decarbonization technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and materials science principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials and related processes used in manufacturing in a wide variety of settings; the synthesis of new industrial materials, including marrying and bonding composites; analysis of materials requirements and specifications; and related problems of system design dependent on materials factors.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize rehabilitation program delivery and resource allocation in correctional facilities through predictive modeling and simulation. Correctional systems face persistent challenges in balancing security, rehabilitation outcomes, and operational costs, yet lack data-driven tools to model complex interactions between staffing patterns, facility logistics, and inmate behavioral dynamics. Our research addresses this gap by integrating anonymized historical inmate records, facility operation datasets, and psychological assessment metrics into a novel agent-based model (ABM) that simulates decision pathways for both incarcerated individuals and administrative staff. The ABM will be coupled with machine learning classifiers trained on longitudinal recidivism data to evaluate how adjustments in program scheduling, counselor-to-inmate ratios, and educational resource distribution affect projected rehabilitation success rates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning 10+ years from three state correctional departments, run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations testing 50,000+ policy scenarios, and train deep reinforcement learning models that identify optimal intervention timing. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that quantifies trade-offs between budgetary constraints and evidence-based rehabilitation practices, as well as generative models capable of projecting facility-specific outcomes under staffing shortages or population surges. By translating behavioral theories and operational data into computational parameters, this work establishes a methodological bridge between correctional psychology and systems engineering. The resulting tools will be validated through partnerships with three mid-sized correctional institutions, with potential to reduce trial-and-error policy implementation while maintaining compliance with ethical constraints on inmate data usage. This interdisciplinary approach demonstrates how computational social science methodologies can address pressing operational challenges in non-traditional HPC domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan and manage institutional facilities and programs for housing and rehabilitating prisoners in the public and/or private sectors. Includes instruction in the principles and practice of correction, facilities planning and management, safety and security, social and health services, staff and inmate management, budgeting, communication skills, correctional psychology, and applications to specific types of correctional facilities approaches.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for sustainable apparel design, focusing on optimizing textile reuse and waste reduction through predictive modeling. The global fashion industry faces escalating environmental challenges, with textile waste accounting for 9% of annual microplastic pollution and over 92 million tons of landfill contributions. Current approaches to circular design remain constrained by manual processes and limited scalability in analyzing complex material interactions. Our research addresses this gap by developing a novel computational framework that integrates lifecycle assessment data, textile degradation models, and consumer behavior patterns to simulate multi-stage reuse pathways for post-consumer garments. The project employs finite element analysis to model mechanical wear across diverse fabric types, combined with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to predict aesthetic degradation under varying environmental conditions. Agent-based modeling will simulate market dynamics of textile recovery systems at urban scales, requiring parallel processing of 10^6+ agent interactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for designers to quantify the environmental impact of design choices during prototyping phases, potentially reducing sample production waste by 30-50% in partner manufacturing trials. The computational intensity of coupling physical simulations with socioeconomic datasets necessitates HPC capabilities for both training deep learning models on terabyte-scale material databases and running Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses across design parameters. By bridging computational materials science with sustainable design praxis, this work establishes a foundation for data-driven circular economy strategies in apparel production while advancing methodological synergies between HPC applications and creative industries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in apparel and textiles, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the electronic structure and reactivity of polynuclear transition metal complexes, which are central to catalysis, energy storage, and quantum materials. While experimental studies have characterized key properties of these systems, their intricate bonding networks, spin states, and dynamic behavior under reactive conditions remain poorly resolved at the molecular level. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform multiscale quantum chemical calculations on polynuclear clusters containing transition metals (e.g., Fe, Mn, Co) with mixed-valence states and non-innocent ligands. Density functional theory (DFT) and post-Hartree-Fock methods (e.g., CASSCF, NEVPT2) will be used to model ground and excited electronic states, spin-coupling mechanisms, and ligand-field effects. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations will probe solvent-mediated reaction pathways and transient intermediates in catalytic cycles. The computational workflow will integrate structure optimization, vibrational analysis, and electronic property prediction using software packages such as ORCA and NWChem, with particular emphasis on parallelized algorithms for large active spaces (>50 orbitals). HPC resources are essential due to the high computational cost of correlated electronic structure methods for systems exceeding 100 atoms and the need for statistical sampling across conformational ensembles. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for redox potentials and magnetic exchange parameters in multinuclear systems, (2) mechanistic insights into ligand-assisted electron transfer processes, and (3) design principles for stabilizing reactive intermediates in inorganic frameworks. This work will directly inform ongoing synthetic efforts in our laboratory to develop earth-abundant catalysts for CO2 reduction and water oxidation. By bridging theoretical and experimental inorganic chemistry, the project aims to advance rational design strategies for functional molecular materials while contributing benchmark datasets for validating computational methodologies in open-shell transition metal chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the elements and their compounds, other than the hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Includes instruction in the characterization and synthesis of non-carbon molecules, including their structure and their bonding, conductivity, and reactive properties; research techniques such as spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and photoelectron analysis; and the study of specific compounds, such as transition metals, and compounds composed of inorganic and organic molecules.

abstract: The increasing burden of vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases in resource-limited regions underscores the urgent need for advanced computational tools to model complex disease dynamics and optimize intervention strategies. Current approaches often fail to capture the multiscale interactions between pathogens, vectors, human populations, and environmental drivers, limiting predictive accuracy. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative, spatially explicit models of disease transmission for pathogens such as malaria, dengue, and chikungunya. The research will combine agent-based modeling, machine learning, and genomic epidemiology to simulate transmission dynamics across heterogeneous landscapes, incorporating real-world data on vector ecology, climate variability, host immunity, and human mobility. Key computational challenges include parameterizing large-scale models with genomic datasets from pathogen surveillance, optimizing spatiotemporal resolution for regional forecasts, and quantifying uncertainty in intervention outcomes. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations to explore scenarios such as vaccine deployment strategies, insecticide resistance evolution, and climate-driven shifts in vector habitats. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to identify high-risk transmission hotspots, evaluate the durability of vaccine-induced immunity, and prioritize targeted vector control measures. By integrating high-resolution genomic and environmental data, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of pathogen adaptation and spillover risks. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to support public health decision-making in endemic regions. This project directly addresses critical gaps in tropical disease management, with potential to reduce morbidity and mortality through data-driven, precision public health interventions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: Agricultural systems face increasing pressure to adapt to climate variability while maintaining productivity and sustainability. Current challenges include optimizing crop yields under fluctuating environmental conditions, improving pest and disease resistance in staple crops, and enhancing soil health management. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-resolution computational model integrating genomic, phenotypic, and environmental data to predict adaptive traits in key crops under diverse climate scenarios. The research will leverage machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-omic datasets (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics) from wheat and soybean cultivars, combined with spatially explicit soil composition data and historical climate records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of sequencing data, train neural networks on genotype-environment-phenotype associations, and run ensemble climate simulations at regional scales. The computational workflow will employ parallelized genomic prediction models, Bayesian inference for trait heritability analysis, and agent-based simulations of pest population dynamics under projected temperature and precipitation regimes. Expected outcomes include identifying genetic markers linked to drought tolerance, generating risk maps for emerging crop pathogens, and optimizing fertilizer application protocols using reinforcement learning. This work will provide actionable insights for breeding programs and precision agriculture, enabling data-driven decisions to improve crop resilience. By quantifying trade-offs between yield maximization and resource conservation, the project aims to advance sustainable agricultural practices while addressing food security challenges. The proposed HPC allocation will directly support scalable analyses that are infeasible on local clusters, reducing model training times from weeks to days and enabling high-fidelity simulations of agricultural systems across multiple spatial and temporal scales.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general principles and practice of agricultural research and production and that may prepare individuals to apply this knowledge to the solution of practical agricultural problems. Includes instruction in basic animal, plant, and soil science; animal husbandry and plant cultivation; soil conservation; and agricultural operations such as farming, ranching, and agricultural business.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven adaptive support system designed to optimize the workflow of teaching assistants (TAs) in large, heterogeneous classrooms. While TAs play a critical role in scaling personalized instruction, they face challenges in efficiently addressing diverse student needs, particularly in STEM courses with high enrollment and variable learner backgrounds. Existing tools for TA support are limited to generic workflow automation, lacking the capacity to dynamically adapt to real-time classroom data or individual student-TA interactions. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that integrates multimodal data—including student forum queries, assignment submissions, and biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking during office hours)—to generate context-aware recommendations for TAs. The system will employ transformer-based models fine-tuned on domain-specific educational corpora and reinforcement learning algorithms to personalize TA intervention strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training these models on large-scale, privacy-preserved datasets spanning multiple institutions (targeting 500,000+ student-TA interactions) and for simulating classroom scenarios through agent-based modeling. Computational challenges include real-time processing of unstructured educational data streams, optimizing low-latency inference for deployment in live classrooms, and ensuring algorithmic fairness across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive TA support, validated through randomized controlled trials in 15 partner courses, and a novel evaluation metric quantifying the impact of AI-augmented TA interventions on both student learning outcomes and TA workload equity. This work bridges educational practice, human-computer interaction, and machine learning, offering a scalable solution to enhance instructional support systems without requiring structural reforms to existing TA training programs.
cip_definition: Any teaching assistant/aide program, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing resource allocation and risk mitigation in large-scale, multi-stakeholder projects under uncertainty. Traditional project management tools often struggle to handle the dynamic interdependencies, nonlinear cost-time trade-offs, and probabilistic risk profiles inherent in complex initiatives such as infrastructure development or enterprise digital transformation. The research will employ agent-based modeling and Monte Carlo simulations to capture emergent behaviors in project networks, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to identify adaptive resource allocation strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process heterogeneous datasets spanning project schedules, workforce capacities, supplier reliability metrics, and environmental variables, while maintaining computational feasibility for real-time scenario testing. The computational architecture will leverage parallel processing to simultaneously evaluate thousands of project pathways, incorporating stochastic demand fluctuations and constraint variations. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that quantifies the cascading impacts of resource allocation choices across temporal and organizational boundaries. This work will advance project management practice by enabling data-driven negotiation of competing stakeholder priorities, proactive identification of critical path vulnerabilities, and dynamic rebalancing of human capital investments. The resulting models will be validated against historical project failure cases and industry partner datasets, with particular attention to improving success rates for projects exceeding $100M in budget. By integrating computational social science methods with operations research principles, this research aims to establish new benchmarks for predictive analytics in complex project governance.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply quantitative and qualitative knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to manage projects in a wide range of fields and occupations. Includes instruction in project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in construction project management and finishing quality through the development of advanced computational models that optimize resource allocation, material performance, and defect detection. Construction projects face persistent challenges, including delays from dynamic scheduling conflicts, suboptimal material curing conditions, and human error in manual inspections. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning (ML), finite element analysis (FEA), and real-time sensor data analytics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process large datasets from IoT-enabled construction sites, including thermal, humidity, and stress data from embedded sensors, alongside imagery from drones and LiDAR systems. ML models will predict material curing times under variable environmental conditions, while FEA simulations will assess structural integrity of finishing materials under load scenarios. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize workforce and equipment scheduling under uncertainty. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing to handle 3D point clouds for automated defect detection, coupled with Monte Carlo simulations to quantify project risk. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for real-time decision support, reducing project overruns by 15–20% and minimizing material waste through precision curing protocols. The project will also generate open-access datasets of annotated construction defects and material performance metrics, advancing computational methodologies in a field traditionally reliant on empirical practices. By bridging gaps between construction management theory and data-driven automation, this work aims to establish scalable benchmarks for sustainable, high-quality building practices.
