The requested HPC resources will enable the iterative training of deep neural networks, large-scale parametric simulations, and the integration of heterogeneous data streams into a unified digital twin platform for construction lifecycle management.
cip_title: Building/ Construction Finishing, Management, and Inspection, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in building/construction finishing, management, and inspection, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance pharmacoeconomic and policy analyses critical to optimizing medication access, pharmacy service delivery, and regulatory decision-making. A key challenge in pharmacy administration is modeling the multi-faceted impacts of drug pricing policies, insurance reimbursement structures, and healthcare system constraints on patient outcomes and costs. Existing approaches often oversimplify dynamic interactions between stakeholders (e.g., patients, providers, payers, manufacturers) or fail to account for large-scale real-world data, limiting predictive accuracy and policy relevance. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework integrating electronic health records, insurance claims, and drug supply chain data to model the cascading effects of policy changes on medication utilization, health disparities, and system-wide expenditures. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions across diverse demographic and geographic scenarios, requiring parallelized parameter sweeps and machine learning-driven sensitivity analyses. Additionally, we will apply natural language processing to analyze regulatory documents and public comment databases, identifying trends in policy implementation barriers and stakeholder concerns. HPC resources will enable the processing of terabyte-scale datasets and reduce runtime for iterative model calibration from months to days. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source policy simulation toolkit for evaluating proposed legislation, plus evidence-based recommendations to streamline drug approval processes and reduce administrative burdens in pharmacy practice. By quantifying trade-offs between cost containment and equitable access, this work will directly inform state and federal agencies, healthcare organizations, and pharmacy leaders in designing data-driven policies that balance economic sustainability with patient-centered care.
cip_title: Pharmacy Administration and Pharmacy Policy and Regulatory Affairs
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply managerial, social, and economic sciences to the study and management of the distribution and use of pharmaceutical products and the provision of pharmacy services. Includes instruction in research design and methods, statistics, social and organizational behavior, pharmacoeconomics, management of pharmacy services, outcomes research, product planning and reimbursement, cost-benefit analysis, drug marketing, pharmacy and pharmaceutics law and regulation, risk assessment, and organization of the health care system.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods in architectural design, specifically targeting the optimization of adaptive urban microclimates through real-time, multi-physics simulations. Traditional design workflows struggle to integrate dynamic environmental factors—such as wind patterns, solar exposure, and thermal flux—into iterative design processes, particularly at the scale of dense urban neighborhoods. Current software tools are limited by simplified models or long computation times, hindering architects’ ability to explore complex, data-driven solutions for climate resilience. This project addresses this gap by developing a parametric framework that couples generative design algorithms with high-fidelity fluid dynamics and energy modeling, enabled by HPC parallelization. The computational approach will involve deploying finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations across distributed GPU clusters to evaluate thousands of design variants under varying climate scenarios. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on simulation outputs to accelerate feedback loops between design iteration and performance analysis. Key outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating microclimate interactions within architectural and urban design workflows, validated against physical-scale wind tunnel and thermal data. The research aims to establish scalable methodologies for embedding real-time environmental feedback into design processes, with implications for reducing urban heat island effects, improving energy efficiency, and enhancing pedestrian comfort. By bridging architectural design with advanced computational modeling, this work advances the integration of sustainability metrics into early-stage design decisions, offering a template for resource-efficient, climate-responsive urban development.
cip_definition: An advanced program of study for architects and related professionals that focuses on theoretical and practical issues in architecture and integrates digital technologies into architectural design, fabrication, and construction. Includes instruction in architectural history and urban theory, 3-D digital technologies, construction, design and fabrication methods, and sustainable practices in architecture.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems demands advanced methodologies to optimize diagnostics, maintenance, and repair processes. Traditional approaches, which rely heavily on manual inspection and static failure prediction models, often lack the precision to address dynamic operational stressors such as thermal fluctuations, mechanical wear, and transient electrical loads. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate and analyze failure mechanisms in electrical equipment, enabling data-driven predictive maintenance strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will employ multiphysics simulations—integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal behavior—to replicate real-world operating conditions of critical components like circuit boards, motor drives, and power distribution systems. These simulations will generate large datasets characterizing component degradation under diverse stress profiles. Machine learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), will then be trained on this data to identify early failure signatures and predict remaining useful life. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of iterative simulations and optimizing hyperparameters for the machine learning models. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive maintenance toolkit that reduces unplanned downtime in industrial and commercial electrical systems, as well as actionable insights into material and design improvements for fault-tolerant equipment. This work will directly inform curriculum enhancements in electrical repair technology programs, equipping technicians with advanced diagnostic proficiencies aligned with Industry 4.0 standards. By bridging computational engineering with applied repair methodologies, the project aims to elevate the precision and sustainability of electrical infrastructure management.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical gap in understanding how interdisciplinary humanities training influences ethical decision-making patterns among healthcare professionals during high-stakes clinical scenarios. Traditional medical education often siloes ethics and humanities content, limiting opportunities to model their dynamic integration into real-world practice. To bridge this divide, we propose developing a novel computational framework that combines natural language processing (NLP), multi-agent reinforcement learning, and immersive virtual environment simulations. The research will analyze 15,000+ historical clinical ethics case records and contemporaneous educational materials using transformer-based models to identify latent patterns in ethical reasoning development. Concurrently, we will build parameterized simulations of complex care scenarios (e.g., end-of-life decisions, resource triage) within a high-fidelity virtual platform, training agent models on heterogeneous ethical frameworks derived from philosophical, legal, and cultural perspectives. By implementing distributed deep learning across GPU-accelerated nodes, the system will simulate over 100,000 provider-patient interaction variants while tracking decision trajectories under competing ethical constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping relationships between humanities education content and observed clinical ethical behaviors, 2) validated predictive models of educational intervention impacts on decision-making quality, and 3) an open-source simulation environment for stress-testing ethics curricula against emergent biomedical challenges. This work directly advances priorities in health professions education by creating scalable computational tools to optimize the integration of humanistic principles into clinical training, ultimately aiming to reduce moral injury among providers and improve patient outcomes through ethically informed care. The project's HPC requirements center on large-scale language model fine-tuning, massively parallel simulation runs, and real-time rendering of immersive ethical dilemma scenarios.
cip_title: Health Professions Education, Ethics, and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health professions education, ethics, and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in understanding the evolutionary and ecological dynamics of ancient ecosystems through computational paleontology. A central challenge in paleobiological research lies in integrating large, heterogeneous datasets—including fossil occurrence records, geochemical proxies, and stratigraphic data—to model species interactions, biogeographic patterns, and responses to environmental perturbations across deep time. Current computational limitations restrict the scalability of probabilistic models and simulations, particularly when analyzing high-resolution, continent-scale datasets spanning millions of years. To overcome these barriers, we propose a multi-tiered computational approach. First, Bayesian hierarchical models will be implemented to quantify uncertainties in fossil preservation biases and temporal correlations among extinction events. Second, agent-based simulations will reconstruct paleocommunity dynamics under varying climatic and tectonic scenarios, parameterized by geochemical and lithostratigraphic data. These simulations will integrate GPU-accelerated algorithms to handle complex spatial interactions among species and abiotic factors. Third, machine learning workflows will classify microfossil assemblages from 3D µCT scan datasets, automating taxonomic identifications while accounting for taphonomic distortion. The requested HPC resources will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets, reduce runtime for iterative model testing, and support high-dimensional visualization of paleoecological networks. Anticipated outcomes include novel frameworks for quantifying extinction selectivity in mass extinction intervals, spatially explicit models of Mesozoic vertebrate dispersal, and open-source tools for microfossil data processing. By resolving computational bottlenecks, this work will advance predictive capacity for ecosystem resilience under anthropogenic climate change while establishing scalable methods for synthesizing paleontological and geological data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of extinct life forms and associated fossil remains, and the reconstruction and analysis of ancient life forms, ecosystems, and geologic processes. Includes instruction in sedimentation and fossilization processes, fossil chemistry, evolutionary biology, paleoecology, paleoclimatology, trace fossils, micropaleontology, invertebrate paleontology, vertebrate paleontology, paleobotany, field research methods, and laboratory research and conservation methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in computational research on Bengali (Bangla) linguistics, with a focus on dialectal variation and historical philology. Despite Bengali’s status as the seventh most spoken language globally, large-scale quantitative analyses of its regional dialects and historical text corpora remain underdeveloped due to computational limitations. The research problem centers on mapping phonetic, syntactic, and lexical divergences across Bengali dialects and tracing their evolution through digitized pre-modern texts, tasks requiring intensive processing of unstructured linguistic data. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for low-resource languages, to analyze spoken and written corpora spanning six major dialects and texts from the 15th–19th centuries. Key methods involve training dialect classification models using phonetic transcriptions, applying diachronic word embedding algorithms to track semantic shifts, and simulating language change through agent-based models. These workflows demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including audio recordings, annotated manuscripts, and lexical databases, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable efficient execution of distributed training for deep learning models, large-scale text normalization, and phonetic alignment across heterogeneous data types. Expected outcomes include the first comprehensive digital atlas of Bengali dialect boundaries, a diachronic corpus with semantic change annotations, and open-access tools for low-resource NLP applications. This work will advance scholarly understanding of Bengali’s linguistic history, support preservation efforts for endangered dialects, and provide computational frameworks applicable to other under-resourced languages. By bridging gaps between traditional philology and modern NLP, the project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven humanities research in Bengali studies while contributing methodologies to the broader field of computational linguistics.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Bengali language (Bangla) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Norwegian dialectal variation and its historical evolution, a critical gap in current Scandinavian linguistics research. Norwegian dialects exhibit exceptional diversity due to geographical, social, and historical factors, yet large-scale, data-driven studies remain limited by the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous linguistic data. The proposed research will develop and apply machine learning models to analyze multi-modal datasets, including digitized historical texts (e.g., Old Norse manuscripts, 19th-century records), contemporary spoken corpora, and dialect atlas annotations. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques for morphological tagging, syntactic parsing, and phonetic feature extraction, with geospatial modeling to map dialect boundaries and their shifts over time. A key innovation involves training transformer-based models on non-standardized orthographies and oral transcripts to identify patterns in grammaticalization and lexical borrowing across regions. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale of data (≥50 TB of audio and text), parallelizing feature extraction across thousands of dialect samples, and optimizing neural architectures for low-resource language scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible Norwegian Dialect Evolution Repository, computational tools for automatic dialect classification, and quantitative insights into the impact of language policy (e.g., Nynorsk vs. Bokmål) on regional speech practices. This work will directly support endangered dialect preservation efforts and inform technology applications such as Norwegian-language speech recognition systems adaptable to diverse dialects. By bridging traditional philological methods with computational linguistics, the project aims to establish a replicable framework for data-intensive research in minority language studies.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Norwegian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Construction projects are complex systems influenced by dynamic variables such as weather patterns, supply chain disruptions, labor availability, and regulatory constraints. Traditional project management tools often fail to account for the interdependencies and stochastic nature of these factors, leading to cost overruns, delays, and suboptimal resource allocation. This research proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model construction project workflows under uncertainty, integrating real-time data streams with predictive analytics to optimize scheduling, risk mitigation, and sustainability outcomes. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute agent-based simulations of construction site operations, machine learning algorithms for delay prediction, and multi-objective optimization techniques to balance competing priorities across cost, time, and environmental impact. Key computational challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets from IoT sensors, historical project records, and climate models while maintaining the temporal granularity required for actionable insights. The research will implement parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify systemic risks and evaluate mitigation strategies across thousands of simulated project scenarios. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that dynamically updates resource allocation plans based on evolving site conditions, probabilistic completion timelines, and carbon footprint projections. By bridging computational science with construction management practices, this work aims to establish new methodologies for adaptive project governance in the context of climate change and global supply chain volatility. The HPC infrastructure is critical for achieving the necessary scale and speed to model multi-year projects with hourly resolution, enabling practitioners to test interventions in silico before implementation. This interdisciplinary approach advances both computational capabilities in business operations and the practical application of digital twin technologies in construction ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution and efficacy of digital communication strategies in lay ministry training programs, focusing on their role in fostering community resilience and spiritual engagement. While lay ministry has historically relied on in-person pastoral practices, the rise of hybrid and fully remote ministry models—accelerated by global shifts in communication norms—demands a computational approach to evaluate how digital tools reshape theological education, congregational dynamics, and cross-cultural outreach. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in pastoral communication effectiveness across diverse demographics, particularly in underrepresented or geographically dispersed communities, where traditional ministry frameworks may lack scalability. Using natural language processing (NLP), the project will analyze multimodal datasets (text, audio, and video) from lay ministry training sessions, public sermons, and virtual congregational interactions to model how theological concepts are linguistically adapted across contexts. Agent-based modeling will simulate community response to different communication strategies, incorporating variables such as cultural literacy, socioeconomic factors, and digital access disparities. These computational methods will enable the identification of adaptive frameworks for training lay ministers in technologically mediated environments. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of annotated ministry communication datasets, predictive models for optimizing pastoral training curricula, and evidence-based recommendations for equitable digital ministry practices. By bridging computational linguistics, social simulation, and practical theology, this research aims to advance the capacity of lay ministry programs to address 21st-century spiritual needs while preserving theological coherence across rapidly changing communicative landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained individuals to serve as lay pastors, religious educators, youth leaders, and other professional positions open to the laity in local churches and other settings. Includes instruction in bible studies, theology, spirituality, pastoral counseling, foundations of ministry, effective communication, and church leadership.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing the dynamic interplay between cultural heritage structures and evolving urban microclimates, a challenge at the intersection of architectural preservation, climatology, and data-driven design. Traditional preservation methods often rely on static models, failing to account for real-time environmental stressors such as particulate pollution, humidity fluctuations, and thermal expansion in dense urban contexts. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale interactions between historical building materials, localized weather patterns, and anthropogenic factors over decadal timescales. The computational approach integrates 3D laser scan datasets of heritage sites with regional climate projections, employing finite element analysis (FEA) for material stress modeling and agent-based systems to simulate cumulative human impact. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify non-linear degradation patterns and optimize preservation strategies through iterative scenario testing. By enabling predictive analysis of structural vulnerabilities under diverse environmental conditions, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for adaptive preservation planning. The anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for heritage stakeholders and novel metrics for quantifying preservation efficacy in urban systems. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to manage the concurrent processing of terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, real-time fluid dynamics simulations, and parametric optimization tasks that exceed the capabilities of conventional architectural software. This work bridges computational science and cultural heritage management, advancing methodological innovation in a specialized niche of architectural research with implications for sustainable urban development and climate resilience planning.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the cognitive and sociolinguistic impacts of neural language model (NLM)-generated feedback on second language (L2) writing development, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between learner behavior, linguistic output, and automated feedback systems. While NLMs like GPT-4 are increasingly integrated into language learning tools, their influence on learners’ metalinguistic awareness, error correction patterns, and long-term linguistic development remains understudied. The research addresses this gap by analyzing longitudinal datasets of L2 writers (N=1,200+) engaging with NLM-powered writing assistants, focusing on how feedback personalization strategies affect syntactic complexity, pragmatic competence, and identity negotiation in multilingual contexts. Computational methods include (1) transformer-based fine-tuning of feedback generation models using domain-specific corpora, (2) multilevel Bayesian regression to quantify learning trajectories across proficiency levels, and (3) agent-based modeling of classroom-scale feedback adoption dynamics. HPC resources are critical for parallel processing of multimodal interaction logs (text, edit histories, eye-tracking) and for training custom embeddings that capture cross-linguistic transfer patterns among typologically diverse L1-L2 pairs (e.g., Mandarin-English vs. Arabic-German). Expected outcomes include (a) a framework for optimizing NLM feedback architectures to balance error correction efficacy with cognitive load management, (b) identification of threshold effects in model-driven language development, and (c) open-source tools for simulating feedback scenarios in low-resource pedagogical contexts. The project advances applied linguistics research by providing empirical foundations for ethical AI integration in language education while contributing novel methods for large-scale analysis of human-AI interaction patterns. Resulting datasets and computational models will be made available through an interactive repository designed to support research in adaptive educational technologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language-related concerns in the everyday world, including language education, acquisition of first and additional languages, discourse analysis, language assessment, literacy, and language policy and planning. Includes instruction in linguistic theory; language teaching and learning; discourse analysis; language and cognition; and language, culture, and identity.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems necessitates advanced methods to optimize equipment reliability, maintenance protocols, and failure prediction. Traditional approaches to equipment diagnostics and repair often rely on reactive strategies, leading to unplanned downtime and inefficiencies in industrial and commercial settings. This project proposes a computational research initiative to develop predictive maintenance frameworks and fault-detection algorithms tailored to electrical and electronic systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the study will simulate diverse operational scenarios—including voltage fluctuations, thermal stress, and component degradation—to model failure mechanisms in power distribution systems, industrial control circuits, and consumer electronics. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and real-world sensor data to identify early warning signs of equipment malfunction. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will further analyze heat dissipation patterns in densely packed circuits, informing design improvements for enhanced longevity. The scale of these simulations, requiring parallel processing of multi-physics interactions and large datasets, mandates access to HPC infrastructure for feasible execution. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms capable of reducing equipment downtime by 20–30%, optimized maintenance schedules validated through probabilistic risk assessment models, and data-driven guidelines for component redesign. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops for repair technicians and open-access datasets to bridge gaps between computational research and applied repair practices. This work directly supports the educational mission of Electrical/Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair programs by integrating computational tools into technician training, fostering a workforce adept at leveraging advanced analytics in equipment maintenance. The project’s computational outputs will provide a scalable framework for adaptive repair strategies in evolving smart grid and IoT-enabled environments.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of electrical and electronic system design by developing advanced computational workflows optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. Modern electrical drafting and CAD/CADD applications face challenges in simulating large-scale circuits, optimizing component layouts for energy efficiency, and validating designs against multi-domain constraints (e.g., thermal, electromagnetic). Current software tools often lack the scalability to handle intricate industrial systems, leading to time-consuming iterative processes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating parallelized electromagnetic field solvers, machine learning-assisted routing algorithms, and distributed multi-physics simulation frameworks. The HPC resources will enable rapid evaluation of thousands of design permutations for power distribution networks and embedded systems, with automated constraint checking against industry standards (e.g., IPC, IEEE). Key innovations include GPU-accelerated parasitic extraction for high-frequency circuits and topology optimization algorithms adapted for manufacturability in printed circuit board (PCB) design. Expected outcomes include a prototype computational pipeline capable of reducing design iteration cycles by 40-60% for complex systems, validated through case studies involving smart grid components and industrial automation controllers. The project will additionally produce benchmark datasets for AI-driven layout optimization, bridging gaps between traditional drafting practices and emerging computational design paradigms. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish new best practices for resource-efficient electrical CAD workflows while enhancing educational materials for next-generation drafting technicians. Success metrics will focus on computational efficiency gains, design error reduction rates, and scalability demonstrations for systems exceeding 10,000 components.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Drafting and Electrical/ Electronics CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working schematics and representations in support of electrical/electronic engineers, computer engineers, and related professionals. Includes instruction in basic electronics, electrical systems and computer layouts; electrode-mechanical drafting; manufacturing circuitry; computer-aided drafting (CAD); and electrical systems specification interpretation.

abstract: The safe and effective administration of anesthesia requires precise pharmacological decision-making under dynamic physiological conditions. However, current protocols for anesthetic dosing and perioperative monitoring rely on population-level models that inadequately account for interpatient variability in drug metabolism, comorbid risk factors, and acute pathophysiological shifts. This project seeks to develop patient-specific pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models to predict individualized responses to anesthetic and analgesic agents, with the goal of reducing adverse events such as intraoperative awareness, hemodynamic instability, and postoperative delirium. Using anonymized electronic health record data from 15,000+ surgical cases, we will implement a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling of drug-receptor interactions, machine learning (ML)-driven feature extraction from multimodal physiological time-series data, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to quantify uncertainty in rare-event scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for three core tasks: (1) parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of anesthetic drug distributions across heterogeneous tissue compartments, (2) training recurrent neural networks on high-frequency vital sign waveforms (200 Hz sampling rate), and (3) real-time sensitivity analyses during model validation against prospective cases. The resulting framework will enable probabilistic forecasting of drug effects at 30-second intraoperative intervals while integrating emergent covariates such as blood loss or allergic response. Anticipated outcomes include clinically validated decision support tools for nurse anesthetists, optimized dosing algorithms for special populations (e.g., obese patients, geriatrics), and open-source simulation modules for anesthesia training programs. By addressing the computational barriers to personalized dynamic modeling in perioperative care, this work directly aligns with the program’s focus on advancing evidence-based practice through technological innovation in patient assessment and crisis management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: Marine microbial communities play a critical role in regulating biogeochemical cycles and ecosystem health in coastal and polar environments, yet their responses to multi-stressor interactions—such as warming, acidification, and deoxygenation—remain poorly resolved at regional scales. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution, three-dimensional coupled physical-biogeochemical model to simulate microbial dynamics and metabolic processes in rapidly changing polar coastal systems. The research will focus on the Western Antarctic Peninsula, a region experiencing accelerated warming and ice loss, where shifts in microbial composition could disrupt carbon export and nutrient cycling. A novel aspect of the computational approach involves integrating genomic and metagenomic datasets with a reactive transport model to parameterize taxon-specific metabolic traits and their plasticity under environmental stressors. The model will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve fine-scale heterogeneity in microbial habitats, such as ice-ocean interfaces and stratified water columns, while capturing basin-scale circulation patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct ensemble simulations across decadal timescales, evaluate uncertainty in trait-based parameterizations, and resolve non-linear interactions between physical drivers and microbial feedbacks. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how microbial community structure modulates carbon sequestration efficiency under future climate scenarios and identification of tipping points in coastal polar ecosystems. The resulting open-source model framework will provide a community resource for predicting microbial-mediated biogeochemical shifts in other climate-sensitive regions. By quantifying linkages between microbial resilience and ecosystem function, this work aims to inform strategies for monitoring biodiversity loss and its cascading effects on marine food webs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: Professional diving operations face significant challenges in safety, efficiency, and environmental adaptability due to the dynamic, high-risk nature of underwater environments. Current approaches to equipment design, decompression protocols, and emergency response planning rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the complexities of real-world diving scenarios, including turbulent flow interactions, physiological responses to hyperbaric conditions, and equipment failure modes. This project proposes a computational framework to address these limitations by developing high-resolution simulations of diver-environment systems using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Multiphysics models will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for water-current interactions, finite element analysis (FEA) for equipment stress testing under extreme pressures, and machine learning (ML) to predict decompression risks based on diver physiology and environmental variables. These simulations will be validated against empirical data from controlled diving trials and sensor-equipped gear. The HPC infrastructure is essential to resolve microsecond-scale fluid-structure interactions in turbulent flows, optimize neural networks for real-time risk assessment, and perform Monte Carlo analyses of rare but critical failure events. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools for decompression sickness mitigation, evidence-based protocols for salvage and rescue operations, and digital twins of diving systems to test novel equipment configurations. The results will advance safety standards in commercial and scientific diving while providing immersive simulation modules for diver training programs. By openly sharing optimized computational workflows, this project will establish a foundation for data-driven innovation in underwater technical operations, benefiting both academic research and industry practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to function as professional deep-water or scuba divers, diving instructors, or diving support personnel. Includes instruction in the use of diving equipment and related specialized gear; diving safety procedures; operation and maintenance of underwater life-support systems; underwater communication systems; decompression systems; underwater salvage; exploration, rescue, and photography; and installation and fitting of underwater mechanical systems and their maintenance, repair or demolition.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing undersea sensor network performance within dynamic and contested maritime environments. Modern Undersea Warfare (USW) systems rely on distributed sensor arrays to detect, classify, and track submerged threats, but current simulation frameworks struggle to model the interplay of acoustic propagation, environmental variability, and adversarial counter-detection tactics at operationally relevant scales. This project aims to develop a high-fidelity computational model integrating real-time oceanographic data, adaptive signal processing algorithms, and probabilistic threat behavior patterns to enhance sensor deployment strategies and operational resilience. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute massively parallelized simulations of multi-physics scenarios, including thermocline fluctuations, biologics-generated noise, and coordinated swarm threats. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize sensor placement and fusion algorithms under constraints of energy efficiency and stealth requirements. By coupling hydrodynamic models with reinforcement learning architectures, the framework will enable autonomous adaptation to evolving battlefield conditions. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for rapid sensor network reconfiguration in response to environmental shifts or adversarial interference, as well as predictive metrics for system effectiveness across diverse ocean basins. This work bridges gaps between traditional undersea systems engineering and emerging computational decision-support paradigms, offering a novel approach to maintaining acoustic superiority in increasingly complex undersea domains. The requested HPC allocation will support parameter space exploration across 10^6+ scenario permutations, enabling statistically robust conclusions about system performance thresholds. Successful implementation will provide the USW community with a scalable tool for evaluating next-generation sensor concepts while informing platform acquisition and doctrine development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, engineering design and military concepts that govern the operational employment of underwater sensors and weapons systems. Includes instruction in acoustics, electrical, and mechanical engineering; mathematics; meteorology; oceanography; physics; operations analysis; human factors; computer science; and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing industrial production systems under dynamic constraints, with a focus on enhancing operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and environmental sustainability. Industrial management faces persistent challenges in balancing competing objectives such as minimizing energy consumption, reducing waste, maintaining product quality, and meeting fluctuating demand. Traditional analytical methods often fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these factors, particularly in large-scale, multi-stage production environments. To address this gap, the research proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining discrete-event simulation, multi-objective optimization, and machine learning. The computational model will simulate complex manufacturing workflows, incorporating real-world variables such as equipment failure rates, workforce scheduling, and supply chain disruptions. Parallelized genetic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning techniques will be employed to identify Pareto-optimal solutions for resource allocation, while stochastic optimization methods will address uncertainties in demand and material availability. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these computations to realistic industrial scenarios, enabling the analysis of millions of potential operational configurations across distributed manufacturing nodes. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive production schedules, predictive maintenance plans, and sustainability-oriented resource utilization strategies. This work will contribute novel methodologies to industrial operations research, with potential applications in automotive, aerospace, and consumer goods manufacturing sectors. By quantifying trade-offs between economic and environmental performance metrics, the project aims to advance the integration of circular economy principles into industrial management practices. The requested computing resources will support large-scale dataset processing, computationally intensive Monte Carlo simulations, and the training of neural networks for real-time anomaly detection in production systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of engineering principles to the planning and operational management of industrial and manufacturing operations, and prepares individuals to plan and manage such operations. Includes instruction in accounting, engineering economy, financial management, industrial and human resources management, industrial psychology, management information systems, mathematical modeling and optimization, quality control, operations research, safety and health issues, and environmental program management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis and preservation of under-resourced and endangered languages across the Australian, Oceanic, and Pacific regions, including Papuan, Polynesian, and Australian First Nations languages. These languages, many with limited documentation and complex morphological structures, face accelerating risks of extinction, yet their study is constrained by the scalability of traditional linguistic methods. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop large-scale models for phonetic, syntactic, and semantic analysis, enabling systematic comparisons across language families and contact varieties. Computational workflows will integrate machine learning (neural networks, transformer architectures) with rule-based approaches to process digitized field recordings, legacy texts, and multimodal corpora, prioritizing low-resource language adaptability. Key tasks include phonological pattern detection in Austronesian languages, automated parsing of polysynthetic structures in Papuan languages, and modeling dialectal shifts in Polynesian pidgins. HPC resources are essential to train models on distributed datasets, run parallel simulations of language evolution, and optimize computationally intensive tasks like acoustic feature extraction from archival speech data. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for language revitalization communities, a comparative database of Pacific language typologies, and novel insights into historical migration patterns through linguistic phylogenetics. By bridging computational linguistics and Indigenous language scholarship, this project aims to advance both methodological frameworks for endangered language analysis and equitable access to technological resources for Pacific-speaking communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Australian/ Oceanic/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages native to Papua/New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and the island groups of the Pacific Ocean, including, but not limited to, the Papuan languages, the Australian languages, the Micronesian languages, and the Polynesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in human sciences communication, focusing on the intersection of family and consumer sciences (FCS) content delivery, digital media dynamics, and audience behavior modeling. The research problem centers on the challenge of optimizing tailored communication strategies for diverse populations in rapidly evolving digital environments. Traditional methods for analyzing audience engagement, content efficacy, and cross-platform information dissemination in FCS contexts lack the computational power to process large-scale multimedia datasets, simulate complex user interaction patterns, or model emergent communication phenomena in real time. The proposed work employs machine learning architectures, natural language processing (NLP), and agent-based modeling to analyze multi-modal communication channels (e.g., interactive educational platforms, social media, and augmented reality tools) used in FCS outreach. Computational workflows will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including textual, visual, and behavioral metrics—to identify patterns in information retention, ethical concerns in persuasive messaging, and cultural variables affecting consumer decision-making. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on curated FCS corpora, running parallelized simulations of community-scale information diffusion, and conducting sensitivity analyses on intervention strategies under varying socioeconomic scenarios. Expected outcomes include novel frameworks for adaptive message personalization, predictive models of audience segmentation efficacy, and evidence-based guidelines for mitigating misinformation in human sciences contexts. This work addresses a gap in computationally intensive social systems research while maintaining direct relevance to FCS priorities such as household resource literacy, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and equitable access to consumer education. The results will inform both academic understanding of human sciences communication ecosystems and practical tools for public-facing institutions.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Communication
cip_definition: A program that focuses on communication of human sciences subject matter and related consumer information to a variety of audiences through print and non-print media.

abstract: The development of stable, efficacious, and scalable pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations requires precise control over molecular interactions and material behaviors under diverse conditions. Current experimental approaches to optimize formulation parameters (e.g., excipient compatibility, rheological properties, and long-term stability) are resource-intensive and time-consuming, particularly when scaling laboratory prototypes to industrial production. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex formulation systems at multiple scales, enabling predictive insights into product performance and manufacturability. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) developing multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to predict excipient-drug interactions and phase behavior in novel topical drug delivery systems, and (2) employing finite element analysis (FEA) coupled with machine learning (ML) to model the impact of industrial processing conditions (e.g., shear forces, temperature gradients) on product microstructure and stability. Computational workflows will integrate quantum mechanical calculations for specific interaction energies, coarse-grained MD for mesoscale aggregation phenomena, and continuum-scale FEA for equipment-scale process simulations. These models will be validated against experimental data from collaborative laboratory studies, including accelerated stability testing and rheological characterization. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter spaces inherent to formulation optimization, particularly for systems containing multiple active ingredients, surfactants, and polymers. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to reduce trial-and-error experimentation in preformulation stages, identify stability risks under real-world storage conditions, and optimize manufacturing parameters for continuous production processes. By bridging molecular-level understanding with industrial-scale operational constraints, this work aims to advance computational pharmaceutics as a decision-support tool for faster, more sustainable product development while maintaining compliance with evolving regulatory standards for quality-by-design (QbD) principles.
cip_title: Industrial and Physical Pharmacy and Cosmetic Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of pharmaceutical sciences and pharmacy to the study of pharmaceuticals production and distribution, and prepares individuals to manage pharmaceutical industry operations. Includes instruction in pharmacoeconomics, industrial management, operations management, preformulation evaluation, product formulation/reformulation, drug product development, stability testing, dosage design, pilot scale-up, drug marketing, quality control, drug information, and legal and regulatory affairs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in social studies teacher education by modeling the impact of pedagogical strategies on student learning outcomes in diverse classroom environments. A critical challenge in social studies education is designing instructional approaches that equitably address complex socio-historical concepts—such as systemic inequality, geopolitical conflicts, and cultural dynamics—while accounting for varying student backgrounds, prior knowledge, and engagement patterns. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods struggle to capture the multidimensional interactions between teaching practices, curricular content, and learner variability at scale. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate classroom dynamics under diverse pedagogical scenarios. The ABM component will represent students as heterogeneous agents with attributes informed by empirical data from public school demographics, state assessment records, and anonymized student surveys. Instructional strategies, aligned with state and national social studies standards, will be encoded as dynamic variables affecting agent interactions. ML algorithms will then analyze simulation outputs to identify patterns linking specific pedagogical interventions to predicted learning gains, particularly for historically marginalized student groups. HPC resources are essential to execute thousands of parallel simulations, enabling sensitivity analyses across demographic, curricular, and instructional variables. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model of social studies classroom ecosystems, (2) evidence-based recommendations for optimizing teacher training modules, and (3) open-access tools for educators to test virtual implementations of lesson plans. By bridging computational social science and teacher education, this work aims to provide scalable, data-driven insights into equitable pedagogical design, ultimately strengthening the preparation of social studies educators to navigate complex, real-world classrooms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general social studies programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in simulating large-scale economic systems with embedded strategic decision-making, a problem critical to understanding market dynamics in increasingly digital and data-driven environments. Traditional economic models often simplify agent behavior or system scale to remain computationally tractable, limiting their ability to capture real-world complexities such as high-dimensional strategic interactions, dynamic pricing mechanisms, and network effects. We propose developing an agent-based modeling framework that integrates game-theoretic principles, econometric estimation, and machine learning to simulate heterogeneous agents—consumers, firms, and policymakers—operating within dynamic, interconnected markets. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize simulations across thousands of agents, optimize equilibrium-finding algorithms using distributed computing techniques, and train deep reinforcement learning models to approximate adaptive agent strategies. Key challenges include scaling Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in econometric parameter estimation, managing memory-efficient data structures for real-time interaction logs, and ensuring numerical stability in high-dimensional optimization tasks. The project will validate the framework using real-world datasets from digital marketplaces and public policy evaluations. Expected outcomes include novel insights into the resilience of algorithmic pricing systems under regulatory constraints, scalable methods for simulating decentralized financial networks, and open-source tools for interdisciplinary researchers working at the computer science-economics interface. By combining economic theory with advanced computational techniques, this work aims to advance predictive modeling of complex socio-economic systems while demonstrating how HPC resources can bridge gaps between theoretical abstraction and empirically grounded policy analysis.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the theoretical and practical connections between computer science and economics. Includes instruction in data analysis, database design, data mining, computer algorithms, economics, econometrics, computer programing, mathematics, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in Tibetan Studies through the large-scale analysis of cultural and historical texts, oral histories, and visual materials. The primary research problem centers on the fragmented and often inaccessible nature of Tibet-related primary sources, which span multiple languages (Classical Tibetan, modern dialects, Chinese, and English), formats (manuscripts, printed texts, audio recordings, and photographs), and institutional collections. Traditional methods of manual analysis struggle to synthesize these heterogeneous datasets, limiting scholars’ ability to trace thematic continuities in Tibetan religious practices, cultural narratives, and identity formation across pre-modern and modern periods. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages, image recognition models to classify visual motifs in thangka paintings and ritual artifacts, and network analysis tools to map connections between historical figures, religious institutions, and diaspora communities. Computational workflows will be tailored to handle non-Latin scripts, degraded textual sources, and multilingual metadata. The HPC infrastructure is critical for training custom transformer models on curated Tibetan corpora, processing high-resolution image datasets, and running iterative simulations to validate patterns in cultural transmission. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital repository of annotated texts and images, computational tools adapted for Tibetan Studies research, and visualizations revealing understudied links between pre-1950s religious movements and contemporary exile cultural production. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to redefine scholarly engagement with Tibetan materials, offering new frameworks for analyzing cultural resilience and identity in marginalized communities while preserving endangered sources through digitization.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Tibet and its borderlands, with emphasis on both pre-modern and modern Tibet and associated religious and exile movements.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the computational challenges of simulating multiscale fluid-structure interaction (FSI) phenomena in biomechanical systems, such as cardiovascular devices and soft robotic actuators. These systems involve tightly coupled nonlinear dynamics across disparate spatial and temporal scales, leading to prohibitive computational costs when using conventional monolithic solvers. Current approaches often rely on simplified models or weak coupling schemes, sacrificing accuracy for tractability. This project seeks to develop a scalable, adaptive parallel algorithm that combines implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, domain decomposition, and reduced-order modeling to enable high-fidelity simulations of FSI systems. The core innovation lies in a hybrid framework that decouples fluid and solid subsystems using asynchronous time integration while preserving strong coupling through iterative substructuring. HPC resources will be critical for implementing distributed-memory parallelism using the PETSc library, optimizing load balancing across fluid (Navier-Stokes) and solid (hyperelasticity) solvers, and validating the method against experimental particle image velocimetry data. The algorithm will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layers near moving interfaces and employ proper orthogonal decomposition to accelerate repetitive subproblems. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in time-to-solution compared to existing partitioned methods while maintaining energy conservation properties, as quantified by dimensionless error metrics. Successful implementation will advance computational capabilities for designing patient-specific medical devices and bioinspired robotics, where accurate prediction of unsteady flow-structure interactions is essential. The developed software toolkit will be made open-source to support broader research in applied mechanics, with particular relevance to NSF’s Harnessing the Data Revolution initiatives. Resource requests include 200,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated clusters to benchmark weak scaling performance up to 8,192 cores and test multi-physics convergence criteria across prototype applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of a broad range of mathematical and computational methods to modeling, analysis, algorithm development, and simulation for the solution of complex scientific and engineering problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, discrete mathematics, operations research, optimization, differential equations, statistics, scientific computation, and applications to specific scientific and industrial topics.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate vast, heterogeneous datasets from electronic medical records, wearable devices, genomic sequencing, and imaging, presenting significant challenges in integration, analysis, and regulatory compliance. Traditional computing methods struggle to efficiently process these data at scale, leading to delays in identifying adverse events, optimizing trial protocols, and validating outcomes. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for real-time, large-scale clinical trial data management and predictive analytics. The research will focus on three aims: (1) implementing parallelized pipelines to harmonize multi-modal data (clinical, omics, sensor-based) using distributed storage and Apache Spark; (2) training machine learning models to predict patient-specific intervention responses and safety risks through GPU-accelerated deep learning (TensorFlow/PyTorch); and (3) simulating trial design adjustments via agent-based modeling to minimize recruitment biases and protocol deviations. The HPC environment will enable rapid processing of terabyte-scale datasets while maintaining HIPAA/GCP compliance through encrypted workflows and audit trails. Expected outcomes include a validated platform for dynamic risk monitoring, automated FDA reporting templates, and optimized patient stratification algorithms. This work addresses critical gaps in clinical research coordination by providing coordinators with tools to manage complex trials efficiently, reduce manual errors, and improve protocol adherence. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a scalable model for multi-site trials, directly enhancing training in data-intensive clinical research methodologies. By integrating HPC capabilities with regulatory workflows, this project aims to accelerate translational discoveries while maintaining rigorous ethical and compliance standards essential for modern clinical research operations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear reactors requires precise modeling of complex multiphysics phenomena, including neutron transport, thermal-hydraulic behavior, and material degradation under extreme conditions. Current computational tools for simulating these coupled processes often rely on simplified models or empirical correlations due to limitations in processing power, which can introduce uncertainties in safety analyses and design optimizations. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate high-fidelity, multiphysics simulations of nuclear reactor systems, with a focus on advancing predictive accuracy for accident scenarios and long-term operational safety. The research will employ Monte Carlo methods for neutron transport simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal-hydraulic modeling, and finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity assessments. These tools will be integrated using a coupled multiphysics framework to capture real-time interactions between radiation, heat transfer, and mechanical stress. Key challenges include managing the computational expense of resolving fine spatial and temporal scales, optimizing parallelization strategies for heterogeneous architectures, and validating results against experimental data from test reactors and international benchmarks. The proposed work will enable the analysis of advanced reactor designs, such as small modular reactors (SMRs), under both normal and transient conditions, with emphasis on cladding failure thresholds, coolant flow instabilities, and fission product dispersion. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for reducing conservatism in safety margins, improving fuel cycle efficiency, and informing regulatory guidelines for next-generation nuclear systems. By utilizing HPC capabilities, this project aims to bridge critical gaps in computational nuclear engineering, supporting the development of safer, more sustainable nuclear technologies while training students in cutting-edge simulation techniques essential for the future workforce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering, knowledge and technical skills in support of engineer and other professionals operating nuclear facilities and engaged in nuclear applications and safety procedures. Includes instruction in physics, nuclear science, nuclear systems, nuclear plant and systems design, radiological safety, radiological applications, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the dynamic mechanisms of membrane protein interactions involved in ion transport and signal transduction, a critical yet poorly understood aspect of cellular biophysics. Current experimental techniques struggle to resolve the nanosecond-scale conformational changes and energy landscapes governing these processes. To address this, we propose a computational biophysics approach combining all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques to model the structural dynamics of key ion channels and G-protein-coupled receptors. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate large membrane-protein systems (≥500,000 atoms) over biologically relevant timescales (microseconds), leveraging explicit solvent models and force fields optimized for lipid bilayers. We will employ adaptive sampling algorithms to map free energy barriers associated with gating transitions and ligand binding, supplemented by hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations to probe electronic interactions in catalytic sites. Expected outcomes include atomistic models of metastable states in transport cycles, predictions of allosteric regulation sites, and quantitative estimates of thermodynamic driving forces. These results will advance fundamental understanding of bioenergetics in transmembrane signaling, with broader implications for designing targeted therapies against channelopathies and neurodegenerative diseases. The computational workflows developed will be disseminated as open-source tools for simulating supramolecular assemblies, bridging gaps between molecular-scale biophysical theory and cellular-scale functional modeling. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on physics-driven mechanistic studies of biological complexity, excluding purely genomic or cell-biological approaches. Resource allocation will enable the scaling of simulations across multiple GPU nodes, with data management plans ensuring reproducibility and interoperability with experimental biophysics datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of multigenerational family systems under stress using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understanding resilience patterns and systemic feedback loops. Family systems, as complex adaptive systems, exhibit nonlinear interactions influenced by cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic variables. Traditional qualitative or survey-based methods often struggle to capture these interdependencies at scale, particularly when analyzing longitudinal or cross-cultural data. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating family decision-making processes, emotional transmission, and resource-sharing behaviors across generations. The model will integrate empirical datasets from sociology and psychology, including trauma response metrics, household economic data, and intergenerational communication patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize thousands of family archetypes, run Monte Carlo simulations testing intervention scenarios (e.g., policy changes, therapeutic approaches), and perform sensitivity analyses on emergent system behaviors. Computational challenges include managing stochastic interactions among agents with heterogeneous belief systems, scaling network analyses for extended kinship structures, and processing high-dimensional time-series outputs. Expected outcomes include identifying critical leverage points for enhancing family resilience, quantifying the systemic impacts of socioeconomic policies on family cohesion, and generating predictive frameworks for risk stratification in social work contexts. This work bridges computational social science with family systems theory, offering a novel methodology for studying relational dynamics that could inform both clinical practice and policymaking. The resulting open-source simulation toolkit will provide a foundation for interdisciplinary research into complex familial interactions that traditional disciplinary approaches cannot adequately model.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity, data-driven simulation platform to enhance training and operational decision-making for commercial vehicle operators and instructors. The core research problem lies in the limitations of traditional training methods, which often lack scalable, adaptive scenarios to address diverse real-world challenges—such as dynamic traffic conditions, cargo-loading efficiency, and emergency response protocols. Additionally, the growing volume of telematics data from modern commercial vehicles remains underutilized in refining instructional strategies or optimizing fleet operations. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a computational framework integrating real-time vehicle dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven scenario generation, and large-scale logistics optimization. The platform will simulate complex driving environments—including variable weather, mechanical failures, and cargo configurations—using physics-based models accelerated via parallel computing. ML algorithms will analyze historical driver performance and telemetry data to generate personalized training modules, while optimization routines will model efficient routing and load distribution across fleets. By deploying these computationally intensive tasks on HPC infrastructure, we aim to achieve real-time interactivity for trainees and instructors, as well as rapid analysis of fleet-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation tool for adaptive skill development, predictive models for identifying high-risk operational patterns, and open-source optimization algorithms for freight logistics. This work will directly support safer, more efficient training protocols and operational standards in the commercial transportation sector, bridging gaps between theoretical instruction and practical, data-informed decision-making. The scalability of the platform, enabled by HPC, will allow future expansion to emerging technologies such as autonomous freight systems and electric vehicle fleet management.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the doctrinal evolution of early Christian Trinitarian theology across multilingual textual corpora spanning the 2nd to 5th centuries CE. While traditional theological scholarship has relied on close reading of select texts, the sheer volume of extant writings—including patristic treatises, conciliar documents, liturgical texts, and apologetic works in Greek, Latin, Syriac, and Coptic—presents a challenge for comprehensive analysis. This research addresses this gap by applying natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to trace conceptual developments, semantic shifts in key theological terms (e.g., *homoousios*, *hypostasis*), and intertextual networks of influence. The computational pipeline will integrate optical character recognition (OCR) for digitized manuscripts, transformer-based multilingual embeddings for semantic analysis, and graph neural networks to model doctrinal transmission across geographical and temporal axes. By processing approximately 15,000 pages of primary texts and 10,000 pages of secondary scholarship, the project aims to identify previously unrecognized patterns in theological argumentation, quantify the impact of socio-political factors on doctrinal formulations, and reconstruct fragmentary textual traditions through probabilistic modeling. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated theological texts, visualization tools for doctrinal development timelines, and statistical models correlating linguistic features with doctrinal controversies. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational linguistics and historical theology, offering a novel framework for studying doctrinal formation at scale while preserving the nuance of theological reasoning. The results will provide new insights into how core Christian doctrines emerged through complex interactions between textual interpretation, philosophical adaptation, and ecclesiastical negotiation, with methodological implications for digital humanities in theological studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the beliefs and doctrine of a particular religious faith from the intramural point of view of that faith. Includes instruction in systematic theology, historical theology, moral theology, doctrinal studies, dogmatics, apologetics, and applications to specific questions of ecclesiastical polity and religious life.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study of Japanese cultural identity as reflected in historical textual and visual materials. The research problem centers on analyzing the evolution of regional narratives and aesthetic motifs across Japan’s early modern period (1603–1868), a time of significant sociocultural transformation. Existing scholarship on this era relies heavily on manual analysis of primary sources, limiting the scale at which patterns can be identified in diverse materials such as Edo-era woodblock prints, travelogues, and regional folklore records. This project addresses this gap by employing computational methods to systematically examine relationships between textual themes, visual iconography, and geographic diffusion across a corpus of over 50,000 digitized items from institutional archives. A hybrid approach combining natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques will be implemented. Transformer-based models fine-tuned on classical Japanese texts will extract thematic clusters from travel diaries and folk tales, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will classify recurring visual elements in ukiyo-e prints and regional maps. Spatial analysis pipelines will then map these features against historical trade routes and administrative boundaries to model cultural exchange dynamics.
