The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of high-resolution image data and large-language model inference across multilingual texts, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes and scalable storage. Expected outcomes include an open-access dataset linking cultural artifacts to geotemporal metadata, a methodological framework for interdisciplinary digital humanities research, and new insights into how local identities were negotiated amid centralized governance. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across heterogeneous sources, this project aims to redefine scholarly approaches to Japanese cultural history while demonstrating the value of HPC infrastructure for area studies beyond conventional computational social science applications.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of Japan, and related island groups and coastal neighbors.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational cultural and artistic networks of the Caribbean diaspora from the mid-20th century to the present, with a focus on underrepresented gender and ethnic identities. The research addresses a critical gap in Caribbean Studies: while historical and sociopolitical dynamics are well-documented, computational approaches to mapping the evolution of creative exchange—such as literature, visual arts, and music—across diasporic communities remain underdeveloped. The study will integrate fragmented archival records, multilingual textual sources (English, Spanish, French, Creole), and digitized artistic works into a unified geotemporal dataset. Computational challenges include processing heterogeneous, non-standardized data at scale, applying natural language processing (NLP) to analyze multilingual cultural production, and employing graph-based models to trace connections between artists, institutions, and movements. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource Caribbean languages, conducting hyperparameter optimization for network analysis algorithms, and parallelizing spatial-temporal simulations of cultural diffusion patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-access interactive platform visualizing diasporic cultural networks, a corpus of annotated multilingual texts for computational humanities research, and new methodological frameworks for studying identity formation in transnational contexts. This work will provide quantitative and qualitative insights into how marginalized groups navigated colonial legacies and globalization, offering scholars and communities tools to reassess narratives of cultural resilience. By centering computational methods within interdisciplinary Caribbean Studies, the project aims to establish scalable paradigms for analyzing cultural data that prioritize regional linguistic diversity and decentralized knowledge systems.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples inhabiting the major islands and archipelagoes of the Caribbean Sea and related coastal borderlands, including immigration patterns and Pre-Columbian, colonial, and modern societies.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of chronic metabolic disorders linked to sedentary lifestyles underscores the need for personalized interventions that integrate physiological, behavioral, and environmental data. Current population-level health recommendations often fail to account for individual variability in metabolic responses to diet, exercise, and circadian rhythms, limiting their effectiveness. This project proposes to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model person-specific energy metabolism and activity patterns, enabling the design of precision wellness strategies. Using high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate continuous glucose monitoring, wearable-derived physical activity data, and multi-omic profiles (metabolomics, gut microbiome sequencing) from a cohort of 500 participants into dynamic systems biology models. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate cellular nutrient partitioning with deep learning architectures trained on temporal patterns in individualized datasets. Key challenges include scaling mechanistic models to handle high-dimensional data streams and optimizing parameter space searches across heterogeneous biological variables. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of predictive biomarkers linking microbiome composition to metabolic flexibility, (2) algorithms to recommend personalized meal timing and exercise windows based on circadian metabolic states, and (3) open-source tools for simulating intervention impacts on mitochondrial efficiency. The HPC environment is critical for running parallelized model variants, managing terabyte-scale datasets, and performing real-time optimization of intervention parameters during iterative validation phases. This work bridges computational biology and preventive health science, offering a novel methodology to move beyond generic wellness guidelines. Successful implementation could inform new standards for corporate wellness programs, rehabilitation protocols, and community health initiatives targeting metabolic syndrome prevention.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares individuals to assume roles as health/wellness professionals in private business and industry, community organizations, and health care settings. Includes instruction in personal health, community health and welfare, nutrition, epidemiology, disease prevention, fitness and exercise, and health behaviors.

abstract: The spatial and temporal regulation of cell behaviors during embryonic development remains a central question in developmental biology. A critical gap exists in understanding how mechanical forces and cellular interactions drive large-scale tissue morphogenesis, particularly during organ formation and axis patterning. This project seeks to address this problem by developing a three-dimensional computational model of vertebrate gastrulation, integrating live-imaging data from avian embryo studies with biomechanical simulations. The proposed high-performance computing (HPC) framework will employ agent-based modeling to simulate individual cell dynamics—including adhesion, polarity, and cytoskeletal forces—coupled with continuum-level finite element analysis to resolve tissue-scale stress patterns. A key innovation involves parameterizing the model using empirical measurements of cell stiffness, traction forces, and junctional remodeling from time-lapse light-sheet microscopy of chick embryos. The computational pipeline will systematically test hypotheses about how local cell behaviors propagate to global tissue rearrangements, specifically examining the role of planar cell polarity in mesoderm migration and neural fold elevation. Resource-intensive aspects include parallelized simulation of 10^5–10^6 interacting cellular agents across developmental timeframes and machine learning-based optimization of force calibration parameters. Successful implementation will provide mechanistic insights into conserved morphogenetic processes while identifying potential biomechanical drivers of congenital malformations such as neural tube defects. The HPC environment is essential for handling multiscale simulations spanning minutes to hours of developmental time, which exceeds the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. Outcomes will yield both a predictive tool for perturbing morphogenetic events and a publicly accessible database of simulated force maps correlated with experimental phenotypes, advancing interdisciplinary approaches in developmental cell biology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of embryology, development, and growth of animals and human beings. Includes instruction in fertilization, oogenesis, histogenesis, gastrulation, and cell differentiation; embryological development including organ and pattern formation, morphogenesis, gene regulation, cell lineage, and fate maps; disease and defect studies; transgenic and evolutionary models of growth and development; and applications to specific organisms and phyla.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators serving students with speech or language impairments. A critical challenge in this field is the dynamic, individualized nature of language development and intervention efficacy. Traditional methods for designing and adjusting individualized education plans (IEPs) rely heavily on manual observation and static assessment data, limiting educators’ ability to predict student progress or optimize interventions in real time. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating large-scale linguistic datasets, longitudinal student performance records, and machine learning (ML) models to simulate and predict language acquisition patterns under varying intervention strategies. The project will utilize natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze speech samples from students with diverse impairments (e.g., phonological disorders, aphasia) and generate synthetically augmented training data to account for low-resource scenarios. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models, will be trained to identify subtle patterns in language development trajectories and correlate them with intervention outcomes. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments to test the scalability of personalized strategies under resource constraints. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of audio and textual data, train complex ML models with hyperparameter optimization, and run high-fidelity simulations iteratively. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access toolset for educators to dynamically adjust IEP targets based on predictive analytics, (2) a repository of anonymized speech datasets with synthetic augmentations, and (3) evidence-based guidelines for deploying computational tools in special education settings. By bridging gaps between special education practice and computational innovation, this work aims to reduce IEP design latency, improve intervention personalization, and empower educators with scalable, equity-focused resources.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Speech or Language Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study and design of educational services for children or adults with speech and language impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with speech and language impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with speech disabilities, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Land use planning requires balancing complex interactions between environmental, economic, and social systems to optimize sustainable development. However, current models often lack the resolution or computational capacity to integrate multi-scale datasets, simulate dynamic feedbacks, or evaluate long-term scenarios under climate change and population growth. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance spatially explicit modeling of land use decisions and their impacts on ecosystem services in rapidly developing regions. We propose developing a coupled modeling framework that combines agent-based simulations of stakeholder decision-making, cellular automata for land cover change, and machine learning-driven analysis of socio-economic drivers. The framework will integrate high-resolution geospatial data (e.g., satellite imagery, soil maps, climate projections) with demographic and policy datasets to assess trade-offs between urbanization, agricultural conversion, and conservation goals. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across diverse climate and policy scenarios, calibrating models using Bayesian optimization, and processing petabyte-scale remote sensing inputs. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify how land use policies affect carbon sequestration, water quality, and habitat connectivity over decadal timescales. By enabling real-time visualization of development scenarios through GPU-accelerated rendering, this work will support stakeholder engagement in regional planning processes. The computational pipelines and open-source tools developed will enhance the capacity of land use researchers to analyze complex systems, while results will inform state and federal policies aimed at minimizing ecological degradation while meeting housing and infrastructure demands. This project addresses a critical gap in scalable, data-driven approaches to sustainable land management, with direct applications in mitigating biodiversity loss and climate-driven land use conflicts.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Land Use Planning and Management/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how public and/or private land and associated resources can be preserved, developed, and used for maximum social, economic, and environmental benefit. Includes instruction in natural resources management, natural resource economics, public policy, regional and land use planning, environmental impact assessment, applicable law and regulations, government and politics, principles of business and real estate land use, statistical and analytical tools, computer applications, mapping and report preparation, site analysis, cost analysis, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in multivalent atomic systems subjected to intense electromagnetic fields, a problem central to atomic and molecular physics. Current experimental techniques, such as attosecond laser spectroscopy, reveal ultrafast electron correlations and ionization processes that challenge theoretical models. Traditional single-active-electron approximations fail to capture collective multielectron effects, necessitating high-fidelity ab initio simulations. The research will employ time-dependent configuration interaction (TD-CI) and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) to model correlated electron dynamics in atoms like argon and xenon under strong-field conditions. These methods require solving high-dimensional Schrödinger equations with adaptive basis sets, a task infeasible without high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to exponential scaling with electron count. The project will leverage parallelized algorithms on GPU-accelerated architectures to optimize wavefunction propagation and reduce memory bottlenecks. Key objectives include quantifying the role of electron-electron interactions in high-harmonic generation and predicting ionization pathways in multivalent species. Outcomes will provide foundational insights into ultrafast quantum processes, aiding the design of next-generation photonic devices and attosecond metrology tools. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across field intensities and frequencies, generating datasets to validate against cutting-edge experiments. By bridging gaps between theory and observation, this work aims to establish predictive frameworks for controlling quantum states in extreme environments, with implications for quantum information science and precision measurement technologies. The computational workflows developed will also be disseminated as open-source tools, enhancing capabilities for the broader atomic physics community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the behavior of matter-energy phenomena at the level of atoms and molecules. Includes instruction in chemical physics, atomic forces and structure, molecular orbital theory, magnetic resonance, molecular bonding, phase equilibria, quantum theory of solids, and applications to the study of specific elements and higher compounds.

abstract: Emerging digital marketing ecosystems require adaptive strategies to optimize cross-platform budget allocation amidst rapidly shifting consumer engagement patterns. Traditional analytical models struggle to process the high-dimensional data generated by real-time bidding systems, social media interactions, and evolving platform algorithms, leading to suboptimal resource deployment. This project proposes the development of a reinforcement learning framework enhanced by high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-platform marketing environments and identify dynamic budget allocation policies. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets—including clickstream data, demographic variables, and contextual ad performance metrics—to train deep reinforcement learning agents capable of navigating complex reward landscapes across competing platforms. Computational experiments will leverage parallelized architecture to run millions of simulated campaign scenarios, incorporating temporal dynamics and competitive response patterns. Key challenges involve managing sparse reward signals in high-action spaces and optimizing model inference latency for near-real-time decision support. The expected outcomes include a scalable optimization engine that reduces customer acquisition costs by at least 18% compared to static allocation baselines while maintaining adaptability to platform policy changes. By employing GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed experience replay buffers, the project aims to demonstrate how HPC infrastructures can enable novel marketing operations paradigms that balance exploration-exploitation tradeoffs at unprecedented scales. The resulting methodologies will provide actionable insights for omnichannel campaign management and establish computational benchmarks for next-generation marketing resource allocation systems.
cip_title: Sales, Distribution, and Marketing Operations, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general process and techniques of direct wholesale and retail buying and selling operations and introduces individuals to related careers. Includes instruction in the principles of entrepreneurial economics, basic sales skills, the distribution channels for goods and services, and supervised practical application experiences.

abstract: Ophthalmic diseases, such as glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, and age-related macular degeneration, require early and accurate diagnosis to prevent irreversible vision loss. Current diagnostic workflows in clinical settings rely heavily on manual interpretation of imaging data, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus photography, which can introduce variability and delay. This project seeks to develop an automated, high-throughput computational pipeline to enhance the precision and efficiency of ophthalmic diagnostics by leveraging machine learning (ML) models trained on multimodal imaging data. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing large-scale ophthalmic datasets, which are often heterogeneous, high-resolution, and require real-time analysis in clinical workflows. We propose a hybrid approach combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and graph-based models to capture structural relationships in retinal layers, alongside federated learning to address data privacy concerns in multi-institutional collaborations. The project will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage parallelized training of deep learning architectures, optimize hyperparameters at scale, and validate models against diverse, annotated datasets spanning demographic and disease subgroups. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for automated lesion detection, quantitative biomarkers for disease progression, and a cloud-based interface to assist ophthalmic technicians in prioritizing high-risk cases. By reducing diagnostic latency and inter-observer variability, this work aims to improve clinical decision-making and expand access to vision-saving interventions, particularly in resource-limited settings. The computational framework will also serve as an educational resource for training ophthalmic technologists in emerging AI-driven diagnostic technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist ophthalmologists and optometrists in examining and treating patients with vision problems, vision disorders, and eye diseases. Includes instruction in taking patient histories, administering directed treatments and topical medications, diagnostic test procedures and equipment operation, anatomical and functional ocular measurements, patient care and instruction, ophthalmic and surgical equipment maintenance, safety and sterilization procedures, and office administrative procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the evolution of rhetorical strategies in multimodal digital writing. As communication increasingly relies on hybrid texts integrating language, images, hyperlinks, and interactive elements, understanding how writers adapt compositional practices across platforms—from academic blogs to professional social media—remains a critical challenge. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to analyze the scale and complexity of such multimodal corpora, necessitating computational approaches. The research will employ NLP tools and computer vision algorithms to process and annotate a corpus of 50,000+ digital documents (e.g., online articles, multimedia essays, and organizational communication), identifying patterns in rhetorical design, audience engagement, and cross-media citation networks. Machine learning models will classify genre conventions and track shifts in persuasive techniques over time, while network analysis will map how ideas propagate through interconnected digital spaces. By integrating these computational methods, the project aims to model how writers negotiate coherence, credibility, and accessibility in fragmented, multimedia environments. Outcomes will include (1) an open-access dataset of annotated multimodal texts, (2) a framework for computationally assessing rhetorical effectiveness in hybrid genres, and (3) pedagogical tools to help students and professionals navigate digital writing demands. The requested HPC resources are essential for training models on large-scale image-text datasets, running parallelized analyses of document networks, and simulating audience interactions with dynamic content. This work bridges computational humanities and writing studies, offering empirically grounded insights into 21st-century compositional practices while advancing methodologies for interdisciplinary text analysis.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of next-generation low-observable materials and configurations for stealth-enabled military platforms through high-fidelity computational modeling of multi-physics interactions. Traditional approaches to signature reduction—focused on isolated electromagnetic, acoustic, or thermal analyses—fail to address the interdependencies between these domains in real-world operational environments. The research problem centers on optimizing stealth performance under dynamic, multi-physical constraints (e.g., simultaneous radar cross-section minimization, thermal dissipation, and structural integrity) while accounting for nonlinear material behaviors and transient environmental conditions. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) electromagnetic simulations, finite element analysis (FEA) for thermoacoustic-structural coupling, and machine learning (ML)-driven topology optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the extreme computational demands of these coupled simulations, particularly at scales relevant to full-platform integration. Key innovations include the development of hybrid GPU-CPU parallelized solvers for real-time feedback between electromagnetic wave propagation and material deformation models, as well as generative adversarial networks (GANs) trained on multi-parametric datasets to predict optimal metamaterial geometries. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for signature trade-offs in complex operational scenarios (e.g., hypersonic flight, submerged environments), a library of adaptive material templates with tunable absorption properties across the RF-IR-acoustic spectra, and a decision-support tool for platform-specific stealth configuration prototyping. This work bridges critical gaps in multi-domain stealth design, offering a pathway to mitigate current limitations in survivability against emerging multi-sensor detection threats. The computational workflows and datasets generated will be shared via a secure portal to enable collaborative advancements in defense-focused applied physics communities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of electromagnetic field theory, electro-optics and materials science to the reduction of radar, optical and acoustic signatures of weapons systems. Includes instruction in computational electromagnetics, electro-optics, acoustics, guided wave theory, radiation capture, antenna applications in layered environments, material characterization, radar cross-section analysis, sonar signature analysis, non-destructive testing, remote sensing, and applications to specific weapons systems and operational environments.

abstract: Respiratory care therapy faces challenges in integrating multi-modal clinical data—such as real-time ventilator metrics, pulmonary function tests, imaging, and genomic profiles—to optimize patient-specific treatment strategies. Current approaches often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for individual variability in disease progression or treatment response. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models and simulations that inform personalized respiratory care. The research will focus on two primary aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to analyze large-scale, heterogeneous datasets from critical care units, and (2) simulating respiratory mechanics under diverse pathological conditions using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models. The machine learning component will employ deep neural networks to identify patterns in ventilator weaning success, infection risk, and drug response, while the CFD models will simulate airflow dynamics in obstructive and restrictive lung diseases, incorporating patient-specific anatomical data from CT scans. Both approaches require significant computational resources due to the scale of data (terabytes of longitudinal patient records and high-resolution imaging) and the complexity of simulations involving multiphysics interactions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing for model training, hyperparameter optimization, and large ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide ventilator management, reduce weaning failure rates, and optimize aerosol drug delivery in mechanically ventilated patients. By integrating these computational tools into clinical workflows, this research aims to advance precision respiratory care, reduce ICU stays, and improve patient outcomes. The resulting datasets and models will be shared with the respiratory therapy community to foster collaborative innovation in treatment personalization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to assist in developing respiratory care plans, administer respiratory care procedures, supervise personnel and equipment operation, maintain records, and consult with other health care team members. Includes instruction in the applied basic biomedical sciences; anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the respiratory system; clinical medicine; therapeutic procedures; clinical expressions; data collection and record-keeping; patient communication; equipment operation and maintenance; personnel supervision; and procedures for special population groups.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in precision medicine by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between multi-omics data, clinical variables, and environmental factors in heterogeneous patient populations. Current approaches to personalized treatment planning often fail to account for the dynamic interplay of these variables, particularly in understudied cohorts, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project will develop scalable computational frameworks to integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets with real-world clinical data, enabling predictive modeling of disease progression and therapeutic responses. Using machine learning algorithms optimized for distributed computing architectures, we will train ensemble models to identify biomarkers and stratify patients based on risk profiles. The HPC infrastructure will support parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, feature selection, and cross-validation, while enabling large-scale simulations of molecular pathways to contextualize observed clinical patterns. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for adaptive data integration in precision health, validated predictive models for cardiovascular and metabolic disorders, and a publicly accessible repository of annotated multi-omics datasets. This work will directly inform clinical decision-support systems under development in partnership with regional health networks, bridging translational research gaps. By advancing computational methods for health data synthesis, the project aligns with institutional priorities to expand interdisciplinary training in health analytics, providing students with hands-on experience in HPC-driven biomedical research. The requested resources are essential to manage terabyte-scale datasets and reduce runtime for iterative model training, which is infeasible on local clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in health and medical professional preparation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis in Talmudic Studies, a field traditionally reliant on manual, labor-intensive methods. The research problem centers on the challenges of analyzing the Talmud’s vast, interconnected corpus—comprising legal debates, narrative exegesis, and later commentaries—which spans centuries and integrates diverse disciplines such as jurisprudence, ethics, and philosophy. Traditional approaches struggle to systematically trace the evolution of legal concepts, identify cross-textual thematic patterns, or model the influence of sociohistorical contexts on interpretive traditions. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for rabbinic Hebrew and Aramaic, machine learning models to detect semantic and structural relationships within multilayered commentaries, and network analysis to map the diffusion of legal and philosophical ideas across time and geographic regions. HPC resources are critical for training custom transformer-based models on digitized Talmudic texts, given the computational demands of processing morphologically rich Semitic languages and managing sparse, fragmentary historical data. Additionally, large-scale simulations will model hypothetical textual genealogies to test scholarly hypotheses about lost manuscript traditions. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for computational Talmudic analysis, new insights into the transmission of Jewish legal thought, and a publicly accessible database linking textual variants to historical contexts. This work bridges computational humanities with religious studies, offering a replicable framework for analyzing complex textual traditions while enhancing pedagogical resources for training students in both Talmudic scholarship and digital humanities methodologies. By integrating HPC-driven approaches, the project aims to redefine the scale and precision of research in Talmudic Studies, with implications for interdisciplinary studies of legal and philosophical corpora across cultures.
cip_definition: A program focused on intense study of the Talmud that fosters values, critical thinking, and scholarship skills; prepares students for entry into a broad spectrum of graduate and professional schools; and prepares students for entry into a variety of careers including the Rabbinate. Includes instruction in Jewish law, Jewish jurisprudence, ethics, philosophy, and related disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing urban park design and management through computational modeling of human-environment interactions in high-density recreational spaces. As cities face increasing pressure to balance green space accessibility with ecological sustainability, traditional planning frameworks struggle to account for dynamic variables such as shifting visitor demographics, climate-driven vegetation stress, and real-time infrastructure usage patterns. The research employs agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques to simulate visitor behavior, resource consumption, and landscape wear patterns across temporal scales. High-performance computing resources will enable the parallel processing of multi-source data streams—including anonymized mobile device location pings, IoT sensor networks from smart park infrastructure, and satellite-derived vegetation health indices—at metropolitan-scale resolutions. By developing a predictive digital twin framework capable of testing hypothetical management interventions, the project aims to identify design configurations that maximize equitable access while minimizing maintenance costs and environmental degradation. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for park administrators and novel metrics for quantifying recreational space resilience under climate change scenarios. This computationally intensive approach bridges urban planning, human geography, and environmental informatics, offering evidence-based strategies for maintaining vital public spaces in rapidly urbanizing regions. The proposed models will undergo validation against observational data from three municipal park systems, with particular focus on predicting emergent congestion patterns during peak usage periods and long-term soil compaction risks. Results will directly inform municipal decision-making processes while advancing methodological innovations in the computational analysis of leisure space dynamics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in parks, recreation, and leisure facilities management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets central to understanding the development of Canadian social and political institutions in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The core research problem involves identifying and mapping patterns of institutional influence, migration, and policy diffusion across Canada’s provinces during a period of rapid industrialization and urbanization. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically process the volume and complexity of digitized primary sources—including census records, parliamentary debates, regional newspapers, and municipal archives—that are critical to tracing these phenomena at a national scale. To address this, the project employs computational text mining, network analysis, and geospatial modeling. Custom Python-based pipelines will preprocess and tokenize multilingual texts (English and French), while transformer models fine-tuned on historical Canadian corpora will extract named entities and thematic clusters. Network graphs will visualize relationships between policymakers, civic organizations, and demographic shifts, with parallelized algorithms running on HPC clusters to manage scalability. Spatial-temporal models, built using R and PostgreSQL, will integrate georeferenced data to track regional disparities in infrastructure development. The computational workflow demands significant memory and processing power due to the terabyte-scale datasets and iterative machine learning tasks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive database of institutional networks, peer-reviewed publications on methodological synergies between computational social science and history, and new insights into how regional identities shaped federalism in Canada. By combining HPC capabilities with archival research, this project aims to advance digital historiography, offering replicable frameworks for analyzing complex societal change in resource-constrained historical contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the society, culture, and institutions of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in Canadian historiography, sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance evidence-based design methodologies for healthcare environments, focusing on optimizing spatial configurations to enhance patient healing and staff efficiency. Current healthcare design practices often rely on static post-occupancy evaluations or anecdotal frameworks, limiting the ability to model dynamic interactions between environmental variables (e.g., lighting, acoustics, spatial flow) and physiological or behavioral outcomes in real time. The proposed work addresses this gap by developing computational models to simulate how design interventions impact stress reduction, patient mobility, and care delivery workflows across diverse populations and clinical contexts. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project integrates spatial analytics, real-time sensor data from IoT-enabled clinical environments, and machine learning techniques to predict how architectural features influence biometric markers (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels) and operational metrics (e.g., staff fatigue, patient wait times). Agent-based modeling will simulate patient and staff movement patterns under varying design scenarios, while deep learning architectures will analyze multimodal datasets to identify non-linear relationships between environmental variables and health outcomes. Parametric modeling tools will iteratively test design permutations, optimizing for variables such as infection control, accessibility, and sensory comfort. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the need for parallel processing of large-scale 3D spatial datasets and real-time simulation of complex human-environment interactions—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to evaluate design prototypes prior to physical implementation, reducing costly retrofits and improving scalability of patient-centered solutions. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven healthcare design, with open-source tools and benchmarks for the architecture and healthcare communities. By bridging computational science and environmental design, the project will contribute foundational insights into how built environments can be dynamically tailored to support healing processes, operational resilience, and health equity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and performance of healthcare environments to optimize healing. Includes instruction in interior design, architecture, healing sciences, healthcare environments, human-centered design, and healthcare delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the psychosomatic mechanisms underlying transpersonal and spiritual counseling practices using advanced computational modeling. While transpersonal psychology emphasizes the integration of spiritual experiences with psychological healing, the dynamic interplay between somatic states, emotional regulation, and spiritual practices remains poorly quantified. Current research lacks robust frameworks to model how interventions like guided meditation, ritual-based therapies, or expressive movement influence neural, emotional, and physiological systems holistically. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models that simulate interactions between self-reported spiritual experiences, biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG), and behavioral outcomes from counseling sessions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process high-dimensional datasets—including longitudinal qualitative narratives and real-time biosensor data—and to train agent-based models that map how individualized spiritual practices affect collective wellness in group therapy contexts. Machine learning pipelines will identify latent patterns in therapeutic trance states, while network analysis will characterize resilience in clients’ spiritual-emotional frameworks across diverse cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational toolkit for predicting optimal transpersonal interventions based on client-specific consciousness profiles, (2) evidence-based insights into the neurophysiological correlates of spiritual healing practices, and (3) open-access visualization tools to help practitioners tailor rituals or meditative protocols. By bridging computational rigor with transpersonal paradigms, this work aims to advance empirical foundations for spiritual psychology while fostering scalable, culturally responsive counseling strategies. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale simulations of consciousness-state transitions and parallel processing of multimodal data, which are infeasible with standard laboratory resources. This project aligns with the program’s focus on synthesizing spiritual wellness with therapeutic innovation, offering novel methodologies to study human consciousness in applied counseling settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to pursue spiritual and psychological practices for counseling. Includes instruction in emotional intelligence, expressive movement, healing practices and rituals, human consciousness, movement and meditation, psychosomatic connection, spiritual systems and wellness, transpersonal counseling, and therapeutic trance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven computational framework to optimize dynamic risk assessment in high-hazard industrial processes, addressing critical gaps in traditional static or heuristic-based process safety methodologies. Current risk assessment models often fail to account for real-time operational variability, interdependencies between failure modes, and cascading effects in complex systems, leading to reactive rather than proactive safety interventions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose implementing multi-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning to model accident propagation pathways under diverse operational scenarios. The computational approach will couple finite element analysis for equipment-level failure modeling with system-level Bayesian network simulations to quantify probabilistic risk chains, while reinforcement learning algorithms will identify optimal mitigation strategies under uncertainty. Key challenges include managing the combinatorial complexity of interacting process variables across temporal scales and the computational intensity of iteratively training predictive models on large-scale incident datasets. The requested HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10^5+ scenario permutations, real-time sensitivity analyses for non-linear process interactions, and accelerated convergence of optimization algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for proactive risk visualization, predictive thresholds for early hazard detection, and adaptive safety decision-support tools benchmarked against industrial case studies. This work aims to advance process safety paradigms from compliance-driven frameworks to intelligent, resilience-oriented systems, with direct applications in chemical manufacturing, energy infrastructure, and hazardous material handling. The computational tools developed will be disseminated as open-source modules to support academic and industrial collaborations in safety-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in developing methods to mitigate damage, reduce risks, and prevent accidents. Includes instruction in design for injury prevention, engineering for process safety, environmental psychology, function-based risk analysis, fundamentals of industrial engineering, operations research, probability and statistics, risk assessment and reduction, and safety engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the precision, sustainability, and scalability of taxidermy practices through computational modeling and data-driven optimization. While taxidermy traditionally relies on manual craftsmanship, emerging challenges—such as replicating biomechanically accurate poses, predicting long-term material degradation, and minimizing waste in specimen preparation—require interdisciplinary solutions that integrate biological data, materials science, and computational analytics. The research will focus on three core objectives: (1) developing finite element analysis (FEA) models to simulate stress distribution in reconstructed specimens under environmental variables (e.g., humidity, temperature), (2) training machine learning algorithms to correlate historical specimen preservation data with optimal tanning chemical ratios, and (3) creating 3D parametric models for customizable armature designs that adapt to anatomical datasets from scanned specimens. These computational workflows will utilize GPU-accelerated simulations for real-time rendering of dynamic poses and Bayesian optimization to refine material formulations. By digitizing and analyzing decades of taxidermy records, the project aims to establish predictive frameworks that reduce trial-and-error inefficiencies while preserving artisanal nuance. Outcomes will include open-source tools for pose simulation, a database linking specimen taxa to preservation parameters, and protocols for integrating computational feedback into manual workflows. This work bridges gaps between craft traditions and computational innovation, offering scalable solutions for taxidermists facing evolving ethical, environmental, and technical demands. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large volumetric datasets from micro-CT scans of specimens and iterating complex multiphysics models, which are infeasible on local hardware. Ultimately, the project aspires to position computational taxidermy as a niche interdisciplinary field, enhancing both artistic expression and scientific rigor in biodiversity preservation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to reproduce life-like three-dimensional representations of living animals for permanent display using elements of the deceased specimen(s) as well as artificial materials, and to manage taxidermy services and businesses. Includes instruction in specimen grading and selection, caping and fleshing, preservation procedures, tanning, drying, measurements, form and armature construction, carpentry and woodworking, molding and casting, drawing, sculptural techniques, painting and finishing techniques, basic business operations, customer communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Mongolian linguistics and literary analysis, addressing critical gaps in digital methodologies for this under-resourced language. The core challenge lies in processing and analyzing large-scale Mongolian language datasets—spanning historical texts, contemporary literature, and oral recordings—to uncover patterns in phonology, dialect variation, and literary evolution. Current tools for linguistic analysis are optimized for Indo-European languages, lacking support for Mongolian’s agglutinative morphology, vertical script systems, and dialect continua. This limitation hinders efforts to systematically study language change, textual relationships, and sociolinguistic dynamics in Mongolian contexts. Our computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) pipelines adapted for Classical and Modern Mongolian, machine learning models for dialect classification, and high-throughput corpus analysis. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on digitized manuscripts and oral narratives, developing algorithms for automated morphological segmentation, and employing geospatial analytics to map dialect features across time and regions. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational load of training language models on heterogeneous datasets (including OCR-processed historical texts and audio transcriptions) and to run parallelized simulations of linguistic change. Expected outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for Mongolian computational linguistics, a diachronic corpus annotated for phonological and syntactic shifts, and interactive visualizations of dialect boundaries. These resources will enable novel research on topics such as the influence of oral traditions on modern literary forms, dialect convergence in urban centers, and the preservation of endangered linguistic features. By bridging computational methods and Mongolian philology, this project aims to establish a foundation for data-driven humanities scholarship while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between linguists, technologists, and cultural heritage institutions.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Mongolian language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; oral and written literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of deploying deep neural networks (DNNs) on resource-constrained edge devices by developing a co-design framework that optimizes both algorithmic efficiency and hardware execution. While advances in deep learning have enabled state-of-the-art performance across domains, the computational and energy costs of modern DNNs remain prohibitive for real-time edge applications, such as autonomous systems and IoT devices. Existing approaches often treat model architecture design and hardware optimization as isolated tasks, leading to suboptimal trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and power consumption. This work proposes an interdisciplinary computational methodology integrating neural architecture search (NAS), hardware-aware quantization, and energy-efficient accelerator design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale parallel simulations of candidate architectures across heterogeneous computing platforms, iteratively refining models using multi-objective optimization techniques. Key computational steps include distributed training of surrogate models for rapid architecture evaluation, hardware-in-the-loop simulations to assess latency and energy profiles, and reinforcement learning-driven exploration of the joint design space. The project’s outcomes will include (1) energy-optimized DNN architectures tailored for edge deployment, (2) an open-source framework for hardware-algorithm co-design, and (3) empirical benchmarks quantifying trade-offs across accuracy, latency, and power for emerging edge devices. By bridging computer science (algorithmic innovation) and computer engineering (hardware optimization), this work aims to advance the development of sustainable, scalable intelligent systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for managing the computational complexity of multi-fidelity simulations and enabling rapid iteration across design parameters, which would be infeasible on local infrastructure. Results will directly benefit applications in smart healthcare, robotics, and distributed sensor networks, while contributing methodological advances to interdisciplinary computing research.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: The study aims to investigate the role of bioluminescent signaling in mediating interspecies interactions among deep-sea zooplankton, a specialized niche in animal biology with implications for understanding adaptive communication strategies in extreme environments. Despite the prevalence of bioluminescence in marine organisms, the dynamic interplay between light-producing species and their non-luminous counterparts remains poorly understood, particularly in the context of predator-prey avoidance and symbiotic relationships. This project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with fluid dynamics simulations to reconstruct how bioluminescent signals propagate through heterogeneous deep-sea habitats and influence collective behavior across species. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these interactions, which involve thousands of individual agents with variable light-emission properties, fluid flow perturbations, and photic noise from environmental sources. Simulations will parameterize species-specific traits—such as flash duration, wavelength, and emission triggers—drawn from empirical datasets of mesopelagic zooplankton. The computational framework will test hypotheses regarding signal interference, evolutionary trade-offs in light-based communication, and the ecological consequences of bioluminescence pollution from human activity. Expected outcomes include predictive models of how bioluminescent signaling networks stabilize or destabilize multispecies assemblages under environmental stressors. This work will advance zoological research by linking individual organismal biology to ecosystem-scale dynamics through a computational lens, offering novel insights into non-visual sensory ecology and informing conservation strategies for light-dependent marine communities. The resource request supports large-scale parallelized simulations, machine learning-driven pattern detection in behavioral outputs, and 3D visualization of interaction networks across varying oceanic depths.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the biology of animal species and phyla, with reference to their molecular and cellular systems, anatomy, physiology, and behavior. Includes instruction in molecular and cell biology, microbiology, anatomy and physiology, ecology and behavior, evolutionary biology, and applications to specific species and phyla.

abstract: The integration of alternative and complementary medicine (ACM) into modern healthcare systems is hindered by limited mechanistic understanding of many therapies, particularly those involving multi-component herbal formulations or non-pharmacological interventions. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the complex biochemical and physiological interactions underlying ACM modalities. Current challenges include the combinatorial complexity of herbal compounds, the dynamic nature of biofield therapies (e.g., acupuncture, energy healing), and the need to analyze multi-omics datasets from clinical studies of ACM interventions. We propose a computational pipeline combining molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning-based network pharmacology, and multiscale biophysical modeling to investigate two primary foci: (1) the polypharmacology of Traditional Chinese Medicine herbal formulations in modulating neuro-immuno-endocrine pathways, and (2) the systemic effects of bioelectrical interventions on cellular redox states. Molecular docking and free energy calculations will be performed on GPU-accelerated nodes to screen >10,000 natural compound-target pairs, while ensemble simulations will characterize time-dependent interactions in representative herbal extract mixtures. For biofield modeling, finite element methods will simulate electromagnetic field interactions with ion channels and cytoskeletal structures across spatial scales. The required computational resources include access to parallelized CPU clusters for long-timescale simulations (≥1ms), high-memory nodes for genome-scale metabolic network analyses, and secure storage for integrating proteomics/transcriptomics data from collaborating clinical sites. Expected outcomes include predictive models of ACM therapy efficacy, identification of synergistic herbal combinations, and quantitative frameworks for personalizing energy-based therapies. This work will establish computational foundations for evidence-based integration of ACM modalities while advancing methodologies for studying complex, system-level healthcare interventions.
cip_title: Alternative and Complementary Medicine and Medical Systems, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in alternative and complementary medicine and medical systems, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to evaluate the long-term impacts of public policy interventions in complex, multi-stakeholder systems, with an initial focus on urban transportation infrastructure allocation. Public policy analysis often grapples with predicting emergent outcomes from nonlinear interactions between institutional rules, individual behaviors, and physical constraints, yet existing computational tools struggle to integrate high-resolution behavioral data with system-scale dynamics. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations that capture heterogeneous traveler decision-making, municipal budget cycles, and infrastructure decay processes across a synthetic metropolitan region of 1 million agents. Computational methods will combine parallelized discrete event simulation for daily mobility patterns with evolutionary algorithms to optimize policy packages under demographic and climate uncertainty. Model validation will leverage anonymized transit smartcard data and maintenance records from three U.S. cities. The project addresses critical gaps in policy evaluation methodologies by enabling real-time sensitivity analysis of equity-efficiency tradeoffs and threshold effects in infrastructure investments. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source policy simulation toolkit capable of processing petabyte-scale behavioral datasets, along with evidence-based recommendations for adaptive funding allocation mechanisms in transportation policy. By quantifying second-order effects of policy decisions at unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution, this work aims to provide policymakers with robust predictive tools for managing interdependent vulnerabilities in public infrastructure systems. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the memory-intensive nature of multi-year simulations with dynamically interacting policy levers, environmental stressors, and population mobility patterns.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues and decision processes. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, microeconomic analysis of policy issues, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: The growing complexity of managing geriatric patients with multiple chronic conditions (multimorbidity) presents a critical challenge in clinical care. Current treatment guidelines, often designed for single-disease contexts, fail to account for interactions between comorbidities, polypharmacy risks, and age-related physiological changes, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model disease interactions, predict treatment responses, and optimize personalized care strategies for elderly populations. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will analyze multi-modal datasets from electronic health records (EHRs), genomic repositories, and longitudinal geriatric studies encompassing over 500,000 patients across acute, ambulatory, and long-term care settings. Machine learning models (ensemble methods, graph neural networks) will identify patterns in multimorbidity progression, while pharmacodynamic simulations will quantify drug-disease and drug-drug interaction risks specific to aging metabolisms. Agent-based modeling will simulate the impact of social determinants and care-setting transitions on health outcomes. The computational scale requires HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale data integration, parallelize millions of treatment scenario simulations, and train complex models with cross-institutional validation. Expected outcomes include: (1) a predictive tool for adverse event risk stratification in elderly patients with ≥3 chronic conditions, (2) optimized treatment algorithms balancing efficacy and safety in polypharmacy contexts, and (3) care-pathway simulations quantifying resource allocation impacts across healthcare settings. By enabling granular analysis of geriatric care dynamics at unprecedented scale, this HPC-driven approach will advance personalized intervention strategies while informing health system planning for aging populations. All workflows will adhere to HIPAA-compliance standards through secure data enclaves and federated learning architectures. The resource request directly supports the program’s mandate to integrate socioeconomic, ethical, and clinical dimensions in aging-related research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the care and management of elderly patients in acute, ambulatory, community and long-term care settings, and the treatment of diseases and conditions associated with the aging process. Includes instruction in ethical and legal issues, behavioral aspects of illness, socioeconomic factors in care and rehabilitation therapies.

abstract: Reproductive endocrinology and infertility (REI) involve complex, multifactorial disorders influenced by dynamic hormonal, genetic, and environmental interactions. A critical challenge in managing these conditions lies in disentangling heterogeneous patient data—spanning genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic, and clinical variables—to identify predictive biomarkers and personalized treatment pathways. Current analytical approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multi-omics datasets at scale or model non-linear biological interactions, limiting progress toward precision medicine in REI. This project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework to address these gaps by leveraging large-scale data integration, machine learning, and dynamic systems modeling. We will analyze retrospective and prospective datasets from 15,000 patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, and unexplained infertility, including whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal hormone profiles, electronic health records, and in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. Computational workflows will employ Bayesian hierarchical models to account for population heterogeneity, graph neural networks to map hormone-receptor interaction networks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize simulated treatment protocols. A key innovation involves coupling single-cell RNA-seq data from endometrial biopsies with agent-based modeling to simulate embryo implantation dynamics under varying hormonal conditions. These analyses demand parallelized processing of petabyte-scale data, stochastic parameter sampling, and real-time optimization—tasks requiring HPC resources for GPU-accelerated model training, distributed memory architectures, and high-throughput job scheduling. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for ovarian response and IVF success, (2) mechanistic insights into progesterone resistance in endometriosis, and (3) a validated computational platform for simulating patient-specific treatment adjustments. By elucidating pathophysiological pathways and enabling data-driven clinical decision-making, this work aims to advance therapeutic strategies for complex REI disorders while establishing scalable computational methodologies for reproductive medicine research.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage complex problems relating to reproductive endocrinology and infertility.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing computational demands of real-time, high-fidelity 3D rendering and interactive media production in graphic communications. As digital storytelling and immersive journalism increasingly rely on photorealistic visualizations, traditional rendering pipelines struggle to balance quality, interactivity, and scalability. The core challenge lies in optimizing complex rendering workflows—including ray tracing, dynamic lighting, and multi-user synchronization—for time-sensitive applications in virtual production and augmented reality environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a distributed rendering framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will implement parallelized rendering algorithms using GPU-accelerated nodes, coupled with machine learning models for predictive resource allocation during scene preprocessing. Computational experiments will benchmark rendering times, frame rate consistency, and energy efficiency across varying node configurations and scene complexities using industry-standard assets from Unreal Engine and Unity workflows. A secondary focus involves simulating networked collaboration scenarios to test latency thresholds in multi-user creative environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive rendering resource management and performance guidelines for HPC-supported graphic communication systems. This work will directly benefit media production pipelines requiring rapid iteration of high-resolution visual content while maintaining artistic control. By quantifying the relationship between computational resource allocation and perceptual quality metrics, the research aims to establish best practices for deploying HPC infrastructure in graphic communications education and professional workflows, particularly for emerging applications in immersive journalism and virtual set design. Results will be validated through case studies with partner media organizations, measuring productivity gains in collaborative 3D content creation.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in graphic communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Ensuring microbial safety while preserving nutritional and sensory quality in processed foods remains a critical challenge in food technology. Traditional thermal processing methods often rely on empirical models that inadequately balance energy efficiency, nutrient retention, and pathogen inactivation, particularly in heterogeneous food matrices. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-resolution, multi-scale computational framework to optimize thermal processing and packaging design for plant-based food products. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations with kinetic models of microbial inactivation, nutrient degradation, and heat transfer to predict system behavior under varying processing conditions. A parallelized finite element approach will model heat distribution in complex food geometries, while machine learning algorithms will analyze large datasets to identify energy-efficient processing parameters that maximize safety and quality. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will assess gas diffusion properties of novel biodegradable packaging materials to extend shelf life. The computational intensity of these multi-physics models—requiring millions of processor hours for parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and 3D visualization—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for optimizing industrial-scale retort systems, data-driven packaging material design guidelines, and reduced energy consumption in food processing. This work will advance precision engineering in food manufacturing, directly supporting the development of sustainable, nutrient-dense food products while addressing global food safety challenges. Results will be disseminated through open-source models and collaborations with food processors to bridge academic research and industry innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical, physical, and engineering principles to the development and implementation of manufacturing, packaging, storage, and distribution technologies and processes for food products. Includes instruction in food engineering, food preservation and handling, food preparation, food packaging and display, food storage and shipment, and related equipment and facilities design, operation, and maintenance.

abstract: The dynamic behavior of silicate minerals under extreme pressure-temperature conditions governs critical geomorphological processes, including metamorphic reactions, crustal deformation, and mantle dynamics. However, quantitative models of silicate phase transitions and their kinetic pathways remain limited due to the computational expense of simulating atomic-scale interactions across geologically relevant spatial and temporal scales. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance multiscale modeling of silicate systems, focusing on coupled quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) simulations of olivine-group mineral transformations. These minerals dominate ultramafic rocks and play key roles in lithospheric rheology, yet their dislocation-mediated deformation mechanisms under shear stress—particularly at subduction zone interfaces—are poorly constrained. We propose to implement hybrid QM/MM simulations using CP2K and LAMMPS software packages, with QM regions treated via density functional theory (DFT) to model bond-breaking/reforming events, while MM regions employ classical force fields to capture long-range strain effects. Simulations will track dislocation nucleation and migration in forsterite (Mg2SiO4) under varying P-T conditions (0–10 GPa, 300–1500 K), requiring >1 million CPU-hours to achieve nanosecond-scale trajectories across 100,000+ atom systems. Parallel tempering methods will enhance conformational sampling of rare events. Outcomes will include (1) atomistic mechanisms for shear-induced amorphization in olivine, (2) rate constants for dislocation creep under lithospheric stresses, and (3) predictive relationships between defect geometries and macroscopic viscosity. These results will directly inform field-based studies of mantle xenoliths and improve constitutive models for tectonic simulations. The computational framework developed will be extensible to other silicate systems, addressing fundamental gaps in linking micro-scale mineral physics to planetary-scale geodynamics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the silicates and other substances formed by chemical and physical geomorphological processes.

abstract: This project seeks to advance image-guided therapeutic interventions in Vascular and Interventional Radiology (VIR) by developing computational models to optimize device navigation, predict procedural outcomes, and personalize treatment strategies. Despite the growing use of minimally invasive techniques such as stent placement, embolization, and thrombolysis, challenges persist in navigating complex vascular anatomies, mitigating complications like thrombosis or vessel perforation, and tailoring therapies to individual hemodynamic conditions. Current clinical workflows rely heavily on static imaging and empirical decision-making, limiting precision in dynamic, patient-specific scenarios. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating high-fidelity simulations of blood flow, device-tissue interactions, and real-time imaging data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale finite element modeling of vascular networks derived from patient CT/MRI datasets, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective procedural outcomes. The models will simulate hemodynamic changes during device deployment, predict stress distributions in vessel walls, and identify risk thresholds for adverse events. A parallel computational pipeline will process multi-modal imaging data (fluoroscopy, sonography) to enhance real-time guidance through adaptive registration and deformation tracking. By leveraging HPC capabilities, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in solving Navier-Stokes equations for pulsatile flow and enable rapid parameter optimization for clinical deployment. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools for stent malposition or embolic material dispersion, a prototype decision-support system for intraprocedural planning, and open-source simulation templates for the VIR community. This work has the potential to improve procedural success rates, reduce radiation exposure from prolonged imaging, and establish a foundation for computationally driven precision medicine in interventional radiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists with additional training in image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize personalized anesthetic dosing protocols using high-performance computing (HPC) to model patient-specific responses to anesthetic agents. Current protocols rely on population-level averages, leading to variability in drug efficacy and adverse events such as intraoperative awareness or hemodynamic instability. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling, machine learning, and multi-omic data analysis. The research will leverage anonymized electronic health records, genomic data, and intraoperative physiological monitoring datasets from a cohort of 2,500 patients undergoing diverse surgical procedures. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelized simulations of drug distribution and metabolism across virtual patient populations, accounting for genetic polymorphisms in drug-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP2B6, pseudocholinesterase), body composition metrics, and comorbidities. Machine learning models will be trained to predict individualized dose-response curves and adverse event risks, with validation against clinical outcomes. The computational pipeline will also incorporate real-time optimization algorithms to guide dynamic dosing adjustments during simulated surgical scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for precision anesthetic administration, reducing postoperative complications by an estimated 15-20% in pilot data. This work aligns with the growing emphasis on personalized perioperative care in nurse anesthesia practice, offering a scalable method to enhance patient safety and recovery trajectories. By elucidating genotype-phenotype interactions in anesthetic response, the project will further contribute foundational knowledge to nursing science regarding biological determinants of interpatient variability. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the computational burden of multi-parametric modeling and achieving clinically actionable processing speeds for complex datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to administer anesthetics and provide care for patients before, during and after anesthesia. Includes instruction in the biochemistry and physics of anesthesia; advanced anatomy and physiology; clinical pharmacology of anesthetics and adjunctive drugs; pain management; acute care and operating room practice; clinical technology and procedures; emergency intervention; patient assessment and education; and legal issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in digital humanities and textual studies, focusing on the analysis and preservation of large-scale, heterogeneous textual corpora. A central challenge in the field lies in processing and interpreting vast collections of digitized historical manuscripts, modern digital texts, and born-digital media, which often exist in fragmented, multilingual, or non-standardized formats. Traditional computational methods struggle to manage the scale and complexity of these datasets, particularly when integrating semantic analysis, network-based modeling of textual relationships, and machine learning-driven pattern detection across temporal and cultural contexts. The proposed research will develop and deploy scalable computational workflows to address these challenges, including natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for historical language variants, graph-based models to trace intertextual networks across centuries of literature, and AI-assisted tools for automated collation of variant texts in critical editions.
