This project proposes to develop computational models leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets encompassing 3D dental scans, biomechanical force measurements, microbial community profiles, and longitudinal treatment outcomes from companion animals and zoo species. Machine learning approaches will be applied to identify patterns in dental wear, periodontal disease progression, and species-specific risk factors, while finite element analysis simulations will model stress distributions in abnormal occlusions and dental prostheses. A parallelized computational pipeline will integrate µCT-derived mandibular morphology data with mastication kinematics from motion capture systems, enabling species-specific comparisons at unprecedented resolution. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabytes of multi-center clinical data, running iterative simulations of biomechanical interactions, and training deep learning models on heterogeneous imaging datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models for early detection of malocclusion syndromes in brachycephalic breeds, optimized dental implant designs for large carnivores, and computational frameworks for evaluating antimicrobial treatment efficacy against oral biofilm communities. Results will be disseminated through an open-access simulation toolkit to support evidence-based treatment planning in veterinary dental practice. This work will establish new computational methodologies for translational oral health research while addressing critical gaps in veterinary dental care capacity across clinical and conservation contexts.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of dental care procedures to the teeth, eating surfaces, and oral cavities of animals. May included related research in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and abnormalities of animal teeth and gums and related parts of the oral cavity; and related anatomical and physiological principles.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and enhance pedagogical strategies in drama and dance education through motion capture and machine learning techniques. A critical challenge in teacher training for performing arts is the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to evaluate the effectiveness of instructional methods, particularly in kinesthetic and collaborative learning environments. Traditional assessments often rely on subjective observation, limiting opportunities for personalized feedback or longitudinal analysis of teaching efficacy. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets of classroom interactions, student performances, and instructor demonstrations. Motion capture data from dance rehearsals and drama exercises will be collected, annotated, and analyzed using deep learning models to quantify movement dynamics, spatial relationships, and verbal-nonverbal communication patterns. These models will be trained to identify correlations between teaching techniques and student engagement or skill acquisition, as measured through multimodal metrics. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothetical classroom scenarios to test the scalability of pedagogical interventions across diverse learner populations. The computational demands of processing high-dimensional motion data, training complex neural networks, and running iterative simulations necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for efficient parallelization and GPU acceleration. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for visualizing teaching effectiveness, generating automated feedback for educators, and informing evidence-based curriculum design. This work aims to advance drama and dance pedagogy by bridging qualitative educational practices with quantitative computational analysis, ultimately fostering more adaptive, inclusive approaches to performing arts instruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex interplay of biological, behavioral, and socio-cultural factors influencing health disparities in chronic disease outcomes using advanced computational modeling. Despite growing evidence that multi-level determinants—such as genetic predispositions, individual health behaviors, social networks, and environmental inequities—interact dynamically to shape health trajectories, traditional analytical methods often fail to capture these non-linear, time-dependent relationships. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating population-level health decision-making processes, integrated with machine learning techniques to analyze large-scale health datasets. The ABM will incorporate individual agents with heterogeneous attributes (e.g., socio-economic status, health literacy, genetic risk) interacting within simulated social and built environments, enabling exploration of how micro-level behaviors propagate to macro-level health outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling simulations to reflect realistic population sizes (>1 million agents), running parameter sweeps to test intervention scenarios, and training deep learning models on linked electronic health records, geospatial data, and behavioral surveys. Expected outcomes include identifying leverage points for precision public health interventions, predicting the long-term impacts of policies targeting health inequities, and generating synthetic datasets to inform resource allocation in underserved communities. By bridging computational science and behavioral health research, this work will advance methodological frameworks for studying complex health systems while providing actionable insights to reduce preventable disease burdens. The requested HPC infrastructure will support the iterative refinement of models, real-time visualization of intervention effects, and secure handling of sensitive multi-modal health data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biological, behavioral, and socio-cultural determinants of health and health behavior, and the interventions and policies aimed at improving community and population health. Includes instruction in behavioral sciences, public health practice and policy, human services, and research methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in dynamic resource allocation for large-scale construction projects, where traditional heuristic methods fail to account for real-time disruptions, multi-stakeholder interactions, and sustainability constraints. The central challenge lies in optimizing labor, equipment, and material flows under stochastic variables such as weather delays, supply chain volatility, and evolving regulatory requirements. To overcome computational limitations of existing commercial project management software, we propose developing an adaptive decision-support framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The model will integrate agent-based simulations to capture subcontractor behaviors, Monte Carlo methods to quantify cascading risks, and reinforcement learning algorithms to iteratively refine allocation strategies across parallelized scenarios. Key innovations include embedding carbon-cost trade-off analytics into optimization objectives and incorporating real-time IoT data streams from construction sites to enable responsive replanning. The HPC environment will facilitate processing of high-dimensional datasets (e.g., 4D BIM models, supplier lead times, OSHA incident reports) while maintaining computational feasibility for projects exceeding 10,000 interdependent tasks. Expected outcomes include a benchmarked framework for quantifying the financial and operational impacts of dynamic resource policies, predictive models for bottleneck mitigation, and open-source tools compatible with existing construction management platforms. This work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resource allocation that balances economic, safety, and sustainability KPIs in complex projects, with potential applications in disaster recovery infrastructure and net-zero building initiatives. By bridging computational engineering and operations research within the construction management domain, the project addresses a critical gap in business-oriented decision tools for the built environment.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply project management knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques in the construction and facility management industries. Includes instruction in facilities operations and maintenance, construction estimating, OSHA standards, sustainability, drafting, construction plans, project planning, risk management, cost and time management, contracts and procurement, accounting, statistics, decision making, and human resources.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the computational analysis of Celtic languages, with a focus on modeling linguistic evolution, dialectal variation, and cross-language contact phenomena. Despite the rich textual and oral traditions of Celtic languages, their historical fragmentation, divergent revitalization trajectories, and complex sociolinguistic dynamics pose significant barriers to systematic study. Current limitations in processing digitized corpora—spanning Old Irish glosses, Middle Welsh poetry, Modern Scottish Gaelic speech, and reconstructed Proto-Celtic forms—require scalable computational methods to analyze phonological shifts, morphosyntactic patterns, and lexical borrowing across time and space. The project proposes a multi-modal approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), phylogenetic modeling, and corpus linguistics to (1) automate the alignment of diachronic textual data, (2) simulate language contact scenarios using agent-based models, and (3) train neural architectures for low-resource machine translation between modern Celtic languages. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of fragmented manuscript data, Bayesian inference of language divergence timelines, and comparative analysis of regional dialects (e.g., Munster vs. Connacht Irish; Breton’s Vannetais variety). Expected outcomes include a unified digital repository of annotated Celtic language corpora, probabilistic reconstructions of unattested proto-language features, and open-source tools for dialect classification. These results will advance philological research on Celtic literary traditions, inform language revitalization initiatives, and refine theoretical frameworks for minority language preservation in computational contexts. By addressing scalability constraints in handling non-standard orthographies and sparse data, this work will also contribute methodological innovations to computational historical linguistics broadly.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the historical and modern languages spoken by the Celtic peoples of the British Isles, Continental Europe, and Asia Minor, including, but not limited to, modern languages such as Irish, Scots Gaelic, Welsh, and Breton; and extinct or revived languages such as Cornish, Manx, Galatian, and others. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Forensic anthropology faces critical challenges in analyzing skeletal remains for medicolegal investigations, particularly when dealing with fragmented, degraded, or commingled remains. Traditional analytical methods often lack the precision and scalability required to address complex taphonomic processes, biological profile estimation under suboptimal conditions, or high-dimensional datasets from advanced imaging techniques. This project proposes the development of computational models to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of skeletal analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning algorithms to automate the classification of skeletal trauma and taphonomic alterations using micro-CT and 3D surface scan data; (2) simulating population-specific osteological variation through probabilistic modeling to improve ancestry and sex estimation in diverse forensic contexts; and (3) optimizing Bayesian frameworks for integrating multi-modal data (e.g., isotopic, genomic, morphometric) in identification workflows. These objectives require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and iterative training of deep neural networks—tasks exceeding the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. The proposed HPC implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for image analysis and distributed memory systems for large-scale statistical modeling. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for forensic practitioners, validated protocols for computationally intensive analytical pipelines, and novel insights into skeletal biomechanics under taphonomic stress. By bridging gaps between anthropological theory and computational innovation, this work aims to establish reproducible, data-driven standards for forensic casework while advancing methodological rigor in skeletal identification. The resource allocation will directly support critical advancements in medicolegal death investigation capabilities, with implications for humanitarian efforts and judicial systems worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and skeletal anthropology in medicolegal death investigations. Includes instruction in biological anthropology theory, crime scene investigation, forensic anthropology field methods, forensic anthropological techniques and procedures, human anatomy, methods of human identification, mortuary archaeology, osteology, and taphonomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced control strategies for autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments, with a focus on optimizing real-time decision-making under computational and energy constraints. The core challenge lies in balancing the high-dimensional sensorimotor processing required for adaptive locomotion and manipulation with the limited onboard computational resources typical of mobile mechatronic platforms. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining physics-informed neural networks for predictive system modeling and distributed optimization algorithms for multi-objective control allocation. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex multi-body dynamics scenarios, train deep reinforcement learning agents through massively parallelized trial batches, and validate control policies across stochastic environmental conditions. Key computational tasks include finite element analysis of compliant actuator arrays, Monte Carlo-based robustness testing of sensor fusion pipelines, and real-time optimization of redundant manipulator trajectories using GPU-accelerated quadratic programming solvers. Expected outcomes include a scalable control architecture that dynamically allocates computational resources based on task criticality, reducing latency in perception-action cycles by 30-50% compared to conventional centralized approaches. The work will directly contribute to enabling resource-efficient autonomous systems for industrial inspection and disaster response applications, while advancing methodological integration of embedded real-time computing with model-based control theory. HPC support is essential given the project’s need for large-scale parameter space exploration, concurrent simulation of heterogeneous robotic fleets, and data-intensive training of multimodal perception models—tasks exceeding the capacity of local laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize forklift operation workflows and accident risk prediction in dynamic industrial environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While forklift operation training emphasizes safety protocols and manual skill development, current practices lack data-driven tools to model complex interactions between operators, equipment, and workspaces in real time. The research problem centers on mitigating workplace accidents caused by situational factors such as load instability, blind spots, and multi-agent coordination challenges in high-density storage facilities. Using agent-based modeling and physics-informed machine learning, we will simulate forklift kinematics, load dynamics, and human operator decision-making across diverse warehouse configurations. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to quantify risk probabilities under variable conditions (e.g., uneven terrain, lighting gradients, traffic patterns) while integrating real-world sensor data from IoT-enabled forklifts. Computational models will be validated against empirical accident datasets and biomechanical analyses of operator response times. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive risk heatmaps for facility layout optimization, (2) AI-driven training modules that adapt to operator skill levels, and (3) a digital twin framework for evaluating safety interventions without physical prototyping. By bridging gaps between vocational training paradigms and computational engineering, this work aims to reduce forklift-related injuries by 15-30% in modeled scenarios while informing ISO standards for adaptive safety systems. The project will also establish a novel HPC workflow template for industrial equipment training programs, demonstrating how high-fidelity simulations can augment hands-on technical education in the Technology and Technical Fields domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate forklifts in a variety of work environments. Includes instruction in accident prevention, forklift operation, materials handling, and worksite safety.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize texture-modified meal planning for patients with dysphagia, a swallowing disorder affecting over 500 million individuals globally. Current dietitian-led approaches rely on manual adjustments to food consistency using standardized scales (e.g., IDDSI), but these methods often fail to account for dynamic interactions between nutritional content, sensory acceptability, and physicochemical stability during preparation. We propose an HPC-driven approach to model multi-parameter relationships between ingredient composition, processing techniques (e.g., mechanical softening, thickening agents), and post-preparation food behavior. A hybrid pipeline will integrate molecular dynamics simulations of hydrocolloid interactions, finite element analysis of mechanical stress distribution in heterogeneous food matrices, and machine learning models trained on clinical outcomes data from 15,000+ patient records. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated parallel processing to iteratively optimize meal plans against conflicting constraints: maximizing nutrient retention, ensuring safe swallowing rheology, maintaining palatability, and minimizing preparation time. Validation will involve 3D-printed food analogs with embedded sensors to quantify real-world deformation forces against simulated predictions. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that reduces dietitians’ trial-and-error workload by 40–60% while improving patient adherence through personalized texture-nutrient profiles. This work bridges gaps between food rheology, clinical nutrition, and computational modeling, addressing a critical need in under-resourced healthcare settings where dysphagia management is frequently deprioritized. The resulting framework will establish scalable methodologies for adaptive meal optimization applicable to other chronic conditions requiring specialized diets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: The growing burden of chronic diseases necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize preventive strategies at individual and population levels. This project aims to develop a scalable, machine learning-driven framework for predicting multi-disease risk trajectories and simulating the long-term impacts of personalized interventions. Current models often use single-disease paradigms or simplified risk factors, limiting their utility in real-world clinical decision-making. We propose integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records, genomic predispositions, social determinants of health, and environmental exposures—into a unified predictive architecture. The computational challenges involve managing high-dimensional data (500+ variables across 2 million patients), addressing missingness through generative imputation, and training ensemble neural networks with temporal attention mechanisms to model disease co-occurrence patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three phases: 1) parallel processing of federated datasets across secure nodes, 2) hyperparameter optimization of deep survival analysis models using Bayesian methods, and 3) agent-based simulations of intervention scenarios across synthetic populations. Expected outcomes include a validated risk stratification tool that identifies 10-year probabilities for cardiovascular, metabolic, and oncological conditions with ≥85% AUC, plus policy-ready metrics quantifying how targeted screening modifications could reduce disability-adjusted life years in specific demographics. The computational infrastructure will enable monthly model retraining cycles using updated clinical data streams while maintaining HIPAA compliance through differentially private learning. This work bridges precision medicine and public health by creating an adaptable platform for evaluating prevention strategies under evolving demographic and environmental conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Preventive Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to develop an adaptive decision-support framework for optimizing undersea sensor network configurations in contested maritime environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address dynamic operational constraints. Modern undersea warfare requires rapid integration of heterogeneous data streams—acoustic, environmental, and tactical—to inform sensor deployment, signal processing, and threat-response protocols. However, existing approaches struggle with real-time recalibration under variable oceanographic conditions, adversarial counter-detection tactics, and resource limitations. The proposed research combines agent-based modeling, adversarial machine learning, and multi-objective optimization to simulate contested undersea domains, prioritizing stealth, coverage, and operational endurance. Computational workflows will integrate oceanographic datasets, probabilistic threat models, and mission-specific constraints to generate resilient network topologies. HPC resources are critical for scaling Monte Carlo simulations evaluating thousands of scenario permutations, training neural networks to predict optimal sensor repositioning strategies, and testing counter-adversarial algorithms under high-uncertainty conditions. Expected outcomes include a modular software toolkit for simulating sensor network performance across diverse undersea theaters, validated against historical operational data. This framework aims to reduce decision latency during mission planning by 40-60% compared to manual methods while improving detection avoidance metrics by 25%. By bridging computational game theory, distributed systems design, and maritime operational art, the project addresses a gap in adaptive resource allocation for undersea platforms operating in denied areas. Results will inform next-generation autonomy protocols for unmanned underwater vehicles and contribute to open-source tactical simulation libraries, subject to security review.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, engineering design and military concepts that govern the operational employment of underwater sensors and weapons systems. Includes instruction in acoustics, electrical, and mechanical engineering; mathematics; meteorology; oceanography; physics; operations analysis; human factors; computer science; and robotics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing the design and safety of electrical power transmission systems, with a focus on integrating renewable energy sources into aging grid infrastructures. The increasing complexity of modern power systems—driven by distributed generation, variable renewable inputs, and evolving load demands—requires advanced simulations to evaluate stability, fault tolerance, and compliance with safety standards. Traditional analytical methods lack the scalability to model large-scale, heterogeneous grids in dynamic operating conditions, creating gaps in risk assessment and installation planning. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations, machine learning (ML)-based fault prediction, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. The computational workflow will simulate grid behavior under diverse scenarios, including extreme weather events, equipment failures, and intermittent renewable generation, using parallelized power system solvers such as OpenDSS and GridLAB-D. ML models will be trained on synthetic and real-world grid data to predict arc flash hazards, insulation breakdowns, and line sagging risks, informing adaptive protection schemes. Additionally, genetic algorithms will optimize conductor placement, transformer sizing, and grounding system configurations to minimize material costs while meeting NEC and IEEE standards. The HPC resources are critical for managing the high-dimensional parameter space and real-time constraints of these simulations, which involve millions of nodes and sub-millisecond time steps. Expected outcomes include validated design protocols for resilient hybrid AC/DC grids, open-source tools for risk-aware installation planning, and data-driven recommendations for updating industry training curricula. By bridging computational engineering with hands-on electrical installation practices, this work aims to enhance the safety, efficiency, and scalability of power transmission systems in transitioning energy landscapes.
cip_title: Electrical and Power Transmission Installation/ Installer, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install indoor and outdoor residential, commercial, and industrial electrical systems, and associated power transmission lines. Includes instruction in electricity, safety procedures, wiring, insulation and grounding, schematic blueprint interpretation, equipment operation and maintenance, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: Reproductive cancers, particularly ovarian and endometrial malignancies, present complex challenges due to their dynamic interaction with hormonal cycles and tissue-specific microenvironmental factors. A critical gap exists in understanding how cyclical hormonal fluctuations and mechanical forces within reproductive tissues collectively influence tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational model integrating hormonal signaling pathways, tissue biomechanics, and tumor growth dynamics to identify microenvironment-driven mechanisms of cancer resilience. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate three-dimensional tissue architectures under hormonally dynamic conditions, parameterized by clinical imaging data and ex vivo biomechanical measurements from patient-derived samples. The computational framework will employ finite element analysis to model tissue deformation during menstrual or estrous cycles, coupled with agent-based modeling of cancer cell proliferation and invasion. Parallelized parameter optimization will be conducted to calibrate the model against longitudinal clinical outcomes, while machine learning approaches will identify predictive biomechanical and endocrine biomarkers of metastatic potential. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational platform for simulating hormone-responsive reproductive cancers, (2) mechanistic insights into how cyclic mechanical stress synergizes with estrogen receptor signaling to drive therapy-resistant phenotypes, and (3) predictive biomarkers for risk stratification in patients with early-stage disease. This work will directly inform targeted therapeutic strategies that account for reproductive system physiology, advancing precision oncology in hormonally driven cancers. The scale of spatial-temporal simulations (10^6+ cellular agents across 100+ cycle iterations) and integration of high-resolution imaging datasets (>50 TB) necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve biologically relevant resolution within tractable timeframes.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of reproductive processes and biogenesis in animals and human beings. Includes instruction in reproductive ecology and behavior, reproductive system physiology, endocrinology, developmental biology, neuroendocrinology, evolution and types of reproductive systems, reproductive genetics, physiopathology of reproductive processes, and applications of molecular biology and biophysics to the study of reproductive physiology.

abstract: The development of advanced ceramic materials with tailored properties requires a comprehensive understanding of atomic-scale processes, microstructural evolution, and defect dynamics under thermomechanical and chemical stressors. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve these phenomena across relevant length and time scales, particularly for complex systems such as ceramic superconductors or high-entropy abrasives. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-scale simulations of ceramic synthesis, degradation mechanisms, and performance optimization. Using molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT), we will model atomic interactions during sintering processes, interfacial reactions in composite ceramics, and crack propagation under extreme thermal gradients. Mesoscale phase-field methods will simulate microstructural evolution in polycrystalline systems, while machine learning models trained on simulation data will predict optimal processing parameters for defect minimization. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated codes (e.g., LAMMPS, Quantum ESPRESSO) to handle systems exceeding 10^6 atoms and long-timescale reactive events via enhanced sampling techniques. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into pore coalescence during sintering, interfacial stability in ceramic-metal composites, and phase transformation kinetics in zirconia-based thermal barrier coatings. These results will directly inform the design of next-generation ceramics with enhanced fracture toughness, thermal stability, and wear resistance for energy storage and high-temperature applications. The generated datasets and validated force fields will be disseminated to the ceramic engineering community, establishing a computational framework to accelerate materials discovery. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with experimental validation, this work addresses critical gaps in processing-structure-property relationships for non-metallic inorganic materials, advancing the foundational knowledge required to meet industrial demands for sustainable, high-performance ceramics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of inorganic non-metallic materials, such as porcelains, cements, industrial ceramics, ceramic superconductors, abrasive, and related materials and systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the impact of enrollment trends, demographic shifts, and financial aid policies on institutional sustainability in higher education. As universities face mounting pressures from fluctuating enrollment patterns, changing student demographics, and evolving funding landscapes, administrators require predictive tools to optimize resource allocation and strategic planning. Traditional linear models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between these variables, limiting their utility for decision-making. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled agent-based modeling (ABM) approach that simulates multi-year enrollment scenarios under varying policy and economic conditions. The model will integrate institutional datasets (e.g., applicant demographics, financial aid awards, retention rates) with external data sources (e.g., labor market trends, census projections) to simulate student decision-making processes, institutional revenue streams, and operational costs. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to refine parameter estimation and validate model outputs against historical patterns. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, we aim to run thousands of parameterized scenarios to identify optimal financial aid distribution strategies, predict enrollment cliffs, and quantify the fiscal impacts of alternative tuition models. Expected outcomes include a scalable tool for higher education administrators to proactively address enrollment challenges, mitigate financial risks, and evaluate equity implications of policy changes. The computational intensity of simulating diverse student populations and longitudinal interactions necessitates access to HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and rapid iteration. This work aligns with national priorities in higher education administration by advancing data-driven approaches to institutional resilience while addressing critical gaps in predictive analytics for enrollment management and strategic finance.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: Hearing aid efficacy is limited by the variability of individual auditory anatomy and the dynamic acoustic environments users encounter. Current methodologies for hearing assessment and device fitting rely on generalized protocols, which often fail to account for patient-specific physiological factors or real-world auditory complexities. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate patient-specific cochlear mechanics and auditory pathway responses under diverse acoustic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element models of individualized ear anatomies derived from clinical imaging data and integrate them with machine learning algorithms trained on large-scale audiometric datasets. These models will simulate how different hearing aid configurations interact with anatomical variations and environmental noise profiles, enabling the optimization of signal processing parameters for personalized hearing solutions. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing capabilities to handle iterative simulations across thousands of anatomically unique cases and real-time acoustic scenarios, tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Additionally, we will employ neural networks to analyze longitudinal patient outcome data, identifying patterns in device performance tied to specific fitting strategies. Anticipated outcomes include a predictive framework for personalized hearing aid prescriptions, reducing trial-and-error adjustments in clinical practice. This work will advance precision audiology by bridging gaps between device technology and biological heterogeneity, while establishing scalable computational tools for future research in hearing rehabilitation. The requested resources will directly support the creation of open-source software for hearing professionals, fostering innovation in a field where computational modeling remains underutilized.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to test the hearing of, and to select, fit and dispense appropriate hearing aids for, patients. Includes instruction in acoustics, anatomy and physiology of the ear, hearing testing, hearing aid fitting and technology, health promotion and rehabilitation, counseling and communication, business management, and professional ethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic, adaptive scheduling for large-scale construction projects under uncertainty, integrating real-time data streams from IoT sensors, supply chain logistics, and environmental monitoring systems. Traditional construction scheduling methods rely on static critical path models that fail to account for cascading delays from material shortages, labor variability, weather disruptions, or equipment failures. The proposed system will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with hybrid simulation (discrete-event and system dynamics) to create a decision-support tool capable of predictive scenario analysis and autonomous schedule reconfiguration. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multi-source data at scale, including geospatial inputs, equipment telemetry, and supplier dashboards, while running parallel simulations to evaluate thousands of contingency plans in near-real time. Machine learning components will be embedded to identify latent patterns in delay propagation and refine risk probability estimates through iterative project benchmarking. The computational architecture will leverage graph neural networks to model complex interdependencies between tasks, resources, and external constraints, with validation against historical datasets from 12 completed infrastructure projects. Expected outcomes include a 15-20% reduction in schedule overruns for test cases involving renewable energy plant construction, along with an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource allocation under volatile conditions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges construction operations research with computational sustainability science, offering novel methodologies for resilient project management in climate-sensitive environments. The work will directly inform revised industry standards for dynamic scheduling in the ASCE Construction Institute’s digital transformation guidelines while advancing HPC applications in construction-specific combinatorial optimization problems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage, coordinate, and supervise the construction process. Includes instruction in commercial, residential, mechanical, highway/heavy civil, electrical, environmental, industrial, and specialty construction; facilities management; budgeting and cost control; logistics and materials management; organization and scheduling; personnel management and labor relations; site safety; construction contracting; construction processes and techniques; and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of next-generation wireless communication systems necessitates advanced computational methods to address challenges in resource allocation, interference management, and energy efficiency. Current analytical models struggle to capture the dynamic behavior of large-scale heterogeneous networks operating at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing distributed antenna systems and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces in ultra-dense urban environments. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement parallelized electromagnetic wave propagation models using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods coupled with multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for stochastic channel modeling with distributed optimization techniques to balance spectral efficiency and power consumption across dynamically changing topologies. By scaling these simulations to networks exceeding 10,000 nodes—a magnitude beyond current experimental testbeds—we aim to identify fundamental tradeoffs between latency, reliability, and energy use in extreme-density scenarios. The resulting datasets and validated models will provide critical insights for 6G protocol development while establishing open-source tools for massive MIMO beamforming optimization. This work directly addresses the computational bottlenecks preventing real-time adaptation in software-defined radios and lays the foundation for energy-aware network architectures capable of supporting emerging applications in augmented reality and industrial IoT. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential for achieving the required simulation throughput and enabling parameter space exploration at unprecedented scales.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronics, and Communications Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical, electronics, and communications engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social interaction patterns among older adults in digitally connected communities, leveraging computational modeling to explore how emergent technologies influence psychosocial well-being in aging populations. While gerontology is traditionally situated within health sciences, this study adopts a social science lens to analyze how older adults navigate, adapt to, and reshape virtual social ecosystems—a niche intersecting aging studies, digital sociology, and human-computer interaction. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable frameworks to quantify the bidirectional relationship between technology-mediated communication and age-related shifts in social needs, particularly in heterogeneous populations with varying digital literacies. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating longitudinal social network evolution among older adults, integrating empirical data from wearable sensors, social media engagement metrics, and demographic surveys. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale parameter sweeps to test hypotheses about how algorithmic personalization, platform accessibility features, and cohort-specific cultural norms modulate outcomes such as loneliness, social capital accumulation, and intergenerational connectivity. The ABM will incorporate machine learning submodules trained on real-world interaction datasets to refine decision rules for agent behaviors, requiring GPU-accelerated workloads for both model calibration and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include a novel computational framework for predicting technology adoption barriers in aging populations and evidence-based insights into designing inclusive digital spaces that align with psychosocial aging trajectories. By bridging gerontological health research with computational social science methodologies, this work aims to inform policy and industry strategies that prioritize equitable social participation in an increasingly digitized aging society.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine approaches in pediatric critical care, where clinical outcomes remain highly variable due to developmental, genetic, and environmental factors. A key challenge lies in integrating multi-omic data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with real-time clinical variables—such as vital signs, treatment responses, and developmental trajectories—to predict individualized risks of sepsis, organ failure, or neurodevelopmental impairment in critically ill children. Current predictive models, largely derived from adult populations, fail to account for the dynamic biological processes unique to pediatric growth stages. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining large-scale data integration, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning. Longitudinal clinical data from electronic health records (n≈10,000 patients) will be merged with single-cell RNA sequencing and plasma proteomics from a prospective cohort of neonates and children admitted to intensive care. Dimensionality reduction techniques and federated learning will address heterogeneity and missing data, while mechanistic models of immune-metabolic pathways, parameterized using patient-specific omics, will simulate pathophysiological responses under varying treatment conditions. Graph neural networks will then identify critical nodes in cross-scale biological networks predictive of clinical deterioration or recovery. These outputs will train ensemble models to stratify patients by risk and optimize intervention timing. HPC resources are essential for parallel processing of omics datasets, large-scale parameter sweeps in mechanistic models, and distributed training of deep learning architectures. Expected outcomes include actionable predictive tools for pediatric intensivists, reducing trial-and-error approaches to life-support decisions. By elucidating developmental stage-specific disease mechanisms, this work will also inform targeted therapeutic discovery. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools to accelerate translational research in pediatric medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the comprehensive care and treatment of all aspects of human growth and development from conception through fetal life, infancy, childhood and adolescence, including preventive and therapeutic regimes. May included related research in behavioral aspects of illness, related family and community medicine issues, and emergency and critical care procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and real-time environmental simulations in architectural design processes. The research addresses a critical gap in current computational design methodologies, which often prioritize formal or aesthetic outcomes over dynamic, context-sensitive performance metrics. By developing a novel framework that combines generative adversarial networks (GANs), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and agent-based pedestrian movement modeling, the project aims to create adaptive design systems capable of iteratively optimizing architectural proposals for energy efficiency, thermal comfort, and spatial circulation in dense urban contexts. The computational workflow will process multi-scale datasets, including high-resolution LiDAR scans of existing urban fabric, historical climate data, and real-time sensor inputs from IoT networks, to generate and evaluate thousands of design permutations. This requires parallel processing of complex 3D geometry operations, coupled with machine learning model training on heterogeneous urban datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for performance-driven architectural design, validated through case studies in three climatically distinct cities. The research contributes to emerging paradigms in computational architecture by bridging gaps between generative design, environmental simulation, and human behavior modeling—advancing both methodological innovation and practical applications for sustainable urban development. Successful implementation of this framework could significantly reduce the computational barriers currently limiting holistic performance-based design approaches in architectural practice and education.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of architecture, cities, landscapes, designed objects, ornament, architectural photography, and material culture in diverse places and time periods, and the social and aesthetic dimensions of contemporary architecture, landscapes, and cities, emphasizing issues of sustainable environments, new forms of urbanism, and the use of digital media for visualization and analysis. Includes instruction in the fundamentals of architecture, design, environmental and sustainability studies, historic preservation, landscape architecture, studio art, and urban affairs and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Punjabi language dynamics and literary heritage. Despite Punjabi’s status as a major global language with rich dialectal diversity and a vast literary corpus, systematic large-scale studies of its linguistic evolution, regional variations, and sociocultural influences remain limited due to computational constraints. The research problem centers on the need to model phonetic, syntactic, and lexical patterns across Punjabi dialects and historical texts, which require processing terabytes of unstructured data, including digitized manuscripts, oral recordings, and modern digital content. The project proposes a multi-phase computational approach. First, parallelized text processing and phonetic alignment algorithms will be deployed to analyze dialectal variations in spoken and written corpora, spanning major Punjabi dialects (e.g., Majhi, Doabi, Malwai). Second, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to automate the semantic and stylistic analysis of pre-modern and modern Punjabi literature, identifying temporal shifts in thematic focus and linguistic innovation. Third, graph-based network analyses will map the diffusion of loanwords and syntactic structures across contact languages (e.g., Urdu, Hindi) in urban and rural contexts. These methods demand significant GPU-accelerated computing power for training deep learning architectures and processing high-resolution scans of aging manuscripts via optical character recognition (OCR) optimized for Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi scripts. Expected outcomes include the creation of an open-access computational repository for Punjabi linguistics, comprising dialect atlases, annotated literary corpora, and tools for low-resource language NLP applications. The project will directly contribute to preserving endangered dialectal forms, enhancing pedagogical resources for Punjabi instruction, and informing policy frameworks for language technology development in South Asia. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work aims to establish a paradigm for interdisciplinary research in less-resourced languages within digital humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Punjabi language (Punjabi) and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time encrypted data query processing for decentralized business intelligence systems, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of cybersecurity, quantum-inspired algorithms, and distributed database architectures. As organizations increasingly adopt hybrid cloud-edge infrastructures, conventional encryption methods create latency bottlenecks when analyzing sensitive operational data across fragmented networks, limiting the agility of decision-support systems. The study proposes a novel computational framework leveraging lattice-based homomorphic encryption combined with quantum annealing-inspired optimization to enable secure, parallelized query execution on distributed business datasets. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-node environments with varying data locality constraints, testing neural network-based workload predictors against combinatorial optimization models for query routing. Key objectives include developing a GPU-accelerated library for privacy-preserving aggregate operations and benchmarking against traditional federated learning approaches using synthetic datasets modeling supply chain logistics and cross-institutional financial transactions. Expected outcomes include quantifiable performance metrics for encrypted join operations at petabyte scale and adaptive resource allocation strategies for heterogeneous computing clusters. This work aims to advance the state of practice in secure distributed analytics, directly supporting compliance-driven industries requiring both rigorous data protection and subsecond response times for complex business queries. The computational intensity of simulating quantum annealing effects on classical hardware and the need for massively parallel encryption/decryption cycles necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with specialized cryptographic acceleration capabilities. Successful validation of the framework could inform new standards for responsive security architectures in management information systems, particularly for organizations operating in regulated verticals with strict data sovereignty requirements.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interactions between dietary components, human metabolism, and gut microbiota in the context of personalized nutrition. While dietary guidelines are often generalized, individual responses to food—shaped by genetic, microbial, and metabolic variability—remain poorly understood, limiting the efficacy of population-wide recommendations. Current experimental methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-scale nature of these interactions, necessitating computational approaches to integrate heterogeneous datasets and simulate biological networks. The research will develop a multi-layered computational framework combining pharmacokinetic modeling, agent-based simulations of microbial communities, and machine learning to predict individualized nutrient metabolism and its health impacts. High-resolution metabolomic and metagenomic datasets from clinical cohorts will inform model parameters, while HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of host-microbe-diet interactions across diverse virtual populations. Key challenges include scaling dynamic flux balance analysis to model microbial community metabolism in real-time and optimizing neural networks to identify nonlinear relationships between dietary patterns, microbial gene expression, and host biomarkers. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform for simulating personalized dietary responses and actionable insights into how specific microbiota configurations modulate nutrient bioavailability in metabolic diseases such as type 2 diabetes. By bridging computational biology, systems nutrition, and data science, this work aims to advance precision nutrition strategies while addressing the computational bottlenecks inherent in modeling biological systems with high dimensionality and stochasticity. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and the storage of petabyte-scale simulation outputs, which are critical for achieving the resolution required to translate mechanistic insights into clinical applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationships between food consumption and human development and health. Includes instruction in the cellular and molecular processes of food processing in the human body, related metabolic processes, the relationship of food and nutrition to disease, and nutritional needs across the life span.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize individualized learning pathways for students with intellectual disabilities enrolled in Comprehensive Transition and Postsecondary (CTP) programs. Despite the growing emphasis on inclusive education, there remains a critical gap in data-driven tools that dynamically integrate academic, social, and vocational progress to support personalized interventions. The research problem centers on the complexity of synthesizing heterogeneous data—such as skill acquisition rates, behavioral interactions, employment training outcomes, and longitudinal well-being metrics—into actionable insights for educators and program coordinators. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations and machine learning models. These computational methods will simulate student trajectories under varying program configurations, identify predictors of successful transition to employment, and optimize resource allocation for skill-building activities. The agent-based models will incorporate anonymized student data, including academic performance, social engagement logs, and workplace training evaluations, to replicate the multifaceted interactions within CTP ecosystems. Concurrently, neural networks will analyze unstructured data (e.g., mentorship notes, self-assessment journals) to detect patterns in self-advocacy development and barriers to independent living. The computational intensity of processing multimodal datasets—spanning terabyte-scale records from 15+ partner institutions—necessitates parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated training pipelines. Expected outcomes include a predictive dashboard for educators to tailor support strategies, evidence-based recommendations for program design, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit to model the long-term impacts of policy changes on employment equity. By bridging computational science and inclusive education research, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for enhancing CTP efficacy while advancing interdisciplinary discourse on equitable resource distribution in postsecondary transitions.
cip_definition: A comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program that provides students with intellectual disabilities with academic enrichment, socialization, independent living skills, self-advocacy skills, and integrated work experiences and career skills that lead to gainful employment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the usability and effectiveness of multimodal technical communication materials, with a focus on optimizing complex documentation systems for diverse audiences. As technical communication increasingly relies on interactive digital platforms, traditional text-centric evaluation methods fail to account for dynamic user interactions, multivariate content delivery, and accessibility requirements across devices. The research problem centers on creating scalable models to simulate user engagement patterns, predict comprehension barriers, and test adaptive content strategies in high-dimensional scenarios. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based simulations of user interactions with technical documentation systems, incorporating natural language processing to analyze semantic coherence across multimedia components and machine learning models to identify patterns in large-scale usability datasets. Computational experiments will evaluate how variables such as information architecture, visual hierarchy, and adaptive content delivery impact user task success rates across different demographic and expertise groups. The project will also employ GPU-accelerated rendering to model real-time document accessibility adjustments for users with disabilities. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing technical communication products during the design phase, reducing iterative testing costs, and improving inclusivity metrics. By enabling large-scale simulation of user experiences that would be impractical to test empirically, this research aims to advance evidence-based practices in technical communication while developing computational methods transferable to emerging domains like augmented reality documentation systems. The requested computing resources are critical for handling the parallel processing demands of multivariate simulations and training deep learning models on interaction log datasets exceeding 10^6 events.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the structural and evolutionary mechanisms underlying host-cell manipulation by RNA viruses, with a focus on elucidating how viral protein dynamics and genetic variation influence pathogenesis. A critical gap exists in understanding the real-time conformational changes of viral entry proteins during host receptor binding and the relationship between viral quasispecies diversity and immune evasion. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of viral envelope proteins interacting with host membranes, alongside phylogenetic reconstructions of viral populations from longitudinal clinical sequencing data. MD simulations will model key glycoproteins (e.g., influenza hemagglutinin, coronaviral spike) to resolve transient structural states that mediate membrane fusion, using all-atom and coarse-grained approaches. Concurrently, evolutionary analysis of whole-genome viral sequences will identify conserved versus adaptive regions under host immune pressure. These computational workflows demand significant parallel processing for ensemble simulations spanning microsecond timescales and maximum-likelihood phylogenetics on terabyte-scale sequence datasets. The integration of structural and evolutionary data aims to pinpoint conserved functional domains vulnerable to cross-reactive therapeutics and predict antigenic shifts in emerging strains. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into viral entry, frameworks for predicting strain fitness, and actionable targets for broad-spectrum antiviral design. This work directly advances virological knowledge by linking molecular-scale protein behavior to population-level evolution, with implications for improving pandemic preparedness and adaptive vaccine platforms. Successful execution requires dedicated HPC allocations for GPU-accelerated simulations, large-memory nodes for phylogenetic inference, and scalable storage for multi-modal data integration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of subcellular pieces of genetic material, called viruses, that inhabit living cells in parasitical relationships and their role in disease. Includes instruction in virus taxonomy and systematics, viral structures, viral genetics, prions, virus/host cell interaction, viral pathogenesis, and applications to specific topics such as cancer biology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of anthropogenic impacts on terrestrial hydrological systems and their feedbacks with biogeochemical cycles, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, multi-scale interactions between land use, subsurface hydrology, and contaminant transport. Rapid urbanization and agricultural intensification have altered natural hydrologic pathways, increasing risks of groundwater contamination and ecosystem degradation. However, existing models often lack the spatial resolution and computational capacity to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including high-resolution satellite remote sensing, geophysical surveys, and long-term geochemical monitoring—into predictive frameworks. To address this gap, we propose a coupled modeling approach combining 3D hydrogeological simulations with machine learning-driven analysis of spatial-temporal biogeochemical data. The HPC resources will enable (1) parallelized finite element modeling of subsurface flow and contaminant dispersion at meter-scale resolution across watersheds and (2) training of convolutional neural networks to identify contaminant source zones from multi-spectral satellite imagery and ground-based sensor arrays. By dynamically linking these components within an HPC-optimized workflow, the project will quantify how evolving land management practices alter contaminant mobility under projected climate scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include improved predictive capacity for pollutant thresholds in vulnerable aquifers, spatially explicit risk maps for stakeholders, and open-source computational tools for scaling process-based hydrology to regional systems. This work directly supports sustainable groundwater management goals while advancing methodological integration of GIS, remote sensing, and physical modeling—a critical need in Earth and Environmental Sciences research. The requested allocation will provide essential capacity for data assimilation, model calibration, and uncertainty quantification across billion-cell domains, which exceed the limits of institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on earth, its environments, human activities, and the linkages between them. Includes instruction biogeochemistry, climate dynamics, geographical information science (GIS), geophysics, hydrology, landscape ecology, meteorology, pollution control and satellite remote sensing analysis.

abstract: The genetic architecture underlying complex phenotypic traits often involves intricate interactions between regulatory elements, epigenetic modifications, and non-coding genomic regions. However, resolving these interactions at scale remains challenging due to limitations in computational frameworks capable of integrating multi-omics data while accounting for population-level variation. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline to analyze the combinatorial effects of regulatory variants, chromatin accessibility, and three-dimensional genome organization on gene expression dynamics. Leveraging whole-genome sequencing, ATAC-seq, and Hi-C data from a diverse cohort of 5,000 individuals, we will employ graph-based algorithms to model spatial interactions between enhancers, promoters, and structural chromatin domains. Parallelized Bayesian inference methods will quantify how allelic heterogeneity in non-coding regions influences transcriptional networks across cell types. A second aim focuses on simulating evolutionary trajectories of regulatory landscapes using forward-time population genetics models optimized for GPU acceleration. These simulations will test hypotheses about selection pressures shaping cis-regulatory architectures in humans compared to non-human primates. The computational workflow will utilize containerized environments for reproducibility and integrate with existing genomic databases through federated querying. By enabling simultaneous analysis of regulatory variant effects, chromatin topology, and evolutionary conservation patterns, this resource-intensive approach will provide novel insights into the hierarchical organization of gene regulation. Anticipated outcomes include identifying functionally coordinated regulatory hubs associated with developmental disorders and establishing predictive models for pleiotropic effects of non-coding variants. The developed tools will be disseminated as open-source packages, enhancing community capacity to interrogate multidimensional genomic datasets. This work directly advances foundational genetics research by bridging mechanistic studies of gene regulation with population-scale genomic analyses.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the organization, recombination, function, regulation, and transmission of heritable information in biological organisms at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in Mendelian genetics, mechanisms of gene regulation, chromosome structure and replication, epigenetic phenomena, DNA repair and recombination, sex determination, genetic interactions between genomes, and molecular evolution.

abstract: The increasing complexity of supply chain dynamics in the automotive, marine, and aviation aftermarkets necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize inventory management and distribution strategies. This research addresses the challenge of integrating real-time telematics and IoT data from connected vehicles and equipment into predictive demand forecasting models for replacement parts. Traditional inventory systems in vehicle parts marketing rely on historical sales data and static regional demand patterns, often leading to inefficiencies in storage, delayed fulfillment, and excess waste. This project proposes a novel computational framework that synthesizes high-frequency sensor data (e.g., engine performance metrics, component wear patterns) with customer behavior analytics to predict part failure risks and regional demand spikes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process terabytes of streaming telematics data, train deep learning models on temporal-spatial demand signals, and simulate multi-echelon inventory networks under dynamic scenarios. The computational pipeline includes graph neural networks to model interdependencies between parts failure cascades and transformer-based architectures for cross-modal fusion of structured sales data with unstructured service logs. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for regional distribution centers, enabling proactive stock rebalancing and dynamic pricing adjustments. The project’s significance lies in bridging the gap between vehicular IoT ecosystems and business operations, reducing supply chain waste by an estimated 15–20% in pilot sectors, while improving service-level agreements for commercial and consumer clients. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances interdisciplinary research at the intersection of operational analytics, embedded systems data, and sustainable logistics—a niche yet critical domain for next-generation vehicle parts marketing.
cip_title: Vehicle and Vehicle Parts and Accessories Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of replacement parts and other end-use supplies in the automotive, marine, and aviation industries. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, principles of vehicular technologies, storage and distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving interplay between Canadian constitutional principles and complex, large-scale societal datasets. The core problem lies in understanding how foundational legal frameworks—particularly those rooted in the Canadian Constitution and Commonwealth legal traditions—adapt to dynamic social, cultural, and technological shifts. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically map the nonlinear relationships between judicial reasoning, legislative amendments, and emergent public values across decades of case law and policy documents. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to process over 150,000 Canadian court decisions, parliamentary debates, and historical legal texts, identifying latent patterns in judicial rhetoric, precedent adoption, and constitutional interpretation. Concurrently, agent-based modeling will simulate the cascading effects of hypothetical legal reforms on institutional behavior and rights-based disputes. By integrating these computational approaches, the research aims to construct a multidimensional network model of legal evolution, quantifying how specific doctrinal shifts influence systemic resilience or vulnerability. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database linking constitutional clauses to their sociopolitical contexts, predictive frameworks for assessing the downstream impacts of landmark rulings, and methodological innovations in computational legal theory. This work will provide novel insights into the adaptive capacity of Canada’s legal architecture while establishing scalable tools for analyzing jurisprudence as a complex, data-rich system. The requested HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based language models on legal corpora, running high-fidelity policy simulations, and managing the terabyte-scale integration of heterogeneous legal and historical datasets.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the Canadian legal system, Constitution law, and jurisprudence. Includes instruction in legal history, legal sociology, philosophy of law, Constitutional law, Commonwealth law, legal procedure, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing equitable, culturally responsive instructional strategies in multilingual K-12 classrooms through advanced computational modeling. Current approaches to curriculum adaptation for culturally diverse learners often rely on static frameworks that inadequately capture the dynamic interplay of language acquisition, cultural identity, and individualized learning trajectories. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) simulating classroom interactions across diverse cultural and linguistic profiles. These models will integrate anonymized student performance data, sociolinguistic surveys, and ethnographic classroom observations from partner school districts serving predominantly immigrant and refugee populations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these simulations to account for complex variables, including code-switching patterns, cross-cultural communication dynamics, and the impact of culturally grounded pedagogical interventions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify predictive relationships between instructional strategies and learning outcomes across simulated student subgroups. The computational pipeline will also leverage natural language processing to analyze multilingual student writing samples, enabling real-time feedback systems for teachers. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating data-driven, adaptive lesson plans that respond to classroom cultural composition, as well as evidence-based guidelines for deploying educational technologies in linguistically diverse settings. By modeling how cultural context mediates learning processes at scale, this work aims to advance teacher preparation programs’ capacity to address systemic inequities in multicultural education. The requested HPC resources will support parallelized simulation runs, large-scale sentiment analysis of student narratives, and optimization of hybrid human-AI teaching frameworks tailored to underrepresented cultural groups.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, and implementation of instructional and advising services for culturally diverse learning populations. Includes instruction in cultural diversity, at-risk populations, multilingual and ESL education, program and curriculum design, instructional technology, information resources, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling and communicating with multicultural populations, law and regulations, and applications to specific cultural groups, educational services, and research issues.

abstract: Gene therapies hold transformative potential for treating genetic disorders, yet their development is hindered by challenges in optimizing delivery systems, predicting off-target effects, and personalizing treatments. This project seeks to address these barriers by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model the interactions of viral and nonviral gene delivery vectors with host genomes, tissues, and immune systems. The research problem centers on the inefficiency of current vector design pipelines, which rely heavily on trial-and-error experimental approaches that are time-intensive, costly, and limited in their ability to simulate complex biological systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven genome editing prediction, and multi-omics data analysis.
