MD simulations will model structural dynamics of adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsids and lipid nanoparticles to identify modifications that enhance tissue-specific targeting and evade immune detection. Concurrently, neural networks trained on CRISPR-Cas9 editing outcomes and single-cell RNA-seq datasets will predict gene expression profiles following therapeutic interventions, enabling in silico screening of candidate therapies. These workflows will be scaled using GPU-accelerated nodes to handle systems with >10^6 atoms (for MD) and terabyte-scale genomic datasets (for ML/omics integration). The expected outcomes include (1) predictive models for vector-host interactions, (2) optimized vector designs with improved efficacy and safety profiles, and (3) a computational platform for patient-specific therapy simulation. By reducing reliance on low-throughput experimental methods, this work aims to accelerate the translation of gene therapies into clinical practice while addressing critical bioethical concerns around off-target risks. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary computational granularity and throughput, which cannot be supported by local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics to the therapeutic treatment of diseases and inherited abnormalities through the targeted modification of gene expression, and prepares individuals to administer genetic therapies. Includes instruction in medical genetics, genome analysis, pharmacology of gene transfer, viral vectors, nonviral therapeutic techniques, genetic screening, targeted gene delivery, vector production, safety and quality assurance, clinical trials management, and bioethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop advanced computational models to enhance threat detection and resilience planning for critical infrastructure systems vulnerable to cyber-physical attacks. As infrastructure networks grow in complexity and interconnectivity, traditional risk assessment methods struggle to account for cascading failures, adversarial machine learning exploits, and dynamic threat landscapes. To address this gap, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model infrastructure interdependencies, attacker behaviors, and mitigation strategies. The computational approach integrates graph neural networks to represent infrastructure topology, reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive adversaries, and fluid dynamics models to predict physical cascades (e.g., power grid failures impacting water distribution). HPC resources are essential for executing millions of parallelized attack-defend scenarios across heterogeneous infrastructure datasets, enabling probabilistic risk quantification at unprecedented resolution. Expected outcomes include an open-source algorithmic toolkit for identifying system-specific vulnerabilities, optimizing defense resource allocation, and stress-testing incident response protocols under realistic constraints. By enabling granular analysis of emerging threats like AI-driven cyberattacks or climate-aggravated physical disruptions, this work aims to advance predictive security analytics for transportation, energy, and communication systems. The resulting models will provide actionable insights for infrastructure operators and policymakers, bridging the gap between theoretical security science and operational resilience requirements. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale graph computations, with an estimated need for 200,000 node-hours to validate the framework against real-world infrastructure case studies.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in security science and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address computational bottlenecks in processing high-fidelity 3-D models for industrial design and manufacturing applications, where traditional computing systems struggle with the scalability of complex geometries, real-time simulations, and multi-objective optimization. The research focuses on leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable rapid iterative design, analysis, and validation of resource-intensive 3-D models, particularly for additive manufacturing and large-scale structural systems. Key computational challenges include the parallelization of finite element analysis (FEA) for stress testing lattice-based structures, dynamic mesh refinement for multi-resolution 3-D scans, and machine learning-driven topology optimization under material constraints. The proposed methods integrate distributed computing frameworks to accelerate CAD-based simulations, GPU-accelerated rendering for real-time design visualization, and scalable algorithms for generative design workflows that balance performance metrics such as weight, durability, and production cost. By deploying these HPC-enabled workflows, the project aims to reduce computational time for industrial-scale 3-D model iterations by 60–80% compared to current single-node systems, while improving predictive accuracy in material behavior simulations. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for distributed 3-D model processing, validated benchmarks for HPC resource allocation in design tasks, and case studies demonstrating optimized manufacturing workflows for automotive component prototyping and architectural formwork systems. This work will directly enhance the accessibility of advanced computational design methodologies for small-to-medium enterprises, bridging gaps between theoretical model complexity and practical production feasibility in engineering technology domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the use of three-dimensional (3-D) computer technology to create technical illustrations and models used in manufacturing, design, production, and construction. Includes instruction in 3-D computer-aided design (CAD), 3-D printing, 3-D model design and construction, and 3-D scanning.

abstract: The integration of multi-modal clinical and anatomic data presents a critical challenge in advancing diagnostic precision for complex diseases. Current approaches in anatomic and clinical pathology often rely on fragmented analyses of histopathology images, genomic profiles, and laboratory biomarkers, limiting the ability to uncover systemic pathophysiological relationships. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a scalable computational framework to unify heterogeneous datasets, including whole-slide imaging (WSI), next-generation sequencing (NGS), and clinical laboratory metrics, for enhanced disease classification and prognostic modeling. The primary research problem lies in efficiently processing and correlating high-dimensional data—such as terabyte-scale WSIs and genome-wide variant calls—while accounting for spatial, molecular, and temporal heterogeneity within patient cohorts. To achieve this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven pipeline leveraging distributed deep learning for WSI analysis, parallelized bioinformatics workflows for NGS data, and graph-based algorithms to model cross-modal interactions. Computational methods will include training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on GPU clusters to detect subtle anatomic abnormalities in WSIs, deploying Apache Spark for cohort-scale genomic variant aggregation, and employing graph neural networks (GNNs) to map tissue-level morphologic features to molecular alterations. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models integrating pathology, genomics, and laboratory data, with validation across retrospective cases from institutional biorepositories. Expected outcomes include (1) a reproducible framework for multi-modal data fusion in diagnostic pathology, (2) predictive models linking anatomic phenotypes to molecular subtypes in solid tumors and inflammatory disorders, and (3) open-source tools to optimize laboratory workflow integration. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy, inform targeted testing protocols, and establish computational best practices for pathology departments transitioning to digital workflows. By addressing critical bottlenecks in data scale and complexity, the project aligns with national priorities for precision medicine and AI-ready clinical laboratories.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease and anatomic abnormalities. Includes instruction in performing general autopsies, forensic medicine, laboratory management, and quality control.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the challenge of optimizing energy-efficient thermal management systems in advanced manufacturing processes, a critical bottleneck in industrial applications of mechanical engineering-related technologies. Current analytical models fail to capture the complex multiphysics interactions between phase-change materials, transient heat loads, and nonlinear fluid-structure phenomena in high-precision machining environments. This project will develop a scalable computational framework combining lattice Boltzmann methods for multiphase flow simulation with finite element analysis of thermoelastic deformation. The framework will be implemented on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to enable coupled 3D simulations at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-10µm scale) and temporal durations (full operational cycles). Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement for dynamic interface tracking and hybrid OpenMP-MPI parallelization to efficiently distribute memory-intensive calculations across nodes. Initial validation against experimental infrared thermography data from CNC machining centers demonstrates the method's potential to predict thermal warping with <5% error relative to physical measurements. Successful implementation will enable virtual prototyping of next-generation cooling systems with predictive maintenance capabilities, directly addressing industry needs for reduced energy consumption and improved machining accuracy. The requested computing resources will support parametric studies across 200+ design configurations, generating a public dataset of simulated thermal profiles to benefit the broader manufacturing research community. Outcomes will advance computational methodologies in mechanical systems analysis while providing practical tools for sustainable manufacturing optimization, with estimated energy savings potential of 15-20% in target industrial use cases.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mechanical engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in pharmacy operations and patient safety by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize medication dispensing workflows and predict medication-related risks. Pharmacy technicians and assistants play a vital role in ensuring accurate prescription fulfillment, yet inefficiencies in workflow design, human error, and complex patient-specific factors can lead to delays, errors, or adverse drug events. Current manual and rule-based systems often lack the capacity to dynamically adapt to real-world variables such as fluctuating prescription volumes, drug interaction complexities, or patient-specific contraindications. To bridge this gap, this research proposes the development of computational models that simulate pharmacy operations and patient medication histories to identify risk patterns and operational bottlenecks. Using anonymized electronic health records, prescription datasets, and pharmacy workflow logs, machine learning algorithms will be trained to predict high-risk scenarios, such as drug-drug interactions or dosage errors, while discrete-event simulations will model staffing and workflow configurations under varying demand conditions. The HPC environment is essential for processing large-scale datasets, running parallelized simulations, and iteratively refining predictive models to account for multidimensional variables, including patient demographics, drug characteristics, and regulatory constraints. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into workflow optimization, predictive tools to flag high-risk prescriptions, and scalable strategies for resource allocation in diverse pharmacy settings. By integrating computational analytics with pharmacy practice, this project aims to reduce preventable errors, enhance operational efficiency, and support evidence-based training protocols for pharmacy technicians, ultimately improving patient outcomes and healthcare system resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Surgical wound healing and tissue reconstruction outcomes remain highly variable due to complex interactions between patient-specific biological factors, surgical techniques, and postoperative care. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individualized healing trajectories or optimize reconstructive strategies, leading to preventable complications such as dehiscence, infection, and poor aesthetic outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale wound healing dynamics and simulate reconstructive outcomes under diverse biological and biomechanical conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate patient-derived genomic, proteomic, and imaging data with mechanistic models of cellular behavior, extracellular matrix remodeling, and mechanical stress distributions. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular interactions during inflammation and proliferation phases, while finite element analyses will predict tissue deformation and perfusion in complex anatomical geometries. Machine learning pipelines will identify predictive biomarkers from multi-omics datasets and clinical records, enabling risk stratification. The computational platform will be validated against a retrospective cohort of 850 surgical cases with longitudinal wound imaging and histopathological data. By enabling real-time simulation of hypothetical surgical interventions—including flap design modifications or adjunct therapies—this resource will advance personalized decision-making in reconstructive surgery. Anticipated outcomes include a validated predictive tool for wound complication risks, biomechanical guidelines for flap design optimization, and novel biomarkers for targeted therapies. The HPC environment is critical for scaling spatially explicit simulations across anatomical variability, managing high-dimensional data integration, and enabling rapid parameter sweeps to test clinical hypotheses. This work bridges computational systems biology and surgical innovation, with potential to reduce revision surgeries, improve functional recovery, and lower healthcare costs in complex wound management.
cip_definition: Research focused on Surgical Wound and Reconstruction

abstract: Habitat fragmentation and biodiversity loss pose critical challenges for global ecosystems, yet predicting long-term ecological outcomes under dynamic human pressures remains computationally intractable with conventional methods. This project seeks to advance conservation planning by developing spatially explicit, multi-scale models that integrate landscape genomics, species interaction networks, and anthropogenic disturbance regimes. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to analyze continental-scale habitat connectivity patterns across 27 threatened vertebrate species in Southeast Asia's Sundaland biodiversity hotspot, where accelerating deforestation and infrastructure development require urgent predictive frameworks. The computational workflow combines maximum entropy species distribution models with circuit theory connectivity analyses across 1km² resolution grids, incorporating temporal land-use change projections from satellite-derived datasets (2000-2030). A novel agent-based modeling component will simulate meta-population dynamics under alternative conservation scenarios, requiring parallel processing of >10⁶ individual agents with genetically informed dispersal behaviors. Machine learning approaches will identify critical habitat corridors and evolutionary significant units most vulnerable to fragmentation effects. Expected outcomes include: 1) predictive maps of genetic diversity loss under proposed development plans, 2) optimized corridor networks maintaining >90% of current connectivity, and 3) open-source computational tools for integrating genomic resilience into protected area design. These resources will directly inform multinational conservation policies under the ASEAN Wildlife Enforcement Network, while advancing theoretical understanding of extinction thresholds in fragmented landscapes. The requested computing allocation enables processing of 850TB of multispectral imagery, genomic datasets from 15,000 individual samples, and stochastic simulations across 10⁴ possible landscape configurations – a computational scale essential for addressing real-world conservation challenges at the interface of ecological complexity and human development needs.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences to the specific problems of biodiversity, species preservation, ecological sustainability, and habitat fragmentation in the face of advancing human social, economic, and industrial pressures. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental science, biological systems, extinction theory, human-animal and human-plant interaction, ecosystem science and management, wetland conservation, field biology, forest and wildlife biology, and natural history.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance digital scholarship in American Indian and Native American Studies through the development of a collaborative, community-centered platform for analyzing and preserving Indigenous cultural heritage. The research addresses a critical gap in accessible computational tools tailored to the ethical and methodological priorities of Indigenous communities, particularly in managing large-scale digitized materials such as oral histories, ceremonial recordings, and language archives. Current methods for organizing and interpreting these materials often rely on generalized text or audio analysis frameworks, which inadequately address the nonlinear storytelling traditions, contextual dependencies, and sovereignty considerations central to Indigenous knowledge systems. To overcome these limitations, the project will implement a hybrid computational approach combining transformer-based language models fine-tuned on Indigenous linguistic corpora, geospatial-temporal mapping of intergenerational narratives, and community-defined metadata schemas. HPC resources will enable processing of multimodal datasets (audio, video, text) across distributed repositories while maintaining strict data governance protocols co-designed with participating tribal nations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for culturally grounded semantic analysis, a pilot database of annotated materials from three Indigenous language revitalization initiatives, and new computational workflows that prioritize Indigenous ontologies in pattern recognition and knowledge retrieval. By centering Native epistemologies in its technical design, this work aims to set a precedent for ethical AI applications in cultural studies while directly supporting tribal efforts to reclaim and sustain endangered heritage practices. The scalability of the platform will foster interdisciplinary collaborations across Indigenous studies, digital humanities, and language preservation, advancing scholarship that aligns computational innovation with community-driven research sovereignty.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the American Indian, Aleut, Inuit, Hawaiian and other native peoples of the Americas from earliest times until the present, with particular emphasis on U.S. and Canadian populations and their problems but including reference to Caribbean and Latin American native peoples.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale linguistic analysis of syntactic and phonetic evolution across West Germanic languages, with a focus on understudied regional dialects and historical texts. The research addresses a critical gap in Germanic philology: while broad patterns of language change are well-documented, the interplay between localized dialect variations, contact-induced shifts, and internal structural innovations remains poorly quantified, particularly for non-standardized varieties. Using a corpus of digitized texts spanning Old High German to contemporary Dutch, Frisian, and Low German dialects (ca. 8th–21st centuries), we will apply neural sequence modeling and phylogenetic comparative methods to reconstruct probabilistic trajectories of morphosyntactic and phonological change. Computational challenges include aligning irregular orthographic representations across time periods via transformer-based models, simulating contact scenarios through agent-based modeling, and conducting high-resolution acoustic analysis of archival speech recordings. The HPC environment is essential for training custom multilingual BERT variants on historical data, running parallelized comparative simulations, and processing terabytes of audio with forced alignment algorithms. Expected outcomes include 1) a diachronic atlas of syntactic isoglosses in the West Germanic continuum, 2) quantitative evidence for the role of trade networks in propagating phonetic innovations, and 3) open-source tools for historical dialect parsing. This work will directly inform debates about language standardization pressures in minority Germanic communities while demonstrating scalable computational methods for non-English historical linguistics. By integrating philological expertise with ML-driven analysis, the project bridges humanities scholarship and computational rigor, offering new frameworks for studying linguistic diversity in resource-constrained heritage languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Germanic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Germanic languages of Western, Central, and Northern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of the interplay between dark matter, baryonic physics, and relativistic effects in the formation and evolution of galaxy clusters, the largest gravitationally bound structures in the universe. Despite their importance as cosmological probes, current simulations struggle to resolve the multiscale physics governing intracluster plasma, star formation feedback, and relativistic turbulence in cluster cores. This work will employ high-resolution cosmological simulations combining N-body, magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), and non-equilibrium radiation transfer to model the self-consistent co-evolution of dark matter halos and baryonic components across 12 orders of magnitude in mass. The simulations will utilize a novel adaptive mesh refinement code optimized for GPU-accelerated exascale architectures, incorporating relativistic corrections to plasma kinetics and radiation fields in curved spacetime. Key challenges include tracking the thermal history of the intracluster medium under feedback from active galactic nuclei, modeling the impact of primordial magnetic fields on large-scale structure, and calibrating synthetic observables against multiwavelength data from Chandra, Euclid, and CMB-S4. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable unprecedented spatial resolution (<100 pc in cluster cores) while maintaining cosmological volume (1 Gpc³), requiring 2.5 million core-hours and 200 TB of memory-optimized storage. Expected outcomes include (1) improved constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections from small-scale structure comparisons, (2) predictions for X-ray polarization signatures of turbulent dynamos in merging clusters, and (3) open-source release of synthetic sky catalogs to support observational campaigns. By bridging numerical relativity, plasma astrophysics, and observational cosmology, this work will critically inform next-generation surveys probing cosmic acceleration and large-scale structure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theoretical, observational, and numerical study of the structure, properties, and behavior of stars, star systems and clusters, stellar life cycles, and related phenomena of the universe on a large scale. Includes instruction in clusters of galaxies, the cosmic microwave background, plasma kinetics, stellar physics, convolution and non-equilibrium radiation transfer theory, non-Euclidean geometries, mathematical modeling, galactic structure theory, and relativistic astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model the transport and fate of emerging contaminants in urban stormwater systems under climate change stressors. Urbanized watersheds face increasing risks of pollutant mobilization due to intensified precipitation patterns and aging infrastructure, yet current models lack the spatiotemporal resolution to capture dynamic interactions between hydrologic processes, infrastructure performance, and contaminant speciation. The research will employ coupled hydrodynamic and biogeochemical simulations using EPA SWMM and OpenFOAM, integrated with machine learning surrogates to accelerate uncertainty quantification across climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to resolve multi-scale processes, including fine-grained sediment-contaminant interactions at the particle level and system-wide hydraulic responses during extreme rainfall events. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure probabilities of green-gray infrastructure hybrids under projected precipitation regimes, while reactive transport models parameterized with field data from partner municipalities will predict heavy metal and PFAS accumulation hotspots. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive tools for prioritizing infrastructure upgrades based on contaminant-specific risks, (2) optimized hybrid green-gray design configurations that reduce treatment costs by ≥20% under uncertain climate futures, and (3) open-source modules extending the HydroShare platform with contaminant transformation kinetics libraries. The computational framework will directly inform resilience planning in three Great Lakes cities, potentially benefiting 1.2 million residents facing combined sewer overflow risks. By enabling near-real-time simulation of complex feedbacks between climate extremes, engineered systems, and environmental health impacts, this work advances fundamental knowledge in sustainable urban water management while providing actionable strategies to meet EPA stormwater regulations. The requested resources will support 18 months of large ensemble simulations, requiring 256-core parallel runs for >600,000 CPU-hours, with data outputs exceeding 150TB for public archive.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the performance, durability, and environmental compliance of medium/heavy-duty commercial vehicles, with a focus on diesel engine systems and hybrid-electric drivetrain integration. The research addresses a critical industry challenge: balancing engine efficiency and torque requirements with stringent emissions regulations and lifecycle costs. Current diagnostic and optimization methods rely heavily on physical prototyping and static datasets, which are time-intensive, costly, and insufficient for capturing the dynamic interactions between engine components, aftertreatment systems, and emerging hybrid technologies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework combining 3D combustion simulation, machine learning-driven predictive maintenance models, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. Large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will model in-cylinder combustion processes and exhaust gas recirculation dynamics at microsecond resolution, while reinforcement learning techniques will train predictive models for component wear and failure modes using heterogeneous datasets from onboard sensors and maintenance logs. These workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization cycles that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The requested HPC resources will enable parameter sweeps across engine calibration profiles, hybrid battery thermal management strategies, and aftertreatment regeneration schedules to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for heavy-duty powertrains, predictive maintenance algorithms with 15-20% improved accuracy over current industry standards, and optimized hybrid configurations demonstrating 8-12% fuel savings in simulated duty cycles. This work will directly support curriculum modernization in vehicle diagnostics and emission control strategies while providing students with hands-on experience in HPC applications for transportation technology.
cip_title: Medium/ Heavy Vehicle and Truck Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the specialized maintenance and repair of trucks, buses, and other commercial and industrial vehicles. Includes instruction in diesel engine mechanics, suspension and steering, brake systems, electrical and electronic systems, preventive maintenance inspections, drive trains, gasoline engine mechanics, HVAC systems, and auxiliary equipment installation and repair.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of biomechanical forces in cancer progression and metastasis, with a focus on tumor microenvironment dynamics. Despite evidence that mechanical properties of tissues influence cancer cell behavior, the mechanisms linking mechanical stress, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and metastatic spread remain poorly understood. Traditional experimental models struggle to isolate and quantify these multiscale interactions, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose to develop high-fidelity biomechanical models to simulate tumor-ECM interactions under physiological stress conditions, specifically examining how interstitial pressure, ECM stiffness, and fluid shear stress drive cellular invasion and vascular dissemination. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) to model tissue-scale strain distributions and agent-based modeling (ABM) to track individual cell responses to mechanical cues. These multiscale simulations will integrate empirical data from 3D bioprinted tumor models and patient-derived histology to parameterize ECM viscoelasticity and cell adhesion dynamics. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle the high dimensionality of parameter spaces and real-time feedback between tissue deformation and cellular decision-making. Expected outcomes include identifying critical mechanical thresholds that trigger metastatic phenotypes and predicting how ECM-targeted therapies could alter tumor mechanics to suppress invasion. This work will establish a predictive framework for evaluating biomechanical drivers of cancer progression, directly informing translational strategies to disrupt metastasis. The requested HPC resources are essential for executing large-scale simulations, reducing computational bottlenecks in solving coupled solid-fluid mechanics equations, and enabling parameter sensitivity analyses across biologically relevant timescales. By bridging biomechanics and oncology, this project aims to advance mechanistic understanding of cancer mechanobiology while providing open-source computational tools for the broader research community.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, anatomical, and mechanical structure and function of the mechanical aspects of biological systems. Includes courses in anatomy, physiology, kinesiology, mechanics, measurement and instrumentation, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interplay between social connectivity, cognitive health, and environmental factors in aging populations, with a focus on identifying scalable interventions to mitigate late-life social isolation. While gerontology traditionally intersects with health sciences, this study adopts a computational social science lens, integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with longitudinal social network analysis to simulate how age-related changes in mobility, communication habits, and community infrastructure influence social engagement over time. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding non-linear cascades of social withdrawal—a multidimensional phenomenon shaped by psychological thresholds, spatial accessibility, and digital literacy. Computational demands arise from simulating millions of agent interactions across heterogeneous urban and rural environments, parameterized using geospatial data, census microdata, and biomarkers from aging cohort studies. GPU-accelerated simulations will test hypotheses about tipping points in community support systems, while machine learning pipelines will identify high-impact intervention targets from simulated outcomes. Expected outputs include a novel open-source framework for simulating lifecourse social dynamics, validated against longitudinal datasets from transnational aging studies. By quantifying how localized policy decisions (e.g., transportation subsidies, telehealth adoption) propagate through aging social networks, this work aims to provide actionable insights for reducing isolation-related health disparities. The project’s computational scale—encompassing 10^6+ agent-time steps with real-world parameter uncertainty—necessitates parallelized workflows and large-memory nodes to manage stochastic ensemble experiments. Findings will advance methodological integration in gerontology while addressing a pressing societal challenge through computationally rigorous, policy-relevant social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences, psychology and the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of trade networks and cultural exchange across the medieval Near East (7th–15th centuries CE). While textual and archaeological evidence suggests that shifting political boundaries and religious transformations reshaped regional connectivity, the scale, chronology, and socio-economic drivers of these changes remain poorly quantified. Traditional manual analysis of fragmentary sources—including Arabic chronicles, Geniza documents, Byzantine fiscal records, and archaeological trade markers—struggles to synthesize disparate datasets spanning multiple languages, formats, and geographic scales. This project will employ computational methods to model large-scale interaction patterns, integrating natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis, geographic information systems (GIS) for spatial network reconstruction, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate resource flows under variable political and environmental conditions. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of digitized texts, iterating complex network algorithms across temporal layers, and running multi-parameter ABM simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of previously unrecognized hubs and pathways in transregional trade, (2) quantitative assessment of how events like the Crusades or Mongol invasions altered connectivity, and (3) open-access visualization tools to map dynamic interactions between urban centers, religious institutions, and nomadic groups. By bridging historiographic gaps between economic, social, and environmental narratives, this work will provide a scalable framework for computational historical analysis while advancing debates about continuity and disruption in Near Eastern history. The project’s datasets and models will be archived for public reuse, fostering collaborative research across digital humanities and regional studies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in evaluating the long-term impacts of health policy interventions on systemic inequities in healthcare access and outcomes. Current policy analysis frameworks often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture the dynamic interactions between multi-level factors, including institutional regulations, regional resource allocation patterns, and individual health-seeking behaviors. This project will develop and apply an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework enhanced with machine learning to simulate how proposed Medicaid expansion policies in four U.S. states might influence care utilization disparities among vulnerable populations over a 10-year horizon. The computational model will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), census-derived socioeconomic indicators, and state-level healthcare facility inventories, to parameterize approximately 2 million agent interactions across demographic and geographic strata. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the parallel processing demands of calibrating model parameters through iterative Bayesian optimization, validating outputs against historical policy outcomes, and conducting sensitivity analyses across 500+ simulated policy scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive health policy simulation, quantitative projections of how specific reimbursement structures and outreach programs could reduce racial disparities in preventive care uptake, and uncertainty-quantified estimates of policy cost-effectiveness under demographic change. By enabling granular, systems-level analysis of emergent policy effects, this work will provide actionable evidence for designing targeted interventions that account for complex feedback loops between policy implementation and community health dynamics. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter space exploration, and storage of multi-terabyte synthetic populations generated through statistical matching of federal survey microdata.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic analysis of public policy issues related to domestic and international health and health care systems. Includes instruction in contemporary health issues and policies, politics and economics of health care delivery, epidemiology, public health, comparative and global health, medical law and ethics, statistical methods, and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for optimizing psychosocial intervention strategies in acute care settings, a critical yet understudied domain within clinical medical social work. The research addresses the challenge of personalizing patient-centered care plans that integrate clinical health data with dynamic psychosocial variables—such as caregiver availability, socioeconomic barriers, and mental health comorbidities—which are often siloed or analyzed in isolation. Current approaches to risk stratification in hospital social work rely on static heuristics, leading to inefficient resource allocation and suboptimal patient outcomes. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining federated learning and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient trajectories across heterogeneous datasets while preserving privacy. The ABM will incorporate multi-modal inputs, including structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinician notes processed via natural language processing (NLP), and real-time social determinants of health data from community partners. HPC resources are essential for scaling these simulations to model population-level interactions across 10,000+ virtual agents, each with unique behavioral parameters derived from empirical datasets. The computational workflow will iteratively train deep reinforcement learning models to identify intervention timing and modality (e.g., crisis counseling, discharge coordination) that maximize 30-day post-discharge outcomes. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of 15,000+ historical cases from three health systems, with model performance evaluated against metrics including care plan adherence, readmission rates, and cost-effectiveness. This work is expected to produce the first open-source toolkit for adaptive intervention design in medical social work, directly addressing healthcare disparities by computationally encoding equity-aware decision protocols. The project’s outcomes will provide hospital systems with evidence-based strategies to allocate scarce social work resources while advancing methodological innovation at the intersection of computational social science and precision health.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the specialized professional practice of social work, in collaboration with other health care professionals, in hospitals and other health care facilities and organizations. Includes instruction in social work, psychiatric case work, clinical interviewing techniques, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient testing and evaluation, patient and family counseling, social rehabilitation, patient care planning, record-keeping, and support services liaison.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of systematically analyzing large-scale, cross-cultural music datasets to uncover patterns in melodic, rhythmic, and timbral structures across diverse musical traditions. While traditional musicological methods rely on manual transcription and comparative analysis, the volume and complexity of global audio archives—spanning field recordings, historical performances, and contemporary genres—exceed the capacity of conventional computational tools. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multimodal music data, including audio signals, metadata, and ethnographic annotations, from over 20 distinct cultural traditions. Computational workflows will integrate audio feature extraction (e.g., pitch tracking, spectrotemporal decomposition), machine learning classifiers for genre and style recognition, and network analysis to map intercultural influences. Key tasks include parallelized processing of 50,000+ audio samples using GPU-accelerated libraries, training transformer-based models on symbolic music representations, and simulating agent-based models to test hypotheses about the diffusion of musical innovations. Outcomes will advance methodological frameworks for computational ethnomusicology, enabling the identification of previously undocumented relationships between musical practices and sociocultural contexts. The project will produce open-source tools for large-scale music analysis, a curated repository of annotated datasets, and publications re-evaluating theoretical constructs such as "musical universals" through data-driven perspectives. By scaling analytical rigor to match the diversity of global music practices, this work aims to bridge gaps between qualitative ethnographic research and quantitative music information retrieval, offering new pathways to study musical change, cultural hybridity, and intangible heritage preservation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the forms and methods of music art, and the functions of music, in Western and non-Western societies and cultures. Includes instruction in music theory, musicological research methods, and studies of specific cultural styles such as jazz, folk music, rock, ethnic musical traditions, and the music of non-Western cultures.

abstract: Orthopedic conditions, particularly those affecting load-bearing joints, present complex biomechanical challenges that are difficult to model using conventional experimental methods. Current limitations in predicting long-term outcomes of surgical interventions or implant performance stem from an incomplete understanding of multiscale tissue mechanics and patient-specific variability. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate musculoskeletal dynamics, bone remodeling, and implant-tissue interactions under physiologically realistic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement finite element analysis (FEA) and agent-based modeling to capture mechanobiological processes across spatial scales, from cellular responses to whole-joint biomechanics. Patient-specific anatomical data, including CT and MRI-derived geometries, will inform model parametrization, while machine learning techniques will optimize computational efficiency by identifying reduced-order representations of high-dimensional datasets. The proposed simulations will quantify stress-shielding effects in orthopedic implants, predict bone adaptation patterns post-surgery, and evaluate the biomechanical consequences of anatomical variations across diverse patient populations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for implant failure risk, data-driven guidelines for personalized surgical planning, and mechanistic insights into osteoarthritis progression. The computational demands of this work necessitate HPC infrastructure due to the requirement for parallel processing of large-scale multiphysics simulations (10^6-10^7 elements per model), ensemble runs for population-level analysis, and iterative optimization of machine learning architectures. Successful implementation will provide clinical researchers with an open-source simulation platform to test intervention strategies in silico, potentially reducing costly postoperative complications and accelerating the development of next-generation orthopedic treatments.
cip_definition: Research focused on Orthopedic

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of architectural design simulations, which increasingly require high-fidelity modeling of structural integrity, energy efficiency, and environmental interactions. Current architectural drafting and CAD workflows struggle to efficiently process large-scale simulations, particularly when integrating real-time data from building information modeling (BIM) systems or evaluating multi-physics phenomena such as thermal load distribution and material stress under dynamic conditions. The limitations of conventional computing resources hinder the ability to iteratively optimize designs for sustainability, safety, and compliance with evolving building codes. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable parallelized simulation workflows tailored to architectural applications. The computational approach will focus on developing scalable algorithms for parametric design optimization, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for structural validation, and deploying machine learning models to predict energy performance across diverse climate scenarios. Custom CADD scripts will interface with HPC clusters to automate resource-intensive tasks such as generative design iterations and multi-criteria decision analysis. A key innovation involves coupling BIM data with real-time sensor simulations to model building behavior under extreme environmental stresses. The project will validate results against physical prototypes and existing case studies to ensure computational accuracy. Expected outcomes include a framework for rapid, high-resolution architectural simulations that reduce design iteration times by 40–60% while improving predictive accuracy for energy use and structural resilience. This work will directly contribute to advancing sustainable design practices and provide open-source computational tools for educators, enabling students to engage with cutting-edge HPC-driven workflows in architectural drafting. The resource allocation will support both ongoing validation of a generative design algorithm for net-zero buildings and proposed work on AI-assisted material optimization, fostering innovation at the intersection of computational design and construction technology.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of algorithmic fairness and bias in predictive policing systems through large-scale computational simulations. While predictive algorithms are increasingly used to allocate law enforcement resources, their design and deployment often lack transparency, potentially reinforcing systemic inequities. The research problem centers on identifying how training data biases, model architectures, and feedback loops between policing actions and crime reporting interact to produce unequal outcomes across demographic groups. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop agent-based models that simulate urban crime patterns, police patrol allocation strategies, and community reporting behaviors at city-scale resolution. These models will integrate real-world demographic data, historical crime statistics, and procedural fairness metrics to test hypotheses about algorithmic amplification of disparities. Machine learning techniques will be employed to analyze simulation outputs across thousands of parameter combinations, assessing how different deployment scenarios affect equity metrics. The computational intensity arises from modeling millions of agent interactions across diverse urban landscapes while maintaining granular temporal and spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include a framework for evaluating algorithmic fairness in public safety contexts, quantitative evidence about risk factors for bias propagation, and open-source tools for simulating police-community dynamics. This work bridges computational social science with criminal justice policy analysis, offering novel methodologies to assess emerging technologies in law enforcement. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration that is infeasible with standard computing infrastructure, directly supporting evidence-based policymaking for equitable public safety strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the criminal justice system, its organizational components and processes, and its legal and public policy contexts. Includes instruction in criminal law and policy, police and correctional systems organization, the administration of justice and the judiciary, and public attitudes regarding criminal justice issues.

abstract: Women’s health nursing requires evidence-based approaches to address complex, multifactorial conditions that disproportionately or uniquely affect women, such as maternal mortality, preterm birth, and gynecologic cancers. Current clinical decision-making often relies on generalized risk models that fail to account for dynamic interactions between biological, social, and environmental factors. This project seeks to develop predictive models for adverse pregnancy outcomes and optimize pharmacotherapeutic protocols for women with comorbid conditions (e.g., gestational diabetes and hypertension) using high-performance computing (HPC). The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including electronic health records (EHRs), genomic data, and social determinants of health—to identify individualized risk profiles and treatment responses. Existing computational tools lack the scalability to process these data at clinically relevant resolutions or timeframes. The proposed work will apply machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate physiological pathways, patient trajectories, and intervention impacts. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of EHRs from 500,000+ pregnancies, genomic variant analysis, and multiscale modeling of drug interactions in diverse patient subgroups. Key computational steps include federated learning to preserve data privacy across institutions, graph neural networks to map comorbidity networks, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic simulations to evaluate sex-specific drug efficacy. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive algorithms for preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage, (2) optimized dosing guidelines for high-risk obstetric populations, and (3) open-source tools for real-time risk stratification in clinical settings. This work will advance precision nursing by bridging gaps between population-level data and individualized care, directly addressing disparities in women’s health outcomes. The scale and complexity of these analyses necessitate HPC infrastructure to manage terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations, which cannot feasibly be conducted on local servers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide health care specific to women. Includes instruction in the wellness and care of women, gynecology, obstetrics, advanced nursing practices for women, evidence-based nursing practice, advanced physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pharmacology, and pharmacotherapeutics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling of infectious disease transmission dynamics in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), with a focus on malaria and arboviral diseases. Despite progress in disease control, heterogeneous environmental, sociodemographic, and behavioral factors complicate intervention planning in resource-limited settings. Current models often oversimplify spatial-temporal interactions between climate variability, vector ecology, and human mobility, limiting their utility for real-world policy decisions. To address this, we propose an integrated computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), Bayesian inference, and machine learning to simulate disease spread at high resolution across diverse LMIC contexts. The ABM will incorporate geospatial data (e.g., satellite-derived land use, precipitation), anonymized mobile phone mobility traces, and longitudinal health surveillance data to capture multiscale transmission drivers. Bayesian methods will quantify uncertainty in parameter estimation, while recurrent neural networks will forecast outbreak trajectories under varying intervention scenarios. The scale of analysis—spanning 10-50 million agent interactions across multi-year simulations—necessitates parallelized computing for parameter calibration, sensitivity analyses, and scenario testing. Expected outcomes include identification of high-risk transmission corridors, optimization of targeted vector control strategies, and open-source tools for evaluating the cost-effectiveness of interventions under climate change. By elucidating context-specific pathways of disease spread, this work will directly inform national health agencies and global partners in prioritizing limited resources. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive analyses that are infeasible with standard infrastructure, thereby advancing methodological innovation in computational epidemiology and strengthening evidence-based decision-making for infectious disease mitigation in LMICs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, the social and behavioral sciences, and policy and communications methods to the study of health problems in low- and middle-income countries and regions, and prepares individuals to function as professional international health specialists. Includes instruction in health education and promotion, research design and evaluation, infectious disease epidemiology, international health policy and management, public nutrition and food security, information systems, program evaluation, medical anthropology, international communication, behavioral sciences, maternal and child health, demography and population policy, and health care finance and economics.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying allosteric regulation in a model multienzyme complex central to nucleotide biosynthesis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in simulating large, dynamic macromolecular assemblies. Despite extensive biochemical characterization, the structural dynamics driving long-range communication between catalytic and regulatory subunits remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to capture transient conformational states, while classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of such systems are computationally prohibitive due to their size (>500,000 atoms) and the microsecond-to-millisecond timescales required to observe allosteric transitions. We propose an integrated computational approach combining coarse-grained MD for global conformational sampling, Gaussian accelerated MD (GaMD) for enhanced exploration of free energy landscapes, and QM/MM simulations to resolve critical electronic interactions at catalytic sites. These methods will be applied to investigate how post-translational modifications alter allosteric networks in the enzyme complex, a process implicated in metabolic dysregulation. The HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across multiple thermodynamic states, significantly accelerating convergence. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic models of allosteric propagation pathways, (2) identification of key residues governing communication between distal functional sites, and (3) predictive insights into how phosphorylation modulates enzymatic efficiency. Results will be validated through collaborative mutagenesis and kinetic assays. This work will establish a computational framework for studying supramolecular assemblies at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution, advancing mechanistic understanding of metabolic regulation while providing foundational data for targeted enzyme engineering. The requested resources are essential given the project’s scale: initial benchmarks indicate that simulating a single 1-μs replicate of the full system requires ~25,000 CPU-hours, with thousands of replicates needed for robust statistical analysis across proposed perturbations.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific relationship of physiological function to the structure and actions of macromolecules and supramolecular assemblies such as multienzyme complexes, membranes, and viruses. Includes instruction in the chemical mechanisms of regulation and catalysis, protein synthesis and other syntheses, and biomolecular chemical reactions.

abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the supporting structures of teeth, is driven by complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and genetic and environmental factors. While advances in high-throughput sequencing and multi-omics technologies have generated vast datasets linking dysbiotic microbiomes and host pathways to disease progression, integrating these heterogeneous data to identify predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate host-microbial dynamics in periodontitis. Using longitudinal metagenomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic datasets from clinical cohorts, we will apply machine learning frameworks to identify microbial consortia and inflammatory mediators associated with disease severity and treatment outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate spatial interactions between microbial biofilms, host immune cells, and tissue remodeling processes in the periodontium, incorporating patient-specific omics data to predict responses to mechanical or pharmacological interventions. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will explore how bacterial virulence factors interact with host cell receptors to modulate inflammation. These computational approaches require HPC resources to manage large-scale data integration, optimize predictive algorithms, and perform parallelized simulations across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a systems biology framework linking microbiome-host networks to clinical phenotypes, (2) predictive models for personalized treatment stratification, and (3) novel insights into mechanistic drivers of tissue destruction. By bridging computational biology and clinical periodontology, this work aims to advance precision therapies and improve long-term outcomes for patients with periodontitis. The scalability of these models will also establish a foundation for studying other oral-systemic inflammatory conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the etiology and treatment of diseases of the gingivae (gum tissue) and supporting bone, nerve, and vascular structures. Includes instruction in periodontium pathology, diagnostic procedures and equipment, occlusion, nutritional aspects of periodontology, surgical treatments, and patient care and management.

abstract: The preservation and revitalization of the Hawaiian language (‘ōlelo Hawaiʻi) face critical challenges due to the scarcity of digitized linguistic resources and advanced analytical tools tailored to its unique phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures. Existing computational methods, often designed for Indo-European languages, inadequately capture the complexities of Hawaiian, including its vowel-rich phonology, verb-noun ambiguities, and dialectal variations across historical and contemporary texts. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a scalable computational framework for analyzing Hawaiian language corpora, enabling large-scale philological research and dialectological mapping. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) constructing a parallelized pipeline for processing and annotating digitized historical manuscripts, oral histories, and modern publications using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for Polynesian languages; (2) implementing machine learning models to identify and classify dialectal features across temporal, geographic, and sociolinguistic dimensions; and (3) simulating phonetic shifts through agent-based modeling to trace the evolution of regional speech patterns. HPC resources will be critical for handling the terabytes of textual and audio data, training deep neural networks on rare morphological patterns, and running computationally intensive phylogenetic analyses of language change. Expected outcomes include the first open-access repository of computationally annotated Hawaiian texts, interactive visualization tools for educators and cultural practitioners, and empirically grounded insights into language contact dynamics between Hawaiian and colonial languages. By integrating computational linguistics with Indigenous knowledge systems, this project aims to empower Hawaiian language revitalization efforts while advancing methodological innovations for under-resourced languages globally. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support graduate student researchers in developing technical skills aligned with both linguistic scholarship and community-driven language preservation.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Hawaiian language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The design and optimization of next-generation aerospace vehicles require high-fidelity simulations to address complex multi-physics challenges, such as turbulent hypersonic flows, coupled thermal-structural response during atmospheric re-entry, and propulsion system performance in extreme environments. Traditional computational approaches are limited by inadequate resolution of critical phenomena, leading to conservative designs and incomplete understanding of operational limits. This project seeks advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) methods, and finite element analysis (FEA) for multi-disciplinary aerospace systems. The research focuses on three interconnected objectives: (1) resolving hypersonic boundary layer transition mechanisms under real-gas effects using adaptive mesh refinement and reactive flow solvers, (2) modeling ablation and thermal degradation of ceramic composite materials in re-entry vehicles through coupled CFD-FEA frameworks, and (3) simulating plasma dynamics in advanced air-breathing propulsion systems for sustained hypersonic flight. These simulations demand petascale computational capabilities due to the need for three-dimensional, time-accurate solutions with billions of grid points and microsecond-scale temporal resolution. The proposed work leverages GPU-accelerated solvers and hybrid MPI/OpenMP parallelization to optimize resource utilization. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for aerodynamic heating, material failure thresholds, and combustion instability mitigation strategies, directly addressing critical gaps in current design methodologies. By enabling unprecedented resolution of multi-physics interactions, this research will advance the development of robust thermal protection systems, efficient propulsion architectures, and high-speed vehicle control algorithms, with applications to orbital launch systems, planetary entry vehicles, and hypersonic platforms. The computational datasets and open-source tools generated will provide foundational resources for the aerospace engineering community.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering, general
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, General
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their systems; applied research on flight and orbital characteristics; and the development of systems and procedures for the launching, guidance, and control of air and space vehicles.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing cyber insurance in an era of escalating digital risks. The rapid proliferation of cyber threats, coupled with inconsistent international regulatory standards and complex liability structures, has created systemic uncertainties in insurance markets. Traditional legal analysis methods struggle to model the cascading effects of multi-jurisdictional litigation, dynamic policy exclusions, and probabilistic risk scenarios at scale. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between insurers, policyholders, regulators, and adversarial actors across heterogeneous legal environments. Computational legal analytics techniques, including natural language processing (NLP) of insurance contracts, case law, and regulatory texts, will inform parameterization of risk scenarios. Monte Carlo simulations will assess the financial stability implications of emerging liability doctrines under varying threat landscapes. By integrating actuarial data with statutory and case law databases, the models will quantify how judicial interpretations of policy language (e.g., "war exclusion" clauses in state-sponsored cyberattacks) propagate through global insurance networks. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for stress-testing regulatory proposals, identifying critical vulnerabilities in coverage standardization efforts, and predicting litigation hotspots arising from artificial intelligence-related liabilities. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale legal corpora, running parallelized scenario analyses across 50+ jurisdictional models, and maintaining probabilistic graphs of liability pathways. Results will advance methodological integration of computational social science with insurance jurisprudence while providing policymakers and industry stakeholders with evidence-based tools to address systemic risks in digital insurance markets.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern distributed networks has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource allocation strategies, particularly under dynamic workloads and heterogeneous infrastructure conditions. Traditional network management frameworks often rely on static thresholds or reactive measures, which struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and fault tolerance in real time. This project proposes the development of a bio-inspired, self-organizing resource orchestration system designed for large-scale, multi-domain LAN/WAN environments. Leveraging decentralized swarm intelligence algorithms, the system will autonomously optimize computational and bandwidth resources across hybrid cloud-edge architectures while maintaining compliance with organizational service-level agreements. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate network topologies mirroring real-world enterprise deployments, including stochastic traffic patterns, hardware failures, and security incidents. Agent-based modeling will be employed to evaluate emergent behaviors of the proposed algorithms under varying scales (10,000–1,000,000 nodes), with comparative analysis against conventional software-defined networking controllers. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify system resilience against cascading outages, while GPU-accelerated neural networks will predict optimal resource distribution during peak demand scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for proactive anomaly detection, dynamic load redistribution without service interruption, and energy-aware provisioning that reduces idle resource consumption by 30–50% in simulated environments. The research directly addresses the operational challenges of maintaining performance parity during infrastructure upgrades, a persistent pain point in system migration workflows. Successful validation could redefine standards for autonomous network management, particularly for organizations managing distributed computing resources across evolving technological ecosystems.
cip_title: System, Networking, and LAN/ WAN Management/ Manager
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to oversee and regulate the computer system and performance requirements of an entire organization or network of satellite users. Includes instruction in performance balancing; redundancy; local area (LAN) and wide area (WAN) network management; system migration and upgrading; outage control; problem diagnosis and troubleshooting; and system maintenance, budgeting, and management.

abstract: Modern applied statistics faces challenges in analyzing high-dimensional and heterogeneous datasets, particularly in domains such as public health and environmental science, where traditional computational methods are inadequate for complex Bayesian models and non-parametric techniques. This project seeks to develop scalable statistical methodologies to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on two primary areas: (1) implementing parallelized Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms for Bayesian hierarchical models that integrate multi-source data with spatial and temporal dependencies, and (2) optimizing resampling-based inference for high-dimensional non-parametric regression, enabling uncertainty quantification in large-scale settings. The computational approach will utilize distributed memory architectures to manage memory-intensive tasks and employ GPU acceleration for likelihood evaluations in stochastic simulations. By overcoming current bottlenecks in computation time and memory constraints, this work aims to produce statistically robust tools for applications such as disease risk mapping and climate impact assessment. The expected outcomes include open-source software packages tailored for HPC environments, methodological advances in efficient Monte Carlo sampling, and case studies demonstrating improved inference in real-world datasets with millions of observations. This project will enhance the capacity of applied researchers to tackle computationally prohibitive problems while advancing statistical theory at the intersection of scalability and uncertainty quantification.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the solution of functional problems in fields such as business, engineering, medicine, and the applied sciences. Includes instruction in the principles in inference, probability theory, regression analysis, descriptive statistics, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, statistical computing, and statistical techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving dynamics of Women’s Ministry programs in diverse cultural and denominational contexts, with a focus on mapping spiritual leadership patterns, community-building practices, and gendered theological frameworks. The research problem centers on the lack of large-scale, data-driven studies examining how non-ordained women navigate spiritual authority, foster collective resilience, and adapt ministry strategies amid shifting socioreligious landscapes. While qualitative case studies dominate existing scholarship, computational methods remain underutilized in decoding complex interactions between theological training, lived experience, and program efficacy. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will process unstructured textual data (oral histories, ministry training manuals, sermon transcripts) and structured survey responses from 15,000+ participants across 200 global congregations. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will identify latent themes in spiritual mentorship practices, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will model relational networks within ministry cohorts. Agent-based simulations will test how variations in curriculum design and leadership structures impact long-term community outcomes. Key computational challenges include managing multilingual sacred text corpora, preserving contextual nuance in theological discourse analysis, and scaling dynamic network models to simulate decade-long ministry lifespans. Expected outcomes include a novel taxonomy of Women’s Ministry archetypes, predictive tools for optimizing lay counseling training modules, and an open-access repository of annotated ministry interaction datasets. By bridging computational social science and practical theology, this work aims to empower faith communities with evidence-based strategies for cultivating inclusive spiritual leadership while advancing interdisciplinary methodologies for studying emergent religious practices. The requested HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models on niche theological lexicons and executing large-scale cultural simulations impractical on local infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained women to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to other women in local churches, parachurch organizations, and other settings. Includes instruction in foundations of women's ministry, women's ministry in the local church, spiritual formation, women's evangelism and discipleship, bible study and theology, homiletics, lay counseling, women's issues, and leadership training.

abstract: The motorsports industry faces increasing demands for vehicle performance optimization under complex aerodynamic, thermal, and mechanical constraints.
