Current design workflows rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping and simplified simulations, which are time-intensive, costly, and limited in capturing multi-physics interactions critical to racing performance. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to model and optimize motorsports systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome these limitations. The research will focus on three interconnected areas: (1) aerodynamic analysis of vehicle-body and component designs under dynamic track conditions using unsteady computational fluid dynamics (CFD), (2) coupled thermal-structural simulations of powertrain systems to evaluate performance limits and failure modes, and (3) data-driven optimization of vehicle dynamics through machine learning models trained on sensor data and simulation outputs. The computational approach will employ parallelized solvers, adaptive meshing techniques, and GPU-accelerated workflows to manage the scale and resolution required for transient, multi-phase simulations. Integration of CAD parameterization tools will enable automated design exploration. By utilizing HPC resources, the project aims to reduce simulation turnaround times from weeks to days while resolving finer spatial and temporal scales than current institutional computing infrastructure allows. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting drag reduction strategies, engine cooling efficiency improvements, and tire-road interaction dynamics under extreme racing conditions. This work will directly enhance student and faculty capabilities in motorsports engineering at the intersection of computational methods and applied design, while generating open-access case studies for curriculum integration. The results will also provide actionable insights for industry partners seeking to adopt simulation-driven design practices, ultimately contributing to safer, more competitive motorsports technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the design, construction, and repair of vehicles used in racing and motorsports. Includes instruction in aerodynamics, design, vehicle dynamics, performance engines, fluid mechanics, computer-aided design (CAD), mechanical engineering, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling of acoustic wave propagation in complex, heterogeneous media, with applications to underwater acoustics and biomedical ultrasonics. A critical challenge in these domains lies in accurately simulating wave behavior across multiple scales, particularly in environments with nonlinear material properties, irregular boundaries, and dynamic fluid-structure interactions. Traditional analytical methods and low-resolution numerical models fail to capture critical phenomena such as frequency-dependent scattering, mode coupling in waveguides, and the effects of viscoelastic absorption in biological tissues. To address these limitations, we propose a computational framework combining finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods with GPU-accelerated pseudo-spectral solvers to resolve high-frequency wave dynamics and multi-physics interactions. The FDTD component will model broadband wave propagation in large-scale environments (e.g., ocean acoustic channels), while the pseudo-spectral solver will handle localized, high-resolution simulations of nonlinear effects in viscoelastic media (e.g., tissue harmonic generation in medical imaging). The hybrid approach requires parallelized workflows to manage data exchange between solvers and optimize memory allocation for terabyte-scale 3D wavefield outputs. Key objectives include quantifying uncertainty in seabed sediment characterization through stochastic inversion of scattering data and optimizing ultrasound transducer configurations for enhanced tumor delineation in hepatic diagnostics. The requested HPC resources will enable parametric studies across >10^4 configurations, reducing time-to-solution for individual simulations from weeks to hours. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting acoustic energy leakage in stratified underwater waveguides and protocols for minimizing thermal dose variability in therapeutic ultrasound. Results will be disseminated as open-source simulation toolkits, providing the acoustics community with scalable tools for wave-based sensing and imaging applications. This work directly aligns with national priorities in marine technology and precision healthcare, bridging fundamental wave physics with computational engineering challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sound, and the properties and behavior of acoustic wave phenomena under different conditions. Includes instruction in wave theory, the acoustic wave equation, energy transformation, vibration phenomena, sound reflection and transmission, scattering and surface wave phenomena, singularity expansion theory, ducting, and applications to specific research problems such as underwater acoustics, crystallography, and health diagnostics.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of diet-related metabolic disorders in companion animals, such as obesity and diabetes, highlights critical gaps in understanding species-specific nutrient metabolism and its interaction with health outcomes. Current empirical models fail to capture the dynamic, multi-scale relationships between dietary components, host physiology, and the gut microbiome, limiting the development of precision nutrition strategies. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to construct mechanistic, multi-omics models of nutrient metabolism in dogs and cats. We will integrate species-specific genomic, metabolomic, and metagenomic data to simulate nutrient absorption, hepatic processing, and systemic utilization under varying dietary conditions. A hybrid computational approach will combine differential equation-based systems biology models with machine learning to predict metabolic fluxes, microbiome-mediated nutrient transformations, and their collective impact on biomarkers of health. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses across diverse physiological states (e.g., age, disease status), and probabilistic simulations of dietary interventions. The computational framework will be validated against clinical datasets from feeding trials measuring postprandial metabolite profiles, gut microbiota composition, and inflammatory markers. Expected outcomes include the identification of optimal nutrient ratios for mitigating metabolic dysfunction, predictive tools for personalized diet formulation, and mechanistic insights into species-specific differences in nutrient requirements. This work will directly inform evidence-based clinical guidelines for therapeutic diets, reducing reliance on trial-and-error nutritional management. By resolving complex interactions between diet, metabolism, and animal health at unprecedented resolution, the project advances veterinary nutrition into a computationally driven paradigm with translational implications for both companion and production animals.
cip_definition: Research focused on the chemical nature of food substances; the processes by which animals ingest, digest, absorb, transport, utilize and excrete food and nutrients; and their relation to animal behavior and health.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a real-time adaptive framework for optimizing tourism promotion campaigns by integrating heterogeneous data streams and predictive computational models. Current tourism marketing strategies often rely on static, siloed datasets and heuristic decision-making, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation during dynamic events such as geopolitical disruptions, environmental crises, or shifting travel trends. The project addresses this gap through the creation of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled system that synthesizes real-time social media sentiment analysis, economic indicator tracking, transportation network data, and climate event monitoring. A hybrid machine learning architecture combining graph neural networks (for modeling destination popularity cascades) and transformer-based temporal forecasting (for demand prediction) will be deployed on GPU-accelerated clusters to process multi-terabyte datasets from global tourism platforms. Agent-based modeling simulations will concurrently test promotional strategy efficacy across 10^5 synthetic tourist profiles with diverse behavioral parameters. The computational workflow requires distributed memory parallelism for near-real-time model retraining and MPI-based coordination between simulation ensembles. Expected outcomes include a quantifiable framework for measuring promotional campaign resilience to external shocks, dynamic budget allocation algorithms optimized for regional economic multipliers, and predictive metrics for emerging tourism niche identification. Successful implementation will provide tourism boards and private operators with evidence-based tools to maximize marketing ROI during volatile conditions while preserving destination sustainability. This work establishes a novel computational paradigm for tourism economics, bridging operational marketing challenges with complex systems analytics through scalable HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and sales operations connected with the promotion of tourism in public and private sector settings. Includes instruction in principles of marketing research and advertising, promotional campaign organization, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in contemporary Latin American digital media through computational analysis of large-scale, multilingual textual and visual datasets. Focusing on 21st-century social movements and diasporic communities, the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital platforms reshape collective memory and cultural belonging across Latin America, particularly among marginalized groups. The study employs natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze over 10 million publicly available social media posts, digital archives of community-led cultural initiatives, and grassroots multimedia content from Mexico, Colombia, and Argentina. Advanced transformer-based models will be fine-tuned for regional linguistic variations and code-switching patterns, while multimodal neural networks will decode interactions between text, images, and audiovisual elements in cultural storytelling. High-performance computing resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous data at scale, conducting temporal network analyses of narrative diffusion, and simulating cultural transmission patterns across virtual communities. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for analyzing digital cultural production in transnational contexts, open-source tools for multilingual Latin American text analysis, and new insights into how digital spaces mediate tensions between traditional cultural practices and globalized identities. The computational infrastructure will enable processing of Indigenous and Creole languages often excluded from mainstream NLP resources, directly supporting underrepresented voices in cultural studies scholarship. Results will inform cultural preservation strategies and educational initiatives addressing digital divides in the region.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic peoples of the North and South American Continents outside Canada and the United States, including the study of the Pre-Columbian period and the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the functional consequences of structural variations (SVs) across diverse human populations, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic datasets. Despite their recognized role in evolution, adaptation, and disease, SVs remain understudied compared to single-nucleotide variants due to technical challenges in detection and interpretation. This project will employ long-read sequencing data from global populations to resolve complex SVs with high precision, integrating these findings with transcriptomic datasets to elucidate their regulatory impacts on gene expression. A key computational challenge involves processing multi-terabyte datasets to identify population-specific SV patterns, associate them with regulatory element disruptions, and model their three-dimensional chromatin interactions. Custom pipelines will combine graph-based genome representations, machine learning classifiers for SV impact prediction, and population genetics statistics to quantify selection pressures. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing alignment, variant calling, and association analyses across thousands of genomes while managing memory-intensive tasks such as de novo genome assembly and chromatin conformation reconstruction. Expected outcomes include a comprehensive atlas of functionally consequential SVs, novel algorithms for SV prioritization in clinical genomics, and open-source tools for population-scale SV analysis. This work will directly advance precision medicine by improving the interpretation of non-coding SVs in underrepresented populations and provide foundational insights into how genomic architecture shapes phenotypic diversity. The requested computing infrastructure will enable scalable, reproducible workflows critical for handling the growing volume of global genomic data while adhering to FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data principles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of whole genome sequences and patterns of gene expression. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular biology, genetics, protein technologies, genomic sciences and techniques, bioinformatics, and scientific and research ethics.

abstract: The increasing diversity of learning needs among students with disabilities necessitates innovative approaches to developing personalized educational strategies. Current methods for designing individualized education plans (IEPs) often rely on manual analysis of behavioral, academic, and sensory data, which limits scalability and real-time adaptability. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to create predictive models that optimize IEP development by integrating heterogeneous datasets, including longitudinal academic performance records, physiological sensor data, and unstructured behavioral observations. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in analyzing multi-modal data streams to identify patterns that correlate with optimal learning outcomes for students with neurodevelopmental disabilities (e.g., autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia). Using parallelized machine learning pipelines, we will train ensemble models on anonymized student datasets encompassing 50,000+ IEP trajectories from national repositories. Computational experiments will focus on (1) clustering students by multidimensional learning profiles using graph neural networks, (2) simulating intervention impacts through agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics, and (3) optimizing natural language processing (NLP) tools to automate analysis of teacher narratives and speech therapy transcripts. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of high-frequency sensor data (eye-tracking, wearable devices) and video recordings at scale, facilitating temporal pattern recognition inaccessible to traditional statistical methods. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating data-driven IEP recommendations, validated through partnerships with 12 special education schools. This work aims to establish computational foundations for precision special education while maintaining strict ethical standards for student data privacy. By reducing IEP development time by 30-50% while improving outcome correlation metrics, the project could transform resource-constrained special education classrooms through scalable AI-assisted decision support.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children or adults with special learning needs or disabilities, and that may prepare individuals to function as special education teachers in a collaborative or team environment. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing real-time communication workflows in frontline receptionist systems, with a focus on enhancing service quality and operational efficiency in high-volume business environments. Traditional receptionist workflows—spanning call routing, visitor management, and information dissemination—often face inefficiencies due to unpredictable demand patterns, cognitive overload among staff, and inconsistent adherence to organizational communication protocols. This project addresses these challenges by modeling dynamic interaction networks and simulating decision-making processes under variable stress and resource constraints. Using anonymized call logs, visitor logs, and sentiment analysis datasets from corporate reception hubs, we will train transformer-based models to predict optimal response strategies, automate routine tasks, and flag high-priority interactions requiring human intervention. Computational experiments will employ agent-based modeling to simulate receptionist-caller dynamics across diverse scenarios, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine task prioritization and scheduling policies. The HPC infrastructure is critical for processing multimodal data (audio, text, temporal patterns) at scale, enabling parallelized training of context-aware recommendation systems. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for reducing caller wait times, improving sentiment outcomes by 15-25% in simulated environments, and generating adaptive workflow templates customizable to specific organizational needs. By bridging computational linguistics, behavioral operations research, and queueing theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for intelligent receptionist systems that balance automation with human-centric service delivery, offering scalable solutions for healthcare facilities, enterprise campuses, and crisis response centers where frontline communication directly impacts organizational reputation and operational resilience.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform frontline public relations duties for a business, organization, or answering service. Includes instruction in telephone answering techniques, responding to information requests, keeping caller and/or visitor records, placing business calls, operating telephone switchboards and/or other communications equipment, relaying incoming and interoffice calls, schedule maintenance, and public relations skills.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of immersive audio production in the Recording Arts Technology field, where traditional workstations struggle to process high-channel-count spatial audio and real-time acoustic simulations. Emerging formats like 6DoF (six degrees of freedom) sound for augmented/virtual reality require dynamic, latency-sensitive processing of dozens of audio streams alongside physics-based reverberation modeling—tasks that exceed the capabilities of standard systems. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable workflows for next-generation spatial audio production. The research will employ parallelized digital signal processing algorithms optimized for GPU clusters, enabling real-time convolution of complex impulse responses for environmental acoustics and AI-driven source separation for immersive mixing. A key focus involves adapting machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) to train neural networks on HPC infrastructure for tasks such as automated dialogue enhancement in multi-mic field recordings and adaptive noise reduction in live broadcast scenarios. The project will validate these methods through case studies simulating large-scale concert acoustics and interactive game audio environments. Successful implementation will provide practitioners with open-source tools for efficient high-density audio rendering, reducing post-production timelines for film and interactive media by an estimated 40%. Outcomes will advance the field’s capacity to handle increasingly complex auditory experiences while establishing best practices for HPC integration in non-STEM media disciplines. All developed code and benchmark data will be shared through industry partnerships and the AES Audio Engineering Society’s research portal, directly supporting the program’s mission to bridge technical innovation with creative practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of sound recordings as finished products or as components of film/video, broadcast, live, or mixed media productions. Includes instruction in sound equipment operation and maintenance; music, dialogue, and sound effects recording; soundtrack editing; dubbing and mixing; sound engineering; tape, disk, and CD production; digital recording and transmission; amplification and modulation; and working with producers, editors, directors, artists, and production managers.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient, reliable, and environmentally sustainable electricity generation necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize power plant operations. Current challenges include mitigating inefficiencies in turbine performance, managing dynamic load fluctuations, reducing emissions under variable operating conditions, and integrating renewable energy sources into conventional power generation systems. Traditional experimental and analytical approaches are limited in addressing these multi-scale, multi-physics problems, particularly when balancing real-time operational constraints with long-term reliability. This project proposes the development of high-fidelity computational models to simulate power plant subsystems—including combustion dynamics, steam turbine thermodynamics, heat exchanger networks, and emissions control systems—using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Coupled computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and finite element analysis (FEA) will be employed to study fluid-structure interactions in turbine blades, transient heat transfer in boilers, and pollutant dispersion in flue gas systems. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to calibrate models against real-time sensor data and predict equipment degradation. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parametric studies of combined-cycle plant configurations, sensitivity analyses of water chemistry impacts on corrosion rates, and probabilistic risk assessments for grid stability during renewable energy intermittency. Expected outcomes include validated operational protocols to reduce fuel consumption by 8–12%, predictive maintenance frameworks to extend turbine lifespan, and optimized control strategies for hybrid power systems incorporating solar thermal or hydrogen co-firing. These advancements will directly support workforce training in power plant instrumentation and industrial controls while providing actionable insights for utilities transitioning to low-carbon generation. The requested computing resources are critical for executing parallelized simulations of full-scale plant systems, which exceed the capacity of local clusters, ensuring alignment with national priorities for energy resilience and emissions reduction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: Hematologic and coagulation disorders present complex diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their multifactorial etiology, heterogeneous molecular profiles, and dynamic interactions between genetic, proteomic, and cellular pathways. Current laboratory methods for analyzing hematologic data—including genomic sequencing, flow cytometry, and coagulation assays—generate high-dimensional datasets that exceed the processing capacity of conventional computing infrastructure. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and apply advanced computational models for multi-omics integration, predictive biomarker discovery, and dynamic simulation of coagulation cascades. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to identify subtype-specific genomic and proteomic signatures in leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and inherited bleeding disorders, and (2) employing molecular dynamics simulations to model aberrant protein interactions in thrombotic and hemorrhagic conditions. The computational workflows will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and clinical laboratory parameters using scalable data fusion algorithms. By deploying GPU-accelerated architectures, we will optimize time-intensive processes such as variational autoencoder training for dimensionality reduction and Markov state models for simulating fibrin polymerization kinetics. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, stratification algorithms for patient-specific anticoagulation management, and predictive models for laboratory test utilization optimization. This work addresses critical gaps in translating complex hematologic data into clinically actionable insights, with direct implications for diagnostic accuracy, treatment personalization, and resource efficiency in hematopathology laboratories. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale datasets, reducing computational bottlenecks in ensemble modeling, and enabling real-time analytics integration with institutional electronic health records.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory and analytical procedures for studying all facets of hematologic and coagulation disorders. May included related research in the management of hematology laboratories.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of gendered and ethnic cultural narratives across Latin American and Caribbean diasporic communities through computational analysis of multilingual textual and visual archives. While traditional scholarship in cultural and gender studies has focused on localized, qualitative case studies, there remains a critical gap in understanding how transnational identity formations intersect with historical memory at scale. This research addresses this challenge by employing machine learning and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze over 10 million pages of digitized newspapers, oral history transcripts, and visual artifacts from 20 countries, dated 1900–2000. The computational workflow involves training multilingual transformer models on historical Spanish, Portuguese, and Indigenous language corpora to detect semantic shifts in identity-related discourse, paired with computer vision methods to trace iconographic patterns in political cartoons and folk art. A central technical hurdle is the development of culturally contextualized embeddings that account for code-switching phenomena and colonial-era orthographic variations. High-performance computing resources are essential for 1) processing terabyte-scale datasets through distributed GPU-accelerated pipelines, 2) fine-tuning large language models on low-resource languages like Garifuna and Haitian Kreyòl, and 3) simulating network models of cross-regional cultural influence using graph neural architectures. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative atlas of pan-regional identity discourse dynamics, open-source tools for decolonial AI in area studies, and evidence-based frameworks for cultural policy interventions. By integrating computational social science methodologies with critical regional studies, this work aims to redefine analytical paradigms for understanding how marginalized communities negotiate identity in postcolonial contexts, while establishing scalable infrastructure for interdisciplinary digital humanities research across the Global South.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: An integrated program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples and countries of the Latin American and Caribbean region.

abstract: The increasing complexity of cytopathological data, driven by advances in high-resolution digital imaging and molecular profiling, presents significant challenges in analyzing cellular alterations for disease diagnosis and prognosis. Current computational workflows struggle to efficiently process and integrate multi-modal datasets—including gigapixel whole-slide images, single-cell RNA sequencing, and proteomic profiles—while maintaining diagnostic rigor. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable, AI-driven frameworks for cytopathological analysis. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating deep learning models optimized for automated detection of rare malignant cells in large-scale cytology screenings, and (2) establishing computational pipelines to correlate cellular morphometric features with molecular alterations across diverse cancer types. The computational approach will utilize convolutional neural networks with attention mechanisms for image analysis, graph-based algorithms for spatial feature extraction, and federated learning architectures to handle distributed datasets while preserving patient privacy. HPC resources will be critical for training complex models on terabyte-scale imaging repositories, performing hyperparameter optimization at scale, and conducting molecular dynamics simulations to investigate protein interactions underlying observed cytomorphological changes. Expected outcomes include validated computational tools for standardized, high-throughput cytological analysis, predictive models linking cellular phenotypes to therapeutic vulnerabilities, and open-source software packages optimized for clinical research workflows. This work will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in precancerous lesion characterization, enable discovery of novel biomarkers through integrated multi-omics analysis, and provide a template for resource-efficient computational cytopathology. By bridging cellular imaging data with molecular mechanisms through advanced computing, the project aims to advance personalized disease management strategies in clinical cytopathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares individuals to study, prevent, and manage human diseases manifested in cells. Includes instruction in laboratory procedures, laboratory management, quality assurance, screening, specimen collection, cytopreparation, cytometric and image analysis, and related immunological and molecular techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting individual variability in drug response by integrating metabolomic and proteomic data with patient-specific physiological parameters, a critical yet underexplored area at the intersection of computational biology and precision health. Current approaches to drug response modeling often rely on population-level averages, neglecting the complex interplay between dynamic cellular processes and systemic factors such as organ function or circadian rhythms. To overcome this limitation, we propose developing a multiscale computational framework that simulates drug pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics at cellular, tissue, and whole-organism levels using individualized biological data. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized agent-based models of hepatic drug metabolism coupled with finite element analyses of vascular transport. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic datasets generated through these simulations to identify patterns linking molecular signatures with clinical outcomes. The computational workflow will incorporate real-world electronic health record data (de-identified and ethically approved) to validate predictions regarding drug clearance rates and adverse event risks. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of predicting patient-specific drug responses with greater accuracy than current clinical tools, particularly for populations with non-standard metabolic profiles. This work will advance personalized treatment strategies while providing a novel educational resource for pre-pharmacy students to explore systems pharmacology concepts through interactive computational modules. The HPC resources are essential for managing the combinatorial complexity of biological networks and enabling rapid iteration of predictive models across diverse virtual patient cohorts. Successful implementation could transform early-phase drug candidate evaluation and inform precision dosing guidelines for special populations often excluded from traditional clinical trials.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in pharmacy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative architectural design frameworks that integrate cultural, ecological, and historical data into real-time spatial simulations. Traditional architectural workflows often rely on static, siloed datasets, limiting the ability to dynamically model complex interactions between built environments, localized cultural narratives, and shifting ecological conditions. The research addresses this gap by creating a computational pipeline that synthesizes heterogeneous data—including oral histories, geospatial climate projections, and material heritage records—into adaptive 3D design models. Using a combination of agent-based modeling, graph neural networks (GNNs), and parametric design tools, the project will simulate how architectural forms evolve in response to socio-cultural priorities and environmental stressors. Key computational challenges include optimizing mesh generation for irregular heritage site geometries, parallelizing climate impact simulations across multi-decadal timelines, and training GNNs on sparse, non-uniform cultural datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify design solutions that balance structural resilience with community-defined cultural values. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for culturally responsive generative design, validated through case studies in post-disaster reconstruction contexts. By bridging architectural practice with computational ethnography and ecological forecasting, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for ethically grounded, data-driven design—one that prioritizes the integration of intangible heritage and participatory decision-making into computationally intensive workflows. The resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, distributed database management for cross-disciplinary datasets, and the development of hybrid AI-human interfaces for collaborative design iteration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop data-driven tools to optimize individualized education plans (IEPs) for students with orthopedic and other physical health impairments through advanced computational modeling. Current IEP design faces challenges in systematically addressing the heterogeneous needs of students, including mobility limitations, assistive technology dependencies, and variable health-related absences. Existing approaches often rely on qualitative assessments, which can lead to delays in identifying effective interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework leveraging machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student outcomes under diverse educational strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multimodal datasets—including academic performance metrics, assistive technology usage logs, and physical accessibility assessments—while training ensemble ML models to predict intervention efficacy. ABM simulations will replicate classroom dynamics, testing how environmental adaptations (e.g., desk configurations, digital tool integration) and instructional methods impact student engagement and learning. The project will utilize federated learning techniques to preserve privacy across distributed educational records from partner institutions. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform that recommends IEP adjustments based on real-time data, prioritized accessibility features for classroom environments, and evidence-based guidelines for educators. By quantifying relationships between instructional strategies, assistive technologies, and student success, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error in special education practices and improve resource allocation for students with physical impairments. The scalability of these models, enabled by HPC, will support future research on equitable AI applications in special education, ensuring tools remain adaptable to evolving policies and diverse student needs.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Orthopedic and Other Physical Health Impairments
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with orthopedic and other health impairments which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying physically disabled students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with orthopedic and other health impairments, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Agricultural productivity faces mounting challenges due to climate variability, emerging pathogens, and the need for sustainable intensification. Traditional crop improvement approaches, which rely on iterative field trials and phenotypic selection, are time-consuming and insufficient to address these pressures at scale. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate the development of climate-resilient, disease-resistant crop varieties through genomic prediction and machine learning. We will integrate multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, and metabolomic profiles) from staple crops with environmental data to model genotype-by-environment interactions. Computational workflows will include genome-wide association studies (GWAS), neural networks trained on historical yield and stress-response data, and agent-based simulations of pest-disease spread under projected climate scenarios. These analyses require parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative parameter optimization, which exceeds the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The HPC environment will enable rapid variant discovery, high-resolution prediction of trait performance in diverse agroecological zones, and dynamic risk mapping for pathogens. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes linked to drought tolerance and disease resistance, open-source predictive models for breeding prioritization, and region-specific recommendations for crop management. By providing scalable computational tools to decode complex trait architectures, this work will directly support public agricultural extension services and breeding programs, enhancing their capacity to disseminate adaptive crop varieties. The resulting frameworks will be shared via collaborative platforms to foster innovation in agricultural research, ultimately contributing to food security and climate adaptation efforts.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general agricultural sciences and related services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a novel investigation into the psychological impacts of urban built environments on stress and social behavior—a critical yet underexplored area in environmental psychology. Traditional methods in this field often rely on small-scale surveys or observational studies, limiting the ability to model complex, dynamic interactions between environmental variables (e.g., noise levels, green space density, architectural layout) and human behavioral outcomes at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning (ML), and geospatial analysis to simulate how diverse urban configurations influence stress responses and social connectivity. The ABM component will simulate population-level interactions within high-resolution 3D urban models, incorporating psychophysiological data (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels) to parameterize stress dynamics. ML algorithms will analyze large-scale datasets from wearable sensors, public health records, and environmental sensors to identify nonlinear relationships between environmental features and psychological outcomes. Geospatial tools will map these relationships across varying urban contexts. The computational intensity of simultaneously modeling millions of agent interactions, training predictive ML models on heterogeneous data, and processing high-dimensional geospatial layers necessitates HPC resources for parallelization and memory management. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying urban design features that mitigate stress and foster social cohesion, (2) open-source tools for simulating environment-behavior dynamics, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for urban planners and policymakers. By bridging computational scalability with psychological theory, this work aims to transform how environmental psychology informs equitable, health-promoting design—a priority in counseling and applied psychology. The requested resources will enable unprecedented resolution in analyzing how everyday environments shape mental well-being at population scales.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of behavioral interactions between human beings and the environment in individual and group contexts, and ways to improve them. Includes instruction in contextual theory; statistics; physiological, social, and psychological responses to natural and technological hazards and disease; environmental perception and cognition; loneliness and stress; and psychological aspects of environmental design and planning.

abstract: Wooden boatbuilding integrates artisanal techniques with evolving material and hydrodynamic challenges, yet the field lacks robust computational tools to systematically optimize designs, predict structural failures, or model environmental impacts on traditional materials. This project seeks to address these gaps by employing high-performance computing (HPC) to develop predictive models for wooden boat performance and longevity. The research will focus on two interconnected computational workflows: finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate stress distribution in complex joinery and planking systems under dynamic loads, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to evaluate hull efficiency and stability across diverse hydrodynamic conditions. Machine learning algorithms will augment these simulations by training on historical datasets of wood degradation, moisture absorption, and failure modes specific to marine environments. Additionally, parametric modeling will explore trade-offs between traditional construction methods (e.g., carvel vs. clinker planking) and modern material hybrids. By leveraging HPC resources, the project will iteratively refine these models at scale, enabling sensitivity analyses across variables such as timber species, fastener corrosion rates, and sail rigging configurations. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools for boatbuilders to virtually prototype designs, predictive frameworks for maintenance scheduling, and evidence-based guidelines for sustainable material selection. This work aims to preserve maritime heritage by enhancing the precision of traditional practices while reducing trial-and-error waste, ultimately fostering safer, more durable wooden vessels. The computational pipelines developed will also serve as pedagogical resources, integrating digital literacy into technical curricula for future boatbuilding professionals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to construct and repair traditional and modern wooden boats. Includes instruction in budgeting, drafting, fairing, lofting, joinery, planking, spars and rigging, and woodworking.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern communication systems and electronic devices necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in design optimization, electromagnetic interference mitigation, and signal integrity analysis. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-physics simulation frameworks for next-generation wireless communication systems and high-frequency electronic circuits. The research focuses on two interconnected objectives: (1) modeling wave propagation and scattering in dense urban environments for 5G/6G millimeter-wave networks, and (2) analyzing crosstalk effects in high-speed printed circuit boards (PCBs) with sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave coexistence. Leveraging finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods and machine learning-assisted optimization algorithms, the simulations will account for multi-scale electromagnetic phenomena, material nonlinearities, and thermal effects across three-dimensional geometries. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated Maxwell solvers with neural network surrogates to reduce simulation costs while maintaining physical fidelity. Expected outcomes include optimized antenna array configurations for base stations, interference mitigation strategies for IoT device clusters, and predictive models for signal degradation in multi-layer PCBs. By enabling large-scale parametric studies across 100+ design variables, the HPC resources will directly support the development of energy-efficient communication hardware prototypes and contribute to standardization efforts for spectrum sharing in smart city applications. The resulting open-source simulation tools and datasets will provide the research community with validated benchmarks for emerging challenges in electromagnetic compatibility and heterogeneous network design. This work aligns with national priorities in advanced communication infrastructure while addressing critical gaps in practical engineering methodologies for industry applications.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of electrical, electronics and communication engineers. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, prototype development and testing, systems analysis and testing, systems maintenance, instrument calibration, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of autonomous robotic systems operating in dynamic, unstructured environments necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize control strategies and ensure real-time adaptability. Current approaches for multi-robot coordination, sensor fusion, and path planning often rely on simplified models or offline simulations, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios where latency, scalability, and uncertainty are critical challenges. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate novel algorithms for distributed, real-time control of heterogeneous robotic systems. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) implementing parallelized simulations of multi-agent interactions in physics-based virtual environments to test swarm intelligence algorithms under variable constraints, (2) training machine learning models for adaptive sensor fusion using large-scale datasets from lidar, vision, and inertial measurement units, and (3) optimizing embedded control code through hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing accelerated by GPU-accelerated computation. Computational methods will include hybrid agent-based modeling frameworks, Monte Carlo optimization for robustness testing, and neural network architectures optimized for low-latency inference. By enabling high-fidelity simulations of complex mechatronic systems and reducing the computational bottleneck in algorithm development, this work aims to advance the design of scalable, resilient automation solutions for industrial logistics and collaborative robotics. The requested HPC resources will directly support the parallel execution of thousands of simulation instances, reduce model training times through distributed computing, and facilitate the transition from simulation to physical prototypes. Outcomes are expected to contribute open-source tools for robotic system co-design and demonstrate quantifiable improvements in task completion times and energy efficiency for autonomous material handling applications.
cip_title: Mechatronics, Robotics, and Automation Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in the support of engineers to the design, development, and operational evaluation of autonomous, computer-controlled, electro-mechanical systems. Includes instruction in computer and software engineering, control engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, and robotics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of health system pharmacy operations, driven by expanding patient populations, diverse medication regimens, and dynamic resource constraints, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize clinical and administrative decision-making. This project seeks to address critical gaps in real-time, data-driven management of pharmacy workflows, medication safety surveillance, and resource allocation within large healthcare systems. Current methodologies often rely on static protocols or retrospective analyses, which lack the scalability and adaptability required for modern, high-volume clinical environments. To overcome these limitations, we propose the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating machine learning (ML) and discrete-event simulation (DES) models. These models will analyze multi-source data—including electronic health records, pharmacy dispensing logs, and supply chain metrics—to predict medication demand, identify latent risks of drug shortages or adverse events, and simulate the impact of operational interventions. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization of DES parameters to reflect real-world variability in patient arrivals, staffing patterns, and facility-specific constraints. Key computational challenges include training ensemble ML algorithms on imbalanced clinical outcomes data and achieving sub-second latency for scenario testing in mission-critical applications. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive tools for proactive inventory management, risk-stratified workload balancing across pharmacy teams, and dynamic scheduling algorithms to minimize medication turnaround times. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for health system pharmacy leaders to evaluate operational trade-offs, mitigate risks, and allocate finite resources with precision. The resulting frameworks will be disseminated as open-source modules to support reproducibility and adoption across diverse clinical settings, ultimately advancing the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of medication use systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on Health System Pharmacy Administration

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border information ecosystems and their impact on strategic stability in contested regions, focusing on how emerging communication technologies reshape state and non-state actor interactions in asymmetric security environments. Traditional frameworks in international relations often overlook the computational complexity of real-time, multi-actor information flows, which increasingly influence crisis decision-making and escalation pathways. To address this gap, the research employs a mixed-methods approach integrating large-scale network analysis, agent-based modeling (ABM), and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate and analyze decentralized information dissemination patterns across social media, state-aligned media, and encrypted platforms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multilingual text corpora (spanning 10+ languages) from open-source intelligence (OSINT) datasets, model multi-agent interactions at scale, and run Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic escalation scenarios under varying technological and geopolitical constraints. Key computational challenges include real-time sentiment analysis of adversarial narratives, dynamic network clustering to identify emergent influence clusters, and ABM calibration using historical case studies (e.g., hybrid conflicts in the South China Sea and Eastern Europe). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for quantifying information ecosystem volatility, predictive models of technology-driven escalation triggers, and policy-relevant insights into platform governance and crisis communication protocols. By bridging computational social science with security studies, this project aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing nonlinear, technology-mediated conflicts while advancing infrastructure for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of data science and strategic studies.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Maternal and child health outcomes are shaped by complex interactions between biological, social, and environmental determinants, yet existing models often fail to capture these multidimensional relationships at scale. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large, integrated datasets spanning clinical records, socioeconomic indicators, environmental exposures, and public health program participation across diverse populations. The research will develop computational models to identify critical risk factors for adverse pregnancy outcomes, childhood chronic conditions, and disparities in healthcare access. Using machine learning algorithms optimized for HPC environments, including ensemble methods and neural networks, we will analyze longitudinal data from 2.5 million maternal-child dyads across five U.S. regions. These analyses will be coupled with agent-based simulations to model the population-level impacts of proposed interventions, such as nutritional support programs or prenatal care policy changes. The computational workflow requires parallel processing capabilities to manage high-dimensional data integration, real-time geospatial mapping of health resource availability, and sensitivity analyses across simulated scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize high-risk populations, evidence-based frameworks for tailoring community health initiatives, and policy simulations quantifying the potential health equity impacts of legislative proposals. By elucidating how structural determinants interact with biological factors, this work will provide novel insights for reducing perinatal mortality, addressing childhood obesity disparities, and optimizing resource allocation in public health systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling petabyte-scale health data while maintaining privacy-preserving federated learning architectures across institutional partners. This project directly aligns with national maternal health equity goals and advances computational methodologies for translational public health research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of public health specializations, public policy studies, and the social and behavioral sciences to issues of health affecting women, children, and families; and prepares individuals to function as maternal and child health specialists. Includes instruction in research design and testing, program evaluation, public policy analysis, public finance, economics of health care, community health, family development and dynamics, women's studies, social psychology, fetal and child development, biostatistics, health education and promotion, nutrition, neonatal development, psychology, and social services delivery.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in precision manufacturing workflows by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize toolpath generation and material behavior prediction in subtractive and additive manufacturing processes. Current approaches to precision production trades, particularly in CNC machining and 3D printing, rely on iterative physical prototyping and simplified computational models that inadequately account for dynamic thermal, mechanical, and material interactions. This results in prolonged development cycles, material waste, and suboptimal product performance. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a multi-physics simulation framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) models to predict tool wear, residual stresses, and microstructure evolution during fabrication. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations across diverse manufacturing scenarios, processing high-resolution sensor data from in-situ monitoring systems to train neural networks for real-time process adjustments. Computational workloads will include parametric optimization of machining parameters (e.g., feed rates, spindle speeds) and layer-by-layer thermal history modeling for metal additive manufacturing, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for ML inference and distributed memory clusters for large-scale FEA/CFD coupling. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of reducing prototyping iterations by 40–60% in precision machining applications and improving dimensional accuracy in complex additive components by 15–25%. The resource-intensive nature of these simulations—particularly the need to resolve micron-scale features across macro-scale workpieces—necessitates access to HPC architectures with petascale storage and low-latency interconnects. Results will advance data-driven decision-making in precision production trades while providing open-source simulation templates to bridge gaps between academic research and industry adoption. This work directly supports workforce development in advanced manufacturing by integrating HPC workflows into technical curricula for precision production specialists.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in creating products using precision crafting and technical illustration.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of advanced architectural design and simulation tasks within the Architectural Drafting and CAD/CADD discipline. Current workflows in architectural modeling, energy efficiency analysis, and structural integrity assessment are increasingly limited by conventional computing resources, particularly when handling complex, large-scale projects or high-resolution simulations. The research aims to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable rapid iteration of parametric designs, multi-physics simulations, and machine learning-driven optimization processes that are infeasible on standard workstations. Key computational methods include the deployment of finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress testing, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for airflow and thermal modeling, and generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate design optimization for energy efficiency. These tasks will utilize parallelized software frameworks such as OpenFOAM and TensorFlow, scaled across HPC nodes to reduce simulation times from weeks to days. The project also involves developing GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for real-time visualization of high-detail architectural models, enhancing collaborative design review processes. Expected outcomes include validated workflows for integrating HPC into architectural CAD/CADD education and practice, novel algorithms for sustainable material optimization, and open-access datasets of simulated building performance under diverse environmental conditions. By overcoming computational bottlenecks, this work will empower students and practitioners to explore innovative, data-driven design solutions that balance aesthetic, structural, and ecological requirements. The resource allocation will directly support curriculum advancements, enabling hands-on training with industrial-scale computational tools while contributing to broader efforts in sustainable architecture research.
cip_title: Architectural Drafting and Architectural CAD/ CADD
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to develop working drawings and electronic simulations for architectural and related construction projects. Includes instruction in basic construction and structural design, architectural rendering, architectural-aided drafting (CAD), layout and designs, architectural blueprint interpretation, building materials, and basic structural wiring diagramming.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in nuclear reactor material degradation under extreme operational conditions through advanced computational modeling. Nuclear power plants rely on structural materials subjected to intense radiation, thermal stress, and corrosive environments, which lead to embrittlement, swelling, and reduced lifespan. Current experimental methods to study these phenomena are limited by cost, time, and the inability to probe atomic-scale mechanisms in real time. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven multiscale simulation framework integrating quantum mechanical calculations, molecular dynamics, and continuum-scale finite element analysis. The research will model radiation damage cascades in reactor-grade steels, zirconium alloys, and advanced accident-tolerant fuel cladding materials, capturing defect evolution and mechanical property changes across spatial and temporal scales. Large-scale parallelized simulations will quantify the synergistic effects of neutron irradiation, hydrogen embrittlement, and thermal cycling on microstructural stability. Machine learning interatomic potentials will be trained on ab initio datasets to balance accuracy and computational efficiency for defect migration energetics. The HPC workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated codes (e.g., LAMMPS, DAMASK) to simulate representative volume elements containing millions of atoms over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. Expected outcomes include predictive models for material failure thresholds, validated against experimental irradiation data from collaborating national laboratories. These results will directly inform safety margins, maintenance schedules, and the development of radiation-resistant alloys for next-generation reactors. By enabling atomic-to-macro property linkages, this work bridges a critical gap in nuclear materials science while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in accelerating the design cycle for nuclear energy systems. The requested computing resources will support over 500,000 node-hours of simulations, generating datasets to advance both academic understanding and industrial applications of nuclear technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of research scientists and operating engineers engaged in the running of nuclear reactors, and in nuclear materials processing and disposal. Includes instruction in basic nuclear physics and nuclear engineering, monitoring and safety procedures, radioactive materials handling and disposal, equipment maintenance and operation, and record keeping.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic relationship between digital communication platforms and emergent linguistic phenomena, focusing on how decentralized, large-scale online interactions drive rapid syntactic and semantic shifts in understudied multilingual contexts. While traditional sociolinguistic frameworks have examined language change in physical communities, the computational demands of analyzing real-time, cross-platform digital discourse—particularly in low-resource languages and non-standard dialects—remain a critical barrier. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to process terabytes of timestamped textual data from social media, messaging apps, and collaborative platforms across five linguistically diverse regions, targeting communities with limited prior documentation of their digital linguistic practices. A hybrid methodology combining transformer-based neural architectures for morphosyntactic annotation, agent-based modeling of lexical diffusion networks, and graph-theoretic analysis of semantic field evolution will be implemented. Custom pipelines will be developed to handle code-switching patterns, non-Latin scripts, and platform-specific orthographic variations, with iterative model training conducted on GPU clusters. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable framework for detecting latent grammatical innovations in noisy, multilingual digital corpora; (2) quantitative models correlating platform affordances (e.g., character limits, reaction features) with rates of semantic change; and (3) an open-access repository of annotated datasets representing under-resourced digital language varieties. By elucidating the computational signatures of online language adaptation, this work aims to advance theoretical understanding of how technosocial systems shape linguistic diversity while providing practical tools for educators and developers working with marginalized language communities in digital spaces. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive graph computations, parallel processing of heterogeneous data streams, and large-scale comparative simulations across linguistic subsystems.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize pedagogical strategies for training secondary psychology educators, addressing the gap in evidence-based approaches for integrating data-driven instructional tools into teacher education programs. While psychology education increasingly emphasizes quantitative reasoning and digital literacy, existing teacher preparation frameworks often lack systematic methods to evaluate how emerging computational techniques—such as simulation-based learning or real-time classroom analytics—can enhance pedagogical content knowledge. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets from simulated teaching environments, including structured lesson plans, dynamic student response patterns, and instructor feedback from three partner teacher training institutions. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions under diverse instructional scenarios, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will assess the alignment between taught psychological concepts and learners’ conceptual understanding. Machine learning models will identify predictive relationships between specific pedagogical interventions (e.g., case-based learning modules, adaptive assessment tools) and pre-service teachers’ competency development. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization across educational variables and Monte Carlo simulations to account for variability in learner populations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for embedding computational thinking into psychology teacher curricula, evidence-based guidelines for data-informed instructional design, and open-source tools to help educators visualize the longitudinal impacts of pedagogical choices. By establishing scalable methods to evaluate teaching effectiveness in psychology education, this work aims to directly improve secondary students’ critical engagement with psychological science while advancing computational applications in subject-specific teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to advance predictive modeling and risk assessment in building inspection processes. Current inspection protocols often rely on reactive, manual evaluations, which can miss latent structural vulnerabilities or material degradation patterns. To address this, the research will integrate computational simulations with real-world inspection data to create predictive models capable of identifying high-risk failure points in residential and commercial structures. The core computational challenge lies in processing large-scale datasets—including 3D building scans, material property databases, and historical inspection records—while simulating complex physical behaviors (e.g., stress distribution, moisture intrusion, thermal expansion) under diverse environmental conditions. Leveraging HPC resources, we will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) models to assess structural integrity across multi-physics domains, combined with machine learning algorithms trained on failure case histories to prioritize inspection targets. The workflows will utilize open-source tools like OpenFOAM and TensorFlow, optimized for distributed computing architectures to handle iterative simulations and probabilistic risk calculations. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform that quantifies failure probabilities for critical building components, identifies inspection priorities based on dynamic risk thresholds, and generates actionable reports for inspectors. This system aims to reduce oversight gaps in aging infrastructure, improve compliance with evolving building codes, and mitigate safety hazards. By transitioning inspection practices from periodic checklists to data-driven, predictive analytics, the project aligns with national efforts to enhance urban resilience and adaptive building management. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the necessary computational scale, enabling rapid scenario testing across heterogeneous building types and environmental variables while maintaining fidelity to real-world inspection constraints.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply industrial, labor, and governmental standards and laws to the oversight of construction projects and the maintenance of completed buildings and other structures. Includes instruction in construction processes and techniques, materials analysis, occupational safety and health, industry standards, building codes and specifications, blueprint interpretation, testing equipment and procedures, communication skills, accident investigation, and documentation.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in precision veterinary care by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between animal health parameters, treatment protocols, and disease outcomes. Veterinary medicine faces challenges in predicting individualized therapeutic responses due to the biological diversity of species, breeds, and physiological conditions. Existing clinical decision-making tools often rely on generalized data, limiting their utility in optimizing care for specific patients. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and multi-scale pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling. The research will utilize anonymized clinical datasets—including hematological, biochemical, and imaging data from companion animals and livestock—to train ML models that predict treatment efficacy and adverse event risks. Concurrently, HPC-enabled PK/PD simulations will model drug metabolism dynamics across species-specific physiological parameters, such as metabolic rate and organ function. These models will be validated against retrospective clinical outcomes data from partner veterinary hospitals. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of datasets (>10^6 data points), parallelized parameter optimization for ML architectures, and stochastic simulations of drug interactions across biological scales. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision-support tool for veterinary professionals, enabling tailored dosing regimens and improved prognostication for conditions like sepsis, chronic renal disease, and post-surgical complications. By enhancing the precision of veterinary interventions, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches, lower healthcare costs, and improve welfare outcomes for animal patients. The project aligns with advancing educational objectives in veterinary technology by providing a scalable computational resource for training students in data-driven clinical practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary/ Animal Health Technology and Veterinary Assistant
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of veterinarians, laboratory animal specialists, and zoological professionals, to provide patient management, care, and clinical procedures assistance as well as owner communication. Includes instruction in animal nursing care, animal health and nutrition, animal handling, clinical pathology, radiology, anesthesiology, dental prophylaxis, surgical assisting, clinical laboratory procedures, office administration skills, patient and owner management, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: Urban forests are critical for mitigating climate change impacts, enhancing biodiversity, and improving public health in cities. However, their sustainability is threatened by compounding stressors, including heatwaves, air pollution, invasive pests, and fragmented habitats. Current models struggle to capture the dynamic interactions between these factors at the spatial and temporal scales relevant to urban ecosystems, limiting actionable insights for management. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate urban forest resilience under diverse future scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate remote sensing data, species-specific physiological traits, and spatially explicit environmental variables (e.g., localized pollution levels, microclimate gradients, and human activity patterns) into an agent-based model. This model will simulate tree growth, mortality, and pest dispersal dynamics across heterogeneous urban landscapes. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to identify tipping points in ecosystem service provision and predict optimal species compositions for climate adaptation. The computational demand arises from the need to process city-scale LiDAR datasets, run millions of parallelized ecological interactions, and perform sensitivity analyses across probabilistic climate projections. Outcomes will include predictive maps of canopy vulnerability, policy-ready thresholds for pollutant exposure, and a publicly accessible toolkit for adaptive urban forestry planning. By quantifying trade-offs between tree species selection, pest management strategies, and ecosystem benefits, this work will directly inform municipal green infrastructure policies, enhancing equitable access to urban forest services in the face of rapid environmental change.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of forestry and related sciences to the development, care, and maintenance of individual trees and forested areas within or close to areas of dense human habitation. Includes instruction in urban environments; effects of pollution on tree species; environmental design and landscaping; urban pest infestation; urban forest management; and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: Emerging zoonotic diseases increasingly threaten global health, driven by environmental change, habitat fragmentation, and shifting species interactions.
