Current predictive models often lack integration of ecological dynamics with epidemiological processes, limiting their ability to forecast spillover risks in heterogeneous landscapes. This project aims to develop a spatially explicit, multiscale framework to quantify how ecological community structure and land-use change modulate pathogen transmission at wildlife-human interfaces. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will parameterize agent-based models (ABMs) with empirical data from longitudinal wildlife surveys, remote sensing, and pathogen genomic sequences across tropical agroforestry systems. The ABMs will simulate host movement, resource competition, and cross-species contact rates under scenarios of deforestation and climate variability. Concurrently, Bayesian phylodynamic models will reconstruct pathogen spread histories using viral phylogenies and environmental covariates. A key innovation involves coupling these approaches through approximate Bayesian computation (ABC), iteratively refining ecological parameters to align simulated outbreak patterns with observed phylogeographic and epidemiological data. This integration requires computationally intensive parameter sweeps and likelihood-free inference methods, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical ecological thresholds that amplify spillover risk, (2) high-resolution risk maps for priority regions, and (3) open-source tools for adaptive surveillance in changing ecosystems. By unifying ecological and epidemiological theory with advanced computational workflows, this work will advance predictive capacity for pre-emergent zoonoses while addressing scalability challenges in complex systems modeling. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling terabyte-scale environmental datasets, running stochastic simulations across parameter spaces, and performing iterative model comparisons—tasks infeasible on standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of epidemiology and biostatistics or a specialization which draws from epidemiology and biostatistics. Includes instruction in biostatistics, disease and injury determinants, epidemiology, health services research, pathology, spatial analysis, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociolinguistic dynamics of understudied sign languages in digitally mediated environments, focusing on how emerging technologies shape language evolution and accessibility for Deaf communities. While sign languages are critical to cultural identity and communication, many remain under-documented, particularly in regions with limited institutional support. The research addresses two interrelated gaps: (1) the absence of large-scale computational models capable of analyzing visual-spatial linguistic features in real-time interactions, and (2) the need to quantify how digital platforms influence sign language vitality and intergenerational transmission. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will process multimodal datasets—including video recordings of naturalistic sign language use, motion-capture data, and user-generated content from Deaf-led online communities—to identify patterns in lexical innovation, grammatical variation, and cross-sign language contact. Computational methods will integrate 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial-temporal feature extraction, graph-based algorithms to model community interaction networks, and agent-based simulations to project language shift scenarios under varying technological adoption rates. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for sign language corpus analysis, predictive models of lexical convergence in digital contexts, and empirically grounded recommendations for inclusive platform design. By centering computational rigor on marginalized linguistic systems, this work advances interdisciplinary scholarship at the intersection of language preservation, human-computer interaction, and social equity, offering methodological innovations applicable to other embodied communication modalities. The requested HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the project’s terabyte-scale visual data and computationally intensive simulations, which exceed the capacity of standard university computing clusters.
cip_title: Linguistic, Comparative, and Related Language Studies and Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in linguistic, comparative, and related language studies and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic pricing and inventory management strategies for omnichannel retail systems, addressing the growing complexity of consumer behavior, supply chain disruptions, and multi-platform sales operations. While traditional retail models rely on static assumptions about demand elasticity and supplier reliability, modern retail environments require real-time adaptive decision-making under uncertainty. We propose a hybrid machine learning and agent-based modeling approach to simulate interactions between customer segments, inventory nodes, and pricing algorithms across physical stores, e-commerce platforms, and third-party marketplaces. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of simulating 10,000+ concurrent agents representing customers, suppliers, and logistics systems while incorporating terabyte-scale datasets of historical sales, web traffic, and supply chain records. The computational workflow will integrate deep reinforcement learning for price optimization, graph neural networks to model supply chain dependencies, and Monte Carlo methods to quantify operational risks. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for simulating multi-echelon retail systems under stochastic demand, (2) evidence-based thresholds for automated price adjustments across sales channels, and (3) predictive metrics for inventory allocation that balance warehousing costs with service-level requirements. This research will provide retail managers with scalable decision-support tools to improve profitability in hybrid sales environments while maintaining computational reproducibility—a gap in current retail management literature. The project’s HPC requirements stem from the need to run parameter sweeps across hundreds of market scenarios and validate models against decade-long temporal datasets, tasks that exceed the capacity of standard enterprise computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operations of a wide variety of retail businesses, including department stores; independent and chain stores; fashion, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical establishments; and online retail businesses. Includes instruction in retail management, merchandise management, customer service management, marketing, organizational behavior, accounting, finance, business law, and personnel management.

abstract: Healthcare unit management faces critical challenges in optimizing staffing and resource allocation amidst dynamic patient care demands, particularly in acute care settings. Traditional scheduling approaches rely on retrospective data and static protocols, often failing to adapt to real-time variability in patient acuity, admission surges, or staff availability. This project proposes a computational framework to model patient flow, predict short-term care demands, and simulate staffing configurations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research integrates anonymized electronic health records (EHRs), real-time bed telemetry, and staff competency matrices to develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate unit operations under diverse scenarios. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs), will analyze temporal patterns in patient admissions, transfers, and discharge trajectories. Monte Carlo methods will assess probabilistic outcomes of staffing decisions under constraints such as nurse-patient ratios, skill mix requirements, and unexpected absenteeism. The computational pipeline will be validated against historical operational data from three tertiary care facilities, with sensitivity analyses quantifying the impact of predictive accuracy on resource utilization metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool that enables ward supervisors to dynamically optimize staff deployment, reduce overtime costs, and maintain care quality during demand fluctuations. By bridging operations research, predictive analytics, and healthcare management, this work addresses a critical gap in adaptive resource allocation strategies for modern clinical units. The HPC infrastructure is essential for scaling simulations across multi-unit hospital systems and achieving the granular temporal resolution required for minute-to-minute operational decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of nursing or medical service administrators, to supervise and coordinate the operations of one or more patient care units in hospitals or other health care facilities. Includes instruction in planning and initiating administrative procedures, personnel supervision, interpersonal skills, general and/or specialized health care operations and procedures, and consultation with other medical, nursing, and administrative team members.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dispersion and health impacts of airborne contaminants in urban environments, integrating dynamic interactions between human mobility, built infrastructure, and atmospheric conditions. Current models often treat indoor and outdoor environments as separate systems, creating gaps in assessing real-world exposure risks exacerbated by climate change and urbanization. Our research addresses this by coupling agent-based simulations of pedestrian movement with high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to predict contaminant transport across interconnected microenvironments. The proposed work will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-scale scenarios, including pollutant infiltration into buildings, ventilation efficacy in transit hubs, and population-level exposure disparities during extreme heat or pollution events. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in uncertainty quantification, enabling sensitivity analyses across diverse urban morphologies and meteorological conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to optimize emergency response protocols, urban design guidelines for pollution mitigation, and evidence-based policies to reduce environmental health inequities. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling large-scale simulations involving 10^6–10^7 grid cells for CFD, parallelized stochastic agent models, and integration with real-world sensor data from municipal air quality networks. By advancing coupled human-environment system modeling, this work will support resilient infrastructure planning and improve public health interventions for vulnerable populations. The computational workflows developed will also serve as a template for future studies on emerging contaminants and climate adaptation strategies in environmental engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: Mental health disorders represent a significant global burden, yet their underlying biological and computational mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the complexity of integrating multi-modal data across genetic, neuroimaging, and behavioral domains. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model the interactions between genetic risk factors, brain network dynamics, and symptom trajectories in psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia and major depressive disorder. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze large-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequencing, functional MRI (fMRI) time series, and longitudinal clinical assessments from multinational cohorts. Key computational methods include the implementation of deep learning architectures to identify transdiagnostic biomarkers, Bayesian network models to infer causal pathways linking genetic variants to neural circuit dysfunction, and graph theoretical analyses to characterize dynamic brain connectivity patterns. These approaches require intensive parallel processing due to the high dimensionality of genomic data (~10^6–10^7 variants), the temporal resolution of fMRI datasets (~10^5 voxel-timepoints per subject), and the need for iterative simulations across diverse patient subgroups. Anticipated outcomes include the discovery of stratified risk profiles for treatment-resistant depression and psychosis, as well as predictive models of disease progression informed by genotype-neurophenotype interactions. The project will also generate open-source tools for scalable multi-omics integration in psychiatric research. By elucidating mechanisms that transcend traditional diagnostic boundaries, this work aims to advance precision psychiatry and inform the development of targeted neurotherapeutic interventions. The scale of data harmonization, model training, and validation necessitates access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes, large-memory capacity, and distributed storage to accommodate petabyte-scale datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on Psychiatric/Mental Health

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial equipment and the critical need to minimize unplanned downtime in heavy machinery operations necessitate advanced predictive maintenance frameworks. Current methodologies often rely on simplified analytical models or limited sensor data, which struggle to account for the multi-physics interactions, material degradation patterns, and operational variability inherent to industrial environments. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate equipment degradation mechanisms and optimize maintenance schedules using high-performance computing (HPC). The research will integrate sensor-derived operational data with multiphysics simulations—including finite element analysis for structural stress, computational fluid dynamics for thermal and hydraulic systems, and tribological modeling for wear prediction—to create a holistic digital twin of heavy industrial equipment. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on HPC clusters to identify failure precursors from heterogeneous datasets spanning vibration, thermal, and lubrication metrics. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, real-time Bayesian inference for probabilistic failure forecasting, and iterative optimization of maintenance protocols under diverse operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable predictive maintenance platform capable of reducing equipment downtime by 20–30%, extending component lifespans through optimized lubrication and load management, and providing actionable insights for resource allocation in maintenance workflows. This work will establish a novel paradigm for data-driven decision-making in industrial maintenance, directly contributing to operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability in sectors reliant on heavy machinery. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the required computational granularity and temporal resolution to resolve complex failure modes while maintaining practical scalability for industry adoption.
cip_title: Heavy/ Industrial Equipment Maintenance Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in heavy or industrial equipment maintenance technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize meal planning for individuals with complex dietary needs, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address scalability and precision challenges in clinical dietetics. Current manual methods for designing personalized meal plans are labor-intensive and often struggle to balance dynamic variables such as nutritional requirements, allergen restrictions, cultural preferences, budgetary constraints, and real-time ingredient availability. The proposed research will construct a machine learning model trained on multi-source datasets, including national nutritional databases, electronic health records, and regional food cost and supply-chain data. HPC resources will enable parallelized processing of these heterogeneous datasets to identify optimal ingredient combinations, portion sizes, and meal sequences while adhering to evidence-based dietary guidelines. The model will integrate constraint satisfaction algorithms to navigate trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., maximizing nutrient density while minimizing cost) and simulate longitudinal outcomes for chronic disease management scenarios. Validation will involve retrospective comparison against dietitian-created plans from clinical records and prospective testing through a pilot study with dietitian assistants. Successful implementation will yield an open-source tool that generates actionable, patient-specific meal recommendations in seconds—a process that currently takes hours. This tool aims to reduce cognitive workload for dietetic teams, improve adherence through culturally tailored options, and enhance scalability of nutrition interventions in underserved populations. The project’s computational demands—including large-scale matrix operations for nutrient optimization and Monte Carlo simulations for cost variability analysis—necessitate HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant throughput. Outcomes will advance both applied dietetics and computational methods in healthcare optimization, with potential integration into telehealth platforms and dietitian training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist registered dietitians in planning, preparing and serving meals to individuals with specific dietary needs. Includes instruction in equipment use, food preparation, diet regulations, food handling, safety and sanitary standards and administrative techniques and procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in commercial vehicle operations and driver training, with a focus on optimizing safety, efficiency, and instructional outcomes. Commercial vehicle operators face complex demands, including dynamic route planning, real-time hazard response, and fuel efficiency management, while instructors require advanced tools to simulate high-risk scenarios and assess trainee performance. Current training frameworks and operational decision-support systems often lack the computational capacity to model large-scale, real-world variables such as traffic patterns, weather conditions, or vehicle telemetry data at sufficient fidelity. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a multi-scale simulation platform integrating agent-based traffic modeling, vehicle dynamics analysis, and machine learning-driven risk prediction. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of fleet operations across diverse geographic and environmental conditions, coupled with probabilistic modeling of mechanical failures or driver errors. Additionally, generative AI methods will be applied to synthesize rare but critical scenarios (e.g., extreme weather, system malfunctions) for immersive virtual training modules. The computational workflow will process terabytes of historical telematics data, driver performance records, and traffic incident reports to identify risk correlations and optimize instructional content. Outcomes include predictive tools for route efficiency, personalized trainee assessment algorithms, and a scenario library for adaptive simulation-based instruction. By quantifying the impact of operational decisions and training interventions, this research aims to reduce accident rates, lower fuel consumption, and enhance the scalability of commercial driver education programs. The project will directly support curriculum modernization in commercial vehicle operator training, aligning technical education with data-driven advancements in transportation technology.
cip_title: Truck and Bus Driver/ Commercial Vehicle Operator and Instructor
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to drive trucks and buses, delivery vehicles, for-hire vehicles and other commercial vehicles, or to instruct commercial vehicle operators. Includes instruction in operating gas, diesel, or electrically-powered vehicles; loading and unloading cargo or passengers; reporting delays or accidents on the road; verifying load against shipping papers; arranging transportation for personnel; and keeping records of receipts and fares.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in the computational modeling of ensemble performance dynamics under varied conducting techniques. Conductors face the complex task of translating musical scores into cohesive performances, balancing interpretive decisions with real-time communication to musicians. Traditional methods for analyzing these processes are limited by subjective observation and small-scale experimentation. This research proposes a computational framework to simulate and evaluate the impact of conducting strategies on ensemble synchronization, expressive accuracy, and adaptive responsiveness. Using motion-capture data from professional conductors, machine learning models will be trained to correlate gestural patterns with ensemble performance metrics derived from audio-visual recordings of rehearsals. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these datasets, as well as real-time simulations of virtual ensembles responding dynamically to algorithmic conducting gestures. The project further integrates score analysis algorithms to map structural features (e.g., tempo shifts, dynamic contrasts) to optimal conducting tactics, generating actionable insights for rehearsal planning. Outcomes will include an open-source software toolkit for conducting educators and ensemble directors, offering data-driven feedback on gesture efficacy and score interpretation. By quantifying the relationship between conducting practices and performance quality, this work aims to advance pedagogical methods, enhance ensemble cohesion in professional settings, and establish a foundation for computational research in music leadership. The requested resources are critical for handling the project’s intensive workloads, including neural network training, multichannel audio analysis, and real-time simulation rendering, which exceed the capacity of standard computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the art of leading bands, choirs, orchestras and other ensembles in performance, and related music leadership. Includes instruction in score analysis and arranging, rehearsal and performance leadership, music coaching, arrangement and performance planning, ensemble operations management, and applications to specific school or professional ensembles.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between digital cultural production and systemic power structures through the computational analysis of multimodal cultural datasets. As digital platforms increasingly mediate cultural expression—from social media discourse to algorithmic content curation—traditional critical frameworks struggle to scale to the volume, velocity, and heterogeneity of contemporary data. The research problem centers on mapping how hegemonic narratives emerge and circulate within decentralized digital ecosystems, particularly examining the entanglement of user-generated content, platform algorithms, and geopolitical influences. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a mixed-methods approach combining large-scale natural language processing, network analysis, and visual culture analytics to process petabytes of multilingual social media posts, image-text memes, and streaming video metadata. Computational models will identify patterns in discursive framing, semiotic hybridization, and cross-platform narrative diffusion, while critical theory lenses—including intersectional feminism and postcolonial technoscience—will inform iterative model design and interpretation. Key technical challenges include developing transformer-based architectures sensitive to context-dependent cultural semantics and optimizing graph neural networks to trace ideological propagation across spatially fragmented user communities. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) a novel computational framework for critical cultural analytics that bridges hermeneutic traditions and machine learning; (2) empirical findings on how platform architectures amplify or suppress counterhegemonic cultural practices; and (3) open-source tools enabling researchers to audit algorithmic bias in cultural recommendation systems. By requiring parallelized GPU clusters for training multimodal models and distributed storage for heterogeneous data ingestion, this work both advances interdisciplinary methodologies and demonstrates how HPC infrastructure can empower humanistic inquiry into 21st-century cultural formations.
cip_title: Cultural Studies/ Critical Theory and Analysis
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the analysis and critique of culture in its varied forms, including values, ideas, belief systems, and expressive acts, and the relationship between cultural forms, everyday life, and structures of power. Includes instruction in anthropology, communications, history, literary studies, philosophy, political economy, and sociology, as well as recent theories and methodologies such as semiotics, deconstruction, postcolonial studies, gender theory, and ethnography.

abstract: Applied behavior analysis (ABA) relies on data-driven methodologies to design and optimize interventions that improve outcomes for individuals with developmental disabilities, including autism spectrum disorder. However, existing approaches to analyzing behavioral data often face limitations in scalability, personalization, and real-time adaptability due to the computational complexity of modeling dynamic, individualized behavior patterns across diverse settings. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing and validating computational models of behavioral change processes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage large-scale datasets comprising longitudinal behavior records, environmental context variables, and intervention histories from clinical and community settings. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and reinforcement learning algorithms, will be employed to identify latent patterns in behavior-environment interactions and predict individualized response trajectories. Agent-based modeling will simulate the emergent effects of intervention variations across heterogeneous populations, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment effect estimates under real-world conditions. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to generate actionable insights into optimal intervention timing, dosage, and adaptation strategies that traditional statistical methods cannot feasibly produce. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for behavior analysts to design personalized interventions using predictive modeling, as well as evidence-based frameworks for scaling effective ABA practices across service delivery systems. The computational infrastructure will specifically support research into reducing disparities in intervention access and effectiveness for underserved populations. This work advances the scientific rigor of ABA by enabling complex, data-intensive analyses critical for addressing the multifaceted needs of neurodiverse individuals while adhering to the ethical principles of behavioral research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principles of learning and behavior to enhance the development, abilities, and choices of children and adults; and that prepares individuals to address the behavioral needs of individuals, especially those with developmental disabilities and autism. Includes instruction in behavior analysis and learning, behavioral and functional assessment, developmental psychology, applied behavioral analysis in developmental disabilities and autism, applied behavioral analysis in mental health and aging, research methods, evaluation of interventions, and professional and ethical issues.

abstract: The study of enzyme-catalyzed organic reactions holds significant potential for advancing sustainable synthesis and pharmaceutical development, yet the mechanistic complexity of these processes often limits rational design. This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting and optimizing enzymatic reaction pathways for hydrocarbon derivatization, focusing on systems where traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve short-lived intermediates or transition states. We propose a computational approach integrating quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations with machine learning (ML)-guided molecular dynamics to model reaction dynamics at atomic resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the scale of these calculations, which involve thousands of parallelized simulations across multidimensional free energy landscapes. The project will utilize software packages such as GAMESS, AMBER, and PyTorch to iteratively train neural networks on QM/MM-derived datasets, enabling the identification of key electronic and steric factors governing catalytic efficiency. Initial work will focus on cytochrome P450-mediated C–H activation in polycyclic substrates, a reaction class critical to drug metabolite synthesis. Subsequent phases will expand to engineered enzymes for asymmetric [4+2] cycloadditions, targeting biocatalysts with improved stereoselectivity. Expected outcomes include predictive models for active-site mutagenesis effects, a database of optimized transition-state geometries, and protocols for rapid in silico screening of substrate scope. These results will directly inform collaborative experimental efforts to develop novel biocatalysts, reducing reliance on rare-metal catalysts in fine chemical production. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale data storage for trajectory analysis, and ML model training, enabling calculations impractical on local clusters. By bridging gaps between computational organic chemistry and enzymology, this work aims to accelerate the design of environmentally benign synthetic routes with applications in medicinal chemistry and industrial biotechnology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of hydrocarbon compounds and their derivatives. Includes instruction in molecular conversion and synthesis, molecular synthesis and design, the molecular structure of living cells and systems, the mutual reactivity of organic and inorganic compounds in combination, the spectroscopic analysis of hydrocarbon compounds, and applications to specific problems in research, industry, and health.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the evidence-based integration of Yoga Therapy and Ayurvedic principles into personalized health interventions. Despite growing clinical interest in Yoga and Ayurveda for managing chronic conditions such as chronic pain, anxiety, and metabolic disorders, a critical gap remains in understanding how individualized practices—tailored to biomechanical, physiological, and dosha-based profiles—elicit measurable therapeutic outcomes. Current studies often rely on generalized protocols, neglecting the dynamic interplay between posture sequences, breathwork, and individual anatomical or metabolic variability. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining biomechanical modeling, multi-omics data integration, and machine learning to simulate and predict personalized Yoga Therapy outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale simulations of musculoskeletal stress distributions during complex asana sequences, optimized via finite element analysis, while parallelized workflows will process genomic, metabolomic, and wearable sensor data to identify biomarkers linked to therapeutic efficacy. Neural networks trained on clinical datasets will map interactions between Ayurvedic dosha assessments, practice modifications, and patient-reported outcomes, enabling probabilistic recommendations for condition-specific protocols. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for designing adaptive Yoga Therapy regimens, validated through partnerships with clinical Yoga therapists. This work will establish a novel paradigm for precision mind-body interventions, bridging ancient practices with computational biomedicine. By quantifying the mechanistic basis of Yoga’s therapeutic effects, the project aims to elevate its clinical credibility, inform accreditation standards, and expand access to personalized, data-driven holistic care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of interactions between atmospheric chemistry and climate dynamics, with a focus on improving the representation of aerosols and trace gases in regional and global climate models. Despite their critical role in radiative forcing and cloud formation, uncertainties persist in modeling the lifecycle, spatial distribution, and reactivity of short-lived climate forcers such as secondary organic aerosols (SOAs) and reactive nitrogen compounds. These gaps limit the predictive accuracy of climate projections, particularly under evolving emission scenarios. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled study integrating observational datasets with the Community Earth System Model (CESM) and a custom-modified version of the GEOS-Chem atmospheric chemistry model. The computational workflow will resolve fine-scale processes, including aerosol microphysics, heterogeneous chemistry, and bidirectional aerosol-cloud interactions, at unprecedented horizontal resolutions (3–10 km regionally, 25 km globally) over decadal timescales. Key innovations include the assimilation of satellite-derived aerosol optical depth and airborne in situ trace gas measurements to constrain model parameters, as well as machine learning techniques to optimize computationally expensive chemical mechanisms. The project requires access to HPC resources capable of supporting large ensemble simulations, petabyte-scale data storage, and parallelized post-processing workflows. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of feedbacks between anthropogenic emissions, aerosol chemistry, and regional climate variability in critical zones such as the Arctic and tropical marine boundary layers; (2) improved parameterizations of aerosol aging and wet deposition processes for next-generation Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) models; and (3) publicly accessible datasets linking emission pathways to aerosol radiative forcing uncertainties. By elucidating chemistry-climate couplings at process-resolving scales, this work will directly inform mitigation strategies and advance predictive capabilities for climate extremes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of atmospheric constituents, reactions, measurement techniques, and processes in predictive, current, and historical contexts. Includes instruction in climate modeling, gases and aerosols, trace gases, aqueous phase chemistry, sinks, transport mechanisms, computer measurement, climate variability, paleoclimatology, climate diagnosis, numerical modeling and data analysis, ionization, recombination, photoemission, and plasma chemistry.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and reliable solar energy systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize installation designs, predict system performance, and streamline maintenance protocols. This project seeks to address critical gaps in current solar energy system modeling by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex interactions between photovoltaic (PV) components, environmental variables, and grid integration dynamics. Traditional methods for system design and fault diagnosis often rely on static models or localized datasets, which fail to account for real-time environmental variability, long-term degradation patterns, and the heterogeneous performance of PV arrays under diverse operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) algorithms, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and finite element analysis (FEA). The ML component will train on historical and synthetic datasets—generated via HPC-driven simulations—to predict energy output fluctuations caused by shading, temperature changes, and panel degradation. Concurrently, CFD and FEA simulations will model thermal stress distributions and structural wear in PV modules under extreme weather conditions, enabling proactive maintenance strategies. By scaling these simulations across thousands of scenarios, the HPC environment will allow us to identify optimal installation configurations, validate repair protocols, and develop predictive maintenance tools tailored to regional climatic challenges. The outcomes of this research will directly inform curriculum updates in solar technician training programs, ensuring alignment with data-driven industry practices. Additionally, the open-source models and datasets produced will serve as a foundation for future innovations in solar energy system resilience, reducing downtime and operational costs for residential and commercial installations. This project underscores the critical role of HPC in advancing solar technology education and practice, bridging the gap between theoretical models and real-world system deployment.
cip_title: Solar Energy System Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair solar energy systems. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Industrial electronics systems are critical to modern manufacturing, yet their increasing complexity poses challenges in reliability, efficiency, and predictive maintenance. Traditional analytical methods and small-scale simulations often fail to capture the dynamic interactions within multiphysics environments, such as thermal, electrical, and mechanical stresses in high-power motor drives or automated control systems. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced computational models that address these limitations. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating machine learning (ML) frameworks for real-time anomaly detection in industrial sensor networks, and (2) simulating the long-term performance of power electronics under variable operational conditions using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). The ML component will leverage distributed computing to process terabytes of historical and real-time sensor data, training deep neural networks to predict equipment failures in systems such as variable frequency drives and programmable logic controllers. Concurrently, multiphysics simulations will model thermal dissipation, electromagnetic interference, and material degradation in industrial-grade converters and inverters, requiring parallelized solvers to handle meshes with over 10^6 elements. These simulations will inform design optimizations to extend component lifespans and reduce energy losses. By integrating data-driven and physics-based approaches, the project aims to establish a predictive maintenance pipeline capable of reducing unplanned downtime in manufacturing by an estimated 15–20%. The computational workflows developed will also serve as pedagogical tools for training technicians in simulation-driven diagnostics. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the scale of data and complexity of models, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations. Outcomes will advance industrial electronics by bridging gaps between theoretical models, operational data, and field-level decision-making, directly supporting the program’s mission to prepare technicians for emerging smart manufacturing challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair electrical/electronic equipment used in industry and manufacturing. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Soil health and microbial community dynamics are critical yet poorly understood drivers of agricultural productivity and carbon sequestration in agroecosystems. Current models lack resolution to predict how soil microbiomes interact with physicochemical variables under climate stressors, limiting our ability to design adaptive land management strategies. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to simulate microbial-soil interactions at scale, enabling predictive insights into soil resilience under varying agricultural practices and climate scenarios. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metatranscriptomic) with spatially explicit soil hydrology and biogeochemical models. Agent-based modeling will simulate microbial community responses to nutrient cycling, moisture fluctuations, and crop residue management, while machine learning algorithms will identify key functional traits linked to soil organic matter stabilization. Parallelized workflows will process terabytes of environmental sensor data and genomic sequences to parameterize models across diverse soil types and cropping systems. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable model quantifying microbial contributions to soil carbon dynamics under drought and intensive farming, (2) predictive tools to optimize tillage, irrigation, and cover cropping practices for enhanced soil health, and (3) open-access datasets linking microbial diversity to agroecosystem functionality. By resolving fine-scale microbial processes within whole-soil profiles, this work will advance fundamental understanding of soil biogeochemistry while directly informing precision agriculture strategies. The computational demands of coupling genomic, hydrological, and climate data necessitate HPC resources to achieve the spatial-temporal resolution required for actionable insights. Results will be disseminated through stakeholder partnerships with agricultural extension services, ensuring translational impact on sustainable soil management.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the soil sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize sustainable and ergonomic interior design solutions through advanced simulation and machine learning techniques. The research problem centers on the challenge of balancing aesthetic, functional, and environmental factors in interior spaces, particularly as design complexity grows with evolving demands for energy efficiency, occupant well-being, and adaptive reuse of materials. Current manual and software-assisted workflows struggle to efficiently integrate real-time analysis of multidimensional variables such as thermal comfort, acoustic performance, spatial ergonomics, and material lifecycle impacts. To address this, the project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale parametric modeling, finite element analysis, and generative adversarial networks (GANs). Computational methods will include parallelized simulations of lighting distribution using ray-tracing algorithms, acoustic propagation modeling in complex geometries, and predictive analytics for material wear patterns under varying occupancy scenarios. Machine learning models trained on historical design datasets will propose optimized layouts that minimize resource use while adhering to building codes and accessibility standards. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated design validation, capable of rapidly iterating through thousands of spatially coherent solutions that satisfy competing constraints. This work will advance computational design methodologies in the visual arts by demonstrating how HPC-powered workflows can reduce trial-and-error prototyping cycles, lower carbon footprints through predictive material optimization, and establish quantifiable metrics for occupant comfort in diverse interior typologies. The resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated rendering of high-fidelity virtual environments and distributed processing of sensor data from IoT-equipped prototype spaces, enabling previously infeasible scale in analyzing human-environment interactions. Results will directly inform curriculum development in digital design integration and provide case studies for sustainable commercial retrofitting strategies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to apply artistic principles and techniques to the professional planning, designing, equipping, and furnishing of residential and commercial interior spaces. Includes instruction in computer applications, drafting, and graphic techniques; principles of interior lighting, acoustics, systems integration, and color coordination; furniture and furnishings; textiles and their finishing; the history of interior design and period styles; basic structural design; building codes and inspection regulations; and applications to office, hotel, factory, restaurant and housing design.

abstract: The proposed research addresses the critical challenge of understanding how prolonged exposure to microgravity and radiation during spaceflight drives physiological deconditioning in astronauts, particularly focusing on musculoskeletal atrophy, cardiovascular dysfunction, and cancer risk modulation. While prior studies have characterized systemic responses to space environments, the integrative mechanisms linking cellular hypoxia, fluid redistribution, and radiation-induced genomic instability remain poorly quantified. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale physiological models that bridge molecular, tissue, and organ-level adaptations. A three-tiered computational framework will be implemented: (1) Finite element modeling of hemodynamic shifts and cerebrovascular autoregulation in simulated microgravity, informed by astronaut cardiovascular telemetry; (2) Agent-based simulations of muscle fiber remodeling under chronic mechanical unloading, integrating proteomic data on myokine signaling pathways; and (3) Monte Carlo simulations of cosmic radiation interactions with bone marrow microenvironments to assess leukemogenic potential. The HPC environment is essential for resolving spatiotemporal complexities across these scales, requiring parallelized execution of coupled differential equations modeling pressure-volume dynamics (10⁶-node vascular networks) and stochastic radiation damage events (10¹²-particle histories). Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for early detection of spaceflight-induced pathologies and optimized countermeasure protocols targeting mechanotransduction pathways. By elucidating cross-system vulnerabilities in aerospace physiology, this work will directly inform NASA’s Artemis program crew health standards and advance terrestrial oncology research through novel insights into hypoxia-mediated cancer progression. The requested computational allocation will enable unprecedented resolution in simulating human physiological resilience at the intersection of gravitational biology and environmental carcinogenesis.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the physiological processes involved in low and high-altitude flight and living in space and related low-pressure and low-gravity environments, including sensorimotor interactions, response mechanisms, and the effects of injury, disease, and disability. Includes instruction in anatomy, molecular and cellular basis of muscle contraction, fuel utilization, neurophysiology of motor mechanics, systemic physiological responses (respiration, blood flow, endocrine secretions, and others), fatigue and exhaustion, systemic environmental pathologies, muscle and body training, physiology of specific exercises and activities, physiology of injury, and the effects of disabilities and disease.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dramatic performance dynamics through large-scale simulation and analysis of theatrical interactions. The central research problem lies in understanding how complex variables—such as actor positioning, vocal modulation, audience sightlines, and real-time emotional feedback—collectively influence the efficacy of live performances. Traditional methods of analyzing these dynamics rely on manual observation, limited-scale experiments, or post-hoc surveys, which struggle to capture the multivariate, nonlinear relationships inherent in theatrical spaces. To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates agent-based modeling, real-time motion capture datasets, and machine learning to simulate audience-performer interactions within virtualized theater environments. Using HPC resources, we will model diverse performance scenarios across historical and contemporary theater architectures (e.g., proscenium, thrust, arena stages) and populate them with AI-driven audience agents trained on behavioral datasets from prior productions. The simulations will quantify how adjustments to blocking, acoustics, or lighting affect collective audience engagement metrics, derived from gaze-tracking and physiological response proxies. Additionally, NLP-driven analysis of dramatic texts will correlate linguistic patterns with optimal emotional pacing in simulated performances. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for directors and dramaturgs to pre-visualize production choices, a repository of performance optimization strategies tied to specific theatrical forms, and new insights into the relationship between spatial design and narrative impact. By bridging computational methods with performance theory, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-informed theatrical practice while preserving the artistic integrity of live drama. The project’s scale—requiring parallel processing of high-fidelity simulations across thousands of agent interactions—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve timely results and enable iterative, hypothesis-driven experimentation.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Drama and Dramatics/ Theatre Arts, General
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of dramatic works and their performance. Includes instruction in major works of dramatic literature, dramatic styles and types, and the principles of organizing and producing full live or filmed productions.

abstract: Periodontal diseases, including gingivitis and periodontitis, represent a major global health burden with complex etiologies involving microbial, immune, and genetic interactions. Current clinical approaches to diagnosis, risk stratification, and implant integration lack precision due to incomplete understanding of these multifactorial dynamics. This project proposes to develop multiscale computational models to unravel the systems-level mechanisms driving periodontal disease progression and implant failure. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to simulate microbial biofilm-host immune interactions at cellular resolution, model biomechanical stress distributions in peri-implant bone under diverse occlusal loads, and analyze multi-omics datasets from longitudinal patient cohorts. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling of polymicrobial communities, finite element analysis of bone-implant interfaces, and machine learning integration of genomic, proteomic, and clinical data. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated architectures to achieve biologically relevant timescales for biofilm development and immune response cascades. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk biofilm compositions, optimized implant design parameters to minimize microfracture risk, and machine learning classifiers for early detection of progressive bone loss. These results will advance personalized treatment strategies and inform next-generation implant materials. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source tools for the dental research community. By bridging clinical observations with mechanistic simulations, this work addresses critical gaps in translating basic periodontal research into precision clinical interventions, with potential to improve long-term outcomes for 500 million patients affected by severe periodontitis worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement and maintenance of dental implants.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven simulation framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, multi-stakeholder construction projects, with a focus on mitigating cascading delays caused by supply chain volatility and workforce availability constraints. Traditional construction scheduling tools often rely on static critical path methods, which inadequately address real-time disruptions in complex, interdependent workflows. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning (RL) to create adaptive resource allocation strategies that account for stochastic material delivery delays, labor productivity variations, and equipment downtime patterns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training deep RL agents on historical project data while simultaneously simulating thousands of concurrent construction process interactions across temporal and spatial dimensions. The framework will incorporate domain-specific constraints from construction contracts, safety regulations, and environmental compliance requirements through hybrid neural network architectures. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting resource bottlenecks 72-96 hours in advance and generating prioritized reallocation strategies that minimize project-wide schedule impacts. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of three completed megaprojects (valued >$500M) and real-time testing on active hospital construction sites. This research advances computational construction management by bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and machine learning, with potential applications in disaster recovery logistics and infrastructure resilience planning. The HPC component enables exploration of emergent project behaviors at unprecedented scale, providing foundational insights into complex adaptive systems within built environment delivery.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage, coordinate, and supervise the construction process. Includes instruction in commercial, residential, mechanical, highway/heavy civil, electrical, environmental, industrial, and specialty construction; facilities management; budgeting and cost control; logistics and materials management; organization and scheduling; personnel management and labor relations; site safety; construction contracting; construction processes and techniques; and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: Pediatric hematologic malignancies, such as leukemia and lymphoma, present unique clinical challenges due to their complex molecular heterogeneity and variable treatment responses. While advances in genomic profiling have identified recurrent mutations, the functional impact of these alterations on disease progression and therapeutic resistance remains poorly characterized in pediatric populations. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omics data with computational models to identify high-risk molecular subtypes and predict optimal therapeutic strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic datasets from pediatric patients enrolled in international consortia, including the Children’s Oncology Group. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to delineate clonal evolution patterns during treatment and correlate these dynamics with clinical outcomes. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will model the structural consequences of recurrent mutations in key oncoproteins, enabling virtual screening of small-molecule inhibitors tailored to pediatric-specific variants. A pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic framework will further optimize dosing regimens for identified compounds using population-based modeling. The computational workflow will require parallel processing capabilities to manage terabytes of sequencing data, iterative model training, and large-scale in silico drug screens. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, predictive biomarkers for treatment resistance, and personalized dosing recommendations to minimize toxicity. By elucidating the molecular drivers of therapeutic failure in pediatric hematologic cancers, this work aims to directly inform the design of upcoming clinical trials and improve survival rates for high-risk patients. The scale and complexity of these analyses necessitate robust HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically actionable insights within a translational research timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Hematology-Oncology

abstract: Epilepsy is a complex neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, affecting over 50 million individuals globally. Despite advances in diagnostic tools and therapies, approximately 30% of patients remain drug-resistant, and the underlying mechanisms of seizure generation and propagation remain poorly understood. Current clinical methods, such as electroencephalography (EEG) and neuroimaging, generate high-dimensional data that are challenging to analyze comprehensively using conventional computational resources. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for improving the diagnosis, classification, and personalized treatment of epilepsy. The research will focus on integrating multimodal neuroimaging, electrophysiological data, and genetic information to identify biomarkers of epileptogenesis, predict treatment responses, and simulate seizure dynamics. A key component involves machine learning algorithms to detect subtle patterns in long-term EEG recordings and structural MRI data that correlate with seizure onset zones and network abnormalities. Additionally, we will employ computational neuroscience techniques to model large-scale neural networks, simulating how genetic mutations or structural lesions alter network excitability and synchronization. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and transcriptomic analyses will be conducted to explore genetic risk factors and their interactions with neuroimaging phenotypes. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the scale and complexity of these datasets, enabling parallel processing of terabytes of neuroimaging data, real-time analysis of continuous EEG streams, and iterative optimization of predictive models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early diagnosis, stratification of patients into subphenotypes based on computational profiles, and in silico testing of antiepileptic drug effects on simulated neural networks. This work has the potential to transform clinical practice by providing tools for precision medicine in epilepsy, reducing diagnostic delays, and guiding targeted therapeutic interventions. By elucidating the multiscale mechanisms of epileptogenesis, the project will contribute to foundational knowledge that informs future research and therapeutic innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of patients with epileptic seizures or with symptoms and signs whose differential diagnosis includes epileptic seizures.

abstract: Effective communication of agricultural research and practices is critical for bridging the gap between scientific advancements and their practical application by farmers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders. However, the dynamic nature of agricultural systems, combined with diverse audience needs and rapidly evolving digital platforms, poses challenges in tailoring communication strategies for optimal engagement and comprehension. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the efficacy of agricultural communication strategies at scale. Using computational methods, we will process large datasets—including agricultural research publications, social media content, multimedia campaigns, and audience analytics—to identify patterns in information dissemination and reception. Natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques will be applied to evaluate how technical agricultural content is framed, translated, and consumed across different demographics and media formats. Agent-based modeling will simulate information diffusion networks to assess how variables such as message timing, platform choice, and visual storytelling impact audience behavior and knowledge retention. Additionally, predictive analytics will forecast emerging topics in agricultural sciences (e.g., climate-resilient crops, precision livestock farming) to proactively design communication frameworks. The computational demands of processing multimodal data (text, video, geospatial) and running iterative simulations necessitate HPC infrastructure. Outcomes will include actionable insights for creating adaptive, audience-specific communication tools and a publicly accessible repository of optimized content templates. This work will enhance the capacity of agricultural journalists and communicators to deliver scientifically accurate, contextually relevant information, ultimately supporting informed decision-making in farming communities and strengthening public understanding of agricultural innovation.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply journalistic, communication, and broadcasting principles to the development, production, and transmittal of agricultural information. Includes instruction in basic journalism, broadcasting, film/video, and communication techniques; the production of technically specialized information products for agricultural audiences; and the principles of agricultural sciences and business operations needed to develop and communicate agricultural subject matter in effective ways.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern industrial and operational systems demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimization, uncertainty quantification, and real-time decision-making. This project seeks to develop a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model and optimize large-scale systems with interdependent human, logistical, and informational components. A central focus is the integration of stochastic optimization and discrete-event simulation to address resource allocation problems in dynamic environments, such as manufacturing process flows or distributed supply chains, where traditional analytical methods fail to account for high-dimensional decision spaces and time-varying constraints. The research will employ parallelized mixed-integer programming solvers and agent-based simulation techniques to evaluate system performance under probabilistic disruptions, including demand variability and resource intermittency. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate scenario evaluation, enabling rapid trade-off analyses between cost, resilience, and sustainability metrics. Key deliverables include an open-source toolkit for systems-level resource allocation, validated through case studies on multi-echelon inventory networks and service facility scheduling. The computational demands of this work—particularly the need to solve stochastic optimization models with millions of variables and simulate heterogeneous agent interactions at scale—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed-memory architectures. Expected outcomes include quantifiable strategies for balancing capital expenditure and operational flexibility in industrial systems, as well as methodological advances in decomposing complex systems engineering problems into computationally tractable submodels. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to bridge gaps between theoretical systems engineering principles and practical implementations in sectors requiring robust, adaptive resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems solutions to a wide variety of engineering problems, including the integration of human, physical, energy, communications, management, and information requirements as needed, and the application of requisite analytical methods to specific situations.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing adaptive security protocols in dynamic, large-scale urban environments, where traditional static security measures often fail to address evolving threats. The core challenge lies in integrating real-time behavioral data, environmental variables, and threat prediction models to enable responsive security systems capable of adjusting to unpredictable scenarios. Current approaches lack the granularity to model complex human-environment interactions at city-wide scales, particularly under conditions of partial observability or rapidly shifting risks. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and reinforcement learning (RL) approach, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate millions of agent decisions across multi-layered urban networks. The computational model will incorporate anonymized mobility patterns, infrastructure interdependencies, and stochastic threat generators to test resilience against cascading security failures. Key technical innovations include the development of a graph neural network architecture to predict emergent crowd behaviors and a parallelized optimization engine for evaluating countermeasure efficacy across simulated scenarios. By coupling these components through distributed computing workflows, the framework aims to identify latent vulnerabilities in existing security configurations while proposing dynamic resource allocation strategies. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible benchmark dataset of simulated threat-response scenarios and open-source tools for adaptive security planning. This work bridges computational social dynamics with security operations, offering a novel paradigm for proactive risk mitigation in complex human-centric systems. The requested HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and temporal resolution in simulations, enabling validation against real-world incident datasets from partner security agencies.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the general application of science and technology to security.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance ethical decision-making frameworks in healthcare through large-scale computational modeling and analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in bioethics: the lack of empirically grounded, dynamic models to evaluate how ethical principles—such as autonomy, justice, and beneficence—interact with real-world variables like resource constraints, cultural diversity, and institutional policies. Current methodologies often rely on static case analyses or qualitative assessments, limiting their ability to predict outcomes in complex, evolving scenarios such as triage during public health emergencies, equitable organ allocation, or AI-driven clinical tools. To address this, the project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating interactions among patients, providers, and policymakers under varying ethical priorities and resource conditions. These models will integrate datasets from clinical trials, public health records, and sociological surveys to parameterize agents’ decision-making behaviors. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) techniques will be applied to analyze historical ethical guidelines, case law, and institutional policies, identifying patterns and biases in ethical reasoning. Machine learning algorithms will further assess how demographic, socioeconomic, and cultural factors influence perceptions of ethical care. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the parallel processing required for Monte Carlo simulations exploring thousands of scenario permutations—necessitates HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to quantify trade-offs in policy decisions, a repository of scenario-based ethical “stress tests” for healthcare systems, and evidence-based frameworks to guide resource allocation in crises. By bridging computational scalability with normative analysis, this work aims to enhance the rigor, equity, and adaptability of bioethics in practice, offering stakeholders actionable insights for policy design and clinical training.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of ethics, religion, jurisprudence, and the social sciences to the analysis of health care issues, clinical decision making, and research procedures. Includes instruction in philosophical ethics, moral value, medical sociology, theology, spirituality and health, policy analysis, decision theory, and applications to problems such as death and dying, therapeutic relationships, organ transplantation, human and animal subjects, reproduction and fertility, health care justice, cultural sensitivity, needs assessment, professionalism, conflict of interest, chaplaincy, and clinical or emergency procedures.

abstract: The study of host-pathogen interactions is critical for understanding immune evasion mechanisms and developing targeted therapies. Many pathogens, such as influenza viruses and antibiotic-resistant bacteria, rapidly mutate surface proteins to avoid antibody recognition. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the dynamic structural changes underlying these interactions at atomic resolution. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of pathogen-antibody complexes, focusing on viral envelope glycoproteins and bacterial surface antigens. These simulations will model conformational dynamics over microsecond timescales, identifying critical residues involved in binding and immune escape. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will analyze evolutionary conservation patterns across pathogen genomes to predict stable epitopes less prone to mutation. The integration of simulation data with mutagenesis and neutralization assays will validate computational predictions and refine models of antigenic variability. By elucidating structural determinants of immune evasion, this research aims to identify conserved therapeutic targets and inform the design of broad-spectrum vaccines. The proposed computational workflows require extensive parallel processing and GPU acceleration, necessitating HPC infrastructure to manage the terabytes of trajectory data and complex analyses. Outcomes will advance fundamental knowledge in microbial pathogenesis and adaptive immunity while providing a framework for computationally driven vaccine development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microorganisms that cause disease and the host immune response to them. Includes instruction in microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, pathogenic bacteriology, disease mechanisms, immunology, immunogenetics, autoimmunity, and bioinformatics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and simulate emergent behavioral dynamics in heterogeneous populations during homeland security crises, with a focus on scenarios involving disinformation propagation and decentralized threat coordination. Current models often oversimplify socio-cultural variables or lack granularity to address the interplay between digital communication networks and real-world collective behavior, limiting their utility for proactive threat mitigation. The research will integrate agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and multilayer network analysis to capture how ideologically fragmented groups adapt to security interventions in digitally mediated environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing large-scale simulations that incorporate 1) real-time social media data streams, 2) cognitive bias parameters derived from experimental psychology studies, and 3) geospatial constraints on physical mobilization patterns. The computational architecture will leverage GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to analyze cross-platform information cascades alongside reinforcement learning agents that simulate adversarial adaptation strategies. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit to identify tipping points in crisis escalation trajectories and evaluate the resilience of communication protocols used by emergency responders. By bridging computational social science with security informatics, this work aims to advance decision-support systems for managing hybrid threats that exploit the sociotechnical vulnerabilities of modern interconnected societies. The resulting models will be validated against historical case studies of coordinated disruption campaigns and stress-tested through scenario-based war-gaming exercises with homeland security stakeholders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in homeland security, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing complex, large-scale transactional datasets in forensic accounting, with a focus on identifying latent patterns indicative of systemic financial manipulation. Traditional forensic accounting methods struggle to efficiently process the growing volume and intricacy of modern financial data, particularly when investigating cross-jurisdictional transactions or opaque supply chains. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in graph-based anomaly detection, where existing algorithms fail to scale effectively for real-time analysis of multi-terabyte datasets spanning millions of entities. The proposed solution combines distributed graph neural networks with novel edge-weighting techniques optimized for accounting semantics, implemented through a high-performance computing (HPC) pipeline. This approach will leverage parallelized graph processing frameworks to model transactional networks at unprecedented scale, incorporating temporal, contextual, and regulatory constraint parameters specific to forensic accounting scenarios. The computational methodology will be validated against both synthetic datasets simulating complex fraud patterns and anonymized real-world case data from international financial institutions. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for forensic accounting professionals to detect emergent forms of financial obfuscation, 2) quantitative benchmarks for HPC resource allocation in accounting investigations, and 3) new metrics for assessing transaction network resilience against manipulation. By bridging computational scalability gaps in accounting forensics, this research aims to establish best practices for applying HPC resources to regulatory compliance challenges at the intersection of distributed ledger technologies, global trade systems, and evolving financial crime methodologies. The project’s interdisciplinary approach—combining accounting theory, graph data science, and high-performance computing—addresses critical gaps in detecting sophisticated financial malfeasance while advancing computational methods for domain-specific resource optimization.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the atomic-scale mechanisms governing ion transport and interfacial stability in next-generation solid-state electrolytes for energy storage applications. Solid-state batteries promise transformative improvements in energy density and safety compared to conventional liquid electrolyte systems.
