However, their practical deployment is hindered by poorly understood limitations, including sluggish ion mobility across heterogeneous interfaces and mechanical degradation during cycling. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve the dynamic, nanoscale processes underlying these phenomena. We propose a multiscale computational framework combining density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and machine learning-accelerated potential models to systematically evaluate ion diffusion kinetics, phase stability, and defect interactions in lithium- and sodium-based solid electrolytes. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to realistic system sizes (>100,000 atoms) and timescales (microseconds), enabling direct comparison with operando characterization data. Key objectives include mapping cation transport pathways under mechanical strain, quantifying the role of grain boundary chemistry on interfacial resistance, and predicting thermodynamically stable electrode-electrolyte combinations. The computational workflow will utilize GPU-optimized codes (VASP, LAMMPS) and custom analysis pipelines to process terabytes of trajectory data, extracting descriptors for microstructure-property relationships. Expected outcomes include predictive models for electrolyte performance under operational stressors and design rules for interface engineering. By bridging atomic-scale insights with mesoscale microstructural evolution, this work aims to accelerate the development of durable, high-conductivity solid electrolytes, directly supporting national priorities in sustainable energy infrastructure. The requested resources will enable 15M core-hours for ensemble simulations across multiple material systems, with dedicated GPU nodes for training neural network potentials on quantum-mechanical datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general application of mathematical and scientific principles to the analysis and evaluation of the characteristics and behavior of solids, including internal structure, chemical properties, transport and energy flow properties, thermodynamics of solids, stress and failure factors, chemical transformation states and processes, compound materials, and research on industrial applications of specific materials.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for modeling the co-evolution of ecological information networks and human decision-making processes in resource-limited environments. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized, adaptive information systems—such as those used in community-based environmental monitoring—interact with human behavioral dynamics under shifting ecological constraints. Current models often treat information flow and human behavior as isolated phenomena, neglecting their bidirectional feedback loops. To bridge this gap, we propose an agent-based simulation platform integrating three computational components: (1) dynamic network models capturing real-time information exchange across heterogeneous nodes (e.g., sensors, human actors, and institutional databases); (2) cognitive architectures simulating decision-making under incomplete information; and (3) ecological disturbance models generating stochastic environmental pressures. The framework will leverage graph neural networks to handle evolving network topologies and reinforcement learning to model adaptive behaviors, requiring high-performance computing resources for parameter space exploration and sensitivity analyses across multi-timescale simulations. Initial pilot studies on wildfire response coordination data demonstrate non-linear phase transitions in information utility that existing linear models cannot capture. The proposed HPC implementation will scale these analyses to continental-level ecosystem datasets while maintaining millisecond-resolution temporal fidelity. Expected outcomes include novel metrics for quantifying resilience in socio-environmental information systems and actionable insights for designing decentralized monitoring infrastructures in climate-vulnerable regions. This work advances computational foundations for studying complex adaptive systems at the human-environment interface, with potential applications in disaster response optimization, participatory conservation planning, and climate adaptation policy design.
cip_title: Computer and Information Sciences and Support Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer and information sciences and support services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in personalized patient care planning and real-time clinical decision support for registered nurses (RNs) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex, multidimensional health data. Despite advancements in electronic health records (EHRs) and wearable monitoring devices, nursing workflows often lack computational tools to dynamically integrate patient-specific data—such as vital signs, medication adherence, psychosocial factors, and longitudinal health trends—into actionable care plans. This limitation contributes to delayed interventions, suboptimal resource allocation, and preventable adverse events. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a machine learning (ML) framework optimized for HPC environments to process terabyte-scale EHR datasets and sensor-derived streams. The framework will employ ensemble models combining recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for temporal pattern detection, graph neural networks (GNNs) to map inter-patient contagion risks in hospital units, and natural language processing (NLP) to extract insights from nursing notes. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in predicted patient trajectories under varying staffing and intervention scenarios. By integrating these components into a dashboard prototype, the system will provide RNs with real-time risk stratification and prioritized care recommendations. Computational demands necessitate HPC resources due to the scale of federated EHR datasets (>500,000 patient records across six hospitals), the need for hyperparameter optimization across competing models, and latency-critical inference during simulated clinical workflows. Expected outcomes include validated predictive algorithms for sepsis progression, fall risk, and medication complication alerts, alongside open-source tools for nursing informatics. This work aims to establish a computational foundation for data-driven nursing science, directly supporting the quadruple aim of enhancing patient outcomes, improving care team efficiency, reducing costs, and promoting clinician well-being.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals in the knowledge, techniques and procedures for promoting health, providing care for sick, disabled, infirmed, or other individuals or groups. Includes instruction in the administration of medication and treatments, assisting a physician during treatments and examinations, Referring patients to physicians and other health care specialists, and planning education for health maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of dance as a dynamic cultural and biomechanical phenomenon through computational analysis of movement patterns and choreographic structures. While dance has historically been examined through qualitative frameworks, the growing availability of motion-capture data and digitized Labanotation archives presents an opportunity to quantitatively analyze large-scale movement datasets. However, processing these datasets—spanning diverse dance traditions, temporal scales, and cultural contexts—requires significant computational power beyond the capacity of standard workstations. The research problem centers on identifying cross-cultural movement signatures and choreographic evolution patterns, which are obscured in smaller datasets or manual analysis. Using motion-capture data from global dance archives and Labanotation transcriptions, the project will apply machine learning algorithms to classify movement sequences, simulate kinematic variations, and model choreographic decision-making processes. Computational methods will include time-series analysis of joint kinematics, graph-based representations of choreographic networks, and probabilistic modeling of improvisational structures in jazz and contemporary dance. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC nodes, the team aims to process over 10,000 hours of annotated dance data, enabling comparative studies of biomechanical efficiency in classical ballet versus folk traditions, as well as the cultural transmission of gestural motifs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of computationally tagged movement elements, tools for automated Labanotation generation, and new theoretical frameworks linking choreographic complexity to cultural narratives. This work will provide dance scholars with unprecedented scalability in analyzing movement as data, while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations between performing arts and computational sciences. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive simulations and training deep learning models on heterogeneous movement corpora, tasks that are infeasible without distributed computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to express ideas, feelings, and/or inner visions through the performance of one or more of the dance disciplines, including but not limited to ballet, modern, jazz, ethnic, and folk dance, and that focuses on the study and analysis of dance as a cultural phenomenon. Includes instruction in technique, choreography, Laban notation, dance history and criticism, and dance production.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize dispute resolution strategies across complex, multi-party scenarios, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome limitations of traditional analytical methods. Dispute resolution processes in settings such as labor negotiations, international diplomacy, or corporate mergers involve dynamic interactions among stakeholders with competing priorities, cultural differences, and asymmetric information. Existing theoretical models often fail to capture the nonlinear feedback loops, behavioral biases, and context-dependent decision-making inherent in these systems. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), game-theoretic simulations, and natural language processing (NLP). The ABM component will simulate thousands of negotiation trajectories using empirically derived behavioral profiles, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize mediation strategies under varying constraints. NLP tools will analyze historical arbitration transcripts and treaty documents to identify linguistic patterns correlated with successful outcomes, informing model parameters. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to realistic participant numbers (50+ agents per scenario), parallelizing scenario testing, and processing large textual datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of simulated dispute resolution benchmarks, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting negotiation breakdown risks, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for adaptive mediation protocols. By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution theory, this work aims to provide practitioners with data-driven tools to de-escalate high-stakes disputes while advancing methodological innovation in multidisciplinary computational humanities research. The project’s scale—encompassing 10,000+ simulation hours and terabyte-scale text analysis—necessitates cluster computing infrastructure with GPU acceleration and distributed memory capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational documentation and analysis of understudied Indigenous languages of the Pacific region, with a focus on Papuan and Polynesian language families. Despite their cultural significance, many languages in these groups remain under-resourced in digital corpora, hindering both preservation efforts and comparative linguistic research. The primary challenge lies in processing large, heterogeneous datasets—including legacy audio recordings, transcribed texts, and field notes—while accounting for complex morphosyntactic structures and dialectal variations. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop scalable pipelines for automated speech recognition (ASR), morphological parsing, and cross-linguistic alignment. Computational workflows will integrate transformer-based models fine-tuned on existing Pacific language corpora, phylogenetic algorithms for reconstructing proto-language features, and GPU-accelerated batch processing of audio data. Key innovations include adapting low-resource NLP techniques to Oceanic languages’ agglutinative morphology and developing probabilistic models to infer semantic relationships in oral narratives. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-access repository of computationally enhanced linguistic resources for 10+ endangered languages, 2) novel insights into contact phenomena between Papuan and Austronesian languages in Melanesia, and 3) community-facing tools for language revitalization, such as interactive dictionaries and pedagogical applications. The scale of data—anticipated at 50TB of audio-text pairs and 1M+ annotated lexical entries—necessitates distributed storage and parallelized computation unavailable on local infrastructure. By bridging computational linguistics with Pacific language scholarship, this project aims to advance both methodological frameworks for linguistic analysis and equitable access to digital preservation technologies for Indigenous communities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Australian/ Oceanic/ Pacific Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the languages native to Papua/New Guinea, Australia, New Zealand, and the island groups of the Pacific Ocean, including, but not limited to, the Papuan languages, the Australian languages, the Micronesian languages, and the Polynesian languages. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Pediatric cardiovascular diseases present unique challenges due to the heterogeneity of congenital and acquired conditions, dynamic developmental physiology, and limited datasets for modeling. This project seeks to develop patient-specific computational models of cardiopulmonary hemodynamics in children with complex congenital heart defects (CHDs), such as single-ventricle physiology and tetralogy of Fallot, to optimize surgical planning and predict long-term outcomes. A critical barrier is the integration of multi-scale, multi-modal clinical data—including 4D flow MRI, echocardiography, and catheterization-derived pressures—into predictive frameworks that account for growth-related changes and postoperative remodeling. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations coupling finite element analysis of myocardial mechanics with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of blood flow. These simulations will be informed by machine learning algorithms trained on retrospective clinical data to parameterize boundary conditions and validate against longitudinal outcomes. The computational pipeline will also incorporate uncertainty quantification to assess model robustness across anatomic and physiologic variability. By scaling these analyses across a cohort of 200+ patients via parallelized workflows, we aim to identify hemodynamic risk factors for adverse events (e.g., ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias) and simulate virtual surgical interventions to guide personalized approaches. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the computational burden of 3D transient simulations, which require ~10^6 core-hours annually for meshing, solver iterations, and sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for clinical decision support, open-source tools for pediatric cardiovascular modeling, and foundational data for future studies on developmental cardiology. This work bridges gaps between clinical observation and mechanistic understanding, with potential to reduce invasive testing and improve quality of life for children with CHDs.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases and disorders of the cardiovascular and cardiopulmonary systems of infants, children, and adolescents. May include related research in public health and community medicine issues.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of identity formation and resistance within digital spaces used by marginalized cultural and gender groups, with a focus on multilingual, non-Western online communities. Despite growing scholarship on digital activism, there remains a critical gap in large-scale, intersectional analyses of how marginalized groups negotiate systemic inequities and co-create counter-narratives across linguistic and cultural boundaries. The research will employ computational text analysis and network science methods to process terabytes of social media data, including non-Latin script texts from platforms popular in Global South contexts. Key computational challenges include implementing transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, conducting multilevel network analysis of cross-community solidarity patterns, and running agent-based simulations of discourse diffusion under different moderation policies. These tasks require high-performance computing resources due to the scale of data (estimated 10^7 posts across 15 languages), need for parallel processing of multimodal content, and complexity of simulating intersectional identity interactions in evolving digital ecosystems. Expected outcomes include 1) new computational frameworks for analyzing power asymmetries in multilingual digital spaces, 2) identification of cross-cultural patterns in community-led resistance strategies, and 3) open-source tools for ethically monitoring platform governance impacts on marginalized users. By leveraging GPU-accelerated natural language processing and distributed computing for large graph analyses, this work aims to advance both computational social science methodologies and substantive theories of digital cultural resilience. The resource request supports critical infrastructure for handling sensitive data through secure, on-premise clusters while maintaining community partnership protocols essential for decolonial computing approaches in cultural studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Ethnic, Cultural Minority, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ethnic, cultural minority, gender, and group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Slavic linguistic diversity, particularly focusing on understudied dialects and historical language shifts. Slavic languages exhibit complex morphological structures and dialectal variation that challenge traditional linguistic models, yet large-scale quantitative studies remain scarce due to computational limitations. The research problem centers on modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical changes across Eastern Slavic dialects (e.g., Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Russian regional varieties) and their contact zones with West Slavic languages. The computational approach integrates corpus linguistics, machine learning, and phylogenetic methods to analyze digitized historical texts, contemporary speech corpora, and dialectal archives. Neural networks will be trained to detect patterns in sound shifts and morphosyntactic variation, while Bayesian phylogenetic models will reconstruct divergence timelines. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured text/audio data, optimizing transformer-based models for low-resource languages, and running parallelized simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database of annotated dialect features, (2) dynamic visualizations of language change trajectories, and (3) methodological frameworks for computational dialectology applicable to other Slavic subgroups. By enabling rigorous analysis of non-standardized language varieties, this work will advance preservation efforts for endangered dialects and inform theoretical debates about Slavic language classification. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support scalability in training domain-specific NLP tools, which currently lack robustness for Slavic linguistic contexts beyond major standardized languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are critical for global carbon sequestration, biodiversity, and sustainable resource provision, yet optimizing their management under climate uncertainty remains a complex, data-intensive challenge. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model forest growth dynamics, harvest scheduling, and ecological trade-offs across heterogeneous landscapes. The research addresses two core gaps: (1) limited integration of spatially explicit climate projections, species-specific growth patterns, and economic constraints in existing forest management tools, and (2) the computational infeasibility of running multi-decadal simulations at fine spatial scales (<1 km² resolution) using conventional methods. We propose a hybrid machine learning and process-based modeling approach, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to parallelize simulations across 10,000+ landscape units while incorporating real-time LiDAR data assimilation. Key computational components include a deep neural network trained on historical growth data from 50+ forest stands, an agent-based model for harvesting equipment interactions, and a Monte Carlo framework to evaluate climate scenarios from CMIP6 datasets. The HPC resources will enable parameter optimization across 15+ tree species, simultaneous evaluation of 200+ management strategies, and uncertainty quantification through 10,000+ ensemble runs. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that identifies harvest schedules maximizing timber yield while maintaining 90% of baseline carbon storage capacity, alongside species transplantation guidelines to enhance climate resilience. By scaling analyses to entire watersheds rather than individual stands, this work will provide forestry managers with actionable insights into landscape-level resource allocation, particularly in mixed-use regions where agroforestry interfaces with industrial timber production. The computational framework will be开源ly released to support adaptive management across boreal and temperate forests globally.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of forestry principles to the production, harvesting, and processing of forest resources and that prepares individuals to perform associated technical and managerial functions. Includes instruction in forest production and utilization, industrial forestry, agroforestry, transplantation, timber harvesting, selection and identification of trees, processing technologies and systems, equipment operations and maintenance, and related management skills.

abstract: Aerospace medicine faces critical challenges in understanding and mitigating the health risks posed by extreme physiological and psychological stressors in air and space environments. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to predict and address these risks, with a focus on optimizing medical protocols for crew health during long-duration missions. The primary research problem involves the dynamic interplay of microgravity, rapid pressure changes, and high-G forces on human physiology, particularly their cumulative effects on cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, and neurovestibular systems. Current clinical datasets lack resolution to capture real-time adaptive responses during critical mission phases, necessitating advanced simulation approaches. The proposed work will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement multi-scale biomechanical models integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for cerebral and cardiovascular responses, finite element analysis (FEA) for bone density loss under microgravity, and machine learning algorithms trained on astronaut biometric datasets. These models will simulate emergency scenarios such as rapid decompression events and sustained hypergravity during re-entry, predicting physiological thresholds for medical intervention. A parallel computational framework will evaluate the efficacy of artificial gravity countermeasures and pharmacological protocols through in silico clinical trials. The anticipated outcomes include predictive analytics tools for decompression sickness risk stratification, optimized exercise regimens for muscle atrophy prevention, and adaptive medical decision-support systems for deep-space missions. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process terabytes of multimodal physiological data from existing spaceflight studies, this research aims to establish evidence-based standards for aerospace medical operations while reducing reliance on Earth-based analog experiments. The computational infrastructure will enable near real-time simulation of crewed mission profiles, significantly advancing the field's capacity to safeguard human health in next-generation space exploration initiatives.
cip_definition: Research focused on the health care of operating crews, support personnel, and passengers of air and space vehicles. Includes instruction in special conditions of physical and psychological stress, emergency medical procedures, adaptive systems and artificial environments. One of three general certificates in the area of preventive medicine.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze the complex dynamics of intergenerational resource allocation within families, a critical yet underexplored area in Work and Family Studies. While traditional research in this field relies on qualitative surveys or small-scale quantitative studies, the proposed work addresses a gap in scalable, data-driven simulations of how families navigate competing demands—such as childcare, eldercare, financial planning, and time management—under varying socioeconomic conditions. The research problem centers on understanding how systemic stressors (e.g., inflation, healthcare access disparities) disrupt decision-making patterns in households, particularly in marginalized communities where resource constraints amplify trade-offs. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate household behavior across diverse demographic profiles, integrating real-world datasets on income, health outcomes, and policy landscapes. Computational workflows will parallelize thousands of scenario iterations to capture nonlinear interactions between individual choices, institutional policies, and macroeconomic trends. Machine learning techniques will then identify emergent patterns in caregiving strategies and resilience mechanisms. By quantifying the cascading effects of policy interventions (e.g., subsidized childcare, flexible work mandates) on family well-being, this research aims to generate actionable frameworks for policymakers and educators. The use of HPC is critical to managing the high dimensionality of variables (e.g., cultural norms, geographic disparities) and enabling probabilistic forecasts at population scales. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for family resource educators and validated metrics for assessing the equity of caregiving support systems. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, economics, and human development, advancing Work and Family Studies into data-intensive domains while preserving its focus on applied, human-centered outcomes.
cip_definition: An introductory program that focuses on family and consumer science concepts and principles at the basic and vocational levels, and the various potential career paths open to interested students. Includes instruction in career, community, and family connections; family and family/consumer resources; human development; interpersonal relationships; nutrition and wellness; parenting; and career possibilities in various related areas.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing hydrocarbon recovery from complex subsurface reservoirs by leveraging advanced computational modeling and high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Conventional reservoir simulation tools often struggle to accurately capture the multiphase fluid dynamics, heterogeneous geological properties, and coupled thermal-hydro-mechanical processes inherent in unconventional oil and gas formations. This limitation hinders the design of efficient enhanced oil recovery (EOR) strategies, particularly in low-permeability reservoirs where marginal gains in extraction efficiency have significant economic and operational implications. To overcome these barriers, this project will develop a high-fidelity, multi-scale reservoir simulator integrating machine learning-assisted parameterization of fracture networks, dynamic fluid-rock interaction models, and uncertainty quantification frameworks. The computational workflow will employ finite volume methods for solving governing equations of multiphase flow, coupled with graph neural networks to model fracture propagation and fluid pathways at the meter-to-micron scale. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across diverse geological scenarios, utilizing petrophysical data from target formations in the Permian Basin as case studies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for evaluating EOR techniques (e.g., CO₂ injection, surfactant flooding) under realistic operational constraints, with particular emphasis on optimizing energy-water-carbon tradeoffs. The resulting models will provide actionable insights for field development planning while advancing fundamental understanding of coupled processes in fractured porous media. By achieving grid resolutions below 1 meter across kilometer-scale domains—computationally infeasible on conventional systems—this work will establish new benchmarks for reservoir simulation fidelity. Successful implementation will directly support petroleum technology innovation through improved recovery forecasts, reduced environmental footprint of extraction operations, and enhanced decision-making tools for subsurface engineers. The project will additionally generate open-source modules for reservoir characterization, fostering collaboration across petroleum technology and computational geoscience communities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of oil and natural gas extraction and processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of petroleum extraction and related geology, petroleum field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, laboratory analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, environment and safety monitoring procedures for oil/gas fields and facilities, facility inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Regulatory science faces a critical challenge in evaluating complex, rapidly evolving medical technologies—such as AI-driven diagnostics or gene-edited therapies—where traditional approval frameworks struggle to balance safety, efficacy, and innovation. This project proposes a computational approach to model and simulate regulatory decision pathways for emerging technologies, enabling data-driven policy optimization. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will develop agent-based models (ABMs) to simulate interactions between regulators, developers, and clinical trial data streams under varying regulatory scenarios. These ABMs will integrate real-world FDA submission datasets, synthetic clinical trial data generated via generative adversarial networks (GANs), and dynamic risk-benefit algorithms that account for evolving post-market evidence. A parallelized computational workflow will assess thousands of regulatory parameter combinations (e.g., evidence thresholds, adaptive trial designs, real-world evidence integration protocols) to identify optimal pathways that minimize time-to-decision while maintaining safety standards. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of historical device/drug approvals and forward-looking case studies on AI-based medical imaging systems. The HPC environment is essential for scaling Monte Carlo simulations across multidimensional parameter spaces and managing petabytes of structured/unstructured regulatory document data. Outcomes will include an open-source computational toolkit for predictive regulatory analytics, quantitative benchmarks for evidence requirements in novel technology domains, and policy recommendations for adaptive licensing frameworks. This work aims to transform regulatory science into a proactive, simulation-informed discipline capable of accelerating patient access to breakthrough technologies without compromising scientific rigor.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the regulatory process for companies innovating and developing cutting edge products in science, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and medicine. Includes instruction in regulatory affairs, clinical documentation, human and animal subject protection, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, data management and analysis, good manufacturing practices, and quality management.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in evidence-based decision-making for human services programs by developing computational models to simulate the dynamics of social service delivery and its impact on vulnerable populations. Despite the growing complexity of social challenges—such as housing insecurity, mental health crises, and systemic inequities—agencies often rely on fragmented data and static analyses, limiting their ability to predict outcomes or optimize interventions. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct large-scale, multi-agent simulation models that integrate demographic, socioeconomic, and service utilization data from public agencies, nonprofits, and community surveys. These models will capture interactions between individuals, service providers, and policy environments at a granular level, enabling dynamic scenario testing under varying resource allocation strategies. Computational methods will include machine learning for pattern recognition in service access disparities, network analysis to map interagency collaboration efficiencies, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risks associated with policy alternatives. The scale of data integration (spanning millions of anonymized client records and longitudinal outcomes) necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and real-time sensitivity analyses. Anticipated outcomes include a framework to identify service delivery bottlenecks, predict the cascading effects of funding changes, and recommend equity-centered resource distribution plans. By translating computational insights into actionable policy tools, this work aims to strengthen the capacity of human services organizations to address systemic inequities, reduce operational inefficiencies, and improve program outcomes for marginalized communities. The project will also produce open-source tools tailored for non-technical stakeholders, bridging the gap between computational social science and applied public administration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and provision of human and social services to individuals and communities and prepares individuals to work in public and private human services agencies and organizations. Includes instruction in the social sciences, psychology, principles of social service, human services policy, planning and evaluation, social services law and administration, and applications to particular issues, services, localities, and populations.

abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with complex mechanisms underlying conditions such as heart failure, arrhythmias, and ischemic heart disease. A critical barrier to advancing personalized cardiology is the integration of multi-modal clinical data—including imaging, electrophysiology, and genomics—into predictive models that account for patient-specific variability. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate computational frameworks capable of simulating cardiac pathophysiology at unprecedented resolution. The research will focus on two interrelated aims: (1) creating multi-scale models of cardiac electromechanics that incorporate patient-derived data from MRI, CT, and intracardiac mapping to simulate arrhythmia propagation and hemodynamic outcomes, and (2) employing machine learning to identify genomic and proteomic biomarkers associated with adverse cardiac remodeling, using whole-genome sequencing and proteomic datasets from longitudinal cohort studies. The computational workflows will utilize finite element modeling, computational fluid dynamics, and deep learning algorithms, necessitating parallelized processing and large-scale memory allocation. By simulating interventions such as catheter ablation or pharmacological therapies in silico, the models aim to predict optimal treatment strategies for individual patients. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for sudden cardiac death risk stratification, the development of open-source simulation tools for clinical researchers, and validation of patient-specific treatment planning protocols through retrospective clinical data analysis. This work addresses a pressing need for computationally intensive approaches in cardiology, where traditional methods fail to capture the interplay between molecular, cellular, and organ-level dynamics. Successful implementation will advance precision cardiology by bridging gaps between computational research and clinical translation, ultimately improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes for patients with complex cardiovascular conditions.
cip_definition: Research focused on Cardiology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the growing computational demands of advanced digital arts research, particularly in the creation and optimization of large-scale, interactive, and AI-driven visual media. Current workflows in digital arts face significant bottlenecks when generating high-resolution 3D environments, simulating dynamic physics-based effects, or training generative neural networks for procedural content creation. These tasks require intensive parallel processing, real-time rendering capabilities, and vast memory allocation—requirements that exceed the capacity of standard desktop workstations. The research will focus on three core areas: (1) developing AI models for generative art and style transfer using multi-GPU training to accelerate iterative design processes; (2) simulating complex particle systems and fluid dynamics for immersive installations through distributed computing frameworks; and (3) enabling real-time interactivity in 4K/8K virtual reality (VR) environments via GPU-accelerated ray tracing and memory-optimized rendering pipelines. Computational methods will include CUDA-optimized algorithms, PyTorch-based neural networks, and MPI-parallelized simulations, validated against benchmarks in rendering efficiency and user experience metrics. The project’s outcomes aim to reduce rendering times by 60–80% for high-fidelity scenes, enable novel artistic workflows through scalable AI tools, and establish best practices for integrating HPC into digital arts pedagogy. By democratizing access to supercomputing resources, this work will empower artists and researchers to explore computationally prohibitive techniques—such as hyperrealistic real-time visuals or billion-parameter generative models—while contributing to interdisciplinary dialogues at the intersection of art, technology, and computational science. Results will directly support faculty-student collaborations, public digital exhibitions, and industry partnerships in game development and immersive media.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A general, undifferentiated program that focuses on the use of computerized digital images as the primary medium of expression in the visual and performing arts, and that may prepare individuals for a wide variety of careers using new media, including graphic design, digital animation, motion graphics, 3D visualization, game and interactive media design, music and sound design, video production, web design, photography, and other fields.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance evidence-based intervention strategies for students exhibiting behavioral challenges by leveraging large-scale, multidimensional datasets through advanced computational modeling. School psychologists often face complex decisions when designing interventions, as student outcomes are influenced by dynamic interactions between individual, classroom, and systemic factors. Traditional statistical methods struggle to capture these nonlinear relationships or optimize personalized recommendations across diverse student populations. To address this gap, we propose developing machine learning (ML) models to analyze longitudinal datasets encompassing academic performance, behavioral assessments, socioemotional surveys, and intervention histories from 50,000+ K–12 students. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training neural networks and ensemble models capable of identifying latent patterns in high-dimensional data, including text-based counseling notes and temporal sequences of behavioral incidents. Computational workflows will integrate feature engineering, cross-validation, and sensitivity analyses to evaluate model robustness, with a focus on equitable outcomes across demographic subgroups. Additionally, agent-based simulations will test hypothetical intervention scenarios under varying classroom conditions. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to prioritize interventions for at-risk students, personalized strategy recommendations, and actionable insights into systemic barriers affecting implementation fidelity. By quantifying the interplay of factors shaping intervention efficacy, this work aims to advance data-driven practices in school psychology, reduce trial-and-error decision-making, and improve scalability of support services. The project aligns with the program’s emphasis on ethical, culturally responsive applications of psychological principles, ensuring models are interpretable for practitioners and compliant with student privacy regulations. HPC resources will enable the iterative refinement required to balance computational complexity with practical utility in school settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the socio-spatial dynamics of equitable housing design in rapidly urbanizing regions, integrating behavioral, economic, and aesthetic factors. Current approaches to evaluating housing equity often rely on static demographic data or qualitative assessments, limiting their ability to predict how built environment features—such as unit layouts, shared infrastructure placement, or access to communal spaces—interact with evolving social and economic pressures. We propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) system coupled with generative design algorithms to simulate how housing configurations influence long-term community resilience, resource distribution, and occupant well-being. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to handle the combinatorial complexity of design variables (e.g., spatial hierarchies, material choices, policy constraints) and large-scale behavioral datasets, including anonymized mobility patterns and household resource usage. The ABM will incorporate dynamic networks of occupant interactions, simulating scenarios under varying constraints such as climate stressors, economic inequality gradients, and policy interventions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to optimize generative design outputs against equity metrics derived from agent behaviors and preference surveys. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking specific design features to measurable social outcomes, a toolkit for policymakers to evaluate housing prototypes computationally, and novel metrics for quantifying "equitable density" in urban planning contexts. By bridging computational social science with architectural analytics, this work addresses a gap in evidence-based housing design tools that account for both human-centered needs and systemic urban challenges. The project’s computational demands—including parallelized simulations of 10,000+ agent populations, high-resolution spatial optimization, and real-time visualization of multi-parameter trade-offs—necessitate dedicated HPC allocations to achieve scalability and practical relevance for global housing stakeholders.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the behavioral, social, economic, functional, and aesthetic aspects of housing, interiors, and other built environments. Includes instruction in analyzing, planning, designing, furnishing, and equipping residential, work, and leisure spaces to meet user needs and the study of related public policies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of simulating large-scale, multi-threat homeland security scenarios to enhance national preparedness and infrastructure resilience. Current computational models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between physical infrastructure, cyber networks, and human decision-making during complex emergencies, such as coordinated cyber-physical attacks, cascading infrastructure failures, or climate-aggravated disasters. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an integrated high-performance computing (HPC) framework capable of modeling hybrid threat scenarios with unprecedented spatial, temporal, and operational granularity. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling, stochastic optimization, and machine learning to simulate (1) adversarial behavior patterns in cyber and physical domains, (2) real-time critical infrastructure interdependencies (e.g., power grids, transportation systems), and (3) emergency response coordination under uncertainty. The HPC environment will enable parallelized execution of multi-scale simulations, incorporating terabyte-scale datasets from historical incidents, IoT sensors, and synthetic threat landscapes. Key innovations include adaptive graph neural networks to predict cascading failures in interdependent systems and physics-informed reinforcement learning to optimize resource allocation during evolving crises. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool for federal and state agencies to stress-test defense protocols, quantify systemic vulnerabilities, and prioritize mitigation investments. The computational outputs will directly inform updates to the National Infrastructure Protection Plan and regional disaster response frameworks. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this work will advance predictive capabilities for emerging asymmetric threats while establishing scalable methodologies for security-critical simulations. Successful implementation requires dedicated access to HPC resources supporting 10,000+ core-hour workloads, large-memory nodes for graph-based analytics, and high-throughput data pipelines for real-time scenario perturbation testing.
cip_definition: A program focusing on security policy, planning and operations dedicated to the protection of U.S. territory, assets, infrastructure, institutions and citizens from external threats. Includes instruction in national security policy, government relations, intelligence, law enforcement, security technology, communications and information technology, homeland security planning and operations, disaster planning and applications to specific threat scenarios.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and application of multiscale quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods for modeling complex chemical reactions in biological and condensed-phase systems. A critical challenge in theoretical chemistry lies in accurately simulating reactive pathways in large, heterogeneous environments—such as enzyme active sites or solvated interfaces—where traditional quantum chemical methods are computationally prohibitive, and classical force fields lack the precision to capture bond-breaking/forming processes. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating highly parallelized ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning-accelerated free-energy sampling. The QM region will employ density functional theory (DFT) with advanced exchange-correlation functionals to model electronic rearrangements during catalysis, while the MM environment will utilize polarizable force fields parameterized via neural network potentials trained on high-level coupled-cluster data. Key targets include elucidating proton-coupled electron transfer mechanisms in metalloenzymes and predicting solvent reorganization effects on reaction barriers in aqueous organic systems. These simulations demand significant HPC resources due to the need for extensive configurational sampling, large-scale parallelization of electronic structure calculations, and iterative training of machine learning models on terabytes of trajectory data. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for balancing accuracy and efficiency in multiscale simulations, atomistic insights into experimentally observed kinetic isotope effects in biocatalysis, and open-source software tools for automating QM/MM workflow management on distributed-memory architectures. The results will directly inform experimental efforts in enzyme engineering and sustainable catalyst design, bridging gaps between theoretical predictions and empirical observations in reactive chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of mathematical and computational methods and fundamental laws of physics to describe chemical phenomena and to develop empirical models of molecules and their interactions. Includes instruction in properties of small, isolated molecules; dynamics of elementary chemical processes; reaction pathways of organic molecules; hydrogen bonding patterns in liquids; reaction rates of biological pathways; and advanced computational techniques.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of symbiotic microbial communities in mediating heat tolerance in agriculturally significant entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs). EPNs are critical biocontrol agents for insect pests, but their efficacy declines under rising soil temperatures linked to climate change. While prior studies focus on nematode physiology, the contribution of their native microbiota to thermal resilience remains uncharacterized. This project integrates metagenomic sequencing, metabolic network modeling, and agent-based simulations to elucidate how symbiotic bacteria influence EPN survival and insect host infection dynamics under thermal stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process terabase-scale metagenomic datasets from heat-exposed nematode populations, reconstruct strain-specific metabolic models for 200+ bacterial symbionts, and simulate host-microbe interactions across spatial temperature gradients. Custom computational pipelines will identify thermal response genes in symbiont genomes, predict metabolite exchange networks sustaining nematode energetics, and model population-scale shifts in EPN foraging behavior under simulated warming scenarios. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting climate-driven disruptions in nematode biocontrol efficacy, identification of candidate thermal-protective symbionts for agricultural inoculation, and foundational insights into the evolution of metazoan-microbe thermo-adaptation. By bridging microbial ecology, thermodynamics, and population dynamics, this work establishes a new computational paradigm for studying symbiosis in invertebrate systems while addressing urgent needs in sustainable pest management. The requested resources will enable previously intractable analyses of multi-species metabolic coupling and large-scale parameter space exploration essential for translating microbial community dynamics into predictive conservation tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of large-scale digital communication networks and their role in shaping ideological polarization, using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions and media effects. While communication theory provides frameworks for understanding interpersonal and mass communication, the rapid evolution of digital platforms—and their algorithmically mediated environments—has created gaps in empirical, data-driven analyses of how information cascades influence societal fragmentation. Traditional methods struggle to process the scale and temporal granularity of modern communication data, which includes billions of multimodal interactions (text, video, metadata) across platforms like Twitter, Reddit, and forums. This project will employ computational social science techniques, including natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and agent-based modeling, to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of public digital discourse. HPC resources will enable the training of transformer-based models for sentiment and framing analysis, dynamic network simulations to trace information diffusion, and Bayesian inference to quantify the impact of algorithmic amplification on polarization. By integrating communication theories—such as social identity theory and spiral of silence—with computational models, the research will identify patterns in how echo chambers form, how misinformation spreads across heterogeneous groups, and how platform design choices mediate these processes. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of annotated communication networks, predictive models of polarization dynamics, and evidence-based recommendations for mitigating divisiveness in digital spaces. This work will advance communication theory by bridging qualitative frameworks with quantitative, scalable methods, offering insights critical for policymakers, educators, and platform designers aiming to foster healthier public discourse in an era of pervasive digital mediation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on theories of communication. Includes instruction in theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing personalized fitness regimens by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral variables in real-world training environments. While advances in wearable technology and exercise science have generated vast datasets on individual performance metrics, current analytical tools lack the computational power to integrate multimodal data—such as motion capture, metabolic rates, muscle activation patterns, and psychological feedback—into dynamic, adaptive training models. This project will develop a computational framework to simulate individualized exercise adaptations, employing machine learning algorithms to predict optimal training loads, recovery intervals, and injury risk thresholds. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution biomechanical datasets from 3D motion analysis systems, coupled with physiological data streams from wearable sensors, to create probabilistic models of training efficacy. A novel aspect involves agent-based modeling of client adherence factors, incorporating behavioral psychology principles to simulate long-term engagement patterns under varying program designs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for fitness professionals to generate evidence-based, personalized programs that balance performance gains with injury prevention. By bridging computational modeling with practical fitness programming, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in non-clinical physical fitness settings, with potential applications in preventive health strategies and adaptive training technologies. The computational demands of real-time multisensor integration and large-scale parameter optimization necessitate HPC resources to achieve the required latency and precision for actionable insights.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in algebraic number theory and arithmetic geometry by addressing computational challenges inherent to studying class groups, Selmer groups, and rational points on higher-genus curves. The central problem involves developing scalable algorithms to analyze invariants of algebraic structures associated with number fields and elliptic curves, with applications to longstanding conjectures such as the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and the Cohen-Lenstra heuristics. Current methods for computing étale cohomology groups, regulator constants, or Tate-Shafarevich groups face exponential complexity when scaling to degrees or conductors relevant to theoretical predictions, necessitating high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The proposed computational approach combines optimized implementations of p-adic cohomology algorithms, distributed parallelization of lattice-based attacks on Diophantine equations, and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures for sieving in quadratic form spaces. Key tasks include enumerating isomorphism classes of abelian extensions with prescribed ramification, computing Hecke eigenvalues for automorphic forms over totally real fields, and verifying divisibility properties in Iwasawa modules. These methods will leverage existing libraries (PARI/GP, SageMath) alongside custom C++/MPI codes for distributed memory models. Expected outcomes include the first large-scale verification of stability patterns in Tamagawa numbers under base change, empirical bounds for ranks of Jacobians of genus-2 curves, and open datasets of class group structures for fields of degree ≥6. The results will directly inform conjectures in Galois deformation theory and refine asymptotic models in analytic number theory. By overcoming memory and runtime barriers in exact arithmetic, this work will enable algebraic techniques to address problems previously accessible only through analytic or probabilistic approximations, strengthening synergies between computational experimentation and theoretical innovation in pure mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the expression of quantities and their relationships by means of symbols, vectors, matrices, and equations, and the properties of integers. Includes instruction in algebraic structures, quadratic and automorphic forms, combinatorics, linear algebra, and algebraic geometry.

abstract: Infertility and reproductive endocrine disorders, such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and endometriosis, affect millions globally, yet their multifactorial etiologies—spanning genetic, hormonal, metabolic, and environmental interactions—remain poorly characterized. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches are often empiric, with suboptimal success rates, due to limited tools for modeling the complexity of these systems. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop integrative computational models that decode the dynamic interplay of biological factors driving reproductive endocrine dysfunction and infertility. The research will focus on multi-omics data integration (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic datasets from clinical cohorts) to identify predictive biomarkers and mechanistic pathways. Machine learning frameworks, including graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be employed to model non-linear interactions and temporal patterns in high-dimensional datasets. Agent-based modeling will simulate cellular and molecular interactions within ovarian and endometrial microenvironments to test hypotheses about folliculogenesis, implantation failure, and hormonal dysregulation. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further analyze uterine hemodynamic changes associated with infertility. These approaches demand HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-scale parameter optimization, and handling datasets exceeding 100 TB. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets, stratification of patient subgroups for personalized interventions, and predictive models to optimize assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes. By elucidating mechanisms underlying treatment resistance and disease heterogeneity, this work aims to advance precision medicine in reproductive endocrinology. The requested resources will enable rapid iteration of models, validation against clinical datasets, and scalable analysis of emerging multi-institutional data, directly addressing a critical need for computational power in this data-rich but hypothesis-sparse field.
cip_definition: Research on how to manage complex problems relating to reproductive endocrinology and infertility.

abstract: The increasing frequency of hydroclimatic extremes and competing water demands necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize water resource management under uncertainty. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, integrated modeling framework to simulate coupled surface water-groundwater dynamics in large, data-scarce river basins, with a focus on adaptive flood risk assessment and multi-objective reservoir operation. The research problem centers on addressing gaps in current models, which often oversimplify groundwater-surface water interactions or fail to incorporate real-time climate forecasts at basin scales. The computational approach combines a physically based hydrological model (SWAT-MODFLOW coupling) with ensemble climate projections and machine learning techniques to improve predictions of water availability and flood hazards. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallel execution of ensemble simulations across multiple climate scenarios, sensitivity analyses of land use change impacts, and optimization of reservoir release policies using evolutionary algorithms. The framework will integrate continental-scale hydroclimate datasets, including downscaled CMIP6 projections and remote sensing products, requiring distributed memory architectures for efficient data handling. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible modeling toolkit for evaluating tradeoffs between agricultural water allocations, urban demands, and ecological flows under changing conditions. The project will directly inform drought contingency planning in the study basin while advancing computational methodologies for water resource systems analysis. By quantifying uncertainty propagation through coupled human-natural systems, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for resilience-informed infrastructure design in water resources engineering, with particular relevance to climate adaptation strategies in transboundary basins. The requested HPC allocation is critical given the 10^6+ computational node-hour requirements for stochastic optimization and the need to resolve sub-kilometer spatial heterogeneities in aquifer-river exchange processes.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for collecting, storing, moving, conserving and controlling surface- and groundwater, including water quality control, water cycle management, management of human and industrial water requirements, water delivery, and flood control.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize modular construction workflows, addressing inefficiencies in resource allocation, scheduling, and material utilization within rapidly evolving construction trades. Modular construction—a process where building components are prefabricated off-site—requires precise coordination of labor, equipment, and supply chains to meet project timelines and cost targets. However, current industry practices rely on heuristic decision-making, leading to delays, material waste, and suboptimal energy use in prefabrication facilities. To overcome these challenges, we propose a multi-scale simulation approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model dynamic interactions between workforce availability, equipment throughput, material delivery logistics, and energy consumption patterns. Agent-based modeling will simulate worker-task assignments under varying site conditions, while discrete-event simulations will optimize fabrication sequencing across parallel production lines. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict material stress behavior in modular units under transport and assembly conditions, informed by finite element analysis datasets. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for stochastic scenario testing across thousands of parameter combinations, including variable weather impacts, supply chain disruptions, and design alterations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for (1) real-time adjustment of fabrication schedules based on material lead times and labor capacity, (2) energy-efficient facility layouts minimizing robotic arm motion paths, and (3) machine learning-derived material specifications reducing waste by 15-20% in modular component production. By deploying these HPC-enabled models through a cloud-based interface, the research aims to provide trade professionals with actionable insights to improve project feasibility in off-site construction—a critical need as urbanization pressures demand faster, greener building solutions. The proposed resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations of up to 10,000 concurrent agent interactions and terabyte-scale analysis of LiDAR-scanned construction site data.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in construction trades, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of non-textual symbolic communication in decentralized digital communities, focusing on the emergence and evolution of visual-iconographic systems within niche online platforms. As digital spaces increasingly prioritize multimodal interaction, communities are developing complex visual languages—such as emoji sequences, custom avatars, and procedural generative art—that transcend conventional linguistic frameworks. These systems raise fundamental questions about collective meaning-making, cultural transmission, and identity formation in post-textual environments, yet remain understudied due to the technical challenges of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous multimedia datasets. The research will employ computational visual semiotics, combining computer vision techniques for pattern recognition in image corpora with graph-based network analysis of usage contexts across temporal and platform boundaries. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing petabytes of user-generated content from federated platforms (including ActivityPub networks and blockchain-based communities), requiring GPU-accelerated feature extraction, transformer-based multimodal embedding, and dynamic network modeling at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a computational framework for identifying emergent visual grammars across decentralized networks, 2) quantitative models of cultural innovation diffusion in iconographic systems, and 3) ethical guidelines for preserving ephemeral digital vernaculars. By bridging humanities-focused cultural analysis with scalable computational methods, this work aims to establish new paradigms for studying twenty-first-century cultural production while addressing preservation challenges posed by proprietary platform dependencies and digital obsolescence. The resource request supports both the development of custom vision-language models tailored to grassroots digital aesthetics and the creation of an open repository for analyzing at-risk community-generated visual cultures.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying metabolic disorders in ruminants, with a focus on dairy cattle experiencing ketosis—a prevalent and economically significant condition in livestock agriculture. Current experimental approaches to study these disorders face limitations in resolving dynamic, multi-scale interactions between hormonal regulation, tissue-specific metabolism, and systemic pathophysiology. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) with physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) models. These models will simulate hormone-receptor binding kinetics, hepatic lipid metabolism, and inter-organ crosstalk under varying metabolic stressors. Machine learning algorithms will identify critical regulatory nodes and predict biomarkers for early disease detection. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of stochastic molecular dynamics simulations (using tools like GROMACS) and large-scale parameter optimization for organ-level models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets to modulate hepatic ketogenesis, predictive models of metabolic resilience, and a publicly accessible database of ruminant-specific physiological parameters. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by enabling targeted interventions, reducing livestock morbidity, and improving agricultural sustainability. The developed computational pipelines will also provide a template for studying analogous metabolic syndromes in non-mammalian species, broadening translational applications in veterinary physiology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the functional dynamics of animal biological systems and their relationship to the diagnosis and treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in mammalian and non-mammalian physiology, laboratory physiology, physiological responses to the environment, endocrinology, animal biotechnology, mechanisms of hormone action, organ systems, metabolism, and pathophysiology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable decision-support platform for education entrepreneurs to optimize resource allocation in innovative learning ventures, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic educational ecosystems. Education entrepreneurs face complex challenges in balancing financial sustainability, equitable access, and pedagogical impact, particularly when scaling interventions across diverse contexts. Current planning tools lack the capacity to integrate real-time data on market dynamics, funding volatility, and learner outcomes, resulting in suboptimal resource distribution and missed opportunities for systemic impact. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling framework simulating interactions between stakeholders (e.g., schools, investors, policymakers) and variables such as funding cycles, enrollment patterns, and operational costs. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of scenarios, including Monte Carlo analyses of risk exposure under fluctuating economic conditions and machine learning-driven sensitivity testing of business model pivots. The computational architecture will incorporate heterogeneous datasets—from philanthropic investment trends to regional education infrastructure metrics—to train predictive models identifying high-leverage intervention points. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation engine capable of forecasting 3-year financial and educational outcomes under user-defined constraints, with applications in venture capital due diligence, philanthropic grant strategy, and adaptive project management for education startups. By quantifying trade-offs between profitability and equity in resource allocation decisions, this work aims to advance evidence-based entrepreneurship practices while maintaining computational reproducibility standards for public benefit. The requested resources will specifically support GPU-accelerated parameter optimization and validation against historical case studies of failed/persistent education ventures, requiring ~200,000 core-hours for initial development and benchmarking. Results will be disseminated through open-access models and integrated into a graduate-level curriculum on computational decision-making in education leadership.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create, fund, and manage innovations in education. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, the design of learning environments, the economics of education, entrepreneurship, evaluation, finance, human-centered design, investing, resource management, project management, and marketing.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of nuclear facilities relies on high-fidelity modeling of complex multiphysics phenomena, including neutron transport, thermal-hydraulic behavior, and structural response under extreme conditions. Current computational tools often employ simplified assumptions to reduce runtime, limiting their ability to resolve coupled physics interactions at scales relevant to safety-critical scenarios such as transient overpower events or loss-of-coolant accidents. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate advanced multiscale simulations of nuclear systems, enabling predictive analyses of reactor performance and accident progression with unprecedented resolution. The research will employ Monte Carlo methods for neutronics, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for coolant flow and heat transfer, and finite element analysis (FEA) for stress-strain evaluation, integrated through iterative coupling algorithms optimized for parallel processing. Key challenges include managing memory-intensive cross-section libraries for reactor core modeling and resolving turbulent multiphase flows in containment systems. By utilizing GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed-memory architectures, the team will perform parametric studies of advanced fuel cladding materials and simulate radiological dispersion under hypothetical accident sequences to inform emergency response protocols. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting fuel assembly degradation and containment vessel integrity, which will directly support regulatory risk assessments and the design of next-generation reactors with enhanced inherent safety features. The computational workflows developed through this work will be shared with the nuclear engineering community via open-source repositories, fostering collaboration in safety-focused simulation efforts.
