By bridging communication theory with computational rigor, this work aims to advance scholarly understanding of how adaptive communication systems can foster resilient organizations while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC resources in non-traditional computational domains. Results will be disseminated through interdisciplinary journals and a practitioner toolkit for diagnosing communication health in complex organizations.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: Blood transfusion safety and efficacy rely on precise antigen-antibody compatibility assessments, optimized donor-recipient matching, and robust predictive models for adverse reactions. Current methods for antibody identification, particularly in patients with complex serologies or rare blood types, remain time-intensive and error-prone due to manual interpretation of agglutination patterns and limited computational tools. This project proposes to develop machine learning (ML) models and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to enhance immunohematology workflows, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical bottlenecks. We will train deep neural networks on multi-institutional datasets—including historical donor-recipient pairing outcomes, antigenic profiles, and hemolytic reaction records—to predict high-risk incompatibilities and automate antibody rule-outs. Concurrently, all-atom MD simulations will characterize the structural dynamics of clinically significant erythrocyte antigens (e.g., Rh, Kell, Duffy systems) under varying storage conditions, informing improved preservation protocols. The computational pipeline will integrate genomic data from blood donors to model population-specific antigen frequencies, optimizing inventory management for diverse patient demographics. HPC resources are essential for processing terabyte-scale immunohematology datasets, running parallelized MD trajectories across antigen-antibody complexes, and deploying ensemble ML architectures with hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support tool for antibody identification, predictive metrics for transfusion-related complications, and evidence-based guidelines for blood component storage. By bridging computational biology with blood bank operations, this work aims to reduce diagnostic delays, minimize wastage of rare blood products, and improve outcomes for transfusion-dependent patients. The developed frameworks will be validated against prospectively collected clinical data from partner blood centers, ensuring translational relevance for health professions training programs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between cultural narratives, psychological resilience, and biological markers in end-of-life decision-making processes. Thanatology, as an interdisciplinary field, lacks integrative computational models capable of synthesizing large-scale qualitative, quantitative, and biomolecular datasets to predict how individuals and communities navigate terminal illness and grief. The research problem centers on the absence of predictive frameworks that reconcile ethical, emotional, and epigenetic factors influencing palliative care choices, particularly in underrepresented populations. To address this gap, we propose a mixed-methods computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP) of longitudinal patient narratives, agent-based modeling of social support networks, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling of stress-related biomarkers (e.g., cortisol, inflammatory cytokines). The NLP pipeline will process ethnographic interviews and digital diaries to identify linguistic patterns associated with adaptive vs. maladaptive grieving, while agent-based simulations will explore how community-level interventions alter collective bereavement outcomes. Concurrently, biomarker data from hospice patients will be integrated to quantify biological correlates of psychological states. HPC resources are critical for managing the heterogeneous data streams, enabling parallel processing of text corpora (>10^6 documents), stochastic simulation ensembles (>10^4 parameter variations), and computationally intensive Bayesian inference across high-dimensional datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) a novel computational framework for personalized thanatological risk stratification, (2) evidence-based guidelines for culturally responsive grief interventions, and (3) open-source tools bridging computational social science and palliative biomedicine. By elucidating the multiscale drivers of end-of-life experiences, this work aims to transform interdisciplinary thanatology into a predictive science, directly informing clinical practice and policy while preserving the humanistic core of death studies.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, philosophical, psychological, sociological, and theological aspects of death, dying, and bereavement. Includes instruction in counseling, ethics, grief, palliative and hospice care, philosophy, thanatology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the computational challenges inherent in analyzing and modeling complex dance movement patterns, with a focus on advancing interdisciplinary methodologies in dance research. While dance is inherently embodied and ephemeral, emerging technologies now enable the capture and quantification of movement at unprecedented resolution. However, processing large-scale motion capture datasets—often comprising terabytes of multimodal data from wearable sensors, inertial measurement units, and optical systems—requires scalable computational infrastructure. The research problem centers on decoding the relationship between biomechanical efficiency and aesthetic intent in improvised contemporary dance, a domain lacking systematic computational frameworks. Current methods for segmenting and classifying movement sequences rely on simplified kinematic models, failing to capture the high-dimensional interplay of physiological, cultural, and creative factors that define dance practice. To address this, we propose a parallelized computational pipeline integrating musculoskeletal simulations, deep learning-based gesture recognition, and network analysis of improvisational logic. HPC resources will enable 1) biomechanical optimization of movement sequences using OpenSim-based simulations at scale, 2) training of transformer models on annotated video datasets to identify choreographic motifs across diverse cultural dance forms, and 3) real-time rendering of ensemble interactions in virtual environments for compositional experimentation. Expected outcomes include a publicly available movement analysis toolkit for dance scholars, quantitative frameworks for assessing injury risk in choreography, and novel metrics linking kinematic complexity to perceived artistic expression. By bridging computational science and dance theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for preserving intangible cultural heritage, enhancing dance pedagogy, and fostering collaborative creativity at the intersection of art and technology.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance foundational research in computational complexity theory by investigating the scalability and practical limitations of quantum-inspired algorithms for solving NP-hard problems. While such algorithms—including simulated annealing variants and tensor network contractions—have shown theoretical promise in approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems, their empirical behavior under large-scale, real-world problem instances remains poorly understood. A core challenge lies in analyzing the trade-offs between algorithmic precision, computational resource requirements, and problem dimensionality, particularly as instances scale beyond classical simulation capabilities. To address this, we propose a dual mathematical-computational approach: (1) developing novel complexity-theoretic models to quantify the asymptotic resource costs of these algorithms under non-uniform input distributions, and (2) implementing large-scale simulations on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to empirically validate theoretical predictions. The computational work will focus on parallelized simulations of algorithm behavior across problem sizes ranging from 10³ to 10⁷ variables, leveraging GPU-accelerated tensor operations and distributed memory architectures. Key metrics will include time-to-solution convergence, memory overhead patterns, and error propagation dynamics in approximation schemes. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the exponential state-space growth inherent to these simulations, particularly when benchmarking against classical baselines like branch-and-bound algorithms. Expected outcomes include new complexity classifications for quantum-inspired methods, optimized implementation strategies for emerging computing architectures, and practical guidelines for algorithm selection in applied mathematics contexts. By bridging theoretical complexity analysis with large-scale empirical validation, this work aims to establish rigorous performance boundaries for next-generation optimization algorithms while advancing methodological frameworks for computational resource analysis in theoretical computer science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical techniques underlying computing, including the theory of computation, and logic in computer science and artificial intelligence.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the role of bioelectrical signaling in non-neural collective behaviors of multicellular aggregates, a novel area bridging developmental biology, biophysics, and synthetic morphology. Traditional studies of cellular communication have focused on biochemical or mechanical pathways, but emerging evidence suggests that endogenous electric fields and ion channel dynamics drive self-organization in systems lacking neural networks, such as regenerating tissues or synthetic organoids. This project addresses a critical gap in understanding how spatially distributed bioelectric patterns coordinate large-scale morphological outcomes without centralized control. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop a multiscale computational framework integrating stochastic lattice Boltzmann methods for ion flux propagation with agent-based models of individual cell responses to electrochemical gradients. The simulations will parameterize experimentally observed phenomena in planarian regeneration and bioengineered mammalian cell clusters, testing hypotheses about threshold-driven phase transitions in collective decision-making. Expected outcomes include predictive models of electrotonic signal propagation in heterogeneous cellular networks and identification of stability criteria for target morphological states. This work will establish foundational principles for designing electroceutical therapies and programming synthetic biological systems through bioelectric interfaces, advancing applications in regenerative medicine and adaptive biomaterials. The computational approach uniquely addresses the nonlinear coupling between cellular-scale ion dynamics and population-level emergent order, requiring parallelized simulations across 10^5–10^6 interacting agents with dynamically updating boundary conditions. Resource allocation will enable parameter sweeps across physiologically relevant electrochemical ranges and machine learning-driven optimization of pattern stability metrics.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the biological and biomedical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for the design and optimization of adaptive thermal metamaterials using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research addresses the critical challenge of dynamic thermal management in compact, high-power-density systems such as advanced microelectronics and energy storage devices, where traditional passive thermal control methods are insufficient. By leveraging engineered materials with tunable thermal conductivity and emissivity, the project aims to create structures capable of real-time heat flux redirection and dissipation in response to operational demands. The computational approach integrates multi-physics finite element modeling with machine learning-driven topology optimization to explore non-intuitive metamaterial geometries and their transient thermal responses. Large-scale parameter sweeps will be conducted to map the relationship between microstructural configurations, external stimuli (e.g., mechanical strain, electric fields), and macroscopic thermal properties. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulation of coupled thermo-mechanical phenomena across multiple scales while accelerating inverse design processes through neural network training on terascale datasets. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for active thermal metamaterials, a publicly shared optimization toolkit for adaptive heat management systems, and prototype designs demonstrating ≥40% improvement in thermal buffering capacity compared to static solutions. This work bridges gaps between solid mechanics, thermodynamics, and computational materials science, offering a foundation for smart thermal regulation technologies with applications in next-generation electronics, aerospace auxiliary systems, and renewable energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and optimization of hybrid photovoltaic-thermal (PV-T) solar energy systems through high-fidelity computational modeling, addressing critical gaps in efficiency and reliability under variable environmental conditions. Current PV-T systems face challenges in balancing electrical output with thermal management, particularly in climates with fluctuating irradiance and ambient temperatures. Traditional experimental approaches are limited in capturing the dynamic, multi-physics interactions between photovoltaic cells, thermal transfer fluids, and storage components at scale. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) for heat transfer modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for fluid flow optimization, and machine learning (ML) to predict material degradation under cyclic thermal stress. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements and transient boundary conditions over multi-year operational horizons. Key objectives include identifying optimal flow geometries for minimized entropy generation, validating adaptive control algorithms for hybrid energy storage, and quantifying the long-term performance of novel anti-reflective coatings. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit for PV-T system design, performance benchmarks for diverse climatic regions, and actionable insights into mitigating efficiency losses caused by thermal cycling. This work will directly support the development of next-generation solar energy systems with higher energy yields and improved economic viability, contributing to broader renewable energy adoption goals. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of system configurations, reducing time-to-solution by orders of magnitude compared to local cluster capabilities. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and integrated into solar technology curricula, fostering collaboration between computational researchers and industry stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing solar-powered energy systems. Includes instruction in solar energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.
